reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I have taken at purdue because of Dr. Z Her lectures are impossible to follow & her exams are so tricky confusing. You can walk in feeling 110% prepared and get a 20% on exams. This is not a student friendly class. There is no real opportunity to learn since there is rarely hw and labs are usually unrelated to lecture.

Zielinski is the worst prof at Purdue. Does not care about her students or their success at all. Her lecture exams & lab exams are impossible and trick you. I am always up for a challenging science course, but she makes this 100-level class impossible. It should be a 300-level bio class with her teaching. Take this class with Humphrey!!! Do better
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very difficult for being a 100 level class, Just beware if you get her for your prof. Also just be on the look out there are weekly quizzes and group discussions that are over very specific information in the lecture slides.

Class averages are consistently in the 60s or even 50s range, with her saying 20% of students got in the 20-30%. No matter how much you study you will be unprepared, her exams are extremely detailed and her lectures can be hard to follow since there is so much information packed into each lecture slide. Take Humphrey instead if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please listen to the reviews when they say to take Humphrey instead. This class is made 10 times harder by her lectures which are extremely long and detailed and her exams are made to trick you. The lab exams are even worse and no matter how much studying you do, it will still not make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Compared to Humphrey in 110, this should be a 300 level BIO course. Quizzes and exams tested extremely specific information. After the first exam, she discussed that many students scores were in the 20s-30s. Her solution was that we need to study better. In my opinion, I'm not absorbing her lectures or understanding her exam questions.

For a 2-credit class, the structure was way out of pocket. I'm in environmental engineering and need this class as a course requirement. I failed with Dr. barely felt like I was capable of learning in her course, and when I took it again with a different professor I got an A. Dr. Z often ghosted my emails asking for help. Lots more could say.
If you want a good grade in this class be ready to memorize all the details on her slides.

Avoid if you can. Worth more than 2 credits. If you take this class, prepare for exams by drilling the slides into your brain and memorize EVERY example used because you will need to use them for the free response. Multiple choice uses a lot of "A and B only" or "Both A and B" and the wording of these answers seems like it's meant to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class wasn't incredible, it was a lot of memorization of terms and not too much critically thinking about questions, the homeworks didn't seem too hard but then I got graded roughly anyway, and the exams are not too fun. Remarkably I did better on the free response than the multiple choice. Just watch the lectures online and write down terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was extremely hard for 2 credits, her homework takes time so go to her office hours. TAs are of no help and think they have more power than her. Exams are extremely difficult and you have to memorize every single detail and still end up with a B/C. Just be prepare to study and learn absolutely nothing.

For a 2 credit INTRO to ECOLOGY class, this was a complete nightmare. Lectures are horrible and the slides are so jumbled with information it's difficult to process. Exams will ask about the most specific details found on only a single lecture slide. Takes forever to get grades and students have to jump through hoops to get fair grades. Horrible.

Dr. Z is very specific and very confusing. She sets very specific criteria for grading tests and homeworks but does not communicate those criteria so there's a lot of guessing and hoping involved. She wants precise examples from her lecture slides and won't give credit for other examples even if they are comparable. Wouldn't take again.

During the quiet week, in which instructors are not supposed to give assignments, she gave an essay out and claimed it was a "headstart" on your exam. It was ridiculous and took away time to study for her extremely hard exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: IT'S HARD TO FOCUS ON HER LECTURES AND HER GRADING SCHEME IS TOUGH FOR PEOPLE TO SURVIVE IN THIS COURSE, IT'S HARD TO IMAGINE THIS COURSE JUST WORTH 2 CREDIT POINTS CUZ I ALWAYS THOUGHT IT WAS WORTH AT LEAST 4!!!!!!! YOU HAVE TO SPEND MORE THAN 30 HRS PER WEEK STUDYING FOR HER LECTURES CUZ THE MATERIALS ARE TOO DETAILED TO MEMORIZE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zielinski has some of the worst slide decks and lectures I have been witness to in my time at Purdue. Her slides are packed full of irrelevant content and not cohesive. The cherry on top is Dr. Zielinski's complete disregard for student accommodations or wellbeing.

When people say don't take Bio 286, LISTEN! Run the other way if Dr. Zielinski is the professor. It is all rote memorization. She doesn't care about teaching at all. She refused to answer questions because they asked for clarification on something she was contradictory. She is the epitome of a tenured professor and Purdue needs to do something.

Too much info for 2 credit hours and I think they know it, they just won't admit it. Grading is asinine at best as the graders never seem satisfied with your answer and will find a way to take off points. It also takes them a month on average to return exam grades and 2-3 weeks for homework. This class is more work to do and more points to lose.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She sets up her exams by pulling random sentences from a slide and puts it on the exam. That doesn't sound bad but the first exam contained over 240 slides of content that are packed to the brim and out of those 240 slides she selected 25 multiple choice with seven written responses. You are not given a study guide to exactly know what to study for

The content of BIOL286 is very interesting and Dr.Z is an ok lecturer. I don't agree with the harshness of the grading on homework and exams. I would feel extremely prepared and confident for an exam and still get a B/C. Takes way too long to grade anything, ESPECIALLY exams. Do the thought questions and PRACTICE EXAMS!!
Class is worth 2 credits, should be 3. Wasn't supposed to pass the class but did because she had to curve so low so that the majority of the class didn't fail and she wouldn't get fired.

Lectures have way too much content and her tests are unreasonably specific in the details she expects you to know. Her tests make it seem like she expects you to memorize every single word on each slide, and they are PACKED with content
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult and showed barely any mercy. The exams were very wordy and asked about minor things. Her idea of extra credit was a research paper and 2-3 bonus questions on the exam. However, the bonus questions were so bizarre that you had to guess

I had friends who took Biol 111 with Humphrey and were shocked when I explained how difficult Zielinski's exams were. To do well on exams, just memorize directly from her slides. Exam averages were never above a D, causing the need for an extreme curve at the end because she won't curve exams.

Honestly, I mostly hated this class, but at the end, the professor is fair in her grading. To be successful in this class, you have to put in the work. The textbook helps, but spend more time on the lectures. There are tons of extra credit opportunities, make sure you do them. I suggest attending lecture and then rewatching it online again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, but lucky for you, every single thing that is asked on exams is found in the slides. People often say this class is impossible but it comes from lack of effort. The grading scale is the most generous I've seen. So many points are offered with the easy scale, so dont lose free pts and exam average can be lower and get an A

Dr. Z expects students to memorize her slides for exams, and if you don't remember the smallest details, you won't do well on exams. I did horrible on exams but did well on everything else. The only reason I managed an A was because of the extra credit, and she curved the course at the end. If you can, take this course with the other professor.
She is one of the worse lecturer ever

For a 2 credit hour class, this class really gave me a tough time. My learning style did not match with Professor Zielinski's teaching style at all, and I found it really difficult to remember every detail that she expected us to know on the exams. I found the exams to be difficult, though she did give partial credit for some multiple choice.
Just graded intensely. High point values removed for small mistakes

Very caring and nice person. But class is a little tough. Be sure to memorize every slide for midterms and do past exams which can be similar. She did an at-home essay for a part of the final which I liked. Multiple choice is tough and the grading on short response for hw/exams is tough also. Be as detailed as you can with including key words.

Exams cover a lot and test on small details from lectures, so just memorize slides. Homework takes forever to finish, can be very vague, and actively tries to make you miss points. Painfully slow at grading (took a month release an exam grade, even after TAs had finished grading weeks prior), blamed low exam scores on COVID (in Spring 2022)

This was the worst class I have ever taken. The grading is extremely specific and the prompts are overly confusing. She clearly cares about the subject and is knowledgeable but makes learning the subject painful.

The hardest 2 credit class I will ever take. Dr.Z is a nice person, but does everything as worst as she possibly can. half the content in her lectures are worthless but she expects you to know ever little detail of over 400 slides for 1 exam. The homework's take 2-4 hours each. Exams are insanely difficult. DONT DO IT.

This is probably the worst class I have ever taken at Purdue. So much material, such tiny details, you have to know everything. TA's are on the biggest power trip, and will take off points even if you have the answer word for word. 0/10 would not recommend.

Zielinski is incredibly knowledgeable about biology, and this is reflected in her lectures. However, the exams are unnecessarily complicated and often outside the scope of the material. The MC section, because there can be multiple correct answers, are like gambling, and the lectures are incredibly dense and overly packed with information.

She's a nice lady outside of class, but I wasn't a fan of her as a professor. The exams are so complicated with her including long passages about a certain disease and then expecting us to answer the next 6 questions related to it. It's the second semester of an intro class, there's no reason to test us on material we don't know. Steer clear!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams focus on extremely specific parts of the lecture, and your grade is determined not on how well you understand the overall concepts, but rather how well you memorize the slides. If you take this class, do not do it with this professor. She is a very nice lady, but she makes this class more difficult than it needs to be.

As a person Dr.Z is very knowledgeable and friendly. However, nothing is clear. The way she words her exams makes it nearly impossible to do well. Her exams cover a very wide range of information and if you do not know all the insane specifics you will not pass. You hardly ever know what the quizzes will be about and she flies through lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible. Avoid at all costs. Exams are made to be as tricky as possible, slides are jam packed with information that she will proceed to read off of during lecture (while constantly out of breath). There's an exam nearly every other week, and 1-2 quizzes per recitation. I would rather retake Calc 2 than take a class with her again.
The exam is really hard. I put lots of effort into it. Do not take it! Try Humphrey!

There is not a lot of homework and lab is fairly easy. The quizzes every recitation do not reflect general lectures but usually a random very specific part of it. If you are unlucky in group discussions, then you will get people who don't contribute. She doesn't explain things well and is incoherent. First exam had a perfect bell curve and no curve
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this professor made a 2 credit hour course seem like a 4-5 credit hour course. there were a lot of stupid petty 5 point quizzes that literally taught me nothing. the homeworks were few and far(ish) between but unhelpful.

Dr. Z is really knowledgeable about ecology and had lots of cool topics in lectures. However, this course is mandatory for all biology majors, so it might not be interesting to everyone. She is a really tough grader for exams which make up most of your grade. Study the thought questions and youll pass. More work than a normal 2 credit hour class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is extremely knowledgeable on ecology, with very interesting and lots of examples that make concepts more relatable and easier to visualize. Kind of a tough grader, so read carefully. Lots of premeds take this class and don't particularly care about ecology, so she gets a bad rap, but if you genuinely care about all of biology, she's great.
She makes a 2-credit course harder than a five-credit course. She does this with almost all of her classes, and yet she still has a job, even though this has been going on for well over a decade.

Dr. Zielinski's I think means well but mainly just reads off the powerpoint slides and doesn't do much else. The exam material is related to the lectures but its not as straight forward and you really have to take good notes and study to do well. Go to PSO they help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was horrible. Dr. Zielinski clearly knew what she was talking about, but the things she talked about would not even be on the exam. The exams were harder than they should have been because the topics discussed in class were easy. This class is also only 2 credits and homework was given out as if it was a 3-4 credit class.

Dr. Zielinski midterms/quiz are 50% SA and 50% multiple choice. Like other profs she post the previous year midterm as practice but get this she ONLY post the multiple choice answer key. You can see why this problematic based on the pervious reviews about her. My advice is to get a coursehero account while taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring yet she makes us show up to class every week by giving these petty 5 point in class quizzes every week. The workload she made for this class is for a 4 credit class while it being 2. Harshest grader ever, wants specific answers to vague question. With 5 course TA's, it took until the very last day to grade our assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is ridiculously hard and Zielenski is a terrible professor. The exams and homework are crazy specific, and you will miss a lot of points for leaving out a small detail. The depth at which she expects you to know for exams is absurd and the work load is too demanding for a 2 credit hour class. THIS CLASS IS HORRIBLE
Not a great professor. Not engaging, NOT clear about due dates. She assigns homework a few days before it's due, even during this pandemic. If you have the choice, take BIOL 286 ONLINE.

She goes into things a little too deep and expects you to know everything. Sorry professor, we have other classes too, specially ones that are over 2 credits. Harshest grader ever, will receive very little credit for explaining things for missing the smallest detail in a word question, even if you had 95% of the answer correct. Never Again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures were unclear. Sometimes cited incorrect information. Snarky and unapproachable. Unprofessional communication via email. I did all of the textbook reading and still did poorly on some exams. I got at A+ with friedman for 110 and a B+ in this class (I read, studied, did all HW, attended all labs /recitations). Would not recommend

She is a very intelligent and nice professor that clearly has enthusiasm for biology. She makes every student work for their grade, but her tests are fair. The subject matter is more difficult than BIOL 110, but is manageable. Overall she is a really fun professor to have!

I don;t care how nice she seems: this professor is hands-down the worst teacher I have had in Purdue's biology curriculum. The only way to get an A in this class is to memorize every tiny detail she brings up in lecture. This includes irrelevant personal anecdotes, Charles Darwin's birthday, and the names of her pets. I learned nothing of value.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is publicly insult students and whistle to students in class.

Prof. Zielinski is very caring for her students and is open to forming relationship with students to further their success out of her class. As for lectures they may seem jumbled, but go and fill out notes leaving room to go back and fill in when slides are posted. GO TO PSO! Study the practice tests and think of similar questions she may ask.

Prof. Zielinski is nice person but a horrid teacher. Lectures are all over the place and includes lots of content that is not relevant to the course. There were several lectures on why fake news is bad. There was even a homework that required us to look up articles on Breitbart News to debunk. You'll learn more ecology on the walk to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Zielinski's slides/lectures can sometimes be a bit all over the place. The exams have tricky multiple choice questions, so you have to really study your lecture notes. I found it helpful to go to her office hours and the PSO sessions. Lab is easy and often gets out early. Take advantage of the several extra credit opportunities she gives!

Dr. Zielinski is a little odd, but she really does care about her students and gives all the necessary information to succeed. The answers to all the questions on the exam are easily found on her slides, studying them thoroughly, paying attention in class, and asking questions will basically guarantee an easy A.

She is a very quick lexturer, talks quickly and in detail. If she gives an example in class, be prepared for a question about it on the exam. I cannot stress enough, DO THE THOUGHT QUESTIONS! That will help you a ton! If you have a question about grading, GO TO HER! She is more than willing to regrade anything and she's more generous than the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ecology and evolution is the worst class I have taken at Purdue so far. Lectures are required due to weekly assessments, but they are all over the place and not very helpful. Exams are extremely difficult and there is no clear grading criteria on what is required to earn a specific letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Zielinski obviously is enthusiastic and well educated, but something with her teaching style didnt work well with me. I found her lectures to be very disorganized and confusing. Her open ended test questions are graded quite harshly and inconsistently (TAs fault, not hers). She offers lots of EC though! Make sure to ALWAYS do her thought Qs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is completely passable. Most of her exams are word-for-word from her lectures. Know the basics of every lecture for exams. Her review sessions (PSOs) are SO HELPFUL. She reviews everything you need to know in ways that make it easy to understand (the weekly quizzes are tough). The lab portion for this class is a little bit of a joke
reviews.rating_tags: Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: She is an amazing teacher. It can be hard to understand the concepts she teaches sometimes but if you go to her after class, she can explain them to you in a much better way. She is very passionate about what she teaches and can be quite odd at times. As long as you go to the lectures, take good notes, and study, you should do alright in her class.

You can tell she knows what she's teaching about, but doesn't necessarily know how to translate it into easier concepts for students to grasp. I  believe she wants all students to succeed, but that doesn't translate to an easy class. Not the best at explaining herself. I respect her as a scholar but not a good professor because of the above reasons
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Denise is simply odd. Her lectures are strange and repeat in weird ways. When reading her exam questions, it feels like you have the translate the questions from her language. It feels as though you think you know what she is asking, but you're never quite sure. She whistles at her students or bangs her microphone to get our attention. Avoid her.

This was her first time teaching ecology and she turned an easy A class into the class that I put the most effort into.  There were weekly "assessments" one day per week so attendance was basically mandatory and she could not get control of her class. Also, she gives 100 short answer questions to know for the exams and chooses 10. GOOD LUCK.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Freaking terrible, try your 100% very best to avoid her. She's stupid and incompetent and lazy. She doesn't care about students and she doesn't even know what she's teaching.

I'm a hard worker, but I can tell you right now I worked harder for an A in this class than any other one, and still came up short. I did outside readings in the book, watched countless videos to try to understand concepts, and went to office hours. But she's just so unorganized and is not clear on the material. Do not recommend unless mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are unreasonably difficult. What she covers in lecture does not appear in many of the exam questions. She knows what she's talking when she's teaching the lecture, about but your grade will most definitely not reflect what you learned in the class.

The lectures were extremely hard to follow, but she writes on the board often (which can not be viewed in the recordings) so I would suggest going to class.  She was very helpful in PSO, and most things covered there were on quizzes and tests, so go to PSO.
Always willing to help after class.

While this is not a slack off class, she gives opportunity to ask questions. While her lectures are sometimes unorganized her help sessions (PSO)are GREAT, should just go every week, she does a very good job during them
Dr. Zielinki used very unorganized powerpoints. Her lectures were incredibly hard to follow. I wish I had used to AP credits and skipped this course.

The material isn't necessarily easy, but she makes a strong attempt to explain it well. The textbook is completely unnecessary though. She tries to help out her students by holding review sessions before each test, which are fair tests, although sometimes a little tricky.

Contrary to what alot of people had said... i am a speech language hearing sciences major and have no interest in bio but still did well in the class. You cannot slack off but if you do your work and study for the exams you will be fine. If you ask her a question, she appreciates your efforts and pretty much tells you the answer. Overall good prof!

HORRIBLE. do not take her class!! "easy class for non science majors" NO. her exams are sooo hard and impossible to pass. I attended every lecture and listented to every word she said but she made no sense. Worst prof at purdue.

Unreasonably difficult tests. Avoid taking a class from her at all costs. By no means an "easy A". Not helpful outside of class and doesn't care about giving someone a bad grade. How could she possibly still be teaching?!

Horrible professor. I was told this was supposed to be an easy class for non-biology majors. Boy was I wrong. Her exams were impossible to get a good grade on. Overall she is an annoying lecturer, and I'm glad I never have to take another course with her.

Her exams are absolutely insane. Prior to the first exam, you will be thinking, wow this is a really great professor, she explains things clearly, easy A!Then about 10 minutes into the first exam you will realize how very wrong you were. Although her lectures are very good, very clear, her tests are impossible. Also, she coughs into the mic a lot.
Made exams ridiculously hard and actually told me not to use the $200 dollar book to study with. Useless in help sessions and terrible lecturer.
Pretty lame. Poor teacher.
tests are impossible.

This professor is horrible. One of the worst I ever had. She is extremely unorganized. I dont doubt that she knows her stuff, but she for some reason is simply unable to present it in a coherent manner. Tests are unreasonably difficult as well.

Very boring, disorganized teacher.  Tests are hard because she does not teach well.  It is hard to follow what she is looking for. Her lectures have no order and are boring. Her TA's grade the labs and some grade easliy, while one in particular is very demanding and picky about little details
No Comments
She's a nice professor, and the material is pretty straightforward...but she goes through her slides really fast, so you have to really pay attention during the lecture.

Best professor on campus if you want to take a philosophy course. Let's you have an additional 5% if you miss less than 7 classes which was nice. Super lenient with grading the written essays and exams. He gives you a list of questions that could come for the exam and only picks questions from there which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Easily one of my favorite professors at Purdue! Very engaging lectures, clearly passionate about the subject, encourages class discussions, and very responsive. Class is well organized, reading quizzes are easy, 3 blue book exams are simple, 3 writing assignments are generously graded. Great class, even better prof. DMFK all the way!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Does not allow DRC for some papers

Professor Kelly was my favorite professor throughout my time at Purdue. I really enjoyed the structure of the class. The discussions were easy to get into, the topics were interesting, the workload was not overwhelming. I ended up looking forward to this class because of how well he ran it and how stress-free it felt.

Dr. Kelly is everything that is right with the Purdue philosophy department. He is a very personable, caring professor. His lectures are interesting and easy to follow. He gives you the exact same questions that'll be on the exams ahead of time. Easiest A of my life. Thank you Dr. Kelly, you are truly awesome!

This class was easy, and Dr. Kelly was passionate about what he teaches. However, I do not find his behavior toward students very respectable. You have to tell him when you have to leave early for another class or he will call you out in front of everyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Absolutely an easy A for those who don't care about the subject, with just 1 exam that you get to prep for, and 2 easy to understand assignment types alternating weeks.
Easy A or not, his lecture style was refreshingly grounded for a philosophy class, and his propensity for movies and tacos was something I always looked forward to listening to.
One of the best Professor at Purdue in my opinion. Would definitely take his class again.

Prof Kelley had some interesting lectures, but a majority of them were very boring, however the class had very few assignments and they were all very easy. When I would ask him questions, he would never get back with me, which was kinda annoying.

Super easy class. Very boring lectures. I pay minimal attention in lectures and study for about two hours before the exams and got A's. Nice guy, but I personally cannot listen to him for more than 15 minutes but I'm not a big philosophy buff. Nonetheless, I recommend.
Awesome professor, really tries to question your thinking. 100% recommend taking this class!!
great professor!
Just a great guy, and a great prof.
Explains the material and concepts very well. Gives relatable examples and makes sure most students understand. Very humorous and nice.

I took PHIL 110 with him, and boy did he make the lectures amazing. He's one of the best professors I've had who not only knows his stuff quite well, but makes the content so interesting with his explanations and commentary that a class with him would probably be the best one you've taken. He also cares a lot about students which always helps.

He was a great instructor who made lectures interesting and worth going to. Almost everything you were tested on/graded on came from lectures so it's important to go to class however missing 3-5 classes won't affect your grade drastically. All lectures are posted online as well if you do miss them.

He's a really smart and interesting guy. There are 3 or 4 papers each semester and 2 essay style exams. He presents the material in a clear and enjoyable way. All of the tests are based on his lectures and he doesn't post the slides online, so you must attend class. The material was interesting, but the course did tend to drag on towards the end.

Super easy class if you choose to have graded participation: basically, miss less than 7 classes by the end of the semester, and receive additional 5% to final grade. Also, posts all lecture notes online, which literally covers EVERYTHING you could possibly need for papers and tests. Easy A for a PHIL class

Prof Kelly is really one of those few professors that are able to grab your attention and keep it for the entire lecture. His grading is based solely on papers and exams, which can be difficult. He does his best to make the class interesting, and I will definitely now be pursuing a minor in philosophy thanks to this guy!

Professor Kelly was a great professor. He made lectures funny and engaging. I took off points for easiness simply because my teaching assistant was not the strongest. Overall, Professor Kelly is very enjoyable making Philosophy a little less confusing and a lot more interesting.
D. Kelly is the bset!

I really enjoyed this class. The lectures are interesting and I learned a lot. He explains the material clearly and will answer any of your questions. Exams are short essays that are over the material he lectures about in class and will give you study questions. I would definitely recommend this class to any student at Purdue.

Professor Kelly is absolutely fantastic - one of the best professors I've had at Purdue. I know the material is introductory, and I may just be interested in it, but Kelly presents content in a funny, intelligible way, and he certainly knows his material. Tests are exactly off the notes from class as essays and are fair.
Knows his stuff. Very patient and thoughtful when answering questions.

Awesome guy, he made this class great. Very knowledgable, I highly recommend. He even helped me out at the end of the year when I asked him to bump up my grade because I recognized a dumb mistake as I walked out of the final!

He's probably one of the most knowledgeable man I've ever met in my life. He really knows his stuff. He challenges you to think. It's a great intro class only if you're up for the challenge. The exams are essays, not multiple choice including the final. You also get the feeling you'd want to have coffee with Professor Kelly once in a while.
Johnstone was a good lecturer and the course coordinator decides how hard the class is not him so that doesn't matter. Funny guy too

Tries to be engaging but most of multivariable calc can be self-taught with chenflix/yt videos. Lectures were boring and most of the grade depended on the exams too which was annoying. Take it somewhere else because calc 3 is brutal at Purdue.

His teaching style is not the most exciting, but he the important bits across. If available, you should take Mummert instead, because he coordinates tests and therefore provides more up-to-date information. As a side note, Johnstone chews and drinks (dr. pepper and mountain dew) loudly in the microphone, which is a less than pleasant experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnstone was an incredible lecturer and makes abstract concepts understandable. The homeworks were long but the exams were forgiving. Make sure to read if you miss a lecture since the content builds on itself a lot. Quizzes could be resubmitted at any point for full credit, with VERY detailed feedback and hints. Overall a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: i recommend going to lectures for this prof. it's not mandatory but he is very good at explaining material that i found almost impossible to understand in the textbook. keeps lecture engaging as well

He is a very good teacher, explains everything very well and is very funny. However the class overall is very difficult despite this. The TA you get for your recitations also plays a major role in your final grade. Overall however, Johnstone is a very good teacher and I highly recommend getting him as your professor for this class
Dude this is genuinely so funny and makes concepts much easier to understand. I attended all the lecturers.

I got a B because I stopped going to lecture, but he is genuinely a great professor and I like how he spends 1/4 of the lecture going over previous material to help cement concepts into our understanding. He is also very open to questions during lecture. I've never been to his office hours but he seems very caring and inviting.

I didn't have many issues with him, he is open to criticism if he makes a mistake during a lecture and cares about his students. 

The difficultly comes from the exams and the quizzes. ChenFlix, Khan Academy, Professor Leonard (YT), and Paulsonlinemathnotes, were helpful in understanding the material. Hope you have a good TA and a big curve.
Pros - Good lectures, funny, accessible;     Cons - Canadian

He teaches well enough that I did not have to review on Chenflix. I'm glad there are good lecture videos and no attendance is required. I don't think a "difficulty rating" is relevant for this professor because it's mostly the exams and TA graded quizzes which are the main difficulty points. Note that the homework takes a nonzero amount of time.

Great professor, lots of content is covered in the course but he made it not as overwhelming as I've heard others do. Has helpful office hours and 2-4 hour reviews before each exam that are very beneficial. Overall good guy and would highly recommend.

Professor Johnstone is great. He's very approachable and seems to genuinely care about the wellbeing of his students. Occasionally he runs out of time during lectures, but his review of the previous lecture's material and examples can really help you understand the course material.

Johnstone is a very funny and honest professor. He's friendly during office hours and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Sometimes he spends too much time on iClicker examples at the beginning of lectures, which causes the last 5 minutes to be rushed, but the examples are very helpful and he explains them well. Overall, great guy
Very great teacher, always happy to speak to students and tries explaining math to the best he can.

Very honest and down to earth professor, honestly shares his knowledge about how the exams will be scored and what kind of questions he recommends to practice.  Always shows up for class on time and holds himself to high standards during lectures.

Johnstone is great. Lectures are super engaging. MA261 is very tough, so get ready for a LOT of out-of-class studying/prep. TBH, your grade in 261 heavily depends on your TA and exams. Johnstone is funny and simplifies concepts really well. His office hour sessions are also great. Take advantage of them! HW is heavy (2x/week) but doable. Good luck!

Overall good prof. Enjoyed the lectures. Sometimes a little bit of time was wasted with iClicker Q's, but he always explained the solution. Definitely cares about his students and is very accessible during office hours. Course was difficult, especially having a year gap between AP Calc BC and this course. Just make sure you study for exams.

I have never loved a professor more. He truly cares about his students and is always helpful outside class. He always explains things clearly and keeps class engaging. Quizzes can be resubmitted for full credit, which really helps with learning. Homework can be tricky, but the tests are more straightforward. Easily my favorite class this semester.

Prof. Johnstone is an incredible professor and genuinely made my life exponentially better. He is very sweet and supportive towards your academics and will go out of his way to answer questions. He is difficult to understand sometimes, however truly wants all of his students to do well in class.

I took this class a few years ago and I still remember him as being a great professor. He had just started teaching and had his moments where he was figuring things out, and I imagine that he is an even better lecturer now after several semesters. I found him entertaining and engaging as a lecturer, especially if you were more inclined to theory.
explained everything every well

(MA 341) Absolutely amazing professor, probably the best I've had in the 4 years of Purdue. He gives clear examples and justifies his proofs very diligently. He gives great feedback on quizzes and lets you resubmit them for full points. He gives advice on thinking and learning as well. Overall goated professor.

(For MA 341)
He was honestly the most amazing professor I have had! He is of course super knowledgeable about the topics, but more importantly he often teaches them with images which is especially helpful in a class like Analysis where intuition is key. His grading is also super lenient; he has "take home" quizzes with re-submits due months after.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great professor overall. I personally like how he arranged his notes and examples. They were easy to follow with and understand. He does make mistakes during examples sometimes but he normally fixes them quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes I had to refer to Chenflix notes as I felt that Pr. Johnstone did not cover everything in class. I also did not enjoy his habit of snacking during the lectures. He is good at explaining tho, and seems really excited when it comes to math
Very caring professor who is willing to answer any of your questions. He is also good at putting concepts into simple terms that make it easy to understand. His office hours are also very accessible.

I ended up switching professors and ended up with Johnstone. As someone who learns with examples, I love all the examples Johnstone does. He is ready to answer any question and will explain it as much as he can (until he starts to hit linear alg and then he says 'just because'). Overall great lecturer for calc 3.

I thought Dr. Johnstone was a nice person but when I took his class it was hard to understand what he was saying, as he was often contradicting himself and going off on side tangents. In my opinion, the way he explained topics made no sense, so I instead resorted to watching the Chenflix for each of his lectures. Definitely not the worst though.

Pretty great professor. He does waste a little bit of time with iClicker questions, which leads to him being able to cover fewer examples in class, but overall he gets through all the material in the lecture and explains it pretty well.

He is very accessible outside of class. Has lots of office hours and responds to questions by email as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best math teachers I've had in years. He's accessible in his office hours and really seems to care that people understand the content. He's definitely knowledgeable on the subject he teaches but he's also very good at explaining it in ways that make intuitive sense. He does snack a little bit but that never bothered me.

For a first time professor Johnstone is pretty good. You definitely want to go to his office hours if you are confused though. He will spend as much time as possible making sure you *get it*. You can tell he really loves Math.

If you want to understand Calc and do well, take it with Johnstone. If you just want to pass you could use Chenflix.

In MA 16100 not MA 26100

Very smart prof who has a few flaws. Classes can be very theoretical with not enough practical examples. Consistently snacks and drinks sodas during class which can be very annoying to listen to (especially when watching lectures back in Kaltura). Liked that he always made sure to answer any questions that come up in class

Great professor, although his lectures can be boring sometimes his notes are very accessible and his teaching style is notably good among professors. He makes sure you are well prepared for midterms and finals with the abundance of resources.
Bro is goated
Great lecturer, no issues with him at all. Will answer any question to the best of his ability. Loves coca cola, has his moments during lecture. Try to not be his first class.

Take this with a grain of salt, as I didn't attend many lectures. Like most others, I watched Chenflix. Prof. Johnstone was new to Purdue/new to teaching entirely for my semester. He went off on a lot of tangents and wasn't always great at explaining things. However, he does care about his students and would communicate well to the class

I took his Calc 3 class during the Fall of 2023. He was knowledgeable on the subject, and I felt well prepared for the exams which is great since the grade was based mostly on the exams. He made the class mostly interesting, and his examples were more or less easy to follow. He was also easy to get into contact with whenever I had questions.

Professor Johnstone is truly one of the premier math teachers of our day. The lectures were very enjoyable as he made calc 3 a very awesome subject. I'd recommend going to the lectures, and listen to what he teaches. Pretty great teacher in general, and he has pretty enjoyable lectures. 5 stars, and Johnstone deserves an award.

Take these points lightly as I did not attend most of his lectures (Chenflix user). He seemed inexperienced w/ his pace & explanations in lectures. He is caring, sending emails to clarify parts of his lecture that he believed he did not teach well. I can see him improving, but if you are a Chenflix user/have other options, stick to those for now.

Very receptive to questions from students and cares a lot about ensuring that you understand everything going on. He's very accessible during office hours and is willing to spend a very long time helping you grasp something you struggle with. Good lectures and depth of content for the course.

Is a lighthearted guy and occasionally makes jokes. Wouldn't recommend. 
Was too theoretical in many of this explanations and rarely works examples out fully.
Initially assumed that students were familiar about vector operations and planes which most were not. Handwriting is hard to read.
 -- Seems willing to improve and may change though

Very funny guy, did a great job for it being his first ever time being a professor, will only continue to get better from here and compared to the other 261 lecturers he is definitely better than average.
He's alright. Lectures get boring and he goes on unrelated tangents (hehe). May not cover the material in time. Go for a different professor, if possible.

Professor Johnstone is knowledgeable. However, he is very inexperienced and has poor organization in his lecture. He is also poor at explaining, despite knowing the concepts extensively. He has bad habits during class such as eating while lecturing, cursing, and drinking too much caffeine.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took him for Calc 3 during Fall of '23, and was the best lecturer which was a low bar to clear. He spends a lot of time reviewing content at the beginning and going over the conceptual ideas for lecture, so there is little time for examples. He's worth it if you pay attention and is very friendly when helping. Also he drinks a lot of soda.

He is VERY receptive to questions and does a very good job explaining things in multiple ways. 

The class is set up a bit wonky, he spends the first 15 minutes of class reviewing the class before so you have less time for new content, but the new content is caught up on in the next class.
i had johnstone for calc 3 and he was really funny ngl. he was also good at teaching the material and is very accessible outside of class. i would recommend him if prof chen isnt teaching.

This class is poorly constructed. We use several platforms without notifications or warnings of when assignments are due. Assignments over breaks, will not teach anything relevant, frustrated at how clearly he just fills lecture time because its his job, but requires attendance. Assignments are a contradictory, painful waste of time. Seems nice.

This has been life changing. Truly. Nothing compares to the being of pure sunlight that is Eric Norbert Waltenburg. He approaches every day with nothing but joy. My GPA has never been higher. My brain is so engorged with wisdom. I'm going to name all 9 of my children after him. Thank you, universe for giving us the lovely Eric Norbert Waltenburg.

I took the research intensive version of POL300. He is the most wonderful professor and a great person. He would go off on tangents occasionally, but he truly cares and wants everyone to get an A. World, please be kind to him.

Professor Waltenburg is a very genuine person. He is very passionate about what he is teaching and enjoys lecturing and having students understand. He also loves it when people participate but never forces them to. His lectures are very interesting but do not assist very much with the assignments. The assignments can be long but grades lenient
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Waltenburg is one of the nicest professors I have had so far. He is also extremely funny and caring, making the class feel like a community. The content can be difficult, but he is a very easy grader and is chill on late work. Only be scared if Ohio State loses a game.

Good prof. I was a senior in this class and the final paper had me lost so I just went to office hours and he said I could just submit whatever and it wouldn't matter since I went to every class. Go to lecture and you'll pass with flying colors as long as u submit everything
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty useless considering you have to do 2 stata exercises a week and he barley provides relevant examples. Assigns python assignments that are so complex when looking at the course objectives. Honestly the worst class I took at Purdue I hated it. He's not a good communicator and the TAs grade things 2 months late. Such a joke

This class is a joke. Directions are never clear, due dates are always changing, and nothing relevant to assignments is gone over in lecture. By far the most disorganized class I have taken at purdue (As a senior about to graduate).

He is OK. Super genuine and interested in politcal analysis but this class is a headache. So many assignments and he barley goes over any of them in lecture. Assigns python and stata assignments for programming use in political analysis and they are not even touched in lecture which is frusturating. This class is just a bunch of busy work.

Took POL 460 but can't select that. Great lectures with lots of information and interesting content. Very engaging and willing to answer questions and change plans. The paper is a big part of the class but the topic is his own research. I enjoyed the class. He is very knowledgeable and will be a great teacher if you are interested in the topic.
A fair grader and responsive, but lectures are overly complicated and needlessly technical. A great person, but lacking as an efficient teacher (his research is awesome though look into it)

Stats heavy course but I took AP stats and it's even easier than that because you just use Stata for hypothesis testing. Lectures're boring but he tries to make them funny and engaging. Emphasis on tries. Other hw is easy to complete. Don't expect to actually learn Python from this course; it's too watered down. Very forgiving prof. Midterm easy.

Took this class pre-COVID. If you've taken a statistics course, you've basically already taken the class. At times, Waltenburg seemed quite disinterested and is not the best explainer in the world, but many of the concepts are self-explanatory even if you haven't taken a stats course. The online "project" was a point of confusion for many.

I really enjoyed POL300 with Waltenburg. He makes the class really easy to be successful in. There is an adequate amount of help offered throughout the semester and most of the time a good portion of the homework assignments would be explained in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class isnt as bad as some people make it out to be. I went to class 75% of the time and got an A-. Go to class and he explains everything you need to know, Python and Stata is covered completely, so the assignments are a breeze. Highly recommend Professor Waltenburg. Hes a great guy in and out of the classroom.

The material is super boring, but he tries to lighten the mood with jokes. Learned a lot of useful things like Python and Stata, but I wouldn't recommend the class unless it was required for your major.

This class requires two textbooks and has weekly reading quizzes to go along with the book. This class is not math heavy, but does focus on analyzing statistics. There was also a period in which we learned to code in Python. Waltenburg tries to make jokes in the lectures, which I thought was nice since the class can be a bit tedious.

Don't let the class's title fool you: this is a statistics class. Waltenburg struggles to understand the material and often teaches students faulty information. As someone who took AP Statistics in high school, this class wasn't too difficult, but the professor made it the most challenging class I have ever taken. Missing class was more beneficial.
Funny guy at times, difficult materials, makes you really work for a good grade

Class is incredibly boring. However, Professor Waltenburg tries really hard to make lectures bearable and almost succeeds. Is also incredibly helpful if you have questions outside of class. The class itself is extremely mind numbing.
A funny, sarcastic guy who teaches a really boring subject.  The final exam was pretty tough and the TA's are mean and unhelpful. I wouldn't take this class unless it was a requirement.

I had him in the Spring of 1997.  He was teaching about the Courts.  Mr. Waltenburg is not even a lawyer and he is teaching this class.  He called me a "silly fool" for giving an opinion in class.  Thank God I dropped the class immediately.  Today I am an attorney in the Chicago area.  I was about to go to Dean Caputo; I did not.

This man gave me the lowest GPA I have had here at Purdue.  Many have taken him for POL300, I took him for an internship.  I had to submit one, and only one paper for 6 credits.  I went into his office to discuss the paper, in which he said was good.  I asked if it was A material.  He said yes.  He gave me a B.  He is a liar and an idiot.
The Prof. loved to ramble as if he were speaking with himself in at a desk in a dark room.
Great teacher. Makes a boring class interesting. He has a rep for being tough but he is actually very fair. Anyone who has a problem with him just doesn't want to do any work. Funny guy at times.
Tough class, but notes are easy to take. good notes=good grade.  DO NOT PUT OFF THE PAPER, you will be sorry if you do.

Very difficult. He made a crappy class we have to take even worse by making it impossibly difficult. The final exam was multiple choice, but graded so correct = +1, not answered = 0, and incorrect = -0.2. WTF, it's not the SATS. The labs made little sense.
Good guy. Just a little over my head.
He's ok, and the class fulfills a requirement.  But, its hard and time-consuming.  Don't recommend.
He's a good teacher but when he tells you not to put off the paper untill the last few weeks for the love of god listen.
Nice guy.  Extremely sarcastic, if you make dumb comments, sleep, etc. prepared to be picked on! Really boring stat class, at least made somewhat amusing by the prof.

He's a huge Buckeyes fan.  We usually spend the first ten minutes of each Monday talking about what happened to Ohio State's football team over the weekend.  If they lose, be prepared for a pop quiz.  Other than that, lectures are really easy to follow.

Super knowledgable! Gets through lectures quickly and cancels class a lot. Does a good job warning you about the tough parts of the exam. He is also very laid back with logistical stuff; and this class is not bad if you took AP stats. They made it less work compared to previous years. I think his rate my professor is super harsh.
Professor was good. Grading on exams were fair, but lecture slides were a bit so,so and unclear. The textbook was better at explaining and problems on exams were easier than homework.

I feel the other reviews here are harsh; he did his best with the course material that he had to teach. He's a very caring and approachable professor. It's not his fault that STAT350 is designed very poorly.

professor was difficult to understand but the slides were somewhat useful. i felt he was good at answering questions. the course has a lot of overly difficult homework that wasn't very related to exams. exams were easier than homework.
The worst professor at Purdue

He used another lecturer's slides and recordings for "quality-control purposes", but I believe he should have given lectures himself. For exams, we were told to type our work and answers into lockdown browser, but we were told that we could upload pictures after I had already submitted. There was a discussion forum that he almost never answered.

Pros
- Insane curve, you won't fail this class
- Book is easy to read
Cons
- Required purchase of online homework service
- Horrible test logistics (typing your math into a non-LateX text window)
- Took someone else's notes and lectures (which were completely not worth watching)
- Doesn't reply to discussion forms

imo the class itself was kinda strange with all the R assignments. tests were graded very nicely (extremely generous with points), but lectures were honestly a waste of time to attend. i don't like the tophat assignments that were due weekly as the content he taught generally deviated/was more specific so that entire platform was a waste.
Why I'm still alive?

prob worst teacher ive had here. hes rly sweet so i hate saying that but i had to teach myself every single concept on my own. he reads off slides and doesnt do example problems at all. coding homework and 3 other homeworks /week that are irrelevant to the exam topics. dont go to class. its a waste of time. pretty close to hs AP stats but worse

He was a very nice and passionate teacher. The lectures involved him mostly reading off of slides without many example problems, so you would have to learn on your own too. He's always open to help if you reach out to him though.

Does not teach, just reads out complicated math out of slides. You will have to learn to code in R by yourself, and its HARD. Additionally, no curve at all and exams are tough (cheat sheet allowed tho). Don't recmend.

He worked under a course coordinator, so a lot of criticism cannot be attributed to him. He had a lot of material to cover each class. Lectures were very boring, but he is an incredibly kind and helpful man who you can access outside of class if you need. Class itself is doable if you do the assignments and study.

Professor Matangi is incredibly kind and understanding. The workload in this class is very manageable as long as you keep up with the lectures and stay organized. One of the great aspects of his class is the practice exams he provides before each test (very similar structure to actual exam). Highly recommend!

I would argue that Dr. Matangi did the best he could under the conditions of the course. There is a lot of content, the course powerpoints are confusing, and there's little to no overlap between hw, computer assignments, and exams. The content isn't too difficult to teach to yourself and he was extremely helpful and kind outside of class.

Probably the worst professor I have had. It is amazing how someone is able to make a class so disengaging. It wasn't even worth it to show up as I learned much more on my own than I did ever coming to class. He just reads off PowerPoints, often skipping over steps when it comes to giving examples. His tests are also so poorly structured. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Matangi seems to genuinely care for his students and is a nice guy. However, this instruction for STAT 511 was quite terrible. He would just read from a PowerPoint and not show any process. I stopped watching lectures after the first week and learned on my own after seeing the lack of effort given on his part. Exams were fair.

He made this class way harder than it needed to be because he doesn't know how to write exams. He expected you to show your work, but the exams were online with only a text entry box. So you had to type everything out while trying to also solve the problems. It took forever and made them way harder. He doesn't know how to run a class like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He just read out the PowerPoint from 2001, and his course design is awful. Maybe he's good at statistics but he knows nothing about teaching.

I have done awful with math classes at Purdue but I consider STAT 511 relatively easy compared to other math classes. It was not easier because this prof was good. He did not go through a single practice problem step by step which is obviously important. He just reads off a powerpoint. I am astounded how he never could understand student questions.
He is not a good teacher.

Martinez is undoubtedly the worst CHE professor at Purdue. He messed up every student's final grade, and we cannot get them fixed until the end of next semester, so our GPAs are lower because of his mistake. His lectures are incoherent and he makes constant mistakes. No one learned a single thing from his lectures. Avoid him at all costs.

This course was a disorganized mess. The lecture schedule was largely ignored. Error-ridden announcements were frequently sent out causing mass confusion. Grading standards were unclear and inconsistent between TAs. Released laughably incorrect final grades for half of the class and missed the final grade submission deadline for the second half.

Martinez shouldn't be teaching. Lectures were hard to follow and constantly filled with wrong information. Homework was a huge time sink, mostly due to poor explanation of topics or topics not being covered altogether. Grading errors between TAs were known and ignored. Failed to input accurate final grades for the majority of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were a mess and exam contained content not covered in class. Unclear grading standards and homework was long due to lack of instruction. Bro should retire asap. Also entered grades horribly wrong when they were due.

Martinez needs to retire ASAP. His lectures were unintelligible and on multiple occasions he taught office hours in Spanish. His grading was all over the place. He had TAs grade a certain number of whole exams with subjective grading rubrics. There were grade discrepancies that he knew about and disregarded. This class was a headache bc of him.
senile and dont recommend

Simply put Martinez is too old to still be teaching. His lectures absolutely blew no matter when in the semester it was. Third exam was impossible, don't know anyone who scored above a 70. Gave us a week and a half to do a project that we were supposed to have available for at least 4 weeks. Do not take a class with him if you want happiness.

(CHE 435) Came to senior engineering lab 30 minutes late every session (even though students are expected to arrive on time). Does not explain assigned projects at all and expects students to be able to conduct an entire 9 week experiment on their own. Released scores for all reports on the final lab session. Solid human but needs to retire ASAP

He's kind and helpful if you go to his office hours but his lectures aren't reliable. He'll write formulas wrong (wrote a formula wrong on exam review day) and doesn't always give you the information you need to do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice guy
His lectures are clear and he's really generous when giving us 50 points for the extra credit option

I think Martinez is getting a little old to be teaching. His lectures are absolutely awful, he basically just reads the material from a powerpoint, and the textbook he uses isn't much help either. Multiple times he assigned homework problems over material that hadn't been covered, and his exams are over concepts that haven't been in the homework.

Lectures are honestly not the best, but he pulls all of his material from the book so it doesn't really matter. Posts all of his lectures online so it is an extra resource outside of the book. Very application based professor, rather than theoretical. Extremely caring and sweet professor. I would definitely take a class with him again.

I'm not sure if Martinez's teaching has gotten worse from the previous reviews but this guy absolutely blows. He has given us 9 wrong equations in lecture (yes I'm counting) which causes frustration on the homework. He seems to love the material but is the worst professor I've had at Purdue. Simply put he is a horrible lecturer.

Tells lots of stories in class and isn't focused on material. Is VERY KNOWLEDGEABLE of the material, but not the best at teaching it to a group. GO TO HIM if you have questions about the material, a really nice guy. Tests are NOT NUMERICAL, you must write out a PROCEDURE for solving the question.
Great guy.
Good humble guy. Always there to help, grading is easy. Would definetly take his class.

Professor Smith is a nice person, but she is incredibly unfit for teaching. This semester's 272 course has been incredibly disorganized and inconsistent. The structure of lecture/attendance was changed midway without formal warning. Exam 2 was abysmally formatted, with many of the multiple choice options having the same answer. Take online if able.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrid. Had her for both 255 and 272. If you miss class and an ICE assignment, that's 1% of your total grade gone (ICE accounts for 20% of your final grade). Insanely rude and inconsiderate, never helps, and constantly assumes the worst in you. Exams 1&2 are impossible. The labs are free tho.
whoever gave a 5 has been paid
didn't learn anything and just waste of time

Said in class that quizzes are made with GenAI. Had am impossible requirement on the final (Lockdown browser and another tab open). There were 2 assignments per class period, plus 3 for every lab period. We weren't taught to code, just to copy examples.
not a great professor but easy class, exams 1 and 2 were hard but generous curve, exam 3 and final are free A's and she gives extra credit, good TAs and easy labs.

Make sure you come to class every single time because she hands out assignments that are due at the end of the class and you're grade will be deducted 30%. Labs are easy. Exams not even what she covered lol, her lectures are disorganized and expects everyone to know everything. you'll be succeeding in class then f up on exams and you get B.

Overall, Smith's 272 class wasn't too bad. She's a nice person but her lectures are a little disorganized combined with all the ICE's and practice's. As long as you study the slides and do a little bit of outside studying, you will do well in her class. Labs were not too difficult, and the group project was pretty easy as well.
much better at teaching 272. lectures were easy to understand and content wasnt that hard if you show up. attendance is absolutely mandatory if you dont wanna lose 30% of your grade.

not really fit to be teaching 2 important courses all CIT majors have to take. if your class average on midterms is usually in the 30s and 50s, i think that shows genuine cause for concern. only highlight is that TAs were good for labs and some extra credit.
Horrible at teaching, difficult to understand, makes students hand-write code

Prof smith was not that bad guys, some of these reviews are very dramatic. I had both 255 and 272 this semester and they were two of my best classes. Yes, the exams are hard in 255, but they were also curved. 272 tests were almost harder than the 255 tests. She isn't that great of a lecturer tho and the 255 7:30 class kinda sucked.
She is not great professor. But she teaches 272 better than 255. Her labs are not bad. 272 exams are not bad too.

She is really sweet person, but her lectures are hard to keep up. The wording on the exams are just really make you confused. Especially 255 exams are hard. I would recommend taking during summer time.

Smith is a nice lady but lowkey she does not know how to teach. I would go to her lectures and learn nothing, you have to teach yourself. Class is definitely disorganized, you have to know some Java before going into it. Overall class wasn't too bad, lab, in class assignments, quiz on the reading, and lecture reflections. 7:30 lecture sucked tho.
you guaranteed will fail the exams lol
I never felt the urge to either drop the school or drop the major this bad
why just WHY

reviews.comment: Smith as a professor is a nice person. If you can't make class for a valid reason she's pretty understanding. That being said the lecture's weren't done well. If you review the slides and use online materials you can still do well in the class. If you know APCSA shouldn't be too bad. Class assignments and lectures were trash.

Professor Smith is nice, but clearly not fit for teaching. My favorite professor by far my 3 years here at Purdue. Very approachable and honest with students, easy to learn from, and always makes the class laugh.

this woman doesn't know organic chemistry and also doesn't know how to teach and also looks like a couch cover at times!
