Very helpful and open to student's suggestions . Really wants the student to understand the materials. Very great class! I learnt a lot from it!

Pros: He really wants you to know the material, he did optional review sessions every sunday and is very easy to receive help. he's a good guy that cares about this students  Cons: Sometimes doesnt fully understand the problem he is trying to demonstrate. Handwritingdiagrams were hard to follow.  overall, not a bad for a new professor.
Honestly, a real cool guy. Went to his office hours and he really cares about his students.

The only grades are the short-answer tests done every 2 weeks, but they have a generous curve and are not super difficult if you show up to lecture and pay attention. Ford has a lot of knowledge on the material and is willing to answer any questions asked. Tests have questions that are sometimes very niche, despite the material being super general.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice person and all, but lecture slides provide 0 information about the course content. No recorded lectures. Talks super fast making it hard to take notes on everything. Grade is entirely on exams but with an extremely heavy curve. A 7:30 section didn't help. Overall if the course was better organized, this would've been a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Little tough but overall good expierence

Best history Professor I ever had. I honestly love his class. Pretty heavy tests though but he does put a 32% curve on them so it's worth it. Go to the review sessions because that can make a big change for your grade. BTW his initials are O.T.

He helps with the history club and puts on a lot of fun events for the club.

Probably my facorite proffessor ever. He's easy to understand and his HIS 123 is a blast. He's extremely kind to everyone and is an amazing person. Grades fairly and actually helps you learn. I genuinely enjoy his classes and hope to have more of him.
not at all good, route learning
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures were a nightmare

Overall the professor is good, but you cannot miss any lectures. The slides are messy and do not contain any helpful information. You will be quizzed on the information he mentions super quickly only once. The quizzes are super random. It doesn't seem that he has any structure during his lectures. Discussed politics for the whole class once.

The course is hard because there is so much content (Survey of global history) and his slides could be better, but he is a good professor; very knowledgeable, enjoyable to listen to, and wants you to succeed.  Go to the review sessions and study before the tests.

Hard to take notes from as his powerpoints tend to not have any bullets or notes on it and lectures are not recorded online so it's an inconvenience if you miss class, especially considering that all the tests are based solely on the smallest things he says in the lecture. However, there's a heavy curve making it easier to get a good grade.

The tests are like trivia games that pick random small things he said from lectures that you probably missed or couldn't write down because he was rambling so fast. Messy lectures. No study guide. However, the test is curved very heavily. Not too hard to get a decent grade but incredibly stressful as every test is a big guessing game.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course is graded on tests which cover lecture material, which is purely verbal with no slideshows, no transcripts. Hard to hear at points, talks fast. The lectures content is hard to follow and jumps frequently. Incorrectly presented some history (Opium Wars). The tests were strange in topics picked, trivia like. Professor quite rude at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He speaks very fast in class and the lectures are not recorded. If you miss anything he says, you are done for because he doesnt upload any notes or lecture content. If you want to get good grades, you will have to type like a maniac and listen to each and every word he says. The saving grace is that all tests are curved well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are just him rambling with no clear emphasis on what is important. Slides show no information outside of pronunciations and maps. He also provides no study material, so it is impossible to predict what material will be tested.

Hes a pretty chil guy, but crams a lot of info in each lecture. attendance is not mandatory, but you're cooked if you dont pay attention to every second. every test and exam is curved, which is amazing.

This class has a bad rep, mostly because it was a new class with a lot of moving parts. Now, it seems to be smoother and more polished, and I have hardly run into any issues. If you want to be a mechanical engineer and get into CAD, this class is a necessity and will provide you with the skills needed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The content isn't too bad but the class is very, very tedious. He assigns a lot of busy work, making a 2 credit hour class feel like 4.
Makes you buy his textbook, which he wrote. Got most assignments wrong and had to change them 1-2 days before the due date

Lectures were interesting and the new Teamcenter site was good to learn. Going to office hours and making sure to follow the rubric really helped me do well. Most important thing is getting on top of assignments and not being against asking for help, as the software can mess up at times.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer, TAs carry the course. He gives extra credit assignments but downcurves at the end of the year based on distribution. So even if you get an A according to the syllabus you could end up with a B. Those extra credit assignments are really just normal assignments. He's the worst and is not transparent about it.

Honestly one of my favorite classes so far. The lectures gave a solid look at how engineering design works in industry, and the labs made the CAD and PDM stuff click. Fuerst is super approachable and helpful with both class questions and career advice. Not sure why people hate on it.

0 lenience & mercy, doesn't care about his students.Not structured to be a 2-credit course,rather heavier than 4-credit.Didn't give extension for a legit technical fault,& asked me to drop the entire course for the 2nd time.I have no motivation to take it for the 3rd time now. He's doing whatever he wants as he's the only professor for this course.

Initially, I was unsure about Fuerst considering the less-than-stellar reviews, but he seemed completely fine. The course itself is super easy if you have any previous CAD experience although there is a lot of homework. Other than the cost of the textbook, I have no complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class isn't hard as long as you do all the work and get every extra credit. By the “final” practical exam, I had so many points I could have skipped and still gotten an A-. Take every assignment seriously and don't be afraid of going to office hours (the lab office hours run by TAs) and and the class will be way easier than you think.
Useful lectures and homework. The content in mfet163 helped me achieve proficiency with CAD and plm in a few months.

I took MFET 10301.

Mandatory $200 textbook, extremely buggy software that barely worked on the school computers, useless information about PDM, and average CAD training made this class really more difficult than it should have been.

If you can avoid taking this class, do so. The TA's made it tolerable and they did the best they could.
85% of the class gets an A so even though its a lot of work can't complain, 200$ textbook is a bit annoying but apart from that pretty chill class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Participating in labs helped me get some extra credit, have to say, got good feedback each time I lost points. He is strict on grading but definitely follows Industry standards. Overall, a tough one but a good one

You can expect a lot of homework, but I gotta say it's worth it. It was frustrating to buy that $200 textbook, but at the end of the day, helped me learn things on my own. BTW, I landed an internship!! Yay!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have to say, I was a bit unsure about this course at first because I'd heard mixed reviews. I had some wrong assumptions going in. The course is good. The only downside is the cost of the textbook, but still, it's worth it. It is mostly for PDM. Even though I usually work with SolidWorks, I got to try a different version of NX.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: At first, I thought this class would be tough, but after a few weeks, I realized how helpful it actually is. It gave me a solid foundation in engineering topics,. Yes, there's quite a bit of homework, but you learn a lot. Eventually, that knowledge helped me land an internship, and I saw how useful PLM systems are, especially in large companies.

The course is a good opportunity to learn CAD, PDM and PLM. There are industry wide used softwares like NX, Teamcenter, Anark that are really helpful in Industry. The learning curve is steep at first but things settle down after a mid-term. Course is designed to make students experience work in Industry. Really good for students new to engineering
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: People complain a lot, but it is a very useful class with lots of practical wisdom given by him and others that he brings in.

Professor Fuerst's course isn't great but it's not nearly as bad as people say. The textbook's $200 which sucks but other than that it's a pretty straight forward course that's not hard to get an A in. Just know that this course is like two seperate courses: in labs you'll learn NX and then in lecture it's more about industry and technical terms.
He's definitely a bit of an attitude shock straight from highschool, but Professor Fuerst manages his class remarkably well.

I dont know why he has a bad rating. This class helped prepare me so much for a future career and if you're going into Engineering you NEED this class. Lecture's are a little pointless but that's how the course is built. The professor makes tutorials which really do help a lot. You have to try and it takes time but it is worth it.
Lectures are terrible, labs are a waste of time. Prepare to do a ton of work outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class at Purdue. $200 required txtbook w integrated quizzes, happens to be written by the prof. Takes half the class to open 6+ apps before working, currently spend 3+ hrs outside for 2 credits. Syllabus is years long + you gotta jump through a hundred hoops to email the professor about anything. I have a strong background in 3d modeling too

He uses NX and Teamcenter, which are some of the worst apps I've used. You can't rename files to match the professor's requirements, nor can you remove or edit them. Instead of repeating instructions to add a part, he links to another document, making task progression tedious and confusing for students trying to follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Don't be scared by Fuerst's score!
If you are a freshman and you know how to CAD take MFET 162 now!
This class should be more credit hours, the textbook is $200, and lecture is mandatory.
But the class is kinda easy, Quizzes/Tests are a joke I didn't even have to do the last practical cause of exam drops. Honestly gets too much hate.

Class is fairly easy and has plenty of extra credit. The lectures are the biggest waste of time I have ever attended. The worst part is that they're mandatory attendance, but you never actually learn the topics in class during them, so they're essentially just hour-long rambles. The labs are alright.

Professor Fuerst was great. I think the overall course itself, especially the exams, could use some improvement but I think he did a good job at introducing fundamental engineering concepts and showing the importance of them. The class isn't too bad, it can just be a lot of work some weeks. Overall, I would recommend taking this course.

It appears that many disagree/dislike Professor Fuerst, but I believe the issue stems less from him and more from the nature of the class. From what I can tell having taken the class, it appears Fuerst was tasked with digging MFET163 out of generation debt and had to experiment some (thus the hate) to make the class better. Overall, easy class.

Professor Fuerst was one of the best professors I had this semester. His lectures where well thought put and throughly enjoyed the guest speakers he brought in from industry. While the grading is tough the feed back was excellent on what I got wrong and if I didn't understand my TA was easily able to explain.

The class has some negatives (like a required $200 book, unintuitive software and annoying quizzes), but I think that he does well providing useful tutorials and material (I think many dislike lecture material because it is often not necessary to the class, but it seems relevant nonetheless). Overall, I think the class prepared me well.

Lectures are mandatory but useless. $200 textbook just for some weekly quizzes. This class is a time sink; only 2 credit hours, but heavy workload & they love shaving off points any opportunity they get, so attend office hours. That being said, work can be interesting at times despite old/laggy interface.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Travis fuerst is an easygoing and generally kind man. With that said, this is a terrible class. Nearly all of the information learned is buzz-words and memorization game, and quizzes require reading the incredibly dense $200 textbook to understand. Lectures are middling at best in terms of usefulness, and most lab work has to be done at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cool dude. He seems knowledgeable about industry and can form an educated opinion. I don't know why I go to lecture other than it's free points. It has little to nothing to do with the lengthy assignments from the lab. The TA's are good in the labs, but lowkey I could watch the tutorials he posts for the labs and get 99% of the class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor, his TAs put in a lot of work to ensure that students understand the topics covered and how to use the software.

Since Prof Fuerst decided to only have 1 lecture a week, this class isn't as intense as last semester. It's an easy A, but the lectures provide no information needed for the class. Your lab TA's will be much more important in teaching the content of how to CAD.

Fuerst is a nice guy who is always trying to improve MFET 163, and his lectures might not be useful but they are pretty interesting and he brings a few cool guest speakers. He also cares about his students and makes time for them.
Useless lectures but easy class because of many opportunities for extra credit and many drops

The lectures are pretty much useless, but attendance is mandatory. There is a 200 dollar textbook that I only used for the quizzes, which could have easily been available on Brightspace. A lot of the assignments will take a while but they usually have tutorials from the professor so that's nice. Grading scale is also weird, but an A is easy to get.

Going to his lectures is a waste of time because he rambles about anything unimportant (attendance is still mandatory). Requires you to buy a $200 textbook just to complete a couple quizzes. However, the class isn't that hard as long as you follow the rubric and use the search function in the textbook.
Grading scale is terrible. 92.99 is a B. 93.00 is an A.

Prof Fuerst does a great job running the class, especially for those with no prior experience. Had no CAD experience going in and had no problem learning using his textbook and video tutorials. Exams were all online and open note. Plenty of extra credit opportunities and drops. He and TA's were very accessible outside of class for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assignment's were very straight forward about what needed to be done, but the grading scale was kind of horrendous.
Spends lecture rambling on boosting his own ego. Homework takes forever and you have to cad "his way" so any prior cad experience will actually hurt you in this awful class.

A month into the class assignment documents were changed after released, at times forcing students to redo work that was done to the initially released assignment docs. Also, during the lectures Fuerst talks about whatever is on his mind and does not actually help you learn for the class.

Siemens NX is not meant to be used in an educational setting, and most of the teaching assistants are just as confused as you are.

How to survive one of Fuerst's classes:

1) Go to as many TA office hours as it takes (it will take multiple)
2) GO TO FUERST'S OFFICE HOURS - in person, he is actually super nice and he is really really helpful!

This class is going to suck no matter what. I hated it and it was one of my worst classes here, but I really don't think it's Fuerst's fault. He was fine in lecture, I stopped going, but the exam things were really easy, the class is really easy but it can be frustrating and take a really long time. And you need to buy the $200 textbook >:(

There is a huge learning curve in the class. I didn't find labs helpful since there was a 40:1 TA ratio. I would rec going to diff. lab/103 labs to find which TAs are helpful. Prof. Fuerst is a great guy; he helped guide me through the course when I was at an F and ended up with a B. Use manual uploads in Aras since the connector can be buggy.

This class has greatly improved from previous semesters as I can tell. Aras is a lot less buggy, and the class generally ran very smoothly. Fuerst is a pretty good lecturer, and the information is actually useful. PDM and CAD skills are very important, and Fuerst communicates that very well. I would have given 5 stars, but the textbook is $200.
He doesn't know what he is doing and often relies on TA's to demonstrate what we need to do. The website used to turn in most homework often doesn't work, so good luck turning in assignments.

Listen, all these reviews that are negative are exaggerated. I read them and was horrified, but I had no other choice but take the class. It really isn't that bad. Work is a little tedious, and lectures are a little unrelated, but interesting. 

Stay on top of your work 
Use the TA's 
Find a buddy to work with 

I learned a lot. 

You will be ok.

This class is not very well organized and the required $200 textbook is a huge pain to use. Most of the class materials come from it and the interface is very old/buggy despite being a brand new edition. The directions for the labs and modeling assignments are often confusing and the mandatory attendance at 8:30 or 9:30 in the morning isn't great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Im not sure why his reviews are so low, I took MFET 163 and the course was well structured and the TAs were extremely helpful. Only bad part is that lectures are not really useful but you have to go since it counts for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ungodly amounts of work for a 2 credit class, but I can definitely say I learned how to CAD. Lectures were overall pretty useless, and your lab section is where you really do everything. TA's are willing to help you through your assignments during lab or office hours.

- Lectures don't really teach you anything you need to know, just talks about industry
- You learn how to do everything in your lab, where you're expected to already know everything
- TA's are nice
- Homework isn't actually that hard, just takes forever and there is a lot of it
- Should get an A, just will make you want to die
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Textbook was useless and ridiculously expensive ($200 and he co-wrote it), Weekly work is tedious, really time consuming, but not too difficult. The real hard part is submitting it through Aras Innovator which has not had a functioning streak of 1 week since its inception and takes forever. Lectures do not teach at all. The TAs will save you.

Horrible class. The class itself is not even that hard, but it is the most disorganized class, despite how much they tell you they have restructured and fixed this class. The TAs don't know what they are doing.  Grading for this class sucks, and they are constantly giving out 0s and 50% with no feedback. This class is time-consuming for no reason.

He's really not as bad as people make him out to be, besides having to buy a $200 textbook you never use. The course had a stupid amount of issues and is really terribly run. ARAS had so many issues it was comical, and I felt bad for Fuerst and the TAs. I thought he was a pretty nice guy and I never really had a bad interaction with him.

Professor Fuerst and his TA's grade harsly. This is very much so a "busy work" class, on av. 4 assignments a week, and half of the semester is a project that you will constantly have to work on. The lectures are not mandatory and seem worthless. Exams are online and a breeze just read the mandatory purchased textbook. I do not recommend Pr. Fuerst
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In general he is a nice guy, and though the technology (both Aras and NX) are sometimes a major pain, they are tech issues not Prof issues. The TAs are knowledgeable and you are honestly good to go if you do your work in lab and don't wait till the last minute. Textbook is expensive though; no way around it. Grade scale is weird (86-93 B, 70-86 C).

Most disorganized class I have ever taken. You need to download like a million things to actually do any work. Submission was incredibly difficult for every assignment and the $200 textbook was required. Awful class.

This was genuinely the most disorganized class I have ever taken. The required textbook for this class costs $200 dollars and is a mess of poorly written directions. You are left on your own as it is impossible to get help on any issue without waiting days. There were constant issues with the software and apps used. Do not take this class.

The way that he grades horrible. Schedule is messy and even when due dates are changed they really aren't. The TA that i got was no help and made everything more confusing. Only saving grace was open software, so you can work on assignments outside of lab.

This class is taught by the TAs. To receive assistance you have to submit a help form, there is no in person teaching. This makes problems that would take 5 mins to solve in person, take days through emails sent back and forth. It created uneeded congestion and resulted in due dates being pushed back for weeks. This is just the tip of the iceberg.

Spring semester was very enjoyable, he made it clear he is dedicated to improving the course. VERY manageable workload, you are given 3 weeks/assignment with 2 hours a week of optional TA lab time for help. Lectures are pretty common sense, but still enjoyable if you really want to get into the inner workings of CAD.

This course was a train wreck. The TA's and the professor don't know how to transfer grades from Aras to Brightspace. In Aras, I have full points on a project and have feedback that I did a great job. In Brightspace, I have a ZERO (and it's worth 4% of my grade!) They also put grades in the Friday of Finals week and are not answering emails

Likely the worst course I've had to take at Purdue. The course load is totally insane given that this is a 2 credit hour class. He makes you buy 2 $90 text books that you will probably forget about after the weekly quiz assignments go away half way throught he semester. The TAs end up teaching most of the class too. Avoid if you can manage it

This course has been the worst experience I have had with a professor. It is two credit hours, but the workload per week for the back half of the semester often exceeded six hours. Much of this time was spent deciphering poorly dimensioned CAD models and dealing with cloud server issues. Responses do not come in a timely manner.

You have to buy both of his textbooks for the class, both because there are quizzes through the textbook software and because the quizzes are filled with terms and abbreviations which you'd only know if you read the textbook. The lectures are bad and useless, they just cover the reading again and don't add anything. Go to lab prep lectures though.

The purchase of 2 textbooks, totaling $190, is required for completing the weekly homework. These texts are so riddled with spelling and grammatical errors that this class could double for a writing credit for the errors I've had to correct to make my own study guides. Also, he manages to talk all lecture, and yet, say nothing. Avoid at all costs.

One of the most infuriating classes I have ever taken. There are $200 in textbooks that are required to do the quizzes, but they only help slightly because the wording on them is awful. Your TA almost entirely decides your grade, as they grade all assignments in the class. Fuerst also doesn't round at all, so if you aren't at a cut-off, that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Just awful. About 30 people come to lecture in a 300 person class, and for good reason. Lectures are just long rambles while he stumbles to demonstrate just about everything. Very little material to study with for the final exam and the textbook has to be the worst part about the class. He makes numerous mistakes on about every assignment.

The weekly quizzes are rough but they don't hold much weight at all when compared to the other assignments. I stopped going to lectures after the first few weeks and did just fine. Just make sure you get started on the assignments early and don't leave them until right before your lab. It is really the TA who dictates your grade, not Fuerst.

Requires you to buy two textbooks which he wrote and are riddled with spelling errors, and you can't even keep them, they are online and you buy a 6 month access window. Encourages using unique solutions to be efficient, but then punishes solutions on grounds which make sense after the fact but were never explained. Prepare to jump through hoops

I have never had a professor that doesn't know the layout of a class over a month in. Fuerst somehow took 4 weeks to decide if we would have a lecture over Thanksgiving break and still hasn't figured out if there will be a midterm assessment, a main portion of students' grades. He is clearly out of his depth and is not capable of running a course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless in this class so students must rely on the textbook to gain any sort of knowledge!! Weekly quizzes given are absurdly difficult and require memorizing every textbook page from the reading!! The workload is extreme when considering the class is only 2 credit hours!! Fuerst is totally unaware of the type of class he's teaching!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hands down best professor so far! Definitely recommend taking her classes. She will regularly attend lab sessions she isn't required to just to help students in between her own work. She is extremely kind and deserves respect.

The nicest Professor (and one of the nicest people) I've met at Purdue. The course is planned very well. Labs are straightforward and educational with ta's always available to help. The course content isn't the easiest, yet she presents and teaches in a very accessible way. Couldn't give higher accolades, great job

She made the material very accessible and was eager to help in lab and walk through how things work. Always patient and respectful in the process. While the course was easy, it wasn't completely handed to us either. Absolutely no cons, this should be the benchmark for how a professor and course should be in the ECET department.

One of, if not the best Professor in Electrical Engineering Technology. I took ECET 229 with her and she is the type of professor that deeply cares about her students. Gentle and caring professor.  is always available for help. She also tries to come to every lab section and help students in need. She is a role model for other Purdue professors
An overall good professor and was pretty chill. We only had 3 assignments per week- 2 being due Wednesday night, and 1 on Thursday night.

Lecture slides/emails often have errors and don't cover what is on the exam at all. He and the TA were unhelpful or unresponsive when I emailed them. 3 assignments a week that were tedious but easy. Would send out emails criticizing us for making up multiple-choice questions that weren't good enough for him to use on his test.

Professor Feld organized SOC383 very clearly. He provided both PowerPoints and video lectures which,made the content easy to understand! At the beginning of each week, he provides thorough instructions on what is expected of us. He is a kind professor that cares about our learning!
Great professor! He is very kind and his class is not very hard. Also took SOC 383 and it was good as well.
Great course to take as an elective. Weekly discussion posts and some quizzes. All the material is in the PowerPoints and easily referenced.

Took this class asynchronously and had a good experience. Dr. Feld had clear expectations and the workload was very manageable. There are weekly discussion boards and assignments as well as quizzes every two weeks.

Tookk SOC100 online this semster; very easy class. One thing I will say is that it is a bit monotonous, but that is normal with any online course. There were exams every 2 weeks, and the questions were generated by students, which was sometimes a bit weird. Overall an easy class and easy professor.

Please don't take SOC 38300 with him, especially if its online.  You have an exam basically every other week and exams are the biggest chunk of the grade.  This lectures and study guides don't even remotely cover what is on the exam, and he did not set any of us up to be prepared for the exams.  The hw during the week is manageable, but not exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took SOC 100 online with him this semester. He is very caring and assigns easy discussion questions. The tests are open note and he gives out study guides before each one. He records his lectures, but you don't have to watch them if you don't want to. He posts exactly what he says via PowerPoint as well.
Enjoyed his class!
This professor is so hard to understand . I dont understand his lectures . Doesnt seem to care about students and pretty weird lectures.
Horrible. Worst Professor I have ever had. He rambles on and his lectures are unorganized and make no sense at all. He is boring and his class is hard to go to and be at.

Avoid this prof at all costs. Extremely bad at teaching. Late to class fairly often. Unclear on what he wants from exam questions. His exams are terrible. He gives 20 extra credit points at minimum on them, and the average was still a C-. Seriously, avoid this guy at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Get off from this class, he talks incessantly without clarifying a single thing. Social research method is supposed to be informative instead of tedious.
it wasn't bad at all.
Absoulute worst teacher I have ever had. I failed miserably when I retook this class with another teacher I got an A. Drop this class immediatly and wait for another teacher.

One of THE worst professors I have EVER had@Purdue. I went to class and struggled all semester only to get a 59% F at the end of the semster. His TA routinely did NOT show up for office hrs & he did not seem to care when told about TA. The text was impossible to understand, he was worse to understand. Most of us failed.GET OUT WHILE U CAN!

Horrible at lectures. Cannot get his point acrossed and does alot of stuff in his head so you don't know where they are coming from. Inconsistent grading and unwilling to talk about how things are graded afterwards. Made review sessions at 3pm on thurs. when most had classes and wouldn't look at changing it.

he makes simple topics extremely confusing.  the TA was the reason I got through the class.  there are a ton of bonus points though, its an easy A if you use the book and go to the TA's office hours when you need help.
useless as a prof.

He is the foghorn leghorn of college professors.  All of the material is made to be as complex and unusable for a real-life purpose as possible.  The class is about collecting and analyzing data and he somehow cannot communicate his thoughts to people at all.  Simply horrible.

Lectures are only worth going in order to get possible assignments, but his lectures are extemely inadequate and ultimately confusing.  Read the textbook and attend lab meetings. imo: great lecturer, very approachable, always answered questions and explained concepts throughly if something's not clicking in class or office hrs. 

however long you think you'll need to study for a regular exam, double it for this class. exams are insanely difficult relative to other intro classes and there's always grading errors

She sucks mucho
Speaks a lot inn lectures goes too fast i think and most of her class are like exam heavy most of the grades are based on exams not that much heavy oriented for participation or hws

I love Dr. Fox as a professor. She is super kind and interesting to talk to. She is one of the best teachers that I've ever had. With that, the grade is 80% exams which is super annoying. Prof. Fox is ok. She is clearly knowledgeable, but runs her lectures a bit like high school. No laptop, no phone (except iClicker), annoying assignments. This class will have you wanting to take a one way trip to Maxistan and never come back (ifykyk) The course content itself is not hard theres just 1000 hops you have to jump in order to get through it... Hours upon hours of studying graces you with TERRIBLE test scores. She does curve so ill give her that. For your own sake chose a diffrent prof!

Dr. Fox was an amazing lecturer and made the content understandable. A lot of the grade is based on exams and a combined class participation/attendance/homework grade. Overall, the work was not that difficult, and the class was easy, but she is a little blunt and not super approachable.

The class is just so poorly set up. The course is over 75% graded on exam performance and Mrs Fox (yes that was said on purpose) is nowhere to be found during them. reviews.comment: The lectures were kind of confusing sometimes, and you have to pay attention the whole time or you'll fall behind, but if you pay attention and take notes its not super hard of a class to get an A in.
Fox did a great job elaborating on content while still keeping the class interested. She runs a bit of a strict lecture, but it is worth it if you are going in there to learn about economics.

I took this class over the summer, and it was condensed into 4 weeks. While the class wasn't necessarily hard, the homework, practice tests, and even actual exams were riddled with errors. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just pay attention and you'll be fine.
good but also bad at the same time. hard to learn because she makes everything seem harder than it actually is. but overall, a kind soul who is passionate about economics. class is VERY exam heavy.

Had Prof. Fox for ECON 252 & took her again for 251—she's amazing! Lectures are clear, recorded, and she truly cares (even canceled class when it was freezing). This course is out of 400 points. 300 points are taken up by the three exams throughout the semester. You do bad in one exam and your grade is already dropped. She gives you homework consisting of an insane amount of questions but it ends up only being out of a few points. Lectures are extremely boring. Avoid if you can.

Fox's class isn't easy, but getting an A is realistic. The hate she gets isn't warranted—she's nice, you just can't loaf. Attendance is 15%, but it made me show up more than I would've. Office hours are underrated—she tutored me 1-on-1 bc no one came. I got 80-90 on exams, 70 attendance. Did provided practice to study & understood each mistake made

I've had her for macro and micro and for some reason micro was taught so much worse than her macro class. We use achieve for homework and when I had missed a couple assignments, she emailed me asking me what was wrong. Not as bad as it seems. Everyone made it seem like she was terrible, but I found the course relatively easy. Just go to the lectures and you will be fine. Exams are 75% of your grade, but that is how it is for all Micro classes.

I took this during her first semester coming to Purdue, which was two years ago. her notes are awful

She's is the worst person ever.

Very exam heavy grader, and there's the occasional tough question. But honestly?  If you show up to lecture and do the practice exams, you'll be fine. 
The exams are not unfair - just be sure you're adequately prepared by studying. 
Always tries to explain things 3 ways (graphically, mathematically, story-wise). She's a perfectly fine professor.

The exam is hard if you haven't taken any economics classes before. About 75% of the final grade is made up of the exams. Lectures rarely help, and you need to learn by yourself. Professor Fox is caring, but it is a large lecture, so it's impossible to know each student well.

reviews.comment: I took Fox for micro and compared to that this class was a breeze. Tests were significantly easier and one was dropped. I do not like her teaching style however because a lot of what she teaches isn't on the exam which isn't very useful but overall easy and didn't have to pay too much attention in lectures.

Very clear what needs to be done in order to be successful. For this class, i attended the lectures, took notes, did the homework, and utilized the textbook readings as supplemental if i needed help on a concept.  That seemed to be work well enough. Uses Iclicker for participation

Melanie Fox's content is not very helpful as the topics get hard. Her lectures are hard to follow and during the summer it is much worse. The exams, assignments, and quizzes are in no way related to each other. For a 4-week course, this is by far the most stressful, disorganized course.

She often gets off topic during lectures and does not emphisize/explain topics that are actually going on the test. Her practice tests/study guides are horrible. They often are just wrong.

Does not care about her students. She takes pride in the fact that Supplemental Instruction is needed rather than working with students to make the class more manageable. Avoid her at all costs, and if you have her, I hope you already know economics.

She was pretty good. I think she is overall complained about too much but the exams are all multiple choice and fairly easy. I didn't study much for exams and did fine.

Good lectures, made the material easy to understand, and was willing to answer questions both inside and outside of class. Occasionally makes errors on homework, but I don't think there were any on the tests. Very clearly knows and likes the material she is teaching.

reviews.comment: She is very understanding and helpful when you need it. As long as you go to lecture you should be good

She moves quickly and there are errors on every practice test/quiz, so it's hard to study. She also sends passive-aggressive emails after poor test grades.

By far the most boring and worst professor I've had. If you had entered her class about some knowledge about economics, you will come out not knowing a single thing.
Exams and study guides are riddled with errors.

I think Fox is a person who genuinely cares about econ, her lectures are interesting but she also makes a decent amount of mistakes. She is also very nice and office hours are very easy to schedule.

I'm actually disappointed in Purdue. Do they not quality check these classes? Like i get a couple mistakes here and there but this professor's consistency just astonishes me. Unbelievable

I am writing a second review (and maybe a third) because 350 characters is nowhere near enough to describe this professor's utter incompetence. I feel like I am viewing my 3rd grade brother's homework when I look at her review guides.

CONSTANT typos that make for the MOST confusing assignments and quizzes. The number of questions that are objectively incorrect on the study guide is actually laughable. She shows her work so you can see the silly mistakes she makes. Honestly it's disappointing and gut-wrenching that we pay thousands of dollars for this quality of education.
She makes mistakes on exams and homework repeatedly, which makes it harder to learn and prepare for exams.

I found her to be extremely rude throughout the entire year and have zero connection with any of her students and when I emailed her after exam two about the study guide errors she had on every single exam and how it messed with a lot of students during the exam, her best response was to remove all of the study guides altogether for all exams....

Although the content itself wasn't horribly difficult. The way she explains most concepts are overcomplicated and confusing. The most frustrating part is that every single review material and exam has errors in the answer keys. Therefore, it's impossible to know if you don't understand the concept or if the answer key is just wrong once again.

The amount of homework that this person gives is insane. Additionally, this professor can't PROPERLY adjust and publish prep quizzes. when doing the homework there were multiple questions that were objectively incorrect. this was also the case on quizes and exams. when it comes to teaching she definitely covers the topics but for each topic she'll do up to 3 or 4 examples making her lectures really boring.

Exams are worth majority of your grade and are written very poorly. Countless typos and other errors that make the exams frustrating. Overall unprofessional teacher inside the classroom and out.

I took notes on literally everything and still somehow got a B.

Dr. Fox is the main reason I genuinely struggled in Econ. She offers practice test, and I did one before an exam, and got an A on it, took the real exam and failed. Later Dr. Fox left a note in the grade book saying, "I saw you did the practice exam, don't do them, they are not an accurate portrayal of the exam" WHY ARE THEY THERE THEN!!!!

The course was generally well taught and concepts were explained in digestible chunks that made it easy to understand. Professor Fox herself was helpful and responded quickly and in detail to anything of concern. That being said, the amount of work was very large and a bit confusing, and there were often mistakes in the exams that she would write.

Pr. Fox's lectures are boring and it's as if she designed them for middle school. The exams are poorly written; they have unclear questions, hand sketched figures, and sometimes even mistakes. There are no good study guides for the exam, so preparing for them is hard.
Makes easy material look hard.
As bad as Fox news.
One of the worst professors I've had at Purdue

Mediocre lectures, uncaring, hard to deal with, unpleasant person.

There are not many options for ECON 251, so if you have to take Dr. Fox, get ready for some boredom. Try to do everything without dealing with her on a personal level. She is difficult and a good slang term for her would be "Karen".

I can tell that Dr. Fox knows her material well. However, tests being 90% of my grade was difficult to adjust to. Also, the exams were fraught with errors, resulting in disorganization. I tried to get an A, but it was hard given my first exam score, so make sure to study lots! There are opportunities for EC, but it requires semester long effort.
Melanie Fox doesn't care about students. She knows things but does know how to teach and she assumes that we are all supposed to know things. try to avoid her.

Most noticeable thing in this course is that exams are 90% of your grade. The lowest exam is also dropped. Make sure to do well on exams and you'll be more than fine, though they can be tough. Professor talks fast and assumes too much for a beginner course. It's a steep learning curve if you never took a microeconomics course before.

reviews.comment: I thought she was a clear lecturer, and I appreciated the ample extra credit. I honestly thought a lot of her lecturing was helpful, even if I found the slides difficult to understand. However, the class was disorganized, especially the exams, which had many mistakes. This is especially bad due to the fact that exams are 90% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lecture is boring, but that's understandable; it's a big class. However, the frequent errors in the exams and review materials are confusing, and the errors are not updated on Brightspace or explained. The exams are not so difficult. It's okay to get an average grade. But I will not recommend taking her class.

Lectures are often mono-tone and slides are very confusing. Exams are utterly disorganized with multiple spelling errors, and print errors across ALL exams. Homework reflects perhaps 50% of the material on the exam, so it's best you supplement it by attending SI sessions and Khan Academy. Find another professor if possible (if offered).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Fox is excellent. This class is a breeze as long as you keep up with the assignments. She makes a recommended pace and publishes it on Brightspace, if you follow that you should be fine. Exams are exactly like practice questions she posts and there is so much extra credit (go to lecture for the points!). Thought this class was a lot of fun

This class has one homework assignment per week and allows you up to 15% in extra credit alone. Melanie Fox is very knowledgeable and designed the questions on Khan Academy if you want to know how her exams are like. She moves quickly in her lectures but that's understandable since this is a large course. Attendance is only needed for extra credit.

Dr. Fox puts on Brightspace a preview of what we'd learn that week. She shows that she cares about students' learning, as well as her passion for teaching the subject. As someone who particularly doesn't enjoy or understand economics and government topics, Dr. Fox does a great job of teaching in a way I understand and find interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Fox was not fantastic, not horrible, but a really middle of the road professor. She is kind and helpful, willing to help students as long as you seek help. Unfortunately, her lectures are incredibly boring and if you already hate economics like me, you will struggle. Exams are collectively worth 90% of your grade. 5/10 average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Fox is a okay teacher but her class is extremely disorganized. We never finish covering content when we are supposed to. She posts all review material like 2 weeks after she says she will. Doesn't respond to piazza. Can be passive aggressive. Her exams are chaotic. She has passed out whole correction sheets, with 8-10 problems wrong.

She explains the lecture content in a very cut and dry manner. Teaches at a relatively slow pace, but is expected for a gen-ed/basic ECON class. The exams are incredibly fair; there's really no reason to do poorly in the course. And there are other opportunities for extra credit and to do well in the course.

Prefix: ECE student taking class for gen-ed req. Overall, easy class. Exams concept heavy (can cram day before, get ~90%), only basic math, 90% of your grade, though can drop one of 4 exams. Free bonus credit ~15 points, iclicker & watching few videos. Classes sometimes slow, though prof. is clear in explaining (you'll get the stuff if you listen).

All around ideal professor. She obviously loves the subject and teaching about it, and she is really good at explaining it. Very good at explaining things with examples. I can't imagine a better professor

Melanie Fox knows a lot about economics but does an extremely poor job teaching it.She acts as if it is all "common sense" and while this might be for someone who has been studying this topic for years, it is not for a student who may be learning about these terms for the first time.Even in her office hours she is extremely unhelpful. try to avoid!
Hardest class this school year. Tests are difficult and large.

Professor Fox is well-versed in economics and although the lectures are a bit boring, the content isn't overwhelming and the course is fairly straight forward. There are also lots of opportunities for extra credit if you do the homework and go to class. All exams are multiple choice.

Be prepared for a lot of homework!!!! BUT the homework is genuinely so so so helpful and super easy. She's a good professor and she genuinely cares about making sure her students are learning. Don't be afraid to reach out for help.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lectures I felt were vague and didn't sufficiently cover the material that would appear in the homework and tests. She posts video recordings, so those are great to use. There are many opportunities for extra credit. Dr. Fox obviously knows the material well, but I don't believe it was conveyed in the best way.

Professor Fox was an overall great professor. Her explanations are clear and give great+abundant practice exams, which is very helpful when the course is exam-heavy. She really cares about students' grades because there are so many extra credit opportunities and lots of help sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she explained micro so it actually made sense. very open to take questions and actually wants the students to understand what she's talking about.
Dr. Fox is tough on you but her lectures are clear and if you pay attention and take notes then you shouldn't have a problem.
Keep track of hotseat for extra credit. Homework can be a bit long but not at all difficult. Exams aren't too bad. Likable personality.

Do all of the "optional" assignments (PCTs and LCs). Use them to study for the exams (LCs especially). Go to class and make sure you understand the HW. Fox is very smart and will be a good professor if you do everything she asks you to do per week.

Professor Fox is great and definitely knows the material they are teaching, but the notes and lectures are not posted anywhere online after the lectures, and this makes the course slightly more difficult due to a few resources not accessible to any students who have to miss the class for any reason. Class is not too difficult, but expect the work.

Homework/CY's are easy. Lectures are optional, but can help with the extra credit she offers. The class doesn't appear hard at the surface, but the exams weigh heavily on your grade, 25%per, and the tests are pretty difficult compared to the rest of the work and concepts taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's always willing to answer questions and help students.

Dr. Fox was very helpful when you went directly to her for office hours. However, her lectures left me very confused. The textbook is a lot to read but more useful and clearer than her lectures. There is a lot of homework, but if you take the time to try to understand the exams are pretty straightforward. Follow her pacing schedule for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Fox is a good professor and I thought she taught well with good examples.  Sometimes there would be stuff on the homework that wasn't covered in the lecture but you get multiple attempts.  You can always find this information in the reading (which isn't mandatory) but it really isn't a problem.  I barely touched the textbook and exams were easy.

This class should not be difficult, however, the material presented in the course makes it difficult. Melanie Fox knows what she is talking about however, her explanation is not good. The homework that is assigned does not equate to the actual lectures. Her lectures are very vague and do not cover what is presented on the homework often.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love professor Fox! She organizes the course very well, giving you a "recommended pace" every week. She provides lots of resources to help prepare for exams (which are not bad if you do all of the homework and look at the resources she provides). There is a decent amount of homework, but if you follow her pacing schedule it is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is very active on piazza, use that to your advantage. Unfortunately there were lecture where I walked out more confused about the content than if I just read the textbook. The textbook is the primary resource; it is honestly easy to read and has everything she bases the CYs and Exams around.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She's definitely a really caring and kind professor who is very passionate about economics, but the class itself is confusing in terms of questions and her lectures don't necessarily allow you to excel on their own. It takes lots of practice problems and asking TAs to re-explain topics since her lectures can be incredibly confusing.

I really love her! The homework isn't super hard and it really helps me keep up even if i miss a class every now and then. She's super helpful and reaches out personally after exams and stuff. And she's always active on piazza to answer questions!! I'd fully recommend tbh.The expensive textbook is a bummer though
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, not a bad class, would still recommend against it. My reason for recommending against it is that you're forced into buying Macmillan's Achieve for >$100 (can't remember exactly). This would be reasonable if Achieve was a functioning website, which it isn't in the slightest. You'll have to redo an assignment at least once, I promise.

The class was easy and but I found the material boring. Professor Flory is so kind and funny and I did enjoy the lectures and talking to her. She's very understanding about any issues you may have and works with you. Two essays, a midterm, and a final, so pretty light work too.

Professor Flory is a brilliant professor who possesses so much knowledge. She encourages but doesn't demand participation, is understanding with absences/extensions, and is available for feedback during office hours. Just make sure you listen to discussions (Especially for inspiration for poems in essays) and complete the assignments.

Professor Flory is a passionate lecturer with a very entertaining teaching style. While the class is graded on only 3 papers, she gives great feedback and truly cares about the success of her student's.

Dr Flory is clearly passionate about English and wants students to become better writers, and succeed in the class. The only gripe is that your grade is based only on three papers, but her feedback is constructive and well thought out. Take her class if you want to engage with the material, and be prepared to write and revise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She really likes to go on tangents during lectures and if you don't agree with her opinions, she makes it clear that you're wrong. She won't give trigger warnings for upsetting topics either. VERY strict grader and very nitpicky when it comes to the wording of papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very discussion heavy class. prof flory is the nicest woman i've ever met in my whole life she is super understanding if you need more time or extensions she's a really nice grader gives great feedback. has a tendency to go on tangents about other works during class discussion but it is very engaging and fun and she also said she liked my poem :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While at Purdue, Flory was a great professor, and even though she was a very tough grader and made me rewrite a ton of papers, she cared about my writing and always wanted me to improve. She loves to get off topic in class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Flory is not a bad professor. She based the final grade off of 3 papers ONLY (you can rewrite them as much as you want though). She did not include a TW to specific readings (SA, Suicide). until a student was upset. Doesn't like differing opinions/interpretations HOWEVER, she is very kind/understanding and will work with you on the papers
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Flory is a kind individual and I appreciated her enthusiasm for her work. The only problem I had was that she was a very harsh grader at times, though she was always willing to discuss your work with you. I didn't enjoy how specific the essay topics were, as it didn't allow for creative freedom when writing. Otherwise, she did a great job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just avoid her if you can. There are so many way better lit teachers at Purdue. Her classes are extremely boring but at least they're easy to pass.

She is not open to alternative interpretations. If you don't see what she sees in the works, you're wrong and she'll tell you that. The whole semester was graded around 3 papers, and if it isn't eye-to-eye with her views, you'll get low grades. She's smart but too self-absorbed

Professor Flory is great. She is blunt and harsh and brutally honest, but that is honestly what you want in a teacher. She told me at the beginning of the semester that I had a "problematic" style of writing but I learned so much from that comment and her helpful feedback. She is a brilliant woman with a ton of information to offer. Loved her!

Her class was really enjoyable. She did a great job at making the interpretation of older poetry relatable and fun. Her papers had tough expectations, but if you made a poor grade, she would work with you to redo and resubmit it. By far the best English professor I've had.

Her class is easy and she isn't bad, but if you actually want to learn anything about poetry, then don't take 237 with her. Class discussions are awful. No one wants to talk because she disagrees with anyone's insights that don't completely agree with hers. She only asks questions to fish for specific answers, not to spark open conversation.
Very fun to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you don't agree with her interpretation of the poetry, don't even bother turning in a paper. You will get a bad grade. She doesn't post to blackboard and doesn't keep you up to date on your grades so you don't know what your grade is throughout the course. However, she is very friendly and will answer questions very willingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very old fashioned. If you write a paper and she does not agree with your argument she will give you a low score because it doesn't match her personal opinion. Very understanding if you need to miss class or need an extension. Lecture is not discussion based just talking at you. This class is straight poetry. She will let you redo papers.

Just took my final, and I can safely say I didn't learn a thing all semester. Interesting woman and interesting-ish class, if you like to sit and listen to someone talk a lot. No grading criteria, syllabus, or real information given out at any point. I have literally no idea what my grade is. All you can really do is show up and hope for the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful person, professor, and very intelligent. All students learn about life from her lectures- she'll surprise you will her wisdom and antedotes. Recommended highly for all students, not just English or English Education majors.
intelligent, fun lectures. Knows how to run a survey course the right way.

Great teacher! She truely cares about her students, and she is always willing to help you out. If you go to her office hours, you won't be disappointed. Very knowledgeable and has actually met many of the writers. Sometimes gets off track, but you still learn a lot.
She was amazing!  Everyone should take her class just so they can see how great she is.  She really knows her stuff!  She has met so many of the people that she teaches about...she is just great!
She is so enthusiastic and fun.  Listens to everyone, and doesn't make you feel dumb for saying the wrong thing.

She is one of the sweetest people I've met at Purdue.  She will always work with you and she'll always tell random stories about her Bristish or Texan life that are funny because they're quirky or just so lost.  I love her!

She definitely knows her poets.  Course requirements were clear.  Not a lot of papers to write.  Class discussion was like pulling teeth, though not through any fault of hers.  Loved her Harry Potter tangents!  I would definitely recommend her.

She knows what she's talking about and is willing to go above & beyond in helping you understand material. She is very approachable and friendly. One of my favorite profs. ever! And as for the tangents, they link the poetry with other seemingly unrelated factors - and make class fun! So there! :)

She tells you in class what she wants... just go and listen to lecture. The tangents are fun, and useful if you're having an off-day and need to space out for a bit. Very knowledgeable about her subject, and an incredibly nice teacher!

I love Professor Flory! I took many classes with her. She is always excellent, and challenges you to think. She does go on tangents, but I find them amusing. If you show up, do the reading, and meet with her about papers, you'll always get an A.

If she doesn't agree with your interpretation of poetry, you might as well not submit a paper. She will find biographical information that you know nothing about and sugges that you add it to your paper. Not helpful!!
Nice woman who clearly knows her stuff, but she goes off on random tangents that have nothing to do with anything and are a huge waste of time.  SO annoying sometimes.

His lectures are extremely disorganized and hard to follow. Never explains definitions or basic concepts, just randomly starts solving problems or showing MATLAB code, and doesn't explain why or what they mean. Moves really fast, skips sections without warning, makes quizzes much harder than other sections, and office hours are not helpful.

Frazho is very eccentric, energetic, and funny. Our section was ahead of others for the entire semester, which allowed him to give us an abundance of examples that helped us understand the material. His quizzes were very easy if you attended lectures. The homework was, at times, too difficult/long and included things we didn't learn in lecture.

Professor Frazho is an energetic professor and cares for his students in AAE 590 (Probability and Estimation Thoery).  He is a bit disorganized when he teaches but you still learn a lot from his well-written course notes.

Professor Frazho lectured 301 really well this semester. His lectures were clear and he made sure you were able to 'see' the math in action with MATLAB to help your understanding. He also gave great hints during the Homework Help Sessions.

Frazho may be a genius, but he isn't good enough to teach. From disorganized lectures to a complete lack of interest in teaching us something (he would show up to class and start doing math without explaining what he was doing nor how to do it), you will feel completely lost in his lectures and will be on your own, as office hours are not helpful.

Prof. Frazho is a very unique character. He's scatter-brained, foul-mouthed, and brilliant; his lectures feel kind of like you're a muggle trying to take a class at Hogwarts. His tests are extremely tough, but he curves most people to a B at the end of the semester. If you sit in the front and pay attention you'll probably do fine.
During prelabs will give you some hints for the labs and lab reports
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You MUST pay attention in class otherwise that will be a pain.

Frazho is very unorganized.  You will never really know what your grades are in the class because he "doesn't know where to draw the cutoff." Generally gives you B's if you're within the standard deviation of exams. Exams are graded inconsistently. You don't really learn FROM him and there is no clear purpose of the class until 3/4 in the semester.

Professor himself seems to be a nice guy but a course itself seems unprepared. This is my first class without course syllabus. Exam was scheduled one week in advance. HW just pop up. Course note is quite unorganize and weird (graphs need to be in color but it's in black and white rofl) and really hard to read. Expect self-taught.

The best course I took in my grad school till now; Prof. Frazho pushes the course forward in a really great way. Most of the projection theorem, Hilbert spaces make sense in the beginning but in the final few weeks he uses them to derive the whole Kalman filter from scratch. Greatly knowledgeable instructor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Its sometimes hard to understand what Frazho is talking about or how what you are doing relates to anything, but if you review the notes he gives after class while you are working on the assignment, it makes scene. Also, prepare to be blown away on exams.
Tough professor to learn from. He knows his material but does not present it well. Be ready to self-teach.

I took 301 with Garrison and dropped it half way through b/c he's incompetent.  I learned more in a day with Frazho than half a semester with Garrison.  I felt very prepared for AAE 364.  If you go to class you'll get at least a B.

I took this class as an undergrad, as did a few others. He said "I admire anyone who is an undergrad and taking this class, so I will not give you less than a B."  I got an A, but he was a genius and tried his hardest to teach.
Very funny guy.  Makes me always want to go to class.  He teaches by example which is great.  Best Purdue Aero professor I've had yet.

A great overall prof.  Can honestly say that I never came close to falling asleep in his class.  He is the only professor that I have ever had that will cuss at math.  Very entertaining and presents the material in a way that I found very helpful.
Has his quirks, but he is a genious.  He doesn't like teaching so he makes his class very easy, which is cool.  However, he is amazing with Math and his knowledge of the subject
No Comments

Good professor.  He has a lot of weird quirks about him, but he is definately the right professor for the class.  He takes a normally hard class with difficult material, and most of the time makes it interesting and easy to learn.

Lower level classes probably aren't the high point of his day (or semester) which is why he practically gives the answers away for his homework.  Good prof if you want to pass, not good prof if you *really* want to learn material.
Very knowledgable and exciting teacher. One of the challenging yet interesting courses I have taken. Final exam was oral and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I am glad I took his course.

Dr. Goldsmith is a great professor, he clearly knows his stuff and cares about his students. He'll give what you put in. He's got a good sense of humor, can make the class enjoyable. It's just a lot of reading, but if you do it you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor who does care about the students' education. There's a lot of reading up until the last month where's there's one big group project. There may be a lot to do, but it should be one of the easiest class for anyone's semester and is very doable. Professor is short, has a wry sense of humor, okay to get along with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you're ever in this class and thinking about what grade you will receive on an essay, take that number and subtract it by 15. There's your actual score.

Professor Goldsmith is a great professor, he grades fairly and you're rewarded for the effort you put into the course. I think the amount of work for a General Ed class is too much, there's a lot of reading for homework, and usually 2 quizzes per week. As long as you show up and put in the effort, your grade will be fine.
Too hard for a gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Let me start with this: There are several people on here who might be unnecessarily harsh on him. While this class is reading heavy Professor Goldsmith himself is a great professor who gives insightful lectures and amazing feedback. I'm not a liberal arts student ( never been the most diligent reader) but Professor Goldsmith made this class great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith is funny, which makes class easy to pay attention to. The workload is not difficult, expect an average of 40 reading pages per week. For his writing assignments, he has a clear rubric and is willing to help you improve in office hours. If you do the reading you will do well. Also, if there is a bug, just evacuate 😔💔🐛
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: he is hilarious and keeps class enjoyable, he is willing to help students with any questions and give constructive feedback. He holds students accountable for attendance and readings which is helpful in order to improve. I greatly appreciate this professor and would take him again. He lacks in bug killing skills so brace yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: A really humorous professor who makes sure students fully understand the material and know exactly what's expected for each assignment. It's easy to earn a good grade as long as you follow instructions and attend class. His grading is very fair. He only deducts points if the assignment guidelines aren't followed or if the content is incorrect.

Very enjoyable class, some funny comments, he makes sure you know what you need to do to get a good grade and is fairly reasonable when it comes to bad grades and extra points. He cannot kill a bug unfortunately, I would say that is one flaw of his, do not count on him to save the day if you see one, you are on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He makes it clear to do well in his class you need to show up and follow instructions. Pretty simple. He gives us readings and the occasional pop quiz which are not difficult at all if you do the readings. We have written papers that boost our grades off participation and then longer papers he grades but not hard. Very funny and nice. Do recommend.

I really have enjoyed this class so far, Professor is a nice guy! and I find myself genuinely cracking up at certain parts of class. While you can expect to have a reading assignment every class, that is reasonable for a collage level course. Pop quizzes are frequent but decently easy if you read, and he drops the lowest one (supposedly) Enjoyable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly coming in I was a bit scared of his class based off of the first day but have enjoyed it. Just have to put in effort but come on like it's college what did you expect. He is pretty funny and I always laugh at his jokes. He is good at explaining more in depth the topics and dumbs it down so you can understand.
He's a good guy who wants his students to really learn the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a super hard grader and genuinely picked on students. never gave good feedback to improve upon, gave over 50 pages of reading for pop quizzes in class. SCLA should not be the hardest class for someone. PLEASE try not to take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: honestly terrible pls avoid him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Big fan of Professor Goldsmith. Frequent in-class quizzes though the material covered is never immensely difficult. Homework outside of class is solely readings, but completion is necessary as it contains the information covered in quizzes. Funny guy in class, accommodating, and agreed to provide networking opportunities within the industry.
Super chill, down to earth prof. Knows his stuff, keeps it light with jokes, and somehow makes even the tough material enjoyable. Just thug it out and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, but sometimes its like 10 pages so not crazy heavy. Prof is understanding as long as you communicate ahead of time/effectively. Lot of hand-writing in the class due to AI policy, but just accept it & thug it out. Class time is helpful cuz it gives you the big ideas of reading + you can gauge what he looks for in answers/writing.

Just show up and do the readings( the readings are a bit much but get it done over the weekend). His classes are pretty fun and I find him funny. But might be too much work. Overall if you have a chill major his classes are super nice and I love the tech detox.

The professor treated this general education class as if it was our main focus. It he assigned ~50 pages for each class with pop quizzes. There were very little speeches for an oral credit. The professor is very judgy, will disagree with you and grade harsher if he thought you claim was bad. I'm an engineering major and didn't have time for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take 101 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class way harder than needs to be. He also is very subjective in grading and will randomly mark you off lots of extra points if he doesn't agree with your claim and won't look at what you are saying. Take another SCLA 101 class with a teacher who grades easier

Discussion-based - Participation matters but there were definitely "right" answers and the prof judged you. This class was very dependent on his opinions of you. Grading was skewed based on how much he likes you and your argument. He would try to relate to students but would call them out instead.  For Oral Com there were very few graded speeches
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a super nice guy and I think he really cares about his job. The problem is he is a very tough grader and sometimes his grading does not makes total sense. I felt that with writing our essays on paper timed was not efficient. I was hoping to take this class to improve my writing but it did not do that. Class way harder than it should be.

Lots of reading assigned every night, from long ancient philosophical texts. Very harsh grader for writing and presentations. Very hard, specific pop quizzes up to multiple times a week based on readings. You have to write and edit 1000+ word essays BY HAND in blue books, timed during class because of massive AI distrust. Take an easier professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For an intro level class i thought it was much harder than needed. There was reading almost every night. He gave pop quizzes which made it more stressful than it already was trying to understand some of the text. And instead of trusting us to not use AI we had to handwrite our 1000+ word papers, which could only be done in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Goldsmith was a good professor overall but a tough grader. Also, he gave lots of pop quiz reading quizzes. If you are not the best English student, I recommend taking this class with a different teacher. An A is very doable in this class if you are a good writer due to the extra credit points you will be given. Also, you can NOT skip his clas
Zach is the funniest professor at Purdue. 10/10 to my short king. Don't use AI if you take his class.

Professor Goldsmith's class was entertaining and engaging. Despite having a lot of material to read, he always made sure that students understood the readings and went through important passages in class. His grading is also pretty easy and he's very funny. Would definitely recommend for SCLA 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith is a great professor, and a really entertaining guy. He grades papers fairly, and you'll do good if you follow the given structure through the essay.
