Easy class, go to every lecture as there is an attendance quiz nearly every lecture. Study hard for the exams via the Blackboard study guides, and you should get an A. The reason I got a B was because I screwed up a few labs practicals.

Very easy class... Just go for class and do the quizzes he will tell u the answer most of the times or else someone will just shout it out.... The exams are really easy if you practice using the question bank on blackboard do the question bank about 6-7 times homeworks are easy labs are easier if you do the homeworks and practicals are a bit tough but manageable  u shud get an A VERY easily if you just attend lectures and labs...
If you don't get an A in this class you have done something wrong. He can't make things any clearer than they are in this class. Good teacher and entertaining.
An easy A if you go to class and take the exams seriously.

He is a good professor, very clear in his teaching style. However, it's not very pertinent to the class, you can get by without going to class. Labs can be easy if you get a good TA. Gives surprise quizzes(esp right before/after holidays) and usually at the end of class, so I used to have a friend text me if there was a quiz. Overall, an easy class
Teacher sets you up for success, but students are lazy. His lectures are boring, but you have to work for an A

The class is only hard cuz he spends little time going over material. Labs are pointless unless you have a nice TA (mine was ok) and tests are hard. He gives you practice exams but there are so many questions so it is still hard. You dont learn anything useful. I got away with a B and I'm just happy to be done.
Useless prof, useless class.

good professor, personable. Very clear about what were going to cover. Goes over schedule of the semester every class. Test are not easy but he gives sample exams that have the EXACT questions so you just have to put in work and ull do good in the class. Easy quizs are given randomly in lecture! Overall very useful class and good professor!

Class was difficult. Exams were challenging, but we were given practice tests with the EXACT questions. Anyone who spends a minimum amount of time studying should do well. Warning: Don't miss lab and be sure to submit assignments on time even if they're only 1/2 done.
Gary is a jerk! His attendance quizzes are basically impossible and his tests are really hard. Good luck!
No Comments

I think she has good intentions and is easy to reach for questions. But, giving very little guidance on a project worth 75% of our grade, lengthy and unclear requirements being added to it at the last minute before an academic break, and having us write 20+ paragraphs of reflection, all for her to obtain a grant, has been incredibly frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course was unnecessarily difficult. Class was online and was disorganized - assignments being added near the end of the semester after having a clear schedule. Expectations were not always clear or were changing. She seemed like a nice person and interested in the students, but she liked to highlight her career/accomplishments.

IDK why she keeps getting selected for integral EEE courses like 350 and 380, she's just not a great professor. She is on sabbatical while teaching so is almost never present. The one good thing is that her courses are almost all graded on homework, plus one generally easy final project and attendance; no exams! ...which for thermo was a lifesaver.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach homework material in class. Spends class time doing things unrelated to homework, then expects us to read the entire textbook and learn homework material for ourselves. Also, homework is worth half your grade.

I thought that Professor Hua did a great job at explaining the course content. Any criticisms I would have would be with the course itself and not the professor. The class just had a ton of group projects that could become quite overwhelming fast, especially if your team members weren't great.

The course material itself was not difficult, but the workload was large but definitely not unmanageable. She was very clear about course and assignment expectations. However, I found the lectures to be too long, especially when the material discussed was always reviewed before class.

One of my favorite teachers here yet. Grading is a little tough as you need to put a ton of time into the homework assignments and there is only one exam, but the lectures are super interesting and the team aspect of the class is super fun. I would recommend reading the book because many of her lectures skip over stuff covered in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No midterms, little problem solving, lots of class time wasted on group work or skits or activities, then offers you no guidance on a cumulative final (will not even reveal layout or topics covered), is strangely secretive about it, and asks you to make an outline of the entire course as your study guide and study everything. Impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not very clear, as her voice is low. And there are a lot of group work in class, which are time wasting. Scores of the assignments really depend on the TAs , and there will be no solutions afterwards. She also don't post practice exams, which make us have no idea about how to prepare for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There aren't exams which, as good as that sounds, makes the final very scary. She doesn't really tell you what is on the final except that its cumulative but we cover so much material that you have no idea what to expect for it. The homeworks take a long time and, other than the book problems, you never know what they want as far as answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: bad professor, no solution for hw/quiz or everything, and have very unclear grading policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A lot of the times, her homework or class assignments are not from the textbook. How are we supposed to know things that are not even on the textbook? Never again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is smart and easy to talk to, but absolutely terrible at teaching. Everyone I spoke to in class, have no clue on what is going on. HW's are random questions, unrelated to the class material and does not really help you learn anything. Answers are not given out either, so you have to look for a needle in the haystack while reviewing for finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is good teacher but the class is hard. attendance is mandatory, she has participation questions to check . Had a group project. Has mini in class test which are worth a lot of points and are relatively hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Meh. Lectures were kind of interesting and she used them to address the practical implications of what we were learning. Only problem was she never actually teaches the material, and there's almost no homework. So by the time you get to the exams you'll have had almost no practice with the material and you'll just be expected to know everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were unique. This was one of the easiest classes I've taken at Purdue. if you do the readings and use her office hour she's really clear. the exams were three questions. two easy from the book and one conceptual. lectures were straight from the text. engaging but not too helpful (required as well)
Very boring and helpless professor
If you do the assignments that she assigns, you'll be fine. If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. Great professor! Helpful in class and out of class!

Teaches in an effective manner including lots of examples and lots of class participation. She even has some game show formatted classes. I strongly recommend this professor. She's probably the best I've had at Purdue and is extremely helpful with any questions you have.

One of the worst professors I've had.  Just goes through the lecture without any class participation.  Requires attendance even though nothing is really taught.  Although the course material did not help to make the course interesting, her teaching style made it even worse.

Attendance is required even though she teaches directly from the book and adds little insight to the material.  2/6th of lectures are either spent on worthless review sessions or quizzes.  Equations are provided for the quizzes but not random constants.
Very Boring Class! She basically just teach straight out of the textbook, and have quizzes every other week, the quizzes include a lot of useless material that you have memorize.

Currently taking this class. Half of the lab reports are graded on things that are barely mentioned in the lab or by the TA. The instructions on lecture or lab assignments will state one thing, but they're actually graded on very specific hidden criteria that is not mentioned at all, so it's impossible to somehow know what they want.

Dr. Hans is a truly incredible professor who loves the material she covers and cares about the people she's teaching it to. However, the TA's for this course really bog down the class, they grade harshly on things things they did not inform you on in lab prep. The lectures are absolutely fantastic, but the labs are a complete nightmare.

Wonderful class experience, she truly cares about the material (especially if it has to do with entomology). The class is very easy and if you pay attention in lecture you should have no problem with assignments.
Lectures were find but the labs and analysis report papers take long to complete and have very vague instructions. Terrible ta

She loves what she teaches and it shows through her lectures. There are not a lot of assignments and attendance was only mandatory during guest lectures. However her labs were difficult due to instructions being vague. My TA for her class would tell us to do one thing then grade completely differently resulting me getting points taken off on labs.

Directions and rubric for analysis reports and labs widely unclear and they grade super harshly. Experienced glitches with iClicker, talked to her about it and still refused to give me credit for showing up to guest lectures. Does not care as much for lectures unless they are about entomology.

Very knowledgeable professor and covers a variety of areas in forensics. Labs are pretty hard, and grading is pretty tough. I found the rubric's were not very clear and they aren't lenient with grading. Make sure you ask all your questions in lab/over email before completing assignments. She's nice, but I found grading tough.
my fav class at purdue. absolutely loved it. considered changing my major to forensics. super interesting, would love to take more classes with her if i have time

I absolutely loved having Dr. Hans as a professor!! I have never had a professor who truly cares about what they are teaching. It makes the class so much more enjoyable. I am taking another class with her and I'm so excited to see how this one will turn out.

Dr. Hans was a good lecturer and she clearly cared about the class subject. She is also very understanding that this intro class was a filler for a lot of people's schedules, so she made sure to have a light coursework. The class is mostly completion other than the quizzes, which you will have to read articles for. Do the work get the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Hans is a great lecturer and very nice who is easy to communicate with. However, I am critical on the cold case project itself. It feels like an unfair project to work on if you're given a victim that barely has any information about themselves. If you don't have any info, you get deducted a lot of points. Other than that, the class was fun.

Labs are somewhat interesting but the lecture material was so boring. I walked out multiple times because I felt she didn't seem interested in her lectures (unless it was about bugs).  She claims that you can TA for her but then as soon as you reach out she says "Spots are full". I wish there were other professors besides her.

This was a great introductory course to forensic science. There are quizzes and/or assignments almost every week and two projects, but if you watch the lecture videos you'll be fine. No late work is accepted but just keep track of the syllabus. Overall a pretty easy and interesting class!

Her lectures were always so interesting and it was cool how she has experience in the field. She has a textbook to use but she gives it to the students for free which was really awesome! I highly recommend her as a professor!

Dr. Hans is an absolutely amazing professor. She is super engaging and extremely passionate about her field. I took three courses taught by her and was a TA for two of her classes; I never had a dull moment! I would highly recommend taking her classes :)

Dr. Hans is hands down the best professor I have had. Her lectures are always interesting and she loves to tell us about cases she has worked on. Having a teacher currently working in the field gives great perspective and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students and the subject she is teaching.

Very easy class with minimum work (max 1 hour per week) and has interesting contents. Although keep in mind that there are very few criteria in homework/few questions in quizzes, and it's easy to get low grade (50 - 70) if you mess up a few questions. No EC opportunities, but it's easy to get an A if you put some care.

Dr. Hans is amazing and this was the most unique class I've ever taken. Dr. Hans is extremely qualified and has some amazing stories/experiences that she shares in lecture. The labs were pretty easy, especially if you put in the proper amount of effort. The analysis reports are kind of annoying while you are writing them, but the grading is fair.

This class was entirely online and asynchronous for me. You have a quiz or an assignment every week but if you watch the lectures, you will be completely fine. She does not accept late work no matter what but everything is due at midnight on Sunday. You'll get an A on every assignment as long as it's obvious you watched the lectures.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!  She cares so much about her students, gives you so many good stories of cases she's worked on, and overall is super personable. She doesn't require textbooks or has exams only online quizzes. If this is an area you are even slightly interested in, definitely take her classes. The labs are also really fun!!!

I have had two classes with Dr. Hans and will have more to complete my minor. I am so thankful that she will teach my future classes. She makes the course so fun and interesting yet you learn so much at the same time. You can tell she is passionate and loves what she does. She is hands down my favorite professor I've had at Purdue.

Professor Hans is by far my favorite professor at Purdue. Not only did she give amazing lectures (even early in the morning when I would usually rather be sleeping), but she really ignited my passion for Forensics. I am so glad she is basically teaching all the classes for my Forensics minor because I feel like I can really thrive in her classes.

By far the best professor I've ever had. Not only did I love the class, but I just loved going to class (even at 9:30 AM on a Monday) and getting to hear her lectures. She loves what she teaches and is always available to answer any questions.

Amazing professor! She really loves her job and her lectures are always very interesting. She also made sure the homework we did was directly related to work in the field of forensics, rather than a bunch of busy work. Labs are very clear and fun as well. Love that she's teaching all the classes in the forensics minor!
good prof, good class. very passionate about her field. She gave some very interesting cases that kept me engaged.
shes a literal queen. she makes the course fun and quite easy to pass.

I LOVE DR.STARR!! She's one of the sweetest professors that I've ever met and she truly cares about her students understanding the content! Her and her TA's do a phenomenal job of helping you as long as you reach out to them (especially in office hours). She gives tricky exams, but she gives many resources to prepare for them.

Dr. Starr is a great professor! I had her for both CHM 125 & CHM 126! She makes her class challenging but doable. Her tests are reasonable and are always related to class material with very few curve balls if any at all. Moreover, she gives plenty of extra credit for students to earn! Going to class isn't required, but counts as extra credit!

Dr Starr is amazing! The class is challenging but very doable. She explains the concepts well and is very helpful during office hours. Labs and homework were fairly easy, and exams reflected the material. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit, go to class and read the instructions on your exam!! Overall, a very fun and engaging class.

Dr. Starr is great. Go to lectures, it will improve your grade. There is no curve for any of her classes but the extra credit helps. If you study you can probably get over 100 on every exam. Study for the final unlike I did!

I love Dr. Starr. She genuinely loves what she does and teaches with passion. Use her office hours whenever you can because they are really helpful. She will help you with any confusion one-on-one. She gives extra credit just for participating in class. I loved 125.

Dr. Starr is one of the kindest professors ever. Her office hours are really helpful, and she offers to meet with students individually after exams. Her expectations are reasonable and fair. She makes class at 8:30 fun.
Dr. Starr is one

This professor's grading criteria is my biggest issue. The amount of homework was definitely manageable, but I did not like that the homework was due the lecture after finishing the homework material, I would much rather prefer the homework have constant due dates (Ex. Every Friday). I did not like that the lab reports were due 3 days after lab.

Dr. Starr is a great professor who is very passionate about chemistry and made lectures engaging. I looked forward to attending every class even at 8:30am. I strongly recommend this class for first year chemistry majors since it is a great class to build foundational knowledge.

Dr. Starr is such a kind person who truly wants her students to succeed. I had her for the whole year and she made freshman chemistry fun and helped make it less intimidating. She has very high expectations, but she gives plenty of resources to help and she offers to meet with students individually. You should definitely go to her office hours.
She was absolutely amazing, so intelligent and so kind. Tests were fair and she provided a lot of study materials and was always so helpful and approachable!
Actually an amazing professor. Class is easy besides for exams but office hours are so welcoming and a great resource!!

Dr. starr is a super caring and kind person, she really cares about her students, and she prioritizes  making meaningful relationships with her students. She have a very strong grasp of the material and has never not been able to answer a question. she gives a good amount of partial credit on the exams and all the exams are very fair. 10/10!

She is accessible outside class, offers helpful advice, and uses a clear grading rubric. Tricky exam questions are flagged in lectures. Attendance, though at 8:30 AM, earns bonus points. Exams aren't curved; most content is covered in lectures, with key lab and recitation topics revisited in the three midterms or final exam.

Class is pretty easy if you have taken AP chem if not, it might be a little harder, but there are so many opportunities to have lectures explained in smaller settings. Overall, she is amazing and absolutely love as a professor.

I had Dr. Starr over the summer and she was great. Even though the class was online, she still had regular times to meet with us and was very clear about what would be on exams. She was kind and supportive and I'm a little sad I couldn't take a course with her in person. She's probably the best professor I've had at Purdue.

CHM 126 has a good amount of assignments, but it also has many opportunities for extra credits. The exams this year were also exceptionally easy, being mostly short answer questions with points for work. Dr. Starr was a good lecturer but I did not go to class much because she went a little too slow. Her notes are great, very concise and neat.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Starr was a great professor. She really cares about her students. Her lecture example problems reflect what she puts on her exam. Her lectures can be fast paced, but she is easy to follow.

I loved Dr. Starr! She has high expectations of her students. The exams were very fair since most of the questions followed her in-class examples. I really like how Dr. Starr is passionate, down-to-earth, and very energetic; even at 8:30 am. She is super helpful and friendly in lectures and office hours. By far my favorite prof at Purdue!

Dr. Starr is one of my favorite instructors I have ever had. It is very clear that she cares a lot about her students and she makes an effort to connect with us. She's a very good lecturer and while she does go quickly through her slides, she is not difficult to follow. If you show up to class and put effort in, you should have no issue succeeding.

Dr. Starr is super accessible and incredibly kind and energetic. It is not hard to do well as the exam questions are almost always formatted exactly as the examples during class. She effectively prepares you for exams and assignments and is very fair with giving partial credit on exams. Great professor for chem majors to build base knowledge with.
She does a good job at keeping up the pace in lectures because this is a very fast-paced course. She's fairly new, but it isn't that obvious!

Fast talker with dense lectures in order to get through all of the CHM 129 content. Get ready to ask for help if you don't have a strong chemistry background - it's easier if you sit near the front of lectures or go to her problem solving sessions - but she's very approachable and very friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Starr talks VERY fast and it is sometimes hard to keep up with notes. It taught me how to take notes efficiently. The class is really homework heavy, but that forces you to study. Dr Starr was really helpful and friendly when I had questions. It's obvious she enjoys what she does. She provides a lot of in class practice problems that help a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors. She covered a lot of info very quickly but that was due to the course and not her. Lecture was kind of pointless as long as you knew how to do the problems but she made lecture interesting and it helped some. Def recommend her

Very fast paced lectures, but taught everything we needed. I recommend going to problem solving sessions as you get limited practice problems in lecture. This class isn't bad especially if you have previous chemistry experience as most of the course was review of topics I have already seen.

Chem 129 is a challenging course, but Dr. Starr made it very manageable. Despite the course progressing at an extremely rapid pace and the tremendous amount of homework, Dr. Starr explained the content in an understandable way and was very engaging with students. Take the course with her, instead of Conklin, as Starr is far superior in my opinion.

Her lectures are very fast. They have a lot of content, if you miss one lecture, you're screwed. Overall, fun chem labs and recitations, but lectures are too hard to comprehend. I recommend READING THE TEXTBOOK to do well in the class. Exam 1 and 2 were easy A's, while Exam 3 was awful. Study up for the final y'all!!.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: CHM129 is such a horrible class and genuinely sucks up at least 10 hours of time every week just to pass the class, however, Starr genuinely cares about her students and tries her best to make lecture understandable. If you have to take CHM129, try to be in her class or just at least attend her lectures instead of Conklin's.
Dr. Chen of Chemistry. Took CHM 116 over summer, but had a copious amount of experience with her. Genuinely cares about every one of her students.

Prof. Starr was a breath of fresh air when she took over the course following exam 2. She included a copious amount of practice problems in lecture which allowed me to understand the content. She has a problem solving session for additional practice and supports you in your learning if you so require. A great professor with an awesome attitude.

She is so sweet and it was a relief when she took over the course. It is clear that she wants her students to succeed and she gave so much practice to help us. She's also very nice outside of class and I always felt like I could reach out to her for help. I hope I can take more classes with her.

Very caring. Makes lectures like SI sessions rather than mindlessly copying notes. Be sure to make acquaintance with a few people around you to go through lecture problems. I was already very burnt out by the time she took over, so my opinion will be a little negatively biased towards 115 overall.

Professor Starr was amazing!! In general, she spent about half of the lecture going over the new content we were learning, and the other half of the class was spent doing example problems (very similar to exam questions). Also, since we only spent half of the class going over content, prof. Starr only covers what you truly need to know.

I absolutely loved Dr. Starr's class! Even if you're not the best with chemistry, Dr. Starr goes over so many examples in class and tries to explain difficult concepts in multiple ways. She's very approachable and even offers problem solving sessions outside of her office hours. I highly recommend this professor!

Starr was AMAZING. She would have warmup problems and would always do practice problems during the lectures. She was super caring and would ask us what we needed. I always felt prepared for labs and exams after her lectures.

She was an amazing professor during lectures and made sure to ask for improvements from the beginning. There were always practice problems to work on throughout the lecture and she made sure to go over the solutions in lecture, unlike some other professors. She also had a problem solving session on top of her normal office hours for extra help.
approachable

Professor Starr is amazing. She is very kind, and I felt like she really cared about our learning. Use the resources offered in chm 115 and the class really is not that bad. Make sure to study for the exams because they can be a little difficult if you do n out study, but one exam is dropped.

Professor Starr is awesome! The "Pet of the Day" started our lectures on the right path. She worked several practice problems and I felt very prepared to take the exams. She's very enthusiastic about the content and chemistry was the highlight of my day. Take Professor Starr if you can!
I enjoy Dr. Starr's lecture style and practice problems. She explains things in depth and writes notes on the slide with her apple pencil.
W
She is an amazing lecturer. Go to her office hours she is very helpful.

You're better off getting a mermaid to teach you how to make fire than you are to get any kind of professionalism, communication or help.  Her lectures are read from the slides which are in themselves entirely unhelpful in working through homework.

Lectures are boring and monotonous. Notes are inconsistent and vary from organized and informative to vague. Doesn't seem interested in helping students. Doubts asked during lectures are not met with explanations, rather with answers like "Just read the example again". Exams do not have review sessions and no effort is made to give extra examples.

She was terrible and went through lecture super fast, even the TA are saying she went through lecture too fast. I understood the lecture but don't know how to do any homework questions, it's super tough. I don't understand why she went through material so fast and the homework is that hard.
She has well-organized lectures and she introduced some useful data structures and algorithms. We have 14 quizzes and her grading is a bit tough.

Everything was based on tiny closed-book quizzes every week that made up your entire grade, and the quizzes were difficult too. I believe I learned algorithms just fine on my own but apparently this class doesn't think I did.

Her grading is a bit harsh, she either gives full or near zero in the quizzes. Her lectures may not be the best, but if you don't understand something, you can ask her any doubts that you have and she will make sure that you get the attention you need. If you reach out to her, she will help.

A very friendly and caring professor. Her knowledge in the domain of Data Structures is unparalleled. She will spend time with you if you don't understand the concepts. The tests/quizzes are graded a bit harshly. Overall, solid choice.

reviews.comment: Professor Pomeranz gives great notes with lots of examples that she does in class. Attendance is not mandatory at all. Homeworks are handwritten and from textbook questions. Some answers are on chegg but she mainly grades the hw for completeness and effort. Exam questions are from past papers. There is a possibility to skip the final exam as well.

I took 201 last semester and had to drop after the first exam. This semester with Pomeranz has been a completely different experience. She gives out note packets and is very good at explaining concepts fully and in a way that is easy to follow. Now I'm getting A's on my exams because they're straightforward and easy if you know the material.

If you attend all the classes, the course is quite easy as there are no exams. There could have been more programming assignments though.

Her policy of not partial credit does not make much sense. Other than that she's pretty decent. Assigns HW once a week, unlike other professors of 201. Her exams are the most straightforward, easy exams, that you can finish in one third of the alloted time, and have much time left to go over and correct math mistakes. I recommend her.

She is a bit on the rude side in class and definitely doesn't like repeating herself when it comes to rules, like getting up during class. But in all honesty her tests are some of the most straight forward and easy ive ever taken. Her class may seem intimidating right off the bat, but put in the effort and go talk to her and you will be fine.
No partical credit.Only four questions in the exam. If you make any error in the calculation,you will not get an A.
luckly  she don't take attendance

I found her class to be quite interesting (granted i had taken a class that helped me understand pointers prior to this). She gave out all programming examples some of which were hard to understand, but the T

She tries to teach C programming from an overhead.  She doesn't explain or actually teach.  It's just the same stuff, droning on and on every class.  You're better off taking somebody else.  The homework is terrible, she comments nothing, there are no standards, the exams...a joke.  A hard joke at that.  DO NOT TAKE HER.
Hard to understand.  Tried to teach programming on an overhead.  Worst ECE professor I've had.
terrible
THE WORST!

Great professor who is funny and genuinely excited about teaching phys. I don't really understand the negative reviews because his class is straightforward and lowkey so easy. Being mad that a professor goes off topic for the excitement of physics is wild, he still covers all of the content with time to spare. Class is so easy its almost offensive

Dr. Arnold is the most caring and hilarious professor, but his course is difficult (as expected with physics). There is quite a bit of online homework, written homework, quizzes, and lab reports, but exams make up most of the grade. Lectures are not super helpful, as he tends to get off track easily.

I enjoyed lectures as he was very friendly and he answers questions thoroughly. However the lectures felt like they were a bit all over the place. He was nice and knowledgeable but the class was hard to study for
Gives great lectures, answers all my questions.

I'm not sure why Dr. Arnold gets a bad rep. He is one of the smartest professors I've had so far. Physics is naturally difficult. But if you go to lecture, do the mini readings, practice exams and go to office hours you'll do good. The tests are not weighted heavily. And he is super helpful if you go directly to him with questions.

Some of those exams were definitely unfair. Labs never lined up with what we were covering in lecture and there was unclear expectations. I emailed him a question once and then he insulted the question in lecture the next day and berated me for 15 or so minutes in front of the class. That was unredeemable to me. Don't take unless you have to.

Passionate and good and speaking, but waits until the last 10-15 minutes of each lecture to go over what we actually need to learn for exams. Labs are unorganized and often have nothing to do with lecture content. Grading and exams are generous and straightforward which is the only saving grace.

Overall, this class needs a lot of work. It is super unorganized, and although exams are relatively straightforward, attending lectures and doing homework do not help at all. Attendance is only required in labs and recitation, but they were such a waste of my time since they were completely disconnected from both each other and from the lectures.

For what this class is, Professor Arnold would be the person to take this class with. He's funny and he seems to genuinely care about the content of this class. Whomever you take this class under, the class is lecture heavy, and you'll have to parse through which material you should know for the exam and which material is more there for context.

Class wasn't hard, but it was disorganized. This was not a great experience for my first ever physics class. He went off topic a bunch, and honestly you were better off skipping lecture and teaching yourself. The class wasn't super exam heavy, and there was either a small curve at the end, or they rounded the grade. Either way, I'm not complaining.

Professor Arnold is very engaging, but the lectures tended to run a little long and supplemental videos were a must. The class in general wasn't easy and covered a lot of content, but Professor Arnold did a good job of explaining the concepts at a level that could be applied.

Labs and recitations are easy—just show up for full credit. Lectures often ran late, never finished covering the content, yet still had time for iClicker questions. Homework was disorganized and took forever. The professor rarely did examples in class and overall, the course felt unstructured and very frustrating.

He was fun to listen to in lecture, but I do have a few small complaints. He acts like everyone has had a basic physics course before and doesn't really teach us the equations (I'd recommend YouTube tbh). He can be a little squirrel-brained. Which I found funny, but some may not like it. He was good overall, but struggled to stay on task often
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Rarely finished a lecture, so you're forced to watch his videos online. Gets off topic quickly and rambles about nonsense. NEVER does examples. Overall I felt like the didn't really get much from lecture and had to do a TON of work outside class to compensate.

Can get very off topic very fast in lectures. Talks super fast. Lots of homework, however it makes the exams worth less. Exams are not super difficult, however if you do bad on the exams your grade won't suffer much.

I loved him a lot more in 234 than 233 but I never didn't like him. He cares about his students and would hold long office hours before exams to study. He even explained a concept right before our final to a student in front of the whole class. Great guy for a class no one wants to take as a bio major. If you have to take it- he's your guy! 10/10

I really enjoyed his lectures and most concepts are explained really well. He also knows a lot about random science which is nice.

The only issue would be the fact that he often takes too long on lectures, but this makes them much easier to follow. However, this meant we sometimes had to watch an extra lecture at home to make up for it.

Ian is a great person, making him a great lecturer. He loves the subject and he loves students. He will often go off on goofy tangents during class but this eases the tension from learning the difficult subject. This was my 1st physics class, use orgo chm tutor on youtube to suplement you learning, study lecture content, youll be good.

Very good guy, very real. Physics for life sciences is never something us bio majors look forward to, but Dr. Arnold recognizes that and tries to make it a bit more digestible for those of us who don't like that physics is a university requirement. Exams are OK, lots of conceptualization, less memorization that I wasn't used to. Overall good class!

reviews.comment: ended up just watching lectures online because he talks SO fast. tons of points available so there's some wiggle room with exam grades (which is good because they are worded very weirdly). nice guy, but not the best lecturer if this is your first time taking physics.

Wouldn't have taken a class with him again if I had a choice. Exams are all multiple choice because he can't figure out how to grade free response questions efficiently. Because the exams are so multiple choice heavy, each question is worth like 5% of the exam, making it hard to do well. Lab is useless but lab TAs are chill and grade easily.

Dr. Arnold made physics a very pleasant experience, I had him for both 233 and 234. I highly recommend this professor, he is very lenient with exam grading and truly cares that the students are learning. The class itself is not as much work as I was expecting it to be and an A is a really reasonable goal if you attend lectures and recitations.

Dr. Arnold is a good guy but his class was just bad. Lecture material was poorly explained. Recitations and labs were almost never related to lecture content. Grading criteria was terribly unclear. Course administration, including assignment instructions, TA responsibilities, and exam grading, was grossly mismanaged. Overall, avoid if you can.

Dr. Arnolds lectures are amazing and he presents the info in a fun and clear way. His exams are tough, however, attending recitation and his review lectures help enormously. He does demos and sometimes talks about pop culture which makes learning physics enjoyable. Some of the labs are difficult, and one of them doesnt relate to the lectures.

He really does try his best I think, but with that being said try not to take physics with him. His explanation of fundamental physics is poor at best. Goes on theoretical tangents and lectures are not helpful in succeeding in course assignments or exams.

Dr. Arnold is a good professor who explains the material pretty clearly. He often starts lectures early and goes over, which was a little frustrating. Super fun/easy class to take esp during the Maymester! It was pretty easy with 3-4 concept quizzes a week, a discussion, and an exam. Exams are fairly easy if you have the online textbook. Dr. Ju is really nice and very responsive! If you have any questions/concerns, emailing him is your best bet. He's very willing to help as long as you ask!

Dr. Ju was a fairly forgettable lecturer. He uses Hotseat once or twice during class for attendance, so you have to show up, but you really don't need to pay attention. If you get the textbook, the online exams are a breeze.

great prof overall

Great guy, pretty entertaining and good at teaching the material. It's not overly complicated material, but I enjoyed coming to his class nonetheless.

Great class. Not overly hard, but you have to put in a lot of time to complete the homework. I'd recommend you have a decent handle on basic python before taking this course. He is a good professor, and a great course designer. I really liked the guy!

Ilias is Funny. So funny. Totally hilarious. His hilarity matters way more than you would expect. I didn't want to miss a single class just because he was so gosh darn entertaining. Great lecturer that goes over all of the concepts well. Very easy class which is comparable to basic physics. Just make sure you do all of the homework, which is assigned 3 times per week and typically consists of 3 problems. Ilias is very chill and does his job well.

Prof. Bilionis is by far one of the best professors I have had while at Purdue. Explains stuff really well. Easy class.   Textbook has the homework that you need to do, but you don't need to read anything on it other than to do the homework.

I have not finished taking the class (ECE 49595NLP) but he just announced 3 exams all within the span of 5 days. The first one is scheduled for 14 hours after his announcement. One of the worst professors and courses. The class materials are outdated and notes are unreadable. There does exist a course recording but you can barely hear anything. Often threaten to fail you if you do not satisfy some requirements.

caused by mislead and miscommunications

Does, in fact, manufactures "A"s. Super funny guy.
His lecture is very interesting.

His knowledge is immense, and lectures are great. He puts in a lot of effort into teaching, and making the syllabus the way it is. The examples and the problem sets are designed to give you an understanding and appreciation of how real world AI systems work. I also appreciated his passion for history in the field of AI/CS. Extremely bright man.

Great professor! Even though he only handed out 3 of the problem sets throughout the semester, he was still very open to questions and took time in getting everyone on the same page. Active participation is highly encouraged in the class.

More or less, the only thing you get out of the course is comfort with Scheme. The assignments are somewhat tough because you are not comfortable with scheme. Or else, it is like an introductory course. He spends a lot of time teaching scheme and in talking about historical perspectives. He goes through the AI part too quickly. The grading is easy.
He spent most of the semester teaching scheme. He never really got around to actually teaching AI. The class was easy, but a waste of time if you actually want to learn something.

so..he's a funny guy. a bit of a show off, but still an EXTREMELY knowledgeable guy. knows his stuff and how to explain it easily very well. his problem sets are tricky, but you will be able to ask for help and he does extend them on occasion.
Great professor!! Cares about students. Very helpful. I had an amazing time taking ECE 473 with him.
The course was well structured, with pop-up quizzes, regular quizzes, and exams. The instructor also provided notes that supported preparation and clarified expectations.

This course was fairly straightforward and manageable. All quizzes and exams are online, and the slides are posted in advance. There are occasional attendance quizzes, so regular attendance matters. The main assignment is a group presentation that makes up a significant portion of the grade. Lectures follow the slides closely.
The class is well organized and always stays on schedule, she's really friendly and approachable, i hope she could teaching other classes as well
She reads off the slides mostly, otherwise the class is very easy so no need to sweat. If you do have this professor though its one of the easiest A's you can get

The class covers basic aviation history and information about airlines. She reads from the slides and they are posted online and available to use during quizzes and exams. Very easy class that you don't need to ever go to aside from a short presentation that you do in a group. Overall boring but an easy A and nothing much to complain about.

Amazing professor if I could take this class again or any other class with her I would do it. Very clear with the grading policy and just show up to class and you'll get an A. Super lenient with grading too.

I took her SCLA 110 class and it was amazing. She really cares for her students and she always make sure everyone is being involved in the class. She provides really good feedback, gives lots of extra credits and kinda lenient about the attendance

If you are the type of person who shows up late to lecture and want to skip scla lectures, DONT take it under prof Kim. She is so strict about attendance and participation I would say . She made sure that she gives us extra credit and As at the end but she is strict and traditional.

In order to get an A and not get silly points deduction, answer questions frequently in classes even if it seems to have little connection to the question, attend some office hours to talk about your assignments so that you can make sure your idea of finishing the assignments will gives you full credit.

super casual (to a fault) about everything.  his lectures feel heavily improvised and include tons of derivations that do not help with hw or exams, almost like he is trying to show off how excellent he is at math.  pray I do not end up with him for any classes going forward.

In order to get what he is saying in lecture you have to had read the book. He just goes straight to it at light speed. Hardly ever helps besides some help in office hours. All his exams are extremely long, is like he does not want you to finish it.

Thomson is probably the best 377 professor. His lectures are typically very beneficial, but there is the occasional class where all you take from it is that he's good at math. Class certainly isn't easy.

Decent lecturer. Exams are not very representative of lectures or homework. Will not respond to email or help in any way.  Seems to not care about students.
greeat

He will NOT REPLY TO E-MAILS, so don't try. He is a good prof who wants to teach and not research. Only reason he is still at Purdue, is because he likes to teach the students. He is also BRILLIANT, but is also laid-back. He tests on the ESSENTIALS for ALL his classes.
Very helpful and clear in lectures. Exams are generally fair.
Tough class with tough concepts. Thomson is a great teacher though and easy to understand and follow. The good: two exams, no final. The bad: no curve (at least for my class there wasn't)
Good professor. Impossible to get hold of.
One of the best profs I have had. Very clear and great at explaining concepts.

Great. Clear and concise. Tests are perfect. made to make you realize a little trick and solve it easily and quickly but if you dont get the trick you lose alot of points. always has time for students. go to office hours.

Great. Clear and concise. Tests are perfect. made to make you realize a little trick and solve it easily and quickly but if you dont get the trick you lose alot of points. always has time for students. go to office hours.
Impossible to get a hold of, doesn't help students AT ALL
Awesome professor! Enough said!

Horrible. Why? 1. Barely follows the text book. 2. Doesn't release study material for exams until the day before. 3. It takes ridiculous amounts of time to receive grades. 4. Assumes that everyone goes to the office hours, and actually releases important information ONLY in the office hour (ridiculous).

Awesome professor. Unlike the typical CHE professor at Purdue, Thomson will sit down with a student for personal time if the student is struggling. He is a great lecturer and his lectures are very helpful. His homeworks are relevant and help you learn the material. Best CHE professor at Purdue, easily.

Proffesor Khan is knowledgable about python but his quizzes and exams are beyond the scope of what he teaches, and he gives you no resources to practice for quizzes. He also assigned a midterm the Thursday before spring break AND a lab the following Sunday. He didn't care that half the class had travel plans and made it an extremely difficult lab.

Dr. Khan is a good teacher; he explains everything pretty clearly and helps when you ask questions. Grading can be tough, but is mostly fair. The quizzes covered some material that wasn't covered in class, but for the most part weren't too bad. Take this class if you want to learn a lot about Python, but be prepared to work for your grade.
I really love the class. I personally learned python exactly the way I wanted to. All the assignments and quizzes reflected what is taught in class and what is needed for Industry.

I appreciate how Professor Khan comes to lecture with positive energy each time. His powerpoint slides are clear and helpful, and made it easy to follow along and complete assignments with. It's
challenging to teach such a large amount of students at one time, so I have a lot of respect for him for maintaining a high quality of lecture.

For a difficult class the professor makes sure to teach everything step-by- step and in very great detail. Professor Khan most definatley cares about his students and it is apparent he wishes nothing
but success for his students. It really helped that we worked together on assignments and projects with partners - helped my team skills.

This course helped me land my dream job in data analytics. The content is super relevant to the industry (realized this more while interviewing) and the way the professor balances theory (in lectures) and practice (through live demos in class) is awesome. Had tons of learning and am grateful to Dr. Khan for teaching this course the way he did.

Professor Khan is very knowledgeable in the course content and usually checks in with students during lectures to make sure we are following along or have any questions since the content can be
a bit technical sometimes. The assignments aid in understanding the content
as well since we are able to apply the skills talked about and demoed in class.

This professor is not at all active with homework, projects and assignments. Till the very last moment, you will be clueless as to what needs to be done. He considers that all people are python experts-whatever he teaches is so simple. You will be swamped with exams, quiz, assignments-all at once and there is no learning cos then AI to the rescue!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was very well organized and I appreciated all the live coding the professor did in class! I learned so much better in this course than I did in my first Python course, and I'm so thankful!

I believe the professor worked hard to teach us about Python. He took the time to ensure we understood the subjects he was talking about, and why the code we previewed did what it did. This
class has taught me a lot about python that I have saved and can implement later in life. The professor is a great guy who wants to see us succeed.

Dr Khan is the typical bad professor. He shows little care for his students and it is shown through his stale lectures. He assigns assignments inconsistently. Some assignments were given 2 weeks before they were due, others were 3 days. Everyone bombs the exams and quizzes and relies on the curve. The scores in his course reflect that no one learns

Professor Khan was very knowledgeable yet equally disorganized. Quizzes and assignment dates are not outlined in the syllabus and are seemingly assigned at random. Lectures are very informative but extremely boring. I sent him three emails over the semester and received zero replies. Classmates have had similar issues through email and Piazza.

Dr. Khan is a really nice guy and a great professor. 388 isn't super test heavy compared to other classes such as math, but it is a pretty difficult course. He teaches it well and if you pay attention you will learn!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most disorganized and unprofessional professor I have had at Purdue. He was always late to class, no class plan, changed grading policies, quiz formats, and exam structures halfway through the semester. Communication was poor, completely unreachable by email and Piazza. Didn't have a course schedule and was rude/hostile to students. Avoid Him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He refuses to make his office hours work for the 50% of his students that all have the same course from 3-4:15pm (3-4pm office hours). It's almost dead week and this has not been resolved. Inaccurate and vague tentative schedule, good luck getting an email response, and coding questions on quizzes and exams are done in brightspace on lockdown.

Disrespectful and condescending to students asking questions. Locked students out of class for being late yet shows up late to his own class very frequently. Incredibly un-engaging lectures so get ready to teach yourself to code. Assigned both a final project and a final exam during the designated quiet week. Poor, disorganized professor.

Very generic lectures that do not keep students engaged. Makes it very hard to be involved in a power hour class. Homework is much more in-depth than lectures, leaving students to wonder how to complete their tasks. Gives little to no time on quizzes and exams where you are expected to write code. Poorly planned class structure as well.

Dr. Khan is an outstanding professor who made learning Python for data analytics both fun and practical. His clear explanations and real-world examples kept me engaged and motivated throughout the course. He's incredibly supportive and always willing to help - his passion for teaching really shines through.

Professor Khan is the worst professor I've ever had. He is late to his own class. He is harsh/belittling when people ask questions. He doesn't respond to emails. He responds to questions with annoyance. He grades incredibly late considering 70% of the exams are multiple choice. He has boring lectures where he makes mistakes. He needs a new career.
This prof is Not at all reachable, doesnt have clear path in class. Doesnt even bother replying to emails. Not fit to be a professor

Not very helpful or respectful to students. When I asked for suggestions regarding the midterm, I was roasted in class and accused of not studying well. He refused to provide a sample solution for the sample questions. Meanwhile, his own slides were not helpful as the questions on the exams were much more difficult than the lectures.

I really like the way he teaches, I think he is very good at what he does, but you have to go to his class everyday, yes he doesn't provide a schedule but he answers questions in class and his office hours are super helpful.

Probably the most disorganized and terrible professor I have had at Purdue. He does not have a course schedule and seems to make it up as he goes. The HW is incredibly vague but will have unknown grading criteria. He also seems to hate helping students or clarifying his assignments outside of class. His lectures are boring and difficult to follow.

This is unfortunately my 3rd time having Prof Khan, each time gets worse. He is very unclear in how many and when assignments are due, all instructions in assignments are disorganized. He fails to communicate with students outside class, doesn't grade in a timely manner, and is rude to students when they ask questions. + He's a bad teacher!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Lectures were structured well and he was very funny. Professor Lipton is very nice and cares a lot about students learning. I will say though that this class does not go into much depth in the why and how reactions work, which is why I think people struggle in CHM 26605. Definitely would take again.

Dr. Lipton was an awesome professor. His lectures were engaging, and you can tell that he truly cares about helping students learn. Although his tests are tough, he's very available to help and is great at explaining tough concepts. I would take another organic chemistry course just to have him as a teacher again.

Not the best communicator during lecturer but his resources make up for it. Lectures were often rushed and without going all that deep into the "why" and "how". However, if your goal in the class is to get a B or lower, this surface level knowledge will do. If you want an A, it will be through your own effort, as with really any college class.

His teaching style is phenomenal! He is a great communicator. There are not a whole lot of grading opportunities, it is mostly homework and exams, So, I would prepare at least a week in advance to study for exams, since they will ultimately determine your grade. He welcomes question openly, so don't be afraid to attend office hours/raise your hand!

Dr. Lipton is amazing. If you make sure to complete the practice exam and review it with him on review days, I can guarantee at least a B (I'm only a senior in hs). People told me that Organic Chemistry was really hard, but Lipton made sure that it was easy to understand and minimized the amount of memorization required for the course.

I loved Dr. Lipton! He is very good at breaking down complex topics. Dr. Lipton is also down to earth and understands his students. Be sure to attend his lectures and participate in iClicker because the extra credit will save your grade! Tests are hard, but not impossible. I would highly recommend taking a course with him.
Dr. Lipton was great!  The tests are exactly like the practice and he cares that his students are learning.
Fun and very good at explaining the material

Despite being regularly late to class, Dr. Lipton made up for it with his lectures. He makes organic chemistry fun and interesting to learn about, and explains complex topics in ways that are easily understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lipton is one of the best professors at Purdue, there's a reason he wins teaching awards year after year. His class is not curved though, he makes up for no curve with copious amounts of extra credit for answering iClicker questions in class. YOU WILL NEED THESE POINTS. Always do the extra credit exam questions, it can only help your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Lipton is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. He explains the  material concisely and stays on top while moving at a comfortable pace. However, paying attention is essential. The test are very hard but there is always an extra credit problem at the end of the exam that could change an entire letter grade on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best Chm professor so far.
He is great and friendly!!

Had Prof. Lipton a couple summers ago for Organic Chem II for Chemical Engineering. Really nice guy. Accommodating. He taught from these huge powerpoint packets he gave  out in class, which I thought was helpful. The exams and problem set material were fair. Good at explaining things in a hard chem class. Enjoyed having him as a professor.
Great teacher, plus his TA Matt gets me hotter than a thermite reaction.
Great teacher, material is quite difficult but he's very helpful if you have questions. Always in his office and the textbook for class is amazing.
Agree with the comment about him being "snobbish."  Lipton is very intelligent and speaks clearly.  He is always on topic.  Homework and exams were definitely very difficult.
Really Good!!!
overall pretty good prof. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow; he covers a lot of material, and most of the time is just spent copying down what he writes. Exams are a bit hard
Very nice person. Extremely smart, too!

Tends to make errors in his notes and can kind of be a snob sometimes. Also seems to never have enough time for students, but is helpful enough during office hours. I also agree with the person who made the exploding head comment-his homework assignments are absolutely monstrous!

Teacher was fun, organized, and crammed as much material into each class as possible.  However, the material was VERY DIFFICULT, to the point of making people's heads explode.  You need to already be talented in Organic Chemistry to take this class.

Great teacher, He has some great stories.  The only negative is sometimes it felt like his lectures would cover so much material that I spent all my time just trying to copy notes without really knowing what I was writing.
Very organized, very good teacher.
For the sake of future students, she needs a new job.

Teacher has a remarkably difficult time speaking english for having lived in the united states for 20 some years. She moves through content very quickly and often struggles to finish all of the slides before class ends.

The class itself wasn't too bad, but the lectures are a little hard to understand, especially when there's a lot of information crammed into one slide. Attendance is also required for every lecture, so you can only miss two lectures.
Must watch videos outside of lectures to stay afloat. Hard to understand her. Final was pretty easy.

The lectures are boring, but the best way to learn the topics are through the homework anyway. My only critique is that the labs are unnecessarily complicated. Most of the time the homework is just that weeks lab with a few extra steps.

I have a lots of programming experience and am a CS major so CS 176 was pretty manageable. If you do not have programming experience, this class is pretty hard and its good to learn some python before hand. The lectures are pretty useful and she pretty much tells you everything you need to know for the exam.

Worst professor I have ever had. Her slides contain several typos and misinformation. I brought her slides to the TA because they weren't making sense and the TA agreed that they were completely wrong. She shows up late for lectures and will yell the whole time. She will scold students for leaving for any reason including using the bathroom.

If you cannot understand a standard Chinese accent (for whatever reason), don't take this class. If you are normal, she is not a bad lecturer remotely. If you choose to pay attention, you will learn everything that you need to. Stop blaming your failures on a lecturer.

This professor is absolutely terrible. Reads directly off the lecture slides, and if anyone asks a question, her response is to simply re-read the material louder. I learned more from watching python tutorials on YouTube than I did from her. She commits academic terrorism...do not take!!!

This 100-level Python class was supposed to be "beginner-friendly," but Xiaojin Liu will personally escort you to the ninth circle of coding hell. I have never been so utterly confused by a class in my academic career. Lectures are mandatory. Xiaojin Liu performs academic terrorism. It's 50 minutes of her reading slide answers aloud. Avoid Liu.

This is easily the worst class I have ever had the misfortune of taking. The "teacher", if you can call her that, genuinely seems to hate her own students. How you could yell at the mic every single day at 9:30 am for no good reason is simply beyond me. The lectures and labs tend to be more gibberish useless busywork than the slightest useful task.

The only problem that I had with her is that i dont always understand her language. However, I think her slides explain stuff well. In general, this course exams are not typical coding questions. You NEED to study past exams and study the textbook because a lot of material comes from there.

The professor teaches at a nice pace and uses lots of examples. Attendance is mandatory no matter the instructor you have. She barely has an accent (especially compared to other professors), and you can easily get a good grade if you review slides and participate in labs.
Gave me a migraine each lecture, is obnoxious and reads off script and asks unintelligent questions that they seem to believe helps students learn but only serve to confuse the lecture hall

Honestly shes not as shi d as people say but her lectures really are not very great. Shes not understandable, she has an accent but its pretty clear honestly its just she only reads off the slides and it can be pretty boring.

Ok this is my first prof review because I have to put some respect on Xiaojin's name. I have literally 0 c experience and I found her lectures very understandable. Her accent is really not bad at all and I have a really hard time with accents usually. Her lectures are actually engaging and I find myself not even looking at the clock. Great Prof

The worst professor I've ever had no competition. She yells at the mic and gives me a headache. I dread going to her lecture every time I do. Also has a very thick Chinese accent and really hard to understand.
Is there a way to program her so her teaching isn't bot mode
Inflexible and imposes assigned seating for lectures which are mandatory.

Terrible prof, attendance is mandatory even though it doesn't help reinforce material. Simply reads off slides and her way of trying to answer questions is simply reading the material louder. Very unclear lab and HW prompts and the autograder doesn't make it any easier. Don't take her class if you don't have to.

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had. Her lectures are mandatory, which i can understand because if they weren't no one would show up. You would get better results by spending the semester watching python coding tutorials on YouTube.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had the misfortune of having. Lectures slides, quizzes, homeworks, and even exams are always riddled with typos and mistakes, the TA's are all useless, and the professor is barely coherent, yells into the mic at 8 in the morning, shows up late, and poorly communicates important information. Avoid if possible.

I had no coding experience before this class and it was so hard to go through can't believe i clutched an A but my god presentations, practice exam and even the final exam are riddled with mistakes. Attendance is mandatory and having her in the morning screaming into the mic is just a recipe for a headache

Do not take from her if you can. She has you going to every lecture and uses iclicker, which would not be a problem if she actually taught the material. The powerpoints that she has are full of typos and do not actually explain how the code works. The exams were difficult but I would say she was very transparent with what is going to be on the exam

I felt this course is not freindly for beginners.
+) I asked TA to fix my quiz grade (bug), but they said I must email professor.
But she is not responding to my email for 2 weeks, so I got 0 for a lecture quiz even I attended lecture.
+) They only have one previous exam to prepare final; even some answer was wrong
DO NOT TAKE IF YOU VALUE YOUR MENTAL HEALTH AND SANITY AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!

1 of the most horrible classes coming from a person with no coding experience. She's pretty unprofessional (late to class sometimes and has slides with incorrect information that are INCREDIBLY frustrating to deal with) and hw and labs sometimes use concepts not covered which is time consuming to deal with and just so annoying

For a person who has barely coded in Python and wanted this class to help lay the foundations, the professor didn't help with anything. She always screams at 8:30 in the morning and doesn't show how the code works, only reads the materials of the slides. On top of that, the midterm has an average of just over 50% showing how she teaches.

She posted maybe 1 due date for the homework on bright space. Her lectures are terrible and it just feels like she is yelling at the class. Most weeks she doesn't even get through all the of material that is needed to do the homework and lab.
Awful, avoid at all costs

i would not recommend this class to anyone, especially if you do not know how to code at all. the professor is loud at 8:30 am in the morning, screaming into the microphone and requiring everybody to attend. class is heavily based on her powerpoint slides that do not really do much. ive had to learn on my own, hoping for the best. midterm was crazy

lectures were mandatory and subpar at best. spent most of the classes just yelling, student body is heavily skewed as some people have a lot of coding experience whereas others have none so our midterm results were all over the place. wouldn't recommend, avoid if u can. prof is very nice and understanding just not very great at being a teacher.
umm she's smth

She has provided us with NO guidelines for our midterms, the content is not helpful at all. Even the TA's don't know what is going on more than half of the time. She does NOT reply to ANY emails, and neither do the TA's, she doesn't talk during lectures, she SCREAMS.

Honestly, this is not a beginner friendly class.
Just Awful
Worst class I've taken at Purdue.

She has a heavy accent that is very hard to understand. The class is at 8:30 in the morning, and the mic is too close to her face. I can't hear anything she says in class. The teacher rages when students leave, repeats unnecessary things, and stutters like she's trying to sing rap god. Vote her out.
TERRIBLE DON'T TAKE CS CHANGE MAJORS RIGHT AWAY PLEASE GOD DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS PLEASE IF YOU WANT TO SAVE UR SANITY AND UR MENTAL HEALTH AND UR EARS.

Heavy accent aside, she makes no sense in class. She reads off the slides, and never answers questions in office hours. I watched One Piece in the lectures and had a blast. You could look up everything in the textbook and do better than rely on her lectures. Her lectures are required because otherwise, no one would go.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed her class and I leaned a lot. Will definitely take another class with her again.

CS176 is taken by non-CS majors & AI majors. I had programming experience before so many concepts were familiar to me. This class is ran in a similar way to other CS classes here (required attendance for lectures/labs and expected to use a lot of submissions/test cases for the hws). Noticeable increase in difficulty in the 2nd half. She's friendly

This professor is very hard to understand and does not elaborate on the course material in a meaningful way. There are also very few clear instructions on assignments and starting the course generates an abysmal feeling of unpreparedness which does not change much with time. If you need to take CS 159 at Purdue pray you get a different lecturer.
Professor Liu is great in explaining concepts. The class is very well organized. Grading is fair.

She's not horrible, but the pacing of this class is bad.  I have never coded in my life, so the pacing in this class was rough, I do not feel she really understood what it's like to never see have seen code, then immediately have to write a program of nums from -100k to 100k.  Very nice, decent amount of extra credit, and the class isn't too hard.

Lectures are utterly useless yet still required. Actually going to labs is utterly useless yet attendance is required or else you will get a 0% on the lab. If you have a question, you have to use this garbage forum website that the professor doesn't even check, so it's a lot of TA's saying they'll ask the professor for you. Take a diff CS course
Can't teach
The only good thing I can say is that it was a nice lecture to take a nap in because attendance is mandatory and you don't miss anything by sleeping.
Terrible. What more can I say

I ended up having to utilize my academic accommodations and this professor fought me about them. Additionally, I needed to take an incomplete for the class and the professor was terrible with communication and timeliness. The homework takes ages to do and the grading software is very strict and doesn't make sense if you've coded before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class itself is a waste but easy. Attendance is required but reading the unnecessarily long slides is equally as helpful as her lectures. I paid attention maybe 30% of the time. There are "discussions" which are just clunky group assignments. Sometimes hw or exam questions were worded in a confusing way which was annoying but generally easy.

The class was quite interesting, and the homework and tests were easy, however, I feel like they could sometimes be worded a little better. Attendance is very important, as she does Hotseat every class, and the points add up at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you can, pick Crum as a professor because he writes the exams and the course book. Liu makes her own slides that do not follow along with the course notes book you have to buy for the class. Lecture attendance is required, and I found the lectures unhelfpul. Exams are a heavy part of grade. Use Boiler Exams to practice and you will do well.

I actually really liked the way that this professor taught; however, I took this class online so my experience may be different than others. This class was kind of difficult because I have never coded before, and I was put into a group that barely put in any effort. Boilerexams is definitely a life saver for this class!
Cannot understand her lectures at all
She is incomprehensible during the required lectures; spend them doing homework instead and use Boilerexams to practice for tests as she just reads out of the textbook during class.

I didn't think much of her as a lecturer until we had Crum substitute for us and he was infinitely better. Upon reflection I realized that her slides are hard to follow and don't really follow the notes packet you are supposed to buy at the beginning of the semester. She's not terrible, but do what you can to get Crum or another professor.

Gotta be one of the worse professors here. While all the other professors teaching CS159 use a packet to go over all the information, she creates her own slide shows that exclude crucial pieces of information that will appear on the exams. Her presentation slides are filled with giant paragraphs of information, making them useless to follow.

reviews.comment: Explains curriculum very poorly and lectures are not interesting and hard to follow. Very boring overall but CS159 isn't too hard in general
Does not know what she is saying in lectures. Repeats unnecessary things. Would not have her again.

She's not as bad as some of the reviews are saying, but definitely not good either. If you can switch, I'd recommend it. She reads of the slides and sometimes doesn't finish. She also doesn't allow people to leave early either.

This class genuinely feels like trying to retake 1st grade math but you have to use the 27-step process they teach kids now. "IF" statements? Never heard of her. Leaving during class? She will call you out in front of everyone. Definition of a level 100 professor on a power trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The professor read straight off the lectures which would be 100 slides per week. It was extremely hard to pay attention because her teaching is pretty boring. reviews.comment: DONT ever take this class if you think it is an easy GPA booster, while you have zero knowledge of how the Internet/computer works like you do not have a desktop built by yourself or you don't even use Discord lmao.

Liu is a sweet lady, but she doesn't teach the material and instead just reads off the slides.
Read off slides that can be read within 29 minutes

She is almost always late or barely on time to her own lectures. She has several errors in her many slides and homework assignments.

reviews.comment: Liu feels like a nice person but does not qualify to be a professor. She had to make attendance mandatory for students to show up to her class. Do not take
Read off slides that could be read within 30 minutes

Lectures are cryptic, and difficult to follow, moreover, the homework is exceedingly difficult for the content taught in class, which is in itself barebones. Students are forced to rely on their parents/eternal sources to teach code. Midterms will be a major pain if you are a beginner, prior experience is a must. She's nice, but a bad instructor.
