reviews.comment: One of the worst professor in CS department. Nothing more than reading slides in lecture time. The lecture, besides, really rarely helps the project. We have to figure most of the things by ourselves. The only homework this semester, I got 7 out of 15, and none of my friends in this course got better score than me. NEVER take his course.
Boring and monotonous, reads slides that are not from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although He does rely On The slides, he does a great job of elaborating on them. He explains things really well and gives good demos too. This course was easy for me since I have prior programming experience. Without that I might have struggled more in the beginning because he went through the basics pretty quickly (since he taught BLK).
I really enjoyed playing Facebook Tetris. His voice was monotonous and he relies heavily on the slides. His beard was on point tho.
He's amazing!!!!!!

Like all other comments. He read slides that is not from him. Perhaps because it is not from him, he don't know the answers for the quiz. It feels like student don't have the right to know the answers. Be prepare not to TALK during ICLICKER!!! We are not allowed to discuss with other students and with him. Watch out for mandatory meetings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He read presentations in a very small voice and monotonously. He gave emails to students which only say we need to meet. Prepare to do a lot of homework and lab without gain anything in the lecture. Basicly you just learn by yourself through the lecture and the book.
He likes to rush through the slides and leave students with tons of confusion. Then, he throws super hard labs and homework out and expect students to figure out on their own.
He has low energy when teaching in class. He teaches like he hasn't fully wake up yet. The coursework are heavy and he doesn't give enough clarification on assignments.
his lecture is boring as hell but exams are not too bad
very boring lectures. very tough on grading and exams are aweful
He just read through slides that are not even his. He didn't even know certain parts of the slides when student ask him questions.
LOTS, LOTs of work and does not know answers for quizzes and is very very boring. Does not explain well and is very rude and strict.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He refuse to tell students the answer for iclicker quiz. It would be beneficial if he can solve the iclicker question just like any other professor
Update...i don't know why but i start to like him...
He just read through PPT most of the time. However he is still a rookie professor. Hope he will do better

Very monotonous and boring lectures with quizzes at the end of most lectures. However, the midterm is easy as long as you read all the slides a day or two before the exam. It was primarily about vocab. The group project is what you make of it. Pick something hard? You're going to struggle. Do pick something that sounds hard, but is actually easy.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Nice guy but boring lectures. Nonetheless, class is rather easy granted you complete the assignments on team and do somewhat well on the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Turkstra is a great guy who just hasn't learned how to give a good lecture. He is often monotonous and simply reads slides. The 1 exam given in the class was just 60ish questions taken straight from around 400 slides. Boring, but he grades fairly, and if your group works well together this class should be no problem.
most boring lectures ever, genuinely want to kms everytime im forced to attend, not even necessary u can learn everything on ur own

The exams were a bit hard, but there was no final. Had to get a Raspberry Pi for the lab but the project with it was easy if you researched a little bit. He does talk a lot, and most of what he does explain isn't as thorough on his slides so its hard to go back to after lecture. The extra credit is pretty easy to do tho.

He is not bad but he is a YAPPER...you will not get anything from the lecture. He knows what he is talking about but it hard to catch on so just review on your own. As for labs, quite confusing and you will have to buy a raspberry pi. the TA are also quite harsh on grading so my best advice is to go to office hours for help.

Prof. Hiday is an amazing lecturer and most people who rate him poorly are just mad they actually had to try. Be aware exams are relatively tough but won't decide your grade completely. There is a buffer window of around 3% extra credit which is extremely obtainable.
While I do believe the prof is very knowledgeable, he has got to be the most boring lecturer ever. Literally reads of slides with way too many bullet points and tests on the most niche topics ever

Overall enjoyed the content taught in this class. While lectures went a bit fast, they were manageable as long as you looked over notes after class. I enjoyed how he would explain each concept in depth if you had any questions. The labs were very interesting and included fundamental computer topics that were touched on in lectures.
Worst course ever

Great professor for CNIT176, though he does move through a lot of material very fast in lectures, so taking notes is recommended. Good sense of humor and very accommodating, though the TAs for the lab sections grade according to their own scales, and some grade much harder than others.

The professor himself isn't too bad. The lectures can be boring but he answers every question and doesn't hesitate to clarify anything students are confused about. The course can feel overwhelming and confusing, mostly because it covers a wide range of topics only at a surface level. Labs are graded harshly, but it wasnt something I struggled with.

He's clearly passionate and knowledgeable about IT, but he's really hard to follow during lectures. Labs, in my opinion, were pretty easy but if you're not careful, you can mess up one small thing and fail them. How well you do in this class is heavily dependent on your TA.

This class is so boring and the labs can be super difficult if you don't have any experience with Linux. Labs are basically learn it yourself and the exams are pretty difficult but not worth much. However, you can easily get a passing grade if you do all of the assignments but the grading is pretty strict.

I NO prior experience going in and I was shell shocked. That said, I learned a lot (I still am getting an A) but NOT from his lectures. Prof is smart but hard to follow. Exams are not worth much, but be prepared to do a lot of extra work to learn the content if not familiar, especially for lab when working with Linux. TA's were a hit or miss

Larry seems honestly like a nice guy and he knows what he's talking about but he talks... and talks...and talks. It's hard to grasp the concepts and you're better off just teaching yourself. Exams are insanely lecture heavy but you can legit fail them and still do well in this class. TA's are straight up awful and unhelpful.

The problem is not the course itself, the content is quite interesting. But the way it is set up makes me want to drop out of his class. Beware of tough TA grading in labs and a very messy course. On the other hand, the professor knows what he is talking about but rambles on. You'd think an intro cnit course can be properly structured.
Great professor. Great course. Great reintroduction to a major I switched out of then back into.
bad professor

Lectures are extremely hard to grasp especially for an introductory class. TAs are inconsistent and can grade harshly on labs with little to no guidance. Exams are worth barely anything which makes it easier to get a good grade in the class

Class is easy. There are multiple opportunities for extra credit, the assignments overall don't require a lot of work and are quick to complete, and the information is pretty basic in terms of computer architecture.
prof hiday is my spirit animal. hes great. don't listen to all the freshmen salty and ungrateful that they had to try in 176. i would've killed to have hiday as my 176 prof

Hiday just reads off the slides and it is very hard to grasp material. Labs have little to no correlation between what is being taught in class and exams. TAs are harsh and inconsistent with grading. Would not take again.

I attended all the lectures but still felt lost most of the time. The class is an introductory class, but it didn't feel like one to someone with no previous experience. There's 2 midterms, and the timing of the 2nd one was so poor. Exams are very lecture-heavy. During lecture he reads off the slides with no extra information added on.

Professor Hiday is nice but he just talks and talks. It was hard to pay attention or even understand the lectures, and he speaks as if everyone already has a basic understanding of how a computer works. The labs don't entirely line up with what is being taught in lecture. Overall, the class is pretty easy, but I taught myself the material.

-Hard to understand in lecture. 
-Labs and lectures dont really go together like in other classes. 
-An 80 and a 89 are apparently both B so you dont need to try that hard.

The class overall wasn't that bad. Ended with an A and I didn't know anything about computer architecture coming into the class. For the lecture material I strongly strongly strongly recommend getting the optional textbook. I realized that's where he gets all his content and images from so it's a good guide. Lecture's boring but he's nice.

CNIT 176 was a pretty average class; lectures tended to be boring, and the labs were pretty fun. Hiday was a nice professor, but I felt it was hard to understand his lectures because he didn't explain his lecture slides well. The exams were hard since there was not any review material online. Be sure to follow the formats the TAs want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hiday is a solid professor, but your opinion on the class will likely depend on your TAs and experience working with computer architecture. Hiday mostly just reads off the slides, but is always open to talk to students and answer questions. 176 is pretty unorganized, and your final grade will likely depend on if your TA is chill (Shoutout Nathan)

Hard class, definitely not an intro. Second Exam was extremely difficult and did not have anything to do with the notes. Takes a lot of outside work, you need google for this class. Would not take again

When I took it was his first time teaching this course. Read off the slides and occasionally went on tangents that were incredibly difficult to follow. Lots of busy work. Coursework and tests are easy enough though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good lecturer, even though he just read the slides sometimes. Some exam and lab information weren't covered in class, Google is your friend. He released grades for materials very late. The TAs took forever to grade labs and could grade harshly sometimes. Some extra credit was available on labs, attendance, and homework which helped.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hiday is a cool dude, but his TAs ruined the course. The TAs graded unnecessarily harshly and were never on time with their grading. Over 70% of the course's labs & assignments were graded the week before final grades were due. Had to go to his office hours to appeal a wildly unfair grade, but he was very understanding and fixed it promptly.

He just read off the slides in class it felt like, there was minimal expansion on the material. There was stuff on the exams that wasn't in the notes or anything he said in class. The labs weren't too bad.

I liked Hide's class, but this was the first time he has taught 176. Sometimes the lectures didn't match the labs, so take good notes and ask TA's for assistance! Lots of in-class participation, but if you skip class you can still submit it afterwards. Don't recommend skipping though, a lot of info is shared verbally instead of on the slides.

The (rare) times we go over easy topics he slows down but any other material that is difficult is incredibly sped up to the point where you need outside resources to understand any of the things going on. You can have full understanding of lecture topics, homework, lab, etc. and still get a bad grade because the exams are made so difficult.

Professor Ngai is a good professor & hands out chocolate in lecture. Exams are difficult, so be prepared to study a lot. People are regularly confused, don't ask questions, and then complain when they do poorly on exams. Ask questions, he will answer them and wants you to learn! This is orgo, it is not intuitive for most and grades reflect that.

Bro truly couldn't give a gaf about you. He has failing exam averages and he just says that YOU could be doing more to do well rather than reevaluating his own teaching methods. He should not be teaching an orgo class designed for CHEM MAJORS if a good chunk of people are currently failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ming acts caring in class, but destroys you on every exam then proceeds to gaslight you to show up to lecture and office hours. Could use more Christian values when writing exams. The TAs convince you that you don't belong studying chemistry, and refuse to help or explain material. If you're a chemistry major, life gets better after this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ward is a great guy who is always ready to help students with any problem.

I enjoyed Dr. Ward's iteration of the Data Mine seminar, and found him and the entire Data Mine staff to generally be pretty helpful and run the data mine in a straightforward way. I have him again this semester for TDM 102, and it's the same smooth sailing.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took TDM 101 to complete half of the computing requirement for the college of science and so far worth it. The seminar projects are fun and you get to drop 4/14 projects. They take as long as you want (not really long) and Professor ward is a great professor who can help you quickly.
I took TDM 101 and 102 two years ago so some things might have changed. The videos are very helpful and the workload isn't that much. The Piazza forum is very active and he is very helpful on there.
This class requires much more effort than it should for a 1 credit course. Students are expected to know information that is not communicated in the weekly instructions for the projects.
very helpful
His videos are very informative! He has a kind personality, so just talk to him if you need any help.
very easy and helpful instructor :D
Hes like the LeBron james of professors no glaze frfr
Great teacher who's passionate about what he does and open to students coming to him. His TDM program is great even for those who never coded.
Responds to Piazza messages quickly but is very stubborn and is not very understanding.

A really upbeat and considerate professor who makes things as easy as possible for his students. Very generous with grading, including 4 project drops, easily accessible through Piazza, and very clear at explaining all concepts necessary for the class. A diamond in the rough that is Purdue Math/CS. Would recommend to anyone of any experience.

Dr. Ward was a great professor for The Data Mine. You could go in with 0 coding experience and still get an A. All of the skills we used in the weekly projects were very well explained by Dr. Ward. For a few of the projects, he just gives you the code straight up.

Dr. Ward provides many videos and resources in The Examples Book to guide you through your projects. The class is very straightforward, and the drops do help you alleviate any concerns about your grade. He is also pretty chill and humorous during seminar.
it was okay
Great professor provides detailed videos for most projects and is always willing to help and answer students questions

I am gonna be super honest. This class is so easy. I went to maybe 2 or 3 seminars and skipped the rest. The projects he guides you through but you still have to do some work but the TA's are always having office hours to help. The outside events are annoying and I did not get much out of them rather than a pain to do. Great GPA boost.

I enjoyed watching Prof. Ward's videos. He is funny, is a great teacher, and does an amazing job of answering students' questions. Professor Ward is one of my all-time favorite professors and I would gladly take a class with him again.

Dr Ward is one of the best professors I have had during my 3 years here. He is a bit quirky at first, but he is a fountain of knowledge who knows the subject well and can communicate it clearly and efficiently. Sometimes his projects are challenging with unclear directions, but he is always open to helping. Dr Ward sets the bar for a great teacher
Dr. Ward's weekly videos for the projects were perfect. They explained the concepts needed for the answers without giving away answers brilliantly.

WOW. Dr. Ward blows me away every semester I've had with him. You'll be hard pressed to find a more committed, dedicated man. He cares about his students, and will go out of his way to help. Great, great professor.
Super enjoyable teacher! The dude is a real character!

Dr. Ward is the best professor I've had at Purdue in my 3 years thus far. He is so caring about his students and goes above and beyond to help you. His material can be difficult, but is very applicable to the real world, as we work with real-life data. He has a great personality and is lively in seminars! He is the embodiment of a great professor!
A very helpful and approachable person. The material gets messy sometimes, but if you seek help you will be fine

Dr. Ward is a very caring a fun personality that is always willing to help students. The projects are sometimes difficult depending on your understanding of R, but they are constantly improving directions to help students. Also use piazza as Dr. Ward or TAs are always responding.

Dr. Ward has done a fantastic job setting up the Data Mine, but some students struggle with the reverse classroom environment. Make sure to go to office hours and look at the projects before class so you can ask questions during your meeting.
An absolute character.

Dr. Ward is one of the best profs you'll ever have; genuinely cares about students; lectures are online and problem sets are done in class for a grade; you will be prepared for the exams if you understand the in-class problems; lets you have a say in exam format; will go to any length to help you (for real, he's a great person and prof!)

All the tools to succeed in this class where given to you at the start. We had four years of past exams and problems to work on. Everyday we would practice the material for homework and then work in small groups in class. I wish that every class could be like this. Dr. Ward was always super caring and available to help whenever you needed him.

Dr. Ward will go out of his way to make time in his busy schedule to meet with students. The class was set up so that lectures are done at home through his videos and then the homework is done in class. This setup works amazingly for class! I often joke that Dr. Ward should make all my classes like this. I highly recommend taking his classes!

Best Professor ever, every class should be taught the way he teaches his class and we'll have a generation of ingenious folks. Humble dude who loves his students and his job, his standout quotes are: "The learning is happening", "Professors are paid to help students, call or text me whenever you have a question and I'll help".
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: One of the most amazing Professors I have ever taken. Very helpful and really cares about his students. If you put in the effort you will do well and make sure not to skip lectures. Highly recommended!

The best statistics professor I have had the privilege of working with.  Is an incredible mentor to many students in the Statistics Learning Community and his general students.  Always willings to discuss class, school, and future endeavors.  If you can take his class you will not regret it!!

Dr. Ward operates on the backwards classroom. You do lectures online and take notes the night before, then you take group quizzes in class.  He takes questions straight from the notes posted online and the quizzes done in class and puts them in his tests.  He completely allows you to customize your own tests (to a limit).

Dr. Ward is one of the best professors at Purdue. He genuinely cares about his students, he is very funny, and is willing to help anyone, when something is not clear to someone. As an added bonus, he puts all of his lectures online, and his explanations at approaching problems are superb. I recommend Dr. Ward to anyone.
He's definitely one of my favorite professors! Incredibly cheerful and eager to help whenever!
He's Great.
Good Professor. Very helpful and approachable.

He's probably the most helpful professor I've ever had. He cares so much about students understanding the material that he will literally do your homework for you, and then explain what you were doing incorrectly.
Difficult to understand and communicate with.

Prof. Mitchell is a great scholar but not a great teacher. She's obviously very knowledgeable in what she teaches and the lectures tend to be pretty interesting, but she isn't very good at answering questions or giving feedback. Her TA (when I took the class) was honestly more helpful. She also treats this level 100 course like a level 300+ course.
Nice enough prof, and class is interesting, but take another history class for your gen-ed. tons of work, and harsh grading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is obviously very well educated, but her course is not very well organized. This class was really interesting to me and I enjoyed most of the assignments but grading criteria and lectures are very vague and can be hard to navigate. TA office hours were very helpful in understanding grading criteria.

Her lectures were vague, disorganized, and often not related to the class work. Her grading was incredibly strict and she provided little feedback on how to improve. She seemed to be looking for specific things or ideas in our writing, yet failed to communicate what they were.

Unclear in her speaking AND her assignment requirements. Wants you to read every week, expected, but if you don't understand the text to the letter in your report, you will be penalized. Gives poor feedback, has lectures with almost NO substance, and contradicts herself often on her rubrics. Not a bad person, just a very bad teacher/professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is terrible. For a course with no prerequisites, I expected an easy, engaging history class, but the assignments barely relate to the lectures and the due dates are disorganized. The grader expects citation and background knowledge at a graduate level, which is unreasonable.

Professor Mitchell is very passionate and loves her subject however her assignments are difficult! Grading criteria is very confusing and she doesn't answer questions very well. I found the Geary book online so save yourself some money and look up the textbooks beforehand. I found myself dreading all assignments. VERY VERY WRITING HEAVY.

Silvia Mitchell really cares and has passion for this class, and it really shows. However, the class is really unorganized and often times you will be doing assignments and readings that have almost nothing to do with the lectures for the week. She also doesn't answer questions very well, she's quick to cut off your question and answer it wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taking this class for fun a free elective. Always have loved history and thought it would be a fun and easy class. Was I wrong. most strict, hardcore grader I have ever met/ Lectures are mandatory but pointless as she just shows a picture of some random map and drones on and on and on about some randomness that has nothing to do with the hw.
Not the best with assistance
I don't like her cuz u have to give very specific answers. Means including every single detail and if ur not. Then you are just wrong. And she doesn't talk with her students respectful enough.

Not one of my favorite professors. She does a good job lecturing but can be very short/rude with students when asked questions. Her class was easy and you can do well without attending lecture as long as you read the book.

Worst teacher/professor I have ever had during my time here on Earth. No disrespect to her accent, but I cannot understand half of the words she says and half of the time she just goes on and on about nothing. Her powerpoints are horrendous and are just pictures of maps that she rambles on about for 25 minutes before switching the slide. FADE HER!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is obviously an expert in her field and an amazing resource for the historical community. However, her teaching style is nothing short of abysmal. She constantly goes off on unrelated tangents while simultaneously grilling you to answer questions in the same manner she would. Great for research help; avoid her classes.
She is not afraid to dig into you, which can sometimes be helpful. Other times it is not. She often does not know what you are asking, and classes are filled with silence.

Dr. Mitchell did a reasonable job in organizing the material for this online course, however, assignment dates would be changed because they were not opened at the correct time so scheduling was difficult. This intro-level history course was graded much harsher than any upper-level history course I have taken at Purdue.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rude and not willing to help students that ask for it

I had the displeasure of having Professor Mitchell for SCLA 101. I'm not pursuing the Cornerstone certificate she strongly advised out of fear of having her or anyone like her. She was always reminding us that she is a historian in a WRITING class where all we talked about was the Italian Renaissance all semester. Worst class I have taken so far
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell assumes that everyone taking HIST103 has a substantial background in medieval history. She jumps right in without explaining anything. She's a tough grader because she looks for very specific answers, and if you don't have them you will be wrong (even on opinion questions). Lectures go on forever and are very confusing.

Not even through the first class I was shot down for everything I said. If you dont explain it EXACTLY how she wants it, even if youre right... youre wrong in her mind. I dropped out of the classes not even 30 seconds after.

Silvia is a below average teacher. When asking questions, she has one specific answer in mind. If you cannot relate to her then you are wrong. She does a poor job of understanding that not all students have the same historical background. She also just tells you to format the paper correctly, but doesn't say what the "correct" way is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is my third semester here at Purdue, and I haven't even gotten a grade yet in her class, but I can say without a doubt that Mrs. Mitchell is the absolute WORST professor that I have had since being here! Literally anything and everything about her as well as her teaching style is negative, I can't think of a single positive thing to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely bad grader and writer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized teacher and makes a lot of mistakes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She shuts down students if they are answering a question. She was disrespectful the whole semester and her syllabus wasnt followed at all. She randomly had 3 quizzes at the beginning of the semester and didnt have any the rest of the year. Would not have this professor again.

The reading you have to do is mandatory, yet she just clams "read this book for tomorrow" not what sections or parts, yet she doesn't expect you to read the whole book (as you read one book every two weeks or so) Lectures often are confusing and jumbled. The overall organization is absolutely horrific.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class to cover a Krannert requirement. It was only 4 weeks long, so it was very fasted paces. There was a lot of reading and the assignments took a fair amount of time, but Dr. Mitchell is a fair grader and it the rubrics were clear. The quizzes weren't terribly hard and you could use your notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her lectures are fast-paced and often doesn't have an outline. She and her TA's grade easy, though. Just show up, take notes, ask questions, and skim the outside readings. Exams are one essay given to you a week in advance (possible 2 questions, she picks 1).Don't need to study until you get the questions. Just write it out a few times and practice
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Mitchell. She is very passionate about her topics, and it's nice to have a professor that really wants you to learn. Sometimes her lectures can be all over the place, but if you say you don't understand, she is more than willing to explain it again or in a different way. 10/10 would take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I thought I was taking a medieval course. Instead, I got to hear about Hapsburgs in the 1600s and the renaissance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a fair grader, and the book is absolutely necessary for this class. Attendance is taken each day by a TA, but there are very few assignments, and what assignments there are take quite a while to do (more than a day). She's a very nice person though and tries to engage the classroom very actively.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is horrible. Jumps all over in the lectures, gets confused while lecturing, never explains religion, claims she studies politics but never says how, tons of historical errors, makes examples of students if they mess up, tons of History channel videos, doesn't follow the textbook and even gives information counter to it. Avoid her.

I love Sylvia!! One of my all time favorite professors. As long as you participate in class and meet with her outside of class she's super laid back and willing to work with you. I was sick and missed a lot of school, she literally couldn't have been nicer about it. Plus she's passionate about what she teaches to boot! 10/10

Professor is passionated and interacts with students a lot. HIST 312 is a really tough course tho, all the way from Italian wars to Spainsh succession war. Lots of readings and paperwork. But if you participate, its a pretty good course.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell treated this course like it was a 500 level course. The homework needed extremely specific answers to be given credit. The book was really hard to navigate. Mitchell however was understanding if you needed an extension for whatever reason and gave you good feedback on project ideas. This class isn't a GPA booster nor easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible class I've ever take never take this class

Fairly easy grader, but really boring lectures. All exams are free response and she gives you the questions a week before the exam so you can prepare (basically easy A on exams if you prepare for it!). Only had 3 quizzes throughout the semester (2 take home) and one group project (easy A as long as you use reliable resources).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If you're interested in learning very much at all, don't take a class with Professor Mitchell.  Her class structure is very unorganized, with no consistency of assignments or lectures at all. The essay tests are fairly difficult to prepare for, as the lectures are all over the place and have no central themes at all.  Very easy pass, however.
Best history exams I've ever taken. Essays about analysis of the events rather than ambiguous multiple choice ones.
She is pretty easy going, and you can convince her of how to conduct her class. Her tests are essay tests however, which can be pretty hard to get an A in if you don't read the assigned readings.

Professor Mitchell may come off stern, but she is a fantastic professor. I have taken more than one class with her, and would gladly take another. Participating in class is a good way to better understand Professor Mitchell, and the material. She truly cares about her students and is extremely knowledgeable on all the material.
Professor Mitchell is quite the experience..
She is a tough grader and it is hard to get an A but she is also a good teacher and the material is well taught.

She never once went into detail about any individual topic. We covered the entire period of Viking invasions of Europe in a five minute span. She's more interested in giving the Feminist perspective of history than any perspective of history at all. We had to read several irrelevant novels and use them to write essays.

No clue what was going on the entire semester because this professor is horrendous. Very biased and an unnecessarily tough grader for papers. She never explains anything clearly. Took this class expecting it to be the easiest for my semester and it ended up being the most difficult. I'd rather drop out than sit through a semester with her again.

she needs to learn how to teach. shes hard to understand and she grades papers like an English class. she takes off points for grammar and spelling. she thinks shes funny but the only joke in the class is her. you have to read the book to pass this class.

Her pop quizzes require that you complete all the reading. The average exam/ essay score is in the b-/c+ range, and only about 20/180 people score better than a B+. She will embarrass you and make you look dumb if you try to answer her questions. I have seen students cry after answering her class questions. This class is NOT fun or easy.
hard to understand and hard to pay attention to during class. have to read the book to know whats going on

Dr. Tucker is an amazing lecturer. He takes time to meet with all of his students, and genuinely cares about his students. His classes are very useful, and you learn great skills that will help you in your future career no matter what that is.

One of the best professors I have had. Truly cares about his students and the material in the class. Dr. Tucker is a very intelligent and genuine person, providing many thought-provoking opportunities in class.

I've had Dr. Tucker as an instructor and advisor all throughout my college career. He is a compassionate, caring professional. He's always willing to work around special circumstances, and understands that sometimes life happens. He shows expertise in his material and is a phenomenal communicator. You won't regret taking any of his classes!

I love Dr. Tucker. not only is he passionate about what he teaches, but he also cares about the students and makes an effort to get to know them. 152 was a fun class, with some reading and some grammar exercises. He makes the material relevant to the students.

Dr. Tucker is a great professor and advisor! The lectures were interesting and Dr. Tucker encouraged participation and questions. He was always happy to help and give advice, and he truly wants everyone to succeed in class.
Dr. Tucker is pretty cool. He lectures pretty well. Any quizzes we had were pretty easy. He also really wants to help you do well.

Everything about him is great, except his teaching style. He goes way too fast, sometimes to the extend that you find it hard to catch up with the material and end up being confused. I have taken two classes with him and this has happened every time. Lectures very content heavy.

During lecture he appears to be a fun and relaxed professor. Attend his office hours and you will begin to see his true colors. He is condescending, conceited, and almost holds palpable contempt for you if you are visibly struggling to understand a topic.

Although he curves grades I would not recommend taking him. Had to teach myself.

Prof. Milisavljevic is an amazing professor with super engaging and funny lectures. He has a very clear understanding of the subject matter and conveys the information to students very well. 

If you attend all the lectures the homework and tests aren't bad - he tells you exactly what to study and where to find resources.
Great prof, funny but good lectures

Dr. Milisavljevic is one of the best educators I have ever come across. He is clearly passionate about the subjects and in learning with the students. The extra credit is worth it. Homework should be done ahead of time and be sure to study for the exams with a group. It would be beneficial to take Calc III beforehand.

He's interested in seeing students succeed and he's really nice. Definitely do the extra credit if you can. The tests and homeworks are really hard, and even if you study a lot there's always going to be something unexpected. It might be easier if you take calc 3 and are in a STEM major, which I wish I had known before

Clearly passionate & always trying to find new ways to help students learn (some classes done in virtual reality!). He also has a great personality & sense of humor, making his lectures super fun! The material is difficult, but he does his best to help you learn. One of my favorite teachers for sure!

Fantastic professor that very obviously cares about both his subject and his students, one of my favorite lecturers at Purdue, and taking more astro classes to learn from him again. Graded on 4 homeworks, a midterm, and an exam, all of which took some time and effort, but definetly worth it.

This is my second course with Prof Milisavljevic & he has been terrific for both! He has such energy, loves to crack dad jokes, & includes unique teaching methods like supplemental VR sessions! He encourages class participation & teamwork. His passion for Astronomy is evident!

Loved this dude's energy. Very enthusiastic about what he was teaching, always smiling, very interactive with his class. I didn't find it too difficult, the clicker questions are super important for learning concepts so I'd recommend going back and reviewing those before exams. Definitely recommend taking with Milisavljevic!

It's a physics class, so it's generally going to be difficult but Prof Milisavljevic is amazing and is very engaging. All lectures use iClickers for questions on topics in class, but he pretty much gives the answer in hints. Weekly homeworks that take some time but they boost your grade if you do well.
Great energy in lecture, explains difficult content clearly and with examples. Grade is heavily dependent on exams but there is usually a curve.

Had him for a class I really struggled with and I definatly think if I had it with any other teacher I would have failed. Would watch many of his lectures online and they were actully intresting. 10/10 would recommend

His lectures always woke me up in the morning with wild and wacky demonstrations. Attendance is mandatory and judged by iClickers, but at least the lecture is fun. He accepts questions and gets students involved in lecture demos and halts lecture by hiding until a brave soul answers his question. He is cute and spunky in a young dad kind of way.

Dr. Milisavljevic is ADORABLE and INCREDIBLE! He makes physics so much easier (but it's still hard, FYI), and will actually make you laugh in class. iClicker questions are attendance points, but he is flexible if you need to miss a day for a good reason! Study the past exams and the iClicker questions (LIKE REALLY DO THIS) and you'll be fine!

Prof Milisavljevic is a great professor, he teaches the material very well, and answers all questions thrown at him in lecture. He also gives about 2-3 iClicker questions each lecture, and normally reveals the answer before closing the poll so most people get it right. He also explains that iClicker for those that don't understand.
This professor is young and gives very lively lectures. Lots of iClickers in lecture and recitation--which are worth a ton of points. Past exams were basically useless to study for his exams.

Milisavljevic was not just a fun lecturer, but good at teaching the material. He also writes his own exams that are heavily based on what he said in lecture and in homework. Very understanding of our other workload too. Overall great, and if you see he's teaching the class and you know you need it, go ahead and sign up, you won't regret it

Honestly, he's gotta be the best physics professor I've had yet. He does his best to help out as much as he can, keeps the mood light, and teaches the material well. He's a pretty funny guy and cares about his students. No complaints at all here, only praise.
He's a really funny, smart professor that you can tell cares for his students. The subject is not incredibly difficult, and he makes it as interesting as he can and explains it as best he can.

Very energetic and funny guy, who understands the material extremely well, yet articulates it in a manner that a first-year can comprehend. Lots of analogies and demonstrations to aid understanding. Brought his nephews in for a demonstration of an idea. I became jealous and now wish he was my uncle.

Prof. Milisavljevic is a funny professor, and often tries to lighten up the mood in our morning lectures with jokes and sharing his research in astronomy. Though the topics covered aren't easy, he does explain concepts well and often invites students to participate in demonstrations with him. Overall most students in the class agree he's great.

Physics 220 is a difficult course if you haven't taken AP physics in high school, but Milisavljevic does an amazing job of demonstrating what he is teaching and if you talk to him at office hours it is obvious that he cares and wants you to understand the material. So many professors just talk, Danny teaches.

Prof. Milisav is a genuinely fun person to be around. He understands how difficult the material is and uses many demonstrations during lecture to try to best explain the content. Plenty of resources outside of class as well. Labs are a bit ridiculous, but that is out of his control. The final exam curve brought me up to an A from a B.

Here's a professor who WILL ROOT FOR YOU if you genuinely put in the effort. Very accessible and friendly. HW and lab assignment every week though neither have anything to do with exams. Exams very lecture based! No extra credit. If you're struggling, the book is your bff; not mandatory tho. There are help rooms open 2X/ week for extra support!
I was lost from the first till the last day. I ended with a 61% and still got a D+ tho. He rounds quite a bit
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: great professor though phys220 is tough.

Given the inherent difficulty of the course material, he does a fantastic job of relaying the information in a way that is easy understand and apply. He does a good job of keeping the class engaged, and he does a great job of making lecture worth your time. If you attend and participate lecture and recitation you will do well in the course.
I really enjoyed Professor Saqib teaching. Course was well organized and he clearly cares about the students learning
takes time to know student, great lecturer!

The lecture notes are informative, detailed, and easy to follow. He explains common mistakes and why they're wrong, making concepts simple to grasp. Attending his office hours will help you 100% ace the class. He genuinely helps you succeed. He makes learning fun, connects with students, and his passion for explaining the concepts shows up!
Top 1 professor oat. Genuinely feels like he cares about every student and it is clear to me that he is passionate about what he does.

Really unnecessarily difficult. Take literally any other eaps 100-level course. There's hours of lecture and readings every week and the homework is unnecessarily time consuming for what the class is. It's really not bad, but compared to the other intro eaps classes it is ridiculous.
I hate this class, way too much work for a 100-level science class. Multiple lectures to watch every week, and each lecture is around 40 to 60 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson is a great teacher who is very passionate about her class. The exams for this class are very intensive for a 100-level course. Studying the weekly wrap-up quizzes is not enough to do well on the exam, but the positive is that there is one exam drop.

A harsh person. Class is easy but she doesn't really want to give the tough student an A. She just try to find some small error then she can curve your grade down. Make you feel confused and disappointed, you only have a little step behind A, but finally you can't touch it.

She is definitely a good teacher, the grading criteria is so clear and keeps tracking your progress.
The lectures are mandatory for credits. The labs are long but easy to get a high grade.
The exams cover too much material sometimes, but she keeps the average above 80. And she is open to drop the lowest score, which is definitely good news.

She was an excellent teacher, and the class itself was laid out in a way that made everything pretty easy to follow. She also gave many opportunities to boost your test grades if one didn't go well, which I appreciated. The only downside was the labs, which were super long and honestly pretty boring.

It feels unreasonable to have in-person exams covering so much material, especially the third midterm. It's surreal that professors expect this level of commitment for a 100-level Gen Ed course. My friend who took it last semester had a much easier experience
Completely terrible
Took this class online it was very easy. There were a couple times where I got points off that I thought were unfair, but that's all I can say about a professor for an asynchronous class.

Overall this class is very easy and you should get an A in it. If you do your work and pay attention to the lectures it is very easy. I will say there is a lot of busywork that got annoying, but other than that it is easy. Take advantage of the extra credit.

Do not take the EAPS 104 online class with her, it is a RIDICULOUS amount of busy work for an 100 level class. One of the most annoying classes I've taken and it is all unnecessary assignments that don't actually teach you anything.

I've had Prof. Nelson for multiple classes and she always makes it clear that she cares about her students and values everyone's time. She's a good lecturer too - learning new lecture material was my favorite part of the class. The labs were tedious and sometimes boring, but graded leniently. HWs and exams weren't hard - overall good class.
i was a bit scared at first for her being known for assigning lots of reading, but honestly, as long as you have good lab mates and work ethic, this course should not be difficult.

I enjoyed the content and she's very helpful. The class itself is very heavy on homework, likely because it's an online course. I probably wouldn't take a class like this again because of that, but I've enjoyed what I've learned so far.

I took EAPS 104 as an elective so that i could get one of my mandatory credits, but the work load is very heavy. there's a quiz every thursday and on every sunday there is either an exploration that takes 1-2 hours or an exam. i spent 2+ hours everyday taking notes/reading. I had to drop it because I had no time for other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS! This was one of the easiest classes I've taken, but I still managed to learn a lot. The workload was very manageable and there was only 1 midterm. Lots of readings and videos to watch, but they're all relevant and helpful to the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I very much appreciate that Jennifer is laid back. I think she understands that most people are only taking EAPS 327 to fulfill a requirement outside of their own major's department. Homeworks and projects are straightforward but can be time-consuming.
She was awesome in lectures, and made me feel like going to lectures was actually engaging

Many people think this will be "minimum effort A" classes like many other EAPS10X classes, but you need to put more work than that. You have to read every week (with the online textbook costing $40) and take weekly quizzes, every 2-3 weeks you have an extra assignment or essay due. A lot of EC opportunities though, and she communicates well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this as an elective, so much homework. Professor was OK though.
If you follow the guidelines and rubrics for each assignment you should be golden.

Professor Nelson is a great professor and the class is extremely manageable. There is one one hour quiz per week and two essays in the class and that is pretty much it. The quizzes are easy questions straight from the book. It is an asynchronous class, but the amount of time you need to put in to do well is not high.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took EAPS 104 as an elective class but never thought I would have to spend this much time on it . There are 30 question quizzes every week. Plus a quiz extra every three weeks. Not to mention you have to write 1000 character long essays and reply to a classmate's essay with 500. She assigns way too much work and avoid taking her course.

You can tell that Jenny really enjoys her field. It shows through her effort put into making the class. However, the class is SO heavy. A LOT of assignments, which are very long. Quizzes are every week and those are also dense. It's a good class, but there's lost opportunity since the material is engaging, she just lacks making the most of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor. He is kind, understanding and extremely helpful. As long as you explain what you are facing, he is very open to help you, give extensions. You will do great in class as long as you reach out for help. Probably one of the most understanding profs i've ever met at Purdue.

The course's lectures were exceptionally well-delivered andpacked with info and that made complex topics easily understandable. However the sheer amount of homework was quite a lot requiring a lot of time investment to keep up with. Overall, it's a highly educational experience for those willing to dedicate effort to reap the benefit.

The class covers a lot of topics and it is hard to connect them as they are wildly different. The course is meant to introduce different architectures and is mostly manageable. The learning experience under his instruction proves to be quite demanding. Some labs are easy but after the first few you need to know some linux to work on Pi projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class overall wasn't too difficult. The labs took a bit of time but could easily be completed with a bit of effort. The lectures were extremely boring. I've taken a class that is similar to this one that is taught by professor Adams who does a much better job of sounding like he is interested in the material he is teaching.

I believe this class is the issue, not the professor. I'm sure he knows his stuff well but is not a good lecturer at all. Some of the labs make no sense and sometimes don't relate to the lectures at all. You have to get lucky with your TA, mine was terrible at grading and explaining. Extremely disorganized class if you don't know what you're doing.

Prof. Nadig is a nice person. He is incredibly intelligent and has done a lot of research in his field. That being said, he is a poor lecturer. His lectures are incredibly boring and it very hard to learn from him as he doesn't do a good job of explaining the concepts. The class itself is manageable but learning from him is difficult.

The class is easy but I have had two friends kicked out of her class for getting sick. she is not understanding about these things at all and does not accept doctors notes. you better be in the best health of your life while taking her class. she will make you take it again if you get the flu and are out for a week
A fantastic instructor. Grades you according to your existing skill level, so if you put effort in you'll be fine.

Ms. Dubikovsky is a very kind and passionate professor. She is always willing to help students understand material and will help with any questions you may have. She is particular about attendance though. I don't believe you can learn the material for her class properly within being in class so I understand why she's so particular about it.

The class is easy but just know that excused, sick absences with doctors notes are still counted to your absences limit of 4. Don't waste your time getting a doctor's note if you are sick. The professor will not level with you if you have 4 absences even if you have doctors notes for them. Also, if you are 10 minutes late, you're marked absent.
This class was actually not bad. As long as you attend class everyday and participate you will be fine. She sometimes plays favorites but overall she is very sweet and a decent professor.

Nadya is so sweet and wholesome, even though the class can seem a bit weird at times. Just leave behind your shame and dance, sing, and play the recorder with her and you'll have a good time. This class has helped me to feel more prepared to be an elementary teacher even though it can feel awkward sometimes. Have fun!

Nadya comes off strong and the class can seem cringey at times, but she is the sweetest woman and grows on you quickly. The class has been the one that I feel has prepared me the most for being a teacher in the future. Don't take yourself too seriously and just let yourself have fun dancing and singing with everyone.

She is absolutely lovely. She's very passionate about music in the elementary classroom and it shows with how interactive and unique her lessons are. She was very understanding when COVID first began, and continued to offer excellent feedback and teaching despite the challenges it brought on.

take anyone but him for this class his requirements are not clear whatsoever and most of the assignments that we do in class has nothing to do with marketing management. he does not lecture properly and the exam is built on very niche things where he says that there maybe multiple good answers but we have to pick the best one AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

I created a RateMyProfessor account because I'm shocked at these low scores. I agree that attendance was highly graded and that he took a long time to grade things.  However, he was usually clear that with grades we would all be okay after the curve(even with the class doing poorly on the pop quiz). Overall, he was a nice guy and a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pretty harsh with grading, and there's lots of assignments that he never gets around to finishing so they just linger on Brightspace ungraded. You have to purchase access to this business simulation website for 60 bomboclat dollars and run trials with a team. He's chill most of the time but also incredibly unenthusiastic at presenting/lecturing.

Very disorganized and difficult to learn from. Lectures are mostly random case studies with sloppy explanations and no slides or structured material to follow. It feels like you're teaching yourself most of the time. For a 7:30am class especially, the lack of organization makes it a waste of time. Would not recommend
Dry and boring is all I have to say. Ended with a 91.8 and got curved down to a B+ and he just says grades don't matter in the real world. Avoid if possible

Disorganized, unclear, and poorly run. Grades posted so late you never know where you stand. Midterm was 13 MCQ with 8 answers each in 20 min and felt designed to trick, not test. Teaching is outsourced to student debates and the syllabus totally ignored. Final project timing is unrealistic. Professor lacks basic course management skills. Avoid.
Sad Sad Sad, the worst professor at Purdue.

Every class feels more like a waste of my time. Very off script and has us doing random assignments that are not applicable to the class outline from Purdue. His grading is subjective and just based on ranking your group against others, and there is very little guidance besides trying to figure out what he may be interested in. Avoid.
I too would like to state that the one star reviews keep getting deleted. sus...

Dr. Nowak is an awful professor. Do not take this class. He grades unfairly if you disagree with him, and missing more than two 7:30 AM classes drops you a letter grade. Most students scored under 40% on the midterm, and you must write a paper to get the curve. I would also like to say that 1-star reviews keep getting deleted- avoid at all costs.

His grading system is inconsistent and highly opinionated. Quizzes are completely subjective and there is nothing you can do to effectively prepare for them. Class averages are almost always below a 50%, and he continually blames students for his historically low-class performance.

Dr. Nowak is disorganized and doesn't know how to prepare or educate students. He also goes off-script, ignoring the course outline in the Purdue catalog for what this course is described as. He makes snide remarks to people who don't agree with his viewpoints, which are opinionated and HIGHLY bleed into his grading style (which is never linear).

No syllabus, no lectures. You're intended to grasp random concepts from different Harvard business cases that groups present on but that he never lectures on. Very unclear what concepts we're supposed to be learning. Class average on our 13-question midterm was below a 50%. Grading is slow. Said he was a "type-B" professor, meaning disorganized.
Awful. No practise questions for the midterm exam.

Dan is a good prof. Extremely strict about AI and attendance (miss more than 3 and you drop a letter grade for every absence). There are a LOT of group projects and discussion posts in this class, but if you just put effort into it he grades nicely. Also, one surprise pop quiz that the entire class failed lol
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Nowak says that he has experience teaching but honestly, I'm not sure that he does. His course is disorganized and he doesn't have a clear grading criteria or a clear schedule for the course. It felt like he was making everything up on the fly and nothing was planned ahead. Lots of group work and some projects were not relevant.

I liked Prof. Novak, he had a very large turn around from the beginning to the end. In the beginning you could tell he was a bit overwhelmed by being a new professor at a new school, but by the end he was comfortable. He's a nice guy, fair grader, and gives everyone equal opportunities. If you don't like group work, you won't like the class

I took 410 and 410 with him. Uses his own book which is exactly what he teach in the class, and both are not very helpful. Doesn't really answers the questions students asks (doesn't like being questioned repeatedly). Few questions on homework but they take forever. Grading is pretty easy though. He is basically the typical old physics professor.

(PHYS410 H Mech I is now defunct) For intermediate mechanics, Nolte teaches from his own textbook, which is adequate but not ideal (the good part is beyond the scope of a non-honors class). When answering questions, he tends to talk in circles until the questioner gives up. Class is difficult and time consuming, but the grading is generous.
Not a big fan of his teaching style.
Hes a great professor but my god the homework and exams are long. Dont expect any plans over the weekend if you have them. Most do fine just the typical Purdue physics course
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is great at teaching the material and is very clear about the things you should expect on the exams and how to prepare for them. The class isn't easy but its very fair. If you do the work, go to lecture, and study, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He knows the material however seems to forget that his students are taking this course for the first time. Class average was consistently a D the entire semester. Very test heavy and likes to try to trip up students with his questions. Be ready to have to teach yourself and pay attention in the lectures. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives good explanations of the material, and he is interesting and lively when he lectures.  A very good professor overall.
Nolte takes the act of teaching the material more seriously than any other professer I've had here.  If you have him, you'll get to enjoy the process of learning again.

classes are lecture heavy - but you don't really have to pay attention, just answer a question or two in class for participation. It's a bit boring but really easy class, he grades fair and usually you get an A as long as you submit it. Only would take it again bc of how easy it was not bc it was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Swanson gave a good, easy introduction to the types of classes you can expected in the honors college curriculum. He assigns easy homework (e.g., watching a 40min documentary) and the class mainly serves as a way to make friends and connections.

I took HONR 19901 in the fall and had the Maps section. Prof. Swanson was a solid professor. The topic of maps and the lectures were a bit boring, but the class itself wasn't hard at all. There is some prep work, but typically never any homework. As long as you show up and participate you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Started every class late, and almost always went over time. Had students give presentations for several lectures, but would talk so much after the first one that the second presenters would be rushed or pushed to the next class. Gave no feedback for most assignments. Topic of the class was very niche, but he seemed to care about student learning.
He is just a chill guy. I think that he likes to teach, but he ends up a lot of the time, just yapping. He knows what he is doing and he's fun to chat with.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Swanson's lectures were very dry but he does know his stuff and as others have said, it's an easy A if you do the work. Group work with other honors' students was enjoyable.

His fall semester's topic was about Maps and it proved to be fairly low stakes and easy. The course primarily revolved around group work and making different types of maps. The readings and out-of-class work was minimal. Dr. Swanson himself is relaxed and gives some interesting lectures. A great course to take if you're busy with other classes.

Lots of lectures and the readings are quite high level, but it's okay because a complete understanding of them is not vital. All the projects are group and little solo homework, just do your part and you will be fine.

Such a fun professor, makes the topics on ANSC relate to real life. His labs are really hand on which is great to learn what we saw during the lectures that week in a different way. Very knowledgable about what he is teaching, honest, and tests are relevant to what we see in lecture. Workload is perfect.

Professor Nicholls is a very solid professor, and I recommend going to lectures as recordings don't always work. There are no study guides, does hand out all the lab quizzes and has a discussion post where he occasionally answers questions. Assignments are straightforward, and you're given a week to complete.

I highly recommend Dr. Nicholls to freshman. He's very funny, nice ,and personable. I would recommend going to class because the recording don't always work. The tests are always straight forward. The labs are interesting. Highly recommend him!
Amazing professor cares about student success and is very funny in class

Dr.Nicholls is by far the best professor Ive ever had. He cares so much about his class and makes it so fun. The labs were amazing opportunities. He is also very down to earth and personable. As long as you pay attention and actually try in this class, you will learn A LOT.
Dr. Nicholls is a great professor! He's very passionate about what he teaches and that made the class so fun. Labs were amazing and I learned a lot. His lectures are also entertaining.
I loved this class. He wasn't even supposed to teach the class, but he did an amazing job, had a ton of fun in the labs, and I learned a lot.
He is a good professor.  Fun guy, class isn't difficult.  He teaches off of slideshows and gave fill in notes.  The slides don't get posted so you do need to go to class.
Nicholls was an amazing instructor this semester. He is super interactive and passionate about what he teaches, which makes the class a lot more enjoyable. He gives very good feedback on questions.

Nicholls yaps a LOT, his lectures are always super long because he talks about every bulletpoint for a hot minute. One thing I didn't like about him was that he refused to be flexible when I was stuck at home after break due to a huge snow storm in my hometown, and did not allow me to join my group mates via zoom/facetime for a presentation.

Professor Nicholls is absolutely amazing. I would recommend him to anyone. He is a beef guy and loves cows. He loves teaching about all animals and is knowledgeable. He is willing to help any student who needs it as long as you reach out to him. He is a hilarious person and so down to earth.  You can get Aan  as long as you pay attention.

Melloch really studies how to learn, and it shows during his lectures. Expect lots of handouts, demonstrations, and learning to build fundamentals and intuition. Content is hard, and the class is very Exam heavy, and can feel all or nothing at times. Melloch is one of the best in the business at teaching concepts and intuition, invaluable skills.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and easy to talk to. Class was a easy A+ if you just showed up.

Prof. Melloch only wants for you to take your learning from this class to excel academically/personally and doesn't want this class to be something you stress over. Attend weekly lectures for attendance points and submit reflections for all your points. Learned useful stuff in his course and recommend for freshman getting adjusted to college.

I really enjoyed this class its pretty interesting and there is no work involved. Attendance is graded but the professor is very understanding and is enthusiastic about the material. It teaches you a lot of important skills.

Melloch is a very good lecturer and is able to make all of his content very interesting. His 10301 class is very easy and actually gives good information, too. He knows his content well, is interested in what he is teaching, and doesn't just read off of slides.

While this class did teach me that I am horrible at taking exams, Melloch was always fantastic and I learned a lot. The homework is just a weekly reflection, with physics problems being for extra credit. He is incredible at teaching Maxwell's equations conceptually and I feel like he is one of the few ECE profs that actually care about students.
Overall a great and interesting class that isn't much work. Professor does a fantastic job lecturing, highly recommend.
Really interesting class! great professor

Melloch is a really great professor. Exams and HW are fair and his pre-recorded videos on Brightspace + practice exams are the script when it comes to doing good in this class. Lecture is a good way to get familiar with the topics and watching the videos is the way to master them. Wish he taught Emag 2.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely caring and genuine professor. Teachers extremely well and answers absolutely any question asked. Exams are very lecture heavy and homework is used as an extra credit opportunity. Overall, grading is very fair for this "difficult" of a class and Melloch made this one of my favorite classes at Purdue.

Professor Melloch is easily the best professor I've had at Purdue. He genuinely cares about his students and makes an effort to help everyone understand the material. His lectures are clear, and the handouts and demos he uses in class really help bring the concepts to life.

I would take a bullet for this professor if needed. he is so kind and genuinely cares. I sucked at the class but he does a great job teaching. he knows everyones names and plays music at the beginning of some classes. he also has an entire online course and demos. I showed the demos to my family at thanksgiving because he is so awesome

Professor Melloch cares a lot about students' success and wellbeing, and it shines through in this class. He told us that he designed Keys to Learning just so that students can learn techniques to do better in school. A decent amount of the material was common sense, but I still recommend this class just because of how well it is taught.
Show up for class, do the reflections, and you will do well on the quizzes.  Easy course, but great information in it.

Imo, the best professor in Purdue's ECE dept. I haven't had many professors that genuinely care about their students and their learning. Lectures were good and they are recorded, but you can win points back on exams simply by going to lecture and office hours.

Keys To Learning is a very new course Professor Melloch just started teaching, its a course he genuinely cares about and is extremely passionate about. Lectures contain so much concentrated interesting and inspiring content, and attendance is the vast majority of the grade making it a very easy course.

Mike is honestly very overrated, i took his section and got a somewhat good grade too. You have to put in extra studying to do well unlike other classes. Homework is extra credit but he makes up for it by absolutely destroying you in the exams crossing questions left and right just because you didn't do the question his way.

Definitely the best professor for 30411. You need to show up to class, though; he doesn't really teach from the textbook, and the notes he posts aren't enough to learn from. The homework is all extra credit, which is nice. Show up, take good notes, and do the practice exams, and it won't be hard to get an A.
This professor goes through material on presentation slides based off on the research book he wrote. It is all very informative on how to study and think when learning how to adjust to college life.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Melloch's ENGR10301 class. Content was engaging and very useful for my academic career. His teaching was clear and memorable, focusing on student success. Exams matched lectures and texts, making an A very achievable. Highly recommend, will be trying to get into his ECE classes next year.

Normally he teaches ECE courses, but he started teaching ENGR 103 which is a course for FYE students about study habits and learning strategies. I found it interesting because he looked at the studies behind learning strategies, but I didn't find this class that useful since most of the strategies are fairly generic but definitely effective.

This class is physics heavy, but professor's explanations are pretty good. 2 cool things about the class: 1) all homework was extra credit, so you might as well do it. 2) if you do well enough on an exam, there's an oppurtunity to get some credit back for a question you missed; just schedule a meeting with him and work out the problem from scratch!

Best ECE professor I've ever had at Purdue. The content was relatively difficult but easy to understand if you attend all his lectures. He makes it worth going to all lectures with extra credit incentives.

One of the best ECE profs. Great lecturer (i.e. go to class and you'll get the stuff). Lots of extra credit. Straightforward exams. As long as you don't slack off (completely ignore class etc.), you'll probably get at least a B. Really cares about students. Very helpful in Q&A. Highly recommended. Only con is wish he taught more ECE classes.
Best professor at Purdue by far. He cares a lot about his students, and his lectures are very interesting. If you do the past exams, you'll do great !

An absolute gem of a professor, completely changed the way I approached the subject. His lectures are incredibly well organized with lots of practical demonstrations, worked out examples, and thorough explanations of concepts. Exams and homeworks are straightforward and not very hard if you put in the effort. One of the best teachers I've ever had.
Easy A I feel. He gives you chance to get some points back if attendance is good. The content is not quite easy but it's easy exams.
Easily the best professor I have had. Offers a lot of extra credit and is very available to help students.
Dr. Melloch is the professor I've had at Purdue. I didn't have that many interactions with him, but I know that I can talk to him anytime!

The best professor I had at Purdue. He is able to take a subject frequently hidden by calculus and derivation, and make it demonstrably intuitive to students. Worked with me and helped me to understand a lot about myself as a student. Dr. Melloch is an outstanding person, a devoted educator, and was a real mentor to me during my time at Purdue ECE.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Truly a hidden gem of Purdue ECE dept.

This was my favorite class and Melloch is my favorite professor. Hands down- he is accomodating of outside situations, willing to meet with students whenever, will explain a problem multiple times and ways to help you understand, bring in real life demos to make sense of some of the weird formulas, and keeps everything fun. Best prof for this class

Professor Melloch is a very extraordinary professor in the Electrical and Computer Engineering department. He can introduce electromagnetic topics very clearly and always do some physical experiments in class. I think that is a valuable experience to observe current and magnetic field effects. His exams are fair and test what you have learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had in ECE. Gives great lectures with experiments. He gives points back on exams and extra credit. In office hours it is obvious he truly wants his students to succeed.
One of the best instructors I have ever come across. Very helpful and inspiring and motivates you to give your best. Always ready to help, if you are genuinely interested to learn.

This is the only professor in Purdue that will give you his 100% to learn. If you dont take a class with him, you are losing big time. Never had a better Professor, I dont think i will (I really hope I do).
One of the best professors at Purdue

Prof. Melloch was the first professor I had in ECE that I could tell really cared about his students.  He would always come in with demos prepared to explain further the topics from the lecture.  In addition, he had a point recovery system on tests based on a short presentation, which really helped me learn the stuff I wasn't as comfortable about

Easily the best professor I've had at Purdue so far, which, in turn made ECE311 the most interesting course I've taken. Truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He's always available to help, and is very friendly. I could write a paper about how excellent he's been this semester. Keep it up, Dr. Melloch.

Prof. Melloch truly cares about his student's success. He makes himself and his TA more than accessible. Additionally, he uses numerous visuals and experiments to really create a good understanding of the concepts.  The only problem was going too slow which might be attributed to the students and the Prof being taken advantage of slightly.

Prof. Melloch is the best professor I have yet to have in the ECE department.  He is dedicated to the success and learning of his students.  He is very personal with his students as well which makes it easy to ask for help.  If you show up to class, do the work, and get any needed help, it will not be difficult to do well.
Cares for his students, I'd take him for any classes he's teaching. One of the best proffesors I've ever had
He's one of the best professors I've had at Purdue! He gives out lots of helpful handouts and homework is extra credit. He really cares that his students do well.

He puts forth an incredible amount of effort to teach, and it really shows! From his illustrative demonstrations, to his thoughtfully-prepared paper handouts and video recordings, he provides many alternate resources to explain and expound upon the phenomena covered in this course. He emphasizes and cultivates a strong conceptual understanding.
