While CHM115 isn't a hard course, Ramachandran is very hard to understand. You can tell how much he loves the topic, but he talks so fast and will rush to try to get through the lecture in time because he always added extra material. Class isn't hard, but he is difficult to understand.

He is simply impossible to understand. I can pick out a couple words in every sentence and that's it. Chem 115 should not be a hard class but because he is impossible to understand, the lectures are useless. I might as well be self-studying.

Not the worst professor I've had but definitely not the best. I think the difficult nature of the class I took with him made it seem like he was a worse professor than he actually is. It's evident that he knows the subject, but he has trouble communicating it to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PVR is extremely hard to understand and will belittle his students in front of an entire lecture hall for asking questions. His exams aren't hard but the regrading process is extremely trying and when the average isn't what he wants he'll spend class time basically calling the class stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: PVR was personally very hard to understand for me. I had him for the second half of CHM115 and he clearly knows his stuff, but he went a little too quickly through lectures and I usually was confused by his examples. If possible, I'd recommend going to someone else's lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He truly finds joy in teaching and wants to help his students learn to love organic chem. I didn't mind having him as a professor, but there were times that I did struggle and he make me feel stupid for not understanding, but he was not doing that out of malice. He knows organic chem like the back of his hand, and hopes that his students will too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was all over the place. PVR seemed confused, the TA's were confused, the students were confused, I'm still confused and the class is over. The labs were pointless and the TA never provided us with feedback. The quizzes were fine and were similar to the homework. I did well because of Youtube videos and khan academy.

This class felt like a complete waste of my time. The entire class was incredibly unorganized and it felt as if the professor had no idea what he was actually supposed to be doing. On top of this, our online lab assignments felt completely pointless and did not contribute to my understanding of the topics whatsoever. Luckily, the TAs were great.

I'll start by saying that I was terrified for this class. PVR was an incredible instructor, and aided by his TAs made orgo one of my favorite classes this semester. It was challenging but super rewarding. There's ample extra credit on exams (earned over 100% on 3/4), comprehensive study, & office hours + SI are readily available for help.

Ramachandran really isn't that bad of a professor. He's very passionate about his work and really wants to get students engaged in chemistry. But, combined with the fact that his accent is thicker than the textbook, he's nearly impossible to understand if you're not in the first three rows. If you get him, you'll be in for a ride.

Ramachandran goes by PVR, just to throw that out there. His lecture content isn't bad, but he can be hard to understand because of a thick accent in combination with not talking into the microphone. Go to lecture, read his slides, answer the iClicker, and watch the lecture video if you need something repeated. You'll probably be fine.

Literally the worst professor I've had at Purdue. If at all possible do not take him for gen chem. Very confusing lectures and skips through several slides. Have to come to class for attendance points. Exams were nothing like the study guides, and were extremely difficult. Felt like he was trying to get most students to fail
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He cares about his students, but His accent is super heavy, even sitting right next to him can be difficult, it makes homework hellish to do, however, the exams aren't that bad if you just do the practice ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had heard a lot of bad things about PVR and was scared about how the class was going to go, but it ended up not being that bad once we got passed nuclear chemistry. If you study and pay attention during lecture the exams are easy. This class should be an easy A if you put in the work and ask questions.

He doesnt really teach anything and is hard to understand. He doesnt work out any examples in class which would actually be helpful. I got an A because I did the extra credit and I took AP chem in high school.

P.V.R. is a really great dude. The exams are incredibly easy, literally copy and pasted from previous years. He gives you access to these exams so as long as you know how to do the old exams you will be fine. On the final he gave us 30 POINTS worth of extra credit, he usually makes it know in lecture what it will be/gives hints. Easy A with a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I liked PVR- he explained concepts well and knows a lot and does really cool research. Tests were not bad at all- he gave practice exams that were very similar and it's not hard to do well if you make an effort to listen in class and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: PVR was quite difficult to understand with his accent (also the mic was never loud enough). The only reason I went to lecture was for the iclicker questions. He definitely cares about his students, though, and he wants us to learn the material. His exams were not overly difficult because they closely followed the practice exams that he gave us.

I really liked PVR. Ive always struggled with chem but I actually did alright in orgo and understood/enjoyed the course. Sit up front in class to better hear him. Dont expect to be on your phone, hell call you out on it. He tried to help us succeed as much as possible. Just pay attention and go to class, be respectful; hes a good guy.

Dr. Ramachandran is a very smart man, but has little knowledge on teaching. His accent is very thick, so I suggest sitting near the front so you can understand him better. The topics he covers are difficult and require a lot of attention outside of class. Overall, he is a very good professor. Go to class for the iClicker points and pay attention.

Very difficult to understand. He definitely knows what he is talking about and is super passionate. He thinks pretty highly of himself, too. If you don't sit in the front row, he will automatically think the worst of you. I sat in the fourth row and he scolded me for not paying attention (but I most certainly was) via email.

Seems passionate about the topic, but extremely hard to understand because of his accent. Focuses on the front-row students, and only makes eye contact with the first few rows. Rarely explains answers to his pop-quiz questions, and complains a lot about students getting the answers wrong. Doesn't assign much homework besides reading the textbook.
A bit hard to follow in class (doesn't always go sequentially). Does have powerpoint which are information heavy, and they are posted on BB.

While students who interrupt class are annoying... He will call them out and spend class time complaining about how you can't interrupt him because the material is a lot to go over, while he is interrupting his own lecture? And honestly printing off the lecture notes beforehand doesn't help because he is all over the place. Rent the book. It helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very condescending and sometimes flat out rude. Chastises students who ask questions in class, and tells them how the content is "so easy" when in reality it isn't. He also embarasses students in front of the whole class if they answer one of his mid-lecture questions wrong. But he is very passionate about Orgo, and this makes the class bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I am usually pretty good at communicating with people with heavy accents but this was not the case. Orgo is already difficult in my opinion and to not be able to understand your professor makes it even worse. Attending the SI sessions really helped and I would recommend going to them right off the bat. All the resources I utilized avoided the prof
The accent is hard to get past. However, he wants to see everyone in his class succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's rude, demeaning, and does not seem to care whether or not you learn the material. He makes anyone who asks a question during the lecture feel stupid in front of everyone, and forget about asking him questions during his office hours because he is even more chastising. Don't take this course with this professor if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Organic chem with PVR was by far the most difficult class I've taken at Purdue. Hard to understand lecture material and his accent is pretty thick and he speaks quietly. Often loses the classes attention.
Very hard to understand.

I don't know some people give PVR high rating. Rather you manage to do well enough to have the curve make you pass the class or not, it doesn't change the fact that he's a horrible professor. Very all over the place when teaching with an accent that is difficult to understand.

After gen chem, everybody is scared of orgo but this guy will make your life easier becoz he has a real teaching technique that will help you in his class n in other classes as well.PVR is very passionate abt the subject and he will keep it fun for u...handouts, homeworks, recitation, all very helpful for exam prep.

He is AWFUL. He is so hard to understand, which makes chem even more confusing since many words already sound alike. He only asks students who do well to rate him on here, so that is what I am doing. I did very well in this class but only because I taught myself literally everything. If you ask him a question he makes you feel very stupid.

I was scared of Organic chemistry.  PVR made it enjoyable.  His handouts highlight key concepts and make it easy to learn.  Graded homework helped to prepare for the exams, whcih were very fair.  He gets annoyed when the class is disturbed by talking and texting.

His teaching method and teaching materials he distributed to us, were straightforward and very helpful in preparing midterms. Moreover, graded homeworks and non-graded homeworks were also helpful in preparing midterms.
I enjoyed the class very much.  The handouts were very helpful; could do without the text.  Graded homework package prepared me well for the exams, which were very fair.

He really does love organic chemistry, and does his best to get his students to understand.  A lot of the material is based on his handouts, so try not to miss class.  He does not like people talking or texting in his class and will stop the class to address any interruptions.

Focused more on ways to make the tests so that the average would be higher than normal for organic, not caring how individual students did. all you had to do was memorize the notes and you could get a high grade without  understanding. Some found this easy and others didn't. Constantly lectured about the people who didn't come to class.

In my own opinion I would describe the class material as "very hard".  But that difficulty rating can be brought down significantly depending on how students use him. If you listen during lecture, read the assigned material, and use his tips and tricks throughout the year I am fairly confident that you will receive an A. Excellent and fair prof.

Ramachandran's organic chemistry knowledge can be, sometimes, intimidating.  However, he is very helpful if you go to his office.  He always responded to my requests for additional meetings beyond regular office hours.  Go to class for extra credit quizzes.  Has a heavy accent, but I got used to it soon. Overall, excellent Professor.
This Professor made CHM 256 fun.  Nice course packets and summary sheets.  Emphasis on the reaction mechanisms that we should know helped.  The TAs were also helpful.

I was afraid of this class at the beginning of the semester.  I felt comfortable as the semester progressed and received an A in the course.  The handouts were very helpful.  The Prof. emphasizes on the logic of organic mechanisms.  I enjoyed the class very much

I liked the way Prof. Ramachandran teaches orgo.  He takes teaching seriously and motivates you to think.  Exam questions are from material covered in class.  Gives lots of extra credits.  If you go to class regularly, you can earn good grade.
One of the best Professors in my two years at Purdue.  If you go to the office hours, he is very helpful.  I got an A in this course and learnt lot of stuff.
The prof were much helpful. I thought he try very hard. Thank proffesor for making good class.
This was one of the class where I learned a lot. He is a very good teacher and explains things really well.

BY FAR THE WORST TEACHER ON PURDUE'S CAMPUS. if you ask a question in class he will make you feel stupid. make use of the TAs. This was his first semester back from a 5 year probationary period. He gave us 40 points of extra credit on the first exam so he would have an A average only to make the second exam impossible since grades were too high

Couldn't understand him at first and thought I was going to do really bad in his class; however if you read his notes and try to understand them yourself, it really isn't too bad(well Mass Spec was horrible, but other than that...) However, you should only take his class if you have great memorization skills (for learning mechanisms)
Got an A with this guy. Make use of office hours/recitation and you'll get an A. He offers ample opportunities for extra credit as well, and the TA's are really hot.
If you go to office hours, he is very helpful and helped me understand chemistry better. If you get the course packets and do the homework you will do well in the class.

I don't know what class the other commenters were attending, but I thought his class was great!!!!!  He was very helpful both in and out of class, and had great TAs. He helped us understand by filling in the blanks and actually teaching chemistry. Rather than giving 'memorize only' material, he helped us learn it the right way. Learned so much!!!!!
Mostly ordinary.  Claimed to spend "5 hours" preparing for each lecture (sure...)

Why? Why keep this guy around! Just let him do research, because he is a terrible teacher! His lectures are hard to follow, and when I asked him a question during office hours he told me that he already went over that in lecture ... Ugh! Just give him his Noble Prize so he'll leave innocent students alone ! If you get him -- DROP!
somebody, please, take this guy away from Purdue!
This man made me despise chemistry
By far the worst professor I have ever had.  Very hard to understand and not helpful.  Expects that you know everything already.  Tests were very difficult.  Avoid this professor at all costs!

Not the worst professor I've ever had, but close to it. I had a strong B going into the final, got average, and my grade was dropped to a C. I drove over break to talk to him about it, and he refused to change my grade. Sometimes hard to understand him. He expects students to know as much as he does. Obsessed with the Nobel Prize.
I failed chm256 with a curve when i took his class. the next semester, i retook the class with anothe professor and got an A without a curve... he's just a really bad teacher
Don't risk a good course here

Worst professor ever. I don't know if he is still in rotation for the 255/256 classes... if he is I suggest you drop the class and take with Chmielewski (she is a great teacher) the following semester.

Awful awful awful professor. I didn't have a clue as to what was going on because he clarify one freakin point. If you have this guy for organic chem ever, my advice is to drop it immediatly and take it from Harry Morrison next semester.
Worst professor I've ever had. Got a decent grade both semesters, but it was torture.

He is SO unfriendly and unwilling to answer questions. He is very arrogant and feels like his students should "just know" things without his having to teach them. He makes the averages on his tests about a 40% ON PURPOSE...I think he likes to see people perform badly in his class.
Hard to understand, but does an alright job teaching. Exams are hard but have lots of bonus points. Not a bad professor.
This guy is the worst prof ever hes such a jerk...avoid like the plague
No Comments
No Comments
this professor def does not know how to teach..and his exams are impossible and he's made many people i kno feel very bad during his office hours!! also he grades unfairly!
Wasn't very helpful. Told us that it's in the book and we should know it.

I had him for both organic classes..not only is his class hard but my god is it boring and frankly i never learned anything in his class i had to ask someone else to clarify things..did i mention he has an accent i dont think anyone would enjoy his class
sometimes i wonder if he even thinks about his class before he teaches it
Does this guy get pleasure from this?
Held "help-sessions" that were not announced to students, extremely unclear, unfriendly.
How did this guy get tenure?
Avoid like the plague.  Once said  A monkey could have done better on this test
Classes are not very helpful, the textbook is much clearer. Exams and homework are easy, but homework is time-intensive (6-8 hours per week). Grading is lenient.

Had him for a seminar class. Grade was basically entirely attendance (No A if you miss like 2 classes) and completion grades. Felt like a waste of time and you could tell he didn't really want to be there. Also talked quietly without a mic and is kinda hard to understand (OK English).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Song was very thorough in his lectures. He was prompt in his responses, reasonable to requests, and fair. I enjoyed his class. Other students may have had a negative experience with the content, but he did a good job making it easier to digest.
He has a good English.

He is without a doubt the most disorganized lecturer I have ever met. He goes way too fast and has trouble communicating the material to grad students. He does not give pragmatic coding examples or clear output explanations. The only saving grace of the class are his homework and exam curve policies. Would not recommend his 526 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Qifan is a good professor who means well and has a clear lecturing style. That said, his lectures are a bit disorganized and he talks fast. His exams are extremely challenging, final project isn't specific, and homework's are really long. But they are graded for completion rather than correctness. Overall his course is a good intro regression class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only graded on homework, one midterm, and final. The lectures were very dry and hard to pay attention in. He just read off the textbook and gave the same examples without really explaining anything further than the book did. Gave practice exams from other professors but no solutions to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor has a very good command of English language. His knowledge of the subject is also pretty good. I was always able to follow his lectures. The course was taught in a way that was easy to understand and build on itself cumulatively. The homework were not difficult and help with learning. Blame the STAT  course content, not the professor!

I signed up for this class and had to drop it. First of all, this professor's ability to explain the material is very limited. It is extremely difficult to follow his lectures. Also, he has a very thick accent. I am not a native speaker as well and I don't judge people easily, but I can easily say that he cannot communicate with the class at all.

He talks to the screen most of the class. Doesn't check if the class has understood the concepts or not.  He needs to improve his English fluency to teach and communicate well.  There's hardly any point taking this class if most of the time you are trying to decipher what he is saying

Prof Qin is not good. Lectures were messy, could barely understand her. Many exam questions are ambiguous. Group project had unclear grading; rubric was released 10 min before the due date. Did not receive group project feedback for weeks because Prof Qin did not know how to increase the volume of the computer. Avoid if possible.

Really nothing enjoyable about the class.Vague description of expectations, especially in the group project. Expect typos in basically every homework assignment. If you're taking this online, you'd be more confused about what she expects in the assignments than the material itself. But project was maybe not as bad as other people on here have said.
Expectations for the final project are incredibly unclear. Otherwise, the class was fine. She posts the lecture notes on Brightspace, which is nice.

The other reviews had me worried, but my experience wasn't bad, maybe because I took the class online. Her lecture style is very robotic. But all the information you need for homework is in the notes. She provides example R code. It's just a matter of deciphering her examples. Her notes have lots of typos and sometimes her notation is ambiguous.
group project took ten years off of my life but whatever
The main issue with the class is that the exams are designed to trick the student taking the exam, also the way the project is laid out is extremely bad. Would not recommend taking this class.

Decent lecturer. 2 exams worth 15% each at the middle and end of semester. Exams are doable (pure MCQ with 1 note sheet allowed) and on Respondus Monitor. Group project is worth way too much (25%) with unclear directions and unclear expectations. I would rather it be a individual project or a lighter part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Listen to the other reviews. It's as bad as they say. Brutal English, very tough exam (no curve in the class despite averages in the 50s and 60s). Project is also graded harshly unless you put a significant amount of time into it.

Her lectures and exams more focused on statistical concepts understanding and real world application. I think most of her lectures explain the concepts pretty well and are align with her slides. I have to say she is teaching much much better than the other Stats class I took last semester. The format of homework is kind of tricky.

Attending lecture did not help at all, I ended up just reading through the slides on my own time. The homework was tedious but all of the answers were in her slides, just might take some people a long time. The exams were not terrible if you actually understood the material, you get a cheat sheet so I just crammed as much as I could on there.

Low exam averages, tricky questions, lectures are not useful. Project is extremely time consuming, quizzes are also confusing, homework is lengthy and not an adequate amount of office hours. DO NOT take this class. Additionally based on the low exam statistics, everyone was expecting a curve but there wasn't one which was very shocking.

If this class with Qin is not required for your degree, DON'T TAKE IT. She is nice and the content itself is easy but the way she lectures about it and tests you on it is so bad. She has no curve which I was appalled by because many students are worried about passing. Lectures never help and they are long. This was my worst class experience ever.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ACTUALLY WANT TO LEARN ANYTHING!!! Exams are difficult and have trick questions, homework and lecture notes are full of typos and inconsistencies. Professor Qin does not know how to teach to save her life. Unnecessarily long group project at the end. Content should be very easy, but made needlessly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Pros:
- HW takes 5-6 hours top so you can defo procrastinate
- professor knows what she's teaching
- not a bad class for learning stat methods

Cons:
- exams have trick questions, so annoying...
- no leniency on HW, strict guidelines for everything, no late days
- mandatory attendance
- group projects 
- didn't give enough guidelines for project

As others have said, slides and homework are full of typos and inconsistent notation - especially earlier in the content. She is not responsive online. Tests and are full of trick questions that make the content appear much harder than it really is. Homework is extremely tedious. Easy content, hard class.

The class material itself is very difficult, so having a professor that added long and hard homeworks and a huge group project made the class so much harder. She had pretty good slides for the lectures, but her lecturing itself was often confusing and hard to follow. Get ready for a time-consuming class if you take stat512 with her.
She is not good at organizing languages, get ready to learn this course on your own!

I took STAT512 with her last spring. She is horrible at teaching. All of the course materials are poorly written. I sent her emails about the typos and she started giving me attitude during office hours. She would also threaten students over Brightspace. I feel bad for the students that will have to take this course with her in the future.

Not sure able her personality since I'm taking a online class that only uses her recorded lecture and homework wrote by her. Horrible lecturer, refer to everyting as "this" rather than the actual terminology but cares a great deal about you using the correct term and notation in homework, frequent typos and unclear language in slides and homeworks.
Professor Qin is probably the worst professor I have ever had at Purdue. Her class is poorly run and all questions on the HW are confusing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER YOU WILL REGRET IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: she sucks. The material isnt hard but she cant teach even if her life depended on it.
I don't know if tiantian knows what proof reading is.

This class would not be that hard but her inability to teach is what makes it hard. The format and organization of her lectures are terrible and there are many typos on the homework that just make it more confusing and longer to do. There are many errors in her slides as well. It seems like she does not know how to use technology.
Worst professor I have ever had, inexplicably bad at teaching. Hard course because of her inability to teach, not the material.

Terrible. She emphasizes the importance of the notation of equations, but there are many errors in her slides. The homework assignments have incredibly unclear directions and are riddled with typos. I spent an hour trying to figure out why lm(count~temperature, BikeProject) was not working. It was because she spelled temperature as tempeture SMH.

She somehow managed to make a class more poorly run than STAT 350. There is no piazza or campuswire, but rather Brightspace discussions where she instructs you to reach out to the TA by email. Everyone spams the TA, but they can only do so much when the professor cannot write clear questions. Avoid this class at all costs.

The homework is hard. The content is not hard, but the way the homework are written makes us so confused. It is like broken English. She expects use to understand what she says in lectures but she talks super fast and mispronounces key terms. The slides are also full of errors that just make the content more confusing. Avoid her at all costs!!!!!!!

The fact she is the only professor for this course is appalling. She cares about the students, but the delivery of course material is horrendous. Gatekeeps corresponding course contents. The class should not be that difficult, but her English is not very good. She interchanges all of the terms and writes poor questions without a discussion page,
Long, badly formatted homework assignments with often outright confusing questions. Class isn't curved not to mention hard to follow lectures.
Dropped her class twice, worst professor

She is caring as a person and tries to help her students, but is utterly disorganised and sometimes makes errors. Her homework is long and tough, while her tests are moderate. The TAs are tough graders.

Not the greatest lecturer, with challenging homeworks and exams. Also for any students prepping for this class prior, just a heads up that Penn State has a good documentation for lecture material. More straight forward and specific than her slides

Prof Qin knows what she's talking about but she isn't a great lecturer. Disorganized slides, mistakes on slides, and lectures too fast. Her homeworks are long and difficult, so start it ASAP. Tests are similar to practice exams but are full of sneaky trick questions. The group project is the saving grace of the course with easy grading on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very harsh graders with no curve in class and super long homeworks
Don't take this course. Go away from her. please, Listen to me, this would be one of the worst courses at Purdue
Homework is easy to get 100 and exam is easy to do. Like this class. Qin is really nice.
She is so nice! I really like STAT512. The exam is really similar to the practice exam and she is always happy to help you! This is the best stat course I've ever taken at Purdue.
Horrible course design, not a lot of online resources available

In STATS 512, Professor Qin was good about showing us how to use the concepts we were learning about, and she did a lot of in-class activities that I thought were helpful in learning how to use the concepts. The only problem was you needed to have learned the concepts during the class in order to participate. Get extra credit for showing up.

Horrible experience. I have went through everything but all in vain! Her lectures are so disorganized! The assignments are way too long and redundant. The group project is fine. However, the questions in the test are super confusing and most cases, language is definitely a barrier for the instructor. Super unhelpful TA.
Be prepared to spend the majority of the semester on homework and group project. Intense course but the professor was very knowledgeable. I enjoyed the knowledge gained at the end of it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: STAT 512 with professor Qin was the most annoying class I've taken. Her lectures are all over the place and you can barely read her handwriting. You're better off reading the book instead and going to TA office hours to ask questions. She also expects you know R before class so learn it before day 1. Search "R Programming Tutorial" on YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Tiantian has a bit of a language barrier and needs a proof-reader for her material (lecture notes, exams, homework assignments). Class was pretty typical in terms of difficulty and time commitment but made unnecessarily tricky by the poor English and tricky questions on exams.

Her recorded lectures were mostly her shuffling papers around as she scribbled something unreadable while not explaining the concept clearly. Too often did I hear "you should know this" and "you should figure this out" when asked a question during live lectures. Sometimes she would get through only 1/5 homework problems during the weekly lecture.

Hard to understand, but provides lecture slides which are pretty helpful. Homeworks are long and grading is pretty harsh, but provides plenty of extra credit opportunities. Had 7 homeworks, 3 quizzes, final project, and final exam, which felt like a lot throughout the semester. Final project criteria is extremely vague, so clarify at office hours

At the beginning of this class it was fine. But at the end, when the staff become more difficult, she skips lots of explanation that makes me so confused. The slides are hard to read since they are not well organized. I would suggest not to take since when materials become difficult she can't explain them clearly.
The professor skip almost all the knowledge needed in the class. I learn nothing from this class, all I remembered is her name.

I genuinely don't understand the critics. She is very organized and starts off from the basics and eventually makes the content challenging. She is very helpful and caring and dresses smartly too. The group project in the class can be challenging due to the nature of the team members. HWs are long but fair as you are given 2 weeks to complete.

My recommendation is that if you do not have strong statistical background, like you are just taking stat as a minor, definitely not taking her class! And I believe the working load is not designed for undergrad cos that is way too much. She gives you the easiest practical sample midterm, but the actual midterm makes me feel failing the course.

The way professor Qin teaches is very confusing. She goes through 20 powerpoint slides a class that are full of examples and R code. If you don't see what she writes before she quickly removes it from the screen, that's too bad. She skips over a lot of "easy" concepts that no one understands making it even more difficult and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: It is deifinitely one of the worst professor I have ever seen. The homework is due every two week. The length per homework is unbelievable. You could imagine spending the whole weekend plus Friday to work on this, but still could not finish it. The lecture is so so so confusing. She only tries to cover the topic without any explaining! Don't take!

Worst professor at Purdue.

This professor is knowledgeable in statistics, but could not be worse at teaching the material in a manor that is accessible or understandable. The majority of time in class is spent in confusion. If you want to bond with other students over just how confused you are, this is the class for you!

The class is not bad, but the homework can take awhile. Study the formulas back and forth and you can do alright on the exams. The online lectures are confusing. It is best to show up to class and pay attention during the handouts.

Before coming into this class i had a working knowledge of statistics. After leaving i can honestly say i have no idea what i am doing. Professor Qin does a poor job of wording her thoughts, has no organization in her lecture, and moves insanely fast through difficult subject matter. Do not take this course.  I spend 10+ hours per week on the homework.  The online book is difficult to navigate and doesn't align well with the class powerpoints.  The instructor moves way too quickly.   Worst course I've taken at Purdue.

Talks very fast, impossible to keep up.  Does not explain concepts well, or how to use the online software. The class is hard, but extremely useful!
Try to find another professor.

She is very nice, but I found lecture completely useless. I've taken a statistics class on the same level and done extremely well. English is pretty decent however speaks VERY FAST.= confusing. Lecture notes are worthless. Suggest getting book. Her calculation questions are easy. Her true/fase. multi choice are hard. Not very easy to understand, but she was quite nice. Always willing to help out in office hours.

Not the best at explaining things, but definitely an easy course.  You can use create-your-own formula sheets for exams.
Easy class

This was the easiest course I ever took. There were weekly quizzes, weekly discussion posts, and a final exam. The quizzes were all easy and directly based on the textbook. My only complaints were that the due dates were confusing and I had to buy a $95 textbook.

This was by far the most easiest class I have ever taken. Most of the times I forget I enrolled in this course. Your grades are dependent of quizzes, discussion posts and responding to 2 people. The professor and the TA do not care about you. They never answer any questions in the discussion designed for Q/A. This course is also poorly structured with due dates being wrong and confusing. Grading criteria is also blurry. One of the worst class I have taken in my life.

This was one of the easiest classes I have taken so far. It was an online course. Each week consisted of a short essay submitted via blackboard and then feedback to two other classmates. Super easy! Please take 578 with someone else, its been two weeks and she breezes over content like you are the next Einstein. She is unfit for teaching college-level courses and needs to be patient. Like others have experienced, she also has communication issues. Above all, I find her very non-chalant and just uncaring.

She was nice but lacks enthusiasm and could not satisfactorily answer most student questions. This shows her lack of understanding of basic ML.; very detached and uninterested or maybe she is highly unprepared for lectures. She was also very difficult to understand. Most students experienced this because of her garbled way of speaking.

The course is mainly focused on statistical aspect of the ML which means that you will need to have background in linear algebra and probability theory.  She writes all the derivatives/mathematics proofs on the board. It is super clear and I can really understand what's the theory behind each models/algorithms. Easy homeworks. Heavy exams.

Rocommend the course ONLY to Phds studying theoretical mathematics... It is almost no experience as homeworks and exams are all related to long and complex theoretical proofs. If the final grades are also low for most, I will not recommend it to anyone....

I have never been more offended by how a class was such a waste of time. I have learned literally nothing in this class. Way better off taking CS 573 instead of 578. she doesnt use a textbook, and intentionally leaves proofs off her slides so you have to show up. class is overly focused on theoretical side of things, so you never actually learn how to use models or compare them. i'm almost convinced that this is the most useless waste of a class in the CS dept, except that compilers also exists, so its close

I've learned all this stuff before, & her way of explaining things isn't helpful. She does a horrible job of deciding which topics to emphasize & which topics to breeze over. She has her PhD in Stats so she focuses way too much on the mathematical proof behind ML models. CS 578 is way too theoretical to be interesting to me, but it's also way easier than CS 573 which assumes we already understand the math theory...

This course was harder than expected in terms of busywork. this is the worst class i have ever taken

Good professor. Knows the material, willing to work with you, and has great commentary. Made what may have been a difficult subject fun and enjoyable.

Very confusing, course is completely disorganized.  She types her emails in subject line, and does not proof read. Only reason I received a good grade was because the first half of the course material I learned in high school physics.

Professor Ray in an exceptional professor, she is good with explaining concepts and if you have questions she is always willing to help out during office hours. Professor Ray is one of the best professors at Purdue. Not only does she create notes for students to copy during class, she is also easily accessible outside of class if there are any questions. The exams are challenging, but she does her best to prepare us.

Professor Ray is the best professor I have had at Purdue. Her lectures are engaging, and she takes the time to get to know every student. Professor Ray is the best. This class is an absolute grind with all the assignments but that is what you should expect taking a 4 credit math/stat class. The class is difficult but without professor ray teaching, it would be even more difficult. Could not recommend enough.

10/10

Great professor!

absolutely LOVE professor sally. there's several times i send late emails (like 11pm) about homeworks and she replied with in 5-10 mins. she tries her very best to help you with anything in the class, also she remembers everyone's name and something about them which is just so impressive!

Honestly, the worst professor I've had at Purdue. I did well in the class, but Saha is unreasonably hostile, makes fun of struggling students who ask questions often by questioning their intelligence, and has a massive ego. If Saha is meant to represent ECE in Indianapolis, he needs to get in check. Also got caught with porn. Shady person overall.
If you're not religious, get one and start praying.
He does not properly communicate with the classroom when going through lecture material; he merely expects us to know how to do the content before ever being shown how to.

One of the best professors I have had, amazing lectures and in class notes. ECE 2K1 is notorious for being hard but if you watch Professor Saha's lectures and do the homeworks, this class should be a breeze. He can come across as passive aggressive however, I believe that's just the way he is with everyone. Besides this I would 100% recommend him.

If you could do this class without having it with saha do it! My class was a sub section of the 2k class because we weren't electrical base majors but me and motorsports and other engineering majors. Because of this he treated us poorly and with no respect. If it was aloud I could write an entire book of reasons not to have him as a professor.

Good. Cares about students, although sometimes blunt in some respects, this reality check is not a negative thing. His lectures cover everything on the exams and he makes sure to address common misconceptions.

I am a repeat student this summer. Prof. Saha's lectures made so much sense for my understanding. I am doing 10x better this summer. He was always very helpful during his office hours and takes our opinions into consideration when teaching. He may need some editing of his quizzes but he graded very fairly when any error was found.

This TA is extremely rude to students. On the online class form he berated students for asking for past exam solutions to be released. He lead the classwide exam review sessions, which due to his unpreparedness and poor organizational skills went 2-3 hours past the review time. Recitation had the same issues and led to us missing out on content.

This professor is extremely rude and unprofessional, especially toward his students. He also goes out of his way to insult students online in Piazza, gives unhelpful and disrespectful feedback, and has one of the worst egos in the ECE department.
He is absolutely full of himself. He is rude and does not respect student. He has a massive ego that needs to get in check.

Disrespectful and full of himself. Every response he has on piazza is either passive aggressive or straight up rude. Never takes a moment to see things from the other students perspective and always assumes they're in the wrong, tries to force his own study method that works for him onto everyone like it's a one size fits all type of thing.

He responds very disrespectfully to nearly all questions asked, often belittling the student asking and ridiculing them. He knows the content very well and can teach it well, but can not be relied on for any help.

Tridib does alright as a GTA and explaining material, but lacks when it comes to handling other matters, such as final grades. While he does not have much control over the matter, he could approach it by explaining results rather than gloating about his own success.

Tridib is probably the best GTA for 2k1 recitations. He has been teaching for quite a few semesters, so he knows what is important in the class and common mistakes. Also, he is very personable and easy going, and always goes out of his way to help students succeed.

Saha is a caring professor who really wants to see his students succeed. He offers hundreds of practice problems, daily office hours, and lots of extra credit. He is always asking for student feedback and really takes everything into consideration. This class is very difficult but Saha provided the tools needed to excel. Would highly recommend.
Often sets arbitrarily difficult exam questions and a absurd amount of work for what should be a introductory class.

Exams harder than they should be. if you were asked to attend office hours for credit make sure you keep track of the TA's names you attended with. Otherwise, you may lose a point or so and according to some policy that we were only told few days before the final, you either get full credit on that or a zero. Not fun...

Tridib teaches this class as you should already know the material. Even then, his examples are extremely basic and he doesn't explain some things at all. This will leave you not understanding the homework or exams. Essentially he doesn't prepare you from the ground up. If you're coming into this class, you should have studied a lot in advance.
Great dude, teaches very well and often asks for feedback.

Professor Saha knows what he is talking about and explains the content really well. The class in general is tough but the way he explains the material made things more simple and is also willing to set up times outside of class to meet with you and discuss any questions you might have.

He is very accessible outside of the class. Always willing to help students who need them. He is also one of the best lecturer Ive ever had in Purdue. Even though the class is hard, he is very knowledgeable at the class material and open to students feedbacks.

Professor Saha was very knowledgeable with regards to the material he was teaching and taught it well. Although he was very accessible outside of class, if you are not fully understanding the material he will come off as rude and condescending rather than helpful.

Professor Saha is very accessible and helpful outside of class. He is also very knowledgable about what he is teaching and seems to genuinely care about his students and their success in this course. The course is only 2 months long in the summer but professor Saha did well to deliver the relevant contents.

He taught a tough class in two months. He does lectures well, creates charts and notes that are easy to understand and helps during solving problems. He is always very helpful and meets students outside class.
He is one of the best instructors I have had at Purdue ECE - great lectures and useful homeworks, exams are tough but graded generously.
Focus on the exams and keep up with him in lecture and you will be fine

Goes quick in lecture does an okay job explaining concepts. 302 is just not horribly interesting. Nice guy but beware of his curve the actual % you earn in the class is irrelevant. It is graded on a normal curve completely relative to your classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were some of the best I have had in ECE, exams were on the harder side. He clearly cares about the students' learning and explains complicated concepts very well.

Good lecturer. Uploads notes containing the weeks info rather than slides, which could be a good or bad thing (not a lot of useful examples in those notes). 302 is a hard class, but I've been pretty happy with Tripathi. He doesn't require attendance, but the class is constantly building on itself, so it's best to go.
This guy is THE GOAT. Scott is amazing in every way possible. He actually saved my dog from a burning building while simultaneously lecturing about MGMT 201. What a guy.

He can be monotoned, but he is extremely helpful and very understanding. I had a situation during my exam, and he was extremely helpful, making me clam down and still have time to finish my exam. He wants to be an actual professor and knows students have situations so he helps rather than punishes them for being human beings.

Overall Scott is a great professor. He cares about his students a lot and wants them to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives extra credit if you come. The class if a little dry but its ok. I didn't do so well on the first exam but was able to bounce back by completing his practice exams and ask questions in class. Take him for MGMT 201

Sorensen is a very caring professor who wants his students to succeed.  He is very accessible if you ever have a question and he provides extra credit for attendance.  Accounting is a subject that is hard to make interesting, but I think he does a good job presenting the material in a very straightforward manner.

His lectures are really dry. Spends most of the lectures hunched over the document camera writing problems. Other than that the class itself isn't too hard. The exams and homework are pretty straightforward.

Overall a good professor. Teaches content well and in an easy to follow manor, but lectures aren't very engaging (its accounting). He is very kind and tries to be understanding. Overall a solid pick for someone genuinely trying to teach and help students.
He is a really understanding and nice professor. It was clear he wanted his students to succeed and do well in his class. He is understanding on extensions even after the deadline.

Thank God the class is over ! What a joke. Like others have said, Sorensen was sooo monotone and boring - I could hardly stay awake in class as he just went on and on and on. I understand this is it for him so that's good for all those taking it starting next school year - not soon enough as far as I am concerned. Purdue accounting is a joke.

I appreciated that he recorded lectures because I could not attend class without falling asleep.  The subject itself was fine because he gave us equation sheets for exams, but he was your typical boring accountant who was very monotone.
Nice guy, very monotone and boring class content. Provides a very helpful formula sheet for each exam. Class content is extremely boring and not practical outside of just getting a grade.
He was a very knowledgeable and helpful professor, but the lectures were just very boring.

I really enjoyed this class and Scott as a professor. I think accounting is fun so I didn't have a problem with the lectures being boring. He answered my emails quickly and answered any questions I had after class. He definitely cares about our success. The exams were not too hard and he provides a good formula sheet for each one. I recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sorensen clearly cares about what he teaches and his students' success. I'm repeating others here, but yes, while his lectures do feel boring, that's just due to the content itself. There's not a lot you can do to make accounting exciting. Homework is not bad, and formula sheets on the exams were very helpful.

Professor Sorensen was very nice and clearly explained things, however, he was very monotone which made lectures difficult for me personally. He provided formula sheets for exams which were super helpful, and he posts the lectures online so attendance wasn't required which was nice.

Professor Sorensen is very nice and understanding! There is only a homework assignment per week. All other points for the class are exams. He gives extra credit during random lectures if you are there. If you know the concepts and how to do the problems done in class you will do well on the exams! He responds fast to emails too.

Great professor and super nice guy, but the class itself is pretty boring. 1 point of extra credit randomly for attendance. Class is manageable and professor is very understanding and accommodates to needs of students. Definitely recommend doing homework to pad your grade - HW is significantly easier than mgmt200.
He is willing to help if you reach out to him. He answers any questions that are given out, and provides a formula sheet with the exams.
Professor is intelligent and nice, but lecture can become boring and distracting at times

I was nervous to take the class going into it because of some of the reviews, but the professor does care about your success if you reach out when needed. He mentioned they restructured the class based on previous years reviews. Only bad part was lectures were hard to hear unless you sat up front.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Sorenson. I accidentally did the wrong homework once and he gave me a 100% for the assignment I missed. He is very understanding, you just have to reach out to him. He gives lots of practice questions and the exams were online with a 24 hr window to take them. Very caring professor and definitely one of my favorites!
Professor Sorensen is pretty nice. He gave us a lots of practice example in the class.
Good communicator, class is 2/3 exams though and they're certainly no joke

Avoid this guy at all costs (take it at Ivy Tech if possible). It is HIM, not the material. I'm not surprised at all that most don't like him, he is a terrible teacher. Yes, accounting is boring but Sorensen makes it 2x as bad. He is NOT helpful - I tried to meet him outside of class but he kept pushing me off to TA. Scott QUIT, you're very bad !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get the dislike for Prof Sorensen! He is a genuinely great and caring professor and it shows in his class. While his class can be a bit boring, a lot of that comes from the generally uninteresting material in 201, not necessarily him. Provides extra credit for attendance, super helpful formula sheets on exams and has shortened class times.

Prof is monotone and boring however, the slides are helpful in learning the concepts which were pretty easy. Exams are straightforward and he provided a formula sheet with the necessary information to complete them. He is an understanding professor that will try to accommodate students if they need it.

God I'm so glad it's over - this guy is TERRIBLE. He is just up there going through the motions - so boring, monotone, just reading PPTs. I hated having to go listen to this guy. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Scott, do us all a big favor and quit, you're not a good teacher, stop trying to play one.

Scott is a great professor and makes 505 an easy class. The exams and homework are very straightforward. He cares a lot about his students and is always open to helping students out. I found it easier to read the textbook instead of going to class. However, he sometimes gives out extra credit if you attend classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He's nothing phenomenal, and his lectures surely aren't that exciting. You can get that from others' reviews. The content however is the important thing. Exams 1&2 are fairly easy, so try to learn that content better as the last 2 are more difficult. The class isn't too hard, but some units are tedious which makes things a little more difficult.
Sorenson is a fine professor. He records lectures and seems to care about student learning. Not an amazing lecturer but most accounting professors aren't.

Sorensen is a good guy and cares about the students, but the lectures can be a bit dry if you are bit tired. There are 4 exams, and he gives 1 point EC randomly throughout the semester for attendance. Exams are online with webcam, but the formula sheets are super helpful. Great communicator and HW assignments take less time than MGMT 200.

Professor Sorensen is a great guy and this class was the best accounting class I have taken yet. He talks a little slow, but he posts everything on Brightspace so you can watch the lectures after class on 2x speed and finish the material in about half the time. The slides are hugely beneficial to the exams.

Good god does this man talk slow. Most of the time I end up skipping lecture and watching it later at 1.75x speed. But he gives an unreal amount of info on the formula sheets you can use during you exam so I like him

Sorenson is a really nice guy and pretty funny from time to time. However to no fault of his own, his voice absolutely puts me to sleep. Staying awake and engaged during his lectures is difficult due to how monotone he is. He seems to know what he's talking about and I'm sure I could've done better in this course if I were able to stay awake.

He is very knowledgeable and accessible for help. I recommend reading the textbook because he teaches right out of it. If you read the textbook, lectures are unnecessary. Lectures are monotonous and boring, but he provides extra credit randomly for attendance. He isn't a bad professor by any means, but the content is just not very interesting.
Good teacher who is fair to all students. Lectures are not the greatest, but being someone who is quite monotone themselves, I can definitely feel for him.

Scott is such a nice and helpful person. He really cares about you as a student and is always there to help. I found the course to be very easy (much easier than MGMT200). I never watched the lectures and instead just read the textbook and took notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He does not give more percentage on exam. He just gave us same percentage as the homework. The grading system was the worst thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Sorenson is honestly a really great resource. He's made it very clear that he cares about students' success in his class. He's very accessible outside of class and he responds to emails relatively quick. During lectures, he is a little monotone and it can be hard to pay attention, but if you really put the work in, you can do really well.

Professor Sorenson is such a nice professor, he genuinely cares about his students and if you email him about concerns or questions he almost always accommodates to help you out. If you attend class regularly he's more likely to help you out when it comes to earning as many points as possible in the class. He's a dad so he understands kids

Although he teaches what many see as a boring class, Professor Sorensen himself is a good instructor and never blindsides you with any material. You can easily get 100s on all homework if you take notes/go to class. Exam questions are pretty fair and often look like the examples he does in class. If you're a good student, you will be just fine.

The material itself that Professor Sorensen is teaching isn't the best, but he honestly gives a lot of feedback for the complex material. I think he is a solid professor and that he makes the class bearable as well. Also, he always gives updates to us as students on due dates and exams which I like.
Although the professor may be a bit boring, this class is an easy A. The average was a B+/A-. Just do all your Mcgraw-Hill homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Its a relatively boring class and like someone else said, he can be a bit dry. He will always be there to answer questions, and he will often end his lectures early. While the subject is boring, the class is what you make of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For everyone saying that he is a "terrible professor", they are upset that they have to put in effort for a class. Yes, he is dry, but he truly does care about his students. He's real down to Earth and will ALWAYS answer any questions you have. His exams aren't too bad if you do the Foundational 15 and Review Problems he gives you as practice. 5/5.

Sorenson is a great professor. He's a little dry, but he's very clear with his lecture materials and due dates. Just take notes on the slides, do the homework on time, and do the practice problems and you'll do great on the exams. These other reviews probably just didn't study. If you do, this is an easy class to get an A in
My guy Scott Sorenson is terrible. Would recommend not taking this course, especially with him. Boring and dry when teaching in lectures.

This is probably the worst professor at Purdue. I'm literally writing this review in his class right now because of how appalled I am he is considered a professor at Purdue. He legit just reads of lecture slides, doesn't look to see if students have questions and does not give proper guidance for the class. Class isn't too hard but WORST PROFESSOR.
Sitting in this guy's class each week listening to his monotone regurgitation of the PPTs was worse than a root canal !
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely TERRIBLE prof ! He CAN'T teach, he just stands there and reads the slides, so bad. I had to put in so much extra time to do well in the class - I'm going to switch to Finance major. because of this guy - what a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As long as you watch the videos and do the homework. This class shouldn't be that hard to pass. Make sure you do the practices on Connect before an exam as it helps a lot.

First off. I do not watch his lectures. I've heard horror stories. His slides, which he provides, are sufficient to teach yourself. He is a really nice guy and I've enjoyed being in his course, though the content itself is well.... accounting. Its boring.
BEST ADVICE FOR U! RUN!!!!!!

I can't believe I have to pay for taking this class, this guy is so bad. Where did they get him??? He just reads the PPTs and is so boring. I'd rather have a root canal done than sit through another class with this guy ! Avoid if possible but I see he is back again for summer and fall and only one teaching it - what a nightmare !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Stopped watching lectures after the second week. Easy class but he really cant teach.
He just slowly reads the PowerPoint to the class every time. You just have to try and teach yourself

Scott Sorenson seems like a lovely person, BUT his teaching method makes for a great lullaby if you want to take a nap in his class. He reads from the slides and has a very monotonous voice and speaks very slowly. He does his examples from slides by reading it to us, rather than showing us. Homeworks aren't terrible because of the unlimited checks.

Very nice professor, impeccable lecture notes. However (maybe because it's a grad class) he doesn't post lecture notes which forces into an attendance mandatory class. Exams are pretty tough. Otherwise, he is one of the better profs out there, definitely recommend him for other classes.
Very caring. For HWs, he basically put emphasis on computation, which is not very helpful for understanding.

Lectures are directly from lecture notes posted on Brightspace. Exams were mostly quite easy but with some tricky multiple-choice questions. HW is overwhelmingly easy but could be a bit more reflective of the exam content.

Not generous with partial credit, so small mistakes on exams can cost you big-time in this class. The final exam was worth 200/600 points in the class, and it was difficult. Homeworks were to be turned in in-person in paper form, which was inconvenient. Lectures were just him writing out definitions and theorems and proofs- not super helpful.

Very fair exams and reasonable amount of homework. His lecture style is easy to follow. MA35301 is the opposite of the "multiply matrices pointlessly" sort of linear algebra class. It's focused on proofs and actually understanding what's going on logically, which Professor Ulrich accomplishes well.

Amazing professor. Material is structured based on the standard text for this course but he makes his own revisions which are quite helpful (clearer proofs, more precise notation). Explains everything thoroughly in lecture and tries to actually develop intuition for the theorems. Exams consist of few questions but aren't unreasonably difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lecture notes are impeccable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the best Professors I've ever had. Very fair but also understanding & kind. He doesn't use a textbook for 503 & doesn't write everything he says on the board. Tip: Listen carefully to what he says and write it down if it isn't obvious to you. He is very helpful during office hours. 11/10
Incredibly consistent and competent. The material in this course is inherently difficult and complex, and the grading curve isn't particularly friendly, but he did a great job teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ulrich is a very precise, organised lecturer. This class was hard, and the homeworks were weekly and difficult, but I learnt a lot of useful pure algebra knowledge.  He's not an exciting lecturer, but is very helpful and friendly in office hours. You will definitely understand the material if you put the work in. Great professor!
He explains all problems in-depth and is a great recitation professor. He does make time to help you after class if you have questions.

Prof. Upadhyaya is an excellent 2k1 recitation professor. His recitations have just the right mix of lecture review and example problems. He's an excellent explainer, breaks down difficult examples/concepts well, and takes time to answer questions thoroughly. Highly recommend his section for 2k1.

Fantastic lectures, seems to genuinely care that students do well. Listens to feedback, holds review sessions and extra problem solving sessions when needed. Attendance is not mandatory but I would highly recommend attending his lectures.

While this class is notorious for having exam averages in the 40s, Prof Upadhyaya really did his best in explaining the material. He recorded his lectures,broke down concepts slowly, worked out examples, and even did supplementary recordings when students had questions. His explanations really made things click, even if the test material was hard

teaches a notoriously hard class, but very clearly cares about you succeeding. a lot of people asked questions during lecture, and he always tried to make sure you understood. maybe not always the clearest on explaining topics or ideas, but will work with you to help understand.
He's a great guy who takes hours out of his schedule to run exam review sessions that basically reteach the whole class
Pramey is a solid professor. He lectures well and was very easy to interact with in office hours when I needed help. Would recommend.

Dr. Upudhyaya's lectures are some of the best lectures I've ever attended. His lectures are paced very well and he is very good at recognizing when students are struggling with new concepts. He is extremely accessible outside of class, and hosts 3-4 hour review sessions before exams.

He is by far one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He is extremely accessible outside the class and is very approachable. His teaching pace is also perfect and you will understand everything clearly if you pay attention. He doesnt mind slowing down and repeating concepts should people need him to. Get this professor, you wont regret it!

Very nice person and very good teacher. He makes sure everyone in the classroom understands each topic before moving on. Dedicates extra time to students when they express a lack of understanding in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a gem of a prof. Lectures aren't mandatory, but lecture + book  much better understanding. Won't hesitate to re-explain material. Make sure to read the book. Exams are fair, but tough for sure. Most of my respect for him comes from his exam review lectures, which he'll go for as long as needed to go over all the material. Love him

Amazing professor! Explains the simplest of doubts cleary with a proper explanation. Breaks down complicated numerical for better understandability. Devoted extra time for students before the exam day to go over important concepts and numerical which was really helpful. Not strict at all, very chill and enthusiastic about his work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Umbeck is one of the best professors at Purdue. Even during a 7:30am class, he still brought energy and engagement to each lecture that made the content easy to follow and understand. The course material can get a little confusing at times, but Dr. Umbeck goes over everything in great detail and answers questions perfectly.
One of the nicest professors at Purdue and teaches really well because he genuinely cares about the subject.

I really enjoyed his class. He does not require attendance yet most of the class still shows up every day because he makes the subject so interesting. I wasn't sure about econ until I took this class.
One of the best professor in Purdue. Always patient to students, answer questions on time.
Hard grader
Professor Ryan is a good teacher but I found his tests to really difficult and hard to prepare for.

Making an entry-level statistical inference course interesting is a very difficult task, but Professor Umbeck has a bright and encouraging energy that makes you want to pay attention simply out of respect for the effort he is putting into making the material understandable. Fantastic person, gives great feedback on issues with Stata HW (use him!).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ryan brings an energy to lectures that is unmatched. He is super knowledgeable in his field and is eager to share with everybody and help however he can. He's always available and answers stuff really effectively. One of the best experiences I've had at Purdue, even though my head struggled to wrap itself around the content sometimes. 10/10

Professor Umbeck is absolutely incredible. He is the ONLY professor that kept me afloat this semester. He made me feel like an actual human and I felt like he actually heard my questions and concerns throughout the course. Would totally recommend taking any of his courses.

If you're taking MGMT 310, take it with another professor. Umbeck's class had very little structure, and it took him weeks to get things graded. He does weekly quizzes and his there is very little info given on what tests will cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hands down best professor at Purdue

Really really nice professor, he is very willing to help. If you go to lecture, you won't even need the book at all. Pretty fair exams and quizzes. Not a terribly difficult class. I expect to get a B and I didn't put very much effort into studying; however I did pay attention in class and take detailed notes.
Very nice teacher as well as a person. His lecture is super expressive and easy to understand. You won't regret taking his class

Decent professor. Exams are straightforward and a mix between free response and multiple choice. I relied heavily on the textbook but others just used their notes in class. Sometimes the homework was a bit time consuming, but nothing awful.

Awesome professor. Lectures are really informative, and he is very clear in how he explains things. He'll stop lecture and re-cover one small item if a student asks a question about it and also throws multiple different scenarios about how questions can be asked. Exams were kinda difficult, mainly because he only gave 50 minutes to complete them.

This was an online class and I'm assuming he may be a little better in person but he did almost nothing for the online section during the summer. He would only answer a few emails and would posts things late giving you less time to read and write the discussion answers. I did however ask for a deadline extension and he gave us that.
Very good prof! Knowing his stuff and explain it crystal clear! You don't even have to read the book. Very useful and exams are very related to his lectures.
His homework are very hard and sometimes impossible to solve!

Condori hate is way overblown. The course structure is extremely forgiving with exam, quiz, HW drops, up to 5-6% extra credit too. Go to his office hours or the TA office hours for homework/quiz help. Exams were very fair and graded generously. Lectures aren't great, but just watch Jeff Hanson on the side and you'll be set for an A. Statics is fun!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really not much else to say as the other comments sum up the professor very well. He told the entire class day one that he was in trouble with the university due to performance from previous semesters. Out of 3 exams 90% of the class was not able to finish any of them in the allotted time. Exam averages were so bad they will not tell the class.

Lectures are behind by a week. We are learning material right now which was literally on the exam study guide. Constantly lost in class. Can't tell when he's teaching material or asking a question.  Doing examples does not equal teaching. Why is that why we answer it like that? So many questions.

I have had him for three classes, the content is hard but he is good at lecturing. A lot of people don't like him and I didn't used to either. However, his exams are incredibly fair and I've had no issues with wondering if I will pass or not. There are way worse professors in the program and he does not deserve all the hate.

I didn't think he was a bad lecturer but the course is not well organized. Felt like I was gonna fail the whole time and then get huge bumps at the end. Difficult class imo and hw is exhausting, expects high quality work. high time requirement and exam prep is miserable. ~8 hours per week on hw

Prof. Condori's classes are by and large quite disorganized and his lectures are somewhat lacking. He is hard to reach outside of class and changes the course schedule and grading policies last minute. He provides a lot of homework and quiz drops, but the classes are generally not enjoyable.

He gets lots of bad reviews because the content of the class is difficult for many people. He clearly cares about what he is teaching and does lots of examples in class that I found make homework easier. I found him approachable after classes. Handwriting can be sloppy at times. Exams had some questions that were way too hard.
Too heavy homeworks

Honestly many people told me when I got to upper CE courses that I would miss Condori. I realized this is because he gives a lot of extra credit and lets students use cheat sheets for the exams. He is genuinely a decent professor when you see what else CE has in store. For this class I'd recommend reverse image search and Jeff Hanson. Good luck!

I have had this guy 3 times in a row now, CE 270, 298, and now 371. Worst lecturer I've ever had. Does not give useful examples that are not comparable to homework questions. Can hardly read the class notes which aren't even useful anyway. Gives quizzes that are nothing like the homework. Extremely unreliable and hard to reach when you need him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nit picky and had unclear grading criteria on homework and exams. Cared too much about neatness/presentation. Expected students to dedicate lots of time- even suggesting that homework should be solved seperately and then rewritten entirely to have cleaner presentation. The lectures were ok but I mainly went for the attendance extra credit.

This professor is potentially the worst professor I have ever had at my years at Purdue. His lectures make no sense and often go off on tangents about advanced theory that you will never need, not be tested on. The exams and homework and unlike any problems from the lectures or each other, so good luck trying to study. Worst Prof experience in CE

Professor Condori's classes are theory-focused and challenging, but homework is supportive with points for attempts (Part 1) and corrections (Part 2). Exams are difficult, though often curved or adjusted late in the semester. He's deeply committed to student success and approachable. You get the grade you earn in his class for sure.

He hasn't showed up for class in weeks. The entire last month of the course has been taught by TA's. We were told his email was "deactivated". Was he fired? Who knows. We should NOT have to take this final if that is the case. Awful experience in his class. All good reviews are fake.

This class was fairly difficult, but it isn't all that bad if you attend all of the lectures. There is a good amount of homework, but it really helps you understand and apply the content. Overall, I think he does a great job teaching the content and helping you understand. He is also helpful during his office hours.
Very traditionalist professor, has no mercy for you if you aren't sacrificing your entire life to learn from him.

He is not a good lecturer. You are better off showing up solely for the attendance extra credit points. His explanations are subpar at best and is not able to answer student questions when asked. He spends far too much time on theory and not enough on actually solving the problems or teaching the steps that should be taken. Positive ratings are cap

For statics I felt like he was a good lecturer and made sure to connect concepts we were learning in class to civil applications. Exams test your fundamental understanding of concepts and are easier than homework and quizzes. Homework is designed to ensure understanding the mistakes made. It's a good basis for civil engineering fundamentals.
he is an awful lecturer; you are better off using the internet compared to how he teaches. There is also no clear criteria for how grading is done, and it is entirely bipolar based on the TA's

Literally horrible, he should never teach statics ever again. :( 
RIP my gpa

Had to do a full grade appeal in order to get a C- because he wouldn't admit that grading mistakes were made on practically all of my labs. Took me over 5 months after the semester ended.
