Lecture attendance is for extra credit, exam 1 wasn't bad but as time went on the class just got more ridiculous. Labs could take hours on end, TAs saved me.
Exam 1 virtually completely unrelated to lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Condori was a very good lecturer. I enjoyed learning about things theoretically in his lectures but the class requires that you do work outside of class. Reading the textbook and asking questions is like 50% of the class because there's too many examples to go over in lecture. He was always available for office hours and i went every week

Lectures could've used more practice examples before delving into heavy theory. Office hour heavy class. Lots of study material from past exams and set up exam practice sessions. Overall, a good person intent on growing from mistakes but hasn't quite landed the execution. Curving due to giving too much extra credit was a very questionable decision.

One of if not the worst professor in the civil department. Does not know how to effectively lecture students on complex material. Homework problems do not mirror lecture, test problems do not mirror homework. Failed 35% of the class Fall 2023. Awful at his job

This dude is a few fries short of a Happy Meal. Spends entire lectures mumbling about theory when exams and homeworks do not reflect his lecture. Proceeded to curve the class DOWN without zero warning after failing 40% of the class the semester before. If you get stuck with him just go ahead and start going to church again, cause you'll need it.

He is undoubtedly the worst professor in civil. Second time taking this class with him again after he failed 35% last semester. He legit curved the class down because he thought he made it too easy this semester. Lectures are useless and mumbles on about theories instead of teaching how to work out a problem. Avoid this man.

My friend scored a 99.5 and got a A-. He himself sent us an email that 100%+ will be given an A and A+. Another friend scored 95.2 and still got a B+. All he does is mumble in his lectures and his TAs are left with the actual teaching bit.

3 lectures a week and they are just 50 minutes of him rambling about theory based stuff, and then the exams are a super specific problem you have never seen before, and his TAs are incredibly tough graders. Was at a 69.5% and he would not round up for me to pass. Just an amazing dude.

For my class specifically he gave an excess of extra credit but then implemented a reverse curve. This reverse curve caused me to drop from a B+ to a B-. I am just disappointed, there is certainly room for improvement. My TA was a lot better at explaining the concepts in office hours. If you are struggling I suggest attending those.

Grade shouldve been an A-. He gave us 6% extra credit, but for final grades he changed the grading scheme to be out of 106 instead of 100. This change was made without notice, my TA didnt even know about it. No mention of a curve all semester so everyone thought the class was uncurved. Finally emailed why and decision to curve down was last minute.

This man goes on a random tangent for 2 weeks about how you need to read multiple 500 page books in their entirety to pass his class and be an engineer, but if you think thats the worst oh brother. This man randomly decided to hit the most devious move since Bill Clinton and fleece every student by illegally curving DOWN two letter grades smh.

Awful class. failed 35% last fall and looks like now will be no different. Lectures are mumbled nonsense, and dropping lower exam is pointless when the averages are all in the 60s TOPS. 270 is arguably one of the hardest yet most important core classes yet its "taught" by a man I wouldn't trust to pet sit for an evening. CE dept should be ashamed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst part of his classes were his disjointed lectures. Uribe would consistently finish class in the middle of a lecture leaving the confusing chapter info incomplete until next class. Beyond this it was near impossible to apply Uribe's longwinded theoretical examples to actual problems encountered in the homework and on exams. good luck.

Worst professor I have ever had throughout my 4 years at school. Very hard to understand lectures and he doesnt even update his lecture notes properly on Brightspace so they are pointless to use when preparing for the exams. He changed his mind about the way he will grade exams several times. He is little to no help when asked to explain things.

Professor Condori speaks softly and mumbles a lot in lecture. He focuses on theory/deriving equations rather than doing examples and teaching how to solve problems. Exams are fair if you prepare properly and do the past exams. Highest Midterm Score replaced lowest midterm score. Weekly quizzes which are difficult, but you get unlimited attempts.

Professor Condori speaks very softly and mumbles a lot in lecture. He focuses a lot on theory and deriving equations rather than doing examples and teaching how to solve problems. Exams are very difficult and do not resemble practice exams. However lowest mid-term was dropped and you get extra credit for attending class.

Professor Uribe speaks very softly and focuses too much on the theory versus actual applications. Most of his class time is spent deriving equations, and when he does examples, he does not finish them or use numbers. Really nice guy. Not the best professor. Used highest exam score as both exams though, and gave extra credit as well.

This professor was AWFUL, lectures were hard to understand and the TA's did most of the teaching. It was his first time teaching, and it was painfully clear. Changed how he was going to grade the class multiple times and did not have one passing average between two classes and four midterms. Exams are nothing like past exams.

That Condori is a professor is an insult to Purdue's reputation as a "world class" university. Mumbles broken english through every class, very vague on expectations and exams are nothing like past exams. No offense to him but you'd honestly be better off if the TAs taught the class, they at least seem competent and in touch with students' needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man has no clue how to teach. Dynamics is a difficult enough course without having to contend with subpar instruction. Highly recommend attending office hours and the textbook is your best friend. However, the best alternative is to switch out of the class entirely, New students beware!

Mumbles during lectures, hard to stay attentive when so monotone. Practice exams given prior to exams are on completely different difficulty scales than actual exams. CE 270 TAs were more helpful than him. Would have hoped for a better experience this semester.

Painfully obvious its his first time teaching CE 298 & CE 270, mumbles through vague lectures loosely related to homework. Overcomplicates basics, TAs do all the teaching. Office hours a necessity, Structures and Dynamics are hard enough without this BS. Study from the book, lectures are a disorganized time-waster, don't know how he got this job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really great professor. I would highly recommend to take him if you can. Lectures are short so we he lets you off like 15 minutes early and still manages to teach a very wide array of material.

He explains complex topics well and respects students. Much more down to earth and approachable than some of the other professors here. He is pretty funny and there is no iclicker or mandatory attendance, yet the class is pretty full which means students actually like hearing him talk.

Dr. Umbeck has been at Purdue since 1975. That said this class was one of the most difficult I've ever taken, given the circumstances etc. Those that did exceptionally well in this class came with strong, even VERY strong background in Finance and Accounting. If you are not strong in Stats, Finance, Accounting you'll find this class VERY difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Umbeck is one of the WORST professors you will meet. On the very first day of class, he will tell the class that he doesn't care if he FLUNKs you. He gives out only a Mid-Term and a Finals Test. It only matters that you obtain his old exams. Memorize the answers on his old exams and you will obtain an 'A'. Otherwise, who knows?

Going into senior year, hardest class I've ever taken without a doubt. I have no chance at pulling my grade up and my GPA is going to take such a hit. Unless you have a great understanding of law and a half decent econ background it's going to be pretty difficult. The class is made up of 3 exams and that's all.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't ever take this class... Three multiple choice exams. Don't take it in summer or spring. Just don't take it. There is curve but it is fixed curve so it does not depend on the average to the class.

I do not recommend this class. Law and Economics course is just horrible. There are three exams and those are impossible. If you want to get a bad grade, please take it. There is no help in this class. Just don't take this course. Horrible... just horrible.

I respect Professor Umbeck. I felt he was very fair. He's a bit long-winded and his tests are hard, but if you do the practice tests and homework you should not be surprised by anything on the midterm or final. But be prepared to work. It's a hard class and a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Teamed up with professor Fisher to team-teach econ and law. This was possibly the worst-run class I have experienced in my time as a student. There was no student support, no specific class schedulecalendar, no exam help, and possibly the worst part of all: full class lectures AND hours upon hours of required deathly boring videos.

Umbeck is clearly a master in his field and makes lectures interesting. I thoroughly enjoyed a lot of the examples that he conveyed to explain different topics of law and economics. The exams are tough, but would still recommend.
Has him 20 years ago and I still recall some of his lectures!  Don't fool yourself though.. He's tough!
awesome
the best prof I've come across
great classes!
He made economics a pleasure to learn
best of the best
One of the best lecturers I have ever had.  He will influence your perspective about the world around you.
Dr. Umbeck is obviously a master of his field. He knows the material as if it were his own vital stats. He conveys it clearly, even though it is a tough field to learn.
Makes economics seem interesting and fun. That's a difficult thing to do when studying economics
I was uninterested in microeconomics till I sat in his class and decided that the world runs on his subject!
best professor i have had at purdue's business school so far.

A Lecture hall of 150 students (2 classes of 150 each) with no attendance requirement was always jam packed. the man talks  very softly, yet the class is so quiet, you can hear him all the way at the back
The way this guy teaches is great and unique. He makes this boring course ECON accessible to anyone and gives a broad understanding to it. Tests and Exams are very challenging.
Awesome teacher. Econ professors should learn Econ from him so that they can teach better in class. Really was an eye-opening class for me. This is the way Econ should be taught folks.
good teacher, explains well, but tests are much harder than they need to be.
No Comments
Awesome teacher--great sense of humor, explains well--difficult tests!
he's cool and funny looking
Professor Uyeda's notes are easy to follow and templates are posted before class. Attendance is mandatory and iClicker is used. I would take a class with Uyeda again.

Dr. Uyeda has got to be one of the best profs at Purdue! His explanations are incredibly clear, and you almost never need to reference the textbook to excel in this class. He's kind, compassionate, caring, and always open to answering students' questions, no matter how "silly" they may seem. 100% recommend registering for his class over Dr. C's.

Probably best chem professor. Has note packets that prepare you very well for the exams. Exams are easy if you take time to practice and study. Show up to lectures because he'll sometimes give out extra points during lecture. Great lecturer. He is also super sweet.

Literally the best chemistry professor ever!!! I am terrible at chemistry but he made the class super understandable and gave a lot of resources to study for exams. The exams, the ones he wrote, were carbon copies to the practice ones. He's so so amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best chem prof! Prepped us well for exams, very approachable in office hours, gave extra credit for iClicker when 3/4 ditched class at 9:30 AM. I scored over 100% on all exams and felt confident before each one (way better than chem129). He is kind + patient when people ask questions and doesn't insult other orgo chem classes (unlike Dr. C).

Chill guy, explanations are aight. Easier to learn on your own, textbook, or online IMO. Started skipping lectures and had 10x easier job getting As. Beware, some participation polls are for extra credit. I guess he's upset that some people don't like his lectures? Weird, but cry I guess? So yeah, be careful of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: awesome lecturer, made the concepts super clear, and office hours are SUPER helpful

Uyeda was very good at lecturing. He explained concepts slowly and thoroughly and provided printed notes for us to use. His tests were very fair, and the notes, PSO worksheets, and practice exams were enough for studying without the textbook. The tests were also graded within a few days. The TAs were very helpful and good at explaining concepts.

The textbook didn't really matter in this course (I used it like one time). Make sure to go to PSO because the example questions are similar to the exam. The TAs are always there to help during their scheduled hours (trust me I went almost every time) & open to emails outside of hours. Take advantage of the resources, and you will do well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Uyeda is a good teacher and will go over everything that appears on the exam, sometimes it is a smaller detail but you have always seen it. The exams are difficult and it is important to get as many points as possible on the first exam because they get harder. He does good practice questions during class just doesn't always give enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall good professor but lectures are boring.

Uyeda is a really amazing professor who really cares about student success. His exams are hard but fair and using the previous exams provided will help you do well. Make sure not to fall behind in this class as it goes fast and content builds. An A is very possible with hard work.
Overall a very nice professor. Knows a lot about what he is talking about. Would recommend anyone interested at taking chm255
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Uyeda is a pretty good professor. He definitely understands what he is teaching and he does a good job communicating. Lectures can be very boring, 50min feels like 5 hours in there. Overall, he's everything that you would need and want in a professor -- just not super funny or anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final grade weighed heavily on exams. No homework or extra credit. Heavy content class. In lectures, he barely goes over them before introducing a new concept. He fills in notes with you but goes too fast to follow along. You are left very unprepared. First class I actually wished for homework/quizzes. Harsh grading. Thinks C averages are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor, and I really enjoyed the class. You have to study to do well, but he gives you practice exams that help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful professor. He is truly a great guy. I really appreciated how he ran his lectures too. Prof was great, but CHM 255 wasn't. The class was nearly completely based on exams. The lab was also separate from the lecture class and only a single credit.

He is a great professor and makes everything very clear. He makes learning the material actually enjoyable. But take notes and watch the lectures for sure! He actually cares if students are struggling. This class is very test heavy, but after a bad class average, he allowed us an opportunity to get points back!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Uyeda is the only professor at Purdue who has made me enjoy AND understand chemistry. He is truly is an AMAZING lecturer and professor and you can tell he cares about what he's doing.
Grádeme was heavily based on tests. Material is complex
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Such a sweet man. I loved sitting in his class and his voice was fun to listen to as it was animated and always upbeat. Fills out his notes by hand with you so you can see all his examples and mechanisms.

Dr. Uyeda is super smart and an amazing lecturer. His lectures are very clear and are on Boilercast. Majority of the grade for the class is exams, but they are pretty easy as the content is straight from the notes. Plus there's always extra credit on exams. Recitation worksheets are graded for completion, providing an easy 100 points.

This man is amazing! Attend the lectures or else you are screwed. Also the recitations are super helpful. The class is 80% test and 20% worksheet completion. There is extra credit on EVERY test. I am horrific at chemistry I really suck at it but this professor somehow taught in a way that worked for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the greatest professors that I have ever had. Although he is a genius and everything is extremely easy for him, he treats you as a beginner and helps you understand concepts with ease. He clearly is passionate about organic chemistry, and it shows during his amazing lectures.

i was 3 points close to getting an A in the class. I talked to him and the TAs and I was able to get 4 points back. He is a very great professor and I do not recommend cramming everything before the exam. You will need to understand the chemical mechanisms.

An extremely good professor that obviously knows the content very well and knows how to teach it to students. Exams can be pretty difficult even though he gives you practice exams. My biggest thing is that there are barely any (500) points in the course, so if you fail an exam and do mediocre on the others, there's a good chance you can still fail.

Very very knowledgeable on the course material and explains things in a super clear way. Getting a good grade is very possible in his classes, as he gives you all you need to learn. You just need to put in the effort to learn it.

Great professor, he explains things very well in lecture. I found CHM 255 to be pretty easy just by going to lecture and doing the practice problems before exams. Recitation is optional and graded only for completion.

So helpful and is amazing at explaining the material, he is such a smart man and a wonderful professor. He made this class so easy and I was nervous about taking organic chemistry after a rough first semester. My favorite professor I have had at Purdue so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: so nice and helpful. I wish he could teach every chemistry class I take!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Uyeda is a WONDERFUL professor.  Easily my favorite so far at Purdue.  For someone who absolutely hates chemistry and did sub-par in chem 115/116, I thoroughly enjoyed orgo and did well,  mainly because of this professor.  He goes through each topic and explains the topics so that they are easily understandable, and he cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Makes hard topics easier. Also takes student questions seriously and reviews material before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Uyeda is an incredible lecturer. He explains things very well and speaks in a clear and precise manner. If you're ever confused he'll make time to sit down with you one on one and he'll take his time with explaining and making sure that you understand. Full of information! He really loves what he teaches and you it shows in his teaching style.

THIS MAN IS JUST WONDERFUL!! First prof ever at Purdue that I have had that actually cares! Always super nice and actually knows how to teach. Gave lecture notes and explain everything clearly. I was shocked how great his class was because of his young age.
The book problems and practice exams help a ton!!!  I loved having him.  You don't get an A without putting in effort but getting a good grade is possible.

Really good professor!  I was scared to take orgo, but he explains everything in a straightforward manner so it's really easy to understand.  He also spends the first couple of minutes reviewing material from the previous class which doesn't seem important but it's a really nice touch!
He is very hard. His class is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was a good class, valuable information taught, very reasonable expectation with homeworks/exams, and learned a lot. His teaching is mediocre sometimes, as he likes to brush through certain topics fast with minimal explanations leaving it up to you to understand it to the depth required to do the homeworks. But it's not impossible and doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Vikas is a pretty basic but good professor. Lectures are sometimes tough to understand but are handwritten, so the pace is easy to follow. Exams are straightforward, with few tricks. He's a pretty chill guy too and keeps things real with the class. Sometimes he will joke during lectures and catch you off guard. Just don't bug him about crib sheets.

He is a good professor but admittedly took some getting used to.  I learned a lot, this class was hard.  The good thing is it counts as a math class.  I would say he is not very good at answering questions in class, either repeating what he already has stated or answering a question not asked.  Apart from that he was a good prof.
Good Professor, really wants to make sure the students learn. Responds quickly to questions.

He proved to be a better professor than I had originally thought. An online class focused on using software that I had never used before was more likely why I had difficulty at first. Thankfully, he was willing to work with me and provide some grace so that I could get back on track and have a better understanding of the course. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor and super nice guy, likes to make his students laugh. If you put the time in and show up to lecture you will be just fine. Lectures are somewhat unstructured but they're informative and easy to follow. Assigns weekly hw, labs, and in class assignments, but they're easy if you go to class. Gives candy to students who ask questions!

Overall, very solid lectures with plenty of practice problems done in class to help out with HW and exams. Additional practice problems were posted that were harder than exams for further practice. He clearly cares about his students with easier grading on harder exams and his attention to questions during class. Tells fun stories during class!

Merwade gave excellent lectures and always uploaded his clear and concise notes. He was very easy to follow and always willing to stop to answer questions. I enjoyed having in-class activities to help practice problems, and we always received a helpful study guide before exams.

Excellent professor who gives clear lectures. Homework grading can be harsh, but make sure to do resubmissions or you will not pass. Tests are very straightforward with nothing unexpected, and labs were step-by-step instructions that usually took about an hour or so to complete. Funny guy who cares deeply about hydrology and his students.
Dr. Merwade is a genuine guy and a caring professor. He puts in the extra time to work with students if you're willing to ask for help. He is the best hydraulics professor at Purdue.

His class was very well organized and I got a thorough understanding of the class topics.  He is very good at explaining the material in a clear and concise manner.  He's also lighthearted and sometimes says funny things.  His class was actually enjoyable.  Practice problems were provided for exams and the exams themselves were relatively easy.
Dr. Merwade has a great lecturing style. I feel like I got the chance to really learn about hydraulics, and I felt very prepared for exams. He grades fairly.

Prof. Merwade is a great guy! He doesn't come across as funny at first, but he made the class laugh regularly and learned everyone's names. His teaching style of lectures and in-class assignments is extremely helpful for homework and tests. On top of that, the labs for this class can be time consuming but they are not that difficult.
Prof. Merwade's assignments are super helpful for understanding the material and homework is reasonable. His lectures are clear and concise, and he is very clear about class expectations.
Great Professor! I had CE340 with him. He has a very clear grading policy. Homework and Exam are related closely!!(Do your homework and you will get good grade on your exam)
CE542 Good at explaining examples, Willing to answer questions after class. Benevolent with grades. Nice personality.

The homework for the class were his example problems word for word, to do actual problems on your own he posted sample problems which you needed the right edition of the textbook for (after he told us that any edition would work). He refused to post anything online & I didn't think he was very good at explaining things.

Great teacher.  Loads of example problems used in class; personally thats how I learn best.  He took time to get students to participate in class and ask questions.  As a student you're able to hear what he has to say, take notes, and have time to comprehend what was instructed.  Homework problems worked out for the most part in class too.

Low exam averages and super picky on how notes are distributed (doesn't post the examples until after chapter is finished) and handled (called student out for taking pictures of her worked through problem). All or nothing attendance is completely ridiculous and the group projects are extremely disorganized

She has a lack of patience with students, whenever students ask questions instead of answering and helping she instead has critiqued students for their lack of knowledge. There are multiple cases of her intercepting students from learning the material or giving them resources to study for exams. It seems she doesn't care for students success at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the worst professors I've had at Purdue. Her attendance policy for 413 was points-based all or nothing (so technically required if you want 10% of your grade). She is hard to hear, she writes on the board but often in places hard to read, and her exams are difficult. The group projects are a mess, too. Avoid if possible!

She honestly shouldn't have a teaching job. The worst instructor I've ever experienced. We asked her to release study material to the class that SHE told us we would need to study for the exam and she said no???
Took 413 with her. This was the worst class of my life.

I can't say I have enjoyed her class at all. The exam was incredibly hard compared to the practice problems and her ability to communicate is nonexistent. I wouldn't recommend in the slightest. Take class with someone else.

Please do not take this class if there are other options available. Grade is basically fully decided by final exam. She cannot solve and gets tripped up on her own in class practice questions. Expects you to be able to complete question perfectly after seeing one example that she struggles to solve. Struggles to answer in class questions as well.

Homework + Attendance = 30%, Midterm = 35%, Final Exam = 35%.  Extremely hard exams.  I felt like I could've just read the slides and gotten the same info instead of having to show up to class.  My raw grade for the overall class was a 53.33%, so the class curve was around 25%.  She can be funny sometimes, but overall usually boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have any other options, absolutely do not take her class. The practice problems she gives in class are almost unhelpful for the exams, and she can't even solve the problems she presents on her own slides. And you are not allowed to ask a question.

Not a bad person but her course is extremely rigorous. Make sure that you get a 70% overall on your iclicker grade to get a 100 in participation, if not you will receive a 0% even if you get a 68% on iclicker. The exams are hard. The 3.0 curve will round everyone up tremendously because of how low everyone's grade is.

Solely taught by reading off the slides, she seemed to believe that if she showed something/did a problem once, you immediately would understand the concepts and how to do them. Final grade determined by 3 exams and homework, leading to many students to drop after failing the first exam. If this class is required for you, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice but the class is hard. I think most of us walking out of the second/final exam felt bad. I think the main issue is sometimes with how fast she goes. Be prepared to spend a lot of time studying if you have mgmt 310 with her.

Not good at all. She is super hard to understand and mumbles a lot. Her examples in class are unhelpful and she makes things more complicated and confuses more than helps. It's hard to get a good grade in this class since each exam is 35% and there are only 2 the whole semester so if you have a bad day then your whole grade is screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is well meaning but very difficult to work with if you have a question. She won't tell you the average score on the exam unless you go to class? Never seen that before...

Even if she were to slow down and speak clearly, her slides don't give clear direction or computations. She does not take the time to truly teach concepts. For our last exam, homework for chapters 12-14 were non-credit, as she didn't leave time to teach them in class, but they will be on the exam. You will be teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She obviously cares about students and seems like a nice person, but the lectures are very hard to follow with her accent and the material is quite boring. No point in going to lecture. 75% of your grade is going to be exams but if you read the textbook and practice they are fairly easy.
i wouldn't check the streets when crossing when exam season came around!

I would recommend another professor. She reads off of slides with an accent that is hard to understand. I can tell she cares for students but explains concepts too fast and can make things overly complicated. Exams are the majority of your grade and are pretty tough. iclicker quizzes are used every class. I have to teach myself everything.

If you can avoid her do so. her lectures are confusing and 70% of your grade is from two exam. the slides make no sense whatsoever and she teaches too fast in class for people to keep up. this is not clear enough for a prereq class

You cannot understand anything she is saying even with a microphone. She reads directly from her very unorganized slides, hardly teaching anything. Really wish I knew that I would be teaching myself the entire course material... there's a reason why no one shows up to class!! Exams at 25% each, setting you up for failure with no assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does not do a good job at explain and breaking down problems and concepts in the class. She does not do many example problems and rarely explains how to do a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good person, unfortunately her accent makes lectures difficult to understand. Slides are also more often confusing than not. Lectures are only somewhat related to topic, ended up just reading the textbook instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moves way too fast and says to “understand, not memorize,” but doesn't make the material clear or digestible. Lectures are dry, slides are overloaded, and it's hard to know what matters. Test averages were much lower than other sections. I did better just reading the textbook than paying attention in class. Recommend another prof if possible.

310 with Yatsenko is easy if you pay attention and study. Her tests involve plugging numbers into formulas from your cheatsheet. She teaches well, providing examples and iClickers are like exam questions, so there are no surprises. Her reviews shouldn't be this bad.

Surprised by her low rating—likely because 310 is tough. Lots of content, hard exams, but practice materials help. She's knowledgeable, keeps class on track, and prepares you well, even if she's newer to teaching.

She cares a lot about her students and how much effort they put into the course. She has an accent that can be difficult to understand, but you get used to it after a few lectures. The exams are close to the practice exams, but are proven to be a bit tricky.

Professor Yatsenko is a very nice woman. She makes a lot of jokes and overall the classroom environment is positive. However she moves very very very fast and its difficult to even attempt to understand a concept before moving forward to the next.

She shows no interest in teaching the material. She is very monotone, almost like a constant whisper. Often times hard to understand and overall, just a lazy professor. She made fun of the class for doing bad on exams rather than trying to help people understand. Would not recommend.

MGMT310 wasn't an option for her to review—makes sense given the course's lack of structure. She relies on poorly made slides that don't connect well with students. After a tough exam, she used memes instead of real feedback. She's a kind person, but her teaching style makes it hard for students to succeed. Would not recommend.
Terrible professor. Does not put in the effort to teach. Mostly just reads off the slides and is not helpful. Changed exam format on short notice. Would avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very passionate about the material, explains in very strain-forward way. 
Loved her class a lot!
Thick accent makes it difficult to understand. Content makes sense to her but she cannot communicate effectively. Would not take again.
terrible and changes syllabus depending on how she feels

Bad professor, mainly due to her inability to communicate. Lectures are not very helpful and are not worth going to unless it is for participation points. She is so bad to the point she offers candy to people who participate, and even then, that is meaningless, as very few people take up that offer.
was really nice and funny, was clear about what he wanted when gradin, gave a lot of feed back quickly, overall great
Made class fun. Grades easy. Try to get him if you can.

Jon was a great professor to have! I took the honors section with him, and he did a really good job on making class engaging. If you do all of the work and actually try, it shouldn't be difficult to do well. Speeches are recorded and he is willing to send the video afterwards so you can learn from your own speech, which helped me a lot.

Jon was really nice and definitely cared about all of his students. Classes were a bit dull sometimes, but overall there was usually one activity per class that would keep you engaged and help you prepare for upcoming speeches.

Great guy. Class is easy, and he gives good feedback on all major projects. Creates a fun environment that succeeds in reducing speaking stress as much as possible. Lots of extra credit available just in case you screw up a big assignment
COM isn't fun but Jon Wright is a great instructor. He makes the class as enjoyable as it can be and gives extra credit opportunities.

Just finished up COM 217 in a horrible semester, but Jon made everything as seamless as possible. Very quick on grading and understanding. Lectures are extremely succinct and helpful, grading is very clear and fair. Would highly recommend.

Jon is a good professor for taking COM217. He offers extra credit during the Summer of 2020 so it was extremely helpful. The online class was structured so for each week there were recorded lectures to watch. Also, he responds very quickly to emails! Yeah... there's reading. The textbook and is lengthy but it helps with the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best professor, Supper easy class. There are 3 papers, 3 individual presentations, and one group presentation in this class, but it was so easy, and he gave us a lot of extra credits. I am an international student, but I still got 878/875 in this class, so don't worry about any English problem.

He is very helpful and clear on what you need to do to get an A. Lectures are short and to the point, and there are interesting activities to help improve your public speaking skills. Pretty much exactly what a COM class should be.

I definitely recommend Jon for communication courses. He's friendly and cares about students, not to mention the (usually) pretty good speaking activities. 4 speeches/presentations, but they weren't terrible. Persuasive essay was a little rough. Missing days  lower grade, must attend 85% of lectures or you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very reasonable instructor that gives great feedback and tries to be very friendly. Sometimes brings food for his class and has no issues letting classes out early. Class has some busy work but was totally manageable. Lectures are not very exciting and the book isn't really worth it, but the focus is on presentations anyways so its excusable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jon has a nonchalant teaching style that translates to a relaxing class. Often dismisses class early, brings food for the class, and is not too hard on grading. The coursework and readings are beneficial and not difficult to complete or understand. I appreciated the variety of assignments and learned a lot about science writing and communication.
Good guy, but I don't appreciate him not being able to come to class on time. So far has been late to every lecture. If the professor is not expected to show up in time, neither should I.

Dr. Ledbetter goes on tangents that take away from his slides. The slides already skips lots of exam material. You'll end up reading the textbook anyways, so the slides feel a bit redundant (though they can help).

He cares about his students. Beyond that the lack of attention span makes the lectures highly uninformative, therefore the tests were very hard because we didn't learn 80% of what was on the tests. Read the book, don't listen to the lecture. Who knows where it will lead anyways.

He yaps about very random things during lecture (one time spent a class talking about an ostrich fable with an AI generated image of it on the screen). I didn't feel like I learned anything when he was talking. His slides that he goes through leave so much stuff out, but the textbook is helpful. Mostly I personally didn't like the material tho lol

He goes on soo many tangents about unrelated topics, the entire room couldn't care less to pay attention in his classes. He doesn't seem to actually prepare the lectures or he's just really bad at teaching, because he overcomplicates a 5 minute concept. Passive aggressive emails are a bonus. Bring earbuds to class.
No words needed. Very likeable professor, you can tell he cares about everyone and loves his job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: (Cnit322) He shows up 10 minutes late to class and then expects people to show up and take attendance. He goes off topic very easily so you're gonna have to self-study. He plays AI-generated lectures and say he's “introducing new technology”. It feels like a waste of tuition and time, and Polytech shouldn't give him the next contract.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There's nothing to say

Seems like a nice guy but is not good at explaining topics at all. Gets side tracked very easily and skips many slides. You have to rely almost fully on the book for info. Lab difficulty depends on TA. Tests are all online and are not too bad. Big group project at the end, not very hard content but it is difficult to split up work as a group.

Very kind and evidently caring professor. Class can be a little disorganized/confusing at times, however, as you're basically on your own for the labs. TA's didn't cover or explain any of the material and released lab grades only just before lab exams so you had little chance to see anything of concern. Also, an A is a 94+ only so 93.9 is still A-.

Look, he's not a bad guy, but his lectures can be really confusing even if you are paying attention. The lab is taught with many materials from the previous professor and if you get a bad TA for lab, you are on your own to figure it all out for the most part with the lab manual and a video. Quiz on each chapter of the book. Big group project too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I've ever taken in Purdue. If possible, please cancel the summer vacation courses. The experience was extremely poor. There was no effective assistance and no real-time courses available. Before I signed up, a friend said he was better suited for conducting research rather than teaching, I completely agreed with her.

The professor graded a month late, used another professor's recordings instead of teaching, and even reused last year's Lab 5 as this year's Lab 6 without renaming it. Group projects were harshly graded—teammates' mistakes hurt your grade, and explanations were dismissed. Late work got a zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly this guy is a super nice individual. Goes on rambles sometimes but I never seemed to mind. Great person overall very nice and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Lectures aren't the most productive, but 180 lab is much more important than lec. Weekly quizzes online. Honestly not the hardest class, use quizlet for your quiz and exam studying.

This instructor should refrain from teaching/offering this course in the summer. From ignored questions in emails, to practically your-on-your-own convoluted labs, to a situation where I submitted a lab "incorrectly" and it instantly earned me a F with no feedback left whatsoever, it seems those who are taught in person have it better.

Pretty chill class. Most people don't go to the lectures, but I found the content somewhat interesting. He is an okay lecturer, does go off on tangents at times but it's not like the material is super hard to understand so it's fine. Assignments and exams are pretty straightforward, with a group project at the end.
Very chill guy. Lectures can be boring but very nice and helpful. No complaints really.

The professor just read off the slides, you can get a good grade by just going through the information yourself. Labs were easy, I enjoyed them. There was a final group project, it was okay just get a good group. It is based on the labs and is pretty simple. Was relatively understanding when issues came up, especially with groups.

Very caring and engaging lecturer. Grading standards for the research paper draft that you submit every few weeks then piecemeal together into a research paper at the end of the semester are very inconsistent even after referring to the rubric. Exams on the other hand rely on rote memorization, but the questions are straightforward nonetheless.

Will is one of the nicest and most caring profs at this whole university. That being said, it doesn't seem like he plans his lectures. He's so knowledgable but the lectures are wild and all over the place. Assignments are actually pretty fun but beware of the grader who takes off points for literally anything. Exams are online and open for a week,

Ledbetter taught about 1/3 of my CNIT18200 class and the other professor taught the other 2/3. Ledbetter is a nice person and is willing to help when you ask for it (especially on project deliverables). However, his lectures can be boring and he can be scatter-brained at times; he seems to know his stuff, he just has to work on conveying it better.
Great Instructor!!

William Ledbetter is a graduate student, but he is a better instructor than most professors I have. He genuinely cares if the student learns the material and will try to find different ways to explain the material so that the student understands in the best way possible. Genuine guy; knowledgable from his experience in the field.
Very unhelpful. When asked questions, answers with sarcasm. Good thing the class is easy.

Dr. Weng is by far the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and it is abundantly clear that he truly enjoys his work. I can tell that he is a professor not only focused on research, but also deeply committed to making a meaningful impact on undergraduate students. I would 100% take any class taught by him.

He's nice and funny, and he's a good teacher. However he's not great at making tests. I would go through all the study materials, and half the questions in the exams are phrased so awkwardly and unsimilar to study materials, which made them way harder. Plus, the average on the final was a a fifty and the curve was five percent

Calc 2 is a hard class but Shuyi is the goat. His teaching skill is on the level of the esteemed Chen from Chenflix - he manages to introduce all of the weird calc 2 topics in a way you can understand, which is not an easy task. Also his enthusiasm will make you actually want to show up to lecture even though he doesn't take attendance.

Homework due 3x a week. Calc 2 in general is hard at Purdue since exam grades are determined purely by multiple choice.  I watched every lecture but really your success depends on how much time you put into doing practice problems until you understand calc 2 itself.

All year he was a great professor, however the final was brutal and he only gave a 4% curve for Calc 2. I would say using previous years' final exams is not very helpful since he write his differently than other professors have in the past.
Shuyi's lectures are pretty good. Course relies a lot on tests with three midterms and a final and he doesn't make them easy. Review salons and quizzes for exams.
Don't know much about him, used Chenflix and did well in the class. Fall25 final was a joke tho, 54% class average with a SD of 12

DO NOT USE THE RMP SCORE TO JUDGE HOW HARD THE CLASS IS. This class is unreasonably hard, sometimes making me question if they want to teach the material or your reading skills. Lectures are pretty ok. Recitation barely helps, and quizzes suck. Past exams don't reflect difficulty of exams. Read lecture notes carefully and use hw to study. good luck

This class was the bane of my existence. So much homework, recitation preparation for quizzes, and obviously exams. The exams were extremely difficult and no amount of studying really helped me. Boilerexams helps to an extent.

Shuyi is a great professor. His lectures were amazing and very well organized. The recitations weren't the best and did not help me. The homework takes up a lot of time and there are three a week. Be sure to really study for the third midterm and especially the final.

Shuyi is great at teaching, but sometimes gives dismissive responses. The salons are not helpful, the quizzes are hard, and all tests and final are incredibly hard. The Math Resource Room is underrated, so please go and do not fall behind. There are 3 HW/week, and they took hours for me to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, but recitations had difficult assignments with Salons and Quizzes that made up a significant portion of your grade. Everything in this class was difficult, HW was not super helpful. You are better off studying for exams with old exams or practice problems. Watching OGT and chenflix carried me for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he has incredibly clear, well-organized and methodical lectures that i found wanting to attend despite not being mandatory. focused on the fundamental concepts which improved my understanding. super approachable and gives tons of help to get you through the course. tests are tough as they always are, they're doable if you practice well.

Shuyi is a phenomenal math professor by all standards. However, his approach to teaching Math is more derivation-oriented, so if you're someone who benefits more from practicing exam difficulty questions, Shuyi's classes may seem a tad drawn out. Personally, I love Shuyi's approach since it helps me understand the concepts from the ground up.

For context, I already had a 5 in Calc BC in hs.

For every unit besides series, I feel he taught it extremely well and concisely. He derives everything before giving you the formula to connect the pieces in your head. His notes are very organized, too.

His tests are extremely difficult and concept-heavy, so don't fall behind. Stay consistent!

Shuyi is a very tolerant professor and does his job very well. He does not hold back on exams. Know what you're getting into. Definitely go to lecture and GO TO HIS EXAM REVIEW SESSIONS. Lots of people skip them to review on their own time. He picks specific question types that will be on the exam.
Pretty good professor. Class was difficult but he helped make it better. Some topics aren't gone into enough in lecture due to time constraints.
Go to lectures or watch chenflix and you'll pass, but be careful on those exams, exam 3 was already bad but final came in like a nuke.

Unfortunately, his lectures were outright bad.
Oftentimes his lectures just turn confusing, and would often just make it harder to understand in general. The material itself is presented good, but his explanations did not do it for many of us.
(Watch out for the final exam!)

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was fair enough that if you kept up with assignments and recitations you would (most likely) pass even with subpar exam scores. He's a good professor, and his exams are usually difficult but not impossible. However, you should watch out for the final. He moves like Von when cooking up the final. Just slaughters the students & their grades
lectures are engaging and you can tell he cares! class is hard just because its a hard class, he doesnt make it harder than it needs to be.

Shuyi truly is very knowledgeable and is quite fun to listen to talk. He always does a lot of problems in class step by step, which is super helpful in understanding. When it comes to sequences and series, I truly believe that no professor can teach that unit perfectly, so I still struggled quite a lot in that regard.
Shuyi was a great professor, his notes were extremely well organized and easy to follow. His lectures were engaging and worth going to. Overall an amazing professor.

Very funny and approachable. Lectures are very clear, but its entirely possible to complete the class by copying the notes later and practicing with the homework. I rarely went to lecture as his notes were written well enough for me to understand without him speaking. 10/10 math professor would take again.

Shuyi is a kind, accessible Calc 2 professor who posts lecture videos and notes. The class is homework-heavy (35 assignments, 3 dropped) with 3 midterms and a cumulative final. Lectures aren't mandatory, but recitations are and include weekly salons or quizzes that equally impact your grade.

Professor Weng was amazing, he has the course set up in an easy and accessible way. He posts his note outline ahead of the lecture, and he also posts his lectures online. Homework and exams are hard, as this is a hard class, but he seemed to be very caring of the students.

Shuyi is an incredibly nice and encouraging human being. That being said, Calc 2 is a hard course, and he doesn't always explain new topics in the best way. He often goes very in-depth with topics, but not always on things that need that much explanation. There is also quite a bit of prior Calc 1 knowledge needed to make sense of certain lectures.
Tough class, but he is a great teacher.
Really awsome professor! Still taking his courses
I love Shuyi.
Great atmosphere and he actually know mathhhh

I really liked Shuyi's easily accessible notes to follow along during and after lecture and his enthusiasm. Homework and quizzes were pretty standard and very difficult, but I especially struggled with the tests. The material on the tests was very difficult and often had a couple questions that did not reflect class topics, with no partial credit.

Probably the best math professor I've had at Purdue. His lectures and notes are clear as day. That said, (may not entirely be his fault), the lecture doesn't always match the depth or difficulty of the homework or exams. If you're willing to put in the time to THROUGHLY understand the homework and ask questions, you'll do well.
Such a great professor with a great personality.
Good lecturer, but came off a bit judgmental when answering questions.  The first exam was difficult but lightened up a lot after that.  Pretty standard IMO
I wish he gave partial credit on tests, but he was a great lecturer, and he records all his lectures. Recitations were helpful

Calc 2 is a challenging course, but Professor Weng makes the material accessible. The class isn't easy by any means, and his exams are quite tough, but he's a professor genuinely concerned with how students learn, where they struggle, and how they can succeed.
The exams are a lot harder than the homework. He tends to go very fast on the complex subjects and slow on the easy stuff. He provides scaffold notes which is great, but the mic didn't always work.

Shuyi is an excellent professor for Calc 2. Admittedly some of the concepts themselves were hard to understand, so for people struggling I would recommend watching Chenflix and then attending Shuyi's lecture as his notes and lectures are far more comprehensive. He's also extremely accessible and helpful during office hours.

Shuyi was a great professor for Calc 2. He explained everything very well, he was very caring, and made sure we did well in the class. If you have a chance to take a class with him, I highly recommend you do. 10/10 professor.

I thought his lectures were easy to follow, and his notes were beautiful, well-organized, and color-coded. He rearranges the order of material, so use boiler exams by topic for midterms rather than by exams. He's kind of sassy in answering questions, so I would lean more on your TAs for that. Class is curved, you'll pass if you do the work.

Shuyi was good at teaching, however I recommend watching a concept video before the class to better understand. For tests, please use your past quizzes and boilerexams-- it'll save you. I have never had a class that required so much work and time to fully understand concepts. He is a bit sassy when you ask questions so don't take it to heart.

Shuyi was my MA 162 professor and he was very helpful. His lectures were very informative so I would recommend you go to as many lectures as you can. He gives outlines for his notes before class and they would help keep you on track as he went through the lecture. I would 100% take his class again if I could.

The curve was generous, but this class was brutal. Afternoon lecture is the worst since he would never finish the material and say to check morning lecture recordings. When responding to questions, he is very blunt. He admitted to making exams too hard and that he was learning how to write better exams. Chenflix is the way to go for this class.
Shuyi is such a goated professor, absolute wizard of curves. Calc II was kind of tough but he explained the concepts pretty well.
Did not answer questions very well. Made exams very difficult and even admitted it himself and didn't change anything about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Shuyi was very well organized. He posts his neat notes for each lecture & reminds students to keep them on track. 

The lecture pacing can feel a bit slow but his explanations were useful to understand the material.
Quite a chill and approachable guy overall. 

Calc 2 material is challenging but he made it simple to absorb.
Do not recommend.

Clear lecturer, easy to follow, and makes notes easily accessible to students. Doesn't answer many questions in class due to the short lecture times, but is very helpful during office hours. Exams are quite difficult, but lots of resources are provided. You'll be expected to know calc 1 thoroughly, so brush up on skills before taking this class.

Great lectures! Shuyi goes through the fundamentals of each topic to help you fully understand and grasp the big idea of the topics learned in class so that you can apply them to the homework.

Notes are also very clean and easy to follow along with.

By far the worst professor Ive had in all my days. the material taught in lecture does not resemble that which is on exams, quizzes, or homeworks. Nor does he provide any materials to aid in being successful in the course. would not recommend ever taking his class.
He is a great professor! He knows how to simplify complex topics and his notes are well organised and easy to study..
He is a great professor, He makes complex topics very easy to understand. His notes are also very illustrative, organised and easy to study.
For such a challenging class, Shuyi helps make the concepts easier to understand. He's a nice guy, who makes time for his students and enjoys answering questions.

Calc 2 is undoubtedly difficult, but Shuyi definitely makes concepts clear and approachable, answering all questions at their appropriate depth whenever they arise. He's a pretty jolly fellow and a nice person, making the content and lectures easier.
Shuyi is a great lecturer very clear and understandable in his explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man is an absolute G. Very approachable, and he is really good at teaching. Dude is way too overqualified for this job. Calc 2 is just a hard class here, not the fault of Shuyi.

He is a great lecturer and manages to get the main ideas across in his lectures. However, he is not so great at writing tests, even with some of the quizzes the TA was struggling to solve them. He could definitely tone down the difficulty of the tests and make it more similar to the content learned in lectures.
Best professor in the math department in my opinion.
Very good lecturer. Does a great job of simplifying complex topics and providing real world applications for the math you are learning.

Weng was a great professor! He explained the concepts of Calculus well, and was very helpful and good at answering questions. He's also just a nice guy in general. Taking Calc 2 with him made a difficult class a lot easier.
Took his class for MA162. Did not get through material that we would have homework or quizzes in the hour given. Just watched chenflix after the first three lectures and did fine.

Dr. Weng is amazing.  I had him for calc 2 and even though it is the hardest calc offered, he made it so much better.  He is very easy to understand as long as you pay attention.  He was so funny and cancelled lectures on occasion.

He's an amazing professor! He comes across as someone who really cares about how students are doing in his class. Additionally, he's extremely patient! I went to his office hours and was struggling with a couple of questions, and he was really understanding and made the concepts pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, answers questions thoroughly when asked, seems to genuinely care about student success in class.

Professor Weng is amazing. Anyone can understand Calculus with him. He explains even the pieces connecting to Pre-Calculus, talks at a good pace(not too fast, not too slow). His exam reviews are also very helpful and usually have the exact type of problems on the exams. He is also very fun, caring, and great to talk and ask questions to.

I think Dr. Gray's rating is rather harsh. A lot of his students don't put in enough effort. He is always willing to help and is a fair grader. His lectures are great if you pay attention. If you miss something, raise your hand and he will answer. He finds great readings for class and his discussions are always fun. All-around a great professor!

Very high quality! 
Super informative and the selected texts are interesting.
The class moved too fast and the professor was unresponsive to my emails.
I really enjoyed his class and he really seemed to care about the topics that he was covering. The reading was light and the only assignments were a few papers throughout the whole semester.

The layout of this class is what frustrated me the most. He refused to put words on his slides, just pictures, because he wants us to listen to him and not just copy words down. I understand that, but it was very unclear to me what was important and what wasn't to write down, I can't write at the speed he talks at. I gave up on reading very early.

Mr. Gray was a very kind professor. I found his lectures very boring however as they only consisted of pictures. This class is VERY essay heavy (you write 6 essays not including the additional 4 papers for exams). I found the essays to be a good supplement to the reading and as long as you stay on top of your work, I believe it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable and passionate about the information, but sometimes can tend to get off course. Did not enjoy the structure and layout of the course, hard to follow and definitely a very heavy reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures, insightful in the field (European history), lots of reading, and writing
Awesome professor. He is so knowledgable and passionate about the material he teaches. Very entertaining to listen to

Really enjoyed Global Crises with him, taking German History with him simply because I enjoyed the other class. Good lectures, hard to keep up with reading. I gave up on reading halfway through the semester and still got an A. Highly recommended
He's very good as long as you show up to lecture and are an attentive student. sit in the first few rows; it helps for him to know who you are. He hates it when you leave class early.
Great professor, easy to get along with. Knows what he's teaching thoroughly.

Very Knowledgeable.  Easy to get along with.  Hard to get a great score on the essay exams.  Finds a way to count off, even with a great essay.  One paper and 3 exams.  A few different books assigned.
Quite passionate about European history.  Lectures are very clear - packed full of information.  Exams provide a fair assessment of the course material.
good teacher
Best history prof.
Very good teacher, very passionate
"Mixed Bag" would be a nice description.  His lectures are pretty good and informative, but is harsh when it comes to grading.
Actually cares about students and made a great reading list for the semester. The rare thought provoking class.

One of the greatest professors at Purdue. His classes were always enjoyable and were the highlights of every week. However, to get a good grade (A), you must put in a good amount of effort. Also, please read the syllabus.

This man is the best 102 professor I think you could ever have. Yes, there can be quite a bit of reading, but he always gives you enough time so space it out. Attend every lecture because he gets to know everyone in the class and knows exactly when you were missing. Lectures were a blast and we always had fun debates. Dr. White is amazing!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor White has great humility and humor, often making jokes of himself or others during his classes. There is a LOT of reading (usually 30-60 pages of the accompanying text per quiz). He has pop quizzes, so you better read. As long as you "become one with the book" then the quizzes are a breeze. Speeches are also graded with lots of leeway.

reviews.comment: Professor White is a funny guy who makes class exciting and enjoyable and honestly chose some good books to read this semester (I don't even like reading that much).
