By far one of my favorite psych professors. Truly cares about students and the content he teaches.

He was a very good lecturer, gave real-life cases as examples and made jokes. I actually enjoyed attending lectures! He was my first contact with psychology and made me decide to change my major to psych. The exams were pretty easy, especially if you watch lectures + read the textbook.

Professor William is really funny, but his lectures seem like they last a thousand years. I ended up not going to lectures after a while and just reviewing the material on Quizlet before an exam. He seems to be really understanding though and gives clear feedback on assignments or questions in general.

Prof. William was a truly exceptional teacher. His lectures are funny, informative, engaging and make you actually want to attend unlike other large lectures. He responds to emails within minutes and is incredibly sympathetic if you need extra time or help on an assignment. I would love to take more classes with him in the future.
Very passionate about his field, and involves the students in his lectures a lot, makes the lectures super interesting

Great lecturer. You can tell he is knowledgable about the subject and he makes class interesting with personal anecdotes, movie clips, and his pleasant and funny demeanor. Easy A class if you show up to most of the lectures or at least watch the recordings. Make sure to read the textbook before exams, he takes questions from it.

He added in jokes and cool stories to keep the lectures interesting. There were 4 discussion boards and 4 exams, but the lowest exam grade gets dropped, so you can miss one. The TA grading the discussion boards was kind of a tough grader. The boards aren't very hard, you write 200 words for your post and reply to 2 people's posts with 100 words.

Professor Williams' class was always the highlight of my week! He was so down-to-earth and relatable. You don't need buy a textbook, provides an online pdf. You do need to read and show up to class to get a good grade! Would take another class taught by him.
He is a really good professor and super down to earth. The only things we have to do are discussion boards and exams, so do well on those.
Only things in the grade book are exams and discussions boards so dont blow them off
Extremely nice and seemed very passionate about his subject and getting students involved in the major.
Take notes and study before the tests and you'll be fine. Put in some effort and you'll enjoy yourself a lot. He makes lectures interesting.
He is an awesome professor. He is super funny and has great stories. He was always awarding us for doing so good even with COVID going on. He celebrated our efforts instead of criticizing us.
Nice guy and hes funny. It was an easy interesting class and I had a lot of fun.

Professor William was the best professor I've had at Purdue so far! I took this class Spring 2020, so half in person and half online. He was always so funny and had the best lectures. He clearly knows what he's talking about and always answers student questions fully. His online lectures were still just as great! Amazing abnormal psych professor.
Yes yes yes. I looked forward to his class every week. He makes every lecture entertaining, engages with everyone in class, and really cares about his students. 100/10 would recommend.

Prof. William was the best professor I have had at Purdue so far. He is an excellent lecturer who actually engages with his students and makes learning fun. He is also the only professors I had this semester who was sympathetic toward his students for dealing with school on top of a pandemic. 10/10 recommend, wish he could teach all my classes.

Prof. Colin is an absolute great lecturer who knows how to keep an audience engaged while still getting to the point. All of his presented material directly correlates with what you will find on exams or discussion boards and he does his best to make everything relatable for his students.
Great professor, definitely take his class for PSY 120, easy class for core requirements and he makes it super interesting

He is an amazing professor that accommodates to students needs and really. cares about what he is teaching 10/10 for this amazing guy. Psych 350 can be challenging if you don listen to him while he teaches, but if you do you can guarantee an A

Colin is such an amazing professor that is such a joy to listen to in class. He explains things very well and seems passionate about what he is teaching. I would 100% take his class again. Tests were difficult but he helped so much during his office hours.
Dr. William gives amazing lectures. Everything on the exams is either covered in lecture or in vocabulary in the textbook. So long as you are diligent, it is an easy A

Colin was brilliant. Very intelligent and well rounded in the content he teaches. His lectures are always interactive and everyone laughs at least once. His exam content is very textbook, so studying direct material is probably best. Overall I've absolutely loved having him.

I loved Dr. William! PSY100 overall is a super easy class and he told so many funny stories during lecture. Beware, though, all assignments are due Friday after he assigns them and he doesn't accept late work, so don't forget the class exists like I did!
Very funny and tells a lot of interesting stories during lecture

Very disorganized class with no real cohesion between topics. Material is light, assignments are simple, exams are almost trivial. Lectures were difficult to sit through as Xue would often spend more time ranting and going on tangents than actually teaching, and when he did he just read the slides verbatim. Easy A, ok intro to AI, lacks substance.

He takes attendance sporadically. This semester alone he took it 4 times at random intervals. It's irritating but it's only 5% of your overall grade. In my opinion, it's easy to get an A since the course is weighted very friendly and tests are graded lightly. Overall fun class.

This semester was the first CS243 class taught by Purdue so I won't be too harsh on Professor Xue. He is very knowledgable about the concepts he teaches although the course is pretty disorganized for a first-timer in AI to understand. The labs and homework are graded pretty harshly and it's hard to understand the directions.
Boring class, you should jump directly into more advanced CS courses if you really want to do ML. Good class for freshmans as an intro to ML tho. Very easy A

hes a really bad lecturer and his slides are horrible, you can't understand anything from them. i had to teach myself off the labs and homework assignments. i feel like this class is so important to AI majors but we didn't even learn it right because he would go on random tangents during class. He over explained things that were obvious.

Worst prof I ever had. He told us that he would drop 1 of the 4 homework assignments from the class, so most of the class only did 3 of the 4 homeworks. He then decided to grade it anyway and gave most of the class a 0. dropped my grade from an A to a B+ in the last 2 days of class.

Terrible lecturer as well.
Interesting and easy to understand lectures, not a huge time-sink as there are only four homework assignments. No curve unfortunately, but probably 5-6% available extra credit.

He was a pretty average lecturer. We had hotseat polls for attendance, monthly-ish homework (written + coding), a midterm, a final, and an essay on AI. Workload wasn't terrible, but some of the coding assignments could be annoying. The final was much more difficult than the midterm, and there was no curve unfortunately.

It was a really good class and I learnt a lot. He was very approachable and helped with any doubts or clarifications. There were discussions on wide array of ways in which what we were learning in class was being used in the real world and towards making a better world. He is not only an expert in artificial intelligence but also a great teacher.

Xue is definitely not the best lecturer, but it is good enough. The homeworks include some stuff that was not covered in lecture which is unfair. Most of the homework was easy besides that. Not many homework assignments and make sure to do the extra credit. Nice professor and tries to give everyone a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Xue definitely deserves a 5.0, even just for his hands-on derivations that get to the real details. He uploaded videos 1-2hs after each lecture, and are responsive to questions. The only thing is that he likes to bluff about the difficulty of this course, especially the project. But the bar is reasonable and 70% got A (with take-home exams).

Course Description: "This introductory course... basic ideas and intuitions..." First Lecture: "This class is for PhD students, maybe masters students if they are exceptional... otherwise you will suffer..." Curve? "A PhD student does not ask that kind of question." "You should already know how to use these tools and algorithms."
Professor Xue always answered questions during Zoom lectures and was very approachable. He also didn't assign that much hw, so the class was doable at a reasonable pace.

Professor Xue is a pretty good choice. He (and I'm sure all professors for CS471) uses a lot of material from Berkeley's CS188 class (lecture slides and homeworks). This class is pretty chill if you can understand the material. Both the midterm and final are take home, and are reasonable. This class isn't too hard overall. There was no curve though

Professor Xue definitely cares a lot about his students. His expectations for the homework and the exams are very clear, and his grading is fair. He is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, and often brought up real life issues about AI to make class more interesting and relevant. One of the best professors I ever had at Purdue.
I Did not learn anything useful.
Not great compared to the previous offerings

Written instructions differ from what is said in class, often tangents about ai usage (not related to class at all), deadlines are absurdly short and almost impossible (ex. having to interview a Downtown Lafayette business in less than 4 days!), and her workload for group projects is difficult to complete given the short time we have to do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: We wrote 8 reports over the course of the semester. The reports were approximately 10 pages each, with the shortest being 5 pages and the longest being 14 pages. We did 4 group presentations as well. Not an easy class.
Lectures can be long and boring, but as long as you participate somewhat and provide insightful, original content in the many projects throughout the semester, you'll do very well.
broke school policies and had our final exam before thanksgiving break
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Find a different professor to take this class with
Not very easy to follow the work assigned in class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hard to follow what she is talking about
Does not use technology well at all and very group project heavy.

It was a twice weekly course and we turned in article reviews each week and presented on our proposal progress. The fist graded feedback we received back in the course was the Final Exam that was on Canvas (graded automatically as it is M/C and T/F). She ended up giving us 100 for everything else. Proposal graded harshly. I did not enjoy the course
She talks a lot in class and majority of assignment are group projects. Shes really flexible about due dates as long as you talk to her. She grades super fair

Dr. Lehto is nice, but get ready to work for your grade. Lots of group work thats tedious and last minute assignments. She is sometimes unclear on expectations but is willing to take time out to explain something. Need to show up to class and have the textbook to pass the tests. I appreciate she is kind, credible, and passionate about HTM.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lehto is really nice and wants her students to learn about the subject, but lectures are extremely boring. The class is basically all about social media, which is important in today's marketing but it would have been nice to learn more about other aspects of marketing. The group project is a lot of busy work and was horribly explained.

I had heard mixed reviews about Dr.  Lehto, but honestly, her class was extremely easy. As long as you participate in the discussions in class, the time flies and she automatically loves you as a student. The group project we worked on was easy overall and extremely interesting. I learned a lot. Also, if you read the book you'll get an A on exams.

Dr. Lechto is extremely nice and experienced, but tends to be very boring in class. She tends to lecture for the whole class and usually gets of topic. You can easily get an A in the class if you show up, participate, do the homework's and quizzes, give at least some effort in the group project, and study a little for her exams.

Lehto is an extremely experienced and respected individual within the Hospitality field. Unfortunately, I did not feel as though I learned as much as I could have in the class as she spent a decent amount of time talking to the class about her past experiences. The group project is extremely interesting and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Lehto's class because she tries to create discussion. As long as you contribute to discussion, she'll like you and respect you. Lectures can be long. My best advice is stay involved in discussion and you'll find exams and projects easy.
Rambles on and on.  Critical.  Boring.  The exams are extremely difficult.  About 50% of all information learned in the class is pointless and self explanatory.
she is so strict to students and her class is much more harder than other professor. The exam is so ridiculous because she ask us what is the ad for Hyatt hotel. No one know!

A terrible professor. Constantly talking and teaching useless information. Does not follow the curriculum that other professors follow. Exams, homework, and projects are harder than other sections of the course. Do not take her class.

She is one of the worst professors I have had at Purdue. She expects that we already have a knowledge on the topic even though its a beginning level class. She's hard to understand at times and everyone I know dreads going to her class.
I liked her classes, willing to take other her classes
Easy grader. Exams are way easier than homeworks.
Worse explanation than Porterfield, more homework than Song, lower grades than Owada.
Better to read the textbook and teach by yourself.

Lectures are trivial and disconnected. She doesn't know statistics at all. Her proofs are not mathematically rigorous. Always struggling on formulating problems and explaining basic concepts. Going to her lectures is a waste of time if you are a PhD student at Purdue. She is not even a qualified PhD student let alone a professor.
Worst education you could possibly get in purdue.

No official HW/Exam solutions.
Tough grading, no curve, if you got 89, it's a B. Nothing like B+ or A+. There is no one who gets an A if no one has a 90+ score.
Your grade is mostly from Midterms and finals.
I got all A/A+ from other courses I took at Purdue except this one, I spent >12 hours/wk on this course, which proved it's not my problem.
Please don't take this course. 1/10 students will get an A (Last semester only 9 students on STAT528, and I think at most 1 got an A). Perhaps no A if no one got 90%. She doesn't curve.

She makes concepts harder to understand and confuses students. She is a tough grader. She will give you example questions for the exams where you cannot find similar ones on the exam. If you get a low grade on midterm she will send messages that are discouraging and say that you will probably fail instead of offering some work to encourage.

She doesn't know how to explain complex concepts. All she does is making everything even harder to understand. Her spoken English is really bad. Its not the accent. She doesn't know how to express things at all. She even pronounces the words incorrectly. Homework questions are difficult with NO SOLUTION!!

A fairly easy class if you study for exams and quizzes and do all the homework assignments. Lectures start off clear, but become more incoherent as the semester goes on. Read the txt. Exams are unforgiving, each point missed is a % off your final class grade. Prof has a bit of an accent, but is understandable. HMK comes from questions in textbook.

She tends to explain the logics behind the methods, which is great, but ends up even more confusing. And she doesn't changed her notes posted even she's far behind the schedule. It just seems like she doesn't update at all. If there's no quiz in lecture, I wouldn't come to lectures, but read textbook at home, which seems more helpful.
Impossible to understand, lecture outlines are average, without them, the lectures are useless

Very friendly, but extremely patchy English and highly unorganized.  I was struggling to follow the lectures the entire time.  Also, ask questions frequently about the homework because she takes off for next to nothing.

Professor Xiangxiong is excellent and very organized. He explains concepts clearly, repeats key ideas, and summarizes them well. He is very responsive on Piazza and always willing to help. I really enjoyed the course and would highly recommend him to future students.

(MA 574 is a grad topics class) Dr. Zhang's lectures are well paced and informative, spending extra time on difficult material. Passing 574 is not very hard, but concepts are difficult and take time & effort to fully grasp. Notes for all of his classes are available on his website, and he's very quick to respond to emails. Flexible office hours.
He knows what he is talking about.

Overall not bad. The course material was pretty easy, but he did go over a lot of topics that were very briefly discussed and not mentioned on homeworks or exams, and then proceeded to load them onto the final. However, he answers your questions quickly online and is pretty lenient on grading.

Weird teaching style and arrangement. For elementary linear algebra he taught a lot of concepts which are not in the course syllabus, and introduced inadequate basic content. Though it is useful academically but unfortunately too abstract and frustrating for beginners in linear algebra. He is also not patient enough in the office hours.
This is the kind of professor that this website was made to warn about.

Goes through concepts many times in homework and class and makes sure that the students understand well. Notes are kinda difficult to read sometimes but are still very useful for reviewing concepts. Homework is very relevant to classes and helps you further understand the topics. Final grade was 80% exams (2mids+1final) but we were well-prepared
Responsible, approachable, intelligent
The grading on homework is tough and strict. Things learnt in this class is hard, but the office hour can be helpful. Except for the hard staff learnt, his explanation is clear enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Home work and text book is so useful that you can review what he have though in class a good way to review for the exam. Even though the office hour held only once per week, but you can always welcome to make an extra appointment with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He tries, but he doesn't explain things too well. If you are to take his class, using a lot of imagination might make things a bit better. Also, be prepared for very harsh grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhang is really good at offering different perspectives rather than directly reading from the text. To me,  the lecture notes are very useful.
Good

Prof Wang taught a very tough class however, her lectures were very informative on how to do the homework so if you do it and apply it to quizzes and exams you should be fine. The 6 quizzes throughout the semester were way harder than any exam question so be prepared for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a project-based class, and professor Wang is a good instructor, guiding students to complete a big project with stakeholders. I have learned a lot through this project under the guidance of professor Wang.

Professor Wang is very great at teaching. She gives clear instruction to students clearly on solving the problems step by step, not only the main materials but also the supplement ones. She also usually emphasizes what's important that will surely be tested. She also cares for students, making sure that everyone has the chance of raising questions

Professor Wang is very great at teaching. She makes new concepts of statistics so digestible, always makes sure students have enough materials to study for quizzes or exams, and she would go through them thoroughly so that students could do well on tests.

Prof. Wang is an amazing professor. She carefully guided us through every step of our project, making sure we stayed focused and organized. Her consistent follow-up with both our team and stakeholders, which kept everyone aligned. Her support made a real difference and helped us grow both professionally and personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She actually cares about students and always being nice whenever you go to the office hour or talk with her after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She just kept on influencing ppl to do regression on a problem which wasn't regression one.

Professor Wang is a very caring professor. If you have any questions, I highly recommend you to go to her Office Hours as it really helped me throughout the semester. Also, MGMT 478 is a more self-paced course but will definitely improve both public speaking and programming skills. I recommend taking Professor Wang's MGMT 478 class!

Professor Wang explained concepts well, and she was extremely caring about students.  She was readily available via email and did all she could to help students.  She has a slight accent, but it's very understandable and explains the material clearly.  Very smart professor, and would recommend her for 305 or 306.

Professor Wang was a wonderful professor to have. While a class like MGMT 306 can be difficult, having such an inspirational professor made the class a lot smoother. She cares and understands her students' personal matters. She takes the time to thoroughly explain class material to ensure student success. I would highly recommend taking her class!!
She was okay, the project we had was a very complex one, the dataset we dealt with was very complex, n she wasn't helpful much, she expected us to know stuff which we haven't taken any classes for.

Professor Wang created a great atmosphere for this class. There is a healthy balance of autonomy and instructor guidance on the projects as well. If you want industry experience in project management and presentation in analytics, this is the course for you.

Professor Wang is very supportive and caring when it comes to each student's learning. She takes the time to help those who may be falling behind or not as much experience in projects. She is very communicative and responds to emails quickly. Due to the adaptive criteria in the course, she is flexible when it comes to students exploring topics.

MGMT 478 is a new course (taught by Wang) on case studies, where student meet with company stakeholders to address real business issues. Attendance is essential for group work. As the class simulates what a real work environment would be like, Professor Wang does a good job in supporting students in being flexible in the adaptative requirements.

Expect nit-picky grading on homework assignments and homework assignments that take a long time to do.

She cares about her students learning but is also a tough grader. I would like to emphasize she genuinely cares about her students learning. The class is just not easy.

Professor Wang was a great professor who cared a lot about our learning. Homework's are very time consuming so be sure to get started on them early. Professor Wang is always willing to answer any questions or give extra to a student.

Professor Wang is very supportive. This was a tougher class for me personally, but I would attend her office hours where she would do her very best to guide me through any problems with homework, exams, or lecture questions. While the content may be hard, she is a very effective professor if you are struggling!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Wang is very passionate about what she teaches and is always willing to help students outside of class. There are lots of resources to help prep for exams and quizzes, and the homework problems are genuinely beneficial for learning the material.

Wang is awesome! So many resources to succeed for exams and quizzes.
Always reachable outside of class. Literally responds to emails in 3-4 minutes.
That said, the material itself is pretty hard so if you fall behind in class make sure to watch the recorded videos & understand the concepts!
Learned so much cool statistics stuff.
No HW drops is sad.

If you need to take this class, I highly recommend taking it with Professor Xue. While the homework can be tedious and somewhat difficult, it's good practice and not overly long. Exams make up a majority of the grade, but they're also extremely similar to the practice exams she provides (similar topics or sometimes just a few things changed).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Xue is a decent lecturer, although the course itself is 80% exams (35% midterm + 45% final) and 20% homework with one HW drop. The exams were around 4-5 questions and very similar to the practice and questions from the homework. So you should be able to get an A if you do just those.

Dr.Xue is very kind. Her exams are not overly difficult, and the homework is manageable without causing too much stress. She takes the time to answer questions thoroughly and ensures that students understand the material. Highly recommend her class for anyone looking for a supportive and understanding instructor.

Lectures can be unclear at times, but homework feedback is in incredible detail. It's pretty amazing, sometimes I get entire paragraphs on what I did wrong in a question and how to do it correctly. However, not harsh on HW grading, so she clearly genuinely cares about your learning. Super nice woman. Practice exams are very similar to exams. 10/10.
The midterms and final were almost identical to the practice ones she gave. Overall easy course, just spent time understanding the homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fei is very nice. Her lectures are informative and she cares about your success in the course.

Can I just say how nice a person she is. One of the true hidden gems in the STAT department. Very empathetic and is willing to help students outside class. Class is hard but she is always ready to help. Very sweet and soft-spoken.I have taken STAT517 with too and she is just as amazing! Will 100% recommend a class with her!!!

The midterm and final time was bad, but he doesn't have much control over it. Otherwise, he is a really good lecturer and explains the concept clearly. He also included some funny examples during lecture, such as the "vs robot chess", where the robot won by going out the box. He also isn't afraid to call out students who talk loudly during lecture.

Very knowledgeable lecturer and responds to emails quickly. Our lecture was at 6pm so they were recorded which is extremely useful when the assignment deadline or exam is coming even if you went to the lecture. The final was a little rough but there was a curve. Make sure to do the extra credit on the homework assignments.

Very good lecturer. He explains concepts pretty well, and most content on the exams and homeworks are taken from these lectures or practice exams. Even if an exam is hard, he curves very generously. A decent chunk of extra credit was also given. Overall it was an easy and fun class.

Awful scheduling in the evening so I never really attended any lectures in person. The lecture slides and videos had examples of how to do various procedures step-by-step, and they were pretty clear. However, the programming homework was kind of  difficult

The best professor I've ever had for all my AI focused computer science courses. He keeps lectures engaging with slides that heavily utilize step-by-step examples and the occasional meme. He gives detailed, in-depth, step by step explanations in Ed Discussion. His exams are difficult, but if you truly pay attention, you shouldn't have an issue.
Extremely unprepared every class. Students who try to go to his lectures to learn will be out of luck.

Sometimes goes too fast during lecture, but overall he's not a bad teacher considering how difficult the class is. He's also a very nice person.

(Talks kind of like Dr. Doofenshmirtz)
Don't be fooled by how sweet and kind he comes off. Overall, will not be a good experience because he just doesn't teach well. You are in for a tough semester.
Tests are extremely difficult. Lectures are also unbearably boring and do not help at all in understanding material.

I had asked around and the averages for our section was ~20% lower than all other sections. This points to an underlying issue with the professor and it shows in how disengaged he is with students in his lectures. Very poor instruction overall and the worst teacher I have come across
Best advice I can give incoming students: Take with mummert if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute waste of my semester going to his lectures. All he does is write in silence and keep his head glued to his notes. Nothing else! No point in trying to go to his class, super unhelpful professor. Very bad look on Purdue hiring this guy... DO NOT TAKE AT ALL COSTS!!!

Really disappointed that this is the standard for Purdue Math Professors. I've had bad math teachers in high school, but I never realized that university could have even worse. I very much liked my other professors for chemistry and ENGR. Hopefully Purdue takes this into account.

I really do not think this professor is a bad guy at all. Genuinely seems very nice. Unfortunately he does not prepare any of us well for the exams. His communication skills are very hard to follow, he clearly does not put any planning into his lectures, and it just looks like he's in another world.
Big GPA Ruiner. Had to work really hard to just get a minimum mark for passing. Never wanna see him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaching style is very bad and clearly disregards the fact that people are suffering because of his poor lectures.
Should be fired. Actually makes me mad how bad of a teacher he was.
I don't know a single one of my friends who actually found his class useful. Now I will have to retake the class. I'm going to self study this time around because no way will I be going back.
So happy that I passed. My gpa standards lowered because of him.
I already retook the class so I ended up doing well this time around, but the professor was way worse than my previous one last semester.
Ended up learning more from the mylabmath examples than this guy. I suggest doing that instead.
The transition from Calc 1 and 2 was already hard enough. This guy made it impossible to learn anything.
Lectures = him quietly copying notes super fast while mumbling. Zero eye contact, zero interaction. Questions? Good luck. Self-teach from textbook if you take him.
Coming from other profs, he was a shock. Just scripts notes on iPad without looking up or elaborating.

This guy is a walking disaster for anyone trying to pass Calc 3. Head buried in his notes the entire time, writing furiously without a single explanation beyond a barely audible mutter. Questions? Forget it, he won't even glance up. Lectures are just him copying stuff super fast with zero context.
I genuinely learned more Calc 3 from YouTube comments than from these lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Imagine watching someone solve a puzzle while refusing to explain the rules. That is this lecture. Head down, mumbling, no engagement. By week four like 90% the room had stopped coming. ChenFlix carried this class harder than anything else.

I kept thinking, “maybe today's lecture will be better.” It never was. He writes extremely fast with messy handwriting and mumbles the entire time. Examples skip importnat steps that magically reappear on exams. I survived solely through external resources. Would not take again.
I did well in MA 261, but NOT because of him. If you are in this class you either go to a different lecturer or just watch ChenFlix. DON'T WATSE YOUR TIME!!!!
Very nice man, very bad teacher.

Prof Yassemi is a good person. But he does not know how to teach MA261. He spends the entire lecture rewriting hard-to-read notes and textbook definitions from pre-written notes that he has on the side; he speeds through the math examples and skips a lot of steps, and the examples are rarely helpful in recitations or exams. SWITCH LECTURES ASAP

Yassemi is one of those guys who's really smart but can't teach to save his life. His handwriting looks like a foreign language, speeds through the slides, and doesn't look up while he quietly mumbles to himself, making some people raise their hands for 10 minutes before he notices. For a class as notoriously difficult as Calc 3, take someone else.

Dr. Yassemi: the Gordan Ramsay of nothing burger lectures. He seems nice, but his lectures were beyond unhelpful. Mostly, he just read definitions from the textbook and sped through examples with little to no explanation, all while mumbling and writing very messily. If you can take MA261 with another prof, do so: your GPA will thank you.

He literally just keeps his head down, doesn't say anything, and writes notes extremely fast the whole lecture. Zero explanations and clearly doesn't care.  Amazed how he hasn't been fired yet. Also doesn't bother to answer questions when students raise their hands because he's looking down all the time.

All he does is copy lecture notes on an ipad and quietly mumbles what he is writing without looking up at all. This extremely hard to learn from especially compared to Matsuki's teaching style in Calc 1 and 2, which was far more engaging. He also does not offer any study guides for exams.
Had this professor first semester. He is very personable and interesting to talk to in office hours

He has conducted wonderful lectures, but he also made some mistakes in the lectures. The grading of homework is fair. However, the setup of the exams is not persuasive since we had only multiple choices for final without partial credits. For a course of mathematics, this isn't representing the mathematical capability of students well.
Very good lectures

Unclear, not helpful and overall does not seem like even she has a full grasp of the concepts. You are better off reading the book and looking up youtube videos than attending lectures. Grading is inconsistent and does not give a good representation of how much a student knows.

Yulia is an average professor in my opinion.  Her lectures aren't very informative so you are better off by just reading the book.  Yulia is also very approachable.  If you have a question or a conflict with your homework she will work with you to help.

This professor should not be allowed to teach! Its shocking how she got into teaching!Please go back to doing another profession.

first midterm the class average was 48.25% and the most common was around 45% most of the class did not do well, for the second midterm the average was 57.98% and the most common grade was 58.75% a minor improvement. messed up lecture slides impossible to understand them if you miss a class (which was at 7:30 freaking AM not his fault but you could help us with better slides)

Bad class, everyone cheats on the quizzes and exams by using AI. Probably going to get a C and just a waste of my time studying this material. I don't even know what the point of having a ranking based class is.

Not a good person

Just go to class!! Attendance is very important but it definitely pays off bc she makes it very clear what you need to know for the exams. If you pay attention and put the time into studying with the resources she provides, you'll be perfectly fine!

Professor Zuelly's class had clear expectations and was not difficult. It was nice to not have final exams with 100% attendance throughout the semester as well. I was not a fan of her as a person. attendance mandatory

Such a fun class - the labs are the best part! I learned a lot and Dr. Zuelly is a wonderful professor. If you had perfect attendance you didn't have to take the final at the end of the semester, which is a plus.

Dr Zuelly is an amazing professor! she does a great job lecturing, and posts recordings of her lectures so you could go back and rewatch the lecture if needed. bro gives amazing lectures. so much fun. absolutely love this class.

He is funny and great.

Loeb was a phenomenal professor who is clearly passionate about his classes, cats, and Star Trek. Besides his dad jokes, his lectures were truly interesting and engaging. The professor is nice and she really respects her students. Attendance is 15% of your grade and lectures are pretty boring. The TA's are a little picky and tough graders when it comes to the weekly readings but easy to complete. Make sure to pick a good group since there is a final group presentation and paper that are worth a lot of points.

Attendance is worth 15% of your grade, but attending it is borderline painful. It's boring, uninteresting, and a waste of time. We had 4 major assignments: an essay, a midterm, a group project, and a group essay. All 4 were based on a road that holds almost no significance to life on campus and had nothing to do with what we learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You have to read a lot for this class and the group work is a pain because she didn't give enough time but was open to change things in the future. She really respects her stufents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: She was not in class for so long yet still takes attendance, and they still use the attendance sheet for such a big class. At the beginning of the semester, the TA didn't tell us where to sign after the class if we didn't get the sheet. Students just pass it around the whole room. Group projects are hard and long (25-30 pages). Don't take it.
She is a tough grader and doesn't want to communicate with her students

I HATE THIS CLASS.
the professor was sick throughout the whole semester for about one month (I know this is not technically her fault but I'm still mad af)!!! The group projects weigh a lot of points, and for a class of over 100 ppl she still uses paper attendance sheets. Grading is super slow, lot of reading before mid-term. JUST RUN.

This class is all busywork and she expects essentially grad-student level work from students which is pretty ridiculous considering the class is just an elective for a majority of the class. She also wasn't in class for 1/2 the semester but still took attendance for points. Her and her TA also don't respond to emails! Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Nyssa is hands down my favorite professor I've ever had. Her Technology and Culture class was extremely interesting and I enjoyed every lecture she gave. The assignments correlated not only with the curriculum but with current events ongoing in society. She has a real heart for her students and her passion for teaching transmits to her students

The accent for non-Chinese speakers takes time to adjust but the content delivered is clear. Her pacing during lectures is good and reserves time to answer many questions asked by students. Professor Zhou is all business, no play, so the lectures will require high concentration. She also cares about her students and hopes they succeed.
It was a good class. She's nice and uses coding demos and quizzes to explain the material
Her lectures are very dry and boring but she seems to genuinely care about the class doing good. This class is pretty easy if you have prior programming experience so lecture isn't that important

I liked Professor Zhou's lectures. This is an entry-level class, but the labs and exams can be somewhat challenging. She is flexible and willing to work with students when help is needed. Overall, I had a good experience in this class.

Professor Zhou genuinely cares about her students and puts a lot of effort into teaching. CS159 is hard, but she explains concepts clearly and makes it easier to understand. Office hours are very helpful, and the lecture quizzes after each topic really help reinforce the material

Lectures are dry. The packet's practice tests are essential for the grade. Don't buy the textbook; it's rarely used. Rigid classroom: assigned seating and no talking. Communication via email and in-class questions is difficult. Quizzes run long. Coordinate with your Lab TA for help.

Her lectures are not helpful. Long lecture quizzes (20–30 minutes) leave little time to learn new concepts. She doesn't explain code clearly and often can't answer questions due to the next class. Learning relies on TAs and self-study. The workload is manageable, but if you want to learn during lectures, I don't recommend taking her.

Noo one better than Dr. Idrissi to teach anything about Arab culture. I took many classes with him and it is clear he cares about the learning of all his students. Staying on top of reading assigned texts and participating is the key to getting an A+ in the class. I don't agree with those that say he's tough, he just wants us to think critically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: English fluency is mediocre. Uses lots of lecturing and little to no interactive activities. Goes off topic often and seems disroganized.
Professor seems to be profiling Non-American students.

I really enjoyed Prof. Idrissi Alami's class, you can tell that he is extremely passionate about what he teaches. He is knowledgeable and well respected. I appreciated all the time he dedicated to making the class worthwhile. A good amount of reading, but just do the work and you should be fine.

I really enjoyed Prod. Alma's class. Sure, theres a lot of reading, but if you do the reading and are prepared for class you have nothing to worry about. Had some really great discussions in this class that got me interested in the subject even further.
Really great and knowledgeable professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Cool concepts taught, but you have to read about 150 pages a week and do a reading journal for each passage. There are a lot of papers and extra work. The prompts for the response papers are very philosophical. Just be prepared to do a lot of critical reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Humorous guy, don't vote E on the clicker quizzes or he'll make fun of you. Overall good and caring professor though. Class is fairly easy although there are a good amount of assignments.

Professor Esmaeili promptly and effectively answered my questions regarding the content of the course. Even though I took the class in an online format, I felt that communication was always a top priority of the professor.
Great professor, lots of assignments, but an easy course. He is caring and willing to help the students.

Tough but fair. Eager to help students outside of class. Slows down when students have trouble understanding; all you have to do is ask. He even offered to drop the first exam grade for the students who failed it, provided they learned the material for the final. Overall a very reasonable professor.
His notion of "teaching" is copying notes on the blackboard. Very often would entrust his TAs with teaching the class, contrary to departmental and university policies.
Overall, not really a good experience.  Several times, his solutions to exam problems has been for us to use a technique that was not taught in class.  Can't say I'd recommend any of his classes.
Lectures as though he is unaware of the blank faces in the crowd
Not good at teaching
No Comments
One of the best lecturers I've experienced. Clearly understands the content extremely well and is able to answer all questions that people have and encourages people to ask them.

He is clear, cares about learning, and explains concepts well. But the course was overly difficult for a class on beam bending. First exam had unfamiliar setups and too many calcs, no one finished, so he added 20%. The second was more fair but too long; average was failing, 20% extra credit assignment was offered. The fair final allowed me to pass

Prof. Agyei is a decent lecturer, however, he presents the content in an incredibly bland way making this class unbearably boring. His exams are often needlessly tricky and have problems that test knowledge not directly discussed in class. Attendance is also required which sucks because listening to the boring lectures at 9:00 am is insufferable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Agyei is very passionate about the material and it does help in learning it. The only issue is the material is kinda boring so his passion can only take you so far. Lectures were very helpful. I think exams were a little too hard imo based on the practice exams and homework, but office hours would definitely equip you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Agyei makes a really easy class really hard. I had to teach myself the lecture content in order to do the homework, because by mid-semester he was 2 weeks behind in lecture. Gives negative points for incorrect multiple choice answers on the exams. Claimed the class wouldn't be curved but then made the final so hard that he had to curve by 5%.

man he is so boring I couldn't take it. And required attendance. He was pretty clear in explaining though. But hw and exams were just strangely tough or a stretch past lecture content. He was much better than the other professor of the semester though. I felt bad bc no one laughed at his jokes, no one paid attention.
Very caring professor who is good at answering questions and will thoroughly explain concepts. Lectures can get long and slow but that is partially the course itself.

Professor Agyei is one of my favorite professors I have had. He is always passionate about the content at hand and does a great job throughout lectures to answer questions the class has. He always leaves time at the end of class for students to come ask individual questions. He will even crack jokes every now and then.

Tried a flipped classroom, which ultimately went poorly and was reverted. Moved slowly through simple concepts and usually didn't complete said lesson by the end of lecture. Seemed to think any students' poor performance was his personal responsibility. Overall not a bad professor; just struggled to figure out a good format for his first class.

I loved taking this class with Dr Aguilar. The lectures are setup in a way that's very unusual in that there are very few words on the slides but they were so easy to follow and the pacing didn't feel like information was being shoved down my throat. He took time to thoroughly answer questions and was always very friendly and wholesome

The course is laid out pretty understandably and the expectations are set on day one. The lectures are very informative and while attendance is not required it is great to be in the course and meet the professor who is a genuinely great and respectful academic. 10/10 course as long as you take the time to learn and question.
Thank you for your lectures and exposure you gave me all through your teachings.

Professor Aguilar was one of the best professors I've ever had at Purdue, he wants his students to succeed as much as possible. If you're struggling in the class, ask for help and email him. He gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit. He welcomes questions during lectures. If you need anything, email him and he will respond quickly.

I started with a very bad grade in the first exam because I did not study enough, but Dr Aguilar gives opportunities to improve your grade. When I had problems,  I contacted him directly instead of the TA. At least the ones for this year were awful. They did not respond e-mails. Professor Aguilar responded my e-mails even after midnight!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The material is not easy but if you pay attention during class you will do well. The professor give several opportunities to improve your grade. This year the TA were not very good, the review sections with them were not very well organized. The TA did not answer e-mails so if better to e-mail Dr Aguilar if you have any problem.

He teaches the worst class I've ever taken. Literally five grades in the book. 4 20 point quizzes, 1 essay, and one 120 point final exam. The quizzes are over several lectures yet consist of two, page long, essay questions. He does not tell you what topic they are over. He does not give your quizzes back, so you don't even know what you missed.

This professor has the vaguest slides and is monotonous. The class grade is based on quizzes, an essay, and a final. I never wished a class had homework until this class. The page for this class is also not consistently updated and there's not even a formal syllabus. This class is the most bare-boned I have ever had thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a solid professor. Lectures are short and easy to understand. Not much work required for the class and extra credit is offered. Pretty easy to earn an 'A' if you watch the lectures and have access to the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The biology professors at Purdue continue to out-do themselves. One of the worst classes I've ever taken. The material is boring and difficult. The professor and TAs are rude and not very helpful. The grading is absurd and all quizzes are short answer based so beware. Avoid taking this class if you can help it.

She's super sweet and understanding, and clearly loves what she does. There was a snowstorm that prevented me from getting to campus safely, and she understood and allowed me to virtually do my work that week. The only thing is she's a little hard to understand at times due to her accent, but otherwise an awesome professor.

One of my favorite professors due to her high energy and insightful advice during class. Is always willing and able to help in class, but is difficult to reach during office hours and outside of class. Would highly recommend as a professor. Regarding the class itself, always check the grading criteria, be available to your teammates. Divide work.

Very clear about what she wants for assignments and projects, which made the class feel organized and manageable. Always quick to help over email and incredibly supportive, even with such a big class. Genuinely cares about her students. Fantastic professor.

ENGR 131 is a tedious class. The rubrics are vague, group work means that your grade depends on others, and if you don't pay attention at the beginning of the semester then the exams will be difficult as they are all Excel based. Prof. Aguilar is cheerful, caring, and can answer any question. I would recommend taking her class if at all possible.

Professor Aguilar was the perfect professor for this class. Concise but effective lecturing, with more than enough time to work in class. She is kind and caring, and answers any questions you have. The grading is generally quite fair, and when you feel that it's not, the TA's in the class are very accessible to help fix your grade.

Prof. Aguilar is one of the best ENGR131 instructors you can have. She cares about all of her students and genuinely wants them to succeed. She is available if you ever have a question and responds to emails extremely quickly. Make sure to cross your t's and dot your i's because the grading is extremely harsh for small mistakes.

The class was quite easy. There was one period with a heavy workload with a project due and a test in the same week, but this was an exception. She gives extra credit at the end and is willing to fix grades if you believe the grade you received is unfair. She is also always willing to answer questions and provide help on confusing assignments.

She is super charismatic, always cares about her students, replies to emails very quickly, and is very understanding. If you have any problem, just talk to her and she will give you extra time to complete your assignments. She is an excellent professor

Aguilar is probably one of the best professors there is for 132. She's kind, caring, and explains things clearly. Our section's GTA was the complete opposite (rude, uncooperative) however, if you don't agree with a GTA's take on your grade for an assignment, you can always go to Aguilar to get it fixed.

She is super sweet and always clear at the beginning of class what she expects on the assignments, when the deadlines are, how to work the MATLAB code etc. My team had major issues personally, and she was super helpful to working with us and was lenient. She's probably one of the best profs you can have for a class structured like ENGR132

At the start, I had trouble with keeping up with the class, not understanding everything that was being said. Over time, you get used to proficiency, but I felt like the studio/lecture part was rushed and that more productivity could be have done in lecture rather than free time. Also, I would mostly read class slides rather than listen.
A kind and understanding professor. Not difficult to understand, made grade expectations clear. Was flexible with missed assignments and grade curving at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Despite the course being pathetically structured (not the professor's fault), Professor Aguilar did the best she could to make it somewhat educational and enjoyable. She was always ready to help with any problems we had with assignments and would go beyond what any other professor would do.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Aguilar was a very nice professor who took the time to help students when facing a problem. A lot of the course relies on group projects, but communication with Prof Aguilar and the GTA can improve your situation if you have a bad group. The work done in class prepares you to do well on the exams and in later-level engineering classes.
Flew through the slides and didn't explain much. Easy exams and work though.

Hello freshman, here's what you need to know about Aguilar's ENGR131.

1. This class is a points game. Always read the rubrics (course tools>assignments). Half the class is between 93-95%, and 94% is an A. Get every point you can.

2. Get a good group. You may be unfortunate and get people that decide they can get away with not doing anything.

Totally recommend this class! My team and I learned so much, and going with Prof. Aguilar is the way to go. She's always there to help, gives awesome programming tips, offers solutions to problems, and really listens to our CATME feedback. Plus, she's super cool to work with.

Awful class in general. The grading is all over the place, and almost none of the concepts you need for assignments would actually be taught during class. The prof is okay, but she can be difficult to understand at times due to her accent and pace. The groups are a hit or miss, but group projects weigh heavily in this class, so hope for the best.

Professor Aguilar will always take the time to help her students truly understand the material. She does lots of examples that are very relevant to the assignments. She is so kind and makes an effort to get to know her students, which I really appreciate.

I love Professor Aguilar! Coding can be difficult if you are new. PLEASE reach out to her if you need help. She always willing to help you with HW and other parts of the class. She is so nice and caring. Do your work and try in the class and you will be fine. The group work 2nd semester is annoying but doable if you have a good group.

Pr. Aguilar is my sun on a gloomy day. Makes your day better. The class is very tough if you are not a coding pro, but she makes is as easy as possible. If you get a bad project partner, TALK TO HER! Do not hesitate! She will do whatever she can to help you. If you feel sick, tell her: she'll let you stay home. You missed assignment?  get extension
She makes the most out of ENGR132. The class can be difficult, but she makes it as much fun as she can . She is very enthusiastic, and I would love to take a class with her again.
THE BEST!

Dr. Aguilar is simply the best! When I first heard from upperclassmen about how this course is very annoying, I was worried. But Dr. Aguilar made this course a breeze! She was always there to help us, and clarified all the doubts we asked. The GTA was amazing too! I really liked this class, even if it was all online.
I definitely recommend to Prof. Aguilar. She is super helpful all the time.

Aguilar is a great professor. She talks really fast, but she always answers every question and she replies to emails very fast. She's one of the best for 131, but it's up to the TAs you get. Practice exams are NOT like real exams, especially the second.
I liked the class! The GTAs and Prof. Aguilar were amazing! Thank you for the great semester!

The grading in this class was questionable in the beginning. Students consistently were counted off for things that they blatantly did correctly. Material was covered adequately, but in no way in-depth. Instructions left unclear, which made students have to ask several questions for clarification. Overall, okay class with cool material.
I took the curse ENGR131 this summer 2020. Professor Aguilar was super useful during the class time. She reviewed all the CATME Surveys and fixed the problems with my teammates.

Prof. Aguilar has an infectious enthusiasm and she is always incredibly helpful whenever her students need something. I cannot emphasize enough how much I appreciate her passion for her students and how valued she makes everyone feel both inside and outside of the classroom (Zoom). She responds very quickly by email.

Professor Aguilar did a great job at keeping our class up to date on everything that needed to be completed for the class. In addition, she was very helpful in class if I had questions and would always respond to my emails quickly if I emailed her with questions. Professor Aguilar also made the class very entertaining and engaging

I took the course ENGR 131 this summer 2020. The instructor was always very eager and energetic in class, which was always great, but especially during early classes. She was involved with the students and maintained great communication when transitioning to remote learning. Whenever my group or I needed help, she would work.

No idea why her ratings are so high. Took her summer online class and almost NO ONE enjoyed her lecture. Her lectures were extremely boring and most of the time she read entirely off the slides. She didn't reply to emails and many points were taken off for no clear reasons. The only good thing was that this class itself was easy.
Nicest woman ever. The course is a lot of work but she made my life a little easier. Easily approachable and easy to talk to. Short lectures and lots of working time. She is the best.

Professor Aguilar is very kind and energetic. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Her teaching team and herself do a great job at interacting with the students to ensure we understand the content and can complete difficult assignments. Mostly uses class time to work on homework assignments or group projects.
Very helpful professor. Expert at MATLAB.

Aguilar is the best 131 teacher. Extremely caring and always open to trying to help her students learn while actually understanding the material. This class in general has a heavy work load for a 2 credit hour class, but having Aguilar definitely made this class easier compared to other professors.
Prof. Aguilar is very helpful and proactive

An absolute gem. 5.0 is an understatement. She is extremely generous, helpful and flexible, and gives great but brief lectures in a way there will still be a good amount of time to work on assignments in class. She walks around class proactively offering help, giving solid advice and feedback. Getting her for 132 next semester is my top priority.

Professor Aguilar makes her classes fun and interesting even when the material we're covering is boring. She also helps a lot if we are having any issues with assignments or homeworks. She does however cover the material too quick, so be prepared before her lectures!

Professor Aguilar is overall a good professor. The class is structured in a way where not much teaching takes place during the actual class and is mostly learned in online modules you watch before attending class, but regardless, she is helpful in answering questions and responds quickly to emails.

Prof. Aguilar is an awesome lady and I truly enjoyed every class with her. She is always available for extra help and is willing to check any work you do in class. She responds to emails very quickly. One thing to be aware of is that she sometimes has issues understanding questions, so be diligent and email her for more clarification if needed.

Would give 0. Worst prof i've had at purdue. The class was curved 16 percent at the end so a 44 was passing. It was a 7:30 class the notes were basically a pdf with chicken scratch where nothing is useful. He just copies off the textbook in lecture like looking back and forth. I learned nothing and he is not helpful and rude. Bad at communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The issue is the way the professor ran the course. He is actually quite nice and good at explaining (with the occasional mistake), and provided free text book pdfs. The issue is he does not clearly define expectations for the exam, grading and does not post lecture videos but does post notes. He listens to feedback. Tough class and exams, big curve
One of the worst professors at Purdue. All lecture material is taken directly from the textbook, but extremely difficult to follow along with. Take the class with someone else.

He doesn't prepare any slides and instead writes directly from the textbook during the lecture, which is really hard to understand. It's almost impossible to study after you go back to your room, so you end up teaching yourself by searching the internet. Also, there aren't many examples for students to prepare for the exams.

The class doesn't seem to matter to him at all. Gives almost no practice outside of what's done in lectures. Gave an idea of what he was looking for in terms of answers on the first exam, and when most people followed what he asked for, it was not reflected in terms of grading and was very inconsistent between many people.

Professor Aggarwal is incredibly knowledgeable and challenges students to think critically. His passion makes the material engaging, and he's always approachable outside class. Tough exams, but you leave the course much stronger. Highly recommend if you want to truly grow.

His lectures were very difficult to follow and he kinda reduced your confidence as he seemed to look down on all his students if they aren't aware of certain topics and asked question. The grade curve is pretty generous tho as everyone does horrible in his tests.

He was always available outside of class, and encouraged us to freely ask any questions we had. His dedication to their students' learning, their clear and insightful lectures, and their willingness to support and guide us through the subject matter made this course a truly enriching experience.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was a research based course I took at KAUST, where the content started from basics to the recent research results. It was mathematically rigorous. The professor covered the new topics well, and knew the material. I enjoyed learning about the contents.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures were great, and well explained. The intuitions developed have been useful in the work after the course. Professor was available outside class, and we could freely ask any questions. The final grades were very lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class learned a ton. Professor is prepared for every lecture and the class is very organized.
I love his style of teaching and he actually cares about students. The professor is accessible outside class for any questions.

Professor Aggarwal's lectures are pretty hard to follow but controls is a pretty tough subject - definitely one of the hardest in IE. I'm not sure if anyone can teach it well but Aggarwal makes plenty of examples in lecture and is accommodating if students want to change an exam date.
Amazing Professor. Attend all classes and you'll do great on exams. Generous curve at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was enjoyable, he answered the questions well in class and was not hesitant to repeat the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It sounds like he was a lot worse during COVID/online, but I thought he was fine this semester. Really heavy weight to exams (especially final), but really solid partial credit and large curve at the end of the course (only a 40% required for passing!). Hes obviously knowledgeable about the material, and I would take this course again with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First exam had 3 problems and no partial credit was given if you messed up on the first step. Imagine learning how to drive without knowing what an automobile is. Thats how this class is. He teaches the motions and blurts out equations without ever explaining real world applications. He is condescending esp when asking clarification on class prblms
Wonderful Professor! A good human being. His course definitely makes you work but is fruitful. He has deep knowledge and is very intelligent!

This professor is atrocious. Everyone did well on the first two exams in the course. Rather than be happy that his students are understanding the material, he shortens the final exam & makes it impossible to solve, just to bring the class average down. He has zero respect for his students. Which is fine because we also have zero respect for him.

Professor said he was going to curve the class down since students during COVID had done too well on his first two exams. Instead of curving the class down, he made the final exam too short time-constrainted and impossibly difficult just to get the class averages somewhere near where he wanted them. Horrible professor who wont work with students

I don't know how the Purdue justifies paying this man 165k a year. Worst professor I have ever had. Thank god the books assigned are useful, because his lectures are impossible to follow, with him just kind of lecturing, without giving any kind of context for what he's teaching. He also regularly sleeps through his class, a class with attendance.

Poor lecturer with poor handwriting. Does nothing to explain the lecture material and ignores/passes off any questions he doesn't want to or doesn't know how to answer (content and course logistics). NO clear grading scheme, with no scale in his syllabus and refuses to set any grade boundaries. Unwilling to listen to and work with students!

Absolutely the worst professor at Purdue. AVOID AVOID AVOID. Insanely unorganized and inconsistent. His lectures are straight reading from the book and he does no additional explaining because he clearly doesn't know the material himself and he makes mistakes very frequently. Insanely arrogant and cocky.
Avoid this professor at all costs. Rude, ignorant, can't teach to save his life. You're better off teaching the material to yourself.
Rude, Arrogant. Bad English. Answers questions rudely. Does not know how to teach. Worst professor at Purdue. Does not even deserve to be a professor. Extremely insecure.
Lots of homework. Giving the lecture just copying from the textbook without explaining why. The behavior of answering questions is like defending, rude and hilarious.
The worst professor I've had at Purdue. Avoid if you can. He doesn't teach the topics, he tests are incredibly hard and he's rude.

He has no prepared slides, and the actual exam is identical to the practice exam, with crib sheet. So we are tested on how good we are at copying. To make the curve he manipulates the points, awarding lower points to the copied questions and adding 1 random question with high weightage. Pretty much outright awful.

For 'lectures' he copied the book onto the whiteboard which is not very helpful. Almost no examples, no practice exams, loosely says what material is going to be on the exam but follows it up with "But it might be different". Never received exam solutions to learn what we did wrong. Very rude and non-helpful when students ask questions. Ridiculous!

He is one of the most awful professors in Purdue. He is rude to students during office hours, has horrible accent and awful in explaining everything in class. He follows the book completely so just reading the book is enough and does not upload solution to exam or practice exams . He also changed a lot of rules in the middle of the semester.

Stubbornly writes with small font on the whiteboard all the time even after students ask him to use the doc-cam. Answers students' questions as if he is in a debate (defending his "teaching" and attacks students' wrong answer). Changes his policies in the middle of the semester. Does a great job in making sure you understand nothing.
The programming homework is useless and takes a lot of time to do.
Really nice professor who tries to help everybody.

Luckily I knew some spanish coming into this past semeser. He does not know how to explain concepts sometimes and when I ask questions in class, half the time he does not know how to answer. I have an A currenlty right now, but I feel bad for the people who are learning spanish for the first time. Also, know he can be very rude aswell.

Professor Quinones was very lecture heavy. If you miss a class you are kind screwed because he takes forever to answer emails and it's hard to ask questions because you are not allowed to speak in English. I understand he wants you to learn Spanish but for Spanish 101, you should be able to ask complex questions in English.

I was very excited to take spanish, but this teacher's abiltiy to teach is horrible. Did not answer any questions and does not reply to emails. He also did not explain concepts well. He was often very rude how he spoke to fellow classmates. I am honeslty thinking about going to the head of deparment because he is very unproffesional.

His actions throughout this semester shows that he doesn't care to help. He would not explain concepts and not answer questions. His brightspace page is not clear with dates of test, quizzes, and homework. He assigned groups projects with people that don't show up to class. It is impossible to contact them. Also you can't ask questions in English.
He doesn't explain concepts very well and sometimes didn't know the answers to the questions himself. The class was confusing but he was good at teaching some concepts.

Quinones is a great professor and he cares a lot for his students. In Spanish 101, there are a lot of tests and he expects each student to understand the material as soon as you start the material so there is a lot of outside of class studying. Inside class he attempts to get everyone to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is the best instructor!

She was fun, but had a thick accent which could be difficult at times, or it could be that the mics at Purdue are really bad. Overall, I had fun. I took this in the summer of 2021 and I was mostly with my group. She made a she made a discord server for all of us. She knows what she's doing and it clearly shows.

THIS REVIEW IS FROM ENGR132 (they didn't have it as an option):

Professor Aguilar was amazing. She explained our assignments very well and her class slides were extremely helpful when working in MATLAB. She is always willing to help whenever asked and genuinely cares about the students' success.
Professor Aguilar was a very caring professor for ENGR 131 in Summer 2021. She made the lecture very engaging

One of my favorite professors within the aviation department. I feel like I learned a lot from his course, yet overall, it did not feel difficult. His grading is lenient as long as you try, and he is clearly passionate about aviation.

Adam is a nice guy and very knowledgeable. He's actively working as an airport director so is a gokd resource for job specific information. It's very lecture heavy and sometimes they can get boring. Would recommend taking his class

I had him for 459. Baxmeyer is not a bad prof. Decent lecturer, and good guest speakers. I've never really reviewed professors on here, but if you have Tim as your TA, you might as well just drop the class. When nobody in the class can get above a C on an essay the entire semester, you might as well just take another class. Don't waste your time.

Great lectures and a really well organized and paced class. The grading scale is also very forgiving. The only frustrating element of the class was having to get up at 8:30 for lectures. Overall incredible class.

He was very open to feedback and was accessible outside of class. He did give quizzes every Friday, so participation is mandatory on Fridays. However, his lectures were very engaging and you could tell he is very passionate in his work. Additionally, he was understanding of our stresses, such as having a Friday quiz during an exam week

Great guy. Wants to know you and always says hello if you see him outside of class. One of the most genuine people at Purdue. You can tell he is such a distinguished person who is truly passionate about his work.

He quizzes every week, but they are easy if you listen to him and do your homework. If you go a step more and listen on Fridays, you'll have near a 100 in this class. Dr. Wasserman makes sure his class is enjoyable even with some pretty boring topics.
Great guy and a great prof. The kind of person you'd expect and want as your first Purdue professor. Can't recommend enough.

Love love love Wasserman. He's so kind and you can tell he cares so much about the students. You need an 85% to get an A, with 3-4 dropped quizzes and either 1 dropped midterm or half-dropped final. Only necessary attendance is Friday quizzes, every week. Would recommend actually doing the reading, but it's not checked. Overall loved the class!

Dr. Wasserman is da GOAT. He wants to get to know and his lectures have amazing demos and clear notes. You only need an 85 to get an A and he lets you drop 4 quizzes, 1 midterm or half the final, and 1 lab. Dr. Wasserman sets you up very well for higher level chem no matter if you plan to go into grad, medical, dental, or whatever career!

Dr. Wasserman was probably one of my favorite professors this semester. He's really creative with his lectures and is happy to answer any questions that his students have. The only thing that gets me are the Friday quizzes, which can be a bit stressful at times to prepare for. There's a lot of outside work, however. But Wasserman is awesome!
His lectures are nice with demos and stuff, I just wish he provided more review material for tests throughout the course. Chill professor.

GO TO THE LECTURES FOR CHM 136. Quizzes and exams have lecture based questions that aren't covered by the homework or textbook. CHM 136 was pretty easy, though. TONS of partial credit was given on exams and lots of things get dropped at the end of the semester.

Dr. Wasserman is a nice guy but I found his lectures to confusing and somewhat irrelevant. Instead of explaining concepts he often derived complicated equations we didn't have to know as a way to teach the concepts. But he posts relevant study guides and practice questions for each test so the exams are very managable- TAs are lenient graders too.
Literally my favorite professor so far, he's so sweet. This class was graded super generously as well.
Pros: -You learn a lot -Interactive class -Connections -Fair grader Cons: -Can be tough sometimes (concepts) -Kinda wants u to attend class badly

He is clearly very passionate about the subject and wants his students to learn. He makes up games and activities instead of lectures on Fridays and uploads lots of resources on Blackboard. Almost every lecture had a demo, which made the morning class better.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had wasserman for the second half of chem 116. His online lectures were interesting and Straight to the point. Him and the professor for the first half of chem 116 wanted everybody to be graded fairly so an A was roughly a 75% due to only 12 multiple choice questions on the exams. The exams were hard but i hear the TA's right them and not him.

He is very organized and gives very clear explanations. We did a lot of problems in class and he went step by step explaining  it. He is also very helpful and wants students to understand the material.
