I felt like Dr. Wasserman did a great job of helping visualize some of the more complex topics. Great teacher.
Nice guy, thick accent but is pretty understandable. Again, be prepared to work a lot of math problems since the exams in this course tend to be about 70% math problems.

Due to my own lack of motivation, I didn't personally interact with him but I notice that he helps students a lot who want to learn. His lectures were clear and I love his accent (kept me awake unlike Robinson...) didn't go to many lectures but the tests aren't horrible. Just keep up and you can get an A.
Terrible professor. Writes ridiculous exam questions. His style is just weird.

I had Robinson for the first half of CHM 116, and he was a good professor, but then I got Wasserman for the second half, and suddenly had a renewed interest in Chemistry. He is an excellent lecturer. He's the best I've had so far. He's good at answering questions and he works through problems by hand in lecture, which is really helpful.

Dr. Wasserman is a good lecturer. When I took CHM116, Dr. McMillan does the first half of the semester and Dr. Wasserman does the second half. Dr. Wasserman is still pretty new to Purdue so that may be why. He is a better lecturer than Dr. McMillan, but harder to understand due to his Colombian accent. Does a lot of neat in-class experiments.
Prof. Bodony is a great conductor and gives very clear, concise feedback. He makes a lot of jokes in rehearsals and has a deep knowledge of musical history.
cool guy

Professor Bodony is a great orchestra director, and I really enjoyed all of the rehearsals. He is a very good conductor, and I like the advice he gives to make our pieces sound better. Show up to class (that is what your graded on) and enjoy.
Prof. Bodony is kind and conducts well, but sometimes seems preoccupied and ended up missing some of our classes in favor of asking us to manage our own sectionals. Overall a great option though!

Professor Bodony was my favorite Purdue professor, and all-time favorite orchestra conductor. He is caring, empathetic and passionate about his students and their success. College is not easy for many, and he makes it known that he is there for his students. He is a great leader for the orchestras and music department as a whole.
great conductor and teacher who is very nice

Professor Bodony is a great conductor and teacher for orchestra. He is very passionate and encouraging and really has helped me keep my passion for violin alive. He really cares about the quality of music but delivers feedback and improvements in a very constructive way.

He's young but he definitely knows his stuff! He goes out of his way to explain what terms in the music mean, the history behind the piece, and what the composer wants or what he wants when we start a new piece. In addition, I think his auditions are very fair, so you don't need to be afraid of them.

Professor Bodony is a really passionate conductor and wants the best for his students. He is super laid back, but do not skip too many rehearsals or he will check up on you. There are no exams in this class, but seating auditions are optional for the concert. If you want to continue orchestra, definitely take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bodony is an amazing guy. In the chaos of the coronavirus, he has been nothing but caring and understanding of how weird everything is for us right now. The first day of the semester, he gave a speech that made me tear up - acknowledging that our lives are strange right now, but as musicians we have the ability to escape through music
Professor Bodony is one of the best orchestra conductors I've ever had. Truly a nice and funny person as well.

Adam Bodony is a God among men. He is by far the most caring, genuine professor I have had. He understands that we are not here as music majors, and understands that we're playing because it's our passion. He picks fun pieces and makes the orchestra sounds absolutely splendid.

I wanted to continue playing violin so I signed up for orchestra. Bodony does a good job picking fun music to play and providing helpful feedback, but I don't feel passionate about playing my instrument. I like that you're not graded for how well you perform so there's no pressure but sometimes that extra push can make music all the more rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Bodony is a really great teacher and conductor. Picks great music for orchestra, makes his expectations very clear, and does a great job of giving you feedback about your playing.
Solid conductor. Picks interesting pieces and all around a nice guy.
He's a really great conductor - the orchestra sounds amazing under his direction. He picks really fun, enjoyable music, and makes orchestra a great experience.

I had him for concert band and he was certainly a great director, even though he usually directs orchestras. He had a very dry sense of humor that made class pretty enjoyable. I wasn't the biggest fan of our musical selections, but that's just  how band is, I suppose.
Best orchestra director I've had in a long time.
He's chill and the music he chooses is pretty good too.
I enjoyed being in his class. I was able to continue with music while studying engineering.
Mobolaji is goated take his class. He is very kind and teaches well while always being encouraging.

Class was organized despite a few last minute changes. Lots of busy work assignments with few that are actually going to make you better at presentations. Finding live audiences is a bit of a hassle so make sure to be ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Mobolaji was the best professor I have had at Purdue so far. He is so passionate about the course and knows that most of us are there just because it's required so his main goal is "just listen to your classmates and learn." (He says that a lot). It's hard not to get an A in this course. Take him if you can get him!
Very easy class and even nicer professor. Makes coming to class enjoyable and will respect your time and values. I would recommend taking any class that he teaches.
Great professor and very easy grader; however, he does not do the best job with responding to emails.

He truly represents what every teacher should strive to be. He cares about each students improvement and makes a direct effort to connect with all those in his class. He is my favorite professor on my schedule. Best guy!

Professor Mobolaji is super chill and always happy. He really wants the best for his students, and he is very understanding of his students. He grades super easy and gives amazing feedback. He lets students re-do presentations with no penalty if they blank the first time. He promotes a fun and stress-free environment. He is a great com professor.

The learning goals could have gone better, and the criteria could have been clearly. The DNA analysis weeks were cool, but dirt is kind of boring. Overall the course was designed with good intentions but didn't have great execution. Good intro to college biology lab but glad to be done.

My only qualm with this class is that your grade is heavily dependent on what TA you have. I've heard great things about some TAs, while I had one would tell us blatantly wrong information. The lab itself is incredibly easy and as long as you try you will get an A. Make sure you have a good lab group or you will do a lot of extra work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took him for 121. Class is super easy, studying is light but don't skip out. Basically no homework other than a couple 15-min reads. Lecture is required, but not super taxing.

He grades based on learning goals so messing up one thing means that you don't get a met. His class is incredibly stupid and dumbed down. You spend basically the whole semester on dirt which is soooooo fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am currently a freshman in bio 135 and 121 and Professor Jacob is a great professor. While the lab is mostly ran by TA/TIs, the lecture is ran by Jacob. All of the teaching team is amazing and wants you to succeed. My best advice is to show up for class and ask questions when you have them. Overall both courses are great!!!

Had JJ Adler for both bio 121 and bio 135. Really cares about his students, both academically and personally. He even sends personalized follow-up emails to your questions/concerns in forms. Lectures are clear 99% of the time. No textbooks. Only bad thing is you have to go "feasting with faculty" for office hours instead of normal office hours.

Dr. Adler is incredibly sweet and caring, but I have also heard that when it comes to grading, this class is very TA dependent. My TAs were nice, but some on Reddit mention how it felt like their TAs were out to get them. Make sure to attend the lectures and labs, reach out to Dr. Alder if you are struggling, and genuinely put in effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cheerful guy, easy class. Beware of grading system. It's not hard, but very easy to mess up. They are very strict graders, but they grade based on a checklist system. If you take your time and complete your work to the fullest, you will get an easy A. This is an easy class as long as you do your work. Don't cut corners.

hes a nice guy but class is boring and assignments are very tedious. your grade for assignments is either met or not met which is BS and you can only get 3 not met for an A in the class. it should have regular grading because this system is super annoying.

I was a TI for him for both semesters last year. He is such a sweet man and you can really tell he cares a lot about his students. He was gentle with us and made a big effort to emphasize mental health.
i don't like his idea using the learning goals, it is meaningless. I would rather do a test.
Very nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't take his class personally but I did TI for him both semesters of my sophomore year (his first year as 135 prof). Very sweet and you can tell he cares a lot about his students. He would make sure that the students had the easiest time possible in the lab. Was EXTREMELY kind to us TA/TIs. Loved that man and would highly recommend him

Dr. Adler makes this class fun and it is a great course for anyone that doesn't have any lab experience. The class is super easy and is graded on whether or not you meet the learning goals. The teaching team is always super nice and helpful. The class can be very boring simply because it is so easy.

His class is unfortunately so boring and it isn't his fault. He is nice and everything is like so easy, I'm pretty sure it's impossible to get lower than an A. He's nice, just the class itself is dumb. There should be a test-out option. Nice guy. Dumb class. He sings songs at the beginning of class which is weird but you do you i guess.

Dr Adler was very friendly and seemed to really care about us. He made sure we knew he was available outside of class even if we needed help with things not related to the class. My only complaint is that the assignments were all pass/fail, which made passing really stressful. It wasn't necessarily difficult, but it was stressful.

Super easy and fun class. Graded based on meeting learning goals. The semester is spent on a group project and end in you making a website to present your findings. Super clear lab outlines that tell you exactly what to do and how to do it. Amazing amazing class with an amazing Professor and amazing TA's.
Simply a poor teacher.

The content itself is useful if you're into strength and conditioning, and the required textbook is solid, but don't expect much empathy or room for individual circumstances. If you're a student who might need any type of flexibility, this class might be more stress than it's worth. Grading is harsh, and he won't give you feedback.

Adam does reverse-classroom style formatting so you will read the textbook/look over his PowerPoint before coming to class and then have a big group discussion during class. He creates a welcoming classroom environment and shares his experiences in the field. Awesome professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The lectures were more of a group discussion then a lecture, and you were graded on how often you showed up and participated. This grade was a HARSH grade, so be sure that you not only show up to every single class and lab, but also actively participate in the discussions held. Adam shared good info from his experience as an RD in the "real world."

Kotanko is an extremely kind and understanding professor. He prompts you to think beyond the surface-level appearance of society. He has great communication and his respect for his students is evident. I would love the chance to take one of his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This is the best professor at Purdue. He is so caring and genuinely gets to know each of his students. He is understanding and wants to see you succeed. He is not a hard grader at all. This is the best professor and class ever.

Most caring professor I've ever had. You attend class and email your group's discussion summary for credit every class (hence "mandatory" attendance). You get plenty skips for when you're sick, and he provides extensive feedback on your submissions. He has a passion in teaching and is a very understanding instructor. Very light coursework.
Kindest Prof ever

He's a great teacher that doesn't believe in exams/quizzes, but rather testing through group discussions, projects, and film reviews. In fact, he is just a grad student, but compared to my friends who had full professors that just lectured and gave exams, I still learned way more. If you take Mr. Kotanko he will make you a better person.

Seriously the sweetest professor I've ever had. This is a really easy class the only way you'll fall behind is if you skip a lot of classes. Technically attendance isn't mandatory (if you're really sick he'll understand) but points are given for discussions so you really have to pay attention to those but you can always make them up. 4 get dropped.

This class was probably my favorite this semester. Class is solely group discussion, no lecturing. Mr. Kotanko is very caring, flexible, and passionate about the subject. No exams, only film reviews. As long as you show up to class and participate in discussions, you will get an A+. I would definitely recommend him as a teacher.
One of the best professors that I have had, I recommend this class.

Very passionate in his field of study, incredibly kind guy. I personally did not like the open discussion format, but I know many students did. Does not lecture, all group work. Lots and lots of reading outside of class, but he's okay with skimming. Very great guy

I had him for SOC402 and he was amazing! Small group work everyday but no exams and super open to feedback about how students want the class to run. Lots of dense theory readings but he always provided resources to make it approachable. Easy grader and created a great learning environment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall great Professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kotanko is a very knowledgeable person when it comes to sociology. His assignments were very easy and never took over an hour to do. The readings were very interesting but not required for the GQ/activities. It is a very chill online course that is easy if you put forth effort. No exams, tests, or quizzes. Kotanko overall is a great professor.

Kotanko is incredibly nice and takes the time to respond to everybody's responses every week. He is clearly passionate about the subject. The readings are honestly not required to do the GQs/activities but they usually are pretty interesting so I would recommend. No tests- only film reviews and a final project which are also interesting/funish.

He is probably the most passionate instructor I have ever had! Attendance was not mandatory, but he made me want to attend class. If you have the chance to take him, I highly recommend it! The way he teaches and what he teaches shows how dedicated he is, which gave me the push to change my major! Absolutely loved this class!

Excellent professor!!! I cannot believe that he is a graduate student and not a professor. He knows so much, and he is so passionate about what he is teaching. He incorporated a great selection of readings, documentaries and podcasts to the course that help understanding and engaging with the material. I hope I can take another course with him.

He is one of the most passionate instructors I've ever seen in my time at Purdue University. There were a lot of readings and podcasts to prepare for the lecture; however, they all were excellent, which goes beyond than just knowing about the content. Thanks to him, my view of society has forever changed, and I highly credit him for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor who actually cares about you as a person. Would definitely take again!

Really engaging professor. Took SOC100 with him, and even though it was a super basic class I feel like I learned more than the upper level SOC classes I am taking. He really cares about his students and wants us to love learning. Would 100% take a class just because he is the teacher.
Fair amount of reading in the class, but no tests. The professor is a very understanding and helpful guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: CSR 315 is a very busy class. The role plays and sales competitions can become stressful. Lala is a very funny and nice man but he flies through his lectures and expects you to know everything.

"Lala" is a phenomenal instructor. Yes, he makes you work hard, but I've never learned more in a class than his. He expects professionalism and hard work, you must follow through with assignments because he does not allow opportunity to make up points. He is extremely helpful and is willing to offer guidance about things that extend beyond class.
Okay
Very helpful
Flies through the slides, it would be nice if English awas used. By far one of the worst I've ever had the luck to witness.
Very respectful, very kind. This class requires a lot of participation. He provides articles to read, but no purchases necessary. Really will help your leadership grow. Not a difficult class.

There's a lot of writing in a short amount of time, but if you're okay with that, the retreat is a very valuable experience and Dr. Watkins does a really good job of engaging with his students. I would highly recommend going on this retreat if you're an Honors student.

A lot of opportunities to participate in group discussions. Be prepared for several group projects that will be the majority of your grade as well as peer review assignments. Overall, Professor Watkins is a very enjoyable lecturer, however he does assign a lot of work for a 1 credit class.

Dr. Watkins taught me how to think differently. This class was mind-opening, which included difficult assignments that were graded harshly, but this was one of the most rewarding classes of my college career.

Lectures are very one-sided, as he tends to be very insistent on his own viewpoints, despite preaching being affirmative and open-minded. He gives very unclear feedback, and is an unnecessarily harsh grader for it being a 1 credit class, taking off points without indicating why just because he can't bring himself to give someone a 100%.

About a quarter of students' grades are based on peer evaluations. Weekly readings are fairly long, (especially for a 1-credit hour class), but the associated discussion posts are very easy to get full credit on. On the whole, far too much work for the associated credit hours, and I would not recommend taking an Honors course taught by Watkins.
For a one credit class, it took up way too much time and effort for low grades.

It was cool to see a professor very passionate about his topic, which was play, and I actually enjoyed some of the readings as it was all very interesting. However, he is a very tough grader and expects high quality of content. Make sure to follow the rubric to the T and include the overall message/theme for a more sophisticated project.

Creates random assignments due before class the next day without warning. Once spent an entire class arguing with me because I didn't like an article and said as much when he asked for opinions on the article.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: This dude gives out so much homework for a 1 credit class. Don't take his class. His feedback consists of praise and only good comments on your paper, but then he gives you an 80 without any explanation. He doesn't tell you when homework is due, he posts it on brightspace in the discussion page so you don't get any notifications or emails.

Watkins' honors course is a little more work than some of the others, but do the readings, put effort into the discussion posts, and participate in group work and you're set. What makes Nature so interesting is Dr. Watkins' way of thinking about it. Legit the first day of class we got into a debate about what nature was/wasn't; he's super fun!
I took 19901 nature. He was an ok professor but graded too harshly and had too many complicated assignments for a 1 credit class. Didnt love the material because he made it a bit boring.
I loved Dr. Watkins! He was an amazing professor and I enjoyed every single one of his lectures. You can tell he really cares about his students and the material he teaches.

He genuinely wants his students to get some value out of his class, and on that note wants to give his students an A given that they show effort. Does a good job keeping his course material and discussions interesting and gives good feedback on every project submission.

Dr. Watkins is an amazing professor, so knowledgeable and his courses are fun and not hard if you turn everything in. He will make exceptions for late work if you have a good reason. Highly recommend his HONR 299 course, my final paper was published in JPUR which is really neat and there is a volunteer opportunity built into the class. Very neat

I took Dr. Watkins "Homegrown" class this last fall semester, as well as taking one of his HONR 19901 classes. He is such a wonderful teacher, and he genuinely cares about his students. I had no problem with coming to his office hours with my questions about his assignments, and he always gave back clear feedback and made everything make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Watkins is a nice professor. He sets out clear guidelines for what is to be accomplished in personal and group projects and grades exactly according to the criteria set down, leading to harsh but fair grading if a project is not exactly as expected. His lectures are insightful and he is generally a fun character to be around.

Not a very organized person. Sends out lots of emails that are confusing and stress out our group leaders. The whole class was based around one large project but the class was structured in a way that made it much more complicated than it needed to be. This was his first time doing the class so hopefully he is able to do better in the future.

Never minded going to class, even though I had it early.  Very hard grader though, he is clear on what he wants and will definitely mark you down if you do not do it correctly.  Make sure you revise the rough draft a lot before turning in the final.  Overall a fun class but tough grader.

I have learned a lot over the semester, but this was definitely not a blow-off class. Of all of my courses, this was the most difficult. He's very cool and understanding though; he just expects you to work and to participate.

He is a really great guy who cares about his students' well-being and their grades. He is very funny and engaging in lectures. I highly recommend him. Just make sure to go to lectures if you want to do well, because lectures aren't recorded, and slides aren't enough.
Loved going for his classes, just concentrate in his class and don't forget to take notes!
As a PoliSci major loved him. Try not to skip class and take notes of what he is talking about. The slides are not enough.

Lectures were awesome and well-instructed. He does curse a lot and do not appreciate diversity in class, so mind before you choose to take classes with him. Exams were all based on lectures and textbook, so attendance is essential, though not mandatory.
Hilarious guy and easy class. Kept me interested all throughout the semester.
The man is hilarious and the class is great to!
He's a really funny professor who drops the F bomb repeatedly. He was able to keep my interest and made class enjoyable. Good Prof

Great Professor, he knows the material very well, however, this is a really hard class! The class ONLY consists of 4 exams (30 questions), so if you didn't do as well on one there is no way to make it up. No homework, No quizzes, I found it VERY difficult to know what he was asking on his exams, although classes were VERY entertaining. Had to drop!
Funny guy, ridiculous exams. Found myself always struggling to study the right material. I wouldn't take this class with him.

There were four exams and no final.Exams were only 25 questions.No homework.Doesn't take attendance.There are online practice exams before each test.Didn't really use the book and only sometimes went to class. Got an A-. One of the practice exams was verbatim the real exam. Funny guy and very knowledgeable. If you have the chance, take this class.

Holy Crap! I am currently in this class (Spring '10) and Professor Hoffman has quickly become my all-time favorite professor. He is hilarious, charasmatic, unbelievably witty, and smoking hot. This guy could stand at the lectern and read a grocery list for an hour and I would still be captivated. I loves me some Professor Hoffman.
great professor,,so enthusiastic and fun. and he is hottt when he speaks..
Professor Hoffman is amazing. He is very funny and keeps class interesting. If you go to class (which is mandatory) you will get a good grade.

AWESOME teacher.  Makes this class a ton of fun and the knowledge Prof. Hoffman has is second to none.  I never had the book for this class and still ended with an A.  I think you only needed like an 80 to get an A with the way the class ended up being curved.
Incredible teacher. Makes everything easy to comprehend.
Amazingly engaging and knowledgeable. Honestly seems to enjoy teaching undergrads. Great class. I recommend taking any course taught by him
Lectures are mandatory but they aren't too bad. There is such a big curve at the end you really can't get lower than a C. No homework, just 6 in class quizzes and exams.
Great Prof
Very interesting to listen to.  Not dry, connects with students, genuinely interested.
Wonderful, energetic professor.  Keep yourself away from stupid comments and you'll be fine.  PS, I'd have his babies.  That's all.
No Comments
I enjoyed the class, kept class involved in what was going on, asked questions and kept it usually to an open discussion.
Great class, was very interesting. I recommend it to everyone, he knows what he is talking about. Great professor.

My favorite class! He goes really fast in his lectures, so it's a little hard to keep up sometimes, but he keeps your attention, and really tries to relate things to our interest. Worthwhile, even for non-poli sci.
Good professor but his name really annoyed me. Explained things very well, and tests were very fair. He definatly had a bias towards Israel which was kind of annoying.

Prof. Morris is a nice person who cares about his student. Overall the course was easy and he solve enough examples to make the concept clear. However,  his class was not well organized. For instance, he was not able to finish a lot of topics that I felt like this class was just like introduction to fluid mechanics.

Currently an ME student set to graduate in 2025. Morris is very easy to understand and can clearly explain fluids material. Fluids is a class that requires sufficient math and theory to understand everything. Morris does a great job explaining the theory but hw's are sometimes a struggle if you don't have a grasp on the theory. 
Random quizzes.

Intelligent, caring and funny prof - but busy and absentminded - I felt like he made a lot of mistakes during lectures. Exam problems were easier than HW. Use Panton's book and Fox and McDonalds', to learn concepts.

This professor could teach a rock how to swim. Lectures also conceptual, not just math, so you understand topic better. HW and practice exams help gauge understanding before exams. Answers emails promptly and is accessible outside of class. Cons: slightly unorganized, wish there were more example problems in lecture. Definitely would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Morris was a great lecturer and explained all concepts and solution methods clearly. He spends time to ensure students understand how to solve problems

Professor Morris is a fantastic lecturer and genuinely cares about the class and material. He is also very willing to help students with the homework and responds well to any class questions. I think if he wrote the homework and exams, the class would be much better. 309 is hard due to things out of his control, but he tries to make it better.

He is a great professor who genuinely knows his stuff and cares about students learning. Always answers questions well and has good examples on the fly. The class is pretty difficult but if you ask questions/read the textbook, its not too bad. Lecture videos were sometimes posted late.
Good lectures with good notes. Always prepared. Tries to be funny. Will prepare you for exams.

A professor who, both, genuinely really knows his stuff and is able to teach it well. Also very good at answering questions on the fly and explaining them in ways easier to understand than if read from the book.
Super great professor. Really funny!

Too much homework, Too much homework, Tooooooooooooo much homework!
This class has the most homework I've ever taken at Purdue. The time I spent on homework each week is the total of the two CS and another math classes I took this semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lecture and explanation are really great. But the homework is way toooooo much compares to other profs' sections. At least spend 3 hours on hw every week, and as far as I know, other sections only 1hr needed for hw every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: (Lin. Program) Dr. Yip's lectures are good, but I often found myself reading textbook too, maybe just because the concepts were difficult (reading not required). He is helpful outside of class and spends extra time in class offering insight and explanation for difficult concepts. Assignments take time, sometimes tedious. Exams are reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teaches Linear Algebra in a way that prioritizes fundamental understanding of the concepts. Very friendly and understanding.

This man is absolutely fantastic! He explains concepts in Linear Algebra extremely well and is always caring for his students. He is very accommodating if you have to turn in anything late. Before our final exam, he even held office hours over the weekend so that students could ask questions. Would definitely take a class with him again. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy, I have had him for both 421 and 366, and he genuinely cares. He grades very fairly, his exams are not a cakewalk, but they are always fair and correspond to the material in the class. Feel free to go to his OH and ask him literally anything related to the class and he will always help you.

Prof. Yip is an amazing professor: he cares about his students and makes sure we learn the actual content of the class. His homework is very fair: when he gives hard assignments he sends out additional help to make sure we can complete it. His exams are very fair and he grades leniently. Take if possible.

This course is very interesting and Professor Yip treats it like a topics class.  You get out of what you put in this course, so you could get by without doing much.  With that said prof yip lectures clearly and makes the class enjoyable.  My only criticism is that he speaks fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Aaron is a patient and helpful person who always give specific examples for each condition. The content he taught is correlated between chapters. Just remember to go through all concepts and notes and don't forget to take notes which is SUPER IMPORTANT! The exam is not that hard and prepare enough by practicing problems from textbook!

Show up to class, take your own notes, do all the homeworks soon after they are released, and study and you will be fine. The content for 366 was not that difficult and Yip's lecturing is very accessible. If you miss one or more classes in a row you will start to drown but beyond that you'll be fine.
Very engaging professor. Although the homework load was heavy, he was accessible outside of class, and was very understanding about late homework submissions.

really hard class, but really well taught. Dr Yip not only knows math but knows how to actually teach it, and is so incredibly accessible outside class to help. the exams are really hard, and the class average was in the 40's on both exams, so you don't really know how big the curve will be until grades are posted, but he is pretty generous with it

His lectures are clearly well planned, he strategically strays from the order in the textbook to present things in a way that makes sense. Incredibly accessible for help, Dr. Yip seems to work harder than any other professor I've had at Purdue in order to make sure he helps his students. Absolutely take him any chance you get for any class!

not an easy class, but he really makes it possible to pass... homework is a fair reflection of what he teaches in lecture, he's abundantly available to help, and a 38% on midterm exam was good enough for a B... the class is hard by nature of the content, but i highly recommend professor yip
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: lectures are pretty good, homework is way too long though, even though it isn't due all that often... these problems take too long to be doing 15 of them, and homework is worth 50% of the grade so you can't blow it off

His lectures are heavy, a lot of information. However, he is really passionate about the class and the material. Office hours are helpful but the tests are heavy, they are kind of similar to sample tests.

When you imagine what a powerhouse university lecturer is like, you probably get Aaron Yip. His lectures are very clear and he uses terrific examples. He makes math seem so logical, it's incredible. He also has a happy demeanor and a sense of humor. Purdue's stupid math grading scheme aside, he's one of the best.

Professor yip is one of the gems of Purdue. The way he elucidates proofs in class is mind blowing. This shows his passion for the subject as well. Doesn't assume any prior knowledge for the subject, pretty much starts from the scratch. His test are mostly proof and application based. The key is his notes and scoring A shouldn't be that hard.

Really good professor, clear note, slow pace, and quite easy tests. Tests are pretty similar to the practice exams. As long as you go over the notes and be able to do all the examples you will be fine. But going to every classes is still a good way to guarantee you an A. Also he is a very nice person, one of my favorite math teacher.

Great professor! Class moves pretty slowly (we only covered 5 of the 6 chapters that the others covered), but it goes pretty in-depth. Expect proofs and application questions on the exams. Curve is extreme (80%+ is A, 60-80% is B, etc) and you can do very well if you prepare adequately.

He gives quiz but it is only 5% of your grade. So attendance is not mandatory. He has really good lecture and could explain those technical terms in a very simple way. The tests are not difficult. As long as you know it, you get it. There are no tricky questions. I spend 2-3 hours for homework every week.

The material in the course is difficult but he was a decent lecturer. He speaks clearly and emphasizes concepts multiple times to get the point across. Exams are similar to homework and examples shown in class with the exception of proofs. Make sure you study and practice doing these because this is the most challenging part.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor is clear both in his method of teaching and speaking. He is available for discussions no matter how basic the doubts are.  He expects class participation.  Homeworks cover more than 50% for grades. Exams are a bit tough but he normalizes the scores of all the students so it does not affect overall grades much. Highly recommended.

Overall a great guy. Homework was from the textbook and was long and tough usually. First two tests were straightforward and fairly easy, but the final had some curveballs. Class got curved significantly. Lab was easy and pretty interesting. He's very friendly, speaks English well, and is easy to talk to. Would take another class with him.

Professor Yip speaks and teaches clearly and quickly. His tests, at least for MA366 do not match up with his lectures because the test often throw curveballs and circumvent concepts we spent a week learning in class. In addition, the sample tests are from 15 years ago, so there's no easy way to know or study for the test. Everything else is fair.
He's very clear and always professional. Proofs are pretty clear, and he has elucidated a few difficult combinatorial proofs with their qualitative (story-based) analogues. Good, quality teaching.
Professor Yip is fantastic at explaining things, and speaks better English than many native speakers. Highly recommended.

Clear--you can tell his accent is Chinese, but every word is spoken perfectly. Very good explanation style with a polite attitude. Moves at the right level for a 300-level math class, and will spend as much time as you need outside of class. Answered a lot of my personal questions unrelated to the class, too, and always helped me with decisions.

Granted that Aaron Yip does move  quite fast when lecturing, if you ask him a question after class, he will help you until you understand it.  Very helpful guy, and as for his accent, it isn't that bad.  He sounds kind of like a muppet, which made class very entertaining for me at least

Yip is a good professor to work with; if you visit him during office hours, he'll listen to what you say and work with you. He wants you to understand the material. However, during class it is difficult to keep up with him - he moves so quickly - and, in combination with the accent, makes it very difficult to understand him. Not an easy course.

I took calc 2 last semester and i Couldn't understand a word he said. He would explain problems the entire class and put everyone asleep. He would explain how to do homework after it was due. I would not recommend taking any calc class with him. If i hadnt had taken calc 2 in high school i would have failed.
He obviously knows a lot about math but he couldn't teach a chimp how to climb a tree. You can't really understand him. If I didn't have a calc in high school, this course could have been rough
This prof knows math pretty well to be honest. But he just simply CANNOT explain them well...I can rarely understand him. I would not encourage anyone taking his class.
I could not understand him well. He went through the easiest problems.

To be quite honest, he wasn't a bad teacher at all, though not a particularly GREAT one either. In retrospect, he did do a decent if not good job at teaching. Though, he NEVER involved the class at all, he never discouraged any questions though. The class itself was the most frustrating part about the course not Dr. Yip. Overall pretty decent prof.

he knows the math very well but he is not the greatest at explaining what he is doing or how he got something.  often just skips a bunch of steps assuming that the students know how to do it and picks up the problem further along.  often times doesnt really explain a concept, just goes through a bunch of examples.

He has a typical Asian accent which some of my peers find it hard to understand. For me though, I found it pretty easy. His knowledge on the course is good, so make use of him. In general, his students need to pay FULL attention in his lectures to ACTUALLY understand, especially if the course material is new.

While I could understand him, my peers could not for the most part. He attempts to be funny, but most don't appreciate it. He doesn't involve the class in his lectures, so its easy not to participate. He is helpful in office hours, and tries to help students as much as he can. Exams are difficult, but he curves a lot.
Previous sums him up

He substituted for my professor for a week, and i went from the first bench to the last just because i found his teaching style to be very different from my professor's(not in a good way); he goes too fast, and also has a very high pitched voice that irritated me and distracted me from what he was trying to teach
His speech is pretty easily understandable in spite of his accent. He is great during office hours, very approachable and friendly. His tests were challenging, but he graded the class fairly.
Intimidating, but easy to get used to when noticing the extremely generous curve.
Very good during lecture and curves a lot.
No Comments
No Comments

Tricked us into thinking the course was hard by giving out really high stats for the curve when handing back exams, but gave all but 5 students in the class As. Exams require some original thinking, while the homework does not, which can be problematic.
Homeworks were on the longer side, but exams were fair and bonus was offered for attendance. Professor Hashemi lectured well.

Lectures were great, professor took time to answer all the questions by students. Homeworks were on a reasonable difficulty level (each homework took 1-2 days, total of 6 homeworks). Midterm was hard, but the grading of the course was very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Insanely Heavy Workload! Avoid This Course If You Have Other Commitments! Don't say I didn't warn you!!!

ECE 69500OPT is one of the most demanding courses I've ever taken. The final project is even worse. If you're balancing job applications, internships, or your own research, I strongly advise against taking it. This course is a huge time sink!

This professor only reads from the slides in class and is always a few minutes late. The grading is extremely tough, which many students are aware of. I regret taking this course because I feel like I am learning on my own all the time, and there are many topics that take me a very long time to understand.
The classes are okay, professor mostly reads off of slides, but does take the time to clarify any questions asked. Slides are good but often miss important information.

The material covers a lot, but the exam didn't require students to memorize all the math and the proofs. As long as you understand the concept and the reason behind each method, it is easy to get an A.

The most skillful communicator I've seen as a grad student. He really knows his material in depth. As far as lectures goes, I'd say he is right now the best professor for ML. He's also really gentle and open when receiving questions from students. His slides are also the best I have seen here, and apparently he created them from scratch.

Covered too many topics in class within a short time. Kept all topics in the final, making it extremely heavy. No regrade scope for the project report. Did not release the grade cutoff. Most importantly he is an extreme tough grader. Got 86 around without curving. Still received B- even after curving as he told.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture aint bad, but he's a tough grader with unclear grading criteria. I ended up with an 87 overall after getting full credit on both the homework and the project, but still received a B. At our university, an 87 is typically a B+ even without a curve. He claimed there would be a curve, but it feels like he actually curved the grades down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mixed Bag. To his credit his course is extremely informative and you will learn a lot. Great slides, answers questions well and very knowledgable in his field. Unfortunately, the logistics are not great. Example: Our first homework was graded months after it was due. I think with better organization, his course could have been perfect.

Abhi is one of the most kind and caring teachers I have ever had. His teaching style wasn't necessarily a perfect fit for me but wasn't bad by any means. He's got all of the intangibles that one looks for in a professor. He cares about his student's wellbeing in and out of the classroom and is very responsive to feedback. Overall great human.

Professor Ramkumar definitely cares a lot about his students. He always made sure that we knew that he was there for us and seemed to genuinely want to connect with us. He experimented with several different teaching styles and was always open to feedback.

Prof Ramkumar took the time to make sure everyone understood the content and tried his best to encourage students to ask questions no matter how basic they were. He also experimented with group style work compared to the other professors. I enjoyed this more and in the end his exam averages were higher.

She is really good at relating to the students during lecture and cares about their success. While she may not explain things in a way that is understandable for everyone and the slides can be word-heavy, the practice exams are helpful and the class is not too difficult.

She is really good at relating to the students during lecture and definitely cares about their success. While she may not explain things in a way that is understandable for everyone and the slides can be a lot, the practice exams are helpful and the class is not too difficult.
Pretty funny teacher, lectures move pretty fast so some concepts didn't stick for me.

Dr. Banan was an excellent professor! Overall, a very manageable class with a decent amount of extra credit offered and many free points from iClicker and homework. Exams can be difficult, but they are very similar to the practice exams provided.

Banan is an excellent professor. Her course material is very well organized on Brightspace, her lectures are easy to follow and well paced, and the lecture notes she uploads after class are high quality. The exams are straightforward, as long as you prepare well, you shouldn't have any problems. There is also a good amount of extra credit available

Professor Banan was a good professor for ECON 251. The last 2 exams were difficult, but if you study a lot and really understand the notes she provides, you'll do fine! She gives a lot of extra credit, so make sure to take advantage of all of it early in the semester. I suggest going to every class and don't fall behind on notes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 75% of the grade are exams. tough exams i cant lie. read the textbook, went to every lecture, reviewed notes, (tl;dr i would spend hours on hours to study and not get above a B). she's a good professor overall though - fun lectures, sometimes can get a bit boring (content/not her). she's also always available. very hard class, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She will care as much as you do. She's competent and witty. Her lectures and exams are content heavy. It's better to develop an intuitive understanding of the material, rather than trying to memorize rules. Read your syllabus before emailing her. The answer is usually in there already, and you don't want to be that person when emailing a professor.

Great teacher, classes are super helpful and videos are great for learning. Homework is super easy and exams aren't insanely hard either.
Shoutout all the TAs as well for helping with exams and difficulties too!

Dr. Banan is clearly very knowledgeable about her field, but I'm not sure how she has such high ratings. Her lectures are slow, boring, and her cadence quite monotonous. She also comes off as quite condescending and rude sometimes, feels like she has a massive ego. But 251 is a pretty easy class and she does give resources to do well on exams.

Dr. Banan is a great professor, her content is well organized and she offers plenty of resources to study and review. ECON251 is well organized and her system for teaching, grading, and homework is well refined.

Dr. Banan was an amazing lecturer, and I found the course content easily digestible through her examples and explanations. Microeconomics can sometimes be hard to understand, but she always made sure to answer each question thouroughly and elaborate on topics when needed.

I enjoyed Dr. Banan this semester. Econ is not my favorite class, but her lectures were engaging and funny. The homework does not feel like a waste of time. Just study and pay attention most of the time, and you'll be fine. Don't go to the TA review sessions-- they are useless. The SI review sessions are better.
She sucks,

Prof Banan clearly knows her stuff and cares. Sometimes she can let little things bother her and let that disrupt class. She also sometimes gives long stories as examples of stuff which bothers some people but I think it makes lectures more interesting. Homework can be tricky (what textbook is required for). Attendance only mandatory for half sem.

Grades are 75% exams. She is a sweet and understanding person if you get the chance to talk 1-on-1. Very smart while also very human. Her lectures are pretty engaging and easy to understand. She's a really good prof imo. Just study and you'll be ok. Don't stress too bad. She also has extra credit. Very fair class in all. Go to office hours trust
She was sometimes condescending. But everything else is good. Her lectures were fun, and she taught well.
Dr. Banan is a great professor. Overall, I struggled with Econ but she's really great if you go to her office hours. Lectures can be a bit dry and exams are slightly difficult. Not bad overall.
This professor is kind of a B word. She is not really respected by students because she will treat you like a child.

This class has a lot of homework! A lot of the weeks there has been 20+ questions with multiple free-response parts per question which end up taking a lot of time. The questions have no penalty for getting them wrong.  Also there is a minimum iclicker attendance which can be annoying. Funny teacher but overcomplicates simple topics for sure.
Best teacher out there, most fun classes Ive ever had. The exams werent hard, If you were just paying attention I think she was an easy A...

Be ready learn pretty much nothing that will help you on the exams. If you have the option to take it with whoever Vargas is, do that. This is not a joke and I don't even have a bad grade. Save yourself.

She is a nice person and is accessible outside of class, but she has the most over-complicated way of teaching an economics course. She has blank versions of the slides for notes but rarely gives example problems which is what the homeworks and exams are, which are all of your grade. Please take this class with Vargas if you can.

First economics class I have ever taken but was fairly straightforward. Practice exams may not be like the actual exams but are still helpful (be mindful there are other practice exams online). Banan knows her stuff and is always willing to help during office hours. Homework is very flexible and digital which I like.

How you feel about this class depends heavily on your background-engineers will likely find this math quite light. Definitely just watch the online lectures at your own pace. Most of lecture not helpful for tests, but the notes themselves were. Prof can make simple things complex. Practice test is not full prep for actual test, beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really chill professor, she's still somewhat new but understands content well and is able to teach. she doesn't speak with a ton of passion in her voice though, but overall she's a very easy professor and it isn't hard to do well in her class if you just show up to lecture.

Lectures are so random, like you'll be sitting there taking notes, and then the topic will change. You'll get really confused because it makes no sense how she organizes notes. Lecture is also so boring that you'll lose focus then literally nothing will make sense. Don't let the past ratings fool you, the exams and practice exams are nothing alike.

Microeconomics was one of the interesting classes I took. The curriculum is organized, with one topic covered in 2 lectures, per week. The homework is balanced and the I-clicker questions were fair/helpful. However, the exam does rely heavily on the exams. Some questions, such as those on the final, could have been explained more thoroughly.

Lectures aren't great, Professor Banan understands the material but the way she structures her notes is not very engaging and not the most helpful, since they are mostly fill-in-the-blank which can be boring. The practice exams that she gives are nothing like the actual exams, which are much more difficult.

Dr.Banan is really good at breaking stuff down for you and explaining new topics. the only negative I can think of is her notes are fill in the blank so you do need to go to lecture. Exams are difficult but using the textbook helps

I tend to struggle in Economics classes, but enjoyed Abi's Econ 301 class. Her lectures aren't required for attendance, but are very informative and help if you pay attention. She was super helpful outside of class, which I appreciated.

Dr. Banan is caring and clearly has a big heart for her students and their education. She is very accessible outside class to answer questions. Exams are difficult and pretty different from most practice exams, but once you learn how to study for them well you will be fine.

very confusing, is not good at explaining 
0/10
The actual tests are significantly harder than the practice exams. It's nothing alike. She does explain the slides in lecture, but it goes so fast because theres so much material to be covered.

I'm not a huge fan of Banan. She's one of those professors who's VERY bothered by people talking in class and frequently stops mid-lecture to shush people, which is really annoying. Her practice exams are not like her actual exams. I am an engineer on the Dean's List, and this is genuinely one of my hardest classes. A LOT of content is covered.
Personally I didn't have a good experience with her but during lectures and after class questions she was very knowledgeable and helpful on the material. Lectures are easy to follow.
she is like one of the worst professors i ever had she think she is funny and its quite hard to understand things in her class and would never recommend anyone to take her classes
I love Dr. Banan. She is super funny, kind and intelligent. I would love to have her as my professor for every class. She is super helpful and dedicated too.
There is a good amount of extra credit, exams are like the content in class. She's a cool person who conveys information well and is very knowledgeable.

Overall great lecturer. Made all economics understandable and easy to learn. I got a high A and didn't study too much. You should easily succeed in this class as long as you attend and take notes. She is very polite, nice, approachable, and makes jokes in class. Highly recommend to take her lectures!

Banan is a great teacher who makes learning about economics fun. The homework assignments are long at times, but they are far harder than the exams she gives. The practice exams Professor Banan assigns are very helpful and closely related to the real exam.

I had her for fall 24 micro econ and she wasnt bad at all. You only have to show up for so many lectures, homeworks easy if you pay attention, and her practice exams really set you up. Also her lectures were pretty entertaining. Shes nice and fair when it comes to grading.

Dr. Banan was by far my favorite professor of the semester. She is relatable, real, and funny during lectures. She's good at using common-world examples to explain microeconomic principles. I went to her office hours once and she's just generally a chill and nice person to have a conversation with and gave good advice. Do the podcast extra credits!
Fantastic Professor- one of my favorites I've had at Purdue 100/10 definitely recommend. She makes learning fun

Although the class content might deem itself to be a bit boring, Dr Banan does an amazing job bringing up examples and interacting with the class in order to help us understand the material. Posts many practice exams that will leave you more than prepared for the exams. Absolutely take her class, even if its the 75min version, its well worth it.

I took her ECON 251 class and overall it was a pretty manageable class. Attendance is not "required" but she does do a lot of iClicker questions that go towards a participation grade. Her class covers A LOT of material but I did not find her tests to be that bad. She is really chill and I would definitely recommend taking one of her classes.

Dr. Banan is an amazing professor. She has multiple extra credit opportunities, and the exams are not bad. Notes for each week are fill in the blank sides, which I found very helpful. Dr. Banan is a great lecturer. She knows her stuff and does a great job at keeping everyone's attention during lecture.

Attend the lectures, do the hw, ask questions. That's all you really need to succeed in this class. The iClicker questions can get you a ton of extra credit points and even get you from a B+ to an A- as it did for me. The hw are really annoying but compared to those questions, the exams are pretty light. She explains everything very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent professor across the board. Receiving an A- instead of an A was my own fault because Dr. Banan's homework assignments, fill-in-the-blank notes, and practice exams make earning an A extremely easy. I'd love if all my professors adopted her teaching and exam style.
Dr. Banan knows her stuff. 5/5
She was a very good professor for Micro. She applied all the topics she taught to the real world. Despite it being a 1.5 hour T/Th class, class usually got out at the 1 hour mark.
Funny, nice, and passionate about economics. Lots of extra credit opportunities and exams are pretty easy. Be prepared to answer a lot of iclicker questions.
Abigail Banan is often regarded as one of the most influential and innovative professors of her generation.

Professor Banan gives great hand written notes and engaging lectures. She is able to answer any question and give a clear explanation why. All the materials that are necessary to succeed on the exams are provided and Banan is always willing to help. Highly recommend her for Econ 251.

Her class was so good I switched majors to economics. She puts a lot of time and effort into her hand written notes and wants to make sure that the students are understanding the lessons taking in class.

Great professor for Econ251, highly recommend taking her for the class. Does an excellent job of explaining concepts that some people may struggle with. Notes are very structured as well and help when reviewing for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good for 251
Lectures are boring. You have to fill out the blanks for the lecture notes.
Her exams are hard but she lots you drop an exam. Her grading criterion is very fair ngl. She wants her students to do well and that shows in her work. Also, she knows her subject very well.
She makes ECON truly fun and is very nice and accessible outside of class. 100% would recommend her class.

There are 4 exams however she will drop the lowest one. I went to every lecture and her lectures were pretty good but she rarely shows examples. She has no practice exams and in class review she will not show example problems. I would not take this class again. Hard exams.

I think that Prof. wasn't the best professor. This semester, every class average for each exam was 65%-70%. This shows how she helped the students study for exams, not about how hard the students were studying. The exams are difficult & there was never a study guide or small cheat sheet we would receive to help. I went to all the lectures as well.
Abi is a great professor! This is a difficult class, but if you do the notes, read the textbook, and go to office hours you will do fine. She is funny and cares about her students.

Abi is an amazing professor who exudes knowledge and caring in all that she does. Her lectures are all handwritten, so you're not scrambling to write down slides. She can answer questions in great detail. The exams are a bit tough, but if you study hard and maybe attend office hours, you will do just fine. She's also just funny and relatable.

I took this class with Abi over the summer, she was very caring and accommodating of students. Content gone over in class is similar to practice tests which are similar to actual tests. Couldn't ask for a better teacher!
Great professor, very enthusiastic and good at explaining topics. Answers questions well and is accessible outside of class. The lectures tend to drag on a bit, but not horribly.
Highly recommend!

Super easy, he has long videos with quizzes to do after. It is all simple, just another thing on your plate. He himself was not always accessible, even if I emailed him directly he would still have his TA to answer questions, but the class was clearly laid out for someone not wanting to do the in person version.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great at teaching new and/or challenging concepts! He is great at explaining concepts, and will take the time to explain it even more if you are still struggling. However, he will not give you a letter grade unless you pass the external FAA exam.

Professor Flores is a fantastic lecturer. He knows his stuff and will make every accommodation to ensure your success in his class. It takes effort to fail with him. Put in the effort, and pay attention, and you'll do just fine. If it wasn't for him I wouldn't have my private pilot license. 100% would take again.

Has a great way of teaching in lectures that makes it interesting to learn. He will go above and beyond to help you and is very open about helping you for your future career than just your short time in class.

The quizzes and exams are easy but also help you learn a lot.
10/10 would take again

Abner goes above and beyond to see you succeed. He cares more about how you'll perform in the workforce than in a 3 credit class. You learn everything you need to know just by attending his lectures (which are actually engaging). I've never had to do any outside studying for his quizzes/exams. The dude has a ton of super cool life experience!!
Abner rocks. He gets you as a learner and really wants to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You're doing yourself a disservice if you don't attend a class with Professor Abner Flores. One of the finest lectures on this side of the Mississippi.
He really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.

Abner is the sweetest professor I've had. He uses emojis in his emails, if that gives an idea of his personality. He goes over all the answers to tests and quizzes before you take them. There's one quiz per week and three total exams, all online. You can find the textbooks online for free, but you don't have to read them to do well.

Abner is without a doubt the nicest professor that I have had in my time at Purdue.  He would always be accessible to his students and went above and beyond to make sure that everyone got an A in the class.
He will go out of his way to make sure you get an A in his class. Dont take the quiz on time? He will open it back up. He is here for his students success.

His section was very disorganized and overwhelming. So many reactions come to you in such a short time, and you will have to memorize so hard in this class. You will have to utilize outside resources, but other work in this class can give you a grade cushion.

His lectures were often hard to follow because he wrote little on the slides, but that could have been my own fault. Soft grader (gives a lot of partial credit). Quizzes did not match the past year's quizzes as they did for the other professors, which could be seen as a good or bad thing depending on how you see it.

I'm sure his actual orgo class is better, but the way he taught PHSC 204 was disorganized. Often we'd be multiple lectures behind in the notes. His questions for HW and quizzes were also poorly written, and they would be nothing like the practice. His exam was written fairly well, but overall his section was sloppy at best.
Very large curve at the end. Very funny and made lecture enjoyable, plus there are lots of opportunities to get help in the class.

He is a very decent professor, if you don't get Kern for 256, do not worry, Axelrod is still a very good professor and has a clear knowledge of the material, I recommend going to Kerns office hours though because his are very awkward and he is not nearly as approachable.

Dr.Axelrod is a really great guy who is clearly super smart and passionate about what he does. He gives a ton of extra credit and basically tells us what will be on exams. His lectures are pretty fast paced, but he pauses to check in and also records lectures to watch back. He is great and I would totally recommend his class even though it's hard.

This professor, in my opinion, was very clear about the course and what was required from it. He explained the content well and made an effort to help answer questions whether in his lecture or office hours. He made sure to prepare everyone for the exams to make sure they had the right materials to study with as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Axelrod knows the material well but I often felt like he explained things as if they were common sense. The exams were very similar to what he showed us in class but often had a question that was way harder than anything we'd been shown. Overall he wasn't my favorite professor but he wasn't terrible. We were given very few practice materials.
Clearly knows the material and is good at explaining it clearly. Can sometimes go fast but provides clear notes. Makes it very clear what you need to know for exams.

He is a great lecturer just goes pretty fast but he tells us what will be on exam and prepares us very well. Only thing is that when you ask questions after class it seems like he is annoyed at you and it doesn't seem like he cares for you.  I just wish he showed more emotion or cared more when you asked questions.

Orgo isn't my strong suit.
This class is doable. Axelrod is very blunt with what will be presented on the exam. As long as you show up to class, go to review sections, and practice on your own, you will pass. Though his interactions with students are sometimes rude and brash, the way he runs the class is chill.

This class was really difficult, but Axelrod was very fair in grading. He got grades back very fast, and he gave lots of good examples/applications of the content in lecture. Lecture not mandatory. I never read the book, but it might be helpful. Favorite part is that he would give you an outline of what would be asked on the exam

Prof Axelrod makes it VERY easy to get an A in his class. Exams are exactly what he says they're going to be and I got A's by studying what he said and doing the practice exams. He gives around 65 points of extra credit throughout the semester and curved final class grades at the end. He wants people to do well and makes it very easy too.

This class has been known to be notoriously hard but Prof. Axelrod made this class not only accesible but also approachable. He breaks it down in a way that is understandable. While the class class is graded on very few things but if you study/practice and put in the work then you will be able to get a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great guy. I did not put that much effort but still did decent in the class. If you did poorly in his class, that means you were lazy.

The guidelines for this class were very clear. There were three homework assignments the entire semester and one exam grade gets dropped. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit on the exams and on the three problem sets. As long as you go to lecture and study the practice exams, you'll do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives multiple opportunities for extra credit which can for sure help you if your grade is in a pinch. I feel like i did the bare minimum by just doing the practice exams, going to lecture, and doing the graded practice sets. He also gives outlines of what each problem on the exam is going to be about. You can get an A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved him. Engaging/funny guy who made it really apparent that he cared about our learning and what he teaches. I ended up really enjoying the content but i felt like he also made himself and the content very accessible to people who struggled/didn't like it. If you show up to office hours, he will clearly outline whats on exams too!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class with Prof. Axelrod. As long as you pay attention, do the homework, and study a reasonable for exams, an A is achievable. He cares about his students and also gives extra credit. He clearly tells the class what is going to be covered on the exam so that you don't have to blindly memorize a bunch of mechanisms.

Axelrod was a nice man overall, I think he could have done a better job at doing examples. He throws information at you during the lecture instead of showing you how it is done. He definitely was open for help, but you need to put in more effort for help and doing practice problems on your own when he is your professor.

Dr. Axelrod is pretty good at teaching but can be rude. You will need to devote a lot of time to studying and the course is very test heavy. You cannot cram or wait last minute to study before exams. The exams are similar to practice exams. He is very honest about what will be on exam. Going to his office hours is helpful. His mode is variable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't try at all in this class and still passed. He's a decent guy who wants his students to succeed. He's receptive to emails and will work with you to see how he can help you out. Would def take another class of his.
Overall, I really liked him. He is goofy and kid of sarcastic, but I didn't mind that. He gives really good study material. I liked him and would say he is one of the better teachers that I have had!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good professor and I really enjoyed learning the subject. He offers a TON of extra credit and you can end up with a 110% in the class. He will also post a study guide that literally tells you exactly what is coming on the exam.
Great professor. He will literally tell you what is on the up coming exam. You pay attention, you get good score.

Good teacher and fair teacher, but an absolutely terrible person. Said some disgusting things about female students. Made some students uncomfortable in office hours with comments and actions. Mocked a student who committed suicide. There's a reason why all of his lab quit working under him and mutinied.

Professor Axelrod was an amazing teacher who cares about his students. If you reach out for help, he will definitely give you it. The class was a bit hard at first, but he truly does want you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Axelrod was a great prof. The class was difficult, but he did a great job teaching it. Attend all lectures, it's hard to catch up once you get behind. He outlines the exams so you know what to study. Problem sets (homework) were straightforward and easy points. He gave lots of EC toward the end of the semester which helped everyone.
Professor Axelrod was a good teacher and clearly wanted his students to succeed! It was a difficult class but he was very accessible and taught the curriculum well
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: great professor. The course requires a great deal of work, but an A is definitely achievable. His office hour is helpful, especially before exams. Plenty of EC to bump grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Axelrod gives lots of EC!!!

A really great professor that teaches a difficult class. His exams are very straight forward, and he gives a lot of EC during lectures. It's clear that he truly cares about his students and wants them to do well, so visit him during office hours! If you're struggling, he's more than willing to help. Overall, one of the best profs at Purdue.

Going into this class I was scared due to his previous reviews. However, Professor Axelrod was overall a good experience for organic chem. Despite this class notoriously sucking, he made it more than tolerable, especially for somebody who isn't great at chem. He also frequently gives out extra credit in lecture, which is nice.

He started recording his lectures online and restructuring his notes for lectures after an exam which half the class failed. The exams cover material in lectures which is very difficult.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Flies through the notes without explaining anything. Tests are unfair and sometimes include information not really covered in class. Avoid him if possible.

I took this class fall 2019. The beginning of the semester was rough, but after the class failed exam two he was quick to make things right. He started making his exams easier and being more fair. He also started helping students by making practice exams much more similar to the real exams and started using boiler cast midway through the semester.

reviews.comment: Worst chemistry professor I have ever had. He bounces back and forth between material in lecture and is frequently wrong when it comes to lectures and problem sets. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class should really be curved, an A should definitely NOT be a 90... this is organic chemistry. Everyone in class is literally suffering, grading is beyond unfair. I would really avoid him as a professor, other organic professors have a MUCH better grading system that allows you to get the grade you deserve and NOT how he decides tests to be graded

Literally the worst professor I've had. You can't read his writing for a class that is very important when it comes to being neat. He grades horribly, hardly gives any study materials, and the ones that he does give, the keys are done incorrectly. If you can avoid him, I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Axelrod hardly ever explains what hes writing, and on the off chance that he does, he assumes you know more material than expected of Ochem II students. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would not take him if you don't want to read and teach yourself. He has no respect for the students and grades are based heavily on the tests. His grading criteria are not clear. When he says this won't be on the test, study it, it will be on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He grades a lot of things all or nothing, but his tests are mainly from the notes and problem sets so go over those a lot. There is basically no homework which means you don't get a lot of practice. Make sure to watch a lot of YouTube videos if you want to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Started off really hard, exam 1 was graded all or nothing, cooled down after a while.
