reviews.comment: The man makes FRQ Tests and grades all or nothing based around his own interpretation of what it should be. DO NOT take this class with him. RIP MY GRADES...
Yeah it was like someone died in the room every single day.

Ive not once heard her given any group actual good feedback. It is only about what you do wrong in this class. She is a very tough grader. I've not met anyone who enjoys this course. It is almost to where there is no actual in class work, everything happens outside of class and there is a lot of it.

Tech 120 is the worst class I have taken, so much useless HW. Ivy is the worst person who could teach this useless course. Whenever I asked for feedback she would bash our ideas without any real feedback. It felt like building a puzzle in the dark and when she turned on the lights, she punched you in the face and threw your puzzle at the wall.

There was a homework that was due before every class and another one due the night of every class. The class says it is "Design Thinking in Technology" but there is nothing about technology taught in her class. There is barely any content in the class, so it is  hard to judge her teaching. It is only busy work that was unnecessarily harshly graded.

She really cares about her students and what she teaches; but, she expects students to know everything she says in lecture verbatim for her quizzes and exams. She often gives extra credit if she likes what you write in free response questions. I took her for 3 semesters despite how hard her classes were because you really do learn a lot.

I am usually an A student and this professor was dehumanizing. She brags about how hard her quizzes are and only one student in her teaching career has gotten a 100 on one of her quizzes they are so difficult. On the first day she will scream at people to scare them into dropping out and she will openly talk about how you did on quiz near yourpeers

reviews.comment: Please do not take this class. The content was interesting but your grades will be based on how the professor feels about you. If you are on her good side then you will obtain a good grade, however, if you find yourself on the other side let's hope you really work hard because a B will be your highest grade. Worst class experience I have ever had.

I liked CHM281 - but it can be ridiculous at times. She is the harshest grader I've ever had, wants you to know exactly the answer she wants, and remember every detail from lecture. Quizzes are very hard, her lectures seem sporadic. She is older and there are some cultural differences, so she says unintentionally offensive things sometimes.
Chinese 281 is a lot of memorization, but it is really not that hard as long as you take notes. She loves what she teaches, which makes her lectures interesting.

Hardest class I've ever met. Could not just get a single A through whole semester. Always tested things outside the review sheet. And the professor is such a hard grader who pick on too many details in the answer. And too many things to remember for a quiz or a critique.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! No point of taking this quiz based lecture.
Very fun and smart professor. Class is a bit hard, but is available during office hours to help you learn material. You will learn a lot of stuff in the class for sure!

Wann is definitely one of the most caring teachers I've met in my life. Attending her class, you feel that she really cares about your education. However, you might have to get used to her different style of teaching. She won't put up with slackers but she cares for them. If you like to sit on your ass, this isn't your class.

Professor Ailor is great! He is extremely engaging during his lectures and cares about his students! He always makes sure to address questions when there is challenging material. He has a great sense of humor that makes his lectures so much more enjoyable! He is very clear with expectations!
God took his time with this man

Professor Ailor has got to be the best professor at Purdue University. Not only is this man fair, caring, hilarious, but he is a sensation. Give this guy a raise because I promise he is the most liked and respected professor to ever walk into this institution. Id nominate this guy for an Oscar. If you see him walking around thank him for existing.

Professor Ailor makes learning fun and it's easy to remember what he teaches. Prepare to take notes though! He will exam you on the details he mentions (that aren't written on the slides). He's also very down to earth and humble, and will use his own experiences to help students understand what he's teaching.
I would d!e for this man.
Professor Ailor is great clinical instructor, professor, and simulation instructor. He's clear about what the objectives are what you should learn/remember.
Best professor
I really enjoyed this class, and Professor Holtan was very easy to get in touch with if you had any questions!
One of my favorite professors at Purdue! Although I'm a little bias with loving to write, she was very flexible with due dates, creative ideas, and always had a smile on her face! 1000% suggest her

reviews.comment: Holtan is a rhetorical analysis minor so expect to be doing a lot of rhetorical analysis while in her class. She's nice, but the course requires writing a ton of papers (not really her fault), but she's very detailed (so be careful when citing) and expects a lot of analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She always made sure that her lectures were as engaging and easy to understand as possible. She was always willing to answer questions and re-explain concepts if people were confused. It is clear that she is passionate about what she is teaching which made the class even more enjoyable. She was always available to talk outside of class.

If you are going into clinical psych, therapy, or working with children, you NEED to take this class. She does amazing in-person activities to learn about assessment methods, interventions, and dealing with children. My favorite class at Purdue, go to class and pay attention to get an A. Exams are easy if you study the slides and study guides.

She is one of the best professors I have had at Purdue. Very engaging lectures and a very interesting subject matter. It is clear she cares about the subject and her students learning the subject. This class is an easy A if you show up to lectures, do the assignments, and put in even minimal effort studying for exams. Overall highly recommend!

I have never had a professor that cares so much about her students. She has restructured the class twice because she asked for our feedback and then actually implemented it. You do have to come to class because there are quizzes everyday over the assigned readings, but there is no final because of this. Also there isn't a textbook.
avoid taking this professor at all costs, save the money you spend on class.

reviews.comment: This class is a nightmare. This professor does not communicate with students and he does not give answers to students. There was 4 quizzes due on the first day of class. The class does not teach students and no help is provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ajith gets to know all his students names and tries to encourage them to put in the extra effort to really understand physics. His grading is harsh and at times convoluted and difficult to grasp, which turns many students off. I think if he simplified his grading and gave students a little more slack he'd be a really great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 4 HW sets a week, Graded by how you use his  methods. If you don't write out your answer the way he wants it, you could possibly fail your assignment, even if you got it 100% correct. It is absolute BS. Stay away. I was an A grader in my A Level College Physics but I got a C in this class, which was relatively much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He changed the syllabus to his liking, making it much more difficult. He stops grading after a tiny mistake. He can even consider a 90% a fail. If you're taking him for PHYS 218, please change.

Ajith was by far the worst professor I've had at Purdue.  He was always rude to students in and out of class.  He refused to explain his poorly written syllabus even when directly asked.  The grading is very confusing and difficult.  He only teaches this class, yet he's almost never available.  Even during office hours, he won't want to talk.

Ajith is the worst professor that I have ever experienced in my 15 years of education, (and I've had some bad teachers). Be ready to teach yourself every single thing in this class, because if you ask him a question, even a simple yes or no question he will go out of his way to make you feel like the dumbest person on the planet.

Even though he may seem like a tough grader at times, to put it in his own words he wants to "light a fire in your a**", so if you take his feedback seriously and try your best you will definitely get a solid grade. His lectures are extremely entertaining and the books discussed in class are very interesting. I would recommend his class to anyone

doesn't have rubrics, believes only a few ppl can get A/A+, doesn't respond to emails, tough grader and won't feedback unless you go to office hours (very vague feedback), will dock points and then say the speech was perfect, if other profs don't fit into ur schedule, change ur schedule, this class isn't worth it at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Jitendranath is a fantastic lecturer who possesses a passion for economics.

That aside, he's a tough grader who doesn't believe in rubrics, so grades are extremely subjective. It took too long to learn this since there wasn't a grade inputted until week 12. 

You'll learn a lot in this class, but avoid it if you care about your grade.

reviews.comment: Please take this class with another professor. He does not believe in giving out A's or rubrics.

reviews.comment: avoid if you can.

reviews.comment: Class lectures are fun and entertaining. If talking isn't your thing then this isn't the class for you. Just beware that you wont get an "A" in the class. Don't expect an A — he flat out refuses to give them. No rubrics for presentations, so you're guessing what he wants. Very few assignments but tons of reading. The saving grace? Class is actually fun because it's all open discussion on controversial topics, and he lets everyone share their views without bias. Great debates, brutal grading.

reviews.comment: not accessible outside of class. doesnt put in grades on time. discussions jump from topic to topic without any clear discourse. doesnt reply to emails. have to remind him multiple times. reviews.comment: Amazing professor

Very hands off but I think he lectures very well. I found it hard to communicate with him and get straight forward answers but he was not a very harsh grader. Overall would take again but be prepared to have to advocate for yourself.

Great Professor!
Very knowledgeable and helpful. Wrote out how to do every problem step by step. My favorite class at Purdue.

Osumi-sensei is really an exceptional teacher. She makes class very interesting and engaging, and is very forgiving with grades. On top of that, the course content is interesting and helpful for any students taking Japanese. I highly recommend this course.

Osumi-sensei truly cares about teaching Japanese effectively, which you see through her preparation for class every day, and the level of engagement she provides. reviews.comment: She cares about student study, althougn there is a lots of homework but it was easy. Strongly recommended, and there is a lots of extra credit activity can attend.

Highly Recommend. Osumi sensei is an enthusiastic instructor and she is always glad to help you with problems and questions. Go to the class every time and you will be fine.

reviews.comment: Great Japanese teacher, very nice, very helpful, would take again

I had Ohashi for both JPNS101 and 102 from Fall 2020 - Spring 2021 and I can say she always made my day better. Over zoom its easy to forget youre in a class but she used cute pictures and had songs for every unit. Japanese is a tough language to learn (as a native English speaker) so obviously this class will require lots of work. Love her :)

At first I thought she was an adorable lady but her voice gets annoying. JPNS 102 is just a beginner Japanese class but she puts too much of emphasis that it should be taken seriously, etc etc. Teachers are not very flexible and strict. Expect lots of time consuming homework that is just repetitive. Also usually there are 4 quizzes a week.

reviews.comment: Incredibly nice and helpful. She will make sure you do well even if you aren't doing too hot as long as you show up.

One of the best professors I have ever had! She was so enthusiastic! She loves teaching and is great at clarifying everything. She really makes sure students understand the material. Wonderful Professor!
Probably one of the most fun, informative, and enthusiastic professors I have ever had the privilege of being a student of.
ADORABLE. Still an amazing teacher. Fun, energetic, interested in you and your grade. A very fun class!

She's a great teacher.  There are very few classes that I actually WANT to go to, but this is one of those classes that you want to go to everyday just to see her teach the Japanese course.  Everything was clear and consice and there was nary a dull moment in there.

Ohashi is the most enthusiastic professor you will have in college.  Ever.  She's energetic, helpful, quite humorous, and makes learning Japnese fun and enjoyable.  Her class is highly recommended, if only to put a bright spot in an otherwise boring schedule.
very helpful and always enjoyable to go to class
her voice can get a little annoying, but it's hard to hate her b/c she is so enthusiastic!

This woman is extremely adorable and so much fun as a teacher, she makes the class a blast to come too, even if the TAs don't teach the material very well. She's very helpful and answers questions about almost anything, even if it's not directly related to the material.
Ohashi-sensei rules!!! I love this woman she is the coolest prof i've ever had. This woman makes learning JPNS fun and interesting. And she teaches it at a pace that you understand.
Ohashi-sensei is so funny!  She teaches class like it's Kindergarten. Remember when you first learned how to read? It's like that, but in Japanese.
I took her 133 and 130 theatre class, she was absolutely amazing.
Great!

Shes the best! What I liked most about her is how well she gets to know her students. Even by the middle of the semester she knew our majors, where we were from, and other details about us. My group did everything he said to do, on time, properly, and went above expectations. With a 0/50, my grade was 5% lower than it should've been!!

Taken 3 of his courses and am now graduated. The hands on skills you learn in his class are very valuable and are 90% of the reason I secured a job quickly after graduating. Exams suck but you can get an A even if you fail them. If you make an ef

Chad is so sweet and genuine, but as a teacher he doesn't do much. Exams are so tough, but I found out that it's all copied from textbook questions so it's all on Quizlet (!!!). Lectures is all him telling stories and about him, so he doesn't teach. The semester project is awesome though and really enjoyed it, it was great experience.
Lectures and Tells stories during lecture. Exams are on nothing we cover in class, only textbook (which he never talks about)
Professor was one of the best.
Great class!

I went to undergrad at Purdue. This is my second semester of my MBA. And Professor Allred has been by far my worst professor. His class is the least structured. The fact that he has a final worth 300 of the 900 total points is insane. Especially with no other quizzes or tests leading up to it. Just terribly setup and executed.

Professor Allred was my first marketing professor. Having taken his 324 course freshman year, it was definitely challenging but he always showed how much he cared for his students and I also had a very good group for the projects!
Grading is completely based on group work. Final exam is entirely based on mandated textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is an extremely disorganized course. The "live sessions" do little to enhance the requried readings, the graders (TAs) make up their own rubric different from the professor's, and there is little direction given in the name of promoting creativity - but the graders will nitpick projects to shreds.

If you have the option, DO NOT JOIN HIS CLASS. The professor & his TAs are ridiculous when it comes to grading. They don't even read the full paper & won't give back points even when they admit they're wrong. This happened to all the groups in my class and we were outraged. If you follow their rubrics, you only get 50-75% of points.

Professor Allred is a nice enough guy, but not a good professor. The entire class was basically graded off of a group project. He provides little to no feedback when he gives tough grades. He assigns a marketing case analysis with no rubric and gives bad scores. His lectures are boring, and I feel as though I learned nothing.

Professor Allred rarely provides feedback, rubrics, or clear guidance. His class consists mostly of him telling personal stories and is rarely on topic. The workload is outrageous and consists of mostly busy work that consumes time while teaching little.
Chad is the man. His lectures are boring at times but he is overall a great teacher that is passionate about what he does. Exams are a little tough but there is a curve on them.
The best prof I've had at Purdue. Period

381 is a very difficult class due to the amount of time you need to put in it along with tough exams. He lectures very well and can answer questions with good examples too. The curve was pretty big at the end.
Good professor overall and breaks complex topics down well. The one downside is that he expects a high level of prior knowledge coming into the class and will skip steps in his notes because of that.

Prof Psomas and CS 381 is what any CS class should be like. Amazing lectures, structured homeworks, informative slides, and fair exams. Is the class hard and going to make you want to jump in frozen wabash river? Yes. Is the class very interesting with a top-notch lecturer? Also yes. Would 100% recommend no matter your CS interests.
Best cs lecturer I have had at purdue. Course is tough but worth taking it.
Really hard, definitely attend office hours to consult your homework, and try your best to solve the homework problems.

Tough class, great professor. He definitely cares about your learning on a subject that many people just can't grasp. TA's were kinda harsh though and graded very strictly. But if you go to Psoma's lectures, you will get a good understanding of the material.

The exams made up 65% of the grade which kinda sucked but the content was really helpful, especially for technical interviews and OAs.  Prof Psomas is really kind, understanding, and wants you to suceed.  Only thing I would have changed about the course is for homeworks, which take about 15-20 hours each, was worth more than 20%.

The best lecturer I've had at Purdue. Psomas is a legendary teacher and 381 is a notorious class. The class is the final gatekeeper for CS degrees. He gives you every tool necessary to fight your toughest battle B)
Alex is one of the most caring professors I've met. Be aware that averages on assignments and tests are very low but that doesn't mean you'll get a bad grade (trust the curve). Highly recommend!

Honestly the best professor you could get for anything related to algorithms. He is VERY VERY passionate about algorithms and it is awesome. His exams are very very hard but he is very generous about the curves. He has empathy for this students and its great. Try to take this professor if you can!
Great approachable professor sharing his passion of algorithms. His slides are extremely clear (for how difficult some of the coursework is) and explains how to understand algorithms well.
Absolutely phenomenal lecturer. Very reasonable when it comes to grading, assignments, and exams. Explains things very well and is very passionate about both research and teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Psomas did a great job making the difficult content more easily understood, and did a good job trying to keep lectures interesting. Very reasonable with homework deadlines and seemed like an approachable guy

Psomas is one of the best professors I have come across at Purdue. Although CS381 is challenging, he makes the coursework really interesting. He is very passionate about algorithms. You do have to put in the work to get a good grade, though. I feel lucky that I was his student. His instruction in CS381 has made me consider grad school.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: CS381 is one of the most notoriously difficult classes at Purdue, and Alex does a brilliant job in conveying the material to students. Readily available outside lecture, willing to get coffee with any student who needs to talk/wants to talk. He says his tests are hard, but curve is nicer. Take 381 ONLY with Alex Psomas :))
One of the best profs I've ever had. He took one of the most notoriously difficult CS classes and made it digestable. I only wish the class was a bit more organized, with master theorem and all that

CS381 is one of the most feared classes in Purdue CS's course catalog but I absolutely loved taking it with Professor Psomas! His lectures made concepts easy for me to grasp and if I didn't, he was usually available outside of class for questions. He seems passionate about the material and his assignments and exams are very fair. Give him tenure.

I had the best experience with Mr. Rhodes. His teaching style is one you can easily adapt to, and he is truly passionate about the work he assigns. He's very open and straightforward about the ciriculum so feel free to ask questions. Would most definitely take again!
Great Professor. Definitely recommend for SCLA 102. Makes lectures engaging and interesting. Have to participate in class but it's not daunting. No exams, but be ready to present.

Great professor! I took him for SCLA 102. Lectures are pretty chill, although you have to participate. Really caring professor, if you need help definitely reach out to him he's super kind and helpful. Attendance and participation are a good amount of your grade. Overall super easy grader and cool professor. Would take again!

Professor Rhodes was great. You must talk in class to earn participation points, but he grades everything super easily. He wants to see you succeed, and he offers extra credit if you wear business attire during presentations. There is a lot of reading for the class, and then all you do during class is discuss. GET READY TO PRESENT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very clear and explains content super well. His class is not hard at all and the practice exam review questions are life-savers. He kept things simple and is overall fantastic.
Very clear and direct. Provides great instruction and is always willing to answer questions. Did not struggle with this class at all, even though I did bad in precalc/trig

Good professor; his homework truly helps you with the exams. His advice is also helpful - do the homework in practice mode so you can truly grasp the content. attendance mandatory. I will say that sometimes it's a bit hard to follow him - be ready to learn the content outside of class. had to teach myself over 5 lessons.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Pothen is a nice and understanding person, giving us a few days of deadline for homework and an extra 10 minutes on the 2nd midterm. The lectures are not easy to follow although the content itself isn't hard. My only complaint is that homework is too tedious. Can take anywhere from 6 to 9 hours.
Lectures have little to no value as he mumbles a lot, and his work is hard to follow. Learning the material on your own is required.

He's a caring professor and he's knowledgeable about 314.
I think his lectures are ok in person but he mumbles quite a bit, making lecture recordings really hard to understand. He also uploads notes, which are hard to understand (better than nothing though).
Homeworks can be tedious, but aren't super hard. Exams are fair. Grades/curved leniently

Pothen is very knowledgable but has quite poor handwriting and vague lectures. The class feels like a repeat of high/middle school: learn how to do a few specific computations and you will do great. Homeworks are cancer, exams are easy

Pothen is alright. It really feels like he wants students to understand by going through some of the more intriguing applications of numerical analysis. BUT beware of his iClicker quizzes if u wanna skip his classes and cram before midterms (def achievable). Overall a sweet guy but holy crap the handwriting reflects on his monotone voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are very interesting but can be hard to follow at times. I believe he is a kind hearted man. Many concepts in the class are much easier than they seem at first. The explanations for topics on the homeworks and in lectures can be excessive / ineffective at times.

I think the best way to understand course material is through the homework and rereading Professor Pothen's lecture slides. The lectures themselves have a tendency to be longer than they need to be and the professor has a habit of mumbling some sentences. The professor can also be a bit passive aggressive with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Amazing lectures cured my stubborn insomnia!

No slides cuz the typing is live! Literally he live typing comments on matlab interative command line. When there's a typo, he starts a new line and restarts typing.

Definetly don't skip a lecture and watch youtube videos that cover the same stuffs within 5 minutes, or you'll miss his sexy pop quizzes!

Lectures were somewhat jumbled and confusing, but with some effort you could get a grasp on the topics with a combo of the lecture notes and book. Luckily, the course material wasn't that hard, so overall it wasn't too bad.

he spend first 10min on reviewing previous lecture; next 30min on write new knowledge on his chalkboard; the rest part he begin reading matlab document. He suspend 1/3 of lectures for his conference social hours. He only prepare material only before the day of the lecture. His aim seems to be put as less effort as possible on teaching.

Professor Pothen's exams are challenging, but aside from that the course is fair. Homework's are straight forward and build off material from the lectures and the textbook. While his lectures are helpful, I found the textbook to be integral to getting through the homeworks and he bases the exam problems off of example problems.

The homework is well crafted, not overly complicated and they do provide a solid preparation for the exams. The professor is helpful in his office hours. The classes are fairly interesting. The expected content of numerical analysis is well presented, and he covered Automatic Differentiation exceptionally well.

Uses chalkboard instead of slides, which helps students keep up when writing.  Lessons are usually fairly interesting, but he can be unintentionally condescending when a student asks a question that is simple in his mind.
Never listen to students arguments. Keeps telling stop arguments listen to me. Not interested to clarify students doubts or queries. Not interested to listen to students.
Overall was a very fun class and not too hard at all. As long as you turn in your lab reports on time getting a good grade in this class is a breeze.

I took this online over 8 weeks and it wasn't bad. He posts good videos. Assignments look like a lot but really aren't bad. He doesn't allow extensions at all. There's grouped book assignments with McGraw hill and those take a long time so work ahead. Tests aren't terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I sent an email because I joinee the class over a week late nad he gave me 2 days to complete all the work and when I emailed asking a question I had to send a follow up days later because he would not respond and when he did it was short unformal and disrespectful.
If you get this guy, run. There are no instructions at all. Run as fast as you can, take literally any other course, that's all I can say.

This guy is inaccessible, rude, and doesn't know how to accept that he's wrong about something. He doesn't read emails when they're sent to him, he just gives a generic response, which is somehow more unhelpful than not getting a response, because god forbid he actually does his job. Course material is just basic stuff you can find on google.

You know its bad when I have to sign up and make an account just to talk about the professor. He was actually awful. There was no form of teaching whatsoever but when it came to projects, nothing made sense, nothing was in the right place and when I emailed him to help he brushed me off and gave me a ss from google search.

He does go on tangents, but it keeps his class interesting. He's a discussion style lecturer, and is interactive with his students. His quizzes and exams have typos &/or poorly worded. Be careful with his online quizzes as you NEED to double check his auto-grading. He WILL NOT fix it without you saying smth, even if someone pointed it out.

This was an overall great class. Some of the lab reports were a little much and exams weren't worded the best, but this class is a fun class that will teach you quite a bit. Mr. Furiya wants his students to suceed and learn the material.

Professor Furiya focuses on learning and discussing more so than assignments. Attendance was never mandatory, but if you were super close to rounding up to the next percentage point, you won't get it if you had poor attendance. I feel like my time was valued and respected, and I was never stressed about this class.

Alvin can sometimes go off on tangents but overall is a very sweet guy and great professor. You can really tell he wants his students to learn and do well in his courses and in general. I took both 205 and 125 with him and enjoyed both classes greatly! A little bit homework heavy in 205, but not unreasonable and not difficult to complete.

prof albitz is an understanding person, she is silly and easy to talk to. her classroom has an open and lighthearted vibe. she is more of a tough grader and i would say you definitely need to put in effort to get a good grade on your speeches, but the rubric is pretty clear.

My opinion of Professor Albitz changed a ton throughout the semester. While she might be on the harder end of grading speeches, getting a good grade in her course is still very achievable. I found she genuinely cares about her students, and even though the course itself is a little flawed, I would still definitely recommend her section!

Albitz is a great person, always bringing energy and good vibes to class. In terms of grading, I always felt it was very fair. There were clear rubrics, and I understood why points were lost on speeches. Also, she is very accessible if you have a question on a speech, project, or homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While she may be one of the "harder" comm graders, that's really exaggerating. I was not the best at speeches, but I averaged a 90 on them and didn't do much preparation. Lectures can be boring sometimes, but that's not her fault it's the department's fault. She truly cares about the students and gets to know them
thumbs up!
Genuinely cared about performance and improvement in the class. Gave good feedback and was very approachable but does grade a bit harsh. Diffidently approachable and sometimes let us out early.

I'm not quite sure what these other reviews are on about but when I had her she was fair and amicable. She cares for her students and wants the best for their academics. I loved this class and it was one of the ones that I always showed up to. Which says something because I don't go to class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This lady had the lowest A rate out of all com 114 professors last semester. All my stem classes had a higher gpa. Horrible person who thinks that her class is the only thing that matters
She told students in class go rate high on rmp for bonus points which is messed up. Terrible professor who made a required gen ed unnecessary stressful. Avoid at all cost
Worst professor of all time avoid at all costs

Half of these reviews are fake. She might be approachable, but is by far one of the worst professors you can have if you are taking this class for a good grade. Average GPA  is the lowest for this semester

Mrs. Albitz was truly a joy. Even with my class taking place at 4:30 pm, including Fridays, I was always excited to go to class. She is a very kind, understanding, and flexible person, and in my opinion, the perfect person to teach this course.

Professor Albitz is a great instructor.  I looked forward to coming to class. She taught us great communication skills and really cares about her students. I would definitely recommend this lady. I wish she taught other classes too.

10/10 if you can take com114 with her, do it! She is such a caring, kind and funny lady. She makes you want to come to class! I told her i would write this review because she truly deserve the best! Class is really easy, you're given the final group project at the start of the semester, so if you can, start early and get it out of the way!
If you go to class and communicate with the professor/ follow her guidelines, this class should be cake! Wish she taught more classes because I like how she sets things up.
Love this lady. Put the work in and get the grade! Great lectures, easy to communicate with
She responds quickly to emails. She is a fair grader. Class was fun and engaging.
Engaging professor. Interesting material. Tries to apply content every major.

Docks unreasonable amount of points for small errors, really hard to get a good grade. When the grades get put in, the percentage doesn't actually reflect your grade. Syllabus isn't updated and is point-based instead of percentage based, so it doesn't actually reflect your grade either. She doesn't retain your attention when lecturing in class.

lectures are very easy to understand. you will leave lecture feeling like you understand what is going on instead of studying for hours trying to figure out what the bullet points are saying. very concise and engaging

yes you have to put in a lot of work in and study a lot, but the more work you put in, the better results you'll get with his lectures! i learned so much from hudmon and he made me excited about biochem. he cares so much about our learning and explains very well by breaking topics down into digestible materials.

He made this class bearable, his lectures had structure and had enough to keep you focused while not overwhelmed. His tests come directly out of class material and makes efforts to help students out on his free time.

Would take again, wish he taught the majority of class as well.

Dr. Hudmon is the one redeemable factor in this mess of a class. He works hard to make sure we are understanding his material, which can be difficult at times. However, his exams are extremely fair in comparison to Krusemark's and he pulls directly from the slides. Exam review sessions are helpful, given he actually answers questions unlike others.

Dr. Hudmon is amazing and picked up the slack for his co-lecturer Dr. Krusemark. Extremely resourceful and caring about students understanding material. His content is tough, but thats just Biochem, he did all he could to ensure we understood and were successful.

Hudmon seems to really care about his students and explains lecture in way for us to understand. His exam questions come straight from the slides or iClicker questions. He emphasized important information that we needed to know (like for homework or exams). He rarely fell behind in slides and if he ever did, he made extra videos to compensate.

Dr. Hudmon is the only reason this class is bearable. His lectures are much easier to follow and he takes time to ensure we are understanding the material. Exam content is pulled straight from the slides and he will even recycle past exam questions. If he was the course coordinator rather than Krusemark, student performance would be way better.

Dr. Hudmon is SO much better than Dr. Krusemark. Don't be discouraged by the horror that is exam one, once you reach Hudmon's content things become a lot more clear. Dr. Hudmon is extremely knowledgeable and seems to care a lot more about his impact on students, he will tell you the key takeaways you need to know for the exams and future courses.

Was WAY better than Krusemark when teaching MCMP 208. His slides were definitely hard to follow, but if you went to lecture and paid attention/took notes, they made sense. His exam questions were a lot more straightforward and everything was pulled from the slides (as it should be)!

I am the type of student who studies so hard and maintains a 4.0 til my junior year. Don't take this class plz. The professor doesn't know what he is talking about and speed-reads all his slides. There are around 400 slides you need to memorize per exam and a total of 1200 slides for your cumulative final. VERY DETAILED exams too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
It was disheartening to see Hudmon misjudging students' talents. 
What concerned me even more was his lack of support when students faced an abusive environment under other PIs in different labs. His failure to stand up for his students during such distressing situations demonstrates a lack of integrity.

This class is nothing but a train wreck and a professor who refuses to upload answer keys for study guides does nothing but make it worse. I can't express my distain for this class and professor in words.
He is a funny man and cares about students. If you communicate with him, he will always help you. If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask him.

Biochem is one of the hardest classes I have taken. Dr. Hudmon is very nice for students who want to know more and ask questions, go to his office hour and he will explain things clearly to you. The exam is hard and needs a lot of time to study.

Most of the class is spent expressing his opinion. I thought he would get better in a few weeks, but as the class progresses, he is expressing his opinion more and more. The test was also based on his opinion. Mentoring students is the worst part, and he, ignoring the facts, is ending g graduates students' lives again with his opinions.
Teaford delivered my baby. - class of 87'

Kindest, most passionate professor I have had. Attendance is mandatory but you will want to show up to every class. It was incredibly fun, and he is an amazing person to be around. I'd definitely take this class again if I could. The content was engaging, and his lectures were even more so.

Professor Bellisari is absolutely amazing. While attendance is mandatory, this is a class that you will want to attend. He is incredibly well spoken during his lectures and extremely kind to his students. If you have the opportunity, absolutely take a class he is teaching. Hist 408
Made what was supposed to be a boring core curriculum class very enjoyable. Stay on top of your work and you can finish with an A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bellisari was one of the best professors I had last semester. He's a very engaging speaker and managed to make 75 minute class periods go by quickly. I'm not the biggest fan of public speaking, but on speech days, he made the classroom a calm and encouraging environment where I didn't feel super nervous about presenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a STEM major, I fully expected SCLA 102 to be a snooze-fest, but professor Bellisari made every period engaging and interesting. Our class discussions were wide-ranging and incredibly thought-provoking, everything we did felt motivated and intentional, and prof. Bellisari consistently made an effort to switch things up to keep things interesting

Professor Bellisari's class was engaging, with frequent discussions on the readings. He doesn't check if you've read but expects participation. Grading was unusual, as he completed it all on the last day before grades were due. He is lenient with grading. Be ready for pop quizzes, but they are fairly basic so spark notes should be enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lectures and assignments. Engaging material.
he is amazing, 10/10
The goat. Take this class.
Absolutely awesome semester. I learned a lot and he cares about all his students. He makes class very fun and is very understanding.

Anderson is my favorite teacher that I've ever had as a student, hands down. He's super funny while also being super clear and helpful during lectures. He knows what he is talking about and makes the material interesting, fun, and easy to follow along which ultimately leads to a successful and enjoyable learning experience. Highly recommend him.

Anderson makes his class fun and is really good at "reading the room" and changing class plans based on the students. He's hilarious and had us play fun games in Spanish using the stuff we'd been learning. He really cares about his students' mental health and if they're taking care of themselves. I looked forward to going to his class every day!

Prof. Carmona runs a casual and conversational classroom widely open to discussion. It makes for an enjoyable time in class no matter how mundane the topics at hand can seem. Honestly a must have professor if you get the choice to take a class with him.
Do not response email, and bad teaching.

She does not answer any emails sent to her Very difficult to understand and writes very lightly on the board so that it is not readable. Late to class and doesn't tell students when there are review sessions. lets students create a cheat sheet but it doesnt really help Seems lost about the course herself, gets things wrong and doesnt know due dates

Unable to answer questions about the material and gets defensive and condescending. Fails to pace curriculum well. Unaware of her own due dates. Tests and quizzes contain errors and take forever to get graded. Unprepared for classes. Has errors on slides. Struggles with Brightspace. Does not communicate necessary info in time. The list goes on...

Has no idea what is going on within her own class. Unable to answer questions, and will belittle students for questioning her responses, even if they are incorrect. Will not respond to emails, and no clarity on what current grades are. Quizzes and exams are graded incorrectly and take numerous weeks to return. Avoid at all costs.

No control over her own classroom. Constantly confused by everything - computers, brightspace, questions, her own lectures, her assigned due dates. Typos in notes, 4 exam questions were graded incorrectly. Didn't think through any assignments, had to make things up on the spot when asked about it. Didn't give lectures of topics in time for 2nd exam

Difficult to understand. Always late and/or unprepared. Bad at answering questions. Doesnt respond to emails. Poor course structure. Aouar wasted so much time at the beginning of lectures, that she would race through the most important information (10-15 slides in about 30-45 seconds). GOOD LUCK
(list of negative feedback goes on)

Where do I begin? Very hard to understand, always unprepared and/or late for class, unresponsive and/or inaccurate answers to questions, and class material is extremely unorganized and out of logical order. Find a different teacher!

I really enjoyed his lectures. He's funny and engaging and he really cares about us. My only complaint is that he is a bit scatter brained and his lectures were at times hard to follow. My main complaints aside from that have to do more with how the course is setup (3 grades, 2 professors, etc) and less to do with him specifically

Hardest class you will take at Purdue but Dr. Applegate is a great professor and is genuinely so funny. The first half of claaa is the other professor and all of the Midterms are completely written. This class basically covers every other class you have ever taken in high detail (genetics, BCHM, Orgo, etc) so STUDY A LOT….

Its a shame he shares a class with 2 other sub-par professors. His section was by far the best. Engaging lectures and very easy to talk to outside class. He's a nice/funny guy who is obviously passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. The class is graded on 3 assignments (3 brutal(but fair)exams) which kind of sucked.

Solid professor and a really nice guy. His lectures are interesting, he adds lots of examples, and breaks down complicated topics. He's obviously very knowledgeable and willing to help students outside class whenever needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Applegate is obviously very knowledgeable about microbiology, but his lectures are not very informative. He often sacrifices teaching for a good laugh, and when he is teaching it seems very scattered and unstructured, and he often goes off topic which is not what I was looking for in an upper-level biology course.

You can tell Dr. Applegate is very knowledgable about the material he teaches (you would think this would go for all professors but you'd be surprised). It's obvious he loves what he does and it portrays during his lectures. He will go the extra step to help. He's also very funny! The class is difficult though since there are few chances for points
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class is difficult since there are not a lot of points. But Bruce is awesome  funny and nice. Go to his review sessions, he really wants to help.
So much better than the other two Bio 438 instructors.  Dr. Applegate listens carefully to student questions instead of immediately throwing back more boiler plate.
Great professor.  Nice, funny, entertaining.

Was not too bad, but the main issue is that she can be a bit harsh in terms of grading and ensures that the TA does the same. For example, there were many correct answers I have given, but the main issue is that she only marks it correct if we do it the way she prefers. Class was also fairly disorganized so that can have some improvement as well
Labs are hard but you'll do fine if you go to lecture and take notes.
She is one of the best professors at Purdue Polytechnic.

She is very nice but she will not cut you much slack. Labs can be very difficult to complete if you do not finish them on time (it is a lab-heavy class). This class and ECET 227 are easily the hardest within the major.

Professor Cheung is easily one of my favorite professors at Purdue, if not my favorite. She is very organized, fair, and the environment she creates in class and labs is very enjoyable. She is always ready to help and I always felt comfortable asking her anything!
Honestly my favorite professor at Purdue. If you put in the work she will help you with anything you ask.

Professor Cheung is a gem! She is easily accessed outside of class. If you do not finish a lab you are given the following week and can go into any of her other labs to finish! She is super nice and is great at explaining topics. Honestly, probably my top teacher in the ECET department.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: great professor, very knowledgeable and passionate. hw is harder than exams, but go to review sessions and she will guide you how to solve them. do not freak out if she says you're "behind" and youre going to fail if you havent started studying like a week before the exam...exams took 2-3 days to prepare if you lock in and understand past exams

Dr. Kasinski was a great professor. Her lectures were engaging and interesting, and she truly cares about her students. The "disrespect" was her asking students to quiet down so others could learn, which I think is a reasonable action.

Makes a very complex curriculum extremely easy to learn, great lectures, and overall just a very easygoing and articulate professor. There's barely any homework but it's still great practice for exams, and exams are pretty easy especially with the practice exams she posts. Really easy class but still very interesting.

Dr. Kasinski gave great lectures, especially at the beginning of the semester. However, over time her quality of lectures tends to go downhill as the material gets more difficult. The exams gradually get more difficult and more specific. Make sure you study both the lecture notes and the uploaded typed notes for this course, as they will be tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best resources for this class in my opinion are her weekly review sessions and the old exams she posts. I unfortunately had a club that met up at the same time as the review sessions so I couldn't attend and I think that's what put me at an A- rather than A.

While I didn't always like her lectures, the exams were very fair. She gave two practice exams for every exam and as long as you did those, you would get a B. She also had review sessions every week where she'd walk us through the entire homework.

Her lectures are very monotonous and boring, and she has mandatory attendance with iClickers that you have to answer correctly to get full points. The homeworks are harder than the tests and only have 3 attempts allowed. Fortunately the tests are just like the practice tests she uploads. Your biggest challenge will be not falling asleep in class.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking this course with Dr. Kasinski! She made the content interesting and easy to understand in lectures. Homework was challenging, but the three attempts were helpful. Exams were similar to past exams and accurately reflected what was covered in class and the notes she releases after class.

Did not like Dr. Kasinski. Her lectures were un-engaging, the exams were terribly worded, and 400 of the total 600 points are from exams. If you don't test well, then you won't do well, period. There's very little to make up from one bad test. She also uses minus grades, which in my opinion, sucks and is unnecessary.
She's super knowledgeable, but I didn't enjoy her lectures

My biggest gripe with this instructor is her grading structure. 400/600 points are attributed to exams with no drop. One exam can and will drop your course grade by a whole letter with no opportunity for recovery. In addition, exams are largely short answer. Lots of opportunity to miss points by not describing enough or writing exactly her answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. The so-called “disrespect” was really Dr. Kasinski asking persistent talkers to quiet down so others could hear. When they didn't, she raised her voice and asked late students to use the back doors. I respect her for protecting those there to learn. If you truly want to learn cell biology, take this class.

Amazing professor. Lecture content is clear and engaging, tests are easy and match the practice exams, and homework can be slightly challenging. For other reviews saying she is “disrespectful”: she got frustrated at the class after several instances of people talking over her up to 5 minutes into the lecture, which I think is reasonable.

She has help sessions every week and most of her exams are similar to practice exams. Homework has 3 attempts with 2 weeks dropped. Same for participation points, which is basically 100 points for attending class. She walks the class through processes to help with difficult concepts. Favourite bio class so far.

She is inconsistent with participation points, and none of the lecture content is in the exams. She always has a negative attitude towards our class and is quite disrespectful to students. Homework is too difficult, and most of the questions are not mentioned in the exams. Barely any extra credit, no drop exams, and no curve, so she's just evil.

She is disrespectful to students, and does not seem to care about them. Her lessons are unorganized and unhelpful for the exams. Her information also does not match any source online. Studying the homework does not help for the exams, and she changes the set up for the exams each time so it is very difficult to prepare.

Great course. Dr K emphasizes thinking about the material opposed to just memorizing. The exams and homework use the information in class and apply it. While knowing content is important, applying it is more important. Can be a challenge at first, but she helps so that we are prepped for higher classes that will follow this way of learning.
Horrible. Does not know how to explain and homeworks have nothing to do with the lectures.
Very knowledgeable, great speaker and caring about her students success

Great course - took it in 2023 but heard she didnt tech it in 2024, but will be back next fall. A lot of what is needed for upper level courses was covered. Also prepared me for MCAT. Glad I was able to take the class when she taught it. Although not sure how it went this year w/o her.

I think Dr. Kasinski is my favorite professor so far. She takes time to explain things during lectures which helps me really understand what is going on. Also, there is a lot of office hours which are really helpful.

Great lectures (mandatory) but this is a hard course. She is very knowledgeable and does not waste any time during lecture. This course is difficult. I never read the book, but be sure to look at the lecture notes she releases after lecture. Go to bio resource room for help on the homeworks

Dr. Kasinski is a dynamic, hilarious lecturer that simplifies content that might otherwise be mind-numbingly difficult to understand. Her grading scheme is fair, if not generous, as exams are derived from lectures (including notes she provides) and old exams. She makes understanding the content easy, no textbook required.

The class was okay, you'll do well if you memorize the notes and the practice exams but I didn't do that so I didn't do well. She got mad at our class near the beginning of the semester for people getting caught cheating on exams and never offered us extra credit on exams like she did for her previous years. She also sometimes had an attitude lol.

Kasinski is an amazing lecturer, she knows her stuff and explains everything very well. Textbook reading is pretty much unnecessary- all you need is to go to lectures and read lecture notes. The exams are vey similar to  past exams which she posts- some questions are reused every year. Hardest part is the homework but you get multiple attempts.

Dr. Kasinski sets very specific guidelines. You earn 100 points from attendance and 100 points from homework which is easy to obtain because you are given 3 attempts. The exams are carbon copies of practice exams. This course doesn't take lots of time, but you'll need to devote time to studying. Everything is very straightforward and fair.

She has a very nice lecture style and covers topics at a good speed. Homework can be tricky but help is available. Exams are quite difficult and are made worse by not allowing calculators for them. Graded on PollEverywhere, Homework, and Exams. The difficulty of the class is largely not her fault, the course is just hard. Study hard and read well!

Her exams are not necessarily hard, but they are very specific on wording. Review the old exams she gives you, as those will be very indicative of the wording they expect. Participation is taken which while can be annoying to some is a nice grade assist, and she allows drops. Study the supplemental notes and go to office hours, and you'll do fine.

Best way to do well in this class is by reviewing the practice exams IN DEPTH. A lot of the exam questions come from past exams. Also, the lecture notes she posts after class are a savior as a supplement to your in class notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The material for this class tough and the lectures can be hard to get through; however Dr. K. offers up to 100 points (equivalent to an exam) for attendance as well as multiple tries for the homework. The exams can be difficult but are very similar to past exams. Be sure to put in the work and study and you can end the class with a good grade.

my favorite so far. class is based on 4 exam (similar to old posted exams), participation (show up and you get 100 points!), and homework (you get 3 tries and two weeks are dropped). do the work and you can get an A. dr. k provides all the tools to succeed. from what i have heard past years did not have the participation or dropped homework.
teaches a difficult class but provides many resources to help students succeed. Uses many questions from past exams and provides the keys to those exams. A nice professor and very smart.

Class was great, the material was tough, but Dr. Kasinski give the tools to help. Wednesday night review sessions and pre-exam review is a great help. Old exams are similar to new exams, so studying those is a great tool. Highly recommend.

Definitely a good professor with a great amount of care for students. Her lectures can be a little heavy from time to time, but overall it did make a lot of sense. Also practice exams were just like the actual exam, so not too bad to study for. Homework makes you think more, but overall not terrible. Definitely really good!
Great instructor - one of my favorites at Purdue. I especially recognize that now, and wish I could go back to Cell Bio. Also wish Dr. K taught another upper level course.

I miss Dr. K every single day. Her lectures are clear and well made with lecture notes for students to reference. The learning objectives make it very easy to make sure you're on track and the provided past exams set clear expectations. I wish I could have this professor for every single class.

Fun class. Learned a lot, but you have to keep up or you will get lost. The class builds on knowledge. If you go to lecture (don't skip!) and review sessions, the class is not difficult. Old exams posted are great study guides.

Dr. K is great. Clearly very passionate about teaching and is very personable. Girlboss. No curve, and class is mostly exams with no drops, so you always have to be on top of things. gives good study materials and really stresses the use of the BRC and studying with the TAs. Great lady. Class isn't easy.

Dr. K was really amazing and made cell bio an enjoyable class. She knew the material well and presented it in a way that made a lot of sense. Had review sessions every week for anyone that needed help on homework and had pre-exam review as well. Exams are tough but very similar to the past exams so start studying at least 5-6 days in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: A few profs teach this. Loved Dr. K. Heard from others In different sections and was glad I was in Dr. K section. Well organized and passionate.

Great lecturer! She teaches the material in a way that is easy to understand and it is very clear that she is passionate about cell bio. She releases her own notes after each lecture which are super helpful and could be substituted for going to class. Her exams are very similar to past exams, so use the ones she posts and you should do pretty well!
Great class. Converted me into a cell biology enthusiast. :-)

Prof K is accessible but this class structure is very messy and has a lot of material. The lectures can be a bit hard to follow and she can be monotone at times. The monday night reviews and practice exams are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really want to like Dr. Kasinski, and I do, but this course was a nightmare. BIOL 231 with her felt like 3 different courses across the lectures, homework, and exams. It is nice that past exams prepare you fairly well for the present, but this class needs a serious restructure. Her weekly help sessions are worth going to, though.

Little to no empathy during an unprecedented semester. 7 nitty gritty exams one every other week, only 45 min in length with about 30 questions. To get an A you could only lose 35 points total. Go to lecture, every review session (she will help you through homework), and review all practice exams provided. It feels like you can never take a breath.

Hard class but helped me prep for my MCAT. Lots of topics covered by Dr. K were on the test. If you want to prep for the MCAT and are serious about your education she is great. If you are not, and don't want to work hard, you will likely not succeed. You get what you put in. But she helps. Wish there were more professors that cared about students.

Dr. K is one of the most accessible professors at Purdue. I had multiple concerns over rate semester and she was helpful and responded quickly. I also really enjoyed the material and thought she did a great job with covid and having to teach both online and in person. thanks for a great semester.

Cell biology sparked my interest in biology and made me realized why I initially wanted to major in biology in the first place. Enjoyed the small exams. Although difficult to study for, at times, with the hyflex course I appreciated not having to study 10 lectures worth of material. It gave you a chance to do poor on one exam w/o effecting grade.

Your grade is decided on 7 nit-picky exams with little to no partial credit they are every other week). They are only 45 min long-gives you no time to check your work, or think. Kasinski is an average lecturer at best and completely lacks empathy. There is no curve, no extra credit, lose 35 points and you lose your A. Do all your hw, review p-exams

Kasinski's cell bio course is definitely difficult. The tests are extremely hard and have short time limits, and much of the class performs poorly. That being said, she is an excellent lecturer and seems to really care about her students.

Review session are super helpful. Good at lecturing, but to do good requires understanding lecture notes AND online lecture notes too. A lot of extra work is required and setup currently is bad. Seven 45 minutes exams. So you learn half material week of, and test EVeRY other week. Good at responding to emails. Have to be active student to do well.
Helpful and really accessible outside of class. I guess it was difficult, but I enjoyed it so not really a bad thing. I learned a lot and was inspired by the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's clear that she tries really hard to be a good professor but her lecture notes don't make sense and her exams were all over the place with difficulty. This was her first year online and it burnt a lot of students out because we tested every other week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: great prof. would take a course with her again, but not sure if she teaches anything else. she should.

Wow - i am so surprised by the previous comments. Granted I just started this course this semester. But without question Prof. K is outstanding. She is soooo responsive (like within 10 minutes of sending multiple emails she responds). Seems very engaged and cares about the students. Perhaps things changed this year, I dont know. But so far so good.

Was the class difficult? YES! Did I learn something useful? Absolutely. And Professor Kasinski was great. She offers after-hours help sessions and plenty of resources to succeed. Honestly, I would have done better had I used the resources on the first exam. You are set up for success, but YOU have to take the initiative.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. K is a great professor. You can tell that she is very dedicated to the course and importantly to her students. The class is not easy, but if you attend class, listen to her advice (she often will 'highlight' exact questions on exams), and study hard, a good grade is very possible. Over 60% of the class got A/B. But you do have to work for it.

Dr. K is a super nice person, but a horrible professor. Her lecture notes do not correspond to the lecture notes given online. I studied weeks for an exam and still failed it. The class is heavily reliant on exams and she does curve the class or give extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr K is fairly new to teaching this course but is doing great. Gives great analogies for concepts in class and her taking notes gives you an idea of what to focus on and time to write. She may seem brusque in class but is kind and approachable 1-on-1. Ask for help if you need it! Exams are very similar to past years, so study previous exams given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was by far the hardest biology course I have taken. Professor Kasinski is not a fair grader, if you don't put the exact words that she is looking for, she will count it wrong. There is way too much material on the exams that is not fully explained in lecture. Exams are all fill in the blank so guessing isn't even an option.

Dr. Kasinski was a good professor it is just a hard class with a lot of information to be covered in only one semester. If you relisten to her lectures and look at the notes provided online they match up exactly and the lectures help tie up the information. What she says in lecture can be word for word on the test you just need to pay attention.

She is very nice as a person but absolutely terrible as a professor. Almost any sort of homework or exam problem that you would encounter likely was not covered in lecture and had to be learned on your own, either from the textbook or other sources. Her exams are ridiculously hard, do not be surprised if you fail one or several of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She has the class laid out so backwards. Her notes that she gives during class - god awful. She is all over the place and doesn't explain anything. She talks the entire time and writes maybe 4 words down to take for notes. She says her exams will be "exactly like past exams" but then are completely different. 44% of the class FAILED Exam 2. No EC.

New professor on Purdue's campus, and after hearing the amazing things about the old professor for a certain class. After having him sub in for one lecture, I truly saw the difference. Lecture material relates little to exams besides figures and charts and she stays true to paper. Homework is useless. Your grade is completely dependent on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Andrea is going to be the new prof for BIOL231 and even though she is fairly new, she is very good. She is an intelligent woman and really knows her stuff. The only issue people had was that you can tell she is fairly new at teaching and gets nervous, but just be patient and you will do just fine. She offers many opportunities for help if you need.

Wonderful, caring, and facilitates so many important discussions about race, gender, class, and other issues that affect today. She has a great grip of history. She guides the discussions well. She chose some amazing books. And what's cool is that she is very open to new ideas and interpretations.
Dr. Sagar is a wonderful, kind, and intelligent woman. She is a wonderful educator and facilitates fantastic discussions. Her classes are flexible and student-led.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED professor Sagar! She has been my favorite professor at Purdue yet. She is so sweet and caring, and the class is all discussion. She does give pop-reading quizzes, but if you read theyre easy! You also write lots of papers, but she makes expectations SUPER clear!! LOVE HER!! Take any course you can with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Sagar is possibly the sweetest person I have ever had the fortune of meeting. She is so understanding and empathetic; I loved attending her class every day. Her assignments are fair and she is more than willing to go through your essay with you prior to turning it in. 100% would recommend her class!!!

She will tell you that she gives pop quizzes, but she almost always announces them ahead of time. The papers are intense, but they are all relevant to what is discussed in class, which make them a lot easier to write. Professor Sagar was by far my kindest and favorite professor this semester, and I wish she could teach all of my classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The vibes in Sagar's classroom are immaculate. If you show up having read the text, comment and think deeply about the experience of reading and expand on other ideas shared, she'll love having you in class just as much as you love having her as a professor. I'm used to being the one English nerd, but I don't feel like I'm alone in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr Sagar is AMAZING. Fantastic prof. I asked her for a letter of rec and she wrote me an absolute glowing masterpiece LOL. She loves having class discussions so as long as you keep up with class readings, you are good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you like talking about literature, take any of her literature classes. This is my second course with her and she is fantastic at facilitating conversation.

Had her for Labor and Literature. An amazing facilitator. Very kind and caring. Truly a good human-being: literature as empathetic practice. My only issue is that, sometimes the class felt too student-led; discussions sometimes devolved into reactive testimonials over history, theory, and analysis. Still, very therapeutic!

Prof Sagar is amazing. After 30 yrs in the US she barely has an accent. She is VERY approachable, knowledgeable and understanding. She expects the best from her higher level classes and will do what she can to support you. She is a lovely individual and I wish I could say at Purdue just to take more classes from her!

I really enjoyed taking a class with her. She is awesome! She makes even the most boring topic seem interesting. Her English is not hard to understand at all and she is always willing to help and is very understanding if you have a problem.

She is awesome! She makes even the most boring topic seem interesting. Her English is not hard to understand at all and she is always willing to help and is very understanding if you have a problem. I really enjoyed taking a class with her.

She is an excellent teacher and makes an effort to keep students interested. However, I find her grading very harsh!(We needed an impossible 98 on 100 to get an A+) If you enjoy a challenge, I would recommend her classes for it is most definitely NOT an easy 'A'.

She is highly committed to her classes and her reading selections are brilliant.  Being white, or straight, or gay, or whatever, does NOT exlude anyone from her classes.   Purdue is lucky to have her teaching here.
wonderful class, wonderful books, i learned how to write papers and make a five page paper out of one symbol.
A complete joke, even when you can understand her.  Total lightweight.

I really liked the readings, and she was very nice; very helpful.  If you feel that being white and middle-class makes you feel left out, then it's only because of the subject matter, not because she tries to exclude anyone.  (So she teaches one of the required, "Be nice to women and minorities" classes - that's really not her fault).
I often felt like being white, heterosexual and middle-classes disqulaified me from being able to participate in class discussion.
reading material didn't make sense.
This prof is AMAZING. Really thought provoking. Demands high levels of thinking. Changed the way I look at the world!
The class didn't make much sense and the readings were terrible.  This was just a waste of time.
She is a great mentor and supervisor. She's straightforward and offers good constructive comments all the time. I would highly recommend her as an adviser and teacher.

This professor can be disorganized, but is incredibly intelligent, helpful, energetic about the material, and a joy to work with. Thanks to her, I worked twice as hard as other MA students I knew, but the final result was worth it. Thanks April!!

This class was very informative.  It had excellent coverage and a good pace.  I would recommend it for anyone who is interested in any type of language testing - including writing exams for your own classes.
No Comments
Best professor at purdue

Amanda Manning is the best instructor I have had at Purdue. Her lectures are so straightforward, and her teaching style is amazing. She genuinely cared about each and every student and took the time to learn everyone's name. Office hours are helpful if you're ever struggling. If you can take her section, I highly recommend it!!

Amanda is so wonderful and full of energy even at 7:30 AM. If you have the chance definitely switch into her section. I hated math in high school but I actually felt like I understood it bc she explained it so well. She absolutely cares about her students success and I truly loved taking her class.
She is a really great math professor and explains the lessons in a super understandable way. Everything learned in class is directly translatable to the exams which is helpful.

She's incredibly caring. I switched to her class, and I don't regret it. She's very caring and passionate about her subject. She always has great enthusiasm. As someone who struggled with math, she made things very understandable.

Amanda Manning was an excellent professor who was truly passionate about what she taught. She genuinely cared about her students, their performance, and was always available to help. Although attendance is mandatory, each class is only worth 2 points, and she drops the lowest three.

Amanda Manning is an awesome teacher! It is obvious that she is passionate about everyone succeeding. Amanda truly cares about her students and also the class. I appreciated how well she taught the material; it was very easy to understand. At any point if you struggle or can't find your mistake on an assignment, go to office hours!

The attendance points dont really matter cause theyre 2/2, but if youre not good at math and dont go to class often you will be behind. The tests are 12 multiple choice worth 8 pts each so you gotta lock in. Make sure to do good on the first exam so you dont dig a hole for yourself right away (thats what I did). Also try not to cheat on homework.
Professor Manning is one of the best professors I have had. She truly cares about each and every student. Her teaching style is amazing and she makes Calculus so much fun.
caring and considerate professor, will try her hardest to make sure everyone does well

Seriously nice, and really focused on making learning more manageable for everyone. I learn really slow, and had previously failed the course with a different teacher, but I communicated my needs for a more personable environment, and she went above and beyond. Seriously, I should have bought her an Edible Arrangements for helping me pass the class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amanda was the best instructor I have ever had. I had her for MA16010 in Spring 2025 and she was present and caring for each student 100% of the time. We had a small class so it was easier, but she explains concepts perfectly. Go to office hours!!! She is super kind as well, so just show up and do not be afraid to ask for help.

I had her for MA 158 and she was really good. She is very good at keeping the class engaged and has very good lectures that are never boring. She genuinely cares for her students and wants them all to do good.

Best professor ever -- NO JOKE. I know Purdue is notorious for its difficult calculus courses, but Professor Manning made the course so manageable. Quizzes are very similar to the hw questions, lectures prepare you well for the exams & quizzes, & she is very accessible outside of class for help. Use practice exams & BoilerExams & you'll do amazing!

Prof Reibman is a very nice professor. She may seem intimidating, but she cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Her homework can be tedious, but if you go to office hours, she will walk you through the problems. The exam averages are roughly in the 80's, and she usually targets them to be 75. Def recommend taking her classes.
BEST 302 Professor.
Great command of the material. Exams weren't difficult at all if you understand the material. Best 302 Professor.
Prof. Reibman does a very good job of explaining concepts to students and always adresses students' concerns.
The exams are just written to test what the students don't know, so many content are not in the lecture notes. Will not take again!

Exams were HARD. They were long and each question was challenging. Lectures were fine, but having lecture late in the day was not ideal, especially since she speaks in monotone most of the time. Not a bad professor, but  there are better options out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework was time consuming and a bit tough at times, though exams were fair. The professor had excellent lecture notes, probably the best ones out of any professor I've had. She teaches concepts very well and it's obvious she cares about the subject and our learning.
