Dr. Reibman does care about our progress and grades. She takes appointments regarding content and exam questions if office hours don't work for you, and she repeats it many times in class. Do practice a lot before the exams. The time constraint is a problem.

Overall very good, caring professor. Lectures could sometimes be a little scatterbrained/boring, but they felt like she actually cared about the content. Her homeworks were challenging, but interesting and actually fun to work on for the most part. Exams were very fair, high quality lecture notes posted online, etc. best 301 prof imo

Lectures are average, lecture notes are very clear and nice to study from. Exams are fair in terms of content, but a big time crunch. Although I've mentioned some cons for Reibman, this is by far the professor you want for 301. She seems to care very much about students success and will accommodate new ideas/learning methods students suggest.

Professor Reibman was one of the best professors I have ever had at Purdue University.  As long as you pay attention in class, she gives all the information needed to complete assignments.  Exams are fair, and she is a very caring and considerate person.  If you have the option, take a class with Reibman.

Prof. Reibman is respected, caring, and willing to learn. FR these traits are exceptional, especially for an ECE professor. Professor's willing to explore new ways to teach, and is especially considerate and well informed on making responsible assessments and learning expectations. Must have for 301 or 302
Tough class but great professor. She makes the content easy to understand but the tests are hard.

Reibman is great at teaching. The content is a bit heavy. She gave good notes and helpful practice problems. If you did listen carefully in lectures and went through practice questions, you will succeed in exams. The grading is not tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind professor who knows her stuff about probability and statistics. She provides lots of practice resources and grades very fairly on exams. Definitely take for 302

Professor Reibman was super helpful when I took ECE 302. She is very accessible outside of class and actually cares about her students learning probability. The has a LOT of resources on the course page as well preparing you for the exams and understanding of the principles she teaches. If you put in the work, your grade should be fine.

Dr. Reibman is so awesome. She is a great engaging professor and talks about real worlds examples. Also, she is really great at helping you understand convoluted topics and is very patient (esp. @ office hours... so go). She's so cool.
She teaches what you need and let you know directly what you need in the exam. Her teaching is based on your intuition.

She was a great professor and really cares about what she teaches. She wants you to do well and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. The text book is not really needed in my experience.
She's caring and passionate about what she's doing and has tone of experience
Lecture pretty much everyday but having the slides open would be useful. Also going to class helps with learning the material.

For a 3 credit class this was the easiest thing ever. Her lectures are very monotone and not the most engaging, but it was easy to zone out or do her homework during it and then get the attendance credit. There are no tests or quizzes, only online homework due every week. The labs were very interesting, and the whole class honestly felt fake.

This is probably the easiest class you can ever take in college. It is genuinely impossible to get below a 98 unless you just skip every class. No tests, exams, assignments are graded by participation, and on the homework you can answer as many questions as you want until you have a 100.
Very easy class with good teacher, would take again.

overall not a bad class. lecture attendance is mandatory but the lectures tell you everything you need to know. most of the class is just inquisitives and the lab recitation. only thing that irks me is the way she says potentially.

She is so amazing!!! ANTH 204 was recommended to me because it is a science that is easy to follow, and it is great if you just need the credit. Dr. Veile makes it easy to get her students to achieve.
Easiest class and professor you'll ever take. Great GPA boast. Used her lectures as a study hall. There's 1 group project but it's pretty easy.

Overall she was a very good professor. The material was interesting, but lectures were lengthy and sometimes she was very boring to listen to. The textbook is mandatory because the weekly assessments have questions related to the reading.

Lectures can feel a bit lengthy, but the material is interesting. Often loses her train of thought but generally speaks knowledgeably. Sometimes falls behind on grading but is not a harsh grader. Sometimes jumps between topics or does not emphasize a key point enough, but generally explains material well.

Awesome professor! Everything is very clearly laid out in the syllabus, and it's easy to contact her. Many chances for extra credit. Class was an easy science requirement for my major! Plus she really cares about what she's teaching and makes lectures interesting. Would recommend to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assignments that I did in September did not get graded until the end of November, so it is hard to gauge your grade. Her lectures are vague and hard to follow, and her grading scale is brutally steep. It is nearly impossible to succeed in this class, avoid this teacher and class at all costs.
Dr. Veile seemed like a great teacher, but it was hard to connect with her over the online course. She was super easy to get in contact with, and her lectures were pretty manageable.
I loved this class! I really enjoyed the material covered and she did a great job explaining everything.
Took her for ANTH 204 and she was amazing. Didnt beat around the push and was clear and concise during her lectures. Very interesting and intelligent lecturer. Adapted very well to COVID.

Dr. Veile was the most amazing professor I have had to date. She is extremely knowledgeable about the topics she discusses. Her lecture can get a bit boring especially if it is over something most people do not enjoy however she always tries to keep the conversation going.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I just finished a class with Dr. Veile and I want to take more. We had some of the best discussions I've had since starting Purdue. She knows a lot about anthropology and biology which is a cool combination. She is relaxed in the classroom and supports all her students. Tests are hard but she grades easy, lots of chances to get extra credit too.

I liked this class much more than I thought I would! The professor is really busy and kind of distracted but so smart and helpful and understanding. You talk about controversial things like sex vs gender and racism and human aggression but its from a scientific and culturally sensitive perspective. we had great discussions too.

If you need to a UC science credit, I highly recommend you to take her ANTH 204. It's a free A. She gives out study guides before exams, and those study guides are basically the exam. Also, it doesn't even matter if you fail those exams because she provides tons of extra credit opportunities. I can feel her passion in her lecture. Amazing professor

I recommend this professor and course. She's really organized and up-to-date on the newest science findings. She talks about science history and tells funny stories about the scientists behind the discoveries, which makes class enjoyable. Each chapter has an online quiz that help you prepare for tests, tests are fair and straightforward.

I absolutely loved her! My favorite professor I've had at Purdue. She has had real experience in South America and she loves what she teaches. I would recommend her to anyone that has a general interest in Anthropology.

This is a great intro course. I am a comm major and was dreading the science requirement but professor Veile made it fun. You learn so much about genetics and primates and fossils but its fun and seems relevant to real life. She also has a lot of cool real life experiences as an anthropologist in the field.

Dr. Veile is extremely knowledgeable and her lectures are entertaining. Walks you through challenging material, like all the different fossil species, and always willing to help students out. Great intro course.

Exams and quizzes are fair based on course material. Rewards students with many extra credit opportunities. Lab is kind of a joke but easy points too. Lots of reading if you want to do well on exams but its not difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fair teacher, gave good feedback, and gave points back on exams when she worded questions poorly. Just go to class, pay attention, and you'll be fine. Book is irrelevant. Lectures are boring, but she's extremely knowledgeable and one of the most fair professors I've ever had.
My favorite professor ever. He was very clear during lectures and provided amazing notes. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but was very helpful to go in person.

Professor Varma made me love learning again! I seriously wish every graduate level professor taught as clearly as him. Hard to beat his course content for Structural Stability; it's very well developed, as he's taught this course for a number of years. He does take a while to grade assignments, but he grades fairly. One of Purdue's best professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor and all around great guy. He's really good at explaining difficult concepts and makes you want to come to class!
He explains everything really well and made me want to get up for my 7:30

Hes one of my favorite professors. Explains everything really well and does good examples. Cares about his students' success too! I had an early class with him so its hard to stay awake but its worth it! DONT SKIP!!
Excellent Professor. Explains everything in great detail. Don't sleep in his class. Very helpful and very intelligent. Always comes prepared, great examples, I highly recommend.
No Comments

The assignment's grading rubric is extrme not clear, and the assignment always happened before lecture (you have to finish before learn the knowledge for this homework). When combine these two things, you will find even an AI will did better than you in the assignment. Also the professor will never tell why you lost your points in the feedback.

What a confusing class. Prof David was helpful during office hours but the entire semester-long project and lectures were super confusing from start to finish. She made video projects due the day after we get back from spring break. Communication was awful and grading system is weird, with everything pass-fail. Not hard, but strange - just be aware

Do not take this class. I have been confused the whole semester. Her lectures are dry and not helpful. Very little content and wants you to do a project with Pepsico where she hands out  Word and Excel documents to do it all by yourself basically. Avoid this class. If this is required for your major, good luck.

The structure of this class was not good. She kept students running simulation for almost a month without summarizing the takeaways from the simulation itself. In fact, I did not learn anything from this class at all. So, if you are in the process of considering to take this course, please think wisely.

The farther away from her the better. I didn't learn anything from her. She only reads PowerPoint and does not give grades or standard answers until the end of the term. The mentor is fine. She didn't even check out our group's initial mistakes until our mentor checked them out before the final presentation.  she's ridiculous.

Amy was helpful and had lots of industry knowledge to apply to lectures and the real world.  There were no exams, and the group projects were interesting.  At times her lectures can be a little dry. but overall a fantastic class and extremely relevant!

There is no textbook. Lectures have very little content. Not much more than the powerpoint slides and sometimes the exercises/quizzes require you to know more than what the lectures teach. What was most annoying to me was the inconsistency in grading. Short answer questions would be scored 0% or 100%, even though the question was subjective
Do not expect too much in her lectures. I have taken 2 of her classes and, to be honest, I feel like I could simply just read the slides at home by myself.......

Probably was not her fault but the design of the course, but the experience was not what I expected. She knows very well her stuff and has solid experience in the field, but probably her teaching methods are not the best.

In this class, you work with PepsiCo in a group of four basically the whole semester. I really enjoyed this project, and Dr. David was great. Her lectures were as a whole really helpful and she gave good feedback as we went along on the projects. You can tell she has a passion for supply chain and her students.

Professor Marconnet is a talented heat transfer professor. Her homeworks are long and at times tedious, but typically written in a way that leads students to the answers. Lectures are well-organized, although I would prefer if she leaned less on written-out equations presented rapid-fire and instead derived them herself at a more reasonable pace.

The class has an unreasonable amount of work and has some of the most challenging homework assignments I've experienced between both my undergraduate and graduate studies. The exams are similar to ME31500, but slightly less challenging. While most classes acknowledge that projects take time and effort, ME50500 doesn't slow down to accommodate.

Professor is a nice person, giving great lectures. There is no doubt you could learn real heat transfer, as well as some essential tools that engineers need. Unavoidably this is a difficult course, hws were super time-assuming, but exams were fair at most of the time. But no worry, she is generous but reasonable at final curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Marconnet seems to be pretty new to teaching. Tries to cram too much material into each lecture/week. Homework assignments were incredibly long. Added a group project to an already overbooked course. Responded well to emails, but was unforgiving and not understanding to conflicts and technical difficulties. Class was unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer, but tries to fit way too much material into an extremely short amount of time. The homeworks take forever. You will have no life if you take this class, burn out, and count yourself lucky to not have your wife divorce you by the end of it. Oh, there's a final project too. You *just* have to invent something completely new.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Marconnet is available outside class, and responds quickly to questions. Her lectures are well done, but cover material very quickly. Her homework assignments are completely unreasonable, often taking 30+ hrs (7-14 days given to complete). She is generally dismissive of concerns raised, and thinks her HW is normal. It isn't. Exams are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Marconnet is great! She genuinely cares about the success of her students and always responded promptly to emailed questions. She has very clear and organized lectures. While I usually hate when professors use ppt for lectures, Marconnet makes it work with easy to follow notes. The homework and exams are challenging, but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely the smartest and sharpest professors in ME.
This is the best lecture I have ever been in my life, Nice ppt files , clear logic, and in depth explanation. Though, a lot of hw, but she just makes it much easier.
Excellent speaker and keeps me engaged. Class is interesting, he doesn't give a crazy amount of work outside of class, exams are fair, and his slides are easy to read.
Cannot understand what he says in lecture and slides are a bit confusing but it's an easy class with online tests.

Steve-O cant get things graded on time-- at all. It took this dude over a month to grade a 2-3 page outline of our research paper when he expected to read and grade everyones 10-12 page final drafts the 5 days of finals week. He needs to learn how to structure this class correctly or he will honestly lose his job. Nice guy though.

His time management is really rough. Lectures never get through what is planned and we were typically behind because of rambling. Grading of papers typically took very long and feedback for it wasnt very helpful. He cares honestly but the class didnt run very smoothly and can be stressful.

Honestly, if you turn something bigger than a lab report in expect at least a month before you get your grade back. And his lectures are just him reading his slideshow that he posts online. And expect to do multiple papers, and projects all at the same time at the end of the class, and him not being helpful when you reach out to him out of class.
Avoid him if you can. He's a professor who dated a PhD student
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lectures. Not really accessible outside of office hours. Standard real analysis content is covered... but demoralizing exams
Material is really tough, but professor explains stuff clearly enough
The course material was incredibly difficult; however, Dr. Petrosyan is very approachable outside of class, and provides insightful comments.

Professor Petrosyan's lectures are enjoyable for advanced mathematics majors.  Yet, if you just breezed by MA 341 (real analysis), the content is very difficult and you will have to invest a sufficient amount of time to complete the homework assignments and perform well on exams.  The final grades were generous.
Gives unbelievably bad exams and class averages are usually 40 or 50. Sends out emails trashing students for not performing. Avoid him at all costs
not very nice :( had poor exam averages and blamed students, very harsh. exams were extremely difficult and took out his frustrations on students over email. would not take class with him ever again

Great professor, his online lectures during covid were great. First exam was easily manageable, but exam 2 and the final were very challenging. Homeworks are useful for learning, and gave his time to make review videos before exams (which were open notes but hard). Last two chapters of the class were very confusing and could be explained better.

This class was really tough, perhaps the hardest I've taken at Purdue. But definitely made me rediscover my love for math and proofs! If you're someone who likes solving puzzles, you'll like Professor Petrosyan because he definitely teaches that way and I find it really engaging.

The material is extremely hard, but intentionally so and his teaching is what makes it doable. He has office hours before each class where he'll give hints and work through related problems. I feel as if Dr. Petrosyan has prepared me for any similarly difficult mathematics I may face in the future. He genuinely believes in all of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Pretty good lecturer but can moved very quickly through the material. Fairly straightforward multiple choice midterms (points only for correct answer, unlike other diff eq profs). Grading is typical for math department. Most of homework is done online Webassign but a portion is handed in weekly in class.
Undoubtedly the best math professor I've had so far at Purdue. He teaches you what you need to know, and he does it well.

Late to class, runs over time, but truly a passionate teacher. You can see him getting excited about class problems that he can probably solve in his sleep. He will run through how to solve things step-by-step. Minor accent, but shouldn't be an issue.

Pros: gave helpful practice problems b4 exams, exams were fair (u shud get @ least 65 if u do ur work, though >85 is difficult 2 get ), friendly. Cons: lazy, only discussed solutions in class (no hard copy), very easy 2 get lost in his class & course cos he's fast, said would drop 1 hw but didn't, pegs B- 2 class average, u have 2 learn urself

He was a really great teacher.  He understood the material well and his quizzes and tests were all based on the homework and examples done in class.  My only complaint was that he was hard to meet up with after class, but that was mostly my fault since I had class during his office hours.

I love this guy. This is the second time i had him(MA271). He is sooo clear with notes, but he moves fast. His tests are not easy, but they are very fair - as in doable. Always bases the examples on the HW, to help you out. Real nice guy. Wants you to learn and get good grades.
It's accelerated Calc III. It's so hard but at least his notes are consistent with the book. He knows what he is doing.

This guy is an awesome teacher. I have never seen an instructor with such clarity of mind. The way he conveys his ideas in a difficult course like MA504 speaks of this guy's potential as a great teacher.
The professor lacks basic understanding of maths and physics overall

ME200 is an incredibly difficult course, but Professor Ardekani teaches the material wonderfully and will answer any question you have very thoroughly and will make sure you understand the material. Couldnt imagine taking this course with any other professor.

Her thermo classes were fun - she has lots of memorable physical demonstrations that help you picture the abstract, but her lecture example problems did not work well for my learning style. She's very good at explaining the theoretical, but I found another prof who better explained his problem-solving approach whose class I ended up going to.

Probably one of the best professor's you will get in the ME department. Loved her lectures. She brings notes to class for everyone - so even if you show up with just a pen you would be perfectly fine. Much better than some of the other professor who teach THERMO here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved her for thermodynamics. She clearly answers your questions and knows a lot about the subject. I definitely passed and actually learned  because of her.
Lacks basics of good teaching: preparation, passion and knowledge. Any takeaway from this course required self-study on my own.
The worst teacher in my graduate school.  Poor planning for classes and worst teaching experience. Dont take this course and read from the textbook. Just a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: At first,  she was really hard to understand because of her accent and the way she talked was kind of monotone. However, stick to going to the lectures and you'll know that they are really helpful and clear. She is also willing to help if she notices that you put in the work. Great teacher.
Best professor you could have to pass Thermodynamics.

(engl 223) He is a very difficult professor, he assigns a lot of books. When it's time for lecture attendance isn't for a grade, and he barley talks about the books we read; he tends to ramble. He does grades based on two essays and a mid term and he harshly grades them. All essays are 7 pages long, but sometimes he will say it's too short.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
[eng223]
most important thing is that he teaches how to THINK DEEPLY ABOUT THE WORLD, not the books. yes he rambles- about the THEMES in the text (which is what he cares about in papers! trust i got A+ on all). he's lenient if you ask for an extension, and graded fairly even when he disagreed with my viewpoint. the class is difficult but he's not.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a good person, but not a good professor. He spends the whole class rambling about things that have nothing to do with what we are learning and never asks questions. He doesn't give a rubric for papers so you have no idea what you are doing but then grades them hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took 223 and all I learned was from reading the books. He tends to ramble lecture and repeat himself. Only ever studied one viewpoint of a topic and he rarely asks questions. Offers extra credit all-or-nothing for attendance. 3 grades. Very interesting man but this causes a lot of namedropping. I'd look elsewhere unless you need his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took ENGL230. Class overall was great, very easy in general. Lectures kind of felt like a waste of time though. Professor is a very interesting man, and I can tell he has had a very interesting and inspirational life. Class time just didn't really teach me anything I didn't already learn just by reading the books.

Lectures are interesting but disorganized, favoring breadth over depth. Often repeats himself, making the same point word-for-word. Minimal class participation. I was familiar with literature so already knew most of what he covered. Essays time-consuming but easy if you start early. Overall: chill class, bit boring, not too hard. Took 223, not 301.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless; he doesn't talk about the novels assigned and only discusses random philosophy. Very smart man, but does not clearly communicate expectations for papers and then is a harsh grader. Overall, terrible class and I regret having switched into it. I took ENGL 223 with him, not 301, but RMP doesn't list that as an option.

Plotnitsky was a nice professor, but his lectures often rambled on and on without any logical connection to course material. I found myself falling far behind in class because the reading is quite heavy in this course. Plotnitsky provides no notes or powerpoints and often goes off track when teaching. It's hard to follow what the class is about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy rambles about the most useless concepts that have NOTHING to do with the books you read. Very disorganized class and is only graded on three assignments. There is no rubric for the essays but he's still a tough grader, so you have no idea what to do on papers. There's one midterm with no clear subjects because again— he doesn't teach.

I am continuously impressed by Professor Plotnitsky's knowledge and rich experiences, but I did not benefit much from his lectures. He tends to ramble. However, I did attend every class because he considers your attendance for slight extra credit of sorts. There are 2 papers about something we've read (you choose the topic) and a take-home midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a smart guy, knows what he's talking about. However, he just doesn't have many things he grades based on. The class had 3 papers... and that was it. It's hard to fail, but it's also hard to get an A. I didn't learn how to do very much, and his lectures ramble. It's hard to teach literature though, especially when it's graded on essay skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is obviously incredibly intelligent. He challenges his students to think in new ways.

Dr. Plotnitsky does NOT lecture in a comprehensive way-- rambles about unrelated things. Does not give in depth information about assigned readings, only his personal thoughts. I understand that literary theory is mostly philosophy, but I couldn't tell you one thing I learned about literary analysis or criticism or theory from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A very easy class. He grading is very kind and generous. Basically as long as you turn everything in you will pass, showing up helps but isn't mandatory. However, I don't think I learned anything in this class.

He is very bright, but it is hard to understand his accent and where he is even going with is lectures. He doesn't allow much discussion and just talks at you with very unclear and sometimes very unrelated topics. If you write well you will get a good grade. I really didn't learn much at all.

He is extremely brilliant but I'm not sure what I learned in the class in regards to English.  He mainly taught philosophy and politics, it was actually kind of annoying.  But if you pay attention and keep up with the reading then you can write good papers.  It is also interesting to hear him lecture because it seems like he knows everything.
Literary theory is more often than not based in philosophy...duh. Plotnitsky knows his stuff and is able to teach it in a way that makes it fun to learn.
He taught me absolutely  nothing. We were supposed to learn about types of literary criticism, but he didn't bother teaching us that.  We spent more time learning philosophy than any literary theory.
No Comments
No Comments

Her lectures and overall demeanor was always entertaining. She is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. While there are occasional pop quizzes, as long as you stay on pace with the schedule, you will be fine. There is a lot of reading, especially towards the later half of the semester but it's an English class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She makes English literature engaging. Exams and quizzes are super easy if you do the reading and show up to lecture. Her essay assignments are extremely clear with what is wanted, and she gives you prompts or you can use your own. This is without a doubt the best non-STEM professor I've ever had at Purdue!

I love Professor Armstrong! One of the best teachers I've had at Purdue. She cares about her students and really wants them to do well. She's always available to help with class assignments. As long as you put forth your best effort in the readings and writing, you should be fine. She's a very cool, down to earth person. Take a class with her!
Fantastic class. Would highly recommend this as an elective. The final projects are really cool and Prof. Armstrong is a great teacher.
Treated us like we were becoming experts on the Odyssey, Aeneid, and Beowulf--have never felt so invested in a class before. Changed my whole outlook on life. She is awesome.

I had her course on medieval history.  Really really enjoyed it.  I transferred from Harvard and found it as good as a professor from Oxford I had there.  Also studied French medieval period at Brynn's mast and she really brought everything together to me.  Easy and fair professor.

This re TeachCo on writing. Didn't think it would help my fiction, but was in meeting of day job, people arguing opposing viewpoints.  I was only one who led my argument with validity of my opponent's position. It worked.  Thanks.

Dorsey is possibly the best prof I've had at Purdue! Wish I could have her again but I'm graduating! She makes the information interesting and is obviously an expert in her field! She grades fairly and gives you multiple opportunities to do extra credit papers and there is extra credit on her exams. Take a class with her if you can!!!

Armstong is one of my two favorite professors from my undergrad career. She's a GEM, both as a person and as a professor. She commands respect, but is kinda motherly towards her students. You will learn a lot about medieval lit and history in her class, you'll become an enthusiastic nerd like her, and you'll love it.
dr. armstrong is a fabulous professor!  her lectures are interesting and fun!  the readings for the class, whill sometimes are a lot, are always interesting and fulfuilling.
I love Prof Armstrong!  She was my favorite professor at Purdue University. hands down.

Dorsey Armstrong is extremely enthusiastic about her subject, gives fantastic lectures and always recaps basic concepts to make sure you've got it down. She's a very fair grader and writes helpful comments (very encouraging too) at the end of each paper she grades. Always smiling and friendly. Brilliant at what she does. TAKE A CLASS FROM HER!
Easily the best class I've had in college so far.
Very knowledgeable on medeival England, entertaining and somewhat relaxed.
Anything that she teaches is good. She always has time for her students and grading is fair...don't get behind.

Dr. Armstrong is truly dedicated to her students. She is a fair grader and is always willing to meet with her students in order to help them improve. However, some students are not smart enough to ask her for help. Therefore, they leave her class with a bad attitude as well as a bad grade. She's great, and I highly recommend her classes.

Just not as cool as she thinks she is. I didn't like her or her attitude. Acts holier than thou in a weird way, and it comes out in the grades.  There's this thing she does with her nose, too. You'll see.
She was the best prof I had at Purdue!
I absolutely loved this course when Professor Armstrong taught it.  She is intelligent and always keeps things interesting.  I'm looking forward to taking another course of hers next semester.
No Comments

One of the best profs I've ever had. Very helpful in and out of class. Had a Medieval feast instaed of a final. It was great fun and the research done for it helped me learn a lot. Take a class with her if at all possible!

She ROCKS! She makes the History of the English language fun. She shows videos, is really nice, and her tests are easy. Not to mention that she is always available to help you and is totally flexible. If you can take her classes!

Awesome Prof! Knows her stuff and explains difficult subject matter into simple terms - painless class for the complexity. Extremely helpful one on one and in clss, always has time for every student. Take this class!
She was the best prof I had at Purdue!
I really liked her teaching. She really knew her material and helped us understand it
Best professor I've had at Purdue

Would face the board, writing most of class, would have to speak out because he'd never see your hand raised. Never put any exams or in class quizzes in the gradebook. Seemed very nonchalant and didn't really care. Way too many proofs too

Do not take if you want to learn. He'd avoid answering questions (very small class) and would be annoyed when he did answer them. He ended early every day, and when a student would stay "after" (class time not yet officially over) to ask something, he'd act like he was being forced to help. Gave very little notice, if any, for important things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very smart and knowledgable professor, lectures are optional but very helpful for solving homework and exam problems. Writing on blackboard can be hard to follow sometimes but lecture notes are uploaded.

Professor Arapura simply did not care about this class. He once wrote a theorem by saying "the new method is the same as the old method". If you want an interesting math class, do not take a class with Arapura. If you want an easy A, I would consider it.

Professor is very smart and has mastery over a seemingly broad range of mathematics. Lectures and course content can be dull but that's expected from a second course in linear algebra anyway. He's fun to talk to. Sometimes I wish he challenged us more.

He's a brutal grader. I took MA 362 with him at Purdue, and as a math major, it's a core requirement. Memorizing lectures and redoing homework isn't enough for the midterms. Homework is straightforward, but his midterms have questions you couldn't have prepared for anywhere.

Comes to class late and seems super bored all the time. Lectures are all over the place and does not teach to the homework at all. Writes very sloppily and goes on lots of tangents. Did not learn anything from the class.

His lectures are very quiet and need to listen carefully. The writing on the blackboard was chaotically unreadable. The lecture note given is not the same as what was taught in the class. It is clearly a simple concept that he has to introduce a bunch of things before he starts to talk about it. Sometimes he will be late for class.

Hands down the best math Professor at Purdue. The lectures were very thorough and the exams were fair and doable, if you paid attention in class. He is very accommodating and a lot more approachable than other faculty in the math department. Really glad I had him for MA 511.

NEVER EVER EVER EVER walk out of his class in the middle of a lecture. He has a very particular set of skills, skills that he has acquired over a very long career. Skills that make people leaving his class a nightmare. If you leave his class, it will be the end of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He frequently comes to class late, but teaches decently. He appears bored to death by what he teaches, nonetheless explains clear enough. He doesn't use any textbook, rather his notes that he posts online.

Donu was clearly bored through the whole of the semester, and was routinely late (even though he taught the class before us, in the same room!).  There was a lot of homework, which took time but wasn't challenging, - I think most of the class got an A. Be prepared to present homework solutions, and class attendance is mandatory. Tedious, but easy

Doesn't teach to the homework at all. Usually unprepared for class, just kinda looks at the syllabus and wings it. Was consistently a week or two behind the online homework, so you had to learn on your own in order to do homework. Exaggerates the difficulty of everything...never as hard as he says
He claims he's going to make the class really hard - he doesn't.  We went so slowly that we never got past the review of MA 351.  I learned almost nothing from his class.

Course is a lot of work, but taught well. Average week is: lectures, homework, quiz AND MATLAB project. There are 4 "Live Quizzes" during the semester that are essentially mini tests. I felt this class took time away from others to do well. Prof is always available and gives 2 attempts on hwks and quizzes. Review MATLAB and Lin Alg prior to course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This prof gives SO much work it is never ending. Definitely a class you have to stay engaged with or it's a steep hill to catch back up. Felt like grading was on a pendulum between very lenient and very strict. His lectures weren't the best but not terrible. Definitely needed the curve at the end. He is very accessible outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from Dr. Prakash.

Lectures were good because he did lots of practice problems but bad because he explained a lot conceptually which confused me was at 7:30am. The labs were good and made more sense. Homework was graded on participation which was great. Tests were a struggle, but if your final was higher, one exam was dropped. Extra credit for going to class.

Prakash is approachable, kind, and explains topics thoroughly. If you have trouble deriving expressions symbolically, you may struggle in lectures, but he does lots of examples. HW is graded on effort, exams are hard but have lots of partial credit, and extra credit for attending lectures. Overall, would recommend Prakash.

He is a good professor, but his teaching style really made things too complicated. Despite investing twice as much time as other courses into completing various assignments and quizzes, you may find that your grades do not reflect the effort you have put in. I think AAE 558 (FE Methods Aerospace Structures) is more helpful than this course.

He's a fantastic professor but the coursework is extreme. In terms of difficulty, the homework gets progressively difficult despite having 2 parts for the homework. On a scale of 5 for difficulty he definitely is a 7.5.

Dr. Prakash is one of the best professors if not the best in his field. The assignments and projects might seem a little tedious but the course overall is perfect to learn and understand right from the basics. The only advice I would give you is to avoid slacking off and you can get an excellent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Prakash sets clear expectations every week with homework and labs for this class (and all his other classes). Lecture style is consistent and clear. Just pay attention in class and take good notes. Go to his office hours and his TA's office hours and you'll be fine. This is true for pretty much every undergraduate class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was overall less difficult than CE570 in my opinion since it was more application-based rather than theory based. The theory from CE570 is absolutely necessary here, but the course is more coding-based. MATLAB haters beware. You will be coding every week applying these finite-element principles. Great and tough class, I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I've had multiple classes with Dr. Prakash at my time here at Purdue. He is a really good lecturer and clearly a genius in his field. This class was the hardest I've ever taken from him. This was due partially due to his teaching style, but also due to the content of the course. To really learn this stuff, it requires hard work and time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terribly difficult to understand the material well from the way this course is taught. Pace of the course is wicked fast. Be ready to learn material immediately after it is presented (two pop quizzes after watching lectures). Good examples are not given in class or in notes. Best chance to do well is to go to office hours a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have had in my 5 years at Purdue. We have 3 lectures with quizzes to watch online before coming to actual lecture, where there are more quizzes. That would not be too bad except the class average is consistently less than 25% on these quizzes. It is impossible to please him and no one knows what is going on in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For structures II, lecture handouts in class are shrunk down to save paper. There are three "quizzes" that are basically exams. They're pretty difficult because you run out of time  and don't have time to go over your problems. I personally bombed a non-difficult final because it was my 5th one and was tired but got a B+. He curves a little.
Decently hard class, but he does a great job explaing concepts. Shows lots of examples which help on homework. Would take a class from him again

Dr. Prakash takes a very rigorous approach to Statics. He explains in depth and assigns the most difficult problems. You really learn the material (and if not, you won't do too well...). He is exceptionally helpful, not only offering regular office hours but also in the semester I took the class, regular review sessions. Inspiring, great prof!

He's a good guy, his lectures are straight forward as are his exams.  That said, the homework takes forever and they're only worth 20% of your grade. Go to his class since he has "in class activities" that can be worth up to 5% extra credit.
Hard class, homework due every lecture that takes a long time to do, but he pretty much stays in his office all day and is available to answer q's. Very helpful.

The concepts of this course aren't extremely difficult, but he finds a way to make Statics extremely tedious. Assigns nightly homework that can take up to 6 hours, which means late, late nights finishing one assignment. Not the worst teacher, but he has difficulty understanding what the students are capable of doing.  Be ready for lots of work!

She really cares about her students, as long as you complete the labs on time and keep up on homework you will be fine. She keeps lectures interesting with real world examples, and offers extra lab time to anyone who needs it at the end of the semester.

Her lecture material is not super engaging but she tries to make it interesting by passing around real examples, quite helpful to keep you locked in. She cares about what she's teaching and is understanding and reasonable. Good in lab and you can tell she really knows what she is talking about. Tests are hard but manageable.

she does not care about this class at all. she frequently cancels classes and I'm 90% certain she doesn't even look at the assignments she grades. She brags about her industry experience despite the fact she's had very little and often teaches wrong information. She will not correct her mistakes

The professor is horrible about communicating to students when classes are canceled. I've had multiple occasions where I commute 30 minutes to class, just to see that she canceled lecture or moved it to webex 30 minutes before class starts. Beware of going to class just to see an email saying that class is canceled after you have already arrived.
Professor Habig is great. I would love to have her as a professor again.

Professor Habig was a great professor that really cared about her students. She made personal connections and made sure to check in with students on their progress often. The class did demand a lot, but she presented it in a way that was approachable and offered solutions. Labs were fun!

She's a really great professor. I think that she does a great job demonstrating how to do the projects for the lab and her textbook for lecture is super helpful. She clearly loves what she does and I would absolutely take her class again.
Very interesting class. I really enjoyed the professor too. A few midterms and quizzes as well as an in person essay at the end. Highly recommend
Absolutely despised this class. Do not take it if you have a choice! By far the worst class I have ver been in, professor sucks and so does the structure of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a bit bland, it's just material but he does a good job of explaining content. I'd highly recommend going to lecture, there are no videos posted and it's easier than reading the slides from home. Read the textbook too!! I found that to be a great resource.

Very intimidating at first but super friendly and funny professor. Lectures can get boring but he is always very excited to answer questions and have discussions. The readings are super dry but all the exams and quizzes are 3 open-ended questions straight off the reading guides. So long as you read the slides and books, you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a pretty enthusiastic Professor who really enjoys talking about the texts covered in SCLA 101. As long as you do the reading and answer the prompt you're guaranteed at least a B. Purely graded on how well you answer the prompt and not on writing skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. De La Fuente is an amazing lecturing and is very nice. If you you read the material and pay attention to key themes you will succeed.

I recommend taking his classes to anyone! You can tell he truly cares about his students and teaching. He's always enthusiastic to answer questions and discuss topics and makes lessons fun and interesting. As long as you show up and read the books, you will do fine.
What a great professor! Makes each student feel valued, and does a great job explaining material. Gives a lot of great ideas for the very few writing assignments he gives. Please take this class.
A really good teacher, and the class was very interesting.

He is a wonderful Professor. Very kind and strives to make sure you understand the point he is trying to make. Loved this class and this Professor. If you attend and participate, you should get an A. Would definitely take another of his classes.

There is a lot of reading to do for this class, but do it because class consists of a quiz and discussion! Points are given for participation in discussions, so doing the reading is a must. You can tell he is passionate and knowledgeable of the reading materials! He is very respectable and understanding, and guides class discussions very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take 211 if you have an interest in soccer or what to expand your knowledge of how soccer and world history fit together. The prof knows what he's talking about. If you understand his overarching concepts and ideas of the lectures, you'll do fine on the exams, which are all essays.

He only graded us out of 4 tests, but the tests were based almost 90% of his lecture. Only two questions in total were not covered in lecture.   He covers the readings during the lecture very well. His lectures are long and boring, but you can usually use him as an audio book and focus on something else.

My favorite professor that I've had yet. We do read a lot but other than that only one presentation for homework all semester. Tries to put humor into lectures which keeps them entertaining. He is a very good lecturer and genuinely believes in his students and their abilities as long as you try in the class you'll be fine and learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lectures can be a bit boring, but he really does try to make them interesting. Overall, he's a very lovely guy who is always willing to help his students whenever they need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures can be VERY boring. Nice Professor. His accent takes some time to get used to. Take this class if you LOVE history. Don't take it if you don't like learning history and reading a lot. Sleeping in class for one minute  miss a decade of history. Wash your face or drink some caffeine, you'll need it in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: AMAZING! He is such and open-minded guy who loves his job, and made history lectures as interesting as he could. It is a lecture heavy class with essay exams, so you never knew exactly what to study. This being said, grading was fair as long as there was some thought and intelligence in your writing. Take his classes just so you can meet him!

Loved this instructor. Funny, engaging, clear, and makes you think about history in a whole new way. Reading assignments weren't long, but reading the textbook was not required to pass tests (except for the sources part). Multiple-choice quizzes, essay-based exams (both of which were not difficult). Overall, wonderful class. Would take again.
Loved this professor. I hate history but he made it interesting. His accent isn't hard to get through. He's a great guy! I strongly recommend him, especially if history is not your strong suit.

He is from Argentina and has an accent so sometimes it's hard to understand.  Most of the time he explains as clearly as possible and is very helpful this more than makes up for difficulties with the accent.  He is very passionate about history and you can't help but feel a little bit too because of him. Questions on the test are broad.
His lectures are informative, interesting, and eloquent. As a professor he is very helpful and funny. One of a kind teacher. Definitely recommend.

Most stuffs are easy and fun other than the quiz, but quizzes take up to 20%. So it looks like an easy A, but if you really want an A, do the reading, carefully! The professor is full of passion since he is a huge fan of soccer and barca, and don't worry if you are not, the lecture is AMAZING, and he is hilarious.

So I took Survey of Global History (HIST 105) and he led this class. He put up lecture slides for each class. He requires reading from the books but usually the slides cover what would be on the test and quizzes (about 10 quizzes per semester). No homework but you should seriously read the required book to understand what you're learning in depth.
He is a nice guy who is interested in the material. If you go to class and pay attention you should be able to get a good grade. If you like history you will enjoy the class.

Neat class!  I took a power hour, so lecture could get monotonous sometimes, but it was clear the professor enjoyed what he was teaching and he often made it interesting. Class wasn't too difficult, but you have to do well on the tests. Overall, nice funny helpful guy. If you enjoy history, you'll enjoy this class!

This professor changed the topic of the class throughout the semester. He eliminated about 1/3 of the books he listed as required by the end of the semester. The majority of the class ended up being about Argentina (I like Argentina but that was not how it was advertised). His lectures ramble and his quizzes & exams were unpredictable (mildly put).
I Loved this class! I learned a lot of interesting things about latin american history!

Great class. Learned a lot about latin american society. Even though it was at 730 he kept it interesting and was always available if I needed help. Also the books he chose were interesting and gave me a new perspective.
He was nice, clear, and easy.  multiple choice tests, 1 paper, long lectures.
Neat Course on Latin American Hist.  Lots of reading, but enjoyable.
No Comments

Great professor, cares about the subject and is very laid back. The only homework consists of readings which can sometimes be boring but are mostly interesting. There are no tests and your overall grade consists of only a few presentations and assignments + participation which are easy A's if you just do them. Overall very easy class and good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: kllllppppkkkk
Very understanding. Just do the reflections, the reading does not matter otherwise. No tests.
I didn't expect to enjoy this class going in as I HATE English, but its actually really enjoyable and she does a great job facilitating class discussion.

I took SCLA101 in the summer and I was really worried about it since I'm bad at English. She gives a lot of work, but if you put in time for it you'll get a good grade. Participation was mandatory, so make sure you speak at least once during each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Purpura is one of my favorite profs Purdue has. I had an incredibly difficult start to the semester and she sat down to make a study plan etc with me and genuinely cared. I took her class as an elective and dont regret it at all. I hope to take another of hers in the future. There arent many assignments, & the class is only out of 100 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Caring

reviews.comment: Shes a religious studies professor that was somehow allowed to teach SCLA in the summer. The books she chose for us to read for the course were all religious in context and she attacks christans relentlessly. She assigned 3 different minimum 5 page essays and a 7 page research paper in a 5 week period.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very average class. Due dates and expectations were hard to understand without asking her about it. She expects you to have read and assumed that the whole class did when that is not the case. Attendance wasn't mandatory but if you don't show up you'll be behind on material.

Very organized in content, but chaotic execution in class. Wants students to do group work every. single. class. Class group work is based on the Utopian model of the expectation that everyone has done the reading, which is usually not true. Other than that, she is caring about students, and is easy to talk to and rely on for guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Had her for SCLA 101 during the summer. She was fair, and always made her expectations clear. Willing to help you if you ask - I brought her one of my essays the day before it was due and she showed me how to get an A on it. Difficult class but getting an A shouldn't be an issue if you work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I got my A+ with sweat, blood and tears. If you don't mind an insane amount of work, she's a good prof to have. Otherwise, stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: SCLA w/ Purpura is easily the hardest class. Not because it's difficult, but it's *a lot a lot* of work. She isn't bad per se, but the class feels way too rushed. I don't feel I learned much because I was overwhelmed with the sheer amount of work. She may love what she does, but I don't think she conveys her enthusiasm for the subject well enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is absolutely wonderful. She is very respectful and knowledgeable of diverse students. She is also an interesting and enthusiastic speaker. You can tell that she loves what she does, and she does her best to break it down. The exams were 10 short answer essays. No multiple choice. So, you really had to know your stuff. Don't take for an easy A.
A great teacher who is passionate about the subject and his students' learning.

Dr. Asunda does a very poor job of conveying what he wants from his students in class. Along with random assignments that did not add anything to the course content, he was continuously instructed on how to use classroom materials by students in the class. Asunda also had a split-second late policy and canceled class often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. The first assignment seems like a lot of work, but he gives you more than enough time to do it. He actually cares about his students, he goes through the effort to learn everyone's names, remembers your comments, and will use what you say as examples. I recommend this course to anyone, even if you do not need it.
Very caring and wants you to succeed, always makes sure you know whats going on in class and will do his best to explain things in a different way

First assignment of the year was to read the entire 300 page textbook and write an entire analysis of it. My analysis was 29 pages long and he decided to give me a 19.5/20 for ONE citation mistake (I probably had 50+ citations in my entire analysis). Can only miss 10 points out of 610 to get an A (what a joke)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found ENGR 131 with Prof Iqbal to be frustrating. The lectures were slow paced, but contained the information needed to succeed in the class. Homework and exams are strictly graded. For Iqbal, in my experience, if you have any issues with your team members not completing assigned team work on time, do not expect any aid or help from Prof Iqbal.

One of the few ENGR132 professors who truly explains concepts well. If you pay attention in class, an A or A- is very achievable. Some exam questions came straight from slides he emphasized. I faced a course-related issue, and he was patient, helpful, and guided me through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great and understanding professor. Had him for ENGR 132 and he was extremely helpful and understanding when I had a bad group for the final group project.

Professor Iqbal was a wonderful class leader. His lessons can tend to run a bit long, but only because he specifies exactly what the course expects. If you listen, you shouldn't struggle very much. The class has clear grading criteria, but the grading is very harsh (one mistake on a test or assignment can easily knock you down 10%).

Assad Iqbal (Sid) is a pleasant lecturer! ENGR 131 is mainly led by the assignments and projects and there's very little teaching to be done, but he is a competent and kind lecturer, who will help you out with any questions you may have. The grading in the ENGR classes is very strict though, so beware of that, but I recommend Sid as your prof.

Iqbal is a wonderful professor. He teaches great information on the basic things you will be doing as an engineer. As long as you pay attention in class, the information is not difficult to understand. Very kind and understanding professor, he gave me an extension on one of our projects. Grading Criteria is clear but tough.

Assad Iqbal gives very entertaining lectures that helped me learn a lot about using different tools that can help solve real-world problems. He posts the slides on brightspce for you to look back on if you need a refresher on how to do things. He does activities that help reinforce important concepts that you need to know for tests

Assad Iqbal was a great professor to have this past semester. His class focuses heavily on group projects which require outside of class meetings. The class is broken into lecture and studio time, and during lecture time he makes sure to engage with the class and get students involved. Grading in this class is very nitpicky if you're not focused.

I didn't like this class, but Prof Odondi was very nice. The class was super easy and didn't require hardly any work outside of class. The class was on class for two hours, but it did not need to be and seemed to drag on.

Asenath Odondi is super sweet!! She takes her time getting to know students and takes the time to check up on everyone! Makes this class as engaging and humorous as it can be! Also bought us snacks which was so nice!

This professor was phenomenal. I went into the year unsure of the class and exited with it being by far my best class. She did a wonderful job at encouraging discussion, critical thinking, and providing a safe and open environment. I would take ANY course she teaches in a heartbeat and felt lucky to experience such an inspirational educator.

This class was amazing, probably my favorite class this semester. Class is mainly based on discussion with your peers as well as online discussions. She is an amazing teacher and made the class a welcoming and safe place to share ones own opinions and feelings.

She creates a strong community in the classroom and is kind to everyone. She got us crumble cookies for the second to last class. She will take the whole time every time but does so because she tries to help he students
Good Professor. Enough said!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a very caring professor and always put us students first. There was definitely a lot of content to go over in this class but she made it very interesting, engaging, and fun. Would 100 % recommend her if you have the option.
I love her! She is so sweet and clearly cares very much about her students! Her class was great and not too difficult.

I did not enjoy this class. There is lots of discussion and it feels like she is dragging the class out to make it take longer. The amount of writing needed is excessive for what we cover. we talk about some good things, but the class feels like a drag.
I took his BMS 233 class, it just isn't listed. Dr. Asem makes his exams unreasonably hard and grades harshly. You need to learn how to study to pass this course.

He is wonderful person! that being said not the best at answering questions. You will have to self teach yourself physiology if you want to actually understand it and do well in future medicine classes.
Dr. Asem is a fantastic teacher. He has the best note sets that really lay out exactly what you need to know. He tests fairly as well. He is kind and caring as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Passionate about Physiology. Knows the material very well and explains it good. A lot of information is covered, but he provides good notes.  Paying attention in class and reading his notes packets cover-to-cover will result in an A on the exams.

There is so much that I have to say but unfortunately, I have to keep it short. This Professor is easily one of the worse professors I've had here. The unfortunate thing is that she is extremely sweet but oh golly is she the most unorganized, unprepared person I have ever interacted with. It makes class a nightmare to be in.

I'm so sorry you cannot take this class with another professor. She is knowledgable but unorganised and cannot communicate directions at all. She gives quizzes with no correct answers, and the students are having to explain what is wrong. She then gives nearly impossible tests and expects them to be easy, even though shes taught nothing
Great professor. Very helpful on projects.

He's really not bad. He's nice but a bit monotone. Participation is not required but highly recommended. Individual assignments weren't hard. Group assignments were a bit too many. Exams were easy, and the review slides included mostly everything. Just go through the review slides, and u will get an avg score on the exam, it's not that hard.

I have Tyler for 505 (not an option in the class menu yet). Many of the slideshows are poorly made, his lectures are dull and confusing, HW is using Excel and completing it helps with nothing else in the class let alone exams, and the only practice for exams are giant FRQ packets not even made for exam studying use, despite the exams being all MC.

Incoherent lectures made going to class a total waste of time. Not sure why this one bothered to become an accounting professor. He has no interest anything other than imposing what little power he has over students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst “professor” I ever had.  Has zero professional experience and a tepid understanding of accounting at best.  Unclear lectures and does not respond to student emails.

Rating him now, as I found out that I have MGMT505 with him next semester. I had him in his first semester teaching. All I have to say is that I am really hoping he's learned from that first go-around, because if it's anything like 305, 505 is going to be harder than I thought.

Tyler is what the average person thinks accountants are like. That works for some, but for most it's pretty difficult to adjust to. He is a new prof, so my expectations weren't high, but between the lectures being optional and unhelpful, and ~90% of the class grade being dependent on a handful of exams, there's a reason why I barely squeaked out.

Professor Atanasov teaches by filling in blanks on a word document, making it impossible to take notes. He claims to be receptive to feedback but gets extremely defensive and unprofessional when such feedback is provided to him. He also does not know the material, and has admitted to not knowing the content until the night before lecture. Awful.
This class was dreadful. The man is teaching for the first time but refuses to take feedback or make any considerations whatsoever.

I really like having a younger professor for once. Homework was pretty simple and went over all the concepts we learned in class. He is sweet. I understand it is his first time teaching and if I was also in his position than I would also make some mistakes. People here are so self entitled and want perfection when they themselves aren't.

Good luck. He is a new professor that thinks he knows what he's doing but he doesn't and he wont take feedback. Average scores on first exams were around 35-40% and he just blames it on us not learning material. His lectures are so boring and monotone. The notes are also very unhelpful most of the time and he goes way too fast on examples in class.
One of the best professors I have had in my academic career. Is very passionate and knowledgeable, but also one of the most humble people I know. It was a pleasure having him as my professor.
Unstructured, unorganised, and weird.

Useless feedback, irrelevant rubrics, meaningless lectures, and bizarre emails are some things present in his classes. I almost failed until I explained how work should be graded, but then I was lectured for pointing something out and made fun of. He's only valuable for his research as the teaching is horrid. Don't take him even if there's no chce
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most helpful class I've taken. Highly recommend!
What a great course!  He is extremely nice and helpful.
This class was very stimulating. It was one of the best classes I have ever taken.
I mean... he teaches a rock and roll class... Does anything else need to be said?
This dude is the best. Take 371

Amazing teacher. Three homework assignments throughout the class that aren't too time-consuming. Three tests require you to write about concepts covered in class which are also not too challenging if you go to class and pay attention. He is also hilarious and very caring. His lectures are worth going to.

I took Hist152 as a student that has had very formal treatment of American history before hand but Dr. Atkinson, through his humorous and passionate "sermons," helped increase my appreciation and love for the subject. Come to class, take notes, connect your ideas, and have fun! Dr. Atkinson takes the effort to get to know his students.

I took HIST 152 as part of Purdue's Early Start program. I could not have asked for a better first class and professor at Purdue.
In high school, history was "This happened... then this..." and so on. Dr. Atkinson emphasized the significance. WHY was this important? His lectures were very entertaining and legible. He is just a genuine, humble guy.

Great professor, hilarious guy. My favorite class I've ever taken at Purdue. While attendance isn't mandatory, you should go to the lectures as you will fall behind if you skip. My only gripe is that there's not many things that are graded, so your grade may fluctuate a lot in the class. The entire class is essay-based so be prepared to write a lot

One of the best faculty members in the history department. Through his lectures you can really tell how passionate he is about history! His TA this semester was great as well, every exam and the paper for the class always had great feedback.

HIST 371 was the best decision I've ever made. Professor Atkinson was absolutely hilarious and charismatic. I seriously wish his classes were twice the length so I could listen to him speak. Make sure to take good notes and read the textbook every now and then and you'll pass perfectly fine. He gives great exam prep! Take this class, you'll love it
Professor Atkinson obviously cares about his students and makes an effort to connect with them, and he also has a great sense of humor.

Take good notes during lectures (which is easy because they're so interesting) and you'll basically know how to most of the classwork without studying. Definitely the best class I've ever taken at Purdue, and it's mostly thanks to Professor Atkinson and his incredible charisma. He makes you wish power hours were longer so you can keep listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Atkinson is God's gift to Purdue. His lectures were really interesting and he is clearly passionate about the subject. There are few grades but if you do the reading and put in a good amount of effort you'll be fine. One of the best classes I've ever taken at Purdue!

Professor was great! Honestly, he was very fun and engaging. The workload was really manageable, but make sure to do the reading reflections because there are so few assignments, they will hurt your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Atkinson is the best! I actually go to his lectures because they are interesting, and he is an amazing lecturer. Exams are easy if you prepare and only three assignments the whole semester.

Professor Atkinson restored my faith in professors at Purdue. I was an FYE student at the time and didn't enjoy any of my professors. Luckily, my SCLA teacher was Prof. Atkinson who had thought-provoking class discussions, added to my understanding of classic literature, and made me enjoy my time in class.

Atkinson is clearly passionate about rock and roll and enjoys lecturing. His dry sense of humor makes every lecture very entertaining. 3 very short writing assignments and 3 essay exams. Possible exam questions provided. Write out answers and memorize them. Morrison left large shoes to fill and Atkinson does an excellent job continuing his legacy.

David is AMAZING. I have never enjoyed lectures more in my life. You have to take GOOD notes, but it's really fun to listen to and therefore easy to remember because it's so fascinating. HOWEVER. The exams are weighted really heavily, so if you're taking this as a gen-ed like I am, take it pass or fail. It makes the class much less stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Atkinson was my favorite Purdue professor. 5 years later he still remembers my name and we swap updates. His lectures are interesting and relatable. Provided the opportunity, I would take every one of his classes.
Great Teacher, Amazing lecturer

Atkinson is extremely knowledgable. He always finds a way to make the material relatable and interesting. I never wanted to miss a class because the lectures were so interesting - plus his dry sense of humor made the lectures that much more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Atkinson can grade difficultly on exams and papers of the few he assigned, but overall he was an excellent professor that made class material interesting and made it so that I wanted to go to class each day. I would definitely take another one of his courses given the chance.

He is an exciting lecture, engaging, and make his class interesting. He proctored class discussions that were actually interesting. The class consisted a two essay exams but there were not difficult even without reading the text books. My favorite aspect is that even after a year and a half, he still remembers my name when I passed him in a hallway

This professor is just not kind to his students. He states he is flexible then refuses to work with students regarding travel plans and trips. Learn how to connect and impact your students positively rather than be controlling and rude.

There was a long list of assigned readings that were not needed. Majority of the people in my course agreed that the text book was not useful nor needed. The professor was very lenient with due dates, meaning you could submit an assignment beyond the date it was due. Others in my course agreed that some major assignments lacked clear guidelines.

I wish he taught all of the courses for Purdue's online MPH program. Great professor and great feedback. He clearly cares about the student actually learning, and I really appreciate this. His expectations are clearly laid out and he is fairly accessible (although he does travel). I HIGHLY recommend taking any course taught by Prof. Hertelendy.

She was very hard grading things that were irrelevant to the course material, such as citations being perfect. She also made attendance points worth 5 instead of the regular 1 surrounding holidays when you might have to miss class, which dropped my grade and I felt like that was unfair. She also gives a lot of homework. Not a fan.

Dr. Atkin was great! I loved the class and the way it was structured! Very organized as you knew what you were going into each week. She was a pretty easy grader as long as you did what you were asked. Textbook was needed for about half the class for weekly comp. quizzes. She incorporates many outside videos that make it more interesting, as well.

While I felt this class was educational, there was way too much homework. Reading assignments were essential if you wanted to do well on the quiz and blog post due at 10 pm Sunday and they would be like 30 pages long on top of another reading assignment or videos/podcasts. Attendance basically mandatory . She is nice but it felt like a power trip.
Easily one of the best professors and lecturers I've ever had. Communicates well, knows his content, and is very caring towards his students.
Great professor with a lot of life and personality. I would recommend him and would definitely have him again.

Best professor I ever had. He made CS381 pretty easy. He explains things intuitively, so if you hate formal proofs, take his class. Homeworks and exams were easy, and he gave great advice and prepared me for any technical interview.

Focuses a lot on theory and proofs, rather than ensuring students understand material, even after repeated requests for more examples. Adds an undue amount of convolution and ambiguity for the sake of 'academic integrity'. Learned much more from external sources than from class materials.

Prof. Atallah cares a lot about his students and makes a constant effort to ensure he is helping them as much as he can, using class time to focus on particularly confusing concepts. He often goes off on tangents, but even these end up being very funny stories and helpful life advice. Don't miss the chance to take a class with him.
Atallah is one of the best professors at Purdue, if he is teaching a class, it is in your best interest to have him as your professor.
Great Professor!
Awesome professor. Make sure to know the slides inside and out, and you will do well. Don't take notes, just listen and read the slides.

*EXCELLENT* professor. great teller of stories and REALLY-REALLY knows his stuff. however, his lecture style is mostly verbal. not very much written on the overhead. you have to be very astute at note-taking to take down what he says
