You can tell he cares a lot about teaching this class.
Very good at explaining, and easy to understand.  Keeps lectures interesting, though has a slight tendency to get side-tracked.
Probably the best professor I've ever had. He does an excellent job of explaining material in a manner that is easy to understand. He keeps lectures interesting, enjoyable, and educational.
LOL
Great instructor!

He was the best prof I've ever had.  Made himself available to students and would explain subjects in multiple ways.  I'm more interested in algorithms than i ever was before.  He gets the teaching awards for a reason!  Generally, the students who didn't like him just didn't seem to want to put the effort into a hard class. Its college not HS!

Despite what other students have said about this course, the professor obviously cares about the course material and is ready to teach it to those who want to learn it. He uses a very hands-on approach, and expects participation, which makes sense in a class like Algorithms. As a non-major, the course gave me a new respect for Computer Science.

As already mentioned, constantly gets sidetracked and tends to talk about papers he's read and written, problems he's worked on, etc. way too much.  Relatively amusing guy and fairly friendly, a poor instructor.  Biggest complaint: he doesn't prepare notes in advance and really makes those who attend class feel like they've wasted their time.

Atallah's exams and homeworks were extremely difficult, but he was extremely helpful outside of class. He was willing to re-explain topics in different ways, and even scheduled additional office hours for anyone who asked. That alone displayed an interest in teaching and a concern that students learn the material that most professors cannot match

One of the best professor I have ever known. I come to love Computer Science because of him. He thinks outside the box. He makes hard problem become easy, by the way he explains, and somehow I see a light in my mind, somehow after he explains, I can totally understand. Plus, my interest in solving problem increases, because of him.

Gets side tracked very easily and expects students to go beyond anything learned in lecture to complete the homeworks.  He may be a very intelligent man but he needs to work on the fact that he's teaching undergrads without any phd's! try to avoid this guy.
He get's angry when you ask him questions that are "trivial" to him but obviously not to us since you're asking him. His exams are balls hard.

Makes everything very difficult to understand.  Thinks everything is 'trivial.'  To him, it is - he wrote a book.  He teaches you a bag of tricks instead of how to solve and learn algorithms.  Does not know how to explain.  Homeworks are extremely hard and graded unfairly.  Tries to make you come up with a new algorithm based on what you learn.
Lectures are interesting but in no way prepare you for homeworks and exams.

makes the material interesting, and presents it in a very clear manner.  He approaches algorithms in a very interesting way.  Instead of just explaining the algorithm and how it works, he goes beyond and attempts to explain the thought process that lead to development of it.  One of the best professor's I've had.
He likes to tell stories a lot, and will change the topic of lecture to suit the students needs.  He's just an awesome prof.
No Comments

Possibly the best professor I had next to Dunsmore.  Brillant guy, funny, actually able to TEACH.  Hw was hard but it was intersting. (better than boring bisy work anyday).  I was much more interesting in crypto after taking his class.

Definitely my favorite CS professor. He knows his material like the back of his hand, and additionally makes it interesting by telling stories related to it. Well, he tells a lot of stories unrelated to the material, too. They usually give a lot of insight on what goes on in the CS dept, though.
Very interactive professor. Very interesting assignemnts and exams. Had to work hard and still enjoyed the class.
No Comments
Great professor. He wins the teaching awards for a reason. He tells amusing stories to keep the material interesting, and this was a computer science course that I actually attended regularly.

Hands down, one of the best and smartest CS professors I've ever had.  He taught everything in plain english and did not go into detail on subjects where it wasn't needed.  If you showed up and paid attention, you more than likely had a good time.
Full time salary, part time teaching. Unprepared. Unorganized. Lots of filler to mask his lack of content preparation.
Best teacher I ever had
All True/False midterm.  Class average = 55%.  Why study when you can guess?
Very interesting teaching style
Just a tough grader that is very strict. Extremely smart guy but expects things that we just flat our never learned before.
Very good. helpfull. clear expelations. nice to see him.

At first, I had a little difficult time understanding Prof. Kulatunga, since his accent was a little different.  After a few weeks, I got use to it and started to really like him and enjoy his class.  I feel that I really learned a lot in class and it was always enjoyable doing some of the things we talk about in lab.
This is definately a class that you can sleep in and still get an A.  This is almost as easy as ECET 107.  If you don't get an A in this class you need to quit ECET and go to Liberal Arts.
so umm ya whats going on in class.  Good luck to all 157 students with this one.

She was amazing. I had her over the summer. If you ever get the chance to be in her class, you take it. Don't ask any questions, don't post a thing on Reddit. Just sign up. She gave good feedback and even when I didn't understand she answered my emails ASAP. She literally allowed me to do an entire project. You just have to get her. Danke.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She is so kind and really cares that her students succeed. As long as you do all of the work, show up to class, and put some effort in, youll get a good grade. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: worst professor ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Clear expectations for every project: you know what you're being graded on. Likes nerdy internet things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prince Attah is an extremely pleasant person to have teaching! A professor can really make or break a class experience and I ended up genuinely wanting to go to class every time. He had just about everything laid out before us before the semester even started. He is sometimes tough critic (which is good) but a very fair grader.

I had his class for AD106 and he was late multiple times, did not very clearly teach concepts (often instead having us watch videos outside of class), and did not return grades in a timely fashion. He also is difficult to consistently reach through email. Though he is a nice person, as a teacher he is not the best.

I had Prince for Intro to Design (105). He was consistently well-prepared to teach class with videos, PowerPoints, detailed project overview handouts, and an archive of past works which he critiqued individually prior to each project. 105 can become very rigorous, but Prince genuinely cared about the success and preserverence of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is overall a good professor and a pretty chill guy. I found the exams to ask a lot of curveball questions that were often buried *deep* in the lecture notes, resulting in some subpar exam scores. He's not the most passionate-seeming, but he does make sure that students understand the material taught in lecture and encourages participation.

Fantastic professor. All of the exam content is clearly covered in his lectures which are easily accessible and the labs are very helpful towards the learning in this course. Just start early on the projects and you will do great.

Nice guy. Midterm was writing code by hand (not bad, I promise), and the final exam was purely conceptual (I took it today). Very clear grading criteria, which is really nice. The class is very "what you see is what you get" in terms of exam quality, so it's really easy to study for it. Not the type of guy to try and trick you with test questions.
Great professor! Puts in effort in his lectures and slides, and explains concepts well.

One of the best professors I have ever met at Purdue. The lectures are very well organized and he explains everything clearly. He also encourages class discussions before giving out solutions. I really learnt a lot and suggest taking this course with him. You won't regret it. The only issue I have is that lecture notes are not shared online.
She is awsome and i would denfintely want to go back to her class.

In order to pass, you MUST attend her lecture class. She is fairly rude. Both her lecture and lab exams are extremely hard because she words the questions very off from the notes in the slides. She reads directly off the slides. She doesn't share the powerpoint so if you missed class it's on you to find someone who'll let you copy their notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She tests on what is taught in lecture but, was not kind/understanding when asked questions about class. Made insensitive statements directed towards students with learning disabilities during first class. During class she spends 5-10 min talking about where students sit/arriving late/leaving early. Only professor I don't highly respect.
She is nice one-on-one, but treats students horribly in lecture. She's very picky and her tests are difficult. The course is fairly easy, but just don't take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Athena Aaaanderson is probably the meanest person in the midwest. I tried saying hi to her and she literally ignored me. She is extremely aloof and unhelpful with all her students, except for her cats. The only way I pulled through her class is that I took AP bio in high school. She mysteriously disappeared this semester, which is a blessing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson definitely had her quirks (esp. w/ people not calling her "doctor") but I think, if you are respectful to her, she is great! She does read from her slides, and does make some inappropriate jokes, but it's a college class, not high school. Exams were tough, but totally doable with flash cards (avoid quizlet). B- in 110, B+ in 111.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lab Practicals are NOT impossible! If you study and memorize everything then you will be fine. I got 136/140 on all 3 of the lab practicals. Make sure you make a good study guide.

I don't know why everyone rated her so badly. She reads directly from her slides that is correct but the class is so easy it doesn't even matter if she does that or not. All her exams are based off her slides so I would just go to class to answer all the iclicker questions and go home and takes notes from BoilerCast and I pass with an easy A.

Easy class, but don't take the class with Athena Anderson. She just reads straight from the lecture slides, and she isn't very professional. She gets offended by little things and she acts a bit immature sometimes. She actually emailed the entire class in all CAPS because she got mad at some student asking question that has been answered before.

Memorize all of her notes and that is all you need to know for the class. She is a communication prof worst nightmare because of her reliance on the powerpoint. Her exams are difficult only because she can't structure her questions decently.

She doesn't have the best format for her online class. I recommend not to take her for BIOL 112 online. We often read 5 chapters with 100+ powerpoint slides. All information MUST be remember in order to pass the exams. She grades terribly on discussion forums as well.

Dr. Anderson is mediocre at best. She tends to go really fast in her lectures, especially at the end. Definitely memorize literally everything in your notes because she will ask really detailed, random questions on the exams. The exams are frustrating because questions are often worded very poorly. Be prepared to put in a lot of work in.

Pay attention in lectures and watch Boilercast if you don't understand something. Be sure to the LearnSmart's in the textbook, even if you don't read the chapters. She gives you nothing to study with, so be sure you know how to take good notes. Don't get on her bad side by goofing around in lecture, she will stop to call you out. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She literally reads the material straight from the power point and does not even explain it and further. She is an awful professor and sadly, I have no choice but to have her again next semester for Bio 111. However, if you put in the effort for this class, you will pass. Anyone who fails it simply does not study for it.

She is the Umbridge in real life! Refuse to provide any learning materials such as past exams and outlines. Because she simply use her original past exam and make no changes even though the question is wrong! A lazy attitude towards her teaching. Worst ever. I dont even wanna give her a 1 ranking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson teaches heavily by lecture. Hardly any homework, and homework is easy, but the exams are very detail-oriented so you have to really pay attention in lecture or on the boiler cast. That being said, Dr. Anderson is not personable, and I have heard horror stories about going to her office hours. I would not take 111 if I didn't have to.

All of the lecture slides are on boiler-cast. 95% of the questions asked on the exam will be specifically covered during a class so to prepare for exams just re-watch the lectures. Extremely boring lectures (but iclickers are graded) and impossible lab practicals. Just show up to labs and recitation and your grade should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Athena is a hard professor. She will go on tangents and then say that it is our fault if we don't get through the slides. However, she will not give you the powerpoints. Her tests concentrate on the details instead of the big picture, which can be difficult if the exam is over a lot of lectures. You will need to study hard to do well.
I like biology, i think that helps.. could be worse
Not bad. Lectures are fast paced, but it just takes getting used to. Dr. Anderson knows what she's talking about. Just don't screw around in lecture... Pay attention.
People are hard on Dr. Anderson. Shes really not bad. Talk to her one on one, sit in the front half of the lecture hall, take good notes, and dont be afraid to ask questions.

She is the worst. She does not even send her students the powerpoints. I have a disability that states that if I request the professor to send me their powerpoint containing notes, they must do it. She refused even after showing her the approved letter from the DRC. This is unacceptable and goes against my rights, showing that she is selfish & rude

She is the worst. Athena Anderson is someone who is not personable whatsoever. Her lectures are very boring and honestly not worth going to. She does not give you the time of day when speaking to her and doesn't seem to even care to try and help you. Avoid her class if you can.

Dr. Anderson is not great. In BIOL110 I could easily skip lecture and focus on what was written on slides, however in BIOL111 it was essential to either go to lecture or watch the BoilerCast. Lab practicals are impossible, no matter how hard you study for them. Lecture exams aren't as bad but include irrelevant  questions.

Athena can't teach. Don't bother going to lectures once you have your 8 attendance days complete because she reads directly off of her slides, which are already on blackboard. She is rude to students, and is therefore very difficult to talk to if you have a problem. The best thing about her is her obsession with cats that she constantly brings up.

This is the second course I've taken with Prof. Anderson. She barely got better from last semester but I seem to be the only one that thinks that. She took away many things from her slides so you do need to be there for the slides to really make sense. I still would not want to take this class from her.

Athena Anderson just doesn't know how to teach.  Her Phd is in ecology which she is mediocre at teach, but everything else is taught poorly.  Nobody goes to her lectures.   And people don't complain about her because the class is hard, because it's not.  It's such an easy A.  Also, her interpersonal skills are sad. She can be very rude.

So I'm sure that Athena is great at Ecology (what her Ph.D. is in) but when it comes to general biology, she just doesn't know how to teach other people the basics. Her lectures are very important when it comes to what is going to be on the tests but if you can, get the exams from last year and you'll be picture perfect. Bad professor, not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For reasons that are beyond me, people tend to give her a bad rep but I honestly thinks she's a great professor. She doesn't go too fast with the material and explains it pretty simply and concisely. She's also pretty chill and caring tbh. Her Powerpoints, iClickers, and lecture recordings are also really helpful. She also gives extra credit.

I think she's a good professor, and I took her again for biol 111. Shes quirky but I think she's funny and smart, especially in ecology. If you aren't prepared to do work on your own don't take the class, but it's far from difficult.

Dr. Anderson  gets a bad rap, but I honestly thought she was a great professor. The course is not difficult if you pay attention to the slides posted online and read the textbook as needed. I would definitely recommend taking her class.

She gets things mixed up in class especially at the beginning of the semester , but not in all the classes. Lecture is kinda boring but is helpful cause she doesn't explain on her lecture slides and it is advised to go to. Once you understand how she teaches and sets questions you will be fine, also the extra credit homework.

Athena was great at teaching ecology. That's it. Besides the 3 seconds she would spend on important slides and the 10 minutes she would spend on unimportant examples, there wasn't enough time in class to actually lecture. All of her tests are based solely on lecture slides and little examples. The final is the same every year though.
reviews.rating_tags: LECTURE HEAVY--TEST HEAVY--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You only have to go to 8 lectures and then after that I never showed up. If you read her lecture slides then you know everything she said in class. She doesn't understand what she is talking about and gives out the wrong information in class a lot of the time anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Athena is hands down the worst teacher I have had. She is supremely lazy and scatter brained to the point of incorrect information and not just distraction.

The first thing you'll notice about Professor Anderson is that she loves cats. She often teaches basic chemical/micro-scale biological concepts wrong and is corrected by students, but she gets into her element during ecology. You need to attend 8 lectures, after which online note-taking should be sufficient. Exams are only over the lectures.

Stands in front of class and reads off slides. Only requires you attend 8 lectures. Says that the tests are based on the readings but really its based off her slides (which are sometimes incorrect). She is a kind person, just not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Just don't.  She knows the material very well, but she is a terrible teacher.  She literally reads off of her slides.  She posts them online so after you get the attendance points you need (attend 8 lectures), you can just read them from the comfort of your room.  I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She has no idea what she is doing and often says inaccurate information, and then she gets mad at the students who try to correct her. She is very disorganized and rude. I only went to class to get my iClicker points then I stopped going. All she does is read her slides. She doesn't explain anything, so you have to read the book to learn anything.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Prof Anderson is quirky and funny at first, but then you realize it's unintentional and she has no idea what she is doing. She teaches some Chemistry at the beginning of the course and has given us completely incorrect information. We've also gotten tests where there are multiple correct answers. She's absolutely ridiculous.
I'd rather watch paint dry than to sit in her classes. Her tests are purely based on PowerPoints though, so she's not that terrible.

Honestly, if you come to lecture, take notes, study, and try (even a little), you can't fail this class. Seriously. Her lectures aren't riveting, but her slides are clear and if you study what's on them, you basically have all the answers to the exam. If you spend more time griping about her than studying, it's a personal problem if you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She isn't a very good teacher, but she tries her best and is passionate about her subject. Her test questions usually have typos and errors, but she throws out a lot questions on tests. Overall, if you study the material it's pretty easy.

Anderson was the worst professor I had ever had. She's not helpful and doesn't teach in lecture. She talks about random things in class unrelated to the topic and makes jokes that aren't even funny. If you have her as a teacher, your life will be miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anderson was the worst professor I had ever had. She's not helpful and doesn't teach in lecture. All she does is read what's on the slides and doesn't explain anything, and her exams are poorly written. She had multiple correct answers on her exams and confuses students. She's rude to her students and doesn't really care about her them. Avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a great teacher. Class was mad easy tho, gave minimal effort, got B+
Unclear knowledge, avoids answering questions, references to syllabus and book about specified questions when asked
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: As a professor she does not cover all the material that is on the test. Unless you're OK getting C's by going off of lecture notes, read the textbook so you can learn the material. While studying, focus on less important topics just as much as tough ones; the exams often focus on the vague topics in lecture rather than the important ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. Being completely disorganized and offering little help during lectures is bad enough, but to be flat-out rude to your students is unacceptable. If you have to take BIO 110, avoid this woman at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nice enough lady, bad professor. Very disorganized. When you ask for help, she never really answers questions and is no help. She knows what she is talking about, but I think she is lacking people skills. It is an information heavy class, so make sure you study for the exams!!!

Ouch. I had her for both BIO 110/111 and she got worse. Easy A if you look at her powerpoints before the exams. But if you want to learn, going to class simply isn't enough. However, put in the hours into reading the textbook and you'll know the material better than she teaches it. Not too impressed by her nonchalant/conversational teaching style.
She just read off her slides in lecture and she was just disorganized. She's not a mean person but the class was pretty easy as long as you read the lecture slides before each exam.

She had absolutely no structure. And the lectures, recitations and labs never matched up together. The homework wasn't helpful and the reading wasn't awful but it definitely takes a good chunk of time to read it all. She gets off track a lot during lecture. Clicker Questions were ridiculous at times especially when it actually counted for points
She is never there to clarify questions and she responds really rude when you go ask her questions. Her lectures are unclear and confusing.

Not as bad as everyone says. She was new last semester, and a lot of people got pissed because she was unorganized. However, it greatly improved over the course of the semester and gave what basically was a freebie final. Not the best, but certainly not the worst.

This was her first year at Purdue but not her first year as a professor. She is very unorganized.  She clearly did not use her own slideshows--which wouldn't be terrible if she reviewed them before lecture. Every slide seemed like a surprise to her. She often didn't know the answer to questions and sent countless emails to correct her mistakes.

Biology is a tree that holds an array of information that is simply not easy to cover in 100 minutes/week. If you want to succeed in this course READ before you attend lectures. Lecture material only provides leaves of information, while the book provides the branches to connect it all together.  Read and you'll find lectures to be enjoyable.

You only have to go to half the lectures to receive full participation credit. There will often be many questions "thrown out" on tests because of oversights. The material is covered randomly. She plans nothing for review sessions so unless you have specific questions it will be the shortest review session you ever attend.

Lectures are online so show up half the time to get iclicker points. Do the homework and extra credit assignment. Show up to lab and recitation. Do the practice questions before practicals/ lecture exams. You'll pass.

Athena doesn't really know what's going on but I used that for my advantage. Only went to the 10 required lectures, other than that, never went to class. Still got an A. Relied on the book and her slides to decipher what material would be on the exams. Lots of resources. Honestly, extremely easy to pass. Relatively easy to ace.

Honestly, the first third of the semester was terrible, but she cleaned it up and isn't too bad anymore. She lost the respect of students within the first 2 weeks, but she has been an extremely easy grader and the lectures are pretty straightforward. Go to class (sometimes), read the book (sometimes) and ride the curve... you will be fine
It is hard to sit in class and listen to her so I stopped going.  If you can, get a file from the previous year's tests because the test questions are pretty much the same.

She does not know what she's talking about until she gets to ecology. The first 2/3 of the semester are terrible. She doesn't take people seriously and the students can't take her seriously. The class is easy if you put time and effort into it, but she doesn't make sense. Very weird and rude to students. Definitely would not take her class again.

The tests are so hard, and Dr. Anderson is the WORST professor I have ever had. I can't even describe how rude she is, and when you email her questions, she refuses to answer and refers you to the syllabus (which doesn't help) The class is awful. Counting down the days till the semester ends.

Tests are very hard. Professor for the most part has no idea what she is talking about. For example, during class she said "sponges are mammals". Very interesting lady, who is unclear about pretty much everything in the course.

There's a lot to learn yeah, but she curves almost all exams and drops questions left and right.  She definitely started the semester rough but she's definitely gotten better now that she's been able to review the material.  She's funny and cracks jokes during lecture.  You've got to ask questions though, otherwise you'll probably be screwed.

SHE IS TERRIBLE. ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. Think you know enough about Bio from High School to get a good enough grade in the intro to bio class? If you have Athena, THINK AGAIN. She doesn't know what she's talking about, and she certainly doesn't know anything about being an educator. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Try to take Chem instead. Way easier.
Doesn't explain anything very well. It is pretty much a self-taught course
It is a worthless class. I wouldn't take it if I didn't have to.

Going to the lectures is absolutely NO HELP. I have learned all the information I need from the book. The only thing I go to lecture for at this point is 1. The I-clicker questions (which she could not figure out how to grade for the longest time) and 2. to watch and see how many questions she answers wrong while the students get riled up. Terrible
Poorly organized.
Absolutely awful. She doesn't seem to really know the material herself, and often gets side-tracked. The class has often had to correct her when she presented inaccurate information.
The absolute worst

By far the worst professor I've had in my college career, expects students to teach the course for her. She clearly doesn't prepare for lectures, it often seems like she's reading her lecture slides for the first time.   Also, don't bother asking her for help, she has an unremarkable gift of answering yes/no questions in the rudest way possible.

By far the worst professor I've had in my college career, expects students to teach the course for her.   Also, don't bother asking her for help, she has an unremarkable gift of answering yes/no questions in the rudest way possible.
Totally disorganized. Didn't even know the information she was presenting to our class.
Has no idea what she's doing

He was very good at responding to emails and answering questions. However, the way the course was set up through brightspace was a bit confusing. Overall, he was a good professor and was very quick to respond to questions.
Ben was my favorite instructor of my entire college career and it wasn't even close. Take his classes.
I'm pretty sure I wouldn't have been hired without my 336 marketing plan. Thanks Ben

mr ben we laughed a lot and I never thought id enjoy an advanced public speaking course. i like your lectures especially your hand gestures and mannerisms or maybe just your hands probably. thank you for them
Bought us breakfast because he forgot to cancel class one day. Cares about your education and will meet with you at any time you want. Very sweet dude.
the marketing plan you helped me build just got me a job. thank you thank you ben
Never in 3 years to date has a professor taken a genuine interest in my education the way ben did. also the neck tattoos just....

Professor Avery is great! His feedback is direct, yet constructive, and despite the class being online, he was very accessible and easy to reach out to. He's very flexible with deadlines too; however, you don't want to exploit that, as it's very easy to fall behind in this class. Definitely recommend.
Ben is so funny and knows his stuff
Ben spent hours of his time --outside of class, going above and beyond to make sure I was understanding the content. TYSM
Ben is an all star. He goes far beyond any of my other professors ever had to make sure we all learned the content. highly effective online instructor. A+++++
Thank you Ben I'll be taking your classes in the future!
Learned more from Ben than anybody else
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Big Ben! I can speak on behalf of all of us...... we loved your class. TY
This is my third year of school and Ben is the first professor I've had that truly cares about his students. Thanks Ben. Also prob the only prof with neck tattoos at Purdue and thats money

Ben has been my favorite in my entire college career. His expertise is incredible and he's so fun. He spends a lot of time to make sure his students learn and you can tell that he loves it. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!
Ben will help you when nobody else will. thank u
Ben is without a doubt my favorite prof this semester. He really knows what he's talking about. The real world experience is awesome to learn about
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Ben is great. You can tell he wants his students to learn and its important to him. Ask him about mini horses
amazing tbh dont change
Ben truly seems to care about his students success and makes class fun. Participate lots to stay on his good side. Id take another class from him if I ever get the chance.

Ben made you earn a good grade but he genuinely cares about his students' success. I would take any and every class from him I can. If you don't want to participate his classes will not be a good fit for you.

Awesome class. Ben made a class i was terrified of fun. He is quite understanding but isn't afraid to call students out. Go to class and stay on his good side. His lecture about how to not screw up college was so rad. For sure take his classes if you have the chance

I would rate this class 3.5 on difficulty. Ben is very relatable and understanding, but don't skip his class and ask for favors he will roast you. If you don't participate you won't be on his good side, but he is an incredible teacher.

Ben was so funny, and we all had a wonderful time in his class. I learned more in his course than I have in any other course my first semester. He is very relatable, and has great content in his presentations. 10/10
Ben was amazing. Lots of laughter and learned a ton. He was my favorite professor my first year.

Profa is one of my favorite professors at Purdue. She obviously cares for all of her students and will support your learning in her class. She is a fair grader and quick to respond to urgent emails. I would take any classes she teaches!

profa nelida is the best professor i've ever had. she is so kind and remembers all of her students by name. she responds to emails fast and is very forgiving with deadlines. if you are taking any 300 level spanish, PICK HER AS YOUR PROF.

I loved Profe. Nelida! She was so kind, caring, and understanding of her students. Similarly, she provided great feedback on assignments and was inspirational/encouraging during her lectures. SPAN 301 underwent many changes, so she was extremely flexible with deadlines. I wish Nelida could be my Spanish professor for the rest of my time at Purdue!
Extremely kind and understanding. Was not especially strict about deadlines, and was flexible when presented with a fair explanation for a missed/incorrect assignment.

Profa. Aubeneau was so kind and understanding. She helped me a lot when I didn't understand what was going on. She does teach the entire course in Spanish and she speaks a little fast, but it's very immersive. Exams are pretty hard but nothing you can't study for.

Loved!!! She has such an enthusiasm that makes learning Spanish so exciting, and she has a kind compassionate heart as well. Grades very fair. Good at resolving issues outside of class. Please participate in class...she gets sad when nobody raises their hand

She is the best! I absolutely loved taking Spanish with her. She clearly cares about the students and cares about us succeeding. She is the best Spanish professor I have had yet at Purdue! If you have the opportunity, take her class!!!

She is so nice and understanding. She just makes the tests unnecessarily difficult. Like, you better know some lecturas and videos that we watched and read in class word for word. And very hw heavy. Hw every mon, wed, and friday's. They go pretty quick tho, some can be difficult but not too bad. She does prepare you well tho.

I love Prof. Aubeneau, she is hands down one of the best spanish professors in the department. I am a spanish major and while I have had other good professors, she is the most caring, funny, and interesting professor I have ever had. She cares about your learning and participation is important, but that goes for any spanish class.

She is so caring and goes out of her way to make sure her students are able to succeed. Her lectures are always fun and she does make you do a lot of talking but you will improve so much. Ive had her for 201 also and I hope I can take another one of her classes in the future. Amazing prof.

Prof. Aubeneau was an amazing teacher when I had her for SPAN30100. She is funny to be around, makes class fun and enjoyable, is highly knowledgable, and she is also compassionate about her students' learning. I would highly recommend Prof. Aubeneau if you are taking any type of Spanish course.
Such a great teacher! Cares for all her students and just wants everyone to succeed in her class. She is also very sweet.
She learned my name. I still don't really know hers to be honest. She is also funny. Basically the best.

I had a great time in Prof. Aubeneau's SPAN 201 class. She makes the entire class engaged in her lectures, she truly cares about each of her student's ability to improve their Spanish, and she is incredibly kind. Definitly take her class if you have the chance.

Overall, a good professor. I enjoyed the class; there was a reasonable amount of work. As she explains in the beginning, the grade is made up of different categories, so if you aren't good at one thing, you can make it up with another.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ricke's class was unnecessarily hard, honestly. Missing small amounts of points on reading exercises and tests could seriously hurt your grade, and she only has two tests (including the final). She offers very little review save for in-class oral lecture, and her powerpoints are super vague, and not very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Worst teaxher I have ever had. Absolutly avoid her at all costs

Hands down, worst ANTH professor at Purdue. She is only focused on her research with German people in Brazil. Expects precise answers to vague questions. No computers allowed, and you'll lose points by having one. I'm an ANTH major and I had to retake this class with someone else, she was that bad. Glad she's only temporary.

Hands down, best Anth professor at Purdue. Although a lot of work is required for students, you will learn the materials.  She makes class interesting and fun. Her office door is always open.  Although she does post powerpoints online, participation is a must. I recommend taking her class and wish Purdue allowed her to each more courses.
I liked the variety of in class activities. The group work  was a great way to interact with my fellow students in class and helped me learn.

Somewhere in our life, we'll meet a teacher that changes our life completely. For me, this teacher is Dr. Ricke. She has changed the way I see the world. Great lecture. Course materials clearly explained even for complicated theories and abstract concepts. How I wish I could take more anthropology classes with her.

Very impractical rules during her lectures. No laptops to take notes or anything like that. She whispers to a lecture hall of 200 students and expects everyone to hear her. Very convoluted lectures that jumped around and made little to no sense. Easy A, but I learned nothing. Complete waste of time.
There are a lot of complainers out there, but Ricke teaches her students to think critically about things. She is extremely intelligent in a broad range of subject areas.

LOOOOOTS of reading, sometimes overwhelming. Very soft spoken and sometimes confuses herself. Sometimes touches on subjects not well versed in - I've taken many psych and soc classes and somethings crossed over but she didn't have correct information at times.  Tough grader on assignments.

Unreasonable course load, does not account that students can have some things to do outside of this course. As a grad student, please do not take this unless you have no research, no other courses, and basically no life outside of this class. The course expects us to spend 1 week on the hws, which I do not understand in what world is reasonable!?

This was the most enjoyable of all the classes I have taken at Purdue as a graduate student. About the two negative reviews: Since the identity of the student who was kicked out by the professor is known, perhaps Purdue should investigate if this student has other behavioral problems that could be potentially disruptive in the future.

This was one of the best classes I have taken at Purdue.  Homeworks were graded not with a numerical score but with the number of attempts it took a student to get the answer right.  The focus was entirely on learning (and enjoying to learn) the fundamental knowledge that underlies computer science and computer engineering.

What we see here is the main problem with RMP. A single disgruntled student can post multiple negative reviews in order to exact revenge on a professor.  As is common with graduate classes, most of the students were foreign born and had no trouble with the professor -- except for this one student who got thrown out because he was mostly absent.

I was in class and I feel this issue could have become much serious. Imagine being forced to drop a class 3 weeks before semester end-> failing to meet visa credit requirement->losing student visa status or getting an unfair F-> failing to graduate on time-> losing job offer. I wouldn't recommend any of his classes to international students.

No clear attendance policy. Told me to drop the class or get an F even though I submitted all the assignments on time with less than 3 weeks till semester ended.  HWs are boring & low standard.

1. Computation, complexity & Formal languages is interesting.
2. I would rather have a computer scientist teach me these topics rather than an engineer.

Lectures are mandatory and have quizzes at the start. He gives quiz tips the night before class. Very passionate, but the "living" textbook he teaches straight from needs to be boiled down into slides. Too much content. He did not cover some important topics for homework because he talked too long during lecture. Exams are heavy on memorization.

This has got to be the most engaging and practically useful class at Purdue.  The professor teaches with a passion that is unusual. The only problem with this class is that it has become too popular for its own good.  Over 250 students in a senior class!  A class so popular is bound to attract marginal students who are looking for easy credits.

Least favorite ECE class. Professor goes over hundreds of pages of material in a lecture. Exams do not test understanding rather more about memorization. Need to use certain words in explanations or do not get points. Do not like how students are picked on in class for not understanding material. Not a constructive learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most engaging and intriguing professor that I have had at Purdue. I get excited to go to his lectures and appreciate being able to learn from such a legend.

Prof. Kak is genuinely one of the best ECE professors. The mandatory attendance policy is kinda strict, but I found that going to his lectures was always well worth my time and I felt like I left with confidence in the material. The lecture notes (that he wrote and had free online for us) were amazing and really useful for the homework and exams.

Prof. Kak is the most knowledgeable ECE prof I've had the pleasure of learning from. He really does make an effort to connect w the students, even in a class of 200+, but attendance policies were a little too harsh, with little forgiveness if you miss attendance quizzes. Little outdated imo. But those actually prep you very well for hws and exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had at Purdue. Very insightful and inspirational. His notes are super simple to understand and yet heavily detailed.

Definitely the most legit professor I've had. Its a lot of work/time consuming but the material is interesting and the prof does a good job during lecture at going over it. If you study the lectures and memorize them then the exams aren't bad.

Good lecturer. Spends a lot of time making sure students understand the material. He gives short attendance quizzes each class covering the material from the previous lecture, but doesn't give much time to finish them. They don't really count toward your final grade, but he gets offended if people don't answer all the questions on them.

Prof focused more on solving the doubts of students (non-ece). Could have focused more on teaching the material rather than just solving the doubts. Felt like there were only 2-3 students in class and he wasted the time of the rest of the students. Encourage students to ask questions during office hours, not in class.
awesome professor. looking back on my college years, he was by far my favorite

This class is popular with ECE students because it helps them get jobs with high-tech companies. A highly knowledgeable professor. Great lectures. Great TAs too. Of the TAs, Constantine Roros was the best.

Given the very large size of this class (I believe 230 students for a senior-level class) and given the pandemic constraints on the exams, this class could not have been taught any better. The lectures were truly outstanding. I got a job at Microsoft through this class.

404 was a very disorganized class. The exams had things barely touched upon in lectures. They were made to take 1 hour but we were given 3. Most students needed all the time. Mistakes in the exams extended them longer and lost many people time. Homework assignments also had bad inputs that clearly hadn't been checked.
The real star of the show was DLStudio. Without DLStudio lending a helping hand every once in a while, I could not have written as much deep learning code as I did for the homework assignments.
Having to show results on the competition-grade COCO dataset made the homework assignments much too challenging and often frustrating. But in the end it was worth it.

Just got my grade. I am over the moon -- since I had to work so hard for this class. During the semester I was often frustrated by the difficulty level of the homeworks. But I learned a great deal in the process. This has got to be one of the most useful courses to take in Purdue Engineering.
Great and passionate Professor, but the disorganization and poor communication takes away from an otherwise fascinating course.
Dr. Kak is an incredible Professor, but the organization and structure of the Deep Learning course leaves much to be desired...
In addition to deep learning, this class will significantly improve your Python coding skills.

This class has the best combination of theory and practice --- probably because it was taught by two highly accomplished professors with different backgrounds, one with a focus on theory and the other with a focus on implementation.

In the middle of the semester, the class seemed a bit disorganized, especially with regard to the coordination between Professor Kak and Professor Bouman, but in the end it all seemed to have worked out. This is the best class I have taken in the grad school at Purdue.
Learned a lot. Great class with a great prof.
Assignments were interesting, but the lack of organization and communication took away from the experience.

I am sure I'll be using Professor Kak's DLStudio for reference implementations for several key aspects of deep-learning programming for a long time to come. I hope he keeps it updated. An excellent class (although very challenging and time consuming).

I liked learning from a professor who can write his own deep learning code that is good enough for public distribution. That is extremely rare in universities and Purdue should be proud of that. Most professors merely regurgitate what they find in a textbook.

At least for the homework part, most deep-learning professors are fond of asking their students to download the famous networks from GitHub and to run them on toy datasets. There's nothing educational about that. Prof. Kak, on the other hand, makes you design the networks from the ground up. Now that IS educational.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I actually enjoyed the difficult programming assignments. They expose you to deep learning Python modules, architectures, algorithms, datasets, research, etc. Prof. Kak's lectures were interesting and I really admire his enthusiasm; he cares about your learning experience. I agree with some of the other reviews that organization wasn't that great.

What made our homework particularly difficult was that we had to show our results on COCO that's well-known as one of the most difficult datasets for deep learning algorithms. Most other professors use toy datasets like CIFAR-10. Although my own code did not work well with COCO, yet it was a great learning experience.

Professor Kak is very passionate and has put substantial effort into this course. The Python assignments, although challenging, are necessary to learn Deep Learning software implementation. Many people were unhappy (and unprepared) for their difficulty. This class could, however, be better organized and communication could also improve.

An amazing class with an outstanding professor. Do not sign up if you are not up for a very challenging class. You do not want to end up like the other students here who have said terribly insulting things about this professor. This class will push you to your limits. If you like challenges, you will learn a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Truly a great class. A great experience learning from a professor who has deep insights in both theory and implementation. It is extremely rare to see a professor who can create his own implementation for a deep learning architecture. Very inspiring! The homework assignments were very tough and time consuming.

This is one of the best graduate courses at Purdue. The professor is passionate about the material and he has created great software modules for teaching the core ideas in Deep Learning. The homework assignments were very challenging and that made several students very angry with him. As for myself, I learned much from the homework.
You're better off reading Ian Goodfellow's book "Deep Learning" than taking this course.

Maybe Professor Kak is an expert in images, but not in deep learning. He really made many ridiculous mistakes when teaching deep learning. Also, we have no way to complain about anything because he and his TA refuse to listen to us. He would only say "drop this class with a "w" in your transcript" if you are not satisfied.

Prof. Kak is a good, knowledgeable professor. Apart from what the previous students have already described, the programming task is GPU-based and not everyone has a strong computer. If you don't have an NVIDIA GPU or you cannot run Cuda on your PC, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! I think "NVIDIA GPU" should be included in the course prerequisite!

I find it extremely rude and disheartening when a Professor's only advice to struggling or concerned students is to "drop my class." This line was repeated several times throughout the semester and really struck the wrong tone with respect to morale and student motivation.

Lectures are useless. TAs are useless. Many students frustrated over lack of communication regarding assignments, expectations, and grading criteria. Some assignments took about a month to return grades. As some of the other reviews say, don't take this class unless you have some knowledge in deep learning already.

Not the most organized course, but this is typical for grad level courses where students are expected to be self-sufficient. Python homeworks aren't terrible, but are built around "teaching" code developed for the class. More time is spent understanding and working around this code.

Don't take Deep Learning unless you have prior experience with the theoretical side of machine learning/deep learning/image processing. Also, proficiency in Python is a must for the programming assignments (worth 50% of the grade). Network with your classmates to solve programming problems because the TAs aren't much help.

BME/ECE 695 Deep Learning is not worth the time. The lectures are split between programming and theory and are largely unrelated (the theory gets far behind the lecture). The programming assignments are less about understanding Deep Learning software engineering and more about navigating through Prof. Kak's custom Python modules.

Overall Prof. Kak is not bad. He focuses on application and he does it well. The one thing I don't like about Prof. Kak is his method of communication. He will write paragraphs upon paragraphs of unnecessarily long sentences where half the words are borrowed from Middle English, but you won't find one sentence in all of that that gets to the point.

He shares the course with Dr. Bouman, with Dr. Kak teaching the programming module. He does an adequate job of explaining the programming elements but nothing extraordinary. It is a good idea to supplement his lectures with online resources for deep learning.

Prof. Kak is very knowledgeable about this subject, but his lectures tend to be code heavy and often skips over theory. He will often go on long tangents about his pet peeves or semi-related topics. Its evident that he is trying to publicize his own work, as many lectures are purely on his past papers or customized libraries.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good Professor, very knowledgeable about the industry. the workload increase thru the semester. you will need TAs help to succeed in the course. lecture is very important to understand the main concept. homeworks takes log time but it is very useful to understand the material in the course.
Unreachable after course. Poor communications with TA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought he really cared about the students, but it became obvious that he didn't when I talked to him after class. Tried emailing him many times but couldn't get past his spam filter. Only had office hours after class and had to have private conversations while other students were listening. Not very accommodating for students who need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boilercast, the streaming system used in the course is poorly and ends sooner than the regular class. The homework is similar to previous classes so people can reference to it. However, sometimes there's some different from previous years, and are usually irrelevant to course content and terribly organized, might be the issue of TA

Its clear he loves the material that he's teaching, as that's also his research area. His lectures have a lot of content but he does a great job breaking them down and making them easy to understand. The TA, Sonali, is incredibly patient and helpful in office hours, and clearly knows what she's doing with the subject.
he notes and lectures are great. I wish we good get feedback quickly on homework and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is an awesome professor. One if the best classes I have ever taken at Purdue. You learn a lot and professor makes even a late afternoon lecture fun.

Professor Kak (he prefers to be called "Avi" by even the undergrads) is one of the best lecturers at Purdue. His lectures are entertaining, the material is interesting, and he spends lots of time updating his lecture notes. Homework in this class is tons of fun, too! This class is generously graded, but attending his lectures are a must to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best undergrad course professors at Purdue. 404 was such an entertaining and interesting class and I learned a lot during his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Purdue. First class I have actually wanted to attend and looked forward to. Every lecture was informative, and kept you actively learning. The homeworks were fun and challenging. This class helped me land an internet security internship. He has a great dynamic with the students, and it was an honor to be taught by him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My favorite part was going through the code examples created by Professor Kak  for computer viruses and worms.  I also loved the professor's Python scripts for attacking computers and networks. This was the best class I have taken at Purdue.

A great thing about this class is that the code that the students are expected to write for homework is often based on the high-quality Python and Perl modules created by Professor Kak himself.  The BitVector module written by the professor is now used all around the world for prototyping hashing algorithms, cryptographic functions, etc.

Remarkable lecturer, and an extremely accomplished researcher. Computer security and systems isn't even his research area and yet he somehow stays up to date with it, not to mention his immense knowledge therein. Most students take his course because of his appeal & status, and they aren't disappointed. Lots of hw & lots of fun. Great assignments.
Wonderful Professor. One of the best lecture environments in college. Covers important Topics and ensures everyone understands before moving ahead.
Best professor in upper level ECE @ Purdue.    If you get a chance to take this class, do it.  You won't regret it!

This course provides very dense look into computer security. The course covers a lot of encryption algorithms and some basic network knowledge. A quiz every class is not graded but counts as your attendance. He explained the core of each material very clear. Best professor I have ever seen!

A great class that teaches you about the vulnerabilities of computer networks and the all the theoretical ideas you need to understand these vulnerabilities.  A great professor --- one of the best I have ever seen!

His multiple "Best Teacher" awards speak for themselves. You will learn faster and better from his programming books than from anything else out there.  His Perl and Python contributions to open source are of great help in computer security and data mining.
Would be better to learn from someone with more experience with real-world applications. He seems to read a lot of programming books, but that won't teach you how to code..

It was a blast to learn computer and network security from this professor.  Professor Kak knows how to keep a class engaged. His sense of humor was of great help in learning what could otherwise be boring stuff.  One of the best classes at Purdue.

Whosoever posted the entry on 3/28/11 should have his head examined.  Kak has not taught 495 in over two years.  The course that he is actually teaching, ECE404, is one of the best courses in engineering at Purdue.
The 3/28 entry is probably by a disgruntled student.  The course that the professor is actually teaching this semester, 404, is chock full of practical knowledge and theoretical foundations.
Kak doesn't have any practical development experience and it shows.

Easily one of the best professors at this university.  May have been a side effect of the smallness of the class, but he was very in tune with the needs and comprehension level of the class.  He is clearly passionate about the material and about teaching, the latter of which is rare these days.

One of the best professors around.  His book on Object-Oriented Programming is one of the best books on the subject.  It is extremely readable, yet it contains everything you'd want to know about OO. You'd be lucky if you get to take a class from this professor.

This guy's a sham. Ever iteracted with him 1-1? Does he take you seriously? He teaches two languages at once because that's what makes the class interesting for him, not because it's what's best for the students.
Best professor I have ever had. If you get the chance to take a class with him, you are quite lucky.

My primary complaint would be with Purdue's program, not Kak himself.  As for Kak, his textbook (that he wrote) is error-ridden, and his entire premise of teaching two languages at once through comparison is flawed, and leads only to confusion.  Other than that, nice guy, O.K. professor.
Has won the best ECE teacher award multiple times - need I say more?

So. Much. Reading.
For a class primarily for engineers / other STEM majors, Dr. Cooper does not hold back on the daily assigned readings. Between 40 - 80 pages of dense, confusing, BORING text. The pop quizzes are pretty tough. He basically expects you to understand/fully comprehend the text before its even discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is very passionate about his field and teaches in an interactive way, making his lectures great. He answers questions well and is fair in evaluating student work. His History of the Nuclear Age course is well organized, but with only 6 assignments (including exams) and no curve, get ready to write some near perfect essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper really pushed the students in this course to produce intellectually rigorous papers, and while the readings were really dense they were also really interesting and intentionally chosen. He was very engaging in lecture. Would recommend for students who want to take a writing heavy and critical thinking course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very organized and has a sense of humor. However, he does not seem to be very caring about his students and can be a bit egotistical. One time I reached out with a suggestion and he laughed at what I said in a disrespectful way, even though I said something thoughtful. He also seems to grade based on his mood and how much he likes the student.

Doesn't have any care for students.
Asks some questions in a perfunctory manner for the sake of asking.
Course has a lot of reading for a speech-related class.
Readings would never be read outside of class (boring, depressing). 
Grading rubric is nonspecific.
He literally can grade you according to his feeling that day or about you, which he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a fantastic speaker and structures his classes really thoughtfully. He has a real passion for what he teaches and genuinely wants everyone in his class to learn and do well. He's also very easy to communicate with and willing to work with you through any issues that you might have in or outside of class.

One of my favorite professors. Interesting lectures. Readings for class are really long but they're in place for homework. You don't have to do the readings to do well in the class. Definitely not an easy history class though requires some studying. Heavily based on writing assignments, but you don't have to be an excellent writer to excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is graded on a couple papers (weights differing), a quiz, midterm, and final. Latter 3 are all straightforward if you've been taking good notes and study up a bit, writing well on papers is more of an art, so use OH. Good professor but hope he gets away from lecture heavy class as it's a bit difficult to study for quizzes/exams.
Very good professor. Show up to class and be willing to participate if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You will do well as long as you put effort in. He has no tolerance for slackers, and those students will be the only ones you see bad reviews from.

Professor Augustin is a witty, dedicated lecturer who captures his class' attention with his sass. The course material is a dull bore at times but he gives great notes in class so regular attendance is recommended. Beware the weekly mini quizzes and writing tasks. He gives out 2 extra credit assignments so this class is an easy A if you work for it

Professor Augustin is an average professor here at Purdue. The course itself is fairly boring unless you are infatuated with philosophy. The readings for this class are all philosophical. Prof. Augustin is a tough grader, make sure to expect explicit notes on why '"this is wrong" on some your returned papers. You will be assigned a short writings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Azar was a really caring knowledgeable prof, let people speak & really listened also saying its important to have contrasting views bc that's how academics learn and grow, talks about race well. Class was organized a little weirdly, but prob bc he cares to cover all the topics and also taught it the first time this sem. No bio hw like other SOC310

His lectures were sometimes boring and the assignments a bit tedious, but he was understanding and laid-back. I didn't find him strict or a tough grader. It seems like the other reviewer might have been offended by the course materials because the AI graphs weren't a major part of the course, and keeping up with quizzes helps.

It is an advanced level gen-ed class I have to take for my ECE diploma. From this perspective, despite I do not fully agree with the concepts taught in this class, it is desirable - professor is kind and respectful; course materials are very easy. Attend the lectures and agree with what they teach (or pretend you do) then it is an easy A.

I think this was the professors first time teaching this course and it showed. Grading was never updated on timely manner. Final exam without any sort of study guide/topics list. Attendance is mandatory and answering discussion questions in class was a big part of the grade.

Most of my gripes aren't actually because of the professor and his lectures but the class itself, and there's only so much he can actually do about that. There's a lot of homework and weekly quizzes that are harder than most midterms. He has fun demos he shows inside of class which make the class more interesting and help you learn.

Many of the gripes I have with the course have nothing to do with Dr. Austin. Overall, he kept lectures interesting with demos + did the occasional unnecessary calculus derivation. If class taken w/ MA261 there is some overlap which is nice. Study Rubello's materials (especially the problem quiz videos and practic exams) + you will be fine.

I had him for ASTR 263 but RMP doesn't have that option. The lectures are pretty dull but the class is a free A. Two easy online quizzes, hard-to-fail slooh quests, and a gimmie final project. The outdoor night observations made this class and they were a good time. I'd still favor Andrew Freed's science credit instead.

Lovely guy, class is pretty tough but he is very caring and super passionate about the subject, he does mess up often while doing practice problems which causes a lot of lost time... overall great guy despite class difficulty.
Boring lecture. Voice is monotone

There are pre lecture videos that you watch to have some understanding before class. He skips over these videos and the hard to understand material in them and teaches the easiest parts so there is lots of material he doesn't explain at all that will be on the tests. The course is not hard but he makes it hard because he doesn't explain material.
He's very dull and gets distracted easily. He focuses on iclicker results really heavily and often does not explain the material very well.
He at least tries to be entertaining but he often gets distracted. Very rarely did I learn what I needed to know for homework from his lectures.
I liked the part where he turned himself into a small insect to demonstrate something
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Austin may not be the best professor but overall he does a pretty good job. His lectures are not the best, but he tries to keep students engaged and explains the content well. Don't expect him to be too helpful outside of class, but compared to some other 172 professors he's a safer pick.
I did not learn a single thing from his lectures. I had to learn everything elsewhere. Only went for the required clicker questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I will start by saying this: compared to other Phys 172 lecturers he is ok. His lectures are extraordinarily boring and sometimes he gets distracted. Very rarely finishes on time.

Dr. Austin is extremely boring and likes to go into in-depth derivations that are completely unnecessary for the class. He relies heavily on lectures, which never correlate to lab or homework. If possible, switch into Dr. Andrew Irrgang's section.

Professor Austin is a very boring lecturer. The only reason people go to his lectures is to receive credit for the IClicker questions that track attendance and are worth points for a grade. Be ready to spend extreme amounts of time on the homework if you haven't taken AP Physics. The best thing you can do is to pay attention to the example problems
This dude sucks
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Austin is an OK lecturer compared to others in the phys department. He is a nice guy, but lectures can be boring. He will not finish the slides so look over them after class. PLEASE complete all assignments like homework, labs, and recitations. IT will save you if you do bad on exams. Asking for help in recitations is very helpful.
Prof. Austin would skip the important slides and mumble through the example problems. If it were not for i-clicker questions I wouldn't have gone to his lectures.

Lectures were AWFUL. Sometimes he wouldn't have time and would just skip the last couple of slides. Explanations in class were not helpful at all. I never learned anything from the mandatory attendance lectures. He's a nice and good guy, but I'm really disappointed in PHYS 172 because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have taken some of my best naps in Professor Austin's lectures. I did not learn a single thing from him all semester, but lecture attendance is mandatory. The homework is way too hard and he is never interested in the lecture content either. If you go to his office hours for help he will explain it just how he did in lecture which was useless.

He goes through lectures slowly when speaking but the slides move very quickly. He likes to skip a lot of slides as well. He loves doing demos in class which are fun, but I don't think I learned anything from the class. also, the sequence of the material makes no sense.

His lectures don't have much correlation to the homework being done for the week. The topics went over in the lecture also don't connect to each other so there is no flow. Austin is a funny guy but will expect you to know a lot information beforehand from other physics classes.

Professor Austin is older and takes his time going through lecture, but if you have taken any AP physics classes it covers these areas again but with their own twist. Not my favorite professor, but you can learn a lot just from showing up and trying to get the key concepts he talks about. Just get through 172, the professor doesn't matter.

This dude can't teach or help anyone and I have no idea why anyone would believe he was qualified to be a professor.  He makes no attempt to see if anyone gets the content or catering to a teaching style that is semi understandable.  If I could give him a 0/5 I would

Since this class is so large, you mainly learn from your TA's. Austin gave good lectures and used many examples. Overall, the class was super straightforward. Highly recommend studying old tests and forming study groups for this class. Homework was easy and relevant to the material. Recitations/labs largely depend on the quality of your TA.
Does not explain content very well. Lectures are very boring and doesnt go through the lectures quickly so he doesn't get through every slide.
One of the hardest parts of his class was not taking notes, but staying awake during his lectures to be able to take notes in the first place.

Professor Austin is a good guy, but his lectures are very monotone and boring. He will frequently not have enough time to go through all the slides during lectures, but will at least post a video online to make up for it. I just wish he would sound more enthusiastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PHYS 172 is a horribly designed class but Prof. Austin tries to make the most out of it.

He seems like a cool guy and I would spend more time learning about the research he did at NASA. However, he just does not seem motivated, 172 may be too low level for him so he lacks the necessary passion to teach this class. But it is important to note that he held office hours and seemed more than willing to help us so part of the blame is on me
Very good professor, anything he doesn't cover in lecture gets posted as a video online. Good lectures, tests are easy to study for but you need to study a lot for a good grade.

Prof. Austin is a great teacher with a clear passion for physics. I came into this class with only a year of non-ap physics during my freshman year of high school, and he is the reason I understand the concepts. Phys172 is a college physics class, so it's going to be hard, but Prof Austin is great.

Most people will say Prof Austin is a nice guy who likes physics, which is true. But holy, the lectures given are an absolutely abysmal. He clearly doesn't make the slides (every phys172 prof uses the same slides), he didn't once finish a lecture, and he sometimes struggles solving the in class questions himself. Nice guy, but the course sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Austin is a nice guy and is clearly trying, but he almost never makes it through all the material in lecture. However, it's important to note that the abysmal curriculum/structure of PHYS 172 isn't his fault (he answers to the course coordinators). Would be a 3 or 4 if he was teaching a half-decent class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The curriculum for PHYS172 is a mess, most of the homework is due days before the concepts are even mentioned. Moreover, a large portion of grades comes from group labs and recitations. Not only have these labs and recitations been so much work that the time given is not enough, a single members work is randomly graded for the entire group.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a really heartless person. very rude and shrew. brags about his research and his mentor all the time. doesn't consider students' time worthy of anything. I got a good grade in his course but this guy has a very sadistic and taunting nature. beware

Everything for the class was taken from a Standford online course. As a result, the homeworks were of very high quality. Lectures were decent. The exams were fully online and way too easy to find the answers on the internet so no one learned as much as they should have.

Lectures are almost entirely useless. Very boring and doesn't go over how to actually solve problems that are on the homework. But he uses all of Stanford CS 221's homework, so it is super easy to cheat. I've learned absolutely nothing from this class and will probably get an A still. I like his personality, but omg this class was terrible.
He tries to be kind.
Lectures are really boring and I struggle to stay awake. He gives Stanford courses' homework without giving the same quality of lectures. Homework is quite long too.

No textbook. Must attend lectures to view new material. Doesn't post class notes online for weeks at a time because he prioritizes punishing students over teaching them. Progresses quickly. Combo'd with  TA's who seemingly have never taught before, resulting in a marathon of pain. Not fun at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Habib is the best! Shocked to see this much hate. Yes his slides are dense but he does a great job at explaining the concepts and tries to make the class interesting. Every time I had a question he was more than happy to help. He seems to really love teaching.

Dude will read off 100 slides in half an hour and be upset when students don't remember much. Lectures make no sense, labs take forever, he clearly lacks a morsel of an idea of what it was like to be a student. If you get him for CE203, good luck.

Professor Habib teaches the photogrammetry part of Geomatics. He is very repetitive and his slides do not have much useful information. The final exam was 90 questions in 90 minutes with calculations that take more than a couple minutes if that gives you any idea on the type of professor. Would not recommend taking a class with him if given option.

Professor Habib's lectures are DENSE, like, hundreds of slides dense. I had him for geomatics though and as long as I followed along with what he was talking about and took notes, I understood pretty much everything. His material is very repetitive but by the end of the class, you should have a really good understanding of what he has taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Habib is an incredibly awful lecturer. He expects students to pick up on material immediately and then criticizes you if you don't.
