He's one of those that makes a huge deal about phones, but can't keep anyone's interest for 2 minutes. Labs are beyond awful. Worst professor I've had at Purdue.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Habib is a very boring lecturer. He covers an huge amount of information in lecture and it is unclear on what is actually important or not. Provides no useful study materials so students have no idea what to expect on the test. Also, weekly labs take at least 8 hours to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand and very boring. Habib is a poor lecturer that gives way too much information. The labs and tests were ridiculously hard and labs took 10 plus hours a week. the tests were difficult to study for. the textbook was very expensive and almost never used. absolutely awful teacher teaching a pointless class. 0/10 change majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's really bad
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: There is no direction in this course. His lectures put half the class to sleep because he looks at the class twice during the hour the lecture because he talks to the white board. Nobody has any clue what is expected or what we are learing. 1/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Irfanoglu is about the best professor you can get for Dynamics. Class is very exam-heavy (75% of grade) but exams were very similar to homework problems and gracious with partial credit. Unlimited attempts for weekly quizzes. Lectures are somewhat boring, consisting mostly of working through practice problems, not a much on the theory behind them.
He is such an intelligent professor to study under, and I would take his classes anytime. He really cares the ones who put hard work.
worthwhile attending

Good professor and very knowledgeable but has some slow lectures. Some classes were just going through two example problems and then leaving. Homeworks were hard, just for participation, but also necessary to learn before the exams. Exams were generally difficult but he said the final grade could override the midterms if it was higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is exceptionally skilled and knowledgeable in his subject and brings various equipment to demonstrate and explain his points. However, his assignments and exams are different from what he teaches and sometimes require us to scavenge through the books and the internet to understand the concepts used in the question. (closed book exam)

He's a kind and caring person who puts a lot of effort into making his lectures as interesting as possible. The homework seems like a lot (especially the corrections) but it helps you study. He gives lots of opportunities to improve your exam grade (he offered to double-count the second midterm grade if you did better on it than the first one).
ridiculously strict on homework policies which adds extra burden to students

He is not the best in lecture, but if you read the book, go to office hours with the TA, and put forth effort on your homework you will be fine. He's super nice, so I definitely recommend speaking with him one on one. Do not use Chegg on the homework- he will find out. Overall, this class is manageable if you stay on top of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He loves teaching and you can tell it from day one. Brings amusing toys to class to explain physics which usually helps. He sometimes gets so engrossed in teaching that he forgets that he is teaching a class and seems almost mumbling but if your frequency matches with his, you will learn a lot. If not, god save you !!!

Irfanoglu is not the most exciting during lecture however speaking to him one on one is definitely the way to go. He'll call you out in class if you are on your phone or sleeping but if you come to lecture and turn in homework he'll generally like you. I did poorly on a midterm but I went to office hours and he worked with me until I fixed my error

Cons  Homework is due at the first minute of class. If you're late even by just five minutes he won't take it. Will call out people who aren't paying attention or look at their phones and say things like you should drop this class occasionally.  Pros  As long as you attempt the homework, you get full points.  Still better than Haikal trust me.

He demands a lot from the students, but fails to show any sympathy for them and is fairly unapproachable. His exams aren't curved, and are very difficult. Gives almost no partial credit either. During his lectures, he fails to outline what he's doing and jumps right into different subjects. You can tell he's smart, but he's a very poor communicator

Awesome, down to earth professor who is very passionate about structural engineering. Hws are past exam problems, due weekly, and are pretty easy. Loves to do example problems in class, and there are additional problem solving sessions with the TA that also help. Super helpful in office hours as well. One of my favorite professors! Go to his class!
Terrible professor. Seems to care about the students, but is not good at teaching Structural Analysis. I went to class always and paid attention, but could never understand what he was doing.
Good class

Yeah I bombed this class because I didn't put in as much effort as I should. But if you go to class and ask for help, he's probably one of the best professors you could ask for. His exams are pretty hard though.

Extremely nice guy. Cares about his students and wants you to learn the material. Exams are always straight forward. Be sure to focus primarily on the homeworks because the exams are pretty similar. Always looked forward to this class.

I had him for Structural Analysis II.  It was the hardest class I took at Purdue.  I did not go to class and when I did I did not pay attention.  However, If you go to his office hours and to the TA and study day and night it isn't impossible.  I don't know how I got an A other than the fact I was in his office 3 times a week.  Great guy though.
He thinks in his head when he does the problem and doesn't write down all the procedures.  So I'm usually confused in class.
I didn't connect with Irfanoglu in class or office hours.  Sorry.

Bad experience.  Buries the class w/ a LOT of impractical busy work, even though he toots practicality. Very confusing in class.  I dont expect to be spoonfed, but he expects you to be masters of calc and differential equations upon stepping in.  His exams are rediculous.  Grading is questionable at best.

Wow, when I look back at how much time I wasted in this class I shudder.  Dr. "I" is a classic smart guy who cant convey ideas to students.  His lesson plans are weak at best.  His assignments are so misguided. I took Dynamics at a different school as an undergrad, and learned so much more from there than from this guy.  Stay away if possible!!!

One of the poorer professors I've had at Purdue.  His teaching style makes simple concepts convoluted.  He doesn't follow the book, nor provide complete notes.  The handouts he does provide are riddled with errors.  Tough to follow the class when you're working with incomplete information.  I didn't get what I could have out of the course.

Nice professor, and very knowledgeable. Helps his students to appreciate the beauty of mathematics. Most bad ratings are from the kids who need all their problems solved on a plate they can memorize to get an A. If one simply does his exam review problems there is no reason one would not score well. Take him, if u don't need spoonfeeding.

Took the class asynchronously over summer. It was pretty chill. The lectures were neat, but you could easily self-study and get a pretty good score on the homework and the exams, which is what I did. I do wish the homeworks had partial credit though.
He clutched up towards the end like 2018 Playoff Lebron. Exams are very similar to review problems, along with a juicy fat curve.

Expects you to know everything from linear, assigns the hardest problems for written homework. Has to be told to move online homework due dates because we did not finish the unit. Does not show up to his own office hours and never responds to emails.
After this class, I have no questions and no doubts. The class is pretty difficult but Maiti explains the concepts well and makes the homework assignments fair.

His homework was not as tough as some professors but the lectures got rather hard to follow. This class is inherently hard but he talks really fast and doesn't exactly explain things the best which makes it a bit harder. His exams are fair but not really similar to practice exams. Just do a lot of practice problems and understand all the topics.

Expects students to memorize everything from a practice exam with a ton of problems that don't even end up being on the exam. Refuses to post solutions to practice problems. Not very helpful with questions about exam, just talks about the solution as if you understand everything completely rather than trying to walk you through it.

Very unresponsive to emails, if you are lucky to get a reply. His office hours are set times and there have been multiple times where he has not even showed up. The practice exams are not a good representative of the actual exam and refuses to post solutions. His in class "exam review" is not very helpful either, instead just gives "hints".

Avoid solving practice problems before exams.
Will not provide solutions to practice problems.
When asked, only drop hints instead of solving problems for students.
Rarely respond to students' emails.
Disappear when we show up to his office hours.
Pick the hardest homework assignments for students. 
Expect students to memorize everything for exams.

Professor Maiti is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable on the material and its applications outside of the classroom. He cares very much about  his students performance and makes an extra effort to make sure his students understand the material. Definitely recommend this professor.
Philip is outstanding. Nice dude, best prof I've ever had. Anyone would be lucky to have him as a teacher.

MGMT 245, he spends his lectures talking about what seems like everything but excel and on certain assignments he told us "I told my TAs to not help on this homework" which leaves you without a support system sometimes. He also took pride in making the class very hard until the first exam average was a 60%.Its a freshman level class not a 500 level

I had him for MGMT245 but it wasn't an option. Baeza is pretty chill, however I do think a lot of us struggled in the class because this course is basically CS-type hard (im not cs tho so dont @ me) but we were lowkey expecting it to be a basic excel course. the first unit is easy but it advances FAST. make sure u pay attention in lectures. lock in

Phillip is horrible. He reads off the slides like a middle schooler doing a presentation for the first time and proceeds to take points off on your project if you do the same. He also goes on random tangents and doesn't teach almost any relevant material to the exams or homework which makes exams extremely difficult. This class is a waste of time.

**MGMT 310** Outstanding professor who cares and wants his students to succeed. The material in this class is super useful in the real world. Lectures are interesting and have I-clickers in almost every class.

I took 310 with Prof. Baeza, he is one of my fav prof at Purdue, yes the class can be challenging but he makes time for you to actually understand the material. If you can, try to get to know him outside of class!!

He is a great professor. He checks all the boxes. He cares about his students and has very reasonable expectations.  This is the most well-thought-out class and probably the best-taught class I have taken at Purdue. The only drawback is that the material leans towards the boring side, but the guest lecturers and prof B's enthusiasm make up for it.

Had him snr year and despite it only being his second-year teaching at Purdue, he was a great professor. Dr. Baeza is a different level of passionate about his studies, he shares his own research but keeps it interesting and quick. One of my favorite professors at Purdue, you can tell he cares and enjoys what he is teaching about. Highly recommend!
He is the goat. Nothing else to say.

Super nice professor, took his class last semester and he was so helpful and willing to accommodate if I ever had any problems with HW/class. Going to class will definitely help you learn the material and do better in the class, I didn't go the first half but did the second and did significantly better. Overall a decent class and great teacher.

Attendance doesn't really matter as long as you understand the homework and are actually completing it. He curved everyone if they completed every single homework to get at least a C even when failing exams. You also get a cheat sheet for each exam.
Professor Baeza is a kind man. You can tell he is very passionate about his subject.

Some students put bad reviews in this semester because they are screwed in class. Yes, professor Ince is very strict on grading and attendance. The material is very hard , but he pushes students to learn concepts behind theories. This was my most favorite class I have taken at Purdue yet while being the most challenging. I really enjoyed this class
Great professor and great class. Some students are whining about this class, because they don't like  being challenged, but rather they want to get easy A and B,   like they get from other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Ince does a good job at challenging us and making sure we only pass the class if we truly understand the material. He presents a lot of information to the class and I have learned way more in this one class than in my entire college career.

This was an extremely difficult class, probably one of the hardest I have ever taken, but it also feels much more fulfilling. Professor Ince is probably, the smartest and the most strict professors I have had but it helped me to learn a lot because of the emphasis on our learning for industry.

Professor Ince is one of the best  Professors. Most MET Professors  are really jokes. They don't have any idea what they are teaching, but give all students A. Those students,  complain this class are those to get an easy A from other class. This is not true for Professor Ince. He takes a very hard subject and makes it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm sorry you have to take this class. The class is being split into 314/315. Ince is too hard to understand and too smart for this class. He belongs in industry and not in the classroom. He is not good for explaining material inside or outside the class. You are given limited resources to teach the material to yourself. Find friends to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend not taking this professor.
Unable to get the material across in lecture. Had to teach myself everything.

Great Professor. Actually wants to challenge you. If you pay attention, go to lecture, and study, you will do well. If you think that a good professor is one that allows an easy A, then this class will be challenging. He is probably the smartest prof. I have had here which is something to respect. You can learn a lot form him if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken. Prof. Ince is too intelligent to actually teach any of the material. He simply cannot "dumb it down" in order to get students to grasp the concepts. Be prepared to teach yourself.
Lectures make no sense so get ready to teach yourself everything.
Good luck you'll need it
Wouldn't take this class at Purdue as long as he is professor if I was you.
Can't effectively relay the information needed to  do succeed in the course. Good luck
can't teach. Worst professor I've had at Purdue
Impossible to understand and doesn't clearly cover the material. Prepare for most people to get C's and D's

Professor Ince is an awful professor and his MET214 class is one of the worst taught classes I have taken at Purdue. He is by far one of the worst professors I've had. I vote for Eddie and French to take over this class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Ince really knows what he is talking about. One of the smarter professors I have had. Could never answer any question. He wants students to learn, but is awful at actually teaching. This has been my least favorite class to date due to time spent vs. material learned, and also the hardest. French or Eddie should teach this instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ince really knows what he is talking about. One of the smartest professors I have had. Always could answer any question. He wants students to learn and creates life stories to explain what is important in the workplace. This has been my favorite class to date, but also the hardest.
This class is awesome. It is  very challenging but very applicable. Prof. Ince does a very good job at relating the class to the real world and it makes the class more enjoyable.
Rough class.

Grades for perfection. Considers skipping class as cheating. Rarely in office for help. Only 10 grades the entire semester (6 HW, 3 exams, 1 final project). Expects too much out this class, especially for the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was the most poorly taught class I have had at Purdue. The professor shows that he is incredibly intelligent, but the presentation of material is done very poorly. He is hard to understand and his work on the board is usually all over the place. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor. The only reason that people complain about this class is because they don't put in enough effort to pass the class. The professor  is straight forward and expect us to earn the grade rather than give us one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ince is without a doubt the worst Professor I've ever had. He's kicked students out of Office Hours because he is "busy with research". His exams are 2 questions and they're worth 15% of your grade, 25% for the final. He won't explain what you did wrong on the exams. There is no practice exam. He skims his own lecture slides. THE worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I find this class interesting, but material is tough. Professor Ince is very smart, knowledgeable and strict. Get ready to study hard.
The time you put in reflects in your grade. Follow and understand the material in lecture and homework shouldn't be a mystery. Don't be afraid to go to his office and ask for help.
Professor Ince is a great professor and his MET214 class is one of the best taught classes I have taken at Purdue. He is by far one of the best professors I've had.
He knows his material extremely well. Its a hard course, but I really enjoyed the course.
very smart and great professor. He knows the course materials very well. If you attend class, take notes and pay attention, you'll do well in the class. Otherwise, good luck!

Ince is a very smart professor. From what I've learned, he knows what he's doing, just doesn't know how to teach. This was his first semester being a professor in the program. Since we are held to a lower standard to what he was, the learning curve is different. He definitely likes to talk about his time in industry and in college.

Very knowledgeable and smart prof. You can get very high grade if you show that you really understand  important course topics and explain well your work and include all your assumptions in the paper. Even if there are numerical errors in your calculations and your numbers aren't quite right.

There's a lot of content, but slides are always posted for review and the topics given are interesting. You learn not only about fossil fuels themselves and how they work, but also history behind them and how our society revolves around them. Teacher is very kind and courteous.

Extremely fun professor. He's passionate about the subject, engaging in lectures, encourages genuine discussion, explains the material thoroughly and meaningfully, and clearly cares about his students. Assignments were all narrative based, requiring you take a position and write about it in discussion posts and quizzes. Great class and an easy A.
Great professor

A really nice professor, many assignments and projects, attendance is needed, but everything is not too hard if you love geography, only need you to pay attention, lectures are interesting, just like telling stories, there also have some funny short talks, you will never feel boring, he loves his students and always smile to them, like a old friend
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took EAPS375 with professor Ballotti this semester and overall its been great, the lecture slides are very good and the professor talks at a good pace, information that we need to know was covered well. Quizzes are what took up about half of the course's grade and you have to answer them thoroughly to do well. Overall good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill and funny dude. Lots of small but easy assignments and discussions. Unit projects were chill, really enjoyed my time.
Prof. Ballotti is very passionate, very knowledgeable, and very engaging as a professor. I got more out of his class than I thought I would. Would love to take more classes with him.
Although this course is completely online that winter, he read through the discussion posts and tried his best to communicate with student. A great professor.

Prof Dean is very passionate about the subject, and I enjoyed this class more than I thought I would. I learned a lot, and his lectures are very detailed and engaging. There is some busy work involved as well as quizzes every couple weeks and a group paper at the end, but there's no final exam. Pretty light, manageable workload.
Great professor doing his best to teach this class! Very grateful for the time I got to spend with him
Great professor, very passionate and cares about his students. Would take more classes by him, nice guy.

Dr. Ballotti is a very passionate lecturer. He is a great advocate for science literacy! My only complaint is that for Maymester '22, we had a small group assignment every single day and then one final semester paper... with our group, but that's how the world works. Overall, very easy class and you become more scientifically literate and aware!

One of the best professors Ive had a Purdue. His passion and knowledge on what hes teaching made the class really enjoyable and informative. Even with the entirely online format, the course was well organized and engaging.

One of my favorite professors at Purdue. His lectures were very engaging and I really appreciated how knowledgeable and passionate he was about the subjects. Online classes can be kind of a drag but he really did his best to make it work and I felt that the content/ workload/ expectations for the course were very organized and manageable.
He cares a lot about what he teaches, cheerful old man! Get ready to read a lot.

He's incredibly passionate about what he teaches. His class might be tad difficult, but he posts very comprehensive study guides, so if you study at least a little and actually focus on what he says in lectures (incredibly dense, but just pay attention and be ready to take notes) you'll do fine.
Taught the subject well and was clearly passionate about it. Graded fairly, and although there was a significant amount of work it was not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: With Ballotti you either really like him or you really dont. Personally I think hes great. Hes a big believer in the education before the grade and supporting students where needed. Yes he does go down rabbitholes at time, but only because hes really passionate and knowledgeable about his field. Hes also great with the dad jokes.

Dean was a terrible teacher, nice guy but he can't teach worth a darn. We were assigned to our lab groups so good luck if you get a bad group. All points are based on your lab partner's success. Exams are very poorly written and Dean is no help in his study sessions. Very off topic and doesn't get the job done.

He's the most knowledgeable professor in his field I have ever had. He tends to be so knowledgeable, in fact, that he can go on tangents that get you interested in the class, but may not be necessarily on topic.  He is motivating, understanding, and inspiration and makes you love science, or at least appreciate it for what it is. I loved him!
he was horrible. always talked about things we didn't need to know. tests were ridiculous... he would give us F's if you did bad on 2 questions out of alot. he is rude and this class is pointless

One of the most uncaring professors I've had so far at Purdue. There is SO much busywork that really doesn't aid your learning at all, it's more reasons for her to find something small and particular to deduct points from. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you can please DON'T take this class! This class requires tons of work, random small points are taken off, and the professor sends an insane amount of announcements. Aside from one useful project, the majority of the assignments were busywork and seemed inconsiderate of students' overall workload.

Prof Bailey is not as bad as these reviews say, but still not easy. She was nice to both me and my groups in emails. The worst part of the class is that she is pretty harsh grading the big group projects, so be sure to do well on the other things to try and offset that. Read the instructions well because she WILL deduct for the smallest things.

Honestly it was nowhere near as bad as the other reviews have said. As long as you write something competent that hits the word count you'll get a perfect on individual assignments. She also grades within 24 hours and is one of the only professors I've had that gives personalized feedback for every single assignment.

I was scared of taking this class with her because of the ratings but she was awesome. My group had a problem with the company we were supposed to work with and she understood everything. I emailed her often to ask her some doubts I had and she responded quickly. Just try to send emails to her in a professional way and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst instructor I have had in 3 years at Purdue. Blunt, lacks compassion, and just plain mean. Bad, bad, bad.

She grades quickly & rubrics are (mostly) clear, but her disengagement is apparent. She requires work with outside companies for a project and you are penalized if unable to secure a partnership with a local business/organization. Grades shouldn't be dependent on anyone besides the students. My A+ was earned in spite of, not because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bailey uploads a document weekly that contains the week's assignments, but this , the individual project rubrics, and the syllabus often contradict each other. She's a tough grader & knocks points off if emails are "unprofessional". One nice thing I will say is she grades quickly. I recommend taking this class with literally any other professor.

Would assign work with an insanely quick turnaround. She never handed out rubrics and the actual courage page was very difficult to follow. I absolutely hated this class and any time I emailed her for clarification she was extremely rude. I would tell everyone who is scheduled in her class to try to get into another section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was scared to take this class because of these ratings, but it really wasn't that bad. Her rubrics are extremely clear. Make sure you finish things before the deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible class would not recommend just take any other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bailey is pretty strict with her grading, but she posts the rubrics before the assignments are due. It's not like you don't know what you need to do to get the grade you want. The group projects are kind of annoying especially if you pick a bad group but they're not terrible. Professor Bailey seems like a reasonable person.

THE S***isht professor in the entire university. She thinks she is so righteous and doesn't allow for makeup that is seconds late. Just take a other similar class. English class is not hard but she will do it to make you suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rachel does not exhibit an ounce of altruism throughout any of her interactions with students. Her demeanor towards the course, expectations, and people create a discouraging, non-engaging learning environment. Her assignments are disorganized and It does not seem she is passionate about teaching.

There is a fast turnaround with projects so you have to keep up with the content, but the hard part is that she grades very harshly and takes off numerous points for small errors that another ENGL 421 professor wouldn't blink an eye at.  Furthermore, her emails are rude and she doesn't maintain the etiquette that she expects in an email to her.

Incredibly inconsiderate, and often times rude. She grades extremely hard and is never accommodating, not to mention she is extremely difficult to get ahold of. I really wish I had looked into her before I decided to take this class, as it was an elective. I thought I would be interested in her class, but she has completely ruined it for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've ever taken at Purdue. She's very harsh at grading and also rude in her emails. Does not give any partial credit even for the simplest mistakes. Do not take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take again. So confusing and almost impossible to reach via email. Uses a Gmail account so the University can't track what she's saying to students. DO NOT TAKE.

Poor course organization and assignment descriptions. Extremely rude and very poor response time on emails. Uses her gmail account so the University can't monitor her ill-mannered responses or lack-there-of. Relatively easy course made difficult by how much she sucks.

Very poor professor. Rude in emails. Not very helpful. Emailed all day trying to get a very small question answered and she never gave me an answer and was extremely rude in doing so. Avoid at all costs. Very easy class. Very poor professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Never take this instructor's course. Not only is she a harsh grader, but she is incredibly rude and will fail you if you simply don't use proper email etiquette. She will tell you your papers are written beautifully and then still give you a B. If you have to take 420, avoid her at all costs.

Don't take this lecturer  she is a tough grader and gives so many assignment in a week. Her replies in email was so rude and rush. Be aware of the group project. She is so unorganized in every details regarding the projects and assignments.

Dr. Barber is one of my favorite professors. His class is very interest-based and open to further exploration. I contracted his class for honors credits, and he was very knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and easy to work with. If you like to be involved, you'll love his class!

Dr. Barber is a decent professor. However, his class DOES NOT need to be an hour and fifteen minutes long. The class itself is fine, pretty boring but not hard. The class consists of mainly papers. He takes a while to get back to you on assignment drafts and isn't very good at communication, which is weird as he is a communications teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Barber was great! He was really easy to talk to if you needed help catching up on things. He is younger so he understands what it's like to be a student and how the stress can become overwhelming. Super accommodating and I would definitely take a class of his again!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Barber was an outstanding professor. He was enjoyable to listen to and talk to outside of class. He is intelligent and seems to care about his students. Sometimes I can get lost when lecturing because his lectures can be disorganized, but he does a good job of getting the class engaged.

Awesome professor! Longer lectures but he keeps them interesting and tries to get people to participate. He is passionate about what he teaches and was helpful when I fell behind and gave me all the time I needed to catch up. Will go out of his way to help students understand the content. Recommend taking any class that he's teaching!
Literally the worst professor I have ever had at purdue. Reads off pdfs for lectures without clear guidance on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Caldwell's lectures are very unique in that he has no slides but rather has paragraphs written out in a Word document, and his lectures are more or less reading them and expanding upon them. It makes for somewhat frustrating notetaking but the grad-level class is more of a thoughtful dialogue.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stay away from this professor at all costs. Cannot teach to save his life.

He just gets word files on the projector and just keeps reading it (tries to joke sometimes- but he's so bad at them), For IE 590 he'll ask the TAs to set a score of 83 and to start deducting/adding points from there. Just a bad professor. Don't ever take a graduate class with him. The grading is so random!. I hurt my GPA so bad with this class.

He is a fair professor as he challenges graduate students to go out and do the extra bit research in order to be prepared for lectures and assignments. Though it can be difficult to understand how things are being graded he is fair. I wish him and his TAs didn't grade as hard for grammar, but overall I learned a lot in regards to systems thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Worst worst Prof ever. Few guidelines for paper while grading extremely harsh. There was no rubric and they just gave out points as they felt like. Projects submitted by companies are very easy and we were asked to do simple tasks again and again and again. To be honest it is really wasting time. Barely learned anything. Avoid him for sure.
I would rather commit suicide than take another class with this professor. This guy is incorrigible and apathetic.

This prof does not teach but rather discusses vague ideas related to statistics. He spends little time in class showing the mechanics behind solving a problem and does not use examples in class. The TA is the only hope. Avoid this professor at all costs.

One of the worst profs I have had at Purdue. I spends the entire lecture reading paragraphs of jibberish and spends no time teaching how to do actual problems. He has yet to do an example and this is a math class.

He is the worst professor I have had in all my four years hear at Purdue. That pretty much sums it up. I've been in the class for over two months now and haven't learned a thing. Classes like his are the reason IE are referred to as "Imaginary Engineers". He has a pleasant enough demeanor but is a completely selfish educator. Avoid if possible.

This is a senior design class and he emphasis on writing skill rather than the real engineering stuff and how the team have help the customer. All the grades is based on deliverable, where huge potion of points are deducted for small spelling mistake while he have typos in his email himself too. He is **** too, so choose a American teammate.
He is not very good at all.  teaches IE but has psych degrees.  not a horrible person, soo much.  well slightly.
Literally the WORST. Complete Ego maniac! Lectures are complete waste, gives no help when requested. Amazing he still continues to teach at purdue!  Complete Waste Do Not Take!

Had heard some negative things going into the class about the professor but as long as you keep an open mind and have a willingness to go to him for help/guidance, the semester shouldn't be too bad.  Can be vague at times but this is intentional because he wants you to go to him for help and not be handed a solution.  keep an open mind
his name said it all, "B.S." Caldwell...

He is very liberal in teaching style, likes to ramble and describe things that have no link to engineering from an engineering aspect. His notes are NOT helpful because they are huge paragraphs of nonsense. It's hard to find out what is the important information from lectures. Lalaine, the TA, however, does a good job of sorting through all his bul

Not to be mean but he is the worst I have ever had and I think most ppl in the class agree pretty much. We learn nothing for real and I don't think he has such credibility and eligibility to teach most our class. I took 330 and 332 twice be4 w/ him and I feel useless infront of others that learn from other prof. I learn nothing compared to them....

The course has been murdered by Prof. Caldwell. There is no sense of order in what he is teaching. The projects and notes have been presented in the vaguest possible manner. Grading is almost random and it seems that there is no structure to the course. He just teaches whatever is on his mind. I hope nobody has to take a course under him.

Caldwell's "alternative" teaching technique is in essence an excuse to do minimal work in terms of teaching and helping students while using students for his research purposes. I learned nothing from him in his 332 class and expect to learn no more in 486.

I wish he'd start teaching for a change.. talks 40 mins of useless information in the most vague manner possible. . lecture notes on a slide again are pointless.. does not look at the course from the students point of view.. i think he knows he isnt a good teacher and thus most of the grade is left for projects etc .. LEARN ON YOUR OWN POLICY

Without exaggerating, the worst prof I've Ever Had.  During an hour lecture, he would spend only 5 minutes teaching vague formulas that didn't apply, and the rest on "housekeeping" (maintaining his own WebCT account).  Offered little help, and often belittle student's who approach him with questions. You'll have to learn everything on your own!
Odd
He tries to elaborate his idea through discussions with his students, without the intention of helping students. Selfish teachear
No Comments
This guy is the most worthless professor I have ever had.  He doesnt know how to use any of the software that he expects us to use, and is the most vague teacher I have ever had.

Invents words to try to look intelligent.  Project and assignments are very ambiguous.  Cryptology should be a prerequisite, it is neccessary or you won't have a clue what you're doing.  I've learned nothing in 2 months.

I would select other tags if I could. There is not a bad thing I could say about this Professor other than the fact I can only take this class once with her. She is incredibly caring about her students, listens to everyone, and actually makes a very caring class environment. I felt like some of my happiest memories were made in that class.

Very kind and inspiring professor, you can tell she cares a lot about her students and the class! She makes a great effort to stimulate class discussion and weighs in with her own points, which were always insightful and often very funny. The books for SCLA 102 were overall good, and the theme of the class (Fall 25) was amazing.

I had Babintseva for SCLA 102 and she was absolutely wonderful! She tried her best to make the reading engaging and seems to actually value student feedback. She was a very complimentary grader, as well. Most of the class was reading outside of class with discussions in class, and there were many extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend her!

She is absolutely phenomenal. Class was a good mix of lecture and group discussion. She has genuine respect for her students' input and intellect, and she is so kind. It is not an easy class, there's a lot of reading, but I found it to be rewarding and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor and really knows a lot about the subject matter. Whenever she was speaking people would be really invested because she provided a lot of insight that we wouldn't have figured out on our own. In general she's super nice and tends to laugh during our lectures which keeps them lighthearted and fun. Just super awesome.
Great course content. Grading chill
She was fantastic!

The course isn't well organized. The instructions provided in class is very different from what is posted online. On the course page, the exam time was posted as 2 hours but the students were given only an hour. Very often the assignments are posted late but the time provided for the assignment was less than a week.

It didn't look like lecture prep was taken seriously at all. The slides used are 10 to 12 years old so students don't get acquainted with current research in the field.  Problem sets are recycled from the previous professor who took this course, so are exams. In the first class, she said international students are likely to cheat and plagiarize.

the professor was new so there was an adjustment period but overall the class was good. there are two quizzes every week and four exams. One exam is dropped. Professor gave a study guide of concepts for the exams, which was very helpful. If you study well, you can get an A. she gives a lot of EC at the end of the semester

this was completely online class. I took it during first year. SO the beginning was rocky, and study guide came late; She did take our feedback in the class so it improved as semester went on. It's just the quizzes and 4 exams, lowest dropped. Quizzes became open note but idk. I mostly read the book to get learning objectives done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most caring profs I've had at Purdue. I remember near the end of the semester she told me that my smile genuinely brightened her day. Said at the beginning of the semester that she would always take our side no matter what. Genuine unconditional kindness that you don't see often elsewhere (but should).

ENGR 131 isn't a hard class. It's not too exciting either, but Prof. Galarza did her best to make classes kinda fun or have us practice an engineering soft skill (teamwork). 
Prof. Galarza is one of the nicest, most caring professors at Purdue. She also bumped my A- up to an A because I asked (the FYE 3.2 GPA, iykyk), because I got to know her.

Professor Galarza is super caring and always makes sure to asks students how they are doing. She is also very helpful when answering students' questions. The class curriculum itself is slow and tedious though so I would recommend taking ENGR 133 over ENGR 131 if you're taking a lighter course load.

Probably the nicest professor I have ever had. She cares so much about all of her students and is willing to help everyone. She has no problem giving points back to students if they ask and she is always willing to give good feedback and listen to problems you may have in this class.

I am very grateful to have gotten Professor Galarza as my ENGR 131 professor. She very obviously cares about her students education and their future. The classes consist mainly of review of pre-lecture videos with group work after.

She might be one of the most caring professors at this university. She's always available for her students and she truly wants you to succeed. ENGR 131 wasn't a hard class but I had a 7:30, and I'm really thankful that I had her class because I didn't often dread getting up to go to it. She also gives you a lot of studio time to work on projects.

ENGR 13100 I think is a pretty tedious class because the course fits a lot into a few months. Dr. Galarza made the class so much more tolerable. She is a sweet and supportive teacher and is the first person at Purdue who made me feel like I belonged. She makes effort to know all of her students personally and really cares about their well-being.
Lovely person, so supportive and kind. Will happily explain anything you're struggling with, gives a lot of extra credit opportunities
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ENGR131 itself is tedious but she helped by giving extra credit opportunities and solving any doubt from the assignments or projects, exam criteria is unclear but she is fair when reviewing exams and if you explain why you deserve the points for an unclear question, she gives at least some or all of them. I'm taking her ENGR132 class next semester.

She is very helpful if you have any questions you wanna ask directly in person. Her lectures are boring but I don't know who could possibly make this class any less boring. She is bad at answering emails though. I still recommend!
Boring, rambling lectures reading straight from slides. Accent not bad at all. Recommend someone else for 131.

I never felt strongly enough about a professor to resort to RateMyProfessor, yet here I am. Dr. Bellisario gives unclear grading criteria for recitation and group assignments. She acts like you can read her mind about what she wants out of your group and then proceeds to be extremely condescending and critical of your work. Switch professors!

She gives way too much homework for a one-credit class. The weekly nature journals are a waste of time. Interrupts you in the middle of presentations to give critiques. Regardless, this class is still easy AF but try to take it with a different prof if possible.
She was very clearly passionate about naturalism, and was super nice, but incredibly unorganized. Be careful you wont know when stuff is due sometimes. Incredibly nice and awesome professor though.

The grading criteria for group assignments tended to be unclear, but it didn't really matter in the grand scheme of things because of the lenient grading in 19902. Beyond the assignments, the topic was interesting and she taught it passionately. She's kind, and the readings aren't long at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her naturalism class and although she was very passionate about the topic, I don't think the class was taught well. She is extremely disorganized and never told us when assignments were due. She was very critical about group presentations, but didn't provide clear criteria for us to go off of. The class was kind of a joke honestly.

She was clearly very passionate about the subject matter (naturalism) but the class itself was so disorganized it was hard to be engaged and know what was going on/when stuff was due. Pretty consistently would contradict herself about certain things and then blame us for making a mistake based on what she said intially.

She is very passionate about the topic, but very disorganized. Its impossible to know when anything is due or what you need to do for next class. She grades everything last minute. She is not a good representation of the honors college.
Very disorganized and confusing on assignment information.

Dr. Bellisario is very passionate about the topic (silence/extinction). Grading criteria were unclear for many assignments and the final project, but this could be due to HONR19902's new format this year. She offered several extra credit and revision opportunities as a result of the unclear criteria. Overall, a good professor for 19902.

This professor is disorganized, doesn't have set standards, and will make getting your honors seminar requirement completed very difficult. This professor was constantly changing her expectations and always talked condescendingly when people had questions.

Very nice guy, as a non-math major, I think sometimes he's too smart for me in a way that he goes into things way deeper than necessary, but if that helps you, then it's a plus. He is a very nice guy and cares a lot about your success, and answers questions very quickly. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he also records all lectures.
Great professor!

Steve Bell is without a doubt the best math professor I have had during my time here in Purdue. He is an artist with the subject and is a really good lecturer. The material is tough, however he is absolutely 100% open to explaining them further in his office hours. Would absolutely recommend to anyone to take his class in a heartbeat is possible.

Professor Bell is one of the best professors I've had. He cares intensely about his students. Not to mention he may be one of the smartest people I've ever met and is a very accomplished mathematician. His passion for problem-solving and beautiful solutions has made me enjoy my major even more. His class is a must-take.
This professor made classes interesting and engaging. Course was enjoyable and all the topics were described well making everything feel a lot easier.

I do believe Professor Bell handled the online nature of this class and the entire Covid climate perfectly. He was kind, thoughtful, and above all compassionate. There were clear and concise instructions throughout the semester and very fair exams. Have not had a better experience with an online class or Purdue math.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bell is a great teacher that cares about his students' well being. He makes very hard concepts seem quite simple. My only complaint is that his lectures have little mistakes peppered lightly throughout the lecture, but the main ideas are always concise.
Professor Bell is the best ODEs professor at Purdue - nuff said

Bell is a great professor and he obviously loves math and is genuinely excited to be teaching calculus. I would 100% take him again because I learned a lot from him. If you do all the homework, do well on the recitation quizzes, and study a lot for the exams you'll do fine. Also this class has a pretty big curve which is nice.

Dr. Bell's MA161 class was the worst experience of my life and made my first semester at Purdue miserable. He hardly teaches the material on the hw/exams and spends most of the time talking about the history of math, which no one cares about. The exams are ridiculously hard. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE NO PRIOR CALCULUS EDUCATION.
Bell's a good lecturer who takes time out of class to answer questions students have. He does get distracted easily, but it's not a problem overall.
Steve Bell is a great professor of Calculus. He makes sure everything is relatively easy to understand and wants you to succeed.

For MA161, Bell has provided online links to his lecture notes as well as his recorded Boilercast videos. Anyone that has bell as a professor will have his website and is accessible to you to live stream his lectures as they happen. Introduces most lectures with a review of last time, and ends with a look ahead at what's next. Fantastic intro to PU
Great, funny guy that really tries to ensure that you understand the material before he moves on. Study for the tests though or you'll beg for death.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor that makes math interesting and lecture fun. Makes a lot of jokes and thoroughly teaches the material and makes sure you understand it before moving to the next topic.
I had a different instructor last semester on MA527. They are both good. I have say MA528 is much tougher than MA527. Don't take it unless you need it !

Bell really likes the subject and makes it as interesting as it could be.  The textbook (Kryzeig) is big, expensive, and not one you can just read and work independently (fairly worthless).  Took it through distance, Bell went way above and beyond to have convenient office hours and answer questions on "Piazza".  Bell is a good teacher, liked him.

Prof Bell is clearly passionate about the subject and this translates to an effective teaching method. He is process driven and succinct. Material is not too tough depending on experience, but you'll probably have to work for a good grade.

He's a good guy but he really tends to talk around subject matters. He seems more concerned with teaching the history of the how certain equations and laws came to be rather than actually teaching how to apply them. It's still interesting but regardless it doesn't help you learn the material very well from lectures. Had to practically teach myself.
Comical with his remarks. He knows what he is teaching and does a really good job at it.
An absolutely outstanding professor, made this course highly enjoyable and far more interesting than your average calculus 2 class.
Awesome guy, brilliant, highly recommend

Professor Bell is terrific. The material is hard if you've never had it before but he's always willing to answer questions. Puts the notes online too which helps if you fall behind (he writes kind of fast). Overall a great professor, would definitely recommend him.
Took the course via distance learning.  Overall Prof. Bell was very helpful and understanding.  Subject matter was difficult at times but I didn't exaclty put a lot of effort into it either.
He is a great professor and is obviously passionate about his subject.
He is with out a doubt the smartest professor I have ever had in my college career. His ease in explaining difficult subjects and the overall zest he has for his job is refreshing.
No Comments

He's da man! He made Diff EQ.. so interesting, very very clear.. explains evry idea with a lot of interest and clarity. excellent professor. if you're taking 266 or 262, just get Dr. Bell as your prof. Even if you dont get a good grade, you'll be satisfied with the amount of stuff you learned.
He can juggle and ride a unicycle at the same time!

Lectures can be long, though I have always felt that it is more efficient to read the slides in my own time. Exams are average diff. Homework can be in weird formats and sometimes not so cohesive. I had him for CS440 and CS473. Hisham does a lot at Purdue in addition to these classes, so he can be busy.
Not that hard. But definitely annoying. Finish your homework on your own and try to solve all the problems they provide in PSO, you will be good in the exams.

He is a very respectable CS professor. The content was moderately difficult but taught well, the homeworks and exams felt fair (at least to me) and there was a decent amount of extra credit. 348 isn't the hardest course, but I felt like he taught us enough to be useful without ever feeling helpless.

The exams were fairly similar to the practice exams, although you have to write code with a pencil which can feel completely different to any of the homeworks. The professor was somewhat forgiving and gave extra credit opportunities. There were online i-clicker activities during the lectures (we didn't have to buy one)

348 has certainly become much more difficult. The exams are extremely challenging. Similar to the practice exams, but just at a much higher degree of difficulty. There was a nice curve, but the class does not follow the reputation it has of being an easy elective

Prof Benotman was a nice professor. His lectures can be boring, but he is teaching databases so I can't blame him. He was accessible outside of classes, and willing to adjust deadlines as needed. Exams were open-note, and he released a practice exam in advance. The project was basically a fullstack CRUD app, so super easy if you have experience.

I don't know it's just this semester, but it was obvious that we're like... not his priority class. He clearly was putting more effort into teaching CS348, which isn't a bad thing but... whyd he make it so obvious? Anyways, it was okay. He posted the practice exam 2 days before the exam on a Sunday night. Lol

His lectures are pretty good, but sometimes hard to pay attention to. He seems like a responsive professor, willing to answer questions and change deadlines to things when needed. The homework and exams are hard, but the project isn't bad if you don't procrastinate.

Poor lectures and lack of engagement. It seems like he didn't read the slides beforehand. The material was interesting, just a bad lecturer. Assignments were extremely tedious but not difficult. Attendance counts. Project was interesting. I would avoid if possible, lectures alone make the class extremely tedious and sluggish.
The amount of time you have to spend in this class is reasonable. Grading is fair. Dr. Benotman makes the lectures very intuitive and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his CS348, and he is one of the best professor among other CS courses professors. He explained well during the lecture and also provided recordings every time after the class for students to review. He is also very helpful in his OH and on Campuswire.

Benotman is not the best at lecturing. He is very knowledgeable about the information. There are many homeworks and they do take a while. The exams are very easy because they are open note. Any of his classes are easy because of this (ex. 471).

Professor Benotman is an overall good professor. He has fair expectations for his class. Was also helpful after class when we asked him about homework specifications. Very flexible when I needed to make up an exam or accidentally forgot to turn in a part of the homework. Curved by a lot and got an A when I expected a B or B+.

Professor Benotman is an overall good professor. He has fair expectations for his class. Was also helpful after class when we asked him about homework specifications. Flexible when I needed to make up an exam or accidentally forgot to turn in a part of the homework. Curved by a lot and got an A when I expected a B or B+.
Good professor in general. Slow but helpful lectures. There's little need to read the textbook. Sometimes the homework grading can seem arbitrary, but overall they are very useful.

Benotman is a fairly good professor. He can be a little dry in lecture and he doesn't really follow his class schedule a lot (he gave one in the beginning of the semester, but it wasn't updated with changes). However, he does seem to care about your learning and is very approachable. He is a safe choice overall.

Nice Professor, Friendly person. I have done a project with him. He is very welcome to students during his office hour and even out of his office hour. But he is somehow not that good at explaining. but mostly, he is a very good professor.
Good quality lectures and assignments. The course covered a good selection of topics.

He was one of the most caring and helpful professors I have had, especially throughout the duration of the pandemic and online setting. He made material that was dry seem interesting and easy to understand through the use of many examples.

If you watch the lectures, youll do well in the class. Goes over all the homework questions during the lectures and is very available to help, and very understanding. Great professor and made the databases class very enjoyable.
He's very understanding throughout the pandemic. Homeworks can be somewhat challenging at times but nothing unreasonable.

He clearly cares about his students from the amount of time he puts into responding to questions on CampusWire, but his teaching abilities are questionable. He was good at explaining simple things in SQL, but when it comes to more complex topics like MongoDB sharding, he reads off the slides like arobot. Rating 4 instead of 3 because he is caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Benotman is one of the best in the CS department! He shows real-world examples of databases that allow students to utilize/investigate numerous cloud-based database services. My database knowledge has improved significantly and feel very comfortable putting my new skills to use in an employment setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Benotman is amazing! He definitely has a deep knowledge of databases and you can see it in his lectures. He cares a lot about his students and is very encouraging. Focuses more on learning than grades and is dedicated to the subject and his students. Gives a lot of assignments (varying difficulty) but you learn a lot. Highly recommend!

He is very strict and makes the course difficult. I always heard CS348 was an easy class but he made it super hard. His homeworks are terrible. He gives assignments about stuff that he doesnt teach in class and doesnt give a lot of time to finish them either. He isnt understanding and does not care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Irresponsible :,(

Lectures are unengaging and difficult to sit through. She is impossible to reach outside of class, with no clear office hours and minimal email responses. I tried to contact her over a dozen times about a TA position for CNIT 271 and only received a response twice, one to tell me to reach back out later, another to tell me there's no more space.

Thanks to her I spent my lovely fall break writing lab reports!
She makes you write a paper about her research paper for her thesis!
Suchly a lovely lady :))
She yaps for hours and hours but literally no one understands as well as cares about whatever she's talking about. I would never like to take class with her ever in my life.

Attendance is mandatory (have to sign your name on a sheet) and the lectures aren't interesting at all. Overall she's a decent professor, just uninteresting. Exams & quizzes are worth a massive chunk of your grade which are all taken in person during class. TAs were generous graders which made the class much easier.
She is very nice and will respond to emails/requests for extensions, lectures are a bit boring but the content is not hard. She does take attendance for lectures

Very reasonable grader and accessible outside class. Had a problem with a quiz and emailed her about it, was immediately fixed. Lectures can be a bit dull but show up and take notes and you'll be fine. Takes attendance every lecture. Labs have some challenging parts but TAs are very helpful.

This is her first semester teaching the course so she was still figuring a few things out. She took a lot of feedback and applied it almost instantly. Labs were easy and mostly relevant to the material learned in lecture. Quizzes can be difficult sometimes, but they are not surprises and she will tell you a week in advance if there is a quiz.

Bhadra is a professor who is very passionate and knowledgeable about what he's teaching and he's happy to engage with students about it. Most of the exam problems come straight from the practice exams or examples done in lecture (so it's a much easier class if you go to lecture), and homework is consistently straightforward and manageable.

I think he is a very good lecturer. Hard to understand at times, but somehow makes very conceptual high level topics seem easy. The homework is very long and difficult in my opinion, and graded strictly. Other than that, the exams weren't nearly as difficult and were very similar to practice done in class. Makes the most of a very difficult subject

Anindya Bhadra is hands down one of the worst professors at Purdue University.  His attitude towards his students is not of  care but out of spite. He puts no effort in ensuring students success and is one of the rudest professors at Purdue. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
This is the worst professor I have ever had. Lectures make no sense, you basically have to teach yourself statistical theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly Bhadra isn't a bad lecturer, his lectures are fine and although he can get a bit snarky during lectures, he is accessible and open to explaining how to approach the homework problems. His exams are weighted heavily, homeworks very from being doable to being difficult. Overall hard class, be ready to read, and learn about stat theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He skipped so many important materials during class but leave the hardest questions as homework. Most ridiculously, his grader always tries his best to make you lose points in your homework. I attend his class all the time but I have no idea what the homework was talking about. Is the math/stat department running out of teachers? Just horrible.
Functions like a typical upper level stat at Purdue - every aspect from lecture to material is just impossible/incomprehensive

Lectures were okay, but really just followed the textbook for the most part. The examples were only sometimes helpful. There was not much homework, but most of the questions were not fully covered in class. A lot of reading the textbook is needed

Graduate level statistics requires good use of clear examples and figures to understand many difficult concepts covered in this class. While the notes included some, examples were largely rushed. The use of the software "R", a software that I will not be using in the future (we use SAS or SPSS in our program) was frustrating/useless.
worst teacher ive ever had... cant understand him at all... only needed a 53% to pass class or I would've failed

The worst teacher I have ever met at Purdue. I even cannot make sense what was he talking about. He gave the toughest homework in the textbook while other professor only gave some easy questions to do. He considered himself as a clever person and treated everyone as clever as he is.

I didn't learn anything from his lecture and can't do any homework after his lecture. He also didn't make use the forum such as piazza which allows students to ask questions on them. The exams are tough and the grades are not curved.

He proved all the theorems that have been proved in the textbook and did not mention how to do his homework. He treated undergraduate students as Ph.D students. His homework was super tough and was not able to be handled without others' help. Statistical theories are actually hard to understand and he made it even harder.

Prof Bhargava really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He'll set aside lots of time to meet outside of class, and assignments and exams are not unreasonably difficult. That being said, his lecture style really did not work for me as he went on many tangents, and I felt I wasn't learning the course material much in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bharat is one of the most caring Prof I have ever taken at Purdue. He is accessible outside of class and if you come to him with questions or doubts, he can go above and beyond to help you. His exam goes deep into details but if you attend lectures, and read the books then it should not be too difficult. The projects and homework are doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've had bad lecturers, but professor Bhargava takes that to a whole new level. Under the assumption that the students already know everything, not once did he cover the material in the slides. He much rather spend 40 minutes on a tangent then fly through 60 slides in 10. The only redeeming factor is that he is very accessible and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely doesn't teach much in class, and never follows the slides. Openly expects the student to read the textbook and magically expects them to know everything before class, rendering his lectures and his slides completely pointless, not that he teaches much anyways. Thank goodness his first homework and project are doable.

As a personality, he is nice in and outside the class. As teaching, he might be the worse that you will take. He doesn't give a curve by the end of the semester, you will need 94% to get an A. He will say that he will consider border cases but that is a lie, do not believe him. If you want to learn and care about the grade, do not take his class

He is a really nice guy, and cares a lot about his students. However, in his lectures he just talks about his research and past jobs. I went to 3 lectures and got full credit for participation. I knida feel bad for the guy since less than a quarter of the class showed up for the lectures, but I did fine just reading the slides.

Professor Bhargava cares about his students and has clear grading scale. His lecture needs attendance so that you can give him a good impression. Very good professor and I enjoy his class in my last semester at Purdue.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice, caring guy. Really makes an effort to be accessible outside of class, prefers to raise students' grades rather than lower them. That said, awful lecturer. Barely talks about the material and goes on tangents constantly. Don't go to class; just read the textbook/slides online. I skipped most lectures and still got 4/5 for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy who is always very willing to provide help. However, I would say I won't recommend his courses. He neither follows the slides or has a clear outline for the lecture. And he likes to give unrelated examples. It did waste lots of time and didn't encourage the students to follow him. It turns out that I learned everything by myself.
Useless Course. You will learn about his personal experiences with airlines more than distributed database systems

Lectures were mental torture. Draws out very simple concepts using examples that don't make sense. Contradicts himself often. However, class is extremely easy if you just read the book. Don't be overwhelmed with his list of topics to be covered either; you won't get to half of them.
Great class to learn Transaction processing and control. Very Classic Prof.
Pray that no one will fall for his style

He was a bit scattered with his lectures. He mixed old overhead transparencies with printouts from other books with old notes. He would have done better to just teach from the book. The thing I liked about him was that he wasn't out to trick you. He was very straightforward about what he expected and how he graded. He seems to care for his students
Disgusting. He talked about his wife and his kids. Learned nothing from his course!!! What a waste of time. I'd rather spend time dancing and playing around than taking his course.
542 was an awesome class.
Sigh!
No Comments
I am wasting my time to rate him here.
The best I can determine, my grade was based on how well he liked me
A total waste of time. He did NOT teach NOTHING.
All he did was talk about his time working at IU Med Center.  Didn't teach much.

I had my work proofread by my husband (from India) and she simply circled the entire essay and wrote “no” on it. I did so much work for no reward. She also came into my work without recognizing me and berated the employees for not letting her eat where we just sprayed for pests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final grade is heavily determined from the only midterm, which is based off of the whole textbook. There is no extra credit, office hours, help, retakes, or final. There are only 4 grades in the semester. Do not take this class unless you have prior knowledge of India.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She seemed more interested in her own life and experiences than in actually relevant history. She spins a good story, but if you question anything, look out, your grades will suffer. Least competent prof I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The midterm had super specific questions, which none of them were the ones she said would be on the exam. Also her directions for assignments are unclear and she does not answer emails. Very condescending if you answer a question wrong. Hard essay grader, and honestly a little scary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS! Extremely condescending and only wants to hear a specific answer to every question, even personal answers. Tests do not have any class material on it leading to most of the class failing. My GPA is messed up because of this class. AVOID!

Dr. Bhattacharya is extremely knowledgeable in her field but uses her knowledge as a way to disconnect herself from her students. She is very condescending to her students and makes them feel dumb. She never gives out instructions and her exams are extremely difficult and never cover anything she specifically told us would be on the exam.

Honestly, I was super excited to take the class and learn about south asian history and I really liked her at first. As time went on, she just seems super condescending. I never have and probably never will raise my hand because she will make u feel bad for answering wrong. She's super educated and knows her stuff though, tests are VERY book heavy.

The course lacks effective planning. For instance, we were given a week to submit a paper according to the syllabus, but instructions were only provided two days before the deadline. A similar last-minute change occurred for the midterm, initially planned as online but switched abruptly to in-person the day before the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Bhattacharya was great, she was always willing to answer questions and help with assignments. Sometimes her directions were a little unclear, but she always clarified it! She provided good feedback on assignments and was a good lecturer. I would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bhattacharya is knowledgeable in the subject matter. However, she tends to make students feel dumb when asking or answering her questions and overall has a condescending demeanor although she has good intentions. Read the textbook and take notes in class and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not recommend. Good luck with her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very intelligent professor and gets you to think critically about history. Can be somewhat condescending which discourges participation. Really not a lot of assigments, but don't miss something because it's difficult to keep your grade up. Sometimes the lectures can drag but she oftentimes lets out early and class was cancelled a lot.

Lectures can get boring and sometimes she could be rude and extremely condescending towards students. The assignments aren't super hard, and don't generally take a whole lot of time, but essays every other week. Luckily no exams, but there are Inquizitives every other week. Overall, the course isn't bad but she wasn't my favorite professor.

Super smart and definitely knows her stuff. Very sarcastic and lowkey condescending at times. Doesnt give much homework at all other than 500 word essays we have to write every other week. She grades the essays really tough but gives helpful feedback. Overall I enjoyed this class and the discussions we had in it. Easy A if you do all the homework.

This class if you like history it is a great find. She knows her stuff that much is obvious. If you are a good essay writer you'll do well. Class is much more personal than a lot especially if you participate and can lead to really interesting discussions and makes you think a lot more about history than normal; just make sure you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought the class was okay. Not too hard or too easy. I feel like the way she talks to students is VERY condescending. I would get a B+ on an assignment but her feedback would be super harsh. I believe she is very knowledgeable and you can tell but the way she gives feedback on my assignments makes me afraid to even ask for help.

Smart & knows what she's talking abt; lectures reflect that. Condescending. Asks ambiguous Qs & make u feel bad 4 answering "wrong". Grades on participation but makes u afraid 2 participate. Refuses to upload lectures online. Examsshort-answer. If u don't repeat what the book says she'll give a 0 even if u understand concept. Terrible grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Strict professor, will not respond to your emails ON PURPOSE. Not a good professor if you're a disabled student, she doesn't like to cooperate with university-approved accommodations. Class is super writing heavy. She doesn't "agree" with multiple choice. Content is kind of boring but it's personal preference.

Only had half the classes that were allocated for the semester. Syllabus is disorganized and she does not upload her lecture slides, so take good notes. There is only one essay, quiz, and exam before a take-home final exam. Grading is fair, but make sure to participate. Be persistent in communication-she doesn't do a good job responding to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy
