reviews.comment: I don't like giving a lessor than 5 rate. This professor could be outstanding, but she's very difficult to follow. She will ask ambiguous questions and then make fun of you if you don't answer correctly. She grades on participation but makes everyone afraid to participate. She's a wonderful lecturer though! I did learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think she's an ok lecturer. She definitely knows what she is talking about, but the way she delivers it can be condescending, especially when a student answer s incorrectly. Exam is all short-answer, but be prepared, because if you do not cough up exactly what the book says, you could risk getting a zero. Incredibly picky grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shes on okay professor but she lectures way too much. There were only maybe 3 main things we were grade don in the whole course: 3 papers and one small assignment. It was kinda a joke in that regard but it is unclear what she wants for some of the papers. Overall she was nice but it was frustrating not knowing what grade Id get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is terrible. She only covers what she wants in lecture and goes on about it for two and a half weeks. Then what you went to class to learn about isn't even on the exam. If she spent more time on other topics maybe we'd actually learn something. Her accent is more interesting than the content she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Bhattacharya, but the layout of this class wasn't my favorite, although it wasn't the worst either!!! She really does care about the subject, is super knowledgeable, and cares about her students. You may/may not need the book, but, spoiler alert, you don't actually have to participate. It's a basic non-Eurocentric history class...

Prof. Bhattacharya makes her class interesting and student friendly. Her class consists of lectures but also lots of discussions. In her HIST 243 (South Asian History) class, I was able to learn so many things I didn't know about the place I'm originally from. Read the book and annotate because if your are lucky you can use your book on exams.

This professor is my favorite person on Purdue's campus, I've taken two of her classes and i'm looking forward to taking a third. To do well in her class participate in the discussion, and you need to read the book or you won't do well on the Midterm of Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her lectures, she cares deeply about the topics that she talks about. Go class with an open mind and if you pay attention during the lectures and read the chapters you'll do fine.
Wonderful teacher, really cares for her students. Best history class at purdue!

This class was easy for the most part because there's no homework assigned. Reading the chapters is a necessity and participation is important but this class is not very labor-intensive at all. Also, make sure you have blue books for the exams - she doesn't give them out and you can't take the test if you don't have one.

Terrible Teacher...Nothing she taught was on the exam. Only after half of the class failed her first exam did she start to care. Also if you don't agree with  her liberal views, you might as well keep your mouth shut.

She's friendly but the class is more difficult than it should be. As a sophomore who aced 2 level 400 history courses last year, I am not struggling in this class but my grade reflects otherwise. Her TA's blatantly grade unfairly and it seems she has no oversight over them. I feel as though her choice in TA's is more of a problem to me than she is.

Dead & Undead in History. Great course topic! Readings are stimulating, interesting, and sometimes difficult, but do-able. Discussions help a lot (be prepared to speak up!). Papers are fair but don't expect many guidelines. She has a very witty sense of humor and is very entertaining. I definitely suggest taking a course with her.

Hmmmm.... You guys must have been her favorites because I cannot recall having the same experience. Just because a Professor is hard on his/her students does not necessarily mean he/she is helping them.

If you're taking an historiography course with a prof that never makes you intellectually (and politically) uncomfortable, you are not getting useful contact with the subject. Historiography is meant to be critical (of EVERY perspective), which is surely a good thing--be prepared for this with Dr Bhattacharya.

It doesn't surprise me that a site built on a customer service model of education would generate unfavorable reviews of Dr B. She will not make things easy for you--because that would be a waste of your time. She was one of FEW profs who truly pushed me during my grad studies. Poignant, incisive, extensive feedback on/in every paper and discussion.

This class was really challenging to start with, but it got easier and more fun.  If you are not willing to put in a 100% do not take a class with Professor Bhattacharya.  She will give you lots of chances, but doesn't tolerate laziness.  An A from her means a lot.  Great teacher.  I wish there were more professors like her.

This is was a very challenging class but the professor made it worth our while.  She let us do several rewrites, even after the deadline was past.  She wanted us to do well and she worked hard with us to make sure that that happened.  I enjoyed being a part of this class and it  made me stronger for the grad school experience as a whole.

Dr. Bhattacharya is the worst professor I have ever had. She does not care to connect with students, nor is she sympathetic to her students. Why in the world is she teaching a graduate level class. Her methods are terrible and no, she does not carry any type of "discourse" very well.

I knew nothing about the history of anything east of Greece prior to this class, but I found it wasn't a problem.  Interesting material and nothing too difficult.  End of the semester may get a little hectic though.
She is a really good teacher.  Cares about her students, and makes the classes interesting.  She has a wicked sense of humor.  I would take her again.
she is very good, caring and interesting.
Unimperessed with lack of orginiality and tendecny to stick to textbook
Has a great sense of humor.  Really funny in class.  Its a cool course.

Professor is very passionate about South Asian history.  This keeps lectures exciting.  However, lectures are taken straight from the text book (which is nice if you don't like to do the reading).  Exams aren't too hard.  Paper assignments are a little vague, but overall not too bad.
No Comments
She was extremely helpful and made the class very interesting.  She was really funny in class.  Take this course.
Seemed to have mood swings.  One day would complain that she wouldn't grade exams unless they were in pen, then would bring in candy for the class another.
Tech120 is a very easy class but your experience will heavily depend on who your groupmates are

Tech120 is already difficult but Professor Kotla makes it as enjoyable as possible. Very nice and has a sweet tooth. Graders for the course (not necessarily her) are fair, as long as you put in effort and some thought you can get a 100.

Bhavana is amazing! Many students loathe Tech120, but Bhavana makes it so much easier and enjoyable. She genuinely cares about every student and is willing to accommodate if needed. She also has a good sense of humor which makes the class that much more enjoyable. She will help you to succeed, and make this class as painless as possible. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Keys to success: showing up to class and simply just doing your assignments, it's that simple to get a good grade. Don't worry about any pop quizzes, hard exams, or strict grading practices and if you are ever having trouble she is super approachable and easy to talk to. She definitely goes out of her way to make the class more interesting.

If you have TECH 120 in Purdue, listen to me, TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. The class has a lot of work, but she makes it simple with her grading. Just do the work and you'll get an A. She grades quickly and isn't tough. My friends are struggling with other TA's and would do anything to switch classes.

While the class itself is not my favorite by any means, this professor seems to genuinely care about her students. One of things that sticks out is how she knows everyone by name. This class is basically "Group Project - The Class". That being said, so long as you do your homework, it is an easy A.

She really seems to care about her students but the class itself is structured kind of weird. As long as you do the work, you should be fine. Also, be prepared for group work! A good amount of the assignments are individual but everything is pretty group-based.
She is awesome
I love her
I love her... she is an awesome prof. thanks teacher for being so lovely!

I absolutely love this class. This is the only history class where I have enjoyed every required text. The instructor is very interested in teaching and knows what she is talking about. Considering this is a survey class, the workload is enormous but for once I learn a whole deal of stuff. Great job !

Very HEARTLESS about any type of personal matter. Takes a defensive approach whenever someone asks questions. Doesn't respond to email very quickly, or just screens the ones she wants to reply to. Rude and out of line for a 100 level class. SO much material.

I never knew history could be so difficult until I took this class. It seems I learn one book a day. The instructor seems to know so much and expects us to understand all of it. She is very demanding and I would warn you if you decided to take her class. Be prepared for very harsh grading.

She is very sweet and tried hard to make the material interesting for the students. But it seems that she will be a hard grader and I do not like that about a 100 level class. One has to be patient in her class.
Genuine teacher
One of the Best professor I ever met.

Dr. Bitt was by far my favorite professor, I suggest that you actually get to know him because he is a great guy and wants all his students to succeed. I recommend this class for literally anyone it amazing and not hard at all.

Very positive, authentic, & caring person. He's passionate & knowledgeable about what he does. Gives great lectures with lots of jokes & life lessons. Easy grader. Not strict about attendance, but you're missing out if you don't go. Willing to help anyone, even students that are not his own.
Dr. Bitt is THE BEST. He cares about his students and wants to see them succeed!

One of the greatest professors teaching at Purdue. Has an incredible amount of industry experience which he infuses into the course. Teaches the content extremely well, is funny and caring. Assignments are challenging but fare but the grading structure is generous. This simulation portion is a lot of fun. One of the best IE courses!

Easily one of the best and most important classes you can take. Class setting focus on real world cases of digital transformation, reviewing cases and technologies, industry speakers who are leaders in their field, interesting labs and is taught by one of the best professors in the university. Class has a decent amount of work, highly recommend!

Digital Transformation in Industrial Business with Professor Biller is enlightening, with case studies on various companies that give us insights on real-world implementations. There are group presentations on cases and technologies. The use of technologies like @Risk, working in labs, and guest lectures are like the icing on the cake.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great industry experience!

I would recommend taking all the courses he instructs. The classes would be highly interactive and practically-oriented and we can learn a lot from his feedback. Summarizing in 5 words: Informative, Applicative, Experiential, Inspirational and Intriguing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. IE 590 is a class you'll learn a lot about corporate intricacies and develop that kind of thought process. There is no textbook based learning, its upto you to make the most of it. Dr. Biller is amazing person to talk to and one can learn a lot by talking to him

If you want to not only learn class content, but learn how to be a desirable engineer to any company on the face of this planet - then TAKE ANY CLASS FROM DR. BILLER. Seriously, his knowledge and experience is unlike any other professor you will ever have in your entire life!

Dr. Biller is a great professor, who strives his best to bring in the knowledge to the class that he has learned in his professional and academic journey. Every Tuesdays and Thursdays were informative, great learning experience and I could walk out after the lecture with the confidence of learning something new that day. Labs are the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Biller is a highly skilled and experienced industrial engineer dedicated to helping his students understand the complexities of the industrial world. He is approachable and continuously refines his teaching methods. His focus on teaching and learning, coupled with his willingness to assist students, makes him an invaluable asset.

Amazing professor, and even more amazing speaker - I can listen to Professor Biller talk for hours. The course itself was quite intriguing and the assessment - based on presentations and assignments was a fun experience.

Prof. Biller is one of the best teachers I have encountered. He has a completely different teaching approach that I think is more than suitable for graduate students. The classes were entertaining and full of knowledge. Group presentations are scary at the beginning but on the presentation day you realize it's not that bad ;).

The professor stands out for his extensive industry experience and deep knowledge. He makes the concepts engaging, utilising real-world case studies and his dynamic teaching style. His approach not only enriches the learning experience but also prepares students for practical applications in their future careers.
He is an amazing professor who encourages the students and builds confidence in them.
Experienced and seasoned professional who is also an amazing professor. Conducts each class with passion and facilitates participation, learning and holistic thinking.

The professor used variety of teaching techniques in this course which made the course very interesting. With the flipped classroom, it allowed us to participate, discuss and learn from each others' experience. Professor also was very helpful outside of the classroom with industry and career advice.

Best class I have taken till date: IE5900 Digital Transformation in Industrial Business.

Unique class offerings:
1. Case Study discussions
2. Team based work
3. Covered various spectrums of Industry 4.0
4. Leveraged top-notch scale-at-lab, Purdue's Lambertus 
5. Real-time examples drawn-in for learning
6. Guest speakers invited
7. @Risk tool used

Took Supply Chain Engineering, one of the most useful and interesting courses in my degree. He is very knowledgeable and his 20+ year industry experience make his teachings relevant. Course was easy to follow with weekly business cases. Power hours felt long but it was ok. NO QUIZZES/EXAMS! Would take another class with Professor Biller, 10/10.

I had a good experience in this class. His lectures were overall clear and well organized. Quizzes were announced well ahead of time and exams were fair, with questions comparable to homework and lecture material. He supplements the book with his own handouts, which I found to be pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got an A. Mr Bickle  is very understanding of mistakes… I forgot any form of ID for the first exam lol. Also he doesn't make the homework or exams so nothing is his fault really. Taught me everything I needed to know
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: MA 265 (Lin alg)* Nothing particularly bad; he's a nice guy but I ended up just watching youtube videos and Boilerexams at home for all of the topics anyways.

Very monotnous lectures. It's very clear he knows what hs is doing and he is very smart, the lectures were just very hard to follow. He told me I should drop the class because he didn't think I would be able to get the grade i needed on the final

Bickle is not a very good lecturer. I went to 2 lectures total and just watched Chenflix. I took this course with zero calc experience and a bad history with math and got an A+. It's possible, but very hard. Before each exam, I took 16 practice tests, the past 30 yrs of em are public. Past exams are very similar to the present. Engage in recitation

dr. Bickle was definitely not a bad prof, but his monotone voice made it difficult to stay engaged during class. he also made the most basic problems unnecessarily difficult. The class itself is not bad at all, but the exams are difficult to get an A in. He seems like a good guy but I just did not enjoy his teaching style.
He seems like a really nice man but just not a great lecturer, he also loves putting none of the above as the correct answer choice, he does it.....a lot.

This Purdue calculus class is as challenging as expected, but the professor's teaching is ineffective. Lectures feel like watching homework being done, with minimal learning. Khan Academy and Chenflix are more helpful, especially since attendance isn't required. The material is tough, and the professor's monotone delivery adds to the difficulty.
His notes were very easy to follow and read, and he explained everything without mentioning that you should have already learned this or skipping over things.

Professor Bickle was dull and his lectures were very difficult to follow as he did not do enough example problems during lectures. After not doing well on the first exam, I went to the other professor and watched Professor Chen's videos online and I improved. Calculus 1 is a hard subject, and Professor Bickle did not help in this for me personally.

I appreciated his teaching style. Lectures were conveyed simply and straight to the point, providing examples that proved useful. Besides the obvious of calculus being challenging and only a few tough topics along the way, the class is manageable.

Bickle taught discrete math fairly well overall. Exams were reasonable if you had studied appropriately. The only criticism I have is that he went a little fast towards the end, but overall he taught the subject matter in discrete math well and also made fair tests. I think he taught discrete math better since he is more of an expert in this area.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I found that I learned from other professors sessions or online (Chen flix) lectures much more efficiently.

This professor didn't feel out of the ordinary for me, positively or negatively. This course was prob easier for me since I took AP calc in high school, but I feel like he did an average job at explaining the concepts. He also holds review sessions before midterms and finals. As long as you practice/take old exams before tests you'll prob pass.

(MA375 = discrete math) Lectures can be somewhat dull, but overall taught well, and any topics that are not in the book, he gives out handouts for (discrete math specifically). Assignments and exams are generally challenging but not unreasonable, though grading is sometimes questionable. Quizzes are announced in advance. Attendance is randomized.
In his lectures, he would overcomplicate topics, but the class was still manageable. It is a difficult course and hard to teach in a huge lecture hall.

Bickle is clearly too smart to be teaching calc 1. He finds a way to explain simple concepts in the most difficult ways possible. After each lecture it felt like I needed 180+ IQ to even begin to contemplate the theorems given. Learning it online or with TA's is much more effective then trying to decipher his PHD jargon.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his MA161 class and it was challenging. He does a lot of example problems in class but the test questions are more complicated and no calculators are allowed. He seems nice and passionate about calculus, but he may come across as "nerdy" to some. Just a warning, his tests are really hard and the class averages are usually around 60%-65%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes a cootie patootie.

Bickle does not know how to teach. If you take this course, be prepared to self-learn all the material via ChatGPT or other things. There are 2 quizzes a week at the end of each recitation, and attendance at the recitations is always mandatory. So good luck to everybody who takes this course, I had to drop it because of how hard it was.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Proffessor Bickle is a really smart and seems like a nice guy. Biggest complaint with the class was that the material covered in class was always extremely easy compared to the sorts of questions on the homework and especially the exams. Learning outside of class will probably be necessary.

If you want to learn pre-calc, don't chose Allan Bickle. Professor Bickle is a super genuis, he's written many papers on incredibly advanced alegbra and calculus; however, that does not make him a good teacher. Watching his lectures is essentially watching a guy do his homework with a monotone voice. He is incredibly boring and taught me nothing.

Honestly, He's a nice guy he just doesn't teach the material well. He is very passionate about the material, but treats every lecture like he is just doing homework and you are just watching. He doesn't teach, you are better off skipping class and just watching the professor delworth videos. I hope bickle becomes better at teaching.

Without a doubt, Professor Bickel teaches the material thoroughly. If you love doing math just for the sake of it, you will do just fine in his course. However, if you are like me, you will probably fall asleep in his class. His lectures are very dull.

The professor is okay, there were 8 extra credits for this course, but this course had 35 homework in total and each of them was pretty hard. This course had one quiz each week and if you did horrible just like me, then congratulations! You will most likely receive a B like me and this is a better situation.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great instructor and thoroughly explained concepts during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assumes that students remember pre calc lessons, covers some lessons quickly, is open to questions but explains things very quickly, somewhat standoffish but not mean

Bickle is not good at teaching. He teaches lessons quickly and doesn't seem to care if students understand. Quiz schedules are usually sent out far in advance. I recommend watching Delworth lectures online and coming to class on quiz days. He is pretty passive aggressive and I think that students are afraid to ask him questions because of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Horrible and grades quizzes wrong. And will give lectors not even about the homework.

Such a nice, caring professor. Class was super easy with a quiz/week, homework every 2 weeks, and 4 exams. He is eliminating book reviews and replacing them with exams and having all exams written and in class due to AI. Lots of super interesting guest speakers every week. Would recommend his class, but he's definitely an old-school teacher.

Mr. Coghill is one of the best instructors I have ever had. There are homeworks, quizzes, exams, and papers but as long as you do your work you can do well on everything. He brings in a lot of speakers so class is very interesting since its not just lectures. He takes the time to get to know each student and is incredibly caring.

THE BEST PROFESSOR AT PURDUE!! He always makes time for his students and treats them with respect, and oh my gosh, he's the sweetest professor I have ever had. I absolutely loved his class, and he wrote me a recommendation letter. As long as you try to pass, you will. I wish every SOC class were with Bill!

The kindest, most caring professor I have had at Purdue. His lectures are so interesting and he always brings in cool but informative speakers from the FBI, etc. Nothing is particularly hard and he has such a passion for teaching it makes you love the content more.

My favorite professor at Purdue! Meet him one-on-one because he is always interested in his students and their well-being. I loved every class taken with him and I hope to interview for his internship program. If he taught all of the law-related courses, I would be much happier attending class. He cares about what he's teaching and has experience!

Professor Coghill use to be a police officer which makes this course interesting. Lectures can be a bit dull and dry at times, but Professor Coghill's stories make up for it. Coghill cares a lot about his student and shows this by greeting each one individually as they come into class. Exams are a bit tough since not all the material is in lecture

Had him for criminal justice and i think the fact that he was a sheriff highly increased not only his credibility, but also his passion when teaching this class. Straightforward and helpful. Only downside was that the class schedule got changed around a lot.

An amazing guy that fosters phenomenal class discussion while providing real examples of everything that is covered. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and if you chat with him he will take interest in your life and ask follow up questions days/weeks later.
My favorite professor at Purdue, I wish he taught every Soc class

I enjoyed his class. He is a very passionate professor and he frequently asks for students' opinions on certain issues. Additionally, he takes the time to remember each students' name, despite the generally large class size.
My favorite professor, super funny and makes class enjoyable. I think what he cares about most is seeing effort, so just do that and you'll be great.
Very kind and truly cares for his students. I learned so much but he did not make it too difficult to understand. Minimal homework, lots of memorization. Great Course!!!!
He is very nice and wants you just to learn the material and not focused on your grade. Awesome guy as well.
Best professor ever
He is a great professor and wish I could take another class with him. If you are deciding if you should take this class or not, take it 100%.

He cares more than any professor ever will at Purdue. He brings in amazing speakers in TLI 213 and if you can take more classes from him I strongly suggest it. It is almost an automatic A, but it comes with some busy work and presentation, it is really about class engagement and makes you want to participate. 10/10!
Dr. Bitt is my favorite professor ever at Purdue. He truly cares about his students and I've met with him even after last semester whenever I had him in class!

Dr. Bitt is by far the best professor I've had at Purdue. He cares so much for each student and goes out of his way to get to know and create a special relationship with every one of them. He is very knowledgeable about his area and passionate about teaching. I will be taking every class that he teaches. He is THE BEST!
Comprehensive course in Thermalhydraulics/Heat transfer. I took ME version as well but I learnt lot more in this course than that.
Learnt a lot in this course.
He is fair in his grading process but exams ( particularly the first) are hard.
I thoroughly enjoyed this course. Dr. Bindra is phenomenal teacher, he not covers basic fluid mechanics fundamentals but also shows examples relevant to nuclear power systems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bindra did not prepare me well to understand fluid mechanics which is a fundamental class for an engineering. His lectures were all over the place. Prof Bindra was difficult to contact with and did not utilize TAs. His exams were nothing like anything in class and through 4 exams his averages never got above a 50%.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He openly admits to giving exams that do not contain content he has taught the class. He said he would've done good so we are just dumb. We had a 27% average on the exam so he spent the entire next lecture bragging how smart he is and how they told him he was the only man for the job so if we're doing bad it's because we aren't trying hard enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Blon is a controversial figure in the department. He can be a bit more picky than the average director, but all things considered, he really cares about his students and wants them to be them to be the best they possibly can be. If you plan on skipping class or not putting in 100% effort (no judgement here), switch to a different professor.

Every band director leads rehearsals and performances in their own way and has preference of repertoire, and Dr. Blon clearly cares about each performer in his ensemble and each instrument. In addition he cares about fundamentals like tuning and attention to detail. I think some of the reviews here are unfair or just inaccurate.

He was super chill during class and picked out good music. He wants you to be there but doesn't make a huge deal about absences/lateness. Not sure what band y'all have been in that plays through pieces completely before stopping for feedback? Overall, chill prof, less strict than my high school director. Not sure what other reviews are talking abt

Was disappointed in the inaccuracies of other ratings. He is not biased against anyone. He is a great man who truly cares. Directors have lives of their own, some have a harder time hiding the effects of their personal lives and state of the world on their mood than others, but this does not make him a bad director/person, he is one of the best.
I like that he actually pushes his students more than most other directors. He definitely loves music. Just do your part and you'll be good.

Honestly felt like I was back in high school band again. Petty, aggressive, and immature. He would continually stop the band just a few measures in to each run of a section of the song. The first time we played through any of the songs all the way through was at the concert. Awful experience, make any excuse to switch to another director.

You know Sisyphus in Greek mythology? That's what's it's like playing for this man. Just as we start to play beyond a few measures at a time, he stops to make some snarky comment and the proverbial boulder rolls back down the hill. He has anger issues on occasion. Band with Dr. Blon is a miserable time all around. Would give 0 stars if I could.
He's pretty funny and gives good feedback. A little intense sometimes, but otherwise a good teacher.
Dr. Blon is very intimidating, I quit band because of him. Avoid if you can

As with any music ensemble, show up and try your best and you will do fine. I wasn't a huge fan of his music selection or directing style, but those are very much based on personal opinion. All around a perfectly good director.

We couldn't get through the same 20 measures without being stopped 8 times over and over just for a new and insignificant comment each time (his comments could've waited until after). We also didn't have a full run-through of any of our 3 songs until the day of the concert because of Blon's inability to let us play longer than 20 measures.

Rather disappointing band experience. Corrections made to our group were vague and not constructive by any means. Quit band for the following 2 semesters (and maybe more) because of him. I presume I can see others' appeal for him and his (sometimes) upbeat nature, but in my opinion, not my favorite professor by any means.
Dr. Blon has a clear passion for music. But he can be scary sometimes, as he has high expectations for his students. I enjoyed his course overall.
Best CS professor and it isn't even close. Insanely good lecturer and great personality. Very responsive to student questions both in class and on Ed Discussion + office hours.

Listens to and actually handles student concerns. Very fair exams. Very fair grading. Helpful lectures and review sessions. Generous curve. Responsive on Ed Discussion. Kinda funny in lecture. Praying he teaches 381 when I take it, could not recommend more. So far, best CS professor I've had.

Amazing professor. Gave me hope of succeeding in Purdue CS. Exams are tough, but fair. Very similar to practice exams. Second half of the course content is quite simple to understand. Final cutoffs were VERY generous. Always responds on Ed. Takes our feedback seriously.

Incredibly kind professor, takes time to respond to Edstem with thorough and thoughtful answers. Exam questions are incredibly fair/just, attainable in an exam scenario, and relevant to course material. Lectures are well structured, and are interesting to pay attention to. Overall, the GOAT of Purdue's CS department!

Although CS 251 was a difficult class, Professor Blocki is very understanding and helpful. Very reasonable/fair, and seems to truly care about his students. In a 300+ person lecture, he takes the time to learn students' names and incorporates feedback. One of the best Professors at Purdue.
Incredible lecturer and fair tests. Explains concepts very thoroughly, is always available to answer students' questions, and takes feedback seriously.
Genuinely just a nice and caring person. You will learn a lot at lecture. Responsive on Ed. Very thorough with student questions.

Great professor with great lectures, makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Very responsive on Ed and seems to really care about seeing students succeed. However, the exams are very lengthy, yet the questions are overall pretty fair.
He's a great teacher and explains the concepts very well. He's also pretty funny. He gave us deadline extensions on homeworks and projects when required, and he's very helpful on Ed Discussion
Professor Blocki was a very good professor, with great lectures. The exams are long, but the questions are all fair. He is helpful on ed discussion and when asked questions.

Prof Blocki is a funny and caring professor. 381 is a hard course but he teaches the material well, gives fair exams and the curve makes up for it at the end. Highly recommend going to his office hours for additional help on certain topics/hws. Always answers student questions on Ed and open to feedback from students. PROF BLOCKI IS THE GOAT!!!

We got professor Blocki as a replacement for Sellke, and overall I think that he was more suited to teach the class. His explanations were very thorough for every topic, but the exams and HWs got much harder in my opinion. However, this came with a healthy curve after the final. He was a chill and funny guy, and I would recommend him for 251.

Good professor for a very difficult class. Increased difficulty when taking over for other professor. Amazing lecturer, good slides and good explanations, as well as receptive to feedback. Overall good experience, but beware the class difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a great lecturer, if you pay attention you should be able to do 3/4 of the homework on your own, however, there were some issues. He made his tests hard to finish on purpose; very lengthly, difficult theory questions. Also, not very lenient. Pretty good curve though. Average college prof.

Professor Blocki is an excellent lecturer, who explains concepts very well and makes them easy to grasp. I found his lectures quite engaging. Though his exams can be quite lengthy, they were quite fair in terms of difficulty. The homework and projects helped reinforce concepts that later showed up on exams.
Very long exams, but gives a good cutoff in the end. He's also very receptive to student feedback and gives amazing lectures. His explanations are great and going to his office hours really helps.

Best professor Ive seen at Purdue CS. Friendly to students and have good professional knowledge. I also have taken his CS 555 which is a crypto class, that class is much harder, but it is b/c the class, not the professor. The exam and the homework are all same flavor as CS 182 and CS 251.

Such a good professor. CS381 is a very difficult class, but Professor Blocki is an excellent teacher. Really open to questions and accessible outside class. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS (or one of the TAs) for help on the homework!!! Makes a huge difference and helps you for the exams. Extremely generous curve.

CS381 is one of the hardest classes you can take as a CS major. Despite the hard material, Blocki tried his best to explain the material . It is a very difficult class, but you can't blame the professor for that. He was very open to questions and graded very fairly. Overall, he tried to make the class as doable as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I had at Purdue! He's always available to answer questions in person, office hours and piazza. Very committed to helping his students learn the material. I zone out in class cuz I think he goes a little fast but that's probably a me problem. Curves generously.

Great lecturer, very nice and approachable outside of class and cares a lot about answering students' questions. Homeworks are tough, but if you start early and go to office hours, they get a lot more doable. Tests are a bit too long for the amount of time given, but he curves pretty generously at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best and most professional CS professors at Purdue. If youll be taking CS 381: 1) Go to every lecture. 5% iClicker does make a difference. 2) Start homework early (at least 3 days). 3) He gave a curve much more generous than the midterm cutoff, so dont be anxious like me just because you got a bad midterm grade. 4) READ THE TEXTBOOK!!

Professor Blocki is a fantastic lecturer. I enjoyed his class immensely and learned a lot. Even more, he is always available on Piazza answering questions even at 3 am some nights. His tests and assignments are tough but fair and he gives a solid curve at the end. Overall I would definitely recommend taking his class.

He has one of the most well run CS classes I've ever taken. The homework is error-free, engaging, he's very accessible in person and online, and hes an extremely fair grader. Always open to questions in class and encourages participation. Work is challenging but very doable. His specialty is in security, but he has very solid algos knowledge. 10/10

He's alright, the lectures are pretty decent to understand but one thing I like about Blocki are his office hours. He's willing to discuss homework answers during his Office hours which is pretty helpful. Make sure to take this course with your friends because it is pretty challenging and takes a lot of time commitment to get 100 on the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet professor who wants everyone to succeed. I was in a 7:30 lecture and she would purposefully start a few minutes late to allow a grace period for people getting to class. If you know/follow the syllabus, you should excel in this class. Show up and participate and you'll be fine and learn Spanish along the way.

Professor Blanca is wonderful. She's so funny and Spanish 202 was a really easy course as long as you did the VHL assignments every night. She is a very generous grader as well and she's super funny. The exams are also open note and online, which makes them very easy. Choose Professor Blanca if you're taking Spanish 4! She does take attendance also

Professor Cabrera was overall funny and understanding. She made Spanish fun! Her instruction was a little unclear and her lecture sometimes dragged on but overall the assignments were pretty simple. The class only has a few grades so just make sure to turn everything in.

Professor Cabrera was so much fun in class. There were only 7 of us, so I think the smaller class helped a lot also. She makes lectures fun and can sometimes get off track, but still a great teacher. She takes attendance, so it is important to not miss. Would gladly take again.

Attendance is required and there are technically readings, but you are able to get by by reading summaries before class so you can participate in the discussion. She likes to call on people and will wait for people to talk. No homework except for a discussion post each week. The final group project was pretty big but we had plenty of time.

Blanquita is one of my most favorite foreign language professors in this campus. She's very enthusiastic when teaching and ensures that we learn as much as we can. Being in this class helped me speak more fluently and also learned useful phrases that can be used in Spanish speaking countries. Take this class. You won't be disappointed!

Blanca is the best professor ever, she cares deeply about all of her students and she makes every class fun. Content wise, this class was easy and bettered by accent/ speaking in Spanish. ALSO: Pro-tip for this class, look up the books online/ rent them first because 3 are required and they are all expensive.

Very very nice professor. She is very conversational and the only issue with her teaching is that she gets off topic pretty often. She grades very leniently and as long as you show up you'll get a good grade.

This class was a great class to wake up to. The content was easy because it exactly the same as any spanish 5 ap class you would have taken. She has a great personality, and despite the lack of strict teaching, our class consistently had the highest test averages. I recommend taking this class for a gpa booster, and for a fun break in your day.
One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. If you actually want to learn Spanish, don't take her class. You won't learn anything. However, if you just want to get an A, go for it.
If you have to get through the class anyway, you might as well have a little fun doing it.  Is a very kind grader on the portfolios and in-class assignments.
Good teacher, easy class.
VERY nice professor, very cool and fun. Had lots of fun in class, and she made it very easy.

Dr. B was super easy and a nice lady overall. Homework were annoying because you have to get the answer perfect from book or she counts it wrong. Had three exams worth most of the grade, and 10 or so homework assignments and that was it for grades. Listen to lecture, take good notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She takes attendance but it's not for points.
Tests are most of your grade and there's not a lot of room for messing up but they're close to the slides (which aren't posted)
Good lectures, and she's really understanding, if you're going through something definitely contact her, she'll help
Homework can be confusing

Bonnie was really cool. Her lectures are kinda long and her homework can be tedious but easy. Her exams are easy if you use the study sheet she gives us, and she always adds points to boost your score. She gives deep examples that help and is just really fun to watch sometimes.
The exams are directly from her lectures, if you take notes and study the slides you will do fine. Her lectures are long and drawn out but not difficult.

Overall Dr. B. is an okay professor, she just sets up the class poorly. I didn't do great on the first exam which ruined my grade because she doesn't make lectures available until after homework is due, which was unclear in the syllabus. Class is very exam heavy (7 exams) and homework assignments are due two days after exams. Good intro class still
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be ready to read. She sets up the class so you don't know how the questions will be framed and then provides no help with constant reminders that everything opens and closes at noon. She does not care and lectures couldn't be more boring. She has a monotone voice and seems like she just does not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just no. She never communicated well with us about anything. Everything is due at odd times and is just not an enjoyable prof.

Bonnie was AMAZING. While the class was online, she always offered to give us help and feedback whenever she could. If you watch the lecture videos and take good notes, you are set to do well. Straight forward class with a manageable amount of work. Bonnie really cares about her students and even offered some extra credit for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took HK100 with her, however, it was online due to COVID. I recommend writing the examples and other information she says during lectures. The majority of the exams are applied questions and she uses her own examples. I found the lectures interesting and the homework is not too bad. She is passionate about her job and loves kinesiology.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class is challenging at times only due to her using concepts covered in class in ways that are not explicitly said in her slideshows. As long as you go to class, pay attention, and write notes on the slides AND what she tells you, you should end up with a decent grade in her class. Her voice can get monotonous at times.
Zero enthusiasm. Students always bored in class. WAY TOO strict on grading the reading assignments.
HK 100 is a requirement for most students and I believe she is the only instructor. Good Luck
Had this class last semester. Avoid Blankenship at all costs, material isnt difficult but lecture info if dramatically different from what is on the exams.
Take notes based on the power point then write more about the info based on what she said. Use the study guide while preparing for the exams! Go to class so you can get these notes!!
All exams are from the textbook- Her notes/lectures do not go along with them. Much more difficult than I was expecting for a 100 level course. I would not take a course with her again.

She uses the same PowerPoint every year, dont just write down whats on the slides, make sure to write down what shes saying and try to understand what she means. She gives a study guide out that you fill out so I find it helpful to do while in class as she goes. Every point counts so do well on homework and study for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 3 Exams, worth 90% of your grade. The way she grades them is nice. Say 50 questions and everyone misses 5 of those. She will decide to throw out 5 questions but you keep the points if you go them right. so if you missed all 5, then you are now at a 45 out of 45. But if you got them all right you end up with a 50 out of 45 on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took COM320 and had the worst experience. Unfair grading, unclear policies, lack of communication, and overall just a terrible professor.

One of the most useful classes I have taken at Purdue. I am a senior and want to work in healthcare so I appreciated the mock workplace projects

Class was mostly discussion-based. He is very passionate about health communication

This class was frustrating due to his ineffective teaching and lack of flexibility. He grades harsh and doesn't provide rubrics. The lectures are boring and he even said they were meaningless himself. He changed the entire course schedule midway into the semester due to an incident of his own. Overall, I would this class entirely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't typically write reviews but this deserves one. While you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching, this course was very disorganized. There were no review materials given for exams, and when asked he refused to post lecture slides for us to study saying someone might steal them. He's also very skeptical about AI.

Zero consistency, constantly changing assignments and due dates but didn't inform class. Admitted his lectures weren't helpful learning material. Terrible communication, no grading rubrics, would only give out good grades if we "wowed him." Was actually interested in the course beforehand, but was let down. Shame it's a required class for my major

I had really high hopes for this course but was significantly let down. Very little lectures, and most days are listening to your peers present. There is little content, and yet a majority of the class failed the first exam. He doesn't give out rubrics, is a boring professor, and ironically is a horrible communicator. The class got worse with time.

prof does not post slides, POOR grading criteria,waits too long for students to respond to a question when no one knows or cares. he thinks the topic is so interesting when its common sense.hes boring &monotone.its so much work for an intro com class&why is there so many projects that take hours to do&if your members are bad, goodluck getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dropping this class halfway through the semester because he changed a lot of his course expectations. When I went to class, he never actually lectured and had students teach the class their research report findings. Randomly started taking attendance and did not warn anyone beforehand. Ridiculously bad communication for a COM professor.

COM 378 (Introduction to Health Communication) is easily one of my most favorite classes that I've taken at Purdue. I received an A in the course, however, I had dedicated a lot of time in order to receive the grade I did since it's only out of 100 points. Show up to class, participate, & do the assigned readings, especially for the book proj.

Grades on personal preference and doesn't include rubrics. Very stubborn when you actually ask for rubrics in advance. He will take off small petty points on assignments where there wasn't a rubric but he expects you to know what to include and what not to include. If this class is a requirement, try get a professor who believes in rubrics.

I didn't have Crum. I had Zhou. But, I'm here to ponder about how someone could devise such evil. This class has shown me how true computer scientists code: with long, nearly-nonsensical script, and relentless hair loss from (attempting to) interpret such code. I thank Professor Crum for helping me decide to never touch computer science again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Crum is not a bad lecturer. The way he explains coding is easily digestible for beginners, and he himself is a nice guy. That being said, the class is very boring and slow if you have coded before. Crum does his best to be engaging, but the lectures are usually just an hour of him talking at you. His exams are also annoying and tedious.

Crum himself is not a terrible lecturer, but the class is super disorganized and it fails to properly teach programming. It teaches students the ability to read bad code, but provides little to no guidance on how to create good code. Studying and memorization will serve better than actual coding knowledge.

Egregious errors in basic C concepts--Claims that variables cannot be declared with the execution code. Quizzes are unfair and composed of content copied word-for-word from the otherwise mostly useless course notes/standards packet written by the department, which makes it impossible to earn an A even if you know C well; you need to learn "Crum-C".

It's clear that this professor cares about his students, it is just a very boring class. He does a good job lecturing, It is just very test-heavy. Coming from someone who hadn't coded before, this was a less-than-kind introduction to coding. That being said it is doable with enough work and TA office hours.

CS159 is a hard course. Ignore all of Prof Crum's old ratings. He is an amazing lecturer and most of the "issues" people have with CS159 are due to the course material. He is the course organizer, but he does care about his students. He's a nice guy, and if you're confused go to his office hours since nobody ever goes you will get 1 on 1 attention

The professor knows his stuff. But if you're taking CS 159 get ready to learn nothing about coding at all. It's frustrating for people who already know how to code. Those who don't know may be in for a rough time. Lots of theory/memorization. Crum is unreachable via email since he prefers physical office hours (which are really short and scarce).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I personally think Bill is a great lecturer, very engaging and makes the material very digestible. The problem with the class more lays within the class structure and design rather than solely with Bill. Although I would assume Bill has some hand in shaping the structure of the course, I think his lectures make up for the shocking test design
Class was super boring. The exams are not the worst things but some of the later exams suck.

Crum's lectures are actually really good for CS159. Since he is the course coordinator, you will learn the most from him. Unfortunately what makes this course hard are the points needed and how you obtain these points. If you do bad on literally any one portion and you can kiss your A away, but great lecturer overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hes a good lecturer but tough grader. This class is a weed out class. Study hard and learn tricks.

Crum is a caring prof and a good lecturer. The lab part of this class is terrible, the 10 minute quiz at the end is worth as much as an entire lab and the labs are tedious for only being 5 points. Grind past exams (especially the T/F questions), they suck but if you practice being a human compiler a few days out from the exam you will be fine.

ATTEND LECTURE! I almost got a C in the class even though I was getting 100% on labs/hw and Bs on tests because I was skipping the lecture quiz. Other people have said it better, you need to be a human compiler on exams, weird/unnecessary course standards etc. This stuff is necessary for advanced coding but useless if this is your only coding class

He is the course coordinator, worst  course plan ever. Lots of homework, however, you will have the same amount whichever professor take. However, Crum is very caring is accessible after the classes and will help you out a lot. I know a lot of people are scared of profs, but I recommend going to his office hours instead of TAs' hours
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: the exams butrse. Crum's goal is not to evaluate your knowledge of the material, but it is his mission to trick you and make you lose points in the exams with questions on codes that are by no means complient with the programming standards that he teaches himself.

The actual coding is not bad and neither are the labs. Do well on each lab quiz if you can. The exams though are super annoying and I believe that students are not given enough opportunities in class and lab to have practice with the types of questions that appear on the exams. Your grade in the glass is almost solely based on exam scores.

As someone who had never coded before, I was worried coming in, but it worked out well. I found Crum's lectures to clear and organized. The daily lecture quizzes are just participation grades, but are formatted exactly like test questions, which are very helpful to use to gauge test understanding. HW and labs usually aren't too long either.

the course itself is sometimes problematic; the Exams are structured in a way that requires student to become human compilers. Not everyone can be one. The lectures are also problematic; I learned more from drilling past papers than attending lectures.

The programming assignments aren't too difficult. You can usually figure out the direction to go in thanks to google. Don't rip off of google though, take ideas and create new code. Now the tests and quizzes, awful. I got a 90 on every homework, lab, and lab exam and am getting a C thanks to how awful the tests and quizzes are.
Bro did not need to go that hard on the homework assignments...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible

Prof. Crum is a fine lecturer. Very clear, laid out presentations make learning the C language easy. He sometimes can ramble about specifics. The course is harsh and unforgiving when grading, using an autograder only. If unimportant output lines (i.e. symbolic boxes) in the code aren't EXACTLY as in examples, you'll get an 80 on the assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Crum's lectures were really useful and I learned a ton in his class. The structure of the class is a bit different than what people would expect from a programming class ie not learning recursion until later in the semester than expected, but the structure helps reenforce the concepts. He is great to talk to and always helps out if needed.

Paradoxically Crum is best if you've never programmed before; if you have you'll have to adjust to his peculiarities in how he refers to things and how he codes because he will NOT tolerate any variation. The course is exam-heavy (60%+ exam grades) and those exams are based around being a human compiler and memorizing how Crum refers to things.

As an FYE student that had some CS experience (& hated it) before college, this class surprised me & I actually liked it. Course is structured a little funny-more experienced coders are the ones that have issues with CS159. Prof. Crum is EXCELLENT at lecturing. They were thorough and clear. TA's are VERY helpful-seek help from them outside of class

In my opinion, Crum is a great lecturer who really does care about his students doing well. However, the lab quizzes and exams are definitely sucker punches in comparison to the work done on homework and lab assignments. CS159 is one of my favorite FYE courses, just try your hardest because there really is no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chill guy. Don't expect to learn much from lecture. The HW and labs is where you learn the most. Tests are hard because he tests your theory knowledge as well as coding literacy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Good op Bill Crum makes tests all about how to read bad code instead of writing good code. Homeworks and labs arent bad but the tests will bore a hole through your confidence. Beware :/

Lectures and lecture book are both helpful in learning the material. Being someone who had never programmed before, I found the exams difficult. In my opinion, doing the homework didn't help with the exams. By the end I got the hang of it and managed a good score on the final.

As a professor, he is all you could ask for, but as a course I think CS159 needs some improvement. He knows everything there is to know about C and the lectures are probably the most useful of any class I've ever taken. As for the course, the exams just test your human compiling skills and the labs/hw take too long for how little they are worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of time. I had no previous experience with coding, but I found his class manageable as long as I put in lots of time. His tests are difficult, but become reasonable if you review and practice the concepts in the homework/labs. Don't buy the textbook. He mostly relies on lecture information.
great lectures and a great intro to programming class for someone who has never programmed before
does a good job of explaining, but very work-heavy course (seems a lot like busy work)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class should be renamed "Class to test who can compiled code in their head the fastest". Absolutely doesn't test on how well someone can code, rather who can compile insanely difficult/tricky codes in their head for 3 points out of 100/150 on an exam. HW's are worth 5 points, yet take hours to complete,grade depends on tests mostly, never again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He gets a bad wrap, but I didn't have a problem with him. I wasn't doing so well in this class, and I went to office hours to get some pointers on how to improve. He was very helpful and nice and helped me get a plan. The class itself is difficult. The exams don't match the homework's or labs at all, and if you've never coded before, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff and is very nice during his office hours.

The Bill Crum of the past that you hear about from students who had him in the mid 2000s is not the one you will get these days.  Guy seems to have mellowed out something fierce, and is one of my better professors this semester.  Very approachable during office hours and is an excellent and enthusiastic lecturer as well. Respect his rubrics though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Crum is not a bad professor, he knows his concepts well and is prepared for class. Having said that, I wanted to fall asleep during his lectures. He is so boring!  The exams are also very hard and don't reflect your coding skills at all.

The exams are very difficult. They do not reflect if you are good at coding. Each question has an option of none of the above causing you to always second guess yourself. The exams are also just a bunch of trick questions. They don't show how well you can code.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's much better than bunning, explains concepts well. The homeworks and labs are graded kind of hard, but if you pay attention in class, skim over the book, and review the general concepts before the tests, you should be able to pass with an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As a Computer Engineer, Bill's explanations of programming logic are spot on. Many people complain, but really, programming is NOT easy to explain. I think he does a pretty good job of getting inexperienced engineers a good basic understanding of programming.
Good teacher; lectures are sometimes boring

I will never understand the hate on Crum. He is an excellent instructor who teaches difficult material; but I guess hate comes in such a territory. He is especially great during office hours, giving you clear feedback on what to fix in your code. Would highly recommend.
Teaches tough material well. Tries to keep things light/humorous. Very pleased

Crum gives great lectures for beginners to CS. He is clear and dynamic with his voice, and gladly takes questions during lecture. If you like taking your own notes like myself, you may find his pre-made (mandatory) notes handbook mildy annoying to use.

He is the worst professor I've had at Purdue in 3 years. He knows the material by heart and teaches it relatively well, but as a person he is awful. When you come up to him asking for help he mocks you. He takes clicker points for credit, gives assigned seats in the 300 person lecture and switches them up every couple weeks to stop cheating.

A good lecturer. Your grades reflect your effort. People who just start coding will find it hard. I know coding, but I still need to spend time on reviewing, because his tests focus too much on the details of C which should be taken care of by machine or looked up when you code. He can't really test anything else, because of course policy.
Crum is a good prof. Very clear in his lectures and he is clear while explaining them. I recommend him for any CS class.
He has improved a lot! He teaches pretty well and is always helpful during office hours.
I don't really enjoy coding so it wasn't the most interesting class for me.

Crum is a great lecturer. The class notebook he uses is very helpful and he works off it every lecture. If you attend the lectures and put in effort I would say its easy to succeed. Yes the homework and tests are difficult but they are as expected.

Crum is a fantastic lecturer. I had his class at 7:30am, but he was always on time and ready to teach. He is exceptionally clear. If you go to his office hours, he will be more receptive than by email. Zero tolerance for cheating. Tests can throw you for a loop, but there's nothing unexpected. If you know the basics of Matlab, learning C is easy.
Hard course with warm hearted but bit unhelpful professor

Show up to class, take  notes for the notebook he wrote. There are no surprises on the exam, everything comes from the homework, labs and lecture. Reading the book helps for homework and for the lab quizzes (sorry I didn't realize this earlier). Concise on the material, good pace and he makes the exams, so try to study with previous exams.

I found his class to be very straightforward and enjoyable. The lectures were always clear, the standards were strict but not unreasonable. Anyone with any coding experience at all should do fine. If you don't have any experience though, be prepared to work and put in the extra time. It will pay off later on.

I don't understand why people are so upset with Crum. He is helpful, uses the notes every lecture, and refers to the textbook. Although the homework and labs are 5 points, they are a bit difficult. This class is easy if you're in ENGR132 at the same time. I was scared going into this class because of the reviews, but I'm glad I risked it.

Why in the world would you not allow students to use concepts that are introduced later in the course? Students should be able to learn extra material and practice that in assignments without being marked down for knowing their stuff.

The class is hard. I came in with no prior programming experience and I was immediately lost. It takes the effort of ALWAYS going to the help sessions and office hours to pull a good grade. I also recommend at least knowing the basics of C language programming before getting to the class.

Not as bad as people make him look. He is extremely helpful if you go to office hour. Don't be scared to go! I took honors with him and it was totally fine. Don't miss assignments and read the syllabus! It's not difficult to get an A.
awful
It's a difficult class but he's a good professor. He's very understanding and helpful if you go to his office hours.

Its a hard course. I never did programming before and generally suck at computers. But I was determined to pass. I stuck with it and got help from Crum when I needed it. Now I'm on track to get an A this semester.   If you do the work and get help when you need it you'll do fine. But you actually need to apply yourself.

this is an intro class but he makes the homework and labs impossible to do for a beginner. you work with a team for lab but you're not allowed to work with other people for hw. he runs everyones hw through a system that highlights similarities in hw submitted and then busts you for cheating if your code is similar to another person. horrible prof.

This class was hard but not impossible. From personal experience, students who complain about it are lazy and just want someone to give them "the answer". Read the text, do the homework and exercises and you'll be OK.

GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS EVERY WEEK AND YOU'LL BE FINE. Seriously. He is a really great professor if you actually take the time to talk to him and try to learn the material. The class is pretty difficult. I retook the class because the exams killed me. They're really tricky but do-able in the end. A's are totally possible; you just have to work hard.

To be honest, his class is hard. He is a really smart professor, and I guess his IQ is higher than 150. I really enjoy his classes, because almost every word he said is useful, and helpful. He can find the problems in your codes within 1 minute in his office hour. His exams are hard, but it is possible to get an A. I really missed him.

he absolutely sucks. he's a bad lecturer and his policies are strict and unfair. avoid this class at all costs because u'll hate it unless you're good at coding. he doesn't teach well at all (esp. for beginners) and his exams are hard and super tricky. he makes u buy a $100+ textbook and a lecture notebook but he never even TOUCHES the the txtbook
Go to his office hours and it is SUPER helpful. Tests are pretty difficult though, a lot of tricky questions. Overall, it's not as bad as people say.
Fairly good lecturer. Not as bad as people say. However, he is unwilling to answer emails, or most questions in general. Fairly arrogant as well.

This guy definitely knows his stuff. Make sure you listen in his lectures, and not even fall asleep for a second, because every word he says is important. His exams are tricky, and the HWs and labs require a lot of procedural thinking, but with enough practice (and a lot of hard work), they aren't bad at all.

Hard class. Bottom line was he was rude and inconsiderate. I had no prior programming knowledge and I went to office hours for help, it was useless. He makes you feel inferior for not knowing the material. Listen just because you know it doesn't mean your students automatically do. It was ridiculous.
Good class decent proff. If you don't like CS don't take the class, he won't slow down for you.
Hard Grader, but a good lecturer. I'd definitely take a class from him again. He knows his material.

He is really a great professor. The class, hw and labs are hard if you dont have prior programming knowledge. Oh and if you get horrible lab partner you are screwed too. But the prof is very helpful and even if you dont understand a thing he is willing to build you from scratch if you go to his sessions. Take help from the TA s too.
No experience going in. Learned a ton. Got an A. Interested in learning more programming after this class. If you put in just a litle bit of effort, this class will not be hard.

I like this kind of professor. He really challanges his student and want to train his students into real programmers. To be in his class/lab. You need to be at least very clever or hard working. programming needs a lot of inteligence especially in his class. if you are not clever or hard working? Oh good luck!

Phenomenal teacher. He actually challenges the students to think like a programmer. I would know, I've been doing it for years before this class. For someone to fail this course, they have to actively refuse to learn the material because he does everything he can to make it clear.

the worst lecturer you can have, he busts students for cheating all the time on the hws, the tests are extremely tricky, hw's are hard, NO CURVE, makes sure to fail half the students. Do Not take this class unless you have programming experience. I would suggest Chm 116 as a science selective instead of this crap class.
He is really a good professor. The lecture is clear and really helpful. Not as bad as people said.

This professor is very clear and concise. He makes it a point not to waste your time so everything he says is important. Unfortunately, this means it is easy to get lost if you zone out for a minute. Don't listen to bad reviews though. It's not his fault people are lazy. I had ZERO prior programming knowledge and still got an A with minimal e

This professor perplexes me more than most.  His lectures are very good and well taught, and if you go to him for help, he is honestly the nicest guy.  As for his exams, they're horribly tricky and confusing.  Additionally, some of the homeworks and labs are hard to figure out.  I'd heavily recommend taking this class in the off (Fall) semester.

This guy is actually a good professor. He makes his lectures matter, he cares about his students, and is very helpful when it comes to exam conflicts. He is paranoid about cheating but all CS profs are so deal with it. He has a bad rap because programming requires intelligence and thinking, things they don't teach in school anymore. Very good prof.

A pretty bad teacher, he does care about any of the students. You need previous programming knowledge to be successful. The worst teacher I ever had in college. His exams are ridiculous, he tries to make you fail. I feel a true professor wants the students to succeed, so I do not think Bill Crum is a true professor.

The worst teacher I have ever had he isn't even a professor and I would never call him one.  His tests are made to trick everyone.  His lectures suck all he cares about are making sure he gets his iclicker quizzes. Don't take this class if you don't have to.
He is such a nice teacher! You should listen to his class! Although the exam is kind hard to do~
This Prof has a really bad rap, but was actually really nice to me when i took his course. he even let me retake an exam

Seemed like a nice guy. But his lectures were hard to understand and his tests were impossible. Even if you knew your material he would purposely try to trick you. Really hard for students without prior programming background.
He is very good at programming, I dont know about teaching.
He is a really good teacher and a nice guy. He knows what he is talking about for sure. As for the course, it's really hard
Bill Crum is full of himself but he is a good professor. The exams in his class are really tricky.
Difficult Class, Programming coding is too hard, without experience, exams are really tricky, PLS DON'T take this class unless you absolutely have to !!!
bill crum the man.his exams are sometimes tricky. but he knows what he is teaching and actually he is quite funny

He's a cool guy! He's nice and friendly if you go to his office hours to ask for help. He does a great jo on preparing the lectures and course itself. As long as you understand it, you know that it's all for you to study programming!

Does not help students at all, lecture is too hard to follow, if you dont have programming experience you might as well not even try. You need to have major programming experience to pass. First class at Purdue I have had a terrible time with and its a 100 level class??

Bill gets a lot of bad rap from people who don't want to take the effect to sit down and practice programming on their own.  If you try to understand and make sure you don't get behind, this class will go smoothly.  I didn't know anything about programming and got an A
my new favorite teacher since he allowed me to retake a test. i know he has a bad rap but maybe he is nicer in the summer
Bill was very helpful and friendly. I'm not sure why he has such a bad reputation. I couldn't program, now I can... 'nuff said. Good guy, good prof.

Extremely easy course; lots of people hate him simply because they're terrible at programming. Seriously, this class is one of the easiest offered at this mediocre university. He is very helpful, and contrary to popular opinion, the exams are EXTREMELY easy. It's all very basic logic.

Don't let people fool you, he is a good teacher. The people giving bad reviews just suck at programming, and are blaming the first person they see, which happens to be the man that taught them. I put forth very little effort in this class, and I got an A+, with no prior programming experience. Go to class, listen, and take notes and you'll get an A
Good
Good guy that has a bad rep
This guy sucks!He make the exam to fail the students!40 percent of students fail the class in spring2009!!1

No matter how bad your life is at least your not Bill Crum.  He makes the unibomber look like a saint and a troll good looking by comparison.  He fails as many students as possible to forget that he is a short bald fatty.  If you cherish happiness you will run as far as you can from this guy.
doesn't have good handwritting at all.... wait, was that an s, or a 7?
Class is easy, test are easy, basically if you read the course manual you will have the answers to the test, and just pay attention in lectures and you will be well off in the exams

Bill Crum teaches like his students already know how to program. He acts like we should know everything he does, and when he does explain things, he does them very broad and unclear. The text book doesn't help much either.
Tests are made to fail students.
Not a horrible teacher, but he struggles in his ability to clearly display programming i.e. you cannot read the content displayed, which is the his main way of communicating in lectures
dont take the class if hes teaching it!!
RUN AWAY WHEN YOU STILL CAN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

first, he is not even a professor. he's a lecturer. second, being in his class is by far the most boring and annoying thing in the world. third, his tests are meant to trick students so he can fail them.
Took the class online over the summer, so ive never met him.  Seemed nice enough tho
He should retire.
Was an okay teacher. Goes over stuff a little fast, but it was good. Seemed helpful, and answered all questions no matter how ridiculous.

I heard a lot of bad things about this class before I took. Apparently, though, the class has gotten a lot easier. He no longer puts trick questions in his exam. Still, you do need to put work in the class to get a good grade. Lectures tend to be a bit boring.

His class is not for those who can't program. Retook course b/c his exams have a lot of tricks that I always missed. Easier second time around. He is tough, but he is very knowledgable, and if you seek him out in office hours he WILL help you. Nice guy if he knows you're putting in the effort. Put in the time and you'll do fine.
