reviews.comment: Great course, teaches with passion and is a great introduction to EEE. I struggled on the first exam cause I didn't prepare well for the open note format (dont rely on your notes, you wont have time to finish if you spend too much time looking for similar example problems) and homework questions were sometimes a bit vague, but still would recommend

A nice change of pace from other CE Courses. The material and expectations are pretty straightforward. I really appreciate that he isn't the type of professor to throw you for a loop with exams. The homeworks can occasionally be a bit long, but they're never obscenely difficult. pretty close to 10/10 imo.

Great lecturer, they are a bit dense with information but that's why the exams are open notes/open everything but the internet. The homeworks take some time but are largely methodology over correct answers. Very passionate and always tries to get people to participate but that got harder online. I hope he continues to lecture and gets better soon.

Class and professor are fine.The one thing that can be improved is how grades are done. Grading in this class is highly dependent on the standard deviation and how others do. You can get 90s on exams and not get an A due to the approach to grading. Last semester I think only 8% of the class got As.

I thought his content would be easy to follow and understand, but when I took his class in the Fall of 2022, I think most people suffered. Don't take this class with him.

reviews.comment: This course is graded by few things but Dr. Blatchley tried his best to make us understand the topics. It could be challenging but everything will be fine

Such a great professor! Honestly, the best one I have had at Purdue so far. Very respectful and was always willing to help out with any comprehension or homework problems. Genuinely wants students to learn and you can tell he actually enjoys teaching. Tests and quizzes were pretty straightforward. If you study and do the work it's easy to get an A
Class was phenomenal. Lectures were very easy to follow and understand the subject matter.

Dr. Blatchley is very knowledgeable regarding water systems, but unfortunately has an assumption that all others share his level of enthusiasm and knowledge on the same topic. He does not give feedback on quality of written work or presentations. This experience was extremely disappointing, and grading was further unjustified with little feedback.

Great teacher. Exams are pretty easy and are open book open note. Homework can be a little tricky but helps prepare you for the exams. Make sure you write down everything he puts on the board he likes to give acronyms on his exams. Always there for the students and legitimately wants students to do well. Teaches CE 350 during the spring semester.

He was helpful over email & during office hours, he was flexible if the office hour time didn't work and needed to schedule a separate session. I would seek out another class with Blendell. He rambles a lot in his lectures and a lot of it is not useful. The lectures don't follow the homework or the exam. Get ready to teach yourself everything. Exam is similar to HW but not exactly. He is good at responding to emails. He's terrible with technology and not very organized. Overall, I don't recommend this class. Tests are hard.

The greatest professor I have ever had since attending Purdue. Anyone who has him for CE211 is guaranteed a B. If you put even the tiniest bit of effort, you will easily get an A. He even gives you extra time on exams.
Professor Boor is an outstanding professor. He creates a safe and cooperative learning environment where students feel safe to ask for help.

Dr. Boor does a great job of applying the problems presented in class to real-world, civil engineering situations. He breaks down the problems in a way that makes the more complicated problems seem much simpler.
Dr. Boor does an incredible job teaching CE 211. He communicates everything clearly and effectively and gives us students all resources to succeed in his class.

Prof Boor does a very good job at explaining topics in a way that is easy to understand. I really appreciated taking a minute before each exam to explain the problems and make sure the students didn't miss anything.

Professor Boor was very helpful during lectures by explaining the concepts well and working out relevant problems in class. I felt prepared for the quizzes and exams through his teaching and
homework assignments.

Dr. Boor is an amazing professor and one I will remember. He learns his students' names, which is both impressive and meaningful. He is very concise and prepares us well for exams, homework, and quizzes.

Professor Boor is a great professor always willing to answer any questions and makes the exams very similar to the practice exams. Understand how to solve the problems on the practice exam well and you'll be perfectly fine for the exams.

Go to his lectures to take notes. If you miss them you will have to teach yourself the material, which is not difficult if you have a good basis of basic chem/physics/math. Easily get As on quizzes if you understand the hw, and easily get As on exams if you understand the hw/quizzes. He gives great practice material to help you not trick you
Dr. Boor teaches this class incredibly well. His communication is clear, and he ensures students have every resource needed to excel.
The way he speaks is infuriating and he will randomly give a homework or a quiz where you have to use a method or formula that he never taught in class.

Go to lecture because he fills in notes in class and does not post them. Homework and quizzes are just like the exams, he's not trying to trick you. He also will do what he can to get to know you even in a class of at least 120 students. Would go back to his class in a heartbeat!!

Attendance is not mandatory except on quiz days, same days homeworks are due. Start the homeworks early since some are quite time consuming even when they look shorter. Exams are a fair difficulty but long.

Exams + Final are very similar to the study guides, which are just past problems with his work shown in solutions. Quizzes are similar to 1 or 2 homework problems. Walks through every exam, the final, and quiz before you start. Extends exam time. Does NOT post exam averages, only tells you the median. Only has blank lecture templates posted online.

Dr. Boor is a caring professor and very proactive about answering student questions. Lectures can be somewhat monotone, but the material is taught very well. Dr. Boor provides previous exams which provide amazing practice. Quizzes and tests, while possibly long, are overall very doable with practice material given. Would highly recommend!

Class was organized very well by the professor. I found the material very interesting, and it was clear which concepts we needed to learn for the quizzes and exams. Also, Dr. Boor is very understanding and listens to his students.

Lectures are a bit slow and monotone, but content is well explained and clear. Homework can be a bit long at times, but is not bad. Class has quizzes given bi-weekly, closely related to HW. Exam are fair and closely resemble past exams and quiz problems. Highly recommend Dr. Boor as a professor.
Boor cares about his students and is helpful and willing to meet outside of class to answer questions. Lectures are a bit dense, but helpful in explaining concepts covered on the exams.

He reads off of empty slides that he fills in each lecture, but doesn't post the filled-in slides after so if you miss the lecture, read the book. Some of the quizzes were rough but overall if you did the HW you'll do fine. The two midterms were rough, especially the second. The final exam was pretty easy and he is lenient towards your final grade.

Lectures can be a little tough to sit through as Dr. Boor is monotone, otherwise he's a great professor. Homework grades are very generous, and exams are very similar to study guides and quiz questions he provides.

Lectures are a bit slow and monotone, but Boor is still a very good teacher; content is clear and well-explained. Grading on partial credit exam problems can be harsher than it needs to be, but homework grading is kind.
His lecture notes are great and he is really good at explaining the course material. Exams are fair if you prepare properly.
He is good at explaining concepts in class. He makes sure we have detailed notes so we can follow the course material. He does a good job answering questions about the homework.

This course is useful for anyone interested in respiratory health and pollutant exposure or  wanting a better grasp on material balance calculations. Very energetic and caring professor.

If you like a clear structure, are willing to attend lectures, and like examples, he is the person you want to teach you. His lectures are formatted logically, he tells you what to focus on and what to ignore for exams, and he explains things thoroughly and clearly. He's possibly the best professor I've had, he makes it very easy if you attend lecs
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Boregowda is a great guy and makes statics a breeze if you actually show up to class every day.

This guy's him. Never have I met a professor with such passion for a subject and his students, a rare exception to the professors across the globe and possibly beyond. A man that values his student's learning more than the rubric is a man that deserves praise, respect, and honor; and don't get me started on his charming and engaging personality.

He is literally the most thoughtful and caring professor I have had at Purdue. Very easy to approach and explains concepts so well. His lectures correspond exactly to the HWs and exams and he preps you very very well while also making the lectures fun to attend. 10/10 would recommend for any class.
Boregowda was one of the best professors here. Clear and concise lectures that directly help with homework and exams. Mixes in funny stories here and there.

It was obvious throughout the semester that he wanted to teach machine design just as little as we wanted to learn it - but he still gave informative lectures and dropped much-needed hints for the exam questions. Funny guy and would love to have a beer with him.

Professor Boregowda is by far the most caring professor I have had the pleasure of having thus far at Purdue. If you care about his class and go to all of his lectures he will remember. He is extremely smart and related real-world examples to his content which helps a ton! Overall I could not have asked for a better statics professor!

350 characters will not effectively describe this superb professor. Well-written, example-filled notes posted after every lecture, great HW hints, great industry connections for content application, timely emails, hilarious side comments & somehow great pep talks, he treats every student more than just a number. Purdue needs more people like him!
Prof Boregowda is the best professor at Purdue. He gives great lectures for ME270 by giving great and solved examples.
He is very nice and explains things well.
One of the nicest and smartest professors I had. He is passionate about the subject matter and makes things interesting with stories from his time in industry.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was by far the best professor I have ever had. He answered questions clearly and communicated outside of class with his students. He provided as many resources as he possibly could to help us learn. He gave ample homework help and made sure to stay connected, even though his class was online this semester. Purdue needs more like him.

Professor Boregowda was a great professor for ME 200, he was the only professor online, and while that was unfortunate he made the best of it. He posts all of his lectures and his notes, as well his own personal notes that he bases the lectures off of. The extensive materials he provides allows you to review these complicated concepts on your own.

Professor Boregowda is a so personable. He genuinely cares about his students and is interested in their livelihood both inside and outside the classroom. He is very easy to get to know and very helpful. 100% would recommend him to any ME student
One of the most caring ME professors

Boregowda is such a great professor, and now my favorite in ME. Thermo 2 is a hard class, but he does all of the right things to make it easier and enjoyable. He gives HW hints and great suggestions to prepare for exams. He cares about students more than bell curves and does everything he can to make sure everyone succeeds.

Told us exactly how to prepare for the exams.  Posted well-detailed notes online and referenced them directly in class.  Pre-announced quizzes.  Made a traditionally difficult class seem must less overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite professor I have had. Work hard and show him that you are trying and you will be fine.
Simply one of the best professor I have studied under so far. Take him if he is available for any the ME class.

Professor Boregowda is one of those rare professors at Purdue who realizes that it is more important that students learn the material than having a perfect bell curve. Lectures are interesting as he does crack jokes and shows neat videos that relate the material to the real world. Most importantly, go to class. He knows who skips and who doesn't.

This is by far my favorite Professor! If anyone ever needs to take ME 200 (Thermo I) make sure that he is your professor. He honestly wants nothing more than to see his students succeed! He is makes material understandable and gives good examples. He also creates his own packet of notes for his students which is super helpful!

He teaches a hard subject, but he breaks it down and makes it easier. He's always making jokes so lectures are a little more enjoyable. His office hours are pretty helpful and he does his best to make thermo seem . Probably one of the better thermo professors at Purdue. I'd recommend him

This Professor is not the easiest, but he really wants all of his students to succeed. He used lots of economic examples to help us try and understand the concept. I highly recommend this professor and plan on taking another one of his courses.
Makes Thermodynamics relatable for all engineering majors not just MEs. Provides an extensive notes packet for each chapter.

Professor Boregowda is probably my favorite professor thus far at Purdue. His class is easy if you pay attention. He makes lectures interesting, and always has tons of examples that are applicable to students.

He is a great professor with a true passion for business.  He's worked for some impressive companies in the past (like NASA) and always has interesting, relevant stories to share that add to the lecture.  Although the textbook is not mandatory, I highly recommend purchasing it as the exams are a 50/50 combination of lecture and the textbook.

Boregowda is a great teacher! He provides useful lecture notes and goes through example problems in detail. To help prepare for exams, he gives out a packet of review problems with detailed solutions! Plus, you're allowed a cheat sheet for quizzes and exams. Take 305 with Boregowda and you'll be glad!
Great teacher overall, yes, can go quickly through class but he will slow down and go over things if you ask.  Great reviews before tests, very helpful. I really enjoyed his teaching.

He is a good professor and willing to help students.  I felt he goes too fast for his lectures, because we have to finish one chapter for one or two classes.  Fortunately, this class is non-cumulative and it is not hard considered to other management classes

Great lecturer, well organized course. People used to disrespect him and talk over him in 180, but glad to see him get more respect now. He's actually really really intelligent if you listen to him lecture. Amazing prof, would happily take again in the future.

Pretty good for how new he is to the department. Listens to and actually handles student concerns. Seems readily available outside of class. Lectures are a little bland and not as good as Blocki's, but still useful. Responsive on Ed Discussion. Generous curve. Fair exams and fair grading. I can see him becoming a 5/5 professor in the future.

Well structured class, very response and kind on Edstem and willing to have conversations with students. Unfortunately CS 251 is a large lecture, which doesn't suite this professor, I think he would be better suited lecturing to a high level smaller class. Overall though, a good professor.

Professor Borkowski was an incredible professor that it is clear cares a lot about his students and wanting to see them succeed. Professor Borkowski's lectures were informative and engaging and would consistently answer students questions on Ed Discussion when assignments were due to make sure all students were helped.
Good lecturer. Not much else to say. You will gain a lot from attending lecture.

Lectures are not useful, as he spends time reviewing niche examples that are not tested, rather than covering the actual course content. Recommend avoiding him.
He is not bad, it's just that his way of teaching is a bit boring. The grading of this course is messed up which has nothing to do with the professor, but still....

He doesn't organize the course but his lecture was kind of boring but he is really nice. I emailed him outside of class and he was really nice and helpful. Overall the course is difficult because of the test and there is LOTS of HW.

most of your learning will come from the homework. You will have to study for the tests, or your grade will be terminated. The test material is very specific and focuses on either small details from the lectures, or wring a lot of code on paper.
DO NOT USE AI! It's allowed but if you rely on it you WILL fail every test.

stop talking during lectures and ur chill. borkowski doesn't manage most of the course and its his first year teaching. stop complaining about the tests and the group project because he doesn't manage that. just ask for help and you'll get help

Borkowski is the goat. He helps me through all of my homework during my office hours and is super nice. People are just whining about him. He didn't write the tests or the homework. Lecture are helpful and have information you need but most people just talk during class and don't pay attention. If you actually listen you'll get an easy a.

Not the most engaging lecturer, but lectures provided sufficient content and he was willing to explain topics further outside of class. The class was mostly focused on projects and homework, and I would recommend going to his office hours if you ever need help.

reviews.comment: Firstly, this semester, while the course was a lot harder, it wasn't due to this professor, the course just became harder overall for both sections. Now, when it comes to my rating I have a lot of reasons why. He is very helpful in office hours, and helps students after class. Keep practicing, go to office hours, and practice handwriting code.

He's a boring lecturer that explains concepts to some degree, but the only way to learn the material is through the homework. He is indifferent to your situation if you end up in a terrible group for the team project, as he believes learning to work with a team is an essential part of the experience, even if some group members drop the class.

Lectures were hard to get through due to his robotic delivery and the volume of meaningless content. Java concepts were conveyed abstractly and with little regard to their application and their relationships with past material. You'll spend an obscene amount of time on homework and projects, and the tests will make you question your life choices.

Very monotone and dry lecturer who fails to engage his students and clearly convey the material, instead spending copious amounts of time covering Java on a conceptual level, rarely demonstrating anything in practice, obscuring the relationships between the different concepts and their applications. Still competent and knowledgeable in the subject.

Very knowledgeable but everyone talks so you can't hear unless you're at the front of the class. The course being hard isn't his fault, exams are just poorly designed and some of the lab/hw assignments are extremely vague and not helpful. This was his first semester teaching, so it's understandable. He does go too fast on his lectures.

So many points were taken off for bad test questions (worth 60% of your grade). Tests are horrendous and in general the requirements for assignments or tests in this course were worded horribly. The content is not hard but is entirely based on if you interpreted the question the same way as he did.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were an absolute snoozefest. The only real way to learn was to do the homeworks at your own pace. The group project can also be disastrous if you have incompetent team members. The format of the exams can be a little questionable.

His lectures were very monotonous and he didn't do a great job explaining concepts. His poor descriptions of how different interactions occurred made it difficult to understand some relationships at a conceptual level. Class wasn't super difficult but it's because it's an introductory course.

Overall great guy and going to lecture was enjoyable. There are very few assignments (homework, cases) and the exams are weighted heavily. Gives useful Excel practice over other 310 sections and the homework is exactly like the in-class examples. Anything... and I mean anything... is fair game on his exams. Loves honors students.

Very good and engaging. I am in/took MGMT310H which is no textbook. His exams are difficult, but only has material we learned in class. He uses excel in the class which I love because it taught me how to do a lot. The most difficult thing is probably the case studies so make sure to start those earlier rather than later. don't email go in person.

He's awesome!! During the lectures he always tells stories to make the content more applicable, and I find that helped me a lot! The tests are quite difficult but as long as you do the HWs and projects you'll be fine. He gave extra credit for doing a Finance case comp. Great guy to talk to! I'd highly advise taking his class.

The professor has a good sense of humor that makes the lectures engaging. There are also video lectures that are good for preparing for tests. If you prepare for the tests you can do well in this class. Overall this a great course and professor.

His classes were a blast, making corporate finance surprisingly enjoyable with his jokes and unique examples. But, I was very new to the subject struggling with his tough exams which are 71% of the final grade. Even with perfect attendance and reviewing his video lectures you are not guaranteed to pass without a deep understanding of finance.

Professor Boquist was awesome! His lectures were very fun and insightful, he had many anecdotes that made concepts much easier to understand. He also posts all the lectures online. His exams are pretty tough, but beyond that it was a great class.
Professor Boquist makes sure his lectures are very engaging and insightful.

Professor Boquist was one of the most disorganized professors I've ever had. He took forever to grade exams/homework and didn't respond to emails. Nothing was graded until the class was two-thirds over. The course material was very difficult. However, he did a great job explaining the topics in class, and I found what I learned interesting/useful.

Dr. Boquist was excellent in teaching the material for MGMT610. His videos and lectures are straight forward and offer clear explanations for the topics involved. The professor does a great job presenting theoretical concepts and also showing how it translates to real world examples. He ensures students take away key concepts for the real world.

The professor had covid so for the first 2 weeks he didn't really record much videos.

The exam is written. The project is SAS heavy.
Most boring class ever, take if you like just copying down what the professor is writing in class. The project is time-consuming. As usual, final exam is killer.

reviews.comment: Professor Boquist has been one of my favorite professors at Purdue! He makes lectures engaging and genuinely cares about both the material and his students. Going to lecture isn't mandatory but is super helpful in learning the material. Would highly recommend!

Professor never grades our assignments, until the end, and he pretty much gives everyone full marks. BUT, the final exam is super tight timeline/hard, and I got a B. During class he just rambles on about personal anecdotes. He also makes everyone give him a review BEFORE our exam (so of course we will write good stuff), for extra credit.
This class isn't a cake walk, but if you go to lectures and do the homework the class is very manageable. Professor Boquist is really engaging and genuinely cares about the material.

Professor Boquist is a great professor who uses his outside knowledge and experience to make the class more interesting and exciting. His exams are tough but fair and the work outside of class is minimal. Overall, he is a great professor and I highly recommend.

Funny, knowledgeable, lectures are thorough, and Prof. Boquist covers the material you are tested on, grading is fair, virtual testing could have been done better. I wish I took the class outside of a pandemic.
Very funny professor that knows what he's talking about. Works very hard to make the class work applicable.
He's very funny and charismatic, and a great professor

Boquist is a great professor. He is funny which makes lectures more fun. Exams are hard but you get a cheat sheet so it makes the short answer easier. the multiple choice is hard. You have to go to class because the examples are the exam short answer questions.

reviews.comment: The lectures are amazing and if you follow his lectures (slides), you will get an easy A. Pay attention to the details in the slides and remember to do the practice exam.
I loved the professor but the exams were very difficult.

Bob is simply put the best TA I have had at my time at Purdue. He cares about every single on of his students, knowing them all by name by the second week. Honestly, bob is perfect and I would take any class he was a TA for. Please let Bob be a TA for Delworths final semester next semester. He is the best.

Bob is the BEST recitation instructor I have ever had. He was funny, caring, kind, and made me like math again. He does a great job with the MA 155 material and made the two recitations a week bearable. I would highly recommend switching into Bob's session if you can. I wish I could retake this class if I could, just because of how great Bob is!

Online this semester was pretty easy for me. Its math you would use in real life. Great professor and great class to take - especially if you only need to take one or two classes to fill a requirement. When i was confused on a problem he reached out to me via phone to make sure he could help me. Great Guy!!
I cannot tell you how much I love Bob, he makes my day every time I see him. He actually cares about all of his students. He's the most lovable old man!
During my stay in Purdue, Bob Madison probed to be one fine teacher.
Awesome teacher.

Bob is fantastic!  He is hilarious, and his lectures are really engaging.  Unlike most of the ratings so far, I actually did learn a decent amount.  It's a class where YOU control how much you learn.  I wanted to learn, so I did.

good stories

This class was math focused. Her lectures were engaging and very clear. The homeworks were pretty straight-forward and easy as long as you went to the lecture. She was pretty responsive in emailing.
Engaging lectures, easy exams. Use unstuckstudy ai alongside the textbook for efficient prep. Mandatory attendance, but worth it for the insightful examples.
Exams are in person, homework is online

Professor Blanchard is a very transparent professor who clearly explains the material and communicates all deadlines. The lectures are clearly taught and set up in a manner to make it easy to pay attention. Would take one of her courses again!

One of the best professors I have ever had at Purdue. Her explanations of economics concepts are by far some of the most intuitive I have seen. The homeworks and exams are easy, and the hotseat extra credit is the cherry on top.

For a class that I never attended in person, this professor did an excellent job of explaining things with examples that students would understand.  Her exams were not difficult, just study the homework and practice exams and you'll be set.  When I took this class, we had an exam drop, so I recommend dropping your final as it was mostly old content
The lectures have hotseat however without going to the lectures the class can be very difficult and you won't do well on the exams. Exams are in person and there are online homework assignments.
very good professor

The class was alright. Kelly Blanchard is a very sweet lady and is definitely willing to help you if you ask for it, but given the class was taught in a massive lecture hall with 200+ people, there isn't a lot of 1-on-1 help during lectures. Definitely go to office hours, rewatch lecture videos, AND GO TO LECTURE FOR BONUS HOTSEAT POINTS!!!

I previously took this class in the spring and slacked off, ended up failing and had to retake in the summer. The course was 4 weeks so it was very intense. Lectures were good, and she is accommodating. As long as you put in the work, watch the lectures, read the textbook, and take multiple of the practice exams, you'll get an A.

Kelly is a wonderful lecturer who explains every relevant concept in great detail. The course is fairly easy, so you can skip class if you want, but she gave extra credit quizzes at about half of the lectures for the people who attended. Exams make up most of the grade, but they are all multiple choice and she gives dozens of practice problems.
Very sweet lady but I found her teaching methods boring and repetitive. Also exams were heavily weighted so there was not much wiggle room with points aside from the exams
I enjoyed taking Blanchard's class. She made economics easy with fun examples that helped me understand and remember the material.

There is a maximum of twelve HotSeat extra credit opportunities to boost your grade. Exams account for most of the total points. However, Professor Blanchard provides review sessions and practice exams to help you succeed on the exams. Additionally, your lowest exam score is dropped and you can easily earn 100% on all the homework assignments.
Allows other students to talk to the class about clubs and other events

Kelly is a good professor however, her style of teaching is just not for me. All she does is draw the same graph over and over again on a blank piece of paper. For me this style of teaching does not work. If she had the class a little more organized with the notes proportion of lecture and went over more practice problems, I would have done better.

Your final grade comes 80% from 3 exams. There are 4 total exams, but you get to drop your lowest. This was certainly my easiest class of the semester and she has been teaching the class for many years, which is apparent. There is a lot of note taking during lectures, but you get used to it.

reviews.comment: Extra credit for going to lecture 12 times

She is a great professor! Very dedicated to helping her students learn and amazing at explaining course content. She reviews the content before exams very well and provides many practice resources for you beforehand. Exams are very straightforward. This year, there are three exams and a final. Your lowest exam is dropped (final can be dropped).

While my brain isn't built for economics, Kelly does a wonderful job of explaining basic economic concepts. Homework isn't hard and it's possible to get 100% on every single homework. Course is exam HEAVY and if you can't pass the exams there is no hope for you, but luckily the exams are not that bad. If you do homework and study for exams you good
Blanchard is amazing. Pay attention to her lectures and you will absorb so much.
She is very knowledgeable and a good communicator. She gave curves and extra credit to help out those who struggled initially. Homework was easy, and exams were manageable with some studying.

Professor Blanchard teaches each topic of econ clearly. She provides many opportunities to get help and truly shows a passion for her job. She uses real world examples related to Purdue which is nice. She also gives past exams as resources to study for the exams with. She also provides many extra credit opportunities to take advantage of.

Ms. Blanchard was really good during the lectures. She made the concepts easy to understand and answered every question thoroughly. Hotseat extra-credit questions come in clutch, and you can always wait til the end for the answer and the EC. All exams are multiple choice, and you can re-do the HW to get 100%. Make sure you review the past exams.

Professor Blanchard is an amazing professor; she knows what shes talking about and explains her material in an understandable way. reviews.comment: She has lots of extra credit. Reading the book and going to SI is what saved my grade in this class. Blanchard is very kind and helpful when you go to her office hours. Her class is more work than you think it will be so make sure to put in plenty of time studying on your own time.

reviews.comment: Easy class and great professor. She is super nice and explains the topics well. You get extra credit just for showing up to class and have one easy hw a week. Exam heavy but the exams are easy if you pay attention or study (you dont really need to do both). She also puts out exam answers the next day with I really appreciate.

I think Prof. Blanchard is a great professor, in part my middle of the pack grade was my fault and also can be attributed to the online format. However, I think she is extremely informative, and really wants to make sure everyone understands the concepts provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took the course this summer. I just watched the lectures and did the past papers, these two were more than enough to achieve an A in the course . The lectures are easy to follow and extremely helpful.
Personnel Economics was a great class. It was in my first semester of the program and Dr. Blanchard was extremely helpful and had clear expectations. Would take her classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Blanchard provides exactly what you need to both learn and retain the material she teaches as well as clear support for the exams in the class. Exams are open-note and open-book, but this does not translate to higher difficulty. Take good notes, jot down key phrases she emphasizes, and you will do spectacular before extra credit factors in.

I don't understand how anyone can rate Prof Blanchard poorly. She is the best! She makes her lectures very interesting (the best I have ever experienced) and gives out easy extra credit that can raise your final grade up to 6%. TAKE THE PRACTICE EXAMS TO STUDY. The practice exams are very similar to the real exams. It is easy to get over 100

Prof. Blanchard seemed very nice and open to help anyone who asked. This class is difficult since exams are worth so much of your grade. Extra credit is also limited, so it can be hard to improve your grade without doing extremely well on the exams.
She is very considerate. I missed my finals because I was sick she was very understanding and let me take the make up exam

This class is difficult. It is hard to stay concentrated. The lectures are long and it feels as if they did not put the exams and homework into proper practice. I think there should have been more practice problems that are similar to exams. Also, your grade is 86% exams. This is a class I wanted over and wanted to mark off my list. Yikes.

Professor Blanchard knows the content well and wants you to succeed. She makes it easy for you to know exactly what is required of you. The one thing is though that the way she explains things is often through specific examples and it makes it hard to apply the content to different contexts. Overall, not horrible.

Course material is simply the same as in high school . Exams are easy with a lot of time per question. You can often complete the exam with only a half of the time. Past papers questions also showed up in real exam. And she gave a tons of extra credit. So it's definitely an EASY A.

I think it is really ridiculous that 86% of grade in this class is based off of 3 total exams. The exams are also NOTHING like the homework or lecture. It's really bad that the average on an open note, open book exam range 70-75%, which in my opinion is extremely low. This class is for my minor and is by far the most difficult class I have taken.

reviews.comment: I'll be honest, ECON 25100 is not for me. I've taken this class multiple times and it isn't at fault of the professor. She is great and tried to help me as much as she could but it just would not click. She is fantastic

Her exam was prohibitively difficult despite the class as a whole expressing concerns about where we were at. Terrible class, avoid at all costs!

Professor Kelly Blanchard gave sub par lectures that did not help on homework or exams. Exam material was significantly harder than material covered in class. Avoid if you can. Condolences if you can't.

Prof Blanchard was awesome! I had her the first semester of my freshman year and had a great experience in her class. She gives tons of great examples that help clarify some concepts. reviews.comment: The entire class was asynchronous, so my experience with the professor is based on her videos. Her videos do a fine job explaining, nothing outstanding but not bad. The videos generally cover all the material, but reading through the textbook chapter in parallel doesn't hurt.

She's an amazing professor. Very non partisan in the way she presents political issues that tie into economics. She always responds to emails fast, and is always willing to help you one on one for anything. She's just a great person overall and although I'm sure I didn't receive an A in her class, I still learned plenty from her course.

Professor Blanchard did the best that she could when converting ECON 251 to an online class due to COVID. I dont fully blame her for the class being extra difficult to learn online simply due to the personal difficulties of learning in an online environment. The class is VERY exam heavy, so make sure to use your resources as best as you can.

reviews.comment: Overall, she seemed like a nice lady. ECON 251 is a workload and you really have to buckle down if you want to pass. I am not an ECON major, nor had any interest, but I had to take this class for a core credit. I ended up withdrawing because I was taking 17 credit hours and ECON 251 was too much for me. I would not recommend taking as a freshman.
Great professor who really cares. Exams that have textbook access.

Dr. Blanchard was a great professor. I took the Honors section, and had a great experience with it. I wouldn't call it an easy A, because you definitely have to go to class and study for it, but there were numerous ways to be successful in the course. She even hosted review sessions over Zoom after we switched to online classes b/c of COVID-19.

Prof Blanchard's classes are very informative. Lectures are not required, but attending will allow you a good portion of extra credit through Hot Seat questions. lots of examples are given during lectures, and those examples translate very closely to the exams, so pay attention. She is well versed in the topic and an overall great professor.

Dr. Blanchard was one of the best professor I ever met. Her lectures were amazing Class materials were quite difficult, but during the class, she did various demonstrations that helped me to understand materials better. Attendance is not required, however, I highly recommend to go to class. It will help you get a satisfying grade on exams.

reviews.comment: Professor Blanchard is an amazing professor. She explains the material in a way that is easy to follow and interesting. There is also no reason for a person to not get 100% on all the homework.

Blanchard is an amazing professor. Her examples are always very clear and easy to follow. The tests are pretty similar to the past exams so if you do well on those before the test it's a pretty accurate indicator of how you'll do on the actual exam.

reviews.comment: Gotta love Kelly "Did you know too much cinnamon is bad for you" Blanchard

Prof. Blanchard is a great professor. This class is manageable but seems to be easier for the STEM majors who are taking it as a pre-req. I've taken the class twice, and it just requires a different type of learning. Also, the huge Elliot hall exams gave me so much anxiety I would literally blank. STUDY GUIDE IS ESSENTIAL.

super easy and straightforward class, attendance is extra credit, and lectures are on boilercast, but her examples are so interesting, going to class isn't even bad. Exams are very reasonable and homework is impossible not to get 100% on.
Easily one of my favorite professors at Purdue, she explains the material well and helps students prepare for tests well.

She's extremely caring and nice, but sometimes she goes a bit too slowly in class. If you've never done econ before, she is an amazing teacher because she uses lots of examples and real-life scenarios to teach the class. Overall, she a very sweet and caring teacher that is willing to help outside of class.
I personally struggled a lot with the class, and I went to every lecture. I guess I'm just not that good at Microeconomics, but Kelly was a great professor, and she always gave feedback.

Great professor! Gives great simple examples to understand concepts clearly. Responds to mail for any kind of homework or concept related doubts. Properly explains complicated numerical. Keeps Hotseat questions almost every class for Extra Credit. Never felt bored in her class.

Professor Blanchard will probably end up teaching you Econ 251 if you choose to take it. It is a great class with straightforward and understandable material that she explains well. I strongly advise attending lectures because you WILL do better if you go to class and answer the hotseat questions.

All around an awesome lady. Her lectures are fun and pretty easy to understand. Homework isn't too difficult. Her exams can be somewhat tough but she does a good job at make sure she is available if you have questions about the material.
Fully prepares you for exam. Minimal homework.

Professor Blanchard is one of the best you'll get at Purdue. Although ECON251 is a fairly tough class to take, she is clear and concise with the lectures and provides engaging examples with about one to two extra credit opportunities every week.

First off, she is an amazing person and lecturer. She has a very kind and nurturing spirit and she really cares about all of her students. I highly recommend her honors version. MEET OFTEN FOR THE PROJECT AND MAKE A SCHEDULE. Do not procrastinate on the project, it will only add unnecessary stress to your finals week. Do redo hw's to get 100%.

Took this class as a first semester freshman with no economics course background. There are only 300 points total, 40 points from homework which you get 100% on, and 260 points from three exams. The three exams are two midterms and then the final. There are only 12 points of extra credit which is easy to get. She lectures the entire class.

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, econ did not make sense until Kelly B. She breaks everything down so well and will help if you do not understand something. Homework is easy and redo-able and extra credit is a huge help.

I would not recommend taking this course if you are not a business major. The material is hard to understand, and the lectures are not engaging at all. Studying for this class is extremely hard because there are no powerpoints.

Attendance is technically not mandatory, but you can get extra credit by answering the hot seat questions so you might as well go! I personally had a difficult time in the course because I didn't put in enough work, so it's not a totally free A. Her lectures are really good though and she uses logical, real-life examples to explain the material!

Dr. Blanchard is a great lecturer. This is the first I have taken an ECON course, and she made the material easier to understand. She's funny and comes up with good examples. I definitely recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor! If you have any quantitative background and an ability to sit down and understand the material for a few hours before the exams you will do fine. HW is a guaranteed 100%. Show up to lecture to get an in-depth understanding of what is going on and to get free points.

Dr. Blanchard is a fantastic professor who is not only passionate about economics, but teaching. She knows how to present material in a logical and intuitive way, and she's always willing to help if you're struggling. Definitely go to her office hours, even if it's just to chat- she's an incredibly cool and caring person!

really easy exams if you prepare. Also go to classes for the hotseat questions

reviews.comment: She is one of the best Professors I ever had! She is one of those people who take passion in teaching and make sure the students enjoy and learn along the way. Idk what people who rate her badly are up to... Get a life peeps! Wish Kelly all the very best!
Her lectures are helpful but her exams are way to hard. The book doesnt help

Kelly Blanchard is an amazing micro prof, she explains things very well to her students and makes sure that you understand the content. Her exams are very easy and are so similar to the practice exams she gives out as study material. There are hot seat questions in class that give you extra credit and she puts her lectures on boilercast.

Kelly was very personable and caring, Her lectures were clear and concise and not boring at all. I went to her office hours once and she was very nice and ask nice questions. She is a very good professor who cares her students a lot. Attendance is just for extra credits and handwriting notes is very useful. Listen the lectures carefully and take the sample exams! GETTING AN A IS NOT DIFFICULT!

The best professor I had for freshman year first semester! She really cares about students and gives many extra credits. She posts boilercast so that even if you don't attend the class you still can get an A. The exams are not hard if you review all her notes she had during lectures. Textbook is not mandatory.
If you're in any science related field, this class will be a breeze.

Professor Blanchard does not use powerpoint presentations when teaching, instead she writes out each step on a projector, making material easy to follow. She has extra credit quizzes in class, and will tell the class the answer before the closes the Hotseat. Taking the class for H credit is just one more project, which is fun and graded generously.

Great professor! Her lectures are concise and straightforward; she's also super nice if you talk to her during office hours. Tests are hard but they're easy if you put in the effort and study for them.
BEST Professor I had Purdue WL (so far). Unfortunately, she just teaches ECON 251:(
She's the best professor I've had at Purdue so far (1 semester). She makes you feel like an Economics genius and is really kind, helpful and uses brilliant examples.

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff. Would really like to commend her for teaching the same material three times a day (since there's three sections), without losing any enthusiasm. She speaks clearly and it is easy to understand her. Go to class for the hotseat points, because of it I almost got a perfect score of 296/300.

The tests are very tough, but if you go to class you can do hotseat questions for extra credit points. The tests are really tough, but she posts the previous two tests so you have something to study from.

reviews.comment: Very nice and clear. Makes great examples in class

Honestly, class was not as difficult as people make it out to be, just put in time. Lecture isn't mandatory but the extra credit HotSeat questions really are a grade booster. Take notes in lecture, they'll help come exam time. All exams are very similar to the ones she posts on blackboard, so study those and you'll do good on the exams.
Her tests are so hard and the homework is worth nothing. I dont like that your class grade is solely based on exams.
Great professor!

Prof. Blanchard is amazing. She's super personable and her lectures are interesting, though econ really isn't. She has great stories to go along with econ concepts and she always draws pictures and uses examples. Tests are difficult, so studying is a must. Participation points are extra credit, so go to class to answer the Hotseat questions!
Attend all lectures and take notes. You won't need a textbook. Do all homework assignments, Hotseat questions, and past year papers and you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: I can tell that she knows what shes talking about but when I cant say the same about me when I listen to her lectures. I feel like she rambles on about subjects that dont make any sense or have any relevance. Her teaching method is really unorganized which makes it harder for me to learn. Also, she talks as if we know what shes talking about..

Dr. Blanchard is one of the best professors I have had during my time at Purdue. She really cares about what she teaches, and she wants every student to succeed. Super approachable and will answer any questions you have. Great at slowing down and using lots of examples to help students understand the material. If you can take her class, do it!!!

Dr. Blanchard takes a dull, gen-ed course and makes it interesting. Shes an excellent professor and explains topics really well. Extra credit is given for correctly answering pop-quiz questions (1/week). If you've ever taken an economics course before just come to class , take notes on key points, and you'll get an easy A. Nice GPA boost

She is a great professor, however, her exams are difficult. You must study for them and take several practice exams in order to do well in the class. Also attend lecture for the Hotseat Questions, they make a difference in the end. There is not really a curve in the class.

Not that good of a professor, constantly rambles about subjects that could be taught in a quarter of the time. She knows what she is talking about but seems to explain subjects in a way that is just not clear at all.
Her lectures are just amazing.

Gives little opportunities and makes her tests super hard and nothing like the homework or what is taught in class. Hands down the hardest class I have ever taken and is very stressful and is not enjoyable. I would not take it unless it's mandatory. She's nice but I feel like her class is too extreme.

reviews.comment: I found this class to be very easy. Don't buy the book, just get the access code for HW (and it comes with review material). If you do past exams (weekly joys has a ton) and go to class (especially for hot seat points) you will be fine. Maybe 1 hr. of work a week outside of class (other than exam weeks).

Mrs. Blanchard is an amazing teacher and cares about her students. She is enthusiastic to be teaching Economics and knows her material really well. I would highly suggest for students to take her as a professor because your learn a lot, but you will have to work your grade. Every time I email her, she gets back to me quickly with a detailed answer.

Professor Blanchard's class is the only power hour I don't mind going to, she's a great instructor! Her lectures and class notes are easy to follow along with and she explains things very well. It is not hard to do well in this course if you pay attention in class and use the practice exams to help you study for the exams.

If Blanchard ran for president I would vote for her. In all seriousness, I feel like she was one of my best teachers at Purdue. Even though my grade wasn't an A i did learn a heck of a lot more than I thought I would and it actually brought me to eventually minor in Econ. She's a very helpful teacher and very knowledgable as well.

Amazing professor! Had some trouble staying awake in lectures, but that's mostly due to the time at which lecture starts. While attendance is not mandatory since she uses BoilerCast to record her lectures, extra credits help towards your final grades. Put in some effort reviewing her lectures and you'll get your A.

She was very nice. They class is structured for you to succeed with the extra credit but the material can become dense if you do not show up to class. Kelly made me want to come to class, I was never bored during class and I found a love for learning through this class.

She adds in extra credit every now and then which is nice. Take this if you can be happy sitting in a class for 75 minutes without speaking to anyone and listening to the prof blab on and on.

Blanchard is an amazing professor: teaches the concepts clearly and attempts to make it as simple as possible with real-life examples. The tests are pretty hard--doing the homework (easy 100%) helps your grade and to understand the information.

Helpful and kind.

reviews.comment: Kelly is a great professor that knows how to translate these concepts into a more basic explanation that's easy to follow. She's also very approachable and is very reasonable with homework.

GO TO CLASS, TAKE GOOD NOTES, & STUDY FOR EXAMS. Very nice lady, lots of examples and thorough notes. There is a lot of information in that class and exams are concept heavy. If you are not good at economics, be prepared. The class moves quickly. If you fall behind or have questions seek help asap.
Blanchard is good at what she does, explains the material in understandable terms, and makes herself available to students.

Kelly Blanchard is amazing. Considering yourself lucky if you take a class that she teaches, amazing clarity, goes over topics thoroughly, and is easy to follow and understand. With that, there are not many ways to earn points in the class. DO WELL on exams, they are hard. GO TO CLASS, free hotseat extra credit points ( they add up).
She's a really great professor. She explains topics clearly and thoroughly.

GOD BLESS KELLY BLANCHARD. She writes her notes out during lecture, which makes it super easy to follow along. Tests are kind of difficult, but there are tons of past exams available to study from (she keeps her them very similar).

Very good, reply to emails on time and very clear

Supper awesome teacher! she is the best choice for you if you take econ!

Probably the best professor I've had so far at Purdue! She always tries to explain the topics as clearly as she can and is always willing to help students. Attend class for extra credit opportunities. Best way to prepare for exams is to go to class, take notes, and do the practice exams.
Good Professor with good notes. Gives extra credit questions if you attend class which the points really add up. She posts past exams. Use those to study

Awesome teacher!

She is one of the best professors at Purdue. Her classes are easy, and everything she talked about will be on the exam. There is little homework for the class. I did not buy a text book, but that's not a problem, because she talks about everything in class.

One of the best professors I've had at Purdue. Makes me want to change my major to Econ. I highly recommend you take one of her classes. Great professor. Would highly recommend. Very clear, made the info seem so easy

Simply the best!

Knowledgeable professor, attempts to answer students' questions. Class was easy because Professor Blanchard taught it.  Very knowledgeable and helpful.  She truly wants students to succeed and to understand the material.
Great teacher. Great at explaining. If you have the choice, take micro just so you can have Blanchard.

one of the greatest professors i've had.  explains things very clearly and has a passion for her work.  HIGHLY recommended.

Really nice prof... Easy to get an A in her class... All u got To do is to go to class and take notes and make sure u give all the extra credit quizzes

Great teacher. She has good examples in class and speaks clearly and generally keeps your attention. Now if only the homework was worth more points, and the exams worth fewer points, this would be a perfect class!

She is very lenient, offers extra credit, and genuinely wants her students to succeed.

She is an extremely amazing professor. She always cares about her students and values the efforts that each student puts into their homework. She once told me "Except for life and death problems, we don't need to rush everything." A very sympathetic woman. When I found out that I could take two courses with her, I was truly delighted.
Might as well just buy yourself a textbook and read it on your own

He's very passionate and encourages questions from students in lecture. The assignments take a while to do and there is not a lot of time to do them. Extra credit at the end was nice and the exams are reasonable. Taking notes during lectures is a must because the slides are complicated and he explains the important parts in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Very convoluted, confusing lectures. Completing readings beforehand is sometimes helpful (if you can understand them), but certainly not exhaustively so. 
The HWs are very lengthy & time-consuming and don't necessarily align w/ lectures.

If you're not sure, I'd suggest taking a different prof/class unless you're already proficient in the subject.
He keeps talking about GNN research all the time. Not everyone cares. Class is too hard. No time left for research.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Seems like a very arrogant person who doesn't like being questioned. The HWs are very time-consuming, but even if you get full grades it doesn't feel like you learned anything really meaningful. The syllabus is very niche and biased towards his research. Symmetry feels like an esoteric concept whose practical utility in DL is taken for granted.

I dont think Bruno deserves 1/5. He couldve spent more time explaining the intuitions behind the maths instead of just reading them off the slides. But in the end it wasnt too bad, if you did the readings beforehand. Course logistics were messy, but also wasnt that bad. He also did his best to cover as many modern topics in DL as possible.

Overall good and well-designed course, although course logistics could have been improved. Lectures were great, but are often tough to understand if you don't pay attention or do the appropriate readings. HWs and exams were decently hard, but lectures were enough to keep up with them. Would suggest if you want to challenge yourself with DL topics.

The course definitely tough and it is heavily mathematic. However, I don't think he was rude or stop student to ask questions. He constantly ask us to ask question.
One thing I would hope him to do is he first explains the concept before going into the mathematical proof. If you want easy course, then he is not your go to option.

The content says its deep learning but its rather just the professor's research in a very niche area being taught to a 100 student batch where hardly anyone is interested in it. Moreover, whatever he tries to teach has so much mathematical background required that he just assumes that everyone knows.

Tough professor to say the least. English is very rough and lectures are hard to understand. A lot of the homework problems are completely unrelated to the lectures, but are doable. Would try to get someone else if there is another option

The course was tough with the lectures being pretty theory intensive. The homeworks were time consuming, but there was a lot of extra credit. Midterm was a shitshow, but the final was one of the easiest cs exam I have given at purdue. As long as you understand what's going on in the class, it's not a bad course. Bruno def made it easier.

This is a pretty difficult class taken with this professor - very time consuming and somewhat difficult homeworks, and decently difficult exams. However, he really cares about students learning and tries his best to teach pretty theoretical and math heavy content. Can be occasionaly tough to understand at times as he reads formulas from slides.
worst class ive ever taken. terrible prof
I have never taken a class this terrible. Horrible lectures and very harsh.
Horrible Lecturer
Worst course I have ever taken. very harsh.

The professor's English is not great and is often an obstacle to understanding the material. It doesn't help that he isn't great at explaining concepts either, nor are the slides. The topics aren't explained in much detail and it's almost impossible to implement them without help after the topic is covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
Prof. Ribeiro is great. He's clearly passionate about his research, is very knowledgeable, is patient with explanations and very approachable.

However, the one issue I find is that he tends to overwhelm us with math. The slides really need improvement. They do a poor job at explaining the material, and it's very easy to get lost because of it.

Riberio is what happens when a circus clown is asked to teach a 300-level CS course. Horrendous slides have no takeaway material to help you with the homework or exams. No communication with the TAs. Will humbly brag how he asked android to change its facial recognition code several times in the semester. Maybe I should write that on the final.
Teaching was very unhelpful and homeworks were extremely time consuming.

This is the worst class I've ever taken at purdue. His course material is very hard to understand and he will not explain it clearly during classes. Sometimes you could understand what the lecture slides is talking about but you may still find you don't know how to solve questions in the tests. There were huge amout of formulas too.
He is very knowledgeable and great at conveying difficult concepts. This was one of my favorite classes for the semester.
WORST LECTURER IN CS
He is an freaking early bird, for the exam, he arranges 8:00-10:00 on winters, who does that. If he is so harsh on himself, he is not going easy on you
The course is not hard in the subject of statistics, but the professor is able to make it harder than you thought.
I don't think anything could improve this recitation. It's BAD as it is
skipping steps makes it hard to understand how they arrived to an answer. Show some more work
If a student doesn't understand how you are doing a problem, explain it in a different way. Also, do the work in a more organized manner.

He cares, don't get me wrong, but it was so hard to understand what he was teaching because he didn't know what was going on in lecture. His work and explanations were difficult to follow and understand.

I don't know what to say. He is passionate and his English is fluent. But his logic is sooo bad that it could make you feel like: what is he doing for the whole class and why am I here. Also, he made too many political jokes and lauged at the joke made by himself, which would be really awkward for international students.
He is trying to persuade us that he is a good teacher and beg us to connect with him at office hour. But, you are unable to convey us the information that you can solve the issue at class.
He is not a good teacher. English is bad and nonlogical
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Worst ever. The slides are not well organized and have many mistakes. The homeworks are peculiar and just wasting of time.

Professor clearly passionate about the subject and teaching. Willing to listen to student feedback and act upon them. Happy to explain and clarify new concepts. Gave up to 10% extra credit in the class (Kaggle performance depending). Homework is challenging and time consuming but not impossible and provides great opportunity for learning.

Lecture goes fast. Pay attention to both what he says and writes. Homework is tricky (Weekly ~25 problems upwards of 70 total parts). There is supplemental reading but isn't "required". Exam was VERY computationally heavy (similar to the homework), but the multiple choice nature of it makes it relatively nicer. 1 crib sheet allowed on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are forced to take it, I'm sorry. If not, RUN!!!

This is the worst professor in my life. He with strong accent speaks so fast, it's impossible to understand. Once a weekly assignment had nearly 100 questions. At exam, I almost laughed, if you were to actually compute the calculation problems step by step, it would take 40+ minutes, as if deriving everything from ancient times to the AI era.

Good instructor overall and also a reasonable amount of homework, but the only tedious tasks are the labs and the checkpoints for a data science project assigned throughout the semester. There are deductions for late assignments, but it is more what the course coordinator set and not him.

He's a good guy in general, but is not very understanding in specific circumstances. Also, the exams are NOTHING like the practice exams and help questions. If you are going to tell people to review something for the exam, it feels like a complete waste of time when the exam doesn't reflect that, and screws students over.

Bruce Peary Solomon is clearly passionate about his job. Screw my class for not laughing at his jokes and puns. He cares about his students. Have one word with this guy and he'll remember you. One complaint I do have about this class is that the homework is very reliant on the syntax of your answers. He wasn't very forgiving about that.
Terrible, disrespectful, avoid at all costs.
There have been multiple times now when I have submitted the correct document, and for some reason, he has given me zero credit he is a terrible teacher and not good at his job at all.

He provides a really good balance between sharing what he knows and making the material fun/engaging during lectures. Very responsive in person/over email, which I've not always had with past professors: He also provides several study resources, and as someone who isn't the greatest exam-taker, it's much appreciated. Glad I took this class :)

Although Bruce can be hard to understand sometimes in class because he wears a mask, his slides are very concise and helpful. He also posts all the lectures online which was a very helpful stud tool for exams. I never met with him outside of class, but he has office hours and encourages reaching out for help.

Generally did not seem interested in the class. He would show up to read the slides but that was it. Coursework is not too difficult and you can learn the required concepts without going to class. I recommend just looking over the chapter summaries and teaching yourself the important concepts and then addressing the professor if you need help.

How to succeed in this class: go to lecture, write down the examples problems, and use the practice questions on the homework to help you. If you get a problem wrong on the homework, take a picture or write down how to properly solve the problem so that you get it right on your second attempt. The labs are easy if you can follow directions well.

This class is an exact repeat of AP stats. Lectures are super boring and he takes attendance, you can miss a few and be fine though. Labs are super easy and the TA's will hand out answers if you word your questions right. The homework's were busy work. Overall I never spent more than 1 hour a week working outside of class. Easy to pass.

I got a B+ by hardly attending lectures but watching them online before tests and filling out the sheet allowed on exams. If I had gone to the lectures, I am sure I could have gotten an A but they were too dry for my test. Not his fault though.

If you dedicate time and ask for help when needed from the TA's, the labs are EASY! I never used the program before and am not that committed to my academics, got a 90-100 on all of them. Exams can be tricky, but Dr.Solomon gives good practice opps. Lectures in-person for points, but are boring/hard to hear him. Old, recorded versions online.
Watch out for labs, if you miss one table you get a zero for the whole thing
The homework was hard for no reason and look some time but it was where I learned most of the content. The labs however were extremely challenging and the TA's did not really help.
He will definitely help you if you ask for it. Hes pretty vague but you have to pay attention to actually understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So here's the thing, he's funny but he's not trying to be. The bandanas? Are you kidding me? That's hilarious. Also, attendance is mandatory I guess but the quizzes are easy, labs are doable with some googling and referencing the lecture skeleton notes on bright space, and do the multiple-choice review he sends before the exams and a B is doable.
He doesn't respect his students at all.

Solomon terrified me at the beginning of the semester by saying this would be the hardest class Ive taken. Completely false. He gives so much opportunity for points. There are 12 homeworks w/ 2 tries each & 6 quizzes with multiple tries. The homeworks and quizzes are really beneficial, they make up for points lost in exams. I earned a B easily.
Solomon didnt really explain things thoroughly in lectures so it was kinda hard to know what was going on but he was nice. Exams were TOUGH but homework/lab were pretty straightforward.
He doesn't respect students at all. The most awful professor I've met ever!
Dr. Solomon is definitely one of the best professors I've ever met. I found my interests in statistics by taking his class.
Easy A with solomon, one of the better stat301 professors. Print off the skeleton notes that he posts & print the review exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's not the sort of Professor most people enjoy since he's older and doesn't convey a lot of enthusiasm but his lectures thoroughly cover everything you need to understand the class and pass the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He doesn't show respect to the others at all. The slides are hard to understand. I learned everything by myself.

While I did not prefer the lectures (got a bit mundane). Prof brian is a very knowledgeable person and is very passionate about the topic. Talking to him outside of the class got me interested in a lot of his projects

The classes were very boring, with attendance dropping to around 15%. Grading was unclear, with poorly explained expectations. The content was very broad and shallow, lacking practical depth or applicability. For this material, CS188 from UC Berkeley is a better option, with clearer lectures and free online resources.

Pretty good professor who taught 471 for Spring 24. There were 4 homeworks for the entire semester, with no quizzes, so a straightforward workload. One midterm, one final. The material was well-presented, but the final was a killer compared to the practice exam. Luckily Prof. Bullins was a fair grader and his grading was generous. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: We had presentations for 355 which he told us the day before the actual details of what he wanted us to do. then he mocked the people who got picked to present and kept making condescending comments about how they didn't do enough research even though he told us what to do the day before...
do not take class, you are being taught by ai and not the professor, might as well take it for credit at ivy tech
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He does not teach the class, AI teaches the class for him, AI grades all assignments, AI writes the textbook, quiz feedback is not legible because AI uses characters that do not align with lockdown browser code, tangents during lectures do not cover anything on quizzes, changes assignments the day before they are due, AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS.

Definitely a hard professor, but he's only looking out for you since consulting is a hard industry. 4 straight weeks of cases are unfortunate, but in consulting you are constantly working so I can understand why he does this. He tries his best to help his students. This class is only rewarding if you put in the work.

If you want to go into consulting then this the guy for it, but you are going to be in for a bad time. You have to do 5 case studies and usually only get a week. 

Also don't expect to get more than an 80% on a quiz. Final project is solo as well and in the middle of exam time.

John Burr is tough but if you want to go into consulting, he WILL prepare you well. He is a hard grader on presentations, and he can spot BS a mile away. (The course material makes it impossible to BS the group work/projects.) 4/5 Cases were in November, which was too much for one month, but he said he'll fix next sem. Not a blow-off class for sure

Burr's grading system, however, was very controlling. His quizzes were insanely hard and the maximum score you can receive on a video response is 94.5/100. He claimed this was due to "natural bias by students." I feel like if he is worried about this, he should just grade them himself instead of automatically deducting points. He's on a power trip.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher and a great person. He makes time to see his students outside of class to get to know them and he's hilarious in his lectures. He's very organized as a professor and makes all his lecture notes accessible.

His lectures are hard to understand and requires (essentially) re-learning the content outside of class.
Wouldn't take again.

Genuine top tier professor. He clearly cares about his students and his class. Really cool guy off the clock too. He always invites his students to eat lunch with him and talk to him whenever they see him around campus. Fast teacher for sure, but he covers his base. If you pay attention, you're chilling.
Really good professor and super nice.

Best professor ever. He truly cares about his students and values their time. He makes himself available outside of class. In class he cracks random jokes, then awkwardly points it out when no one laughs. When you laugh, he keeps awkwardly going and stretching it, he kills me. He also rounded my grade up by 3%. Such a kind and genuine man overall!
Didn't take attendance but his lectures were clear and concise. The best part is how willing he is to spend time after lectures or outside of class to discuss.
very humble and caring professor , is there for the students and always clears doubts happily . Some might find the course in the second half harder but he will make sure everyone goes along with him
Awesome guy
He did not take attendance for CHM115 but he does have attendance for CHM116. But overall amazing professor.

Genuinely one of the best professors/teachers I've had. He cares for all of his students and makes sure that everyone can understand and apply the material taught in the course. His dedication to making sure everyone succeeds is unmatched, and I wish that I could have him as a professor again.

Genuinely an amazing, respectful person with a heart for his students. One of the best teachers I've ever had in my life. I felt welcomed into university knowing I could walk down the steps after lecture, say hello, and shake his hand. Although I don't have him anymore, I'm going to try to meet him for faculty lunches.Course wasn't too hard either.

He cares a lot for your success and proves it by the amount of time he pours into his students. He offers study sessions prior to each exam and is willing to communicate with his student directly instead of going through a TA. His exams are pretty easy and he provides plenty of study material to help you do well.

A very good prof who prepares his students well for their exams. Cares for each and every student and is willing to answer any questions during lectures. Probably one of the most compassionate professors I've met.

Had Dr. Budhi for ochem. Fantastic guy who really cares about his students success. When he saw that our test average fell he felt as if he failed us as a teacher. While he does have an accent, its not hard too adjust to it. He posts every lecture online and office hours are incredibly accessible and helpful.
Pretty good guy. Does study sessions before each exam and records them. The sessions make the exams more doable. 10/10
Dr. Budhi is a very good professor. He is very knowledgeable and makes the material interesting. He is very accessible during office hours and is willing to help students who are struggling.

Dr. Budhi is a kind, helpful, and approachable CHM 11510 professor. He chats with students before class and around campus. Though some struggle with his accent, he posts lecture slides and recordings. Tests reflect class concepts, and he avoids spoonfeeding answers. Despite teaching >400 students, he tries to get to know each one. Great guy, 10/10!
Very smooth and well organized course. Went through the basics of probability and random variables clearly.
A weird professor…Lecture is boring and not accessible in office hours

I really enjoyed his lectures as he explained the topics very well, even the more difficult topics later in the course.
Grading was quite lenient and exams were of a reasonable difficulty and similar to the practice exams that he sent and the course homeworks.
Would definitely recommend.

Buzzard is a great professor with clear notes and expectations. That said his exam problems are extremely challenging and have a lot of curve balls. However he is 100% open to helping and giving clarification. To succeed at 519, do all the problems in Ross both graded+ungraded and you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment:
Great prof overall. If you can get him, go for it - and select early. I messed up my final exam pretty bad (MCQs) and ended up with an overall score ~ 84 out of 100. Still got an A-.
Advice: Attend his lectures in person. You will never get time again to watch the lectures online. It doesn't happen. You don't have to pay attention-just attend!!!
Great professor! Exams are tough but he is a reasonable grader.
