Great lectures. Makes the content easy to follow. You can tell that he cares that students are learning. Overall a great experience taking the course with him.

I really enjoyed Buzzard as a professor. He shows great examples and gives time for you to try things on your own. I found it very helpful to go to office hours since the class was hard but he does a great job of explaining things, especially during 1 on 1. Funny guy and really enjoyed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Buzzard does a good job overall. His penmanship won't win any awards, but is still mostly readable. His lectures are useful, but I watched Chen's lectures on BoilerCast instead because I liked his style more. The exams sucked all the fun out of the course for me and I actually CODOed out of math. Prepare to work hard. Good luck. You will need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very approachable as a person. All of his lectures are very well organized. He always starts conceptual, and then moves on to examples that are useful in the online homework and in exams. He tries to interact in lecture, and if a student gives a wrong answer, he looks at it from their perspective and explains where they were right and wrong.

Wonderful professor. Always smiles and makes the lectures fun, keeps the class alive. I wasn't enrolled just wanted to sit in his class and he was super supportive of this, his attitude really helped motivate me.
Teaches concepts well. Very helpful. Makes it fun sometimes
Awesome professor! Speaks clear English and is very clear in class. His exams had difficult questions, but they were curved very fairly.

Fantastic. Best math professor I have had. I love math but I feel that my success in this class was in large part, due to Buzzard. He speaks clear english, is very accessible outside of class, and is very willing to help. The way he presents material is well though out and organized.
Very good! Lectures are easy to follow, very accessible in and out of class.

Possibly the most enthusiastic professor I've ever had. Homeworks take a very long time but only one is due per week. Exams are open-note and based very heavily on homework with plenty opportunity for bonus points. Lectures tend to get sidetracked or sometimes feel irrelevant, but overall fairly average for CoE. Lots of work but not hard to pass.
chiller, lots of homework though

He's nice enough and knows the material he's teaching, but is not considerate of your time at all. Homeworks, while not necessarily difficult, take hours, and many homework questions and quizzes require a separate time commitment outside of just answering the questions (physically going somewhere on the edge of campus just to take a picture)

Class isn't horrible, just a ton of pointless work, and most of it is just busy work that barely relates to the topic. He is very enthusiastic about the topic which is great but he doesnt know how to give a reasonable homework or even exam preparation.

Great professor.
The homework problem sets are long and can take up to several hours.
The work isn't at all hard but it is time consuming.
The exams are fair and based on the homework.
Attendance isn't required but I would strongly recommend it if you want to do well.

This class is a lot of work for the information talked about with quizzes, homeworks, field trips, and exams. Unfortunately you have to go to remote parts of campus for some homeworks which is difficult at times, and you have to pick up barely mentioned things in lecture for hints on homeworks and exams.

Exams are worth 70% of your grade, with most questions related to the homework. Homework could take 2+ hours to complete each week so make sure you have enough time (also required to take selfies at certain areas of campus). Every students have one mandatory presentation in front of class. Everything is doable, but not an easy grade.

Overall, CE361 with Professor Bullock is a great class. It is not very difficult, and exams reflect homework problems. Homework can be long and frustrating but you take a lot form them. Lectures can be annoying cause he won't really talk about course content and instead random stuff about transport engineering. Really good guy tho, high energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's nice, and clearly knowledgeable about the topics, but don't expect to get much from the lectures. The homework and exams stem from book content for the most part, and unfortunately the lectures are a huge waste of time, he isn't very clear on what types of problems he puts on the exams either, and doesn't offer study material either.

Prof. Bullock is eccentric, courteous, and high-energy. He loves class participation and his lectures are engaging. Homework is doable and as long as you study for exams, you will be fine. I would definitely take his class again!

The exams and HW he gave were very reasonable. Learning primarily occurred outside the classroom through reading the textbook, but going to class is still a good experience because he provides some nice real world examples.
really boring lecturer and serves no doesnt really teach the material.
he was kind of a prick, but a decent teacher.
uh uh uh uh studder but easy A just go to class
No Comments
Very ineffective style of teaching.  Very distracting lecture habits. Cannot express any thoughts without stuttering repeatedly.
Great easy class, great prof, definitely choose in person section. Textbook required. Take with friends!

Took class fall semester of senior year. It was during Covid so the class was virtual for me which kind of stunk but made it crazy easy. You can find answers to any assignment online and even if you do terrible on your wine video you still get full credit. Lectures are interesting just super long. Cheers
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor, he was really fun and wine appreciation was a good class. It was asynchronous online so you didn't have to complete anything until finals week if you didn't want to.

Good professor, known mostly for his wine appreciation class. Concentrated too much on the history and background of different wine regions, a lot of theory. Did not teach how to identify flavours or aromas during actual tasting. Still a great course, helpful in real life.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You get 3 different wines, cheese and bread at every class. The lecture is pretty boring though. Bring homework. Good class, but take it pass/fail if you can. Very detailed exam. Great to take with friends!

This professor is pretty much the king of wine. He knows every detail of every piece of wine information possible, and will teach you ALL OF IT. The class wasn't as easy as it seems as you have to know over 700 slides of information per exam. Exams are 80% of your overall grade, along with a wine visit and class serving teams. (20%) Overall not bad

This class is not necessarily an easy A. You have to memorize a lot of inane details for the tests. First half of semester is kind of fun. Second half is insanely boring. Take HW to do during lecture.

Bunning always had good informative lectures that were easy to follow and take notes. However, the CS159 course is terribly designed which is not Bunning's fault. Group labs were terrible as one person ended up doing most of the work and the grading on the your code being efficient rather than working was not cool. If the code works its works.

Professor Bunning was fantastic at explaining the C language. His way of teaching made learning more complex topics easier to grasp. While his lectures aren't the most engaging in the world, they are very informative and critical if you want to do well in this class. Overall, this course is overly hated and isn't too bad in reality.

There is something monotone about his voice that never fails to put me to sleep. Other than that, he was a pretty okay prof.

Tests are designed to trick you, the questions are heavily worded and they always have a 'all of the above' or 'none of the above'. The tests are not designed to gauge your performance but trip you up.
Really clear and engaging lectures. Explains difficult topics very well
Too high of an ego
Bunning was the best professor I have had at Purdue so far. Good lecturer and you can tell that he cares about his students.
Bunning is a good lecturer and you can tell that he is passionate about computer science. Attendance is pretty much required, otherwise you will lose iClicker lecture quiz points.

Bunning - great professor and lecturer. Not only did he teach programming in C, but he taught the importance of computer science and its applications to many disciplines. His lectures were very enjoyable because they emphasized a variety of skills rather than focusing on purely coding. 4/5 because he got frustrated from to time and hard iClickers.
You can pretty much live without reading the book, but it is needed on occasion for lab problems. The lecture slides are great to study with.
Professor does a good job lecturing. SI is helpful if you are struggling in some areas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had no problem getting an A. Good professor. Enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He teaches alright, but to truly understand content, I recommend taking notes on the book as well. Having mandatory class, especially seating assignments (for a lecture hall? really?) is annoying to say the least. He also cracks jokes that most of the time aren't humorous. However, if you just want a prof that can teach, Bunning is alright.
The coronavirus was not his fault. Still ended up being a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was one of the best lecturers I had at Purdue.
Attendance is important and you have to pay attention in class. But he is a good lecture and fair.

This professor could have a very enjoyable class. But he ruined the topic of Computer Science my Freshmen year. He won't even start lecture until all computers and phones are put away but it is a COMPUTER science course. "Don't email me" which is just crazy to say as a prof. He makes a notebook every year with all of his notes that you need tobuy
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall not a bad professor but he has dry lectures. If you get the 9:30 lecture and know you will probably not be awake on time switch out of it because ATTENDANCE is MANDATORY.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man is nuts, he wrote a 300 page book called "The Church", he reads his lectures straight from the slides and has none of his own thoughts to offer. BEWARE!

Acceptable teaching. You can also search C Programming tutorial online to learn by yourself. Usually, you have two choices on CS 159. Choose Bunning, his curve on test is large!!! Lectures have quiz questions, but corrections are not important. You give answers, you get scores. Homework is not difficult, not many. Lab work depends on your team.

I have bigger issues with the class itself than Bunning himself. He makes an effort to answer students' questions and explains the material as well as he can. The main problem is that tests and clicker questions test your human compiling ability more than your ability to write code. This class will be hard if you're not good at quick arithmetic.
Excellent lecturer. I didn't know if I would like coding, but now it is my favorite subject.

He teaches as if everyone taking his class already has coding experience. Lectures are extremely dry and hard to take notes on. He forces you to buy his own book that consists of the notes he puts on a projector by going through notes too fast for you to copy down. Tests are tough even if you have prior coding experience. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Having to get up for an 8:30 lecture in the winter only to sit in his lectures was a bit of a pain. The room he taught in, EE 129, made you want to sleep. His teaching style was hard to follow and honestly not overly engaging, although he had his moments. Make sure to run the attend command at lab, or you will fail, which is why I did lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bunning did a poor job of properly teaching people how to code. He expects all of his students to have already had previous programming experience and gets off topic a lot during the lecture. Additionally, the content he discusses in lectures does not pop up anywhere on his exams. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bunning was a decent lecturer and the clicker questions each class were free points.
good
Bunning was a really cool guy and he taught very well

If you have previous programming experience then this class won't be too hard. I showed up for the Iclicker questions and then didn't really pay too much attention afterward. Labs/Homeworks can be time-consuming depending on the assignment but I didn't really struggle with any of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The lectures are good and cover pretty much everything you need to know for the tests. SI also helped reinforce a lot of the concepts. I wasnt thinking that I would like programming, but this class changed my mind.
I really learned a lot from Professor Bunning and was one of the better lectures I have had. The programs you have to write are not easy, but they have lots of TAs to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bunning drones on and on during lecture, literally reading off of slides word for word that are already in the course packet. His voice does not change tone once, and anything you learn is either from the textbook or during lab. At least the clicker questions dont have to be correct to get points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm very mixed about this professor. He is the most relatable for CS 159 and the easiest grader. He knows how to teach this class super well. The only problem is that he makes some extremely sexist remarks sometimes. As one of the few girls in his class, I could not believe some of the things he'd say and my guy friends agreed. Book is not needed.

I enjoyed Professor Bunnings lectures even though they were always the latest one of my days. He is knowledgeable in his field of specialty. He explain how the mechanisms behind both hardware and software. He is an easier grader than his colleague. If you are new to coding, SIs are helpful for exams from my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, but the class is difficult. Don't skip class or you will lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: As someone who had never seen computer programming before coming to Purdue, Professor Bunning did a great job explaining things. It was very hard at times, but I felt that his notes & lectures helped a lot. Also read the textbook. Labs and homework are not related to the exam. Exams are more logic based.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gives extra credit for every exam (Points could range from 3 to 15 points). Lectures aren't the most interesting you would find, but then again its CS 159. You'll do fine if you put in extra work in the class (i.e try to not miss homework, labs or lectures, even if they are difficult, because most of the time they will be.)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Bunning teaches basic C programming in a clear, easily understandable way with readily accessible lectures and notes.  The labs were sometimes tedious but usually worthwhile for understanding, as was the homework.  Overall fun and good professor

He's a boring lecturer. Not much homework throughout the class. He curves all the exams, but they have nothing to do with coding - just tests you on whether you can read logic and there are some true / false questions.  Comes off as a rude and isn't very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great lecturer but you have to keep with the work to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pretty good lecturer. His lectures can get pretty bland at times, but he knows what he's talking about and will answer your questions aptly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Bunning is quite possibly the best lecturer at Purdue University. Actually, I take that back. He is the best professor at Purdue. Professor Bunning not only deepened my understanding of computer science; he made me a better person and student. I will always look back fondly on CS159. Alan Bunning: man, myth, legend.
Lectures can get kind of boring, but attendance is mandatory via iClicker questions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You need to attend class and study hard to succeed in this course. C is not the easiest language to learn, especially for one with no prior programming experience. That being said, Professor Bunning was very helpful throughout my course and did his best to ensure we had a firm grasp of concepts taught in class. One of the better lecturers I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Bunning is one of the more enjoyable professors I've had at Purdue so far. He is actually enthusiastic about what he is teaching, and he always answers questions during lecture. However, there were still lectures where I fell asleep, but coding is only so interesting to me... My only problem was that he seemed arrogant during office hours.
Lectures are good. Need to attend class to get iClicker points.
Bad lecture, and you must follow assigned seat

Lectures are good 90% of the time. If you need homework/lab help in this course go to TA, the earlier in the week the better. If you need help understanding something else go to office hours. Wish I would have know this earlier. I missed an A by 6 points. Use the textbook for studying.  Background in coding helps, but not necessary to get an A.

Does iClicker questions at the beginning of lecture for attendance. Answering them at all is sufficient. Don't talk too loudly during lecture or he'll call you out. Don't share homework code with one another, they catch it easily. His notes cover almost all the material; I'd say the book is redundant. Exams are tough - know your concepts and terms.
Amazing professor
Professor Byun is an amazing professor who truly cares about his subject and his students. The course work is light but relevant and effective. I would highly reccomend this class to everyone.
Half of your grade comes with the final and a project due during finals week which sucks. Overall energetic guy and class is not too time consuming

I switched into a 7:30 section to have Professor Byun. Never regretted it. He is super kind, very knowledgeable, and overall one of my favorite business professors. The class consisted mainly of a few short writings (1 paragraph max), some case study analyses, a midterm, final project, and final exam. AI is encouraged on the final project. 10/10!

Lectures were very interesting and easy to follow-he really cares about what we are learning about. There are case studies, so there is a decent amount of reading, but the cases are easy to be interested in & he's not harsh on grading. His midterm was difficult imo, but the average wasn't bad. Final project is not difficult, AI is encouraged!
The course material can be somewhat uninteresting at times, but Byun is an awesome professor to have.
Really enjoy the class, professor Byun is very inspirational
wonderful lectures, love those case studies, they help me to get a more thorough understanding about the concepts

One of the most caring and helpful professor in Purdue! The case study materials are very fun and I learned a lot from them. Also, the workload is not heavy.

Professor Byun is so nice and helpful. He helped me a lot in classroom and even write me a wonderful recommendation letter.  I love the class and the professor!
Loved this class and professor. He was very inspiring and did a splendid job explaining the material. Definitely take this class and take it with Prof Byun! Would love to do more classes with him!

Taking this class with Professor Byun was one of the most fun experiences I had at Purdue! The class was very interesting to be in and he was very well prepared for each class. Highly recommend this class and this professor. Wish there are more professor's like him out there who are out to be a good person and inspirational teacher!
He is a smart and funny guy. The materials are based on all the Powerpoint he made. It is fun to watch. The exam are tricky. I would like to give him 100/100 if he reply email.

Take MGMT 352 with Byun! He is a really easy professor and the average for assignments was never less than 98%. There are 10 writing assignments but the max was 2 pages, most of them he just wanted a paragraph. He makes the lectures engaging and by going to lecture you will understand the cases much better.

A lot of the lectures are based off of case readings you do for homework. Some concepts are a bit tricky but he does a good job of explaining. There's not a lot of things for grading so you have to do well on all assignments.
Inspired to teach and does a good job at it too!

The problem with this class isnt the professor, its the way its designed. its a trap induced to fail students. i dont blame jung for making this class hard but his attitude towards us at the end was horrible. he didnt respond to emails when we asked for our grades/grade boundaries (finals) and i still dont know my final exam score so thats that

Prof. Jung's lectures were engaging and he explained the most conceptually difficult parts of 2k2 well. His dad jokes were some of the best moments of an otherwise tough class. The exams this semester were brutal, but not written by him, and he did his best to prepare us for them.

Professor Jung's lectures were incredibly hard to follow and were not very well organized in terms of content. The textbook for the class was way more helpful his lectures. No homeworks in the class, just 2 exams and 2 design project submissions. All learning happened by reading textbook, searching for things online, or talking with classmates.

Byunghoo is the best professor to take ECE 2k2 with. His lectures are great and he makes sure to keep students engaged with jokes during the lecture. His exams are managable and he provides lots of great hints during lecture about what he might test on.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is actually rating for ECE20002. Lectures more complicated than needs to be, much material not covered on HW & exam; can also move fast at times and was still behind schedule. HW more complex than what was on exam, but TAs will help. Exams were mostly fair, but little in class practice or review. Overall, ok; just review material periodically.

ECE 201 is a hard course but Jung makes the best of it. He puts a lot of work into his lectures and tries to ensure that students understand the concepts. Homeworks are useless for exam practice (much more time-intensive than actual exam problems). Focus on doing past exams and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kinda a thick accent. Course in itself is really difficult, and he does an okay job of explaining such things.

This is a tough class, but Jung is a great professor to learn from. He does a great job explaining things in simple terms and emphasizing key concepts. Go to class because the book is extremely unorganized and poorly written garbage.

Professor Bynum did a really good job at teaching this course. I would not describe myself as a person who is good at history, but the way he explained the material just made so much sense. While your grade is only determined by three essays, as long as you engage with the assigned reading and attend class, it isn't too hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really chill professor that has a good sense of humor. There are 3 tests that make up all of your grade but the class is not too hard if you have a background in US History

Dr. Bynum is so funny and so great. Attendance is not mandatory, but that is the only way to do well on the exams because those exams require information you can only get from lecture. Exams are three essays throughout the semester about the textbook and lectures, and those are the only grades in the gradebook. Just go to class and you'll pass.

If you're going to take any of this prof's classes you need to make sure you go to as many lectures as possible and participate in in-class discussions. He only has three things for grades and they're all exams. He had the final at 50% of class credit which was super frustrating and you will fail if you don't show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures. He made a point to answer students questions and also connect history to the modern day. He made some boring topics fun and interesting for me. If you attend the lectures you will have no problem passing this class. For the final, read the book (not the textbook) because you will seriously struggle if you haven't.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't want a B or worse, then don't choose his course. The lecture was extremely heavy and there was no complete PowerPoint for each of the classes. Your grades only depended on three essays, there were no homework quizzes or participation. Those essay graders were tough, so just be careful if you can't avoid his course.

The class itself seems straight forward. For a 100-level class, it should be an easy gpa booster. But depending on when you take it, the grading assistants will turn this class to a gpa lowering class if they can. Bynum doesn't answer emails, grading assistants dont respond to emails, no grading rubrics or feedback on essays. Poorly managed overall
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great professor... often went on tangents and I didn't find the lectures effective. If you do the readings and watch supplemental videos online you will be fine for the exams. He told us at the beginning of the year he was not really into it anymore. Which is fine, but it seems to have impacted his care and excellence for teaching the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bynum is a great lecturer, especially in a small class setting. We read three books over the course of the semester and lectures helped supplement for the three exams (which are the only grades for the course). Lecture attendance was completely optional but the lectures are engaging enough that I went to all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked his lectures. he actually wants you to connect historical events rather than just cite facts. 2 exams and final are the only grades. as long as you actually go to the lectures you'll understand the content. attendence isn't necessary but exams are set up to fail those who don't show up regularly, and read the book or you'll fail the final.

I hear a lot of people say they dislike him, which I understand why, but I think the class is a very easy A. Never paid attention in lectures and did fine with all our exams because they were all online. He did go on tangents a lot but if he confuses you then make sure to take advantage of the TAs. They usually do a good job at clearing things up.

Worst professor I have ever had. Often times goes on tangents about random things that have nothing to do about the class topic. Heard from some people to not take this professor, and to drop the class, wishing I did. I leave this class every lecture wishing I had never taken the class. Very poorly run class, grades are based upon 3 essays.

He canceled class all the time and then was very unclear about what would be covered on the tests. I did all the reading and went to class whenever he held it and still only got a B. Don't take him if you can avoid it.
Super hilarious and a great teacher, he delivers important information effectively, has a good taste in movies and music, very generous grader, offers extra credit.

Honestly the worst professor and the worst class I have ever taken at Purdue. All three of the exams (the only grades in the class) are based off reading the textbook and other assigned books. He doesn't believe in study guides, but he will let you bring in a list of what you think mine be short answer topics, but knowing the info doesn't even help

Professor Bynum is easy going but enjoys preaching his own political viewpoints rather than just teaching us history. Attendance is not mandatory and his lectures are irrelevant because only material from the readings are on the exams. If you want a class that you can completely blow off then this is the class for you.

The class was easy but I do feel like I learned a lot. He assigns a lot of reading but you don't have to read every single page to do well. We had a great class atmosphere and Bynum was always very willing to clarify/answer questions. He encouraged debate and discussion which led to very educational conversations. Overall, great class!

The class was not very difficult but I do feel like I learned a lot. He assigns a lot of reading but you don't have to read every single page in order to do well. We always had a fun class atmosphere and he was always VERY willing to clarify things. He encouraged debate and discussion which led to some very educational conversations. Great class!
Great class as long as you do the assigned reading the exams are easy! Professor is very funny and keeps you engaged!

Very easy going teacher. Attendence not mandatory and the class was very conversational. If you ask a question he will go above and beyond to answer. 3 tests, no hw, but as long as you read the assigned readings you'll  just fine. Really funny guy, enjoyed the class.

Good proffessor. Really easy going and very accomodating to any absences or problems i had. Easy to talk to and get along with, makes the subject interesting, and knows alot about it. exams are not hard, can pass with an A with 1 days study. Would definately recommend taking his courses

Professor Bynum is the worst professor I've had at Purdue. His exams cover nothing from lecture, even things from previous exams in a non cumulative class. He cancels lectures constantly, skipping material that should be covered on the exams. Professor Bynum doesn't believe in study sheets for exams, and that grades do not matter. Steer clear.

Worst professor I've had @ Purdue! Exam material has nothing to do with lectures and there is no incentive to go to class. Grade is 3 exams and honestly, there was nothing from lecture on the test. Spent 10 hours studying to fail a test. Won't talk about the tests bc he knows how pissed off students were. Very lazy teacher and it shows through majo

Prof. Bynum is very easy going and easy to get along with.  He doesn't take attendance and shows quite a few films on African-American History.  The books he assigns for outside reading are interesting.  No homework, just 3 exams, so each one is a huge chunk.  Exams are essay and short answer

He's the worst professor I've had in a long time. His lectures do not go with his exams. He is not willing to work with absences, even if you had a good reason not to be there. His attendance policy is each class you miss you get 1/2 a letter grade deducted from your final overall course grade. It's ridiculous.

I agree with the other student from 396 about his lecturing. Although, it seemed like he really did not enjoy the course topic and repeatedly mentioned that it wasn't really his area. Maybe he would have been better in another class. He seemed like a nice guy
he is very straight forward and over all very good

Bynum is not a great lecturer, he too often says "umm" and "uh", and sometimes students call him on outright errors.  He does put forth effort and care about the class though, and overall he's pretty good.

Professor Bynum is one of the most intelligent and easy going teachers I have ever had!!! He was always there to over his help and he was able to make class very interesting. I would recommend taking one of his history classes on the Civil Rights Movement.
Very fair teacher.  Good sense of humor.  Good stories.
Very good professor.  Funny guy!

He is a really straight forward teacher.  No big surprises on the test and is fair to all students.  His style of teaching (mostly reading directly from his notes) takes some getting used to, but he tends to make class more fun as the semester goes on.

Min is an awesome professor. The slides are very high quality, he demonstrates respect for his students, and he is very helpful if you need it. The class can be challenging at times, but he is very helpful. Also shoutout to his TAs, they are very helpful as well. Plus he is a chill guy too.

I took 315, and it was amazing! Prof Min demonstrated coding in class and explained it line by line, which was very helpful. Although the textbook was outdated, he provided updated materials as lecture notes. I wish CIT had more professors like him because he genuinely cares about the course. He has quickly become one of my favorite professors!

I was able to feel that how much he prepared for every single lecture. His lecture note contains all the necessary information to understand the course materials, and he explained each of them clearly. Overall, he does a great job understanding what his students need and is a very humble, genuine, kind, and funny professor.
Prof. Min explains each line of code and uses parts of codes to explain. He also teaches how and what we are learning could be applied in real world experiences. Highly recommend!

Professor Min teaches each and every topic very efficiently. I believe the instructor is well prepared for the lectures and explains everything in a perfect way. I liked the labs a lot and thought that there were very helpful in reinforcing the learned materials. Moreover, Professor Min is very friendly, approachable and entertaining!

Professor Min is an excellent professor. Ive had him for CIT 355, 425, and 581. I think I am one of the few who have had all of his courses. He has a bit of an accent, but he prepares class very well and he is super chill!

Byung Cheol Min is very hypocritical. He acts very nice and caring, but in truth, all he cares about is whether you can produce paper for him. Whenever you seek advice from him, he tries to tell you things that will benefit himself. He'd tell you to relax for your thesis defense and then you will give you a hard time during the defense. Stay away!
Very good at lecture and provided relevant examples using robots from his research. Excellent slides and very informative!

gives good feedback; respected; accessible outside class; group projects; clear grading criteria; amazing lectures; caring; one of best Prof I've met in Purdue. just one drawback: accent (moderate level) may distract non-English native speakers like me from the lecture. PS: cnit 355: moderate level homework:2  5 hours each week

Professor Min is an excellent instructor and he is incredibly effective in instruction. He explains even the most difficult material well. He cares about his students and takes their questions and concerns seriously. I really liked the student seminars we did and it was a wonderful experience for the entire class. My favorite class I took!
Prof. Min is my new favorite CIT professor. I learned a lot from him and this class, and I really feel like I'm a better programmer.
This professor knows about the subject well and explains step by step with interesting examples. The PowerPoint slides on blackboard are very helpful!

I took Software Design and Development for Robotics Class taught by Dr. Min. Simply, Dr. Min is a great professor. He really cares that his students gain knowledge and not just pass the class. He understands his student's needs and makes sure to make labs and class as convenient for us as possible!

Dr. Min is the best professor I've ever had in CIT. This guy is just all sorts of awesome, and a dedicated professor. He's ALWAYS happy to help. I can't even count how many times he's stayed after class. Dr. Min is a very nice good natured person and he really really cares about his students and their work. Take his every class!
You need to read many papers, but the professor will recommend it. There is a lot of homework but it is really helpful for your research.

Very disorganized. Vapid or needlessly long assignments. Easy, but extensive labs that can be a pain to finish during the given time. Professor is very unwavering and not empathetic. Utilized some statistical techniques/knowledge that wasn't taught in the class. Communication issues between her and everyone else, TAs included.
Possibly the worst professor I've ever dealt with in my college career. Completely unorganized and shows no empathy for students.

The class is extremely unorganized. There will be different versions of rubrics/requirements for the same project. 

I wasn't taught how to data visualize outside of Excel at all. There was no guidance on any other visualizing tools. 

POOR COMMUNICATION. Always a technical difficulty. Don't buy the textbooks.

This class is not easy at all, but if you go to class and prepare the material well then an A is not hard. Professor Byrd is not a great person in terms of course organization, but if you take time to discover the material then the course is definitely achievable.

Dr. Byrd is very unclear with her due dates and the class is very unorganized. You are likely to miss a lot of assignments and get a 0 just because she wont even tell you what assignments are due. She is very unclear. The material is overcomlicated for no reason and the TAs are low key unhelpful.
I hate this class so much dont take she sucks

The combination of awful communication, often dropping assignments the night before they are due the following morning, or failing to make clear the requirements, and her rigorous unforgiving harshness in grading, combines to create a frustrating experience. If you get this teacher, switch immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is terrible, and I mean it. Save yourself and don't take this class. The quizzes are impossible to study for and the class is organized terribly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Confusing instructions with no help or explanation, drops a lab, homework, and readings onto the class the night before classes begin with no possible warning. Her way of teaching is time consuming and headache inducing, but the side effect seems to be I'm understanding quite a lot, however this has to do more with me having to figure things out.

This class was terribly unorganized. There was little communication on how to complete assignments and she does not get around to grading anything until the end of semester. We have tried to talk with the department head about the problems with the class but there was little to no change.
Avoid CGT 270 if you can.

I took CGT 270 in fall 2020. Dr. Byrd's class is incredibly disorganized, and is front-loaded with readings, labs, and lectures. The biggest issue was a grading scale where a 90% was considered failing until she changed it on the last day of class. Regardless, she is great to talk to outside of class, particularly if you are interested in research.

This professor was one of the worst teachers to ever teach a class that I've taken. The course was completely disorganized and there seemed to be technical issues all the time. We've had a meeting with the head of the department two times about this with hardly any change from her. If you don't have to take this course, then please don't take it.

If being disorganized and unbearable was a professional sport, Byrd would be an Olympic gold medalist. Her communication is horrible, has the most ridiculous policies, goes over more ways of how you can fail the class rather than succeed, and issues happen every single class. Avoid this class like the plague if it isn't required for your major!!!

Every other post is accurate. This is the worst class I've ever taken. Byrd is the worst professor I've ever had. It doesn't matter if you like data vis or if you're typically a good student, there is no succeeding in this class. It's disappointing that the school hasn't done anything about it even though we have met with the head of the department

This is the worst class I've ever taken and I've had high school teachers give me panic attacks in public. Everything about this class is frustrating and enraging, from Dr. Byrd's conduct, to her TA's incompetence and lack of communication with the professor, to her ridiculous grading criteria. If you can avoid it, STAY AWAY.

Content is not hard. But, understanding data visualization has nothing to do with your performance in this course. You must read Byrd's mind to succeed. All her directions are wrong, but you won't know that, so you'll fail the assignments. You won't be able to submit anything, the software doesn't work. You'll lose points because of this. STAY AWAY

I was in this class for just 2 weeks . I've taken quizzes based on info I have not been taught. It is extremely disorganized and difficult and the TA is short and unhelpful. I have never been this stressed from a course and emotionally drained. Prof seems to not want students to succeed and treats them like an annoyance when they are lost, avoid it

This class is the most over complicated course I've taken. The Brightspace (course portal) is overly complex with dates and times where if you miss one assignment it disappears and then you can't access the next assignment. The class Instructor and TA struggle to answer questions. The lectures and labs are always confusing.

Terrible professor, incredibly disorganized. She's one of those professors that are like "do not call my mrs. byrd" and "make sure to address your emails properly, I will not respond to emails without a proper greeting" It has been 1 week since the semester started and the whole class is already done with her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Despite being very disorganized, Dr. Byrd cares more about logistics than assignments. She doesn't make her expectations clear (read: no rubrics) and rarely responds to email. Your lab grade comes solely from completing outdated and unhelpful "Tableau training" videos on your own, not labs, and Tableau isn't formally taught despite using it in lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She cares about what she's teaching, but the class was extremely unorganized. I found it difficult to tell what was due when and she was very strict about insignificant details. She seemed very helpful and personable outside of class, but in class I found her to be intimidating and unhelpful.

I'm sure Professor Byrd is a good person, but her teaching style is unorganized and caused too much suffering. Be prepared to use "Tableau" and access lots of excel worksheets. She is difficult to get a hold of through email sometimes, but enough annoying emails will get your message though. Just stay on top of the workload (front-loaded class!)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Byrd teaches a masterclass in disorganization and poor communication. Right from the beginning of the semester Dr. Byrd and her TA excel at making things as difficult as possible for the student, making them go out of there way to find out whats happening. She treats the class as if its Junior High. She does the clap thing for silence like ????
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Byrd doesn't seem like she cares at all about this class. The whole thing is completely unorganized and the students are left to fend for themselves to figure out assignments and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Byrd is an absolute terrible teacher. Gives quizzes based of dozens of pages of reading, and only has a single question from that reading on the quiz. She never talks about the quiz again. She will sometimes not even mention an assignment, let alone give us instructions about it. It really seems like she doesn't care about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most frustrating professors I've had at Purdue. I'm a 5th year senior so I've taken my fair share of classes and hers is one of the worst.

I took her CGT270 class as an online student, but she had an in person class as well. She often would walk away from the microphone and then blame students online for not being able to hear her. When asked a question, she would say to refer to lecture notes and when you would point out the answer wasn't there, she would just ignore you. Truly awful
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really do think she is a good prof but she is unorganized. You learn tableau and the fundamentals of data viz and she has a lot of knowledge. I really do wish she was more organized because she has a ton to share. Try to get to know her outside of class she is cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is the most unorganized professor I have ever had. The due dates and instructions to assignments are unclear. We just finished the midterm to her class and I feel like I have not learned anything. She doesn't really teach, it is up to the students to teach themselves. In lab, we have to sit and watch videos for two hours.

The worst teacher I've ever had. I was excited for this class because it has to do with my major, but it feels like she just throws a bunch of stuff at us with no clear direction. She doesn't actually teach, but gives us a bunch of videos to watch instead. I'm gaining nothing important out of the dozens of assignments we're given each week. Useless

The most unorganized professor. Assigns a lot of work with unclear deadlines and barely any instructions. Does not use lab time correctly. Does not teach any relevant information during lecture, makes students teach everything to themselves through readings and videos. We have finished the 5th week of classes and we don't know how to make anything.

It started off with a fun, drawing activity about data with other students. Then, it just spiraled out of control. Juggling MULTIPLE projects, unclear directions w/ hw and shes constantly changing the deadline/syllabus. For our final presentation, she lectured us about getting a 5% deduction if we were late while she was 10 minutes late herself smh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Probably the worst class I've ever taken. The entirety of the course had 0 organization. Syllabus changed constantly. Multiple times she came to class asking us about a reading prompt she forgot to even assign us. This professor took an easy A class and made it impossible to follow. Lectures were also mandatory but had no relation to the labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Despite it being a 7:30 course, Dr. Byrd always comes to class prepared and ready to teach. Most of the course is project based, two with partners and one alone. The only thing I did not like was that because Dr. Byrd is so busy, her grading falls behind, as most of the work was graded in the last week. She is very flexible & receptive to critique.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. One of the select few professors who know how to teach.
honestly if you keep up with lectures it ends up being okay

i think overall they made cs 180 much easier (spring 25) than last sem (fall 24), really enjoyed dunsmore energy while teaching. he definitely kept my attention during lectures. wasnt fond of the plagiarism accusations. class overall was pretty easy tests are generally very specific to the slides, group project was a disaster.
Great professor, make sure you actually watch lectures otherwise you will fall behind quickly.

He's a pretty good professor, and explains the CS concepts pretty well. He's also pretty approachable after class. Although the class itself is intended to be a weedout, he actually tries to help people pass.
His examples for these concepts help but i think he uses too many of them (maybe 3-4 instead of 1-2).
Still pretty good.

Professor Dunsmore is a fantastic professor for an introductory-level CS course. CS 180 is a very difficult course, ever since they made it a "weed-out", but Dunsmore does his best to ensure his students still do well in the course. It's fast-paced if you don't have prior experience, but don't fall behind and pay attention to his lectures.
he was inspiring truely

Dunsmore himself is a great prof but cs 180 itself is a horribly structured and organized class. trivial questions on exams more about java syntax and cs 180 coding style rather than actual cs concepts.
Amazing lecturer. Great for an introductory course. Final project was a bit tough.

Professor Dunsmore is a great professor. The issue is how the class is run, the midterms had fair questions but the grading was way to harsh losing an absurd amount of points for a small mistake. The final asked questions that were uber specific having no relevance to real life coding or knowledge and did not fairly represent the course material.
Prof. Dunsmore is a really good professor. His lectures are enjoyable and he responds to emails quickly. I enjoyed being in his class and he taught really well.

The CS 180 course for this recent semester was horribly structured. The final exam questions were extremely specific for no reason. Throughout the semester, you will have to look up javadocs on Google to learn how to code yourself because these weren't covered in lectures and they expect you to know them. Projects are extremely time-consuming.
The test is crazy hard, and final just don't make any sense at all.

Professor Dunsmore is engaging and explains concepts well, but the slow pace and plain lecture slides can get boring. Use Unstuck ai and the free textbook to supplement and stay on top of the daily quizzes for an A.

Dunsmore is very nice, the lectures have a good vibe to them. Despite this, there definitely seems to be a disconnect between his attitude and the difficulty level of this semesters course. Midterm questions were fair but graded very harshly.

Professor Dunsmore is a phenomenal professor, and he clearly has such an immense passion for what he teaches his students, he really does seem to care about his students. The class itself, while pretty hard in terms of the exams and the sheer amount of work, is doable if you put in the effort, although I do wish there was more organization.
His lectures are great and he makes sure to explain concepts to the best of his abilities. The class is hard but he cares about the students and is always open to questions.
This guy is the best

He makes classes very interesting. Since I was new to Java, I had to go through lectures twice, even thrice to understand the entire material but apart from that it was a great experience. His material was easy to understand and gave real-life analogies as well.

Very good professor. He makes lectures very entertaining, and very informative. Despite the amount of topics in the course, he makes them all very understandable and engaging by showing examples from basic to real world application. Class is lecture heavy, however they aren't a burden to attend.

Good guy, pretty good professor. Brought us cookies for our TA's birthday! Definitely a hard class and work will pile up in the middle of the semester. However, not impossible. Dunsmore is funny and tries to make concepts understandable.

I enjoyed doing the work, however, at some point the amount of work was unreasonable. Like another user mentioned, we had a project, homework assignment, and team project all while studying for an exam. The exams were on paper and it was heavily graded. Not to mention this course lecture heavy, although the prof is very humorous during lectures.

All the teaching is through a PowerPoint. Although there is live coding once a week, it doesn't truly go over everything we learned in class. We learn basic syntax through the PowerPoint, but the homework and exams are extremely difficult, not matching what we learned in class. In one week I was given a group project, homework, project, and exam.

This professor reads straight from PowerPoint, focusing on random concepts like sentinel variables instead of practical coding skills. Vocareum, the coding platform, provides vague feedback, making it tough to learn. TAs lack expertise, and overall, the course feels more frustrating than helpful. Test out if possible.

Took CS180 over the summer as a rising high school sophomore, and this was indeed a hard class. Prof. Dunsmore taught the material extremely well. However, you better pray you get a good team for the team project. One of my teammates dropped the class last second and messed up our product.

The semester I was in unbelievably hard for no reason. We were employing CS182 and CS251 concepts into our code and expected you to be a god at coding. The group project was worse because one of my teammates dropped the course and one of my other teammates was useless. Then that teammate threw my peer review. I coded 75% of final project btw.

I had a bigger problem with the course itself rather than Professor Dunsmore. He makes tons of jokes and does his best to keep things engaging. However, he talks and moves through content incredibly slow, and his slides are plain white with black text (literally not a single bit of color). So ultimately I found lectures incredibly boring

He is a very good instructor who knows all too well how to keep his lectures engaging and interesting while scaffolding slowly to increase the rigor to a point where the students feel challenged yet enjoy it, which makes them give their absolute best!
He's a great professor and explains all the concepts really well
W Guy W Professor

Professor Dunsmore did an incredible job teaching the fundamental concepts of Computer Science in his CS180 (Java) course. At the start of the semester, I was worried I would struggle because of my lack of background knowledge. However, as the course continued, this concern faded. Dunsmore clearly has a passion for the subject.
W professor

Truly one of the kindest and most well-spoken professors I know of. I took CS 180 two years ago. Homework and projects can be challenging, but you'll learn a lot. Very reachable outside of class and replies to emails quickly, in my experience.

Dunsmore is a top-tier teacher. I came into this class without any CS experience and left with an A+. He has a very example-heavy lecture style, which is perfect for helping to understand abstract concepts. Pay attention in lectures, and it will pay off so much. As long as you work hard, you should be able to get an A.
Don't forget to do the daily quizzes and cooperate on the group projects and you'll be fine in the class.

Professor Dunsmore was an amazing first CS professor during my freshman year. He also made the material easy to understand and was very relaxed and respectful as long as you gave him that same respect while he was lecturing.

Professor Dunsmore is a good professor, especially for an intro-level class and I really appreciated the work he puts in. If you come in with no programming experience, you might have to work a bit outside of class.

The mic prof Dunsmore used was completely broken, which made it very hard for students to hear and follow his slide. We gave feedback about the mic problem and it was never resolved. Overall, he's a good professor, but not that good when you go to his class and can't even hear a word he's telling. If the mic is fixed, I'd give a solid 5 star.

Great professor who left me feeling prepared for future CS classes after coming in with zero CS knowledge.

Beware of the last two projects!! Getting bad groupmates can be detrimental. Start work early as the later assignments are impossible to do in one sitting. Do the weekly homework, as they're critical for cementing knowledge.
Great Class & Great Professor. A really good introductory course to object-oriented programming.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dunsmore and his lecture notes are all you'll need for this class. P.S: clap when the class is done!
Difficult course if this is your first CS class, but still doable. Start homework and projects early.
BEST CS COURSE EVER

Dunsmore is a really good professor to welcome freshman into CS at Purdue. He clearly cares about what he's teaching and is eccentric in all of the right ways. Unfortunately I'm only pursuing a CS minor, but I would've loved to have taken another one of his courses.

Dunsmore does a great job introducing new students to CS at Purdue. Really nice person once you get to know him but his lectures are kind of boring so they go by slow. There are quizzes after every lecture so don't forget to do them and the homework assignments can be really long and frustrating at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not to much homework, but it takes a long time to complete. Projects are easy other than the group project. The group projects do take a substantial amount of time. Good profesor and cares about us understanding the information.
Solid intro class, homeworks and projects are not too difficult, but start group projects early. The final is composed of a bunch of facts you can only know if you go to lecture.
Really down to earth guy who has a knack for breaking down and simplifying information well

Very nice, but hard to approach. START PROJECT EARLY. Can be frustrating at first to learn since it is all new, but keep at it and youll be okay. Just be aware of the time commitment. TAs werent very helpful and couldnt help much. Take CSBridge if you can, (its hard) but it helps a lot and you get to know him more personally!

Decent professor but his powerpoints were really boring, and hard to learn from. When explaining though he'd often make funny noises and those kept me engaged. Great professor for the intro class though.

Def a hard class, but Professor Dunsmore makes it fun. He makes concepts easy to understand if you have no prior knowledge. Funny and enthusiastic about eacher. The course starts off slow but picks up after the first project. A lot of work, but def doable if you put in the time to get things done ahead of time or ask help when you're stuck.

ONE OF THE BEST PROFS AT PURDUE!!! His lectures are so easy to follow and he's hilarious as well. He tries to get to know his students on a personal basis and I appreciate that a lot. He wants you to succeed in the class and he shows that. Tests (mostly coding) are not hard, just make sure you're familiar with the fundamentals
Dont know why hes rated so high here. His lectures are SO much harder than the hw assignments and projects. The TAs do all the work and they are so strict about everything.

Professor Dunsmore was one of the best teachers I've ever had! I was initially concerned about this class being online, but the lectures were amazing, the TAs were a great help, and the exams and homework were very straightforward if you watched the lectures. This class was a great introduction to core CS concepts.
Great intro class
Extremely easy A, easy quiz/assignment/exam.

Probably one of the best professors I have ever had. He is experienced in the material he is teaching and explains it very well and thoroughly, giving examples in multiple different scenarios. Although he is unable to handle students' questions himself, he employs TAs who are more than capable of assisting students well.

at the start of the semester you'll love him. he makes fun of IU,he seems chill,what could go wrong?by the middle of the sem you're drowning in homework,his lecture don't help,his slides are crap, you can't find any answers to the quizzes. it's just a dumpster fire. honestly don't think this class would be possible without the TAs, they're saviors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's really great at explaining complex CS concepts through examples, and seems like a personable and helpful professor (though I was asynch so what do I know). Tough class, but doable if you watch the lectures and refer to TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There are weekly MWF lectures , HW, and projects. The professor is very knowledgable, and teaches you why and when to use concepts instead of just telling you how. However, he categorizes students by "dumb" and "smart" in a way that I think he may not be receptive to a struggling student asking for help. The TAs are better suited for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think he is probably a good in person teacher, but right now he is very disconnected from his students. The TAs do absolutely everything in this class, including making our exams. He needs to put in more effort for us even though we are lowly freshmen, as the TAs do not really have any idea what they are doing.
Love the guy. Makes fun of IU on the regular. Really enthusiastic and gives amazing lectures.
Lectures are thorough and amazing, but they can feel a little slow-paced at times. Expect some spicy IU roasts.

If you take this class, you will going on trouble at homework. Every week has twice homework with project. There are really sucks which it makes you trouble on grading. His class and powerpoint? Nothing helpful on your hw and project. You need to search on google to find some information for java. Do not take this class ever
He is a tough grader. Lecture is not helpful, and theres lots of hw, projects and quizzes. I would not recommend to take him. A lot of people dropped it.
Dunsmore is my favorite professor in the CS department. Get him if you can.

He's not easy to reach outside of class and when I did get the chance to, he didn't respect my major. If you're not in cs, he doesn't want to hear it. He lets a TA run the entire class while he lectures so you won't really get to know him. Typical yt professor that has average slides but acts enthusiastic so the class is hard but not because of him
Fantastic human being, TA's are the ones who make the class practically impossible.

Daddy Dunsmore is a reason to come to Purdue on his own. I'm so glad I started learning programming with him. Class is large but TA's are usually quite good. Class is generally well designed. One of my more enjoyable classes.

Professor Dunsmore is a funny and charismatic professor who truly cares about his students. I took this class with no programming experience and finished the semester learning so much from him! The course overall has lots of resources to help you succeed as long as you're willing to ask for help. He is one of the best professors I've had at Purdue!

A well respected and humorous professor who does his best to keep endless black and white PowerPoint slides of code interesting. Lectures will never be a good way to learn how to code but Buster does his best. (recommend reading the textbook since it's hard to focus in class)
Best professor so far.

Dunsmore lectures are amazing. A definitely laugh at least once in each of his lectures. The way he explains the subject makes it clear that he loves Computer Science (and his jokes makes it clear that he hates IU). Dont't cheat! Dunsmore will "tell you to drop the class, encourage you to change majors and write a letter for your permanent record".

Prof. Dunsmore is very caring about his students and you can tell that he tries his best to make sure everybody succeeds. Definitely be prepared to work hard and pay attention during the lectures. He makes the lectures very fun to listen to and overall it's a very good class. :)
A really good professor. Makes you want to work harder and be like him. Very inspirational. HIs lectures are very easy to understand, and with some dedication and effort one can easily do well.

One of the best professors I've had. He gives great, entertaining lectures, and all the coursework comes directly from them. Having him as your first CS professor will give you a great groundwork to build upon. Just pay attention in class and make sure you understand the homework/labs and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is very hit or miss. If you have a decent grasp on coding concepts already this class is a breeze. If you struggle with coding you'll be fine if you pay close attention during the lecture which are amazing and hilarious anyway. Both midterms are live coding and every other assignment is live graded so you can resubmit till its perfect.
He makes IU jokes, what more do you need?

I came into this class with no programming experience, and I was scared that CS wasn't meant for me. After taking this course, thanks to Professor Dunsmore, I found my true passion for CS after everything I learned in this course. I have never seen a professor that cares more about his students. He is such a fantastic and inspirational guy.
Dunsmore is a great lecturer. Pay attention in class or the final will be extremely difficult.

He seems like a great guy and he seems to understand a lot about Computer Science, but as a non Computer Science major, it was extremely difficult for me to understand Computer Science from him. I think he's pretty overrated and trying to understand was like him speaking in a foreign language or something :/
He is definitely the best professor for cs

I messed up HARD on the first exam as reflected by my final grade, but nonetheless, Dunsmore makes what can be a pretty dry subject (especially if you've taken AP CS) quite lively. Be prepared for a good amount of project work, but with a fair amount of effort, this class may even be considered an 'Easy A'. If you haven't coded before, read textbk.

His lectures are super lively and he does his best to make it fun. The class is designed for someone with no prior coding experience--it moves quickly, but he explains things clearly enough that you should be fine if you keep up and do the work.
Good Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really funny guy that makes learning code fun.

Professor Dunsmore is really good. I took Java in high school but he explains it so much better and I know a lot more already. He explains really well and his expectations are clear. It was a pleasure to be in his class.
Very funny guy but the course is too difficult.
Dunsmore really cares about us. Thank you for all your hard work Dr Dunsmore!
He's a great professor and really funny. CS180 wasn't an easy class, but Dr. Dunsmore makes it enjoyable.

He mostly teaches Engineering Programming but is volunteering teaching this class.   He believe the first course in CS would be important for the students's success. He teaches with great clarity and passion,  always make nice jokes and vivid examples. Going to his class, get the projects and tests done, you will get good grade in this course
If Dr. Dunsmore couldn't be categorized as an excellent professor, I couldn't tell anybody can. He is the person worth receiving serious respect.
He's pretty cool. Really helpful.

Buster has a great teaching style, however if you come into his class with little experience you will get lost in lectures pretty easily unless you put in extra work. This class is tough, but its definitely doable!

This class is insane. I had no experience prior to this class, which shouldn't be an issue considering that it is a beginners course, however it was extremely difficult. It was probably the teaching. I understood the concepts, but I wasn't able to put it all together, and I think the prof expected us to just know how to. Worst class I've ever taken
Dr. Dunsmore said when no one was willing to teach CS 18000 which is a hard course for beginners, he volunteered to teach this class. He is definitely a good professor. He is always nice to students.
Dr. Dunsmore is absolutely an excellent professor.

Great lecturer, great at explaining concepts. The course itself is hard - long projects with nitpicky grading, unhelpful TAs, and hard exams (you have to code solutions to 4 (deliberately obtuse) problems in 90 minutes)

Overall not too difficult of a class if you pay attention, but the homework and projects are horribly graded. If you don't follow the instructions exactly (eg. if you find a different or even more efficient solution) you'll get points off, and often receive 0 credit - as has happened to me several times.
I came in with no prior experience in programming. He is an amazing professor and explains with really great examples. Don't miss his classes if you're new to OOP.... but beware of the long projects.
Pay attention to class if you're new to programming/Object-oriented programming.

Dunsmore is absolutely a great professor and makes showing up to lecture totally worth it. He's very good at breaking down and explaining concepts and the flow of programs. Just make sure to have your phone silenced, or you WILL be good-naturedly called out.

Professor Dunsmore is a great professor. Very respected. His lectures are interesting and always well put together. He really cares about his students: all you have to do is shoot him an email and he'll even have lunch with you at a dining court.
Always enjoy sitting in the first row.

Professor Dunsmore is fantastic! Lecture slides are accurate and learning objectives are clear from the start. Dunsmore injects humor into lectures, making them more interesting. Students highly respect him and are not afraid to ask him questions.
Lectures are great and very helpful, but getting office hours is like pulling teeth.
he is definitely the most brilliant and kind professor in Purdue

Prof Dunsmore is passionate about what he teaches and it shows in lecture. His slides have good examples and explanations and you can always approach him after class to ask questions. CS 180 is not a easy course just like any other CS course at Purdue. However if you work hard and keep up, then you can get a A or B in this class.

Very helpful. To do well in the class you just need to go to class and bring your textbook to labs. He is easy to understand and really wants you to learn. He tries his best to make the material interesting to everyone and cracks a few jokes here and there. Overall, he's a great professor.
This guy doesn't have a clue.

Great Professor. Makes a tough subject interesting. His projects aren't easy, but that's at the fault of the TA's, not directly him. But his class is a very good experience. I smile whenever I see him. I wish I could have him for a couple more semesters instead of those boring profs with heavy polish accents...
Very nice professor. Wants people to learn. Teaches in a fun way.

He is a Great Professor!! He is trying to keep every students' attentiont by using interesting sentences and funny examples!! Also, he can explain a abstract concept by using daily life example , which make the problem more clear and easiler to understand. Totally, a great Teacher.
Great professor, explains things to someone who doesn't know much about the subject. Hard subject but it would be your fault if you didn't do well.
Good man!
Great Professor, knows what he's talking about.

Lecture is mildly entertaining, but the info and speculation on notes is great. Class is difficult and so are projects, unfortunatly Dusmore doesn't write the tests, some retarded person does and they are 'coding races' I got 100 on nearly every project (a rare feat) but the tests required much coding practice before this freshmen class.

An overall good guy. Puts all of his notes online, which comes real handy for people with laptops. Tries his best to keep everyone awake (which is actually a good thing!). Though learning about code at 8:30AM isn't exactly thrilling, it wasn't bad with Dunsmore.
Dunsmore is an awesome prof.
The Greatest who ever lived

Dunsmore's awesome.  That sums it up quite well.  The class starts out slow but soon picks up lots of speed, so if you have no prior programming experience (like me) don't be surprised when you get left behind, choking in the dust.

He's the most organized professor I've ever had and all his notes used in class are online.  He's not afraid to slam a table on the ground to wake you up and the class was admittedly easy, but any class with him will put in a good position to learn.  I T.A. for his class.  A great man.
Buster rocks.  Seriously.  He does a great job with his class, the best you could ask for.
Great prof, hope you all have the opportunity to take his class.
Clear, good notes, fair and for the CS department, quite easy.  However, required attendance in a 7:30am class did not sit well with me

Funny guy..keeps you interested.  Class is difficult if you are new to CS.  Class moves at a very fast pace and can be difficult to keep up with.  I may not get a good grade but I am learning quite a bit.
Totally awesome.  Best teacher thus far.  Very knowledgable.
Maybe it's because I had class at 7:30 AM, but he put me to sleep.
This guy should run a teaching clinic for the majority of professor in the CS department who are "required" to teach.
Incredible professor!
Pretty good
Eh
A bit egotistical
No Comments
Best Professor in the Computer Science Department!
A great teacher
Sometimes too banal.  If you can't pass CS180 with him, try another major.
Great Teacher. One of the best in CS.
Great prof.  Couldn't be better.

He tries to be somewhat entertaining, but it doesn't work.  His classes are ususally poorly structured, not in lecture, but in conjunction with labs and exams.  He is far to busy to teach a large class. He is nice.
The best instructor!
Without a tutor, you don't have a chance.  His class is impossible
He teaches to a large class, so it is hard to ask questions sometimes.
No Comments
Buster is a good prof
Good lectures.You need a tutor to pass (blame the course administrator)
Good teacher, but you cannot pass
Very hard class with hard professor to deal with.

Ronda simply does not know how to engage or instruct a class. She uses slides and information that alone would not prepare a student for their commercial written or practical. I have never had such a sad experience in a class as I have had with Ronda.
She does not teach what needs to be known. She didn't prepare me well for my exam at all. I had to use other sources to prepare. Attendance is mandatory by law.
Her lectures are the most boring thing ever. Makes jokes that don't make sense. Adds comments that don't need said.
Ronda is a fantastic person and a good instructor, but the course outline doesn't exactly prepare the students very well for the written let alone a checkride
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ronda is a great person but when it comes down to it she simply cannot teach. We spent about 3 classes learning how to draw holds and hold entries and on the third day after her not teaching us properly for the last 2 classes, she shows us a 7 minute video which explained it perfectly.

Absolutely terrible professor. Ronda no idea how to teach. If you get her for a professor you should seriously consider finding tutoring or online help as she can't explain anything. Worst experience I've had at Purdue so far.
Ronda is great as a person, but teaching is a little more difficult for her. Incredible human being but simply doesn't know how to effectively teach.

she is such a sweetheart and loves what she does but she gives so much work for 255. the quizzes are so odd its like a specific sentence from a specific part of the textbook and the entire quiz is on that, super unfair grading.

She is such an amazing professor. She grades very fairly and makes sure that any questions you have get answered. She genuinely cares and wants to see people succeed. Talking to her is extremely easy and as long as you put in the effort and do the work she will make sure that you get a decent grade. Read the textbook and take notes!
sorry i love you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She gave good lectures. She was engaging and connected stories to concepts, which helped deepen understanding. However, her grading practices were unfair, as she often strayed from the rubric, grading based on her subjective assessment rather than what students were doing, and she is difficult to talk to, as she tends to shut individuals down.

Professor Putman ALWAYS brings the energy to class and it makes it a lot of fun even during a 7:30am. She does a great job incorporating stories into her classroom which helps the lecture material soar in engagement and help legal concepts stick.

Cara is, in many ways, an awesome person and professor; she cares for students and does not make you feel left out. She is always willing to meet with students to help them prepare for the weekly quizzes this course requires, but make sure you know your stuff, especially by reading the textbook.
