reviews.comment: Dr. Chapple is an amazing professor who is truly dedicated to helping his students become interested in biochemistry. He teaches BCHM100 through a series of case studies which makes the concepts easy to understand. The homework is hard, but manageable. Exams are very concept and application based.

I had Dr.Chapple for his last time teaching BCHM100. He is a nice professor but overall it seemed like he was lazy in helping students. The course material was hard to understand and the homework grading is brutal unless you go to see a TA for 'help'. Basically he just wants you to know what a protein looks like and if you can draw it.
a very fair grader and doesn't make the class difficult to excel in. Tries to make biochemistry fun to learn through case studies and really cares about his students.

He is very passionate in teaching the subject of biochemistry. There isnt a lot of homework assigned, and a few quizzes. That being said, there isnt a lot of chances in raising a grade because of it. I believe he grades fairly. Quizzes are a little tuff at times.

Great professor and he loves to teach. Im a biochem major so Im probably biased, but I LOVED this class. So interesting and dr Chapple is great. Not a ton of points so you have to be careful on each homework and quiz. Not a ton of effort put into this class except studying for exams, theyre all free response so you have to know your stuff

Dr. Chapple knows his material and does not try to trip you up, what is on the slides is on the exam, but make sure you are very familiar with the slides. Some of the questions on the exams are non traditional but not necessarily more difficult. He enjoys lecturing and does not want to overwhelm students. The TA grades pretty hard.

This class is very oriented for more biochemistry and other related majors. As a person who is not in to or good at biochemistry, this class was horrible. Doctor Chapple only teaches to people who already have a lot of background in this subject and it sucks for everyone else. I would definitely say this is not a 100 level class. It sucked.

Grade: -Easy 5 Quizzes -Easy 5 HWs -Kinda tough 2 exams Pros: -Very very smart -Can ask questions -Organized Cons: -A bit slow sometimes -Some things are only said once and expected for you to remember -easy class but tough for a 100 level class

reviews.comment: Dr. Chapple is an amazing professor and knows how to lecture. The material in this class was difficult and it was very heavy but he made hard concepts understandable and almost enjoyable. However this class is hard and I would not recommend it if you are not very interested in science, not a class I would recommend for someone just exploring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Coming into this class, I was extremely intimidated since I had never taken biochem before. Although it took a lot of work, Dr. Chapple explained the material so well and reiterated all the material you need to know for exams in lectures. He is extremely knowledgeable and to do well, paying attention is important

reviews.comment: So enthusiastic about teaching and his job!! Professors like him are what makes students want to keep their major :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: During his lectures he seemed very knowledgable. Biochemistry didn't really click with me so most things he spoke about went over my head. However, he was very nice. But he mostly made jokes toward one person in class. But anyway, there was little homework and few quizzes. I didn't really know what to study except for what was on the lecture slides
Pretty tough with homework.

Dr. Chapple is great! He is very knowledgeable and doesn't over complicate things; however, he will not spoon feed you. You really need to put effort into learning the material and if you do, a good grade is definitely possible. The homework assignments are valuable but are graded pretty hard by the TA. Study for the quizzes!

Dr. Chapple is an incredible professor.  I thought the course was very doable.  It does require studying.  There were only 4 or 5 quizzes and they were not bad at all.  Homework is graded harshly, but that just depends on the TA.  I really enjoyed this class, but I am a biochemistry major, so I could see how others would think it was challenging.

This is definitely not a 100 level class. Prof is great & you learn a lot of useful stuff but extremely difficult. I've been getting A+ on all of the assignments, and pretty sure I was one of the top students in class but did bad on just one final and I got a C. quizzes&hw easy, exams are ridiculously hard. its ridiculous. def not 100 level

Very hard for me.  I came in with no introduction to the material covered so I had to study a lot.  However, he is a great professor and is very helpful.  He loves to answer questions in class when you don't understand something.  The material covered was used in many subsequent courses that I have taken.
Excellent teacher.

Professor Clawson not only gave out an amazing online class, but she was kind and accessible by email at all times. I really enjoyed the content - especially the discussion of feminism and how it has advanced over time. Overall, a great online class if you need a civics requirement/POL credit!

The online class is one of the easiest things I have ever done. It is 1 discussion board post with 1 response per week. The reading (although mandatory) does not really matter unless you are taking a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was interesting and super easy. Only assignment each week is a discussion board and a peer response. There are quite a few of supplemental readings that need to be done each week as you are tested on them, but quizzes and exams are pretty easy otherwise. Great class to take for civics literacy or other requirements.

Prof Clawson wasn't exceptional, but not terrible either. The exams are closed book, while quizzes are open book. There are multiple articles, papers, videos, etc. that need to be read/watched weekly. That part of it was annoying, and I felt most weren't even helpful. There are no extra assignments, so you're just graded on tests/discussions.
Prof. Clawson is an amazing professor; she really cares about students and their success. As long as you participate and make an effort, you should do well.

For a 500 level class, this class was very manageable in terms of workload. Professor Clawson was very easy to work with and was super understanding and supportive. She is one of the best professors I've ever had, who is constantly kind and willing to help you learn and succeed. The class is graded by few things, so participate and read!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For an online class, it's a bit difficult to get a full picture of a professor, but Clawson does well at making herself available, while simultaneously maintaining a level of professionalism and care for her study and students, especially during COVID. The subject matter is interesting, and you will read some of her own publications in the course.

I really enjoyed my time in Cliff's MGMT 254 class. I would definitely recommend taking MGMT 254 with Cliff, as you learn so much in a fun way. Tests are 80% of your grade, and they are online, and 20% is participation, which is just going to class and doing the "project" in the first 5 minutes of class.

Genuinely cares for the learning of students with a mix of good humor and clear communication. You read textbook / watch lecture videos before class then discuss the material in class. There are short quizzes at the start of class to check if you read/watched the material. Would 100% recommended taking with Fisher.
Great classes and very interesting/interactive and useful. This guys the goat
Lectures are both entertaining and insightful. The content you learn from this class is both applicable to your future job and personal life.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cliff was probably my favorite professor at Purdue. Really helpful in and out of class. Definitely take 529 if you are planning to go to law school because I learned so much about law school and the legal profession that I would not have known
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cliff is a great professor and is very generous with the curves for each exam. Attend (almost) all classes because he gives 2 questions in the beginning of class for attendance (but all graded if you at least did it, not necessarily the right answer). For his exams, mainly watch his lecture videos and take notes, and read the book.

Great guy. 80% of MGMT254 was exams and the other 20% was attendance. He will pick on you in class if you don't have your name tag up. If you're on his good side, he leaves you alone and enjoys asking you for help when doing class assignments. I got an average of 67% on all exams but the curves are GIANT because many people fail. Great guy overall.

Prof. Fisher was great. Loved coming to his class. He curves his exams a lot because they are so difficult and because of that I expected a higher grade but until the final grades came out I didnt understand how heavily he enforces the participation grade so make sure you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cliff is a crazy & passionate. To me, I think he's intimidating b/c he cold calls & if you aren't on his good side, he'll lowkey pick on you the whole semester--so be on his good side. Show up to class b/c lectures are heavy in material and the stuff he talks abt will be on the exams. Exams are difficult but there aren't any assignments, so do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cliff was great! Highly recommend taking a class taught by him, he's an extremely great lecturer and definitely makes coming to a 7:30am class worth it.
by far my favorite professor that i have had. great lecturer, hilarious, smart, and engaging.  absolutely loved this class.

Cliff has a great instructor and teacher! He teaches in a very unique way that does not include PowerPoints or lectures. The class consists of 3 exams and a research paper that is 25% each. The class requires a lot of reading, but it is a class you should take if you plan to attend law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this man, he is so nice and clearly loves his area of work. Lectures are nice, go to them, class is an easy a if you pay attention and take notes.

Fisher is an amazing teacher! Your grade is mostly tests, with quizzes, and 1-2 assignments. Everything is open note so take good notes on lecture videos and during class. Go to class- things discussed in class will be on the exam and the quizzes will take place here. The class is very interactive so come prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TAKE HIS CLASS. Class is pure discussion but its never boring. If you do the reading, watch the lectures, and actually try (emphasis on actually), you will have so much fun with this course.

Professor Fisher not only as a professor but as a person values the idea of wisdom very highly, which he states as "taking knowledge and turning it into something useful." He highly encourages involved students to take their learning seriously and his tests greatly follow this idea. This class is not an easy A, you will have to actually learn here.
Amazing lectures, clear grading criteria, gives good feedback.

Cliff is an experienced and fun lecturer, I learned a lot from his class. Encouraged to watch lecture videos before coming to class as there might be pop quizzes. Exams are tricky but you can prepare better by reading and researching the articles he gave, and asking him questions about the article before exam.

Fisher is a very interactive professor and this is not a traditional course. Be prepared to participate in class almost every session. There are four exams, and in-class quizzes throughout the semester that are worth 20% (Other exams are worth 20% each). Take good notes on the lecture videos as this is a "flipped" course, and videos are first.

Great lecturer, must pay attention in class to really understand everything. He tries to make law into a more udnerstanding topic. Everyone in my section just loved him. he will answer any question you have after class, and emails back.

Cliff is a really great professor. He made a sometimes confusing subject very interesting and more understandable with his use of everyday life examples. This class was easily my favorite class I have taken so far!
Read the articles and youll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVED Prof. Fisher's lectures. They were always entertaining and I looked forward to listening to them. I took the 4 week asynchronous summer class, and we were grade consisted of 4 exams. The exams tended to be tough, but I found that reading the chapters and listening to the lectures helped. Overall, I really enjoy this class and Prof. Fisher!

He is such a loving professor. He only takes 4 exams 25% each. No homework, papers, or projects. He also curves. A textbook is required but honestly just watching the lectures is enough. He explains complex law concepts with great (and funny) examples which makes his lectures easy to follow.
Do NOT take this class!!!
I took the business law class last semester and loved Dr. Fisher. I would highly recommend his class.

I personally found Dr. Fisher's class to be enjoyable. He is a very entertaining lecturer, and does a good job of keeping the class engaged with the material. I recommend going to class and doing the readings. Exams can be somewhat challenging, however, Dr. Fisher is a fair grader and gives you many chances to show your knowledge of the material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I did not use the textbook once. Cool professor, but lectures can be boring.

Dr. Fisher has made Business Law, a class that is typically very boring and difficult, into a very fun and exciting class. He always engages with everyone and loves to make jokes to keep you engaged. The COVID class has your grade be 100% exams, but he helps A LOT if you show up to class. He practically gives you the answers if you show up.
He is one of the best professors I've met in my undergraduate. Thinking about taking his course again. I can really learn things although his courses are kind of hard for me.

Really enjoy his online course. Ive heard people complain about the test is difficult, honestly? 90% of his exam questions come directly from his lecture. He like to use the examples he talked about in exam, so as long as you pay attention to lecture videos exams shouldn't be a problem. Make appointment with him to go through materials.

Don't ever take this class... Three multiple choice exams. Don't take it in summer or spring. Just don't take it. There is curve but it is fixed curve so it does not depend on the average to the class.

reviews.comment: Great Professor, makes legal text more bearable. very funny guy, gives good examples.
He is very careless about those students who struggle in his class. He does not provide any study material for the exams!!! He is a good person but not as a professor!
I do not recommend him. He is tough and he thinks his exams are fair. In fact, his exams are ridiculous. Do not take his class!!

By far my favorite professor to have at Purdue. He makes learning about something that i would usually find boring so exciting. He's funny and so intelligent. Was very helpful and always re-explained things if you got confused.
Such a nice professor!!!!! Really helpful!!!!!

reviews.comment: Online course, not given adequate time to fill out exam answers and work

Great guy. Took his MGMT 44428 at Purdue during the Spring 2016 semester. 4 exams. All pretty easy to prepare for. Multiple in-class projects with group. Multiple guess speakers. Good content. Definitely the funniest teacher I've ever had at Purdue.

Cliff is the most entertaining professor I have ever had. The lectures had me anywhere between looking on in awe at his knowledge of the topic and intelligence, and holding my sides together from laughing too hard. He is ridiculously smart, humble, helpful, and overall and amazing teacher. Don't be fooled though, this class is not an easy A.

I absolutely loved Cliff. I had him at 730 and he was always able to keep me awake and interested. He really understands the material and is always willing to explain more in depth. He randomly calls on you throughout the class so you have to pay attention. VERY little homework and grade is based on 5 exams. The 5th exam being an optional final.

Great Teacher who really relates to the students and is easy to contact. Grade is basically based off of 5 tests and they can be quite difficult if you don't completely understand the material. Other than that no complaints.

Cliff is one of the best professors at Purdue. He is a very enthusiastic and energetic professor for business law. He shares news articles that help you understand the class concepts and he is really easy to talk to. He's very friendly and works to ensure that students do well. If you're taking business law, definitely take his class. Very useful.
Cliff is the best teacher I had at Purdue.   Goes above and beyond to help students.  If you're interested in law, he's the guy you want to talk to!

Cliff is absolutely amazing! I still have about 3 semesters to go, but this has been by far the best class I've taken at Purdue. It is so useful and relevant. He'll meet with you outside of class hours if you need extra help or if you are considering going to Law School. Effort mainly consists of paying attention in class. I ended up getting an A+!

He is super awesome. You can learn a LOT from his lecture, and it will be useful for life. He is a closer friend and also a great lecturer, you have to take his class if you are a krannert student. Law is boring and this class is not easy (cuz it's law ..), but I enjoyed his class for the whole semester.
Cliff is the man! His contract law class got me to go to law school. Hell of a guy!

YOU. MUST. HAVE. THIS. PROFESSOR. Best professor I have ever had at Purdue. He is wonderful, his lectures are enjoyable. He does random attendance, but you will WANT to be there anyway. Very entertaining, in your face! Leave your phone at packed up, you won't need it in this class.
Great guy! I love his law class!

Awesome professor - his classes are so interesting, I never space out like other classes. He makes law fun, and I never thought that was possible. Also, his notes are incredible so do NOT buy the book!
Amazing professor. If you're thinking about law school his independent study is perfect preparation.
Great Professor, entertaining, useful, explains concepts well using examples
Great guy, great profressor. I still say hi to him on campus and he still remembers my name after 2 years and no doubt hundreds of other students.

Tracy Clark, while well-intentioned, is a subpar professor whose course and material did not teach me about--nor reflect principles of--technical writing. Her Brightspace is bloated, with redundant class assignments taking longer to explain than complete. You can do well, but sitting through her mandatory lectures is tiring. Go online if you can.

Tracy's Brightspace setup is confusing; assignments are giant text blocks that require multiple tabs to decode. Lectures are long with little substance—she once spent 5+ mins explaining how to click a button. Attendance is strict; missing over three classes drops your grade by multiple letter grades even with perfect HW grades. Avoid this class.
TOO HARD. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: like everyone else said, she talks *so much* without conveying much of substance. she attempts to make her BrightSpace navigable and fails since her attempts at clarity result in an overwhelming amount of information. the course is easy, the grading's light, the late "policy" is laughable, and she makes you do things in class that never get graded.

Tracy is like a disorganized teenager. She is exceedingly passive aggressive, talks excessively without saying anything of substance, and bends her own rules when its to her own convenience. 

Given her role as an English teacher, I am surprised by her lack of proficiency in the writing. Purdue should discontinue her employment. Advice? Avoid her.

The worst teacher you can ever have. I have had middle school teachers who could teach better than her. Her lectures are all over the place and she is never on point. It just feels like she has no teaching plan for her lectures. Its impossible to understand the assignments and what she is looking for due to her explanation being all over the place.

She likes to talk and talk and talk. Make sure you don't have a class right after this class you will be late every single day. Although she talks and talks all the students still have no clue on what to do. She takes extra time to explain something useless and takes no time to explain the work we need to do.

This professor wrote 10 pages when 1 page could do the job. I was often lost on the course page trying to find instructions for assignments. Despite being longwinded, instructions were also general/nondescript. Feedback is similar. Not insightful and overwhelming amounts of text. Expect to be torn apart over details you never expected to matter.

She is very wordy with everything she posts. To the point where you aren't clear of what to do because she says so much. Is very critical of assignments even if you have all the required information. Overall, a terrible professor.

Really terrible learning experience, course materials are confusing and rambling. Feedback/grading is impossible to predict (you'd lose points for using the word "Note" instead of "Hint") and critical in weird ways ("Purdue already decided to do blah blah 3 years ago, so your report isn't useful to Purdue"). She's unexpectedly passive aggressive.

Ironically, she's terrible at writing, which mattered significantly when all of her communications were through Brightspace posts during an asynchronous summer class. Describes otherwise simple assignments in absurdly long, rambling, and confusing essays. For example, her syllabus is over 5000 words, and you are quizzed on it. Pointless, dumb work.

One of the worst professors I have taken at Purdue. Took the summer portion of ENGL 421 and did not receive 75% of my grades until the grade deadline set by Purdue. The irony of it being a technical writing class is that she is a terribly incoherent writer. The entire course revolves around Brightspace and her Brightspace is terribly laid out.

Worst class I have ever taken. The class content was focused entirely around Brightspace and how great it is. I then found out she was one of teachers who got us using Brightspace. Weekly busywork assignments dedicated to using Brightspace and helping students and professors like Brightspace. A completely useless class. The class is organized poor

T/R Power Hour. Talked the entire time, yet still managed to not provide very few examples for how to complete projects and even fewer grading criteria or instructions for them. Discussion board participation counted for a laughably high portion of the grade. Very difficult to take the course seriously because of how painfully frustrating it was.

Too verbose in her teaching. Does not have clear and concise expectations. Passive aggressive in her feedback, almost to the point of insulting and disparaging. 0/10 for this class. Can not stress how much I do not recommend this class with Professor Clark.

reviews.comment: Avoid her is the only advice.
