reviews.comment: Marta was my favorite professor this semester! She really cares about her students and teaches the material pretty well. The class itself is not too difficult as long as you try.
She is amazing help during office hours but there are also TA hours that are both very beneficial
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: She lectures very fast and most of it is pointless, only go for the hot seat attendance points. Very homework heavy (busywork) and labs are mandatory. Some homework is challenging so make friends in your lab class. TA's are very helpful in lab. Overall not a bad class to learn excel/access in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was a Teaching Assistant under Marta. Easily one of my favourite professors to work with. She is excellent in communicating to students and TAs, and was very understanding if a mistake was made (within reason). To students taking CS235/110, do not be afraid asking Marta or the teaching assistants questions. Class is easy if effort is being put in.

The class is incredibly easy, but the lectures are so pointless. The only reason I show up to the lectures is because she does hotseat that are worth points. In lecture she teaches us about things that we previously learned in the last lab so it makes the lectures so incredibly boring. Show up to class and lab and you'll be fine in the class.

CS 110 is an easy class, especially if you have the least bit of prior experience with MS Office. Crowe wants to help her students succeed and is accessible for any questions. The lab manual is absolutely worthless unless you want extra help. Exams are easy if you do the homework and practice exams. Homework often feels like busywork.

Crowe is a really good professor and is willing to help and accommodate anyone who needs it. However, I do feel that the mandatory lectures were pointless because all of the exam and lab questions came directly from the online homework. There is lots of homework and it's time consuming because I took this as a hybrid. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Mrs. Crowe is a great instructor and is always willing to help a student with any problem that she or he has.  I love this class and the way she handles the lectures because she really understands the material and what is happening in the course. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you have to take CS159, take it with Crum. He is the best for this because of his experience, and he goes very slowly over all the content. The class is not an easy A. So make sure to pay attention and talk to Crum about your problems. Crum is very understanding, and his lectures are great. There is no point in complaining about course material.

I would highly recommend taking Professor Crum for CS 159 as his lectures are very well organized and he explains the content clearly. He cares about his students and makes it easy to meet outside of class. He also writes the tests so what he teaches is most likely on the exam.

The course syllabus and exam content is tough on students. But it is not due to Professor. Crum makes it easy to understand. Even if someone takes a different professor, the finals are going to be the same. There is no point bring frustrated towards Crum when he tries his best.

He is very approachable and understanding, and explains concepts at a pace that makes the material easy to follow. His teaching style helps make the content more manageable if you stay engaged in class. He is also willing to provide help outside of scheduled office hours. I would recommend taking this course with Crum.
Make sure you MEMORIZE ALL THE COURSE STANDARDS.

Horrible teacher. Exams had me on all fours especially with the MCQ as there was always the option for “none of the above”. Lectures are extremely content heavy and Crum teaches until the last second and CRAMS all the content he can. He has the lecture notes packet but never follows it so it gets confusing. Get another teacher🙏🏻🙏🏻

Iclicker is used for lecture and they have a TA seeing if your in assigned lecture seat so you cant cheat the iclicker and is really annoying if you have to get up if u have the 8:30 lecture time. All sections do this. Lecture is pointless, labs and homework are easy but most of ur grade is exams.

Entire class is designed to trick you and waste your time but getting a good grade is very easy. It may be more difficult if you don't have prior coding experience since the lectures are terribly boring, and he explains coding in a confusing way.

Obviously, the exams were awful and designed to trick students. Make sure to take some practice tests so you are prepared for that and pay close attention the the wording of questions. Prof Crum seemed like a nice guy and was a good lecturer. The labs can be awful if you get a bad group. You need the course notebook but not the textbook.

Easily the worst class I have ever taken. Lectures never touched on the difficulty of material on the labs and HW's Exams are ridiculously hard. Assignments are graded very strictly with so many point lost for the smallest mistakes. Class is literally designed to discourage people from asking for help. Very hard to do well without prior experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CS159 is not a well organized course. It's supposed to be entry level programming but beginner progammers will stuggle a little in the class. Crum knows his material very well and does a fine job teaching it. Exams are very difficult (use BoilerExams to study) and lab quizzes are impossible if you have lab before your second lecture.

Homework and labs aren't that bad, just start early. Lectures are nothing crazy but Crum explains stuff well and as long as you go and pay attention, you'll get most of the info. Exams have you read over code and find the output as well as answer logic questions which sometimes try and trick you which is slightly annoying. Use BoilerExams as well.
As a professor, he is good, does a good job explaining things and answering questions. As the course coordinator, he's nothing short of awful.

Honestly I learned more from the labs than the lectures, but lectures were free points so I went. Crum is a fine lecturer, and answers questions pretty well, although anytime other than lecture you'll probably have to ask a TA.

Crum teaches CS 159 well, even for those new to programming. The course itself has some tedious HWs and confusingly worded lab quiz questions, but Prof. Crum's lectures cover the content well and he is open to answering students' questions after lecture. He shows many example questions in lecture which is very helpful for HWs/labs.

I think Crum gets a bad rap on here. I think he is really personable and eager to help, and I liked his class. One tip for the course is to make sure you start the homework early and don't wait for the weekend before it's due to start. Also, use boiler exams to study, and make sure you watch the videos.
Crum is a decent professor. His lectures are very boring, but he explains everything clearly. The course itself sucks, and he designed it but if you look at his actual teaching he is pretty good.

CS 159 exams do not test your ability to program in C, they test your ability to interpret intentionally convoluted logic. Crum does little to guide students toward success, but enough practice on boilerexams can make up for testing struggles. His lectures aren't particularly engaging or insightful, but I'd recommend attending for the bonus points.

CS159 aside, Crum is a very good professor. The course itself is pretty meh but there are a lot worse structured classes you could encounter (like chm 116) so its relatively bearable. Crum himself is a good lecturer however, and likely the best you'll get for this class. He knows what he is teaching and aside from not being super engaging he's good

The whole CS 159 course kind of sucks, but Crum is probably your best bet. Lab quizzes are impossible, but failing them isn't too consequential on the final grade. Exams are designed to trick you and have intentionally misleading questions about niche topics that don't actually matter when programming. Still a better class to take than Bio or Chem.

Crum will be the first professor to ever give me a C. He is a great lecturer, which makes him an incredibly boring teacher. The tests intentionally trick you, showing that he does not care about your learning whatsoever. No matter the time I put into learning the code, I am constantly struggling. The class is more about course standards than code.

Crum as a lecturer is relatively to others good, but I would recommend taking a pillow to the class as even the most attentive students tend to dose off, however, attention in this class is very important. The reason why everyone hates  Crum is that his exams are very hard with just little time for completion. Lots of memorization for theory needed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is a weed-out class that is a lot harder than it needs to be, with professor Crum just sprinkling in his excessive course standards with a little bit of knowledge about C. His exams are heavily based upon course standards, so if you don't know the course standards, you won't do well in the class even if you know C.
A weed out class.
Isn't a good lecturer.

I think Crum gets a lot of hate for how his exams are structured, but he is really not a bad professor. His lectures are very helpful and although attendance isn't mandatory, you get points for going. I was doing terrible at the beginning of this course and was able to get an A on the first exam. Go to lecture, STUDY, do Boilerexams practice tests.

Prof. Crum is not a bad professor, but the class itself is super tedious. He wrote his own workbook and you must attend lectures to pass the class. It is imperative that you work well with your lab group partners. Also, do not procrastinate on the HW bc it is assigned a week in advance for a reason. Crum is hard to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although the class isn't great, Crum does a good job during lectures by going through specific examples. He also does a good job answering questions, and I overall enjoyed his class.

Definition of average. He gives great good lectures and does a good job going through examples of code. But the homework was really annoying to do because the most efficient way to code the solution was never allowed. The whole class is graded on course standards, and the midterms are difficult. Do not wait till the last minute to start hw. Don't!!

I never actually interacted with professor Crum. As a fully-online student, I literally never had a two-way conversation with any of the instructional team. Any problems I had, I had to solve myself. The grading criteria was really unclear. We had points deducted for "programming standards", but were never really explained what the standards were.
The tests and quizzes do not really test your knowledge of the code, they test your test-taking abilities. But, the lectures are clear and if you watch them all you will do well in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He sets up his class in a way to try and trick you at every corner. The exams are really hard and worth a lot of your grade. Make sure you start studying for the exams a week out. It's unlike any other exam you have taken be prepared. The coding assignments are also annoying but doable even if your group does nothing. This is where grit is needed.

Exams are the worst as they expect you to be a compiler while doing them. I think prof does a great job in explaining but the course itself is not easy and requires basic programming knowledge previously. HWs were difficult but SI and office hrs helped A LOT. Lecture quizzes r annoying. Don't expect any curve/ECs and try to always be on top of lecs

I took the class fully offline. The attendance was done in the first 5 minutes of a 8:30 am class, so I missed nearly half of them. There were quizzes during lectures and labs. The homework and labs were big and difficult for inexperienced students. The exams were awful. There were theoretical questions, code reading, and calculations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: We've had online class all sem, and it has been nowhere near easy. You would think Crum understands this, but he does not care about his students at all. Assignments in this class are tedious. If I could give any piece of advice, REMEMBER: THIS CLASS IS NOT A PROGRAMMING CLASS! IT IS A PROGRAMMING STANDARDS CLASS. You will learn nothing about code.

Crum is not a good prof. Prepare to lean on outside sources for learning the material. This would be a better class if at the very least, the profs and teaching team were empathetic of students, but even the bare minimum of basic human respect is oftentimes unachieved. The teaching team shooes away students, and is overall unhelpful. Bad professor.
Litteraly the Worst Class ever. the teacher and TA's have no respect for otehr humans. almost like you mean nothing other than that you fail the class. DONT TAKE THE CLASS. hours spent for nothing

Grading is extremely inconsistent across lab groups. My friends lab group was permitted to use loops on an assignment that forbid them. The exams are the worst part of this class as they expect the students to compile complex looping code in their heads in under three minutes. Exams Should definitely be weighted much less than they are currently.

Crum is THE BEST prof Ive ever seen:he honed ur will by making intro level course tediouslx;he made u understand theres no end to learn by making the tests asHARDas he can;he cultivates ur circumspection&confidence by making u calc a large iteration BY URSELF(YES U R COMPUTER)in 3mins Qs CANTbe revisited&code Qs alwys goes before def Qs

Grading is extremely inconsistent. Some TAs expect one function for every line of output, some don't care about functional programming at all. I'll echo what everyone else says about exams that don't really evaluate programming skill, extremely punishing grading for the most minute mistakes, multiple mistakes on exams, unclear expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think by biggest problem would be the design of the class itself especially with the questions that appear on the exams. It makes it appear the the teacher are out to punish students for forgetting even the most miniscule of things. This does not make it hard though since you can do well on hw and labs if you put in the effort and time.

This course is not designed to be an introductory course as it supposed to be. TOUGH graders. They literally cut off points because the letter in the output is supposed to be capital not small. There is no such a thing called human error for them. Midterms are insane, they give you a long code and expect you to find the output in three minutes.

Crum is not a good prof. His teaching team is not good either. The teaching team is not held accountable for issues in grading/proctoring, issues that were caused by the teaching team hurt the students' grade and they are unwilling to change anything because of that.
Crum is a bad professor. He really doesn't care about students during online teaching, and this course has gone to sour because the teaching team is incompetent.

The class is very reliant on knowing advanced geometry always focusing more on geometry than actual coding. There are "course standards" that make everyone follow the same absurdly exact formatting. Miss a comment on one variable? Didn't like the name of a variable? Points off. Very very harsh graders (the TA's). DEFINITELY NOT an intro course.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!!

Stringent grading and mandatory course attendance when COVID-19 isn't in session. Not to mention that they give redundant topics to learn that you will never encounter in programming again to get students to "think outside the box."

Crum is a great lecturer and explains the material well, but the tests are weighted a lot and very different from other material. People got 100s on hw+labs then Cs or worse on tests. Doable but you will be combing through the textbook/vids for small, non code related facts or doing repetitive calculations by hand. Go to SI sessions for a leg up

Crum does a nice job in lecture with explaining things, and he is helpful if you ask questions. The assignments are straightforward and are not horribly difficult. In the times of COVID, the class was not as exam heavy as normal, but the exams are difficult, and not as related to coding. It would be good to decrease the weight of the exams.

During the online lesson this semester, the professor rarely respond my emails about technical issues. And the professor gives unfair rating. I only have 2 people in my group in comparison to four people as a normal group. The professor still rated me as fail. The course is difficult and the professor is harsh on rating. Don't take his course.

I have never felt so defeated by a class before. I did not have much previous experience with coding and this is supposed to be an intro class. The labs and homework are difficult but they are worth basically nothing. The exams are very difficult and not like the assignments. They are also the majority of the points. Not easy to help. SI is a g.

Crum is a decent lecturer. However, his class is extremely exam heavy. Which is super disappointing since the exams have virtually nothing to do with actual coding. On the other hand the labs and hws which are actual coding count for nothing. You're better off picking a different professor who weighs everything more fairly.

I thought Crum was a pretty good lecturer, and did a good job of explaining things. Exams, on the other hand, were a poor way of testing one's proficiency in programming. Overall, not a bad class but it did have some painful parts.

Professor Crum in general is not a bad professor; he explains material well and the class is organized with access to outside resources. However, his lectures can be boring, group projects (labs) are a main focus of the course, and the grading scheme is frustrating considering very few +/- letter grades are given. Overall, an alright professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of my hardest Classes at purdue. Had to retake the class twice. He is a decent guy naturally but CS159 is a terrible class on another level. Study your notes, make sure your familiar with the labs and the Hw, do the past exams and be prepared for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Crum is neither a good nor bad professor. I believe that his lectures cover topics adequately and that he is very knowledgeable about C. Unlike other FYE courses, there are only 2 midterms, so be sure to really focus on studying for those. The final has a lot of weight as well. Finally, really pay attention to every quiz, they count a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not sure why Professor Crum receives a lot of hate. I thought, for the most part, he handled the course well. Was understandable during the lectures and provided examples in a compiler to see how code works. Lecture quizzes were easy points, homework only once every other week, labs are weekly. Overall good prof. Not great during COVID-19 though...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All lectures are mandatory via clicker quiz and seat checked. all hw and quizzes are worth 5 points each while the exams are 200 and final 150.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Currently taking this class, the professor gets a bad rep however he has changed, he does an extremely good and detailed job of explaining the concepts presented in the course and speaks clearly. Also, he will pop a joke once in a while.

Crum's full understanding of the C language is very apparent when he lectures. He explains concepts clearly and well. I loved him as a professor - I would have taken any other class that he taught. The exams and labs in this class are difficult, but Crum and the TA's are willing to help. Overall - Crum is a great guy and great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Crum is a super nice dude, think dad type. He goes pretty slow in lecture so it's not too hard to follow. Labs and homework can get hard, and they are only worth 5pts each. He's available for help, but be aware your TA grades everything and they could be either amazing at feedback and helping you or not at all.

Grade is based solely in how well you do in his compiling exams. Homework is more about commenting everything than actually coding. Going to lecture is useless as it doesn't help in getting the homework/labs done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Course programming standards are in place solely to make the work more tedious and to take away points that do not relate to your actual code whatsoever. The typical FYE class but amplified to a whole new level. Formatting is about as important as the code you turn in, which is, at least for me, about the worst thing a class can do
Good professor. Explains the materials well and is willing to work with students

He does a good job of explaining the material in class. I just paid attention in class, took down notes in the prescribed note packet (did not need the textbook even once). He's also really friendly during his office hours. He genuinely wants to help his students.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Annoying.

reviews.comment: Crum is very good at teaching programming. The course is easy if you've programmed before and a bit hard if you haven't. Your grade is almost completely based on the tests which can be a bit difficult.

reviews.comment: Crum is a very good professor. He could explain everything in a good way but his homework are pretty hard but if you want to go further to take ECE264 class, you have to be proficient with his material.
So fast lecture, and the too much big portion as exam. almost exam based
This is a good class and mandatory for many engineering majors, but Crum can be a little snooty in his teachings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I know a lot of my fellow classmates really give the class a bad rap, but I think it's just because they're finding this class to be pretty difficult. You have to go in with the right attitude and be willing to use your brain when doing the homework. He teaches you everything you need to know, you just need to figure out how to use it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Never again!
The homework and lab tasks can be hard sometimes
A lot of work, but labs and homework are extremely helpful in teaching content matter. Crum is an excellent and clear teacher.

I came into this class with zero coding experience and now I absolutely love it. Crum is a great lecturer and the homework assignments help one get a better understanding of the material, although they are very time consuming. At first the class seems impossible but if you put the time in to learn, youll do great. Oh and DO NOT CHEAT IN THIS COURSE

The class itself is very easy and straightforward. However, be ready to devote ALOT of time to homework (thankfully there is only 7 assignments!!!) if you are relatively inexperienced with coding (such as myself)!Dr. Crum is a good professor, but homework IS unnecessarily hard.
He knows his stuff well. Extremely clear.

His teaching is not related to the textbook, he pay more attention to test us, not teach us. I feel so confusing when I take this classes, I cannot totally understand his classes. However, this class is required for my future study, he is the only teacher that I can choose in Purdue. Feel sad about that

He is a good professor on teaching an entry-level C language. Passion and clarity are his advantages, if you pay attention to his lecture, it's very helpful to understand conception of C programming. Of course it is hard for computer rookie, but working hard and coming up with questions would help a lot. His OH is very worth to go very frequently.
He is the best professor I have ever had. He is very nice and helpful. Go to his office hours to solve your problems.

He is a really smart professor. His class is hard, but it is absolutely possible for most people to get an A, as well as they tried hard. The professor was really smart. He can view your program in 20 seconds, and fix it right after that. His tests are hard, and in my opinion, too much questions on basic concepts.

His class is difficult, but if you honestly try, then it is completely doable for even someone without any programming experience. He's serious, but is very clear when he speaks and keeps your attention. He's a good professor and if you try you can definitely get an A or a B.
He is really a good professor. The lecture is clear and really helpful. Not as bad as people said.

In lecture CPS pad questions seemed aimed more at tricking us than getting a sense of how well we understand the material. He seemed to take too much amu****t when only five percent of the class would get a question right, when he should have been more concerned about us.

He really is not as bad as what people say. Don't cheat, and if you do you better not make it the same code with different variable names. 2 friends got busted yesterday.  Just read the book, it is much more helpful than trying to understand lectures. He teaches well though, do the work, read before tests, you'll pass with a B or A.
if you need help, try first and then ask for it otherwise hell ignore you. but if u actually try, he'll do it for u
He's awful, boring, and very hard to follow during class. The majority of our lecture hall does the word search or crossword during class.

Bill Krum is the worst professor i have ever had.  He gives labs and homework with unreasonable deadlines and then the next homework/lab is based off the incomplete homework/lab you have from the previous week.  His teaching style is horrible, and as far as MATLAB is concerned he is entirely clueless.  I would not recommend Bill Krum as a professor

Interesting course, teaches non trivial topics very well as he puts in a lot of effort in the course. Only complaint is that feedback for homework takes a long time to get, dont expect to get feedback before the semester ends. But it's doable if you pay attention and try, just a lot of work. Recommend the course.

Content was good but course organization was very poor.

-Homework releases were routinely delayed or bugged, sometimes without notification

-Homework grading and feedback was terrible. Took about 2 months for the second homework to be graded, right before the last homework was due. No chance to make improvements because of lack of feedback.
He has all of his bad reviews removed from RateMyProf. Tells you everything you need to know

Very good course on design optimization fundamentals. I have no doubt I'll use the knowledge from this course later on. Very structured course content with clear instructions, good Piazza resonse times, and so on.

I was in industry for 7 years and this was my first class back while pursuing my masters. I was apprehensive as its been a long time since I did math. The prof gave lots of info on the background knowledge needed, and the pace of the class lended itself to getting results through hard work. Very matlab heavy and can be challenging but, Great Class!

Great class, well structured and clear lectures. Yes it is a tough class, and it requires the student to be ready to use matlab, which is a pillar of the class. I was not a matlab user at first, and was able to do well in the class with the help of the lectures, the TAs and the professor.

Dr. Crossley is an excellent professor and laid out all the course content very well. The class was interesting, and having some freedom to pick your own topic for the final project was fun and rewarding. Also, no exams was definitely a bonus for this class.

Truly one of the best professors at Purdue. His lectures are entertaining and informative. He lays out very clear examples that make the assessments and homework very doable. Would absolutely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Crossley's classes were interesting, his homework informative, and the class was not excessively difficult. I have found myself using the optimization methods on personal projects in my spare time, if that tells you anything about the course.

Took as an online student. Interesting material and fair grading. I'm not a big fan of his lecture style since it seems like so much of it is watching him fill in the notes. I'd rather have him focus more on the concepts/interesting tidbits/motivations since the math itself for MDO is pretty easy to follow on your own in general. Overall good class
Easy to understand, tries to be entertaining, fair grader and made clear the expectations.  Nice guy.  Would recommend.
Amazing teacher! He really knows his stuff and is really easy going. Makes lots of really dumb jokes but what do you expect, he is an engineer! The class was a lot of work but I learned tons!

Crossley is the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. He was my first experience with grad school courses and made it fantastic. He truly goes above and beyond to make sure students understand material; several times he would email me separately when I asked TAs for help so that he could elaborate on their explanation. He's kind and funny, too.

Overall, the professor was excellent in the lectures and put in some effort to be available outside of class. Grading was usually fair and the regrade policy was generous. Flexibility in assessment and project due dates was extremely helpful and greatly appreciated. I would definitely take another course taught by this professor.

The buildup in the class content was also particularly helpful for someone like me getting back into school and easily pick up the graduate level content and still be very challenging. Dr Crossley has definitely set the bar on how a distance learning class should be run.
Excellent caring proffessor.  Very skilled at distance learning with off-campus students.

Dr. Crossley is an EXCELLENT professor.  His lectures are interesting, and presented in a way that keeps your interest and ensures learning.   Tests are challenging, but not tricky for tricky's sake.   He is personable, approachable, and responsive.  He's also corny and self-deprecating, which most people find endearing.  Great prof!
Very energetic, young professor.  Easy for students to interact with.
easy class, hot prof!
Great prof, explained things clearly and was very fair with the homework and exams.
Excellent Professor, will recommend any of his class. Good TAs as well

A very nice and down to earth guy.  Professor Crossley will help you whenever you need and he will answer all of  your questions.  Not only is he smart, but he also loves the Simpsons.  He's definitely a good guy and I learned a lot from him.
Great prof.  I learned a lot.
No Comments
This Aeronautical & Astronautical Engineering (AAE) professor is a funny, friendly and well organized person

Dr. Crain is the best lecturer I've had at Purdue and the best teacher I've ever had! He is very caring and genuinely cares about his students learning the materials properly. He offers a ton of extra credit and grades very fair. He provides lots of feedback on his grading so it is easy to learn and improve. I wish I could have him for every class.

Dr. Crain is one of the best professors I have ever had at Purdue. He is provides great feedback on all speeches and has a genuine care for his students. He can be a tough grader at times, but gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit at the end of the semester!

Dr. Crain was wonderful. I was very nervous about taking this course, but he made it very easy and clear. He truly does care about his students doing well. He will work with you and your schedule, even asking students their availabilities before assigning presentation dates. If you're taking COM 217, please choose Dr. Crain if you can!

Dr. Crain is great! As a com major in a science presentation class, I thought that I would struggle, but it is very similar to COM 114 (I'm pretty sure they use the same textbook too).Though the textbook was necessary for the quizzes, they don't won't ruin your overall grade. I averaged 3/5 on most of them and still ended the class with an A.

Professor Crain is such a kind professor. Giving presentations can be stressful, but he does a great job at creating a classroom environment where everyone is comfortable with each other. He gives great feedback on how to improve as a writer or speaker and is an easy grader. If you hate public speaking, he's the professor for you.
Grades a bit harshly. Lectures are boring but he has good presentation skills. Attendance policy is painful. Seems to care about students.

Crain is a wonderful prof. He clearly cares for all of his students and is just a nice guy to be around. The curriculum is already planned (not by him), but he does a good job of working through it. If you have to take COM 217, take it with crain. Also very clear about what he expects from you in each presentation.

Very chill professor, COM is a pretty easy A with him. Just follow his instructions and you will do fine. Some of the assignments were a bit pointless, but they're not hard and give you free points. He also offers 30 points of extra credit. For us, the class was hybrid online and he was accommodating due to that. Overall great person and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Crain is such a nice man. I was weary about having an 8:30 3 days a week my last semester at Purdue, but this man made it so much better. He cares and really seems passionate about what he teaches. I'm not a fan of public speaking or communications classes, but he made my learning experience better.

Dr. Crain is genuinely one of the nicest people I've ever met. The man has the patience of a saint and his class is never boring. The class is set up in a very organized format and I feel like an improved public speaker and author as a result. Plus, he has a really cute dog and will share pictures if you ask.
He puts in a lot of work into preparing the lectures and you can tell he really wants his students to succeed.
The best professor! Appreciate!!

Professor Crain was a great professor. He had a clear grading rubric for every assignment, taught us everything we needed to know to get an A, and gave good feedback. Everything was clear cut in his class. His lectures aren't boring and he keeps everything upbeat. He treated everyone respectfully even if they didn't do the same. Overall great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Mumbles sometimes, sit near the front.
Consistent with surprise quizzes
Really hard midterm not a whole bunch of study material either

Crawford is a decent lecturer, though she tends to use language and terminology that surpasses what we have learned or what we should know for the exams. She has some really neat experiences in the field, and overall seems like a cool person. She does provide lots of good resources for the exam, but TAs will be your best resource when studying.

She is an ok professor, I think that I say ok because the content was pretty advanced and you have to play close attention and read the textbook to understand what is going on. She definitely knows what she is talking about, but with no prior experience in photogrammetry, it was difficult to keep up, but that might just be the course.

Lectures are tough to understand. In class quizzes at least once a week. Exam was difficult as well, 40+ MCQ's and 7 Written Questions. Labs can be long and take significant time to complete. Labs also require software that cannot be installed on personal computer, requiring you to use software in computer lab.

Random in-class quizzes at least once a week. The exam consisted of around 40 multiple choices (worth 50% of exam) and around 3-4 pages of free response questions (worth 50% of the exam). Both parts of the exam were confusing. Not hard to get at least a C since the class is pre-curved, but the course is tedious.

We are expected to do homework using a specific program that no one has used before yet we are not taught how to use the program. The lectures and textbook do not help while trying to complete homework. The entire course is a mess. Don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her pace is unbearable, she steamrolls through her lectures and its impossible to comprehend the content, let alone take notes. There's no textbook for the course so it's pretty hard to get help. The labs are alright since they differ from the lectures, as long as you get a good TA. I'd strongly recommend finding a different teacher if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: WE ARE DONE LIKE YESTERDAY'S DINNER
Amazing professor and person. He enjoys what he does and it shows!

LOVE CRAIG! He is the HK dad! He starts class off with music and dad jokes! He loves what he teaches and is good at it. He actually makes me want to go to class, and enjoy it! Craig is very caring and supportive of all of his students. He strives to have a personal relationship with everyone. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO IT!!

Professor Voll is an incredible professor. All of his students adore him and he is very personable to everyone. For example, before every class he plays music and says hello to every student who walks through the door, he usually knows them by name. He always has a smile on his face. I will be taking another class with him, he is amazing.
Professor Voll is a wonderful person.  This is my favorite class.  He gives out candy, and the class is actually entertaining.  Please take his class.
I took the 4-week summer course for COM217, and although it was condensed, the course didn't feel overwhelming. The professor gave good feedback and is not a harsh grader.
Professor takes a while to post the grades for projects. Other than that, he is a good professor and is not too strict with the grading of presentations and papers.

Cared a lot about the students and made public speaking approachable. Lectures were very fun and down-to-earth; made it worth getting up at 7:30 for them. Offered office hours on weekends before each presentation week and graded very generously for speeches. Got everyone donuts for the last class.

This man needs to retire. He is obviously knowledgeable about the subject but he is just an awful teacher. He reads off the powerpoint slides word for word in a slow, almost inaudible monotone voice so there was no point in even attending class. The powerpoints werent even good, so you often have to consult the textbook for clear answers.

Dr. Csonka is one of the worst biology professors as his teaching style is horrible as he only wrote on the chalk board with an outline given to the class. His tests are mostly application and he does class discussions that he randomly selects students to answer the questions. Students only knew 40% of their grade before it was on their transcript.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Csonka is an amazing professor. He is incredibly intelligent and cares for his students. He does have a thick accent which may be hard to hear through but it is able to be deciphered. Overall love him and would take his class again.

Dr. Csonka is simply a very bad instructor. I was disappointed to find that Biol 438 was co-taught by him and Dr. Applegate. Applegate was great, and it was a shame Csonka brought him down. Csonka doesn't really teach, he just very quietly reads off powerpoint slides. People stopped coming to his lectures because there was no point.
Amazing i loved the class and he was very helpful and nice.

He's a really nice guy, especially if you're in one of his smaller (i.e. not the core bio) classes. He was very helpful with lab experiments in the class I took with him, and even did the experiments himself in case we messed ours up so we could see how it was supposed to turn out.
Yells at people when they don't understand yet won't answer their questions
If you could understand the man's mumblings through his thick accent, you found that he was repeating things several times.  Test questions were worded weird...Friedman was much better.
Prof. Csonka was an allright professor. Made genetics a lot more enjoyable after he took over for Friedman. His homeworks were basicly word-for-word from the lectures.

You can tell Professor Csathy is passionate about physics but lacks the ability to teach affectively. Half the time hes doing a practice problem incorrectly and the other half is spent helping him figure out Webex meetings. He flies through lectures with no time for questions. Sadly, none of the PHYS 172 professors are significantly better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes just very monotone at least online but solid for the most part

Prof. Csathy's lectures can be dry to some, but he tries his best during demos and explanations. Physics is hard, but if you learn the lectures/ ppts., you'll be ok. Expect the following: 2 midterms (averages were 50% & 55%!!) and a final, weekly lab reports, weekly online homeworks, and iClicker participation. 7 - 8% curve at the end of the sem
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Csathy is a decent professor. The class was very large and I feel that he did his best to meet everyone's needs. He always made us aware of his office hours, which were very helpful. I-Clicker questions are graded and are based on the lectures. He will typically give hints to the question. He also did many demos in front of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: With Gabor, the course really wasn't to difficult, essentially his lectures are from the textbook and he uses a lot of examples from the textbook and the practice exam. His exams are straightforward and relatively easy. Put in the effort and you should be able to get a good grade no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His tests aren't bad. He's impatient and gets frustrated if you can't keep up. And he will let you know that he doesn't have time to help you anymore than he already has.
He has a thicker accent which made it hard to understand him. It personally affected my learning since the lectures didn't help me. His voice also made me tired often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Csathy is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. He just seemed like a teacher who was there for the students and actually enjoyed physics. He helped us out a lot on the Clicker questions too, especially when people didn't seem to understand what the question was asking (none of the other PHYS 172 teachers did that).

Professor Csathy is enthusiastic about what he teaches and loves to do demonstrations and show students how to do problems. He is helpful, and his accent is fun to listen to. PHYS 172 is a standard lower level 400-person class, and he makes it very bearable.

Very friendly guy who is obviously very knowledgeable on the subject. His teaching can be a little hard to follow sometimes and lectures are a bit long and boring. Fortunately though, he almost always gives you the iClicker answers and helps you work through them.

Would definitely recommend Csathy for PHYS 172. I don't have a single complaint about him. He obviously loves physics, and he explains all of his demonstrations very well. He pretty much gives you the answer for all the clicker questions too.

The class is tough, but Csathy is awesome. All my friends started coming to his lecture, because their lecturers weren't as good. He really helps you out with the clicker questions and he's passionate about teaching physics and loves to do demonstrations.

He has a cool accent. Sometimes a little hard to follow but is usually pretty clear. Always checks clicker answers to make sure the majority of the lecture understands the topic and if the class is split or not getting it he goes into more detail. Seems to really enjoy the topic and teaching. All around a nice and good professor

Thought Professor Csathy was a very knowledgable and intelligent person. As for being a teacher, he was decent. He tried to answer questions as much as possible and literally gave us the answers for the clicker quizzes.
Rambles in class, hard to follow, doesn't follow the book. useless incomprehensible. honestly not sure if he is trying to tell jokes. Condescending. CRAZY!!!

He's one great guy!  His Romanian accent is awesome and just that alone sometimes made me want to come to class.  Explains things very well and you can fully understand him.  Some may just find the subject hard.  Although I said attendance was mandatory, it isn't, it's just that you have clicker questions you and get some points for being there.
It doesnt make sense he just rambles and the book doesnt help
Prof. Gabor is someone who is interested in his students progress and is always ready to answer questions.
the professor was pretty good...however, the material is terrible
Great Prof, cool accent, easy to understand, made the class fun, basically gives you the answers on in class quizes if you pay attention to what he says during them

His accent is freaking awesome.  Although the material is pretty simple, he tends to go on small tangents which are pretty interesting to listen to.  He knows his stuff and is much better than other professors.  Not the best, but definitely not the worst.

He was just an OK prof.  All he did was read the lecture notes and besides the clicker points, there was no reason to go to class.   He was not the worst prof I have had here but definity not the best either.
He has a really cool Romanian accent. I went to his office hours before the class started and got the syllabus. He really explained the subject to me.
An enthusiastic lecturer and a fair grader.
This was highkey the hardest grader I ever done had in my life, chill though.
Probably one of the best professors I have ever had. I thoroughly enjoyed her class, and she takes time to get to know her students.
Dr. Cuthbertson was the highlight of my first year. Best SCLA professor. Great discussions and very accommodating with grading.

Course taken Spring 2024. Dr. Cuthbertson during lecture made class not boring, and showed a lot of emotion and would sometimes talk a lot during lectures. I would zone off, and be completely fine, the course was very easy even with the papers and presentations. Group discussions are a big part, and making sure you talk is an important part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Cuthbertson's class was a highlight of my week. She was always ready to make class fun but also a place where we could learn and ask questions. The class is based entirely around readings done outside of class, but they usually aren't super long. Participation is important and she'll try to get everyone to talk, even if it's only one thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very caring and understanding. She gives opportunities for extra credits and have a very fun personality. Participation matters a lot, you should contribute to class discussion semi-frequently to do well in class. I love that the books she requires for class is accessible, cheap, and have rich literary history and importance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every week we had a small 150 word reading response that needed to be quote based. Participating in class discussions is not mandatory, but beware that participation is 10% of the final grade. She's super caring, offers extensions when needed and is super fair when grading.

Super understanding and caring, willing to make exceptions and help you in any way necessary. refuses to give a paper above a 94, even if the comments say it was a perfect essay. You don't need to do the readings but at least read the SparkNotes and talk once a week in class.

Dr. Cuthbertson is an awesome English professor. She is very caring and offers students extra help outside of class if needed. Each class revolves around discussions of the reading, and while some of the readings were quite philosophical, she brought unique insights into the discussions. Overall, it was a fun class.
Her discussions were always very fun and attentive, she always made everyone feel included.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment:
Professor Cuthbertson is the GOAT.
You need to do the readings and participate in class discussions, but they're pretty fun and you can really say anything. She's very understanding and always ready to help students with the writing, willing to give extensions, lets you resubmit an essay after working in the feedback.
Best part of my day!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: So far my favorite professor so far. She always makes sure students are having a good time in her class and isn't shy from deviating away from the agenda if the class discussion is interesting and unique.

Professor Cuthbertson has been my favorite professor at Purdue so far. She is unbelievably smart and so passionate about her passions that it helped inspired me to be more involved in the class. The books required can be a bit difficult to understand sometimes, but she does a great job explaining in class. I would absolutely take this class again

This class was a blast, and Dr. Cuthbertson was a joy to have the whole time. She is so passionate about her work and it is clear to see. She is always wiling to help if you need advice on one of the three papers in that class. Everything was fully manageable and I never felt overwhelmed. She was amazing!

Other reviews said she was a strict grader, but she really was not. I got nothing lower than an 86 and I am a terrible writer. She cares lots about her job and even more about her students. She can talk for a while, but she encourages class participation, and it is nothing boring. She was probably by best professor this past semester.

Dr. Cuthbertson was easily my favorite professor of my first semester. She is super kind and caring, and values everyone's voice in her class. She grades fairly and allows you to resubmit papers based on her feedback, which is awesome.

Dr. Cuthbertson is probably the best professor I have ever had. She is caring, passionate, and very knowledgeable. Though she is a tough grader, she is more than willing to help her students and provides the means for them to succeed. Get ready to have a fun, philosophical, and mostly stress-free class!

Prof Cuthbertson is a very caring prof. She encourages group discussions a lot which can be good or bad depending on whether or not you're a person that likes that. I found her grading pretty fair. If you think she's a harsh grader she still gives a) tons and tons of feedback and b) allowed me to resubmit essays I did really poorly on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cuthbertson's class is rather easy as there is only one assignment a week and three essays throughout the entire semester, however she can be a bit of a harsh grader at times. It does help though as she ensures that you are becoming a better writer. She is really kind and understanding and is super accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course is a very easy A, although people say she grades essays harshly, it doesnt matter because I got B's on 2 of my 3 essays and still ended the class with a 98%. Her harsh grading does not affect your grade but it is also to genuinely help you learn to write. Most of the assignments are for completion anyways so just make sure to do them.

Dr Cuthbertson's class is very mediocre. she goes on tangents a lot and is an extremely difficult grader regarding the 3 essays that are required for the course. She is a very genuine person, but an ok professor. Be prepared to talk as she makes everyone provide a thought or comment about the class readings. She takes attendance very seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I honestly think her class is virtually a free ride if you attend class and just write stuff. Weekly reflection papers are cake. I hate writing, so 3 big essays were painful but manageable. You really don't have to do a thing during the class other than showing up. She is a very likable person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cuthbertson is great. You can tell that she is very passionate about what she does. The way that she runs her class is everyone gets in small groups to discuss the reading, she then shares her personal thoughts, and then we have one large class discussion. The class is very chill with only 3 papers the entire semester.
Tara made this one of my favorite classes.

Her class is entirely discussion based. Whether or not you like that or not, the class is an easy A. As long as you participate, stay off your phone, and do the assignments, you will be fine. If you enjoy class discussions and thought provoking discussions then you will love this class.
Nice lady but goes off on tangents a lot. Easy A though, would take again as an SCLA101 for sure.
Dr. Cuthbertson is a fantastic professor who has interesting discussions with students and cares about her students very much.

Professor Cuthbertson is a super nice person who sincerely cares about her students. Her lectures can be hit or miss (people mentioning the tangents hit the mark) but you don't really have to participate in class all to often. Class is discussion based. There's minimal work for the class as well as super lenient deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Professor Cuthbertson is a wonderful professor who genuinely cares about the well-being of each of her students, sometimes class was boring due to her tangents. The class was extremely discussion based however only graded on a few papers and a presentation. Sometimes her grading is a little harsh and expects great writing from everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Painfully boring class that will make you dread showing up. She is a super nice professor but she tends to just go off on tangents for the entire class while you just sit there and zone out. The class discussions were so surface level that you gain nothing from it and the essays are way too open ended to write anything of substance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cuthbertson is an extremely open-minded and kind professor. Her class is mostly discussion based. We do the readings outside of class (short readings) then talk about whatever relates to the general ideas during class. She is very lenient about grading and deadlines. Easy class, caring teacher.

She does not keep up with grading assignments so no one has any idea how they are doing in the course. Lectures are boring and drag on for the entire hour, she only gears discussions towards what she wants to talk about and will shut you down if you try to change the subject. Overall just a poorly organized course with a lackluster professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While she is a kind hearted person, Professor Cuthbertson's rants and tangents made this class borderline miserable. Showing up felt like a chore and the class discussion was often pointless as she only gears it to her interests and babbles. Her classroom is a no screen zone forcing you to waste money on books that have pdfs available.

Literally the easiest class ever. Gives extensions on whatever you want, only 3 papers for the entire semester in a writing class, very understanding and inspirational. Many extra credit opportunities.

Was not a good professor. Acts like he is caring and kind but will penalize grad students for working. Homeworks were 5+ hours and he didnt explain in lectures. He is a printing guy playing space. Run. RUN. RUN!!!

AAE 340 used a terribly difficult class. Prof Cunningham is improving it so that the material is learned thoroughly without making the content impossible. Lectures are very dry and not worth much, but homework is engaging and kind of fun. Exams are a time crunch but are graded generously. It is obvious that Prof Cunningham cares about his students.

Cunningham is the GOAT. I had him for 203, 251, and now 450. Each time he made learning the material fun and, by extension, easy. He has unc status. He's that guy who is always looking out for you, but will challenge you in ways that make you grow. 10/10 professor and 10/10 person.

(shoutout Talaria and the entire Despicable Me franchise)

This is the quintessential Cunningham course. Very clear lecture style, first half of the course is a breath coverage of the spacecraft subsystems which can be a little dry if you are already familiar with them. Second half of the course is much more interesting coverage with failure analysis and operations procedure. Also very joyful person!!

Thomas Cunningham is who you want all your AAE professors to be like. Great notes, charming guy, and he makes a somewhat boring class (203) pretty interesting. Occasionally gives hints for HW and gives great tips for exams.

This class is chill, but man the grading is kinda petty, and it's a lot of MATLAB assignments so be prepared. It's nice that it's group work tho. You will survive the class, and I would say "Tom Cat" is a good choice.
I took this class over the summer with Cunningham and he was a good lecturer. Pretty clear with the content, good lectures, good exams, he's a very nice guy. I would say I recommend him.
Great Lectures

Awesome professor; super knowledgeable about anything aerospace! This course is insufferably tedious and the homework rubric can be frustrating, but Cunningham is forgiving on any projects he grades. There is plenty of extra credit (up to 4%) to make up for bad grades. Prof. Cunningham is quite amiable and makes this challenging course bearable.
Heavy material but lighter grading, Meaning if you come prepared for tests you will do better than expected. Excellent class for improving Spanish.

Abysmal. I came into this class a fluent native speaker with C1 profiency and left feeling like I'd never encountered Spanish in my life. To this day I do not speak a lick of Spanish and find most episodes of Dora impossible to follow. DO NOT TAKE.
Great professor, very funny as well. Participation does matter, easy A

Prof Cui has an accent and not the best handwriting, which I didn't really have a problem understanding after the first couple days, but if that is typically a problem for you, maybe consider a different lecturer. Overall, seemed like a nice guy, lectures were good, but exams were stressful.

Simply a lovely professor with care and consideration for his students as to what they need to know to succeed. His provision of relevant examples are incredibly important for understanding and while my grade may not reflect that, it is without a doubt that he is an excellent professor especially for showing critical 3-D shapes in relation to math.

Cui was a great professor overall. His lectures are very clear and help you understand the topics. He also goes over many of the upcoming homework problems which makes doing the homework easy to understand. Has great test review lectures. I knew many calc 3 students who had other lecturers that went to Cui's lectures instead.

Professor Cui did a very awesome job teaching calculus III. He goes over most of the proofs (though not required to know) which will help you understand where the equations come from. Lecture notes are always posted on brightspace after class.
Very quickly paced but everything is well organized and explained. Many examples to practice which are very helpful. He makes sure you understand the concept rather than only memorization.

He is an okay professor. His lectures can be really hit or miss, so it gets to be really tempting to skip. You can learn just as well from the textbook, honestly. His notes can be pretty hard to read.
Sometimes hard to understand, but definitely better than the other options. Well organized.

His lectures follow Chenflix pretty closely and he keeps them lighthearted. Sometimes he stumbles on his words but he has good pacing in his lectures. You will be there for the full fifty minutes, he never ends early and sometimes fills with proofs not needed for the class.
W professor. His lectures are really well-organized, and he explains everything pretty well. He does go through pretty fast, but he does a lot of examples every lecture.
Cui is the goat
Although he may be an occasionally competent lecturer, his notes are poorly organized as they are too dependent on the textbook used in this course.

Dr. Cutter is very clear about the way he grades things and emphasizes the importance of communication. Gives good insight on the industry. The assignments consist of multiple papers that won't burden you as long as you start early.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was transparent about grading criteria. Emphasizes communicating problems early and paying attention to instructions, which was not bad if you just put in the time. Overall easy class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy intro class with a couple of papers to write. Took less than 10hrs total over the whole semester to do, and 1/2 of the grade is just by following instruction on stuff like formatting and having a title page. Attendance is by QR codes at end of each class and they count towards the grade.

Easy class. Grade is basically determined by turning in research papers and there are lots of extra credit points given out if you still somehow don't have an A. Speakers are interesting, but definitely a filler class for you to have more credits. Mandatory attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not have many assignments, but expects you to do them early on, long before the deadline. Many of his classes have guest speakers, which gives a good insight into the industry, which I liked.

Professor Cutter is one of a kind. His class was not always the most entertaining, but he tried his best to make it enjoyable. He has a lot of wisdom and good advice about the aviation industry and is an all-around great guy!

There were 2 writing assignments in the entire semester and they were pretty easy. Mostly, he brought in guest lecturers who you had to listen to and interact with during class, but you didn't need to take notes or anything because there were no tests of quizzes. He gave my whole class 100% on our final because he forgot to schedule it.
Professor Cutter is very kind and laid back. Basically just show up, follow assignment instructions, and turn the assignments in on time and you'll receive the easiest A of your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a nice enough guy and you can tell he loves aviation. He doesnt seem very enthusiastic in his lectures however and half the time he will let you out early because he doesnt want to be there. Attendance is mandatory but its a super easy class.
AT100 is super easy, show up and pass. Two or three written assignments that a middle schooler could do. He is a really nice guy too. Very accessible and willing to talk. Also pretty interesting guy.
Easiest class I have ever taken: no exam, no textbook, show up once a week and pass. Cutter seems pretty knowledgeable, and most of the topics discussed in class are very relevant and informing.

Professor Cutters Aviation Systems class might just be the easiest youll take outside Nolans AT10000 class. Theres one group presentation at the end of the course, and the tests are basically the study guides with answer choices. I had the 0730 slot and even though I sometimes fell asleep, I still had an A. If I can pass, you can too.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor made me hate Purdue and pharmacy. Pray you never are required to speak to him. Im a quality student and I achieved my desired grade but this professor is terrible in understanding and speaking to students

Dr. Cushman is honestly like a 3rd grandfather to me. He is always super nice and checks in with students during lecture with clicker questions to see if "learning is occurring" and gives extra credit for these. His question on exams and quizzes were always easier and better understood than his counterparts questions. This man is my favorite.
daddy Cush is so cool I love him and he taught me a lot about organic things I am smart so I got an a+ but I can't say the same for others. -cc

Dr. Cushman cares about students' comprehension.  He gave quizzes before and after class (not for credit) to check on whether "learning was occurring."  He is also excited when you answer his questions correctly, pumping his fist and going "Yes!"
Eclectic individual with some great stories to share.
Class is so easy, only one project and a few lecture reflections. Make sure to go for attendance. Easiest A of college for sure.
Could careless about nursing students. Uses a lot of guest lectures so she doesn't have to do anything. Not helpful. Did not stick to study guide.
PHPR 202 would be great if there were fewer people telling us what is important and what is not.  There is seemingly little communication b/t lecturers, so one cannot answer all the questions.

This professor relies heavily on the use of guest lecturers in her PHPR 202 course, making it difficult to find a consistent format.  I think she thought that using guest lecturers would give us more view points, but it was not helpful.  Also, study everything for her exam, even if she gives you "focus  points", because she may not stick to them.

She's worthless when it comes to explaining homework assignments, essays, or any other important part of any college english course. Picks favorites and ridicules her other classes during class, including names of students she dislikes which I found annoying and unprofessional. Shouldn't be teaching.

I am an English major, and she made me consider changing majors because of her negative and unconstructive "feedback". I always made great grades, and was in AP English in high school, but she dropped my grade from a B to an F the 2nd to last class of the semester and told me to drop out-because I missed ONE class due to an emergency. HORRIBLE.
She is so passionate!  It's infectious.  It's obvious she loves her work and that makes it easy for me to show up and do the work.  She likes student discussions and lets us create our own projects.

She is the best professor I have ever had at Purdue. Sometimes she is not clear with her saying but it makes sense afterall.  she is very helpful and knows how to make an intersting class for her students.
Nice teacher! She was not required a textbook and she was really full of passion. Her project is progressive and don't have strict restriction of your writing! Excellent!!
She is a very interesting lady! Kinda liberal. I did enjoy the books we read though. she is easily side tracked and very involved with students. Excellent person. Bad teacher!
Inspiring.
really nice

An amazing professor!  We did not have a "certain" textbook, but we did have to purchase three novels.  She can adapt the material covered in class with issues or subject matter, but maybe influential to the class.  She gives very positive feedback, extremley helpful, but she tends to get sidetracked.
A fun teacher who manages to make the subject of english interesting even for students that don't like the subject. I loved every minute of my time in her class.
Very good at explaining how to write. Absolutely terrible at explaining assignments. Uses WAY too many adjectives.

Dr. Fortner is a excellent professor.  She is always helpful and understanding.  She is extremely clear on how she wants papers written; however, she is not always clear on what you are to write about.  Overall I hate English classes but this one was worth taking.

99% of the professors at Purdue enjoy their job or at the very least treat you as their own. Czader does neither. Consistently mocks or is rude to students who have made genuine mistakes (in some cases for no reason at all), Goes on tangents trying to make points about something that has nothing to do with the assigned reading, makes up rules.. etc
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was on her good side, idk if this is due to my reading the syllabus/instructions or some other reason. She is fairly strict on grading with somewhat arbitrary rubrics, but if you put in effort and read the material, you can succeed. Once we got further into the semester, it became apparent she did care, but hard to tell with her behavior.

I think that you'll like her if you try and want to learn but she can come off as rude sometimes. She can sometimes seem mean but I think it's just a language barrier since English is her third language. In higher level French classes she might be nicer cause it's more natural, I speak pretty fluently and I love her class and her personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Whatever you do is always wrong. Blatantly does not understand her own rubrics and will mislead you with in class slides. Drop unless you're french or a woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Probably the meanest person I've ever met. The words please and thank you aren't in her vocabulary and don't expect her to help you unless you beg. Raises her voice often at students and will never accept she's made any mistakes.
She berates and interrogates students in class and punishes them by taking off attendance points immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: She talks about AI 24/7 and is not lenient when it comes to attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Talks about AI constantly and is very strict on attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very interestingly, I noted in the review at end of semester that it spoke volumes that she had even a 1.5. Magically over the summer, he ratings went up to 2.0. It's awfully funny how that works, isn't it?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Withdrew from the course after the first class. She is extremely strict for seemingly no reason. Visibly hates her job. Was rude to students who were 10 minutes late on the first day. Made up her own rules such as "you are not allowed to switch sections without my consent". Plus, her english is not even great for an english professor.

Professor Czader is one of the most passionate professors I've had. She actually cares about the messages from the readings. In the beginning she can be tougher on grading but as long as you show up and know what happened in the book, she will lighten up. She is a great professor. Just don't be stupid and use AI because she is pretty strict on it.

Strict grader and strict on attendance too, but forces you to learn the APA format through this. Some of the group activities done in class are interesting too. Often keeps extended office hours for feedback and is nice outside class. Choice of books for reading is not great, as a lot of them tend to be historical French books.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's strict on deadlines, but in my opinion that's a good thing. I learned more from her class than from most of my other courses.  She's engaging with the class and keeps the conversation productive. Learned a lot about APA formatting. She's more than willing to offer guidance and gives good office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She tells you what she expects from you right from the start. If you are unwilling to do the homework, readings, and show up to class on time/participate, DO NOT take her section. If you follow the rubric for the essays and presentation, you should get a good grade. I think she was a good professor as long as you showed interest in the lecture.

Spoke more about how we should not use AI for papers in class than doing something relevant to the coursework. Cannot think of more than 2 interesting "lectures" over the course of 4 months. Work is tedious compared to other sections of the same course and graded more harshly. Somehow manages to cram only french stories in all the readings.

1. way too much hw for 100 level course
2. does not teach you APA format, forces you to learn it online by yourself
3. harsh grader 
4. Does not seem like she cares much abt her students 
5. Very strict for seemingly no reason
6. god forbid you run 30 sec late. get counted absent

only good quality is that the course is extremely well organized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Listen, I respect a strict teacher. But she was beyond that, she would make fun of of other classes and would start conflict for stupid reasons. She has a problem admitting she is wrong at times, and her English could be better. Very monotone and seems like she hates her job. If you get her as professor, at the very least switch professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor just needs to learn about being better to her students. I am sure she can see these comments, but nothing seems to change. I wish she could have been better. She is impeccably rude and harsh to her students. I understand if she might be having a bad day, but I do too, yet I don't cast it on everyone else. I heavily do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Taking her class was a bunch of mixed emotions. If you aren't willing to put in the work, don't bother signing up for her class. She assigned easy homeworks, but graded harshly on presentations and would bad mouth about her other classes and students who were. Attendance is mandatory, but don't bother sending an email, she won't look at it.

- Actively antagonistic towards students
- Will target students for no apparent reason
- Instructions are often unclear, resulting in her getting angry when students misunderstand
- Treats the class like French History rather than an English course, ignoring the curriculum
- Refused to grant me university-required accommodations multiple times
Fine scla course
I don't feel like explaining why because people already have, just switch to a different professor.

Professor Czader is the type of teacher who demands respect from her students but does not show them respect. She does not hesitate to call out and embarrass students, even for the smallest mistakes. She is very nitpicky with your writing. I felt like her class was more of a French history class rather than an English class. Don't take her class.
Drop the class while you still can. Not worth your GPA going down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: SCLA101 is an easy course, with very doable work and an easy grade, but Dr. Czader herself is not a good professor. She can't teach well, and can't relate to her students or understand them at all, and leaves your outcome from the course as really lackluster and bare minimal. Easy course, but theres definitely better profs out there for SCLA101.

Professor Czader grades extremely harshly and expects the most out of you. She profusely picks apart everything that you submit. She often shows no regard for her students' feelings or concerns. She does have a sense of humor, but please do not let this distract you from how awful her class is. If you have the opportunity to switch, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This teacher is probably my worst one to this point in college and probably my worst teacher of all time. An extremely tough grader who doesn't care about this class and seems to not care about her students either. If you have her, I would highly recommend to switch to a different teacher.

Despite SCLA 101 being a very easy class, professor Czader was not properly equipped to teach it. Her instruction and in-class activities were often unclear and drawn out, and it would sometimes seem as if she had not read the books we were discussing. While I still believe that she genuinely cares about teaching, she's bad at teaching SCLA 101.

Other users have already covered all the problems with this professor. They sound exaggerated, but her class is really that bad. I think she does care about teaching her students, she's just very bad at it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters
