reviews.comment: Czader is very bitter towards students and bullies and humiliates random people for no reason. She gives a ton of homework and expects you to read 100 pages and take notes for homework. Class discussion is unorganized and unproductive. As you can see from the terrible reviews, DO NOT TAKE.

Would not recommend for SCLA 101. She is unclear about what exactly she wants from papers, assigns way too much reading and too many assignments for a 3 credit hour class, and she's just generally mean. If possible, I would try to switch to a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
First, I took SCLA101 instead of FR201.
Although I earned an A- in this class, I wouldn't recommend her. She is intimidating, strict, stubborn, and unwilling to admit mistakes, often shifting blame to students. The last one has caused me unnecessary inconvenience and took more of my time than this class should have. Definitely not recommending!

Unpredictable mood, can be strict, can be playful. Seems unapproachable though appears to want students succeed. Can be intimidating and doesn't hesitate to indirectly call out faults in front of the class.

After having a higher level French teach above FR202 I realize how great of a teacher Czader is, she is great at helping you understand things and makes sure you keep up with the work by having daily (yes daily but they arent hard, like its 20 minutes youll live) assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very harsh on students. She never offers helpful advices. She humiliates and embarrasses students in class.

I was very intimidated by Dr. Czader at first, but with time, I began to really enjoy having her as a professor. The course was challenging, had a lot of homework, and grading could be tough at times. Still, I found that she was a great professor, and enjoyed getting to know her. Show effort and respect during class, and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Didnt normalize making mistakes. Scolded students during class for errors, and made learning hard. Not very available outside of class and inconsiderate of busy college schedules. Would wait a week to respond to emails

Very rude when discussing in class about French. If you don't know something she becomes frustrated and takes it out on you and makes the class very toxic for students to listen to. Most people have stopped coming to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I do not recommend taking any class with this prof. She is tough and strict but also unorganized, a frustrating combination. She is passionate about her job and is enthusiastic, but her teaching skills are not well-honed. Very harsh grader, requires a lot of work, a stickler for attendance. She is not accomodating or supportive.

The worst teacher I have ever had. She is not only harsh on grading but also super disrespectful to students. She mocks at students all the time. She is weird. I would never take her classes if I were you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof has good sense of humor, but a stickler for attendance/food-in-class/participation. Not flexible and not easily-accessible outside of class. Textbook required. Do yourself a favor and take advantage of any EC opportunities. Be respectful and put some effort in and you'll be okay!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CHEM 111 is one of the most difficult classes I've taken because of Dr. Hardwood. It's not a difficult class, but she goes off on tangents and genuinely forgets what she is saying. She'll stop mid-lecture and stare off into space randomly. The same also goes for CHEM 112 with her.

Poor lecture delivery. Lectures are unengaging and often confusing due to frequent tangents and errors. There doesn't seem to be a clear plan or flow, which makes it hard to learn from class time. I struggled to stay focused and felt that the lectures did not support the course content well.

Very nice lady, but she's a bit scrambled and doesn't seem to always know what's going on, ranging from a confusing brightspace page to messing up simple calculations in lecture. Its an easy class, but she makes it confusing

Such a sweet woman. However, she is all over the place. Constant technical difficulties, lots of mistakes when explaining problems, lots of rambling at the beginning of class, and unclear due dates for the surveys that she assigns. All that said, she is a wonderful person.
All over the place. Messes up simple calculations. Couldn't calculate percentages. Forgets what she is talking about in the middle of her sentence.
I love this women

Harwood is really nice and cares a lot. Do the practice exams she gives you online and you will be fine! She curves the class at the end of the semester. Have your TA help you with the prelabs and labs. You should be fine! Basically high school chem

I disliked her very much. She is all over the place all the time and very scatterbrained. She never teaches what needs to actually be explained for labs or exams. She never responds to emails, although she begs people to email her with questions. She is an amazing and caring person, but in my opinion not a good professor.

If you're a type A, organized & prepared student, this class is NOT for you. If you keep track of when things are due, it will be IMPOSSIBLE in her class. She seems like a lovely lady, but this class isn't designed for student success. Grading is unclear, subjective, & irrational. For 50k a year, there's other classes that aren't built for failure!

Prof. Harwood is very caring and makes sure to help students out and answer questions during lecture! Extra credits points for attendance via iClicker. She explains things well and its easy to get extra help. Take advantage of SI, office hours (prof. and TA), free tutoring, and chem resource room! Make sure to do all of the assignments!

Prof. Hardwood was extremely caring. She likes all of her students and she does things for everyone's best interest. She cant read her own handwriting and she's all over the place. If you have never taken chemistry before…don't take it with her. I honestly don't even know what I've learned. Great personality…should not be a professor.

Prof. Harwood seems to be an amazing professor but she's terrible at teaching in the lecture halls. The exams are hard so you definitely need to STUDY. If chemistry isn't your thing, then BE PREPARED because you're going to be studying for 7+ hours for exams, in ONE day.

Harwood is very kind and clearly wants her students to succeed. Unfortunately, though, lectures are VERY difficult to follow. You will likely learn more in sessions with your TA than in the actual lecture. I'd recommend going to Harwood's office hours because she seems to do better when not teaching to a hall with hundreds of students.

Not a great professor. Gets mixed up with her own handwriting in lectures making me and others really confused. When rewatching her lectures her handwriting is so hard to read. Gives A LOT of other assignments that don't even help. Those are things I am doing to get a grade doesn't help at all. On exams tests us on stuff from other chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized but well-intended professor she clearly cares about her and wants you to succeed but it is a lot of work, not only that but the material is a lot heavier and there is more math. if I were taking this course again but I AM NOT THANK GOD, I would put a lot of focus on the labs and hw because the exams get harder as you on.

Gets confused by her own work during lectures but cares about students doing well. Exams are very hard especially if you did not previously have a chemistry class in high school. Lots of assignments, not too hard but just a bunch of work every week and labs are kind of annoying.

Dr. Harwood is extremely kind and passionate. She is very understanding that chemistry is not for everyone. There is a lot of material, so don't get behind and I would highly recommend going up to her after lecture or during office hours for any questions because she is always very helpful. Hard class, but great professor.

Harwood was a deeply caring professor who clearly wanted to get to know us all, even though we were in the thousands. Class was informative and exams diverse and not that hard. Only complaints is lots of piddly homework and she sometimes was unorganized in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I recommend looking at

Prof. Harwood was a good lecturer, when she was prepared. I found that her lectures were disorganized and hard to follow. I gave up on attending the lectures and started watching the recordings from each class period, because the information in her lectures would vary, and that was the only way I felt I was getting the full picture.
Her class was enjoyable, make sure you go to the lectures and do the worksheets
Was not a fan of this professor at all. She did not have office hours of her own to help students. We would not get much done in lecture because she would ramble on about everything off topic.
I took the summer course. Had some sort of homework everyday. If I put more effort I could have gotten a better grade, however, its summer and I also work. She's nice and welcomes all questions.

She cares about her students and understands what topics are difficult and takes time on them. Only a midterm and final with an online quiz every two weeks. Class was well put together and I loved her easy lectures. You do get a lot of homework, but it is easy and helps your grade.

I had no exams, but there will be exams in every CHEM111-112 class after mine. Dr. Harwood seemed unprepared at times, but was a good lecturer when prepared. I preferred Dr. Towns, but still learned with Harwood. Available to help over email. Understanding and kind. You need to watch lecture and keep up. Most easy material but can get overwhelming.

I liked her during CHM 111, she was great. This semester, she came to lecture very unpreparedly. Mumbled the whole time. Lots of my worksheets were graded incorrectly. I would go back and check and go from a 50% to a 100% because I was getting graded wrong.

Dr. Harwood was good. She is more straightforward and strict in her teaching. As long as you go to lecture and pay attention, you will be fine as there are no exams, open note quizzes, 3 attempts on homeworks, etc. However, do not let that mislead you to thinking you don't have to try, the content can still be difficult especially if you zone out!!

Harwood seems to know what she's talking about, but at the beginning of lectures, she can get a bit off track. She ends up talking about stuff we don't really need to know and, due to this, we ended up being behind where we needed to be. However, the setup of the class is amazing (no final, 3 chances on homework, etc.).
Lots of worksheets, can be time consuming. My class didnt have exams though.

I thought this was a great class. The contents of the (open book/note)quizzes were always easy and there was no final, just a couple of worksheets. I thought that all activities furthered my knowledge and weren't just busy work. I also liked that the schedule of assignment due dates was the same every single week.
Good class, I actually learned things which didnt happen in most my other classes. Open note/ book for quizzes and the final. Some lab instructions were confusing though.

Dr. Harwood is very knowledgable about chemistry. She may move through lectures quickly but is always available in person and through email to answer any questions you may have. Plus iClicker points gets you an easy 20 bonus points. Also she posts old exams for you to practice with and get an idea what real exams will be like.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was okay. She didnt really explain concepts very well and she was kind of mean. I barely passed her class because she did not motivate me to do anything and the labs/homework sucked.

I think that people who judge professor Harwood on her mistakes in classes do not understand the fact that she is human and that she makes mistakes. I think that if you know highschool chemistry well then there is a good chance that most of the things covered in this course will be easy. If you don't have any don't worry the homework will help.

Really just not a great teacher. Unclear about expectations, not helpful when asking for help, will not accept that her students failures are her fault. Don't expect going to classes to be helpful nor office hours, rely on the book only as she literally has no clue what is going on either. Does not fit in with the other professors at Purdue.

Not a shining star of Purdue's Profs, teaching a BEGINNER class and exam averages are in the mid 60's and will blame anything but herself. Don't bother going to class, she doesn't know how to do the examples either. She'll just confuse you. She's poorly prepared all the time and will do an example, say its wrong, then quit and leave you hanging.

She truly is a smart woman, but I think she struggles conveying what she knows in a way that other people can understand. Makes so many last minute changes in lab that there's constant confusion. A large amount of students don't even go to class as the textbook explains way better.

There is homework due every week which can be lengthy so dont wait till last minute. If you understand all the material, exams should not be too difficult. Make sure to participate in i-clicker questions as they are extra credit. Professor Harwood is always willing to help outside of class. Do not be afraid to ask for help!!!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There's homework due every single week which can be pretty lengthy. Lectures are a lot of notes.

Dr. Harwood is one of my all time favorite professors. If you are willing to put the time and effort in to succeed so is she. Sometimes she gets going so fast in lecture that shell forget a detail and mess up a problem. Seriously love visiting her during office hours though. She is really helpful one on one and really wants you to do well

I do not think this professor is good at conveying her knowledge to students. She goes way too fast and all of my friends and I are very confused. The homework has nothing to do with her lectures, so you basically have to rely on google to assist you in completing problems.
pretty good at explaining things, but exams were pretty unpredictable
If you have taken chemistry before it is definitely a breeze. It's basically a review class for chemistry and very basic. Dr. Harwood likes to use different ways to solve problems.

Harwood cares about your learning but won't take the initiative to make sure you're understanding the material unless you come to her with questions. CHM 111 and 112 aren't super challenging classes - if you go to lecture and turn in the homework due every Friday you should do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She gave me a lot of help in class and out of class. She is more than likely the best professor you could ever get at a college. I am not surprised that everyone loves her class. I would not skip out even if I was paid $100.
Awesome Professor.  Best one I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I went to  class every week, but I played on my phone in the back and didn't take any notes. Ever. I only went because she gives so much extra credit through Iclickers. She's  super nice and a good lecturer, and anyone can pass this course with minimal effort if they took high school chemistry and go to lab.

She's usually unprepared for lecture and can ramble at times. She loves explaining easy concepts and minimizes the importance of other complicated concepts. The book helped me more than her lectures did. Attendance is optional, but you could earn iClicker extra credit points at each class.
EASY A.

Her office hours are the best thing ever. She is always super flexible with them, and easy to get in contact with. The first exam I got a D and then went to her office hours and got an A on the second.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Never seemed prepared for lecture. Very scatter brained and forgetful. She always spent the most time where it was least needed, such as office hours and simple concepts, and didn't fully explain the complex topics.

She's really friendly and nice but is unprepared for lecture. She spends too much time explaining easy concepts and rushes through the more difficult concepts. Very scatter-brained.    Attendance is optional but you get iclicker extra credit points.
Clicker questions  easy points,  sympathetic with the level of difficulty of subjects throughout the course

Decent lecturer, but for me, the book helped me more than she did. She would rush through lectures and would usually only cover the very basics of new material. For some reason I just could hardly stay awake in her lectures, even at 10:30. She was always available for office hours and was helpful then, but I found the book more useful in overall.

Great lecturer in my opinion. A lot of extra credit is given that is due at the end of the semester, try not to fall behind with it. I read most chapters in the book which helps tremendously. She gives learning objectives which tell you exactly what content you need to know which is very helpful. You have to work in this course but it is doable.
I enjoyed her as a professor. She explained the material well.
Her lectures are thorough and clear, but you still need to spend time reading the book. She also has a pleasant speaking voice.

Not helpful. Lectures are rambling, disjointed, and poorly timed. Often speeds through new and complex slides but spends excessive amounts of time on topics either too simple or too outdated to be applicable. Usually introduces the most important and complex concepts in the last 5-10 minutes of lecture. Good personality but class feels like a mess.
She explains individual concepts well, but fails to connect them together.  Really is helpful and there for you.
lectures are clear but if anything is hard to understand she explains it really well during office hours. some tough material over all but she explains it well.
Come to class so you can answer all the clicker questions for extra credit.
Professor Harwood is extremely boring and unhelpful, especially after having Professor Towns for Chem 111. She knows her stuff, but doesn't make it fun to learn.

She is a great professor, but she comes off a little aggressive. However, once you have introduced yourself she is very nice and there if you need any help for anything. It is good if you have any questions that you ask, but she generally gets the information to you in a clear and concise way. She likes to work a lot with examples so be prepared.

So glad I got to have her as a teacher, going to lecture doing the work and reading the chapters will get you an A. You have to put in the work but she is always there to help if needed. I was terrified of taking chem but with her as a teacher it made it enjoyable and easy
Loved her!
She is not very engaging and that makes it tough to learn any of the material and getting the motivation to come to class.

Dr. Harwood is such a nice, helpful professor. She explains things so well and makes sure that people understand the material. She has office hours, is very approachable, and eats at a dining court every Friday inviting students to ask her about Chem or talk about anything they want to!

Is SO caring about her students. I appreciated all the extra efforts she makes to meet with students through out the semester including lunches, office hours, and helpful review sessions. I really felt like she was a professor that I could really talk to and get help from. Really enjoyed her classes!!
Great prof. Wish she would of taught the whole semester
Really good professor. Easy to understand and helpful in the way she teaches.

Harwood is a very good professor. She knows the material, she is VERY good at communicating lecture material as well as other course info (recitation notes, lab prep, etc), and she doesn't drone on like most lecturers. If I had to take another Chem course, I would want her to teach it.
She was very clear and helpful in lecture.  She explained the material very well and made it easy to understand.
Great Teacher, my grade has gone up a lot since she took over. She's a little unorganized but it doesn't effect the class much
Very good at explaining. Made the course very easy.
Harwood is one of the more interesting professors I have had for chemistry, but her tests have been the hardest. Talks alot and sometimes gets sidetracked.
She is a little spacey at times and forgets a lot but she is sweet and lectures are always interesting. Sometimes she give away the answers to the iclicker questions which is always nice.

I've fallen asleep in every one of her lectures so far this year. The only thing that keeps me awake is the crossword puzzle. Hopefully she will eventually realize that some of us haven't memorized the exact chemical properties of every compound in the universe. Anyway, thank you for helping me decide that ME, with no chemistry, is right for me.
She does a good job explaining things, and I like her tests. I don't like the CPS pads that we have to use, but they get me to class. She isn't a bad professor though.

Professor Harwood doesn't offer much student interaction with her lectures, which does not provide for a very interesting class environment.  However, she's a knowlegeable, kind person who is one of the most helpful people I've ever met, and is always there for any student who needs her.  She also has a very fair grading system. Recommended!

I was skeptical when I heard that CHEM 123 had a new professor for this year, but Prof. Harwood has proved to be a fine teacher.  I think that our lecture covers information far better than CHEM 115 does.  Her one vice is that she uses the pronoun "guys" for many chemistry terms, which can be confusing sometimes.  Great course, though.
Very caring professor, lectures are content heavy but exams are very fair. A lot of studying but enjoyable content.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: lectures are very dry and monotonous.Exams are impossible to get a good grade on if you do not have a photographic memory. It will ask things never talked about or mentioned on a very small text on a photo in the slides. No real direction in what to study besides every little detail. I would not recommend for people who are not Neurobiology majors.

Great person he's super caring and accommodating, however class is very hard. No matter how much you study you won't do good unless you have a photographic memory. Picks very specific details for the exams and you have to know everything. Exams are extremely hard and there is next to nothing to make your grade better if you do bad on the exams.
Dr. Suter is a great
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes at Purdue, not easy by any means but very interesting and engaging. Dr. Suter is an awesome  professor.

I loved BIOL436 with Professor Suter. The course material is hard and he does expect a lot, so be prepared to put in time outside of class and lecture to read the supplemental textbook pages he assigns. The exams are difficult, but you can tell the passion that Dr. Suter has for neuroscience in his teaching and it makes the course worth it.

Dr. Suter can be a bit dry, but he is very knowledgeable and gives interesting lectures. There are only a few assignments outside of exams, but all the assessments are graded extremely fairly. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is important to attend or watch lectures in order to keep up with the material. Syllabus says to buy the textbook-don't.

Dr. Suter expects a lot out of his students, therefore his exams can be quite challenging due to them being so in depth and detailed. However, Dr. Suter himself is a great professor, super approachable, and loves to talk about tennis.
Good class, but the tests are pretty difficult. Suter is a very nice guy, loves to talk about tennis.

Dr. Suter is the nicest guy! His class is moderately challenging. If you go to class, read the book, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. Make sure to go over the study questions because he definitely uses those on tests. Just put in the time for the class, and you should be able to get a really good grade.

He was incredible. Probably one of the kindest professors I've ever taken a class with. 

Lovely to interact with, even outside of class. Taught every concept very clearly and gave us time to understand the applications as well.
Loved the class. Extremely well structured, and homework was very helpful to better learn the material. He is very caring and understanding. Always willing to answer questions.

I like that he explains concepts in an applicable way, like what types of questions can be solved using this model. I don't think he focuses too much on the model itself, which makes it understandable. He is also very smart and accessible.

He is knowledgeable but he is not a good teacher. He might need to understand different learning styles and respect the diversity of the student body in his classes. Students who do not actively ask questions are not stupid. Sometimes his class time is occupied by a few of the students who ask too many repqested questions.

he has been teaching this course for more than 5 years but still does not have a systematically organized lecture note and HW Qs. Most of the time he just brings a piece of a white sheet where he writes something. He stares at the whole class asking if they have any questions. When no one volunteers, the whole class is weirdly silent.

I am surprised to see his rating on RMP - I feel like the classroom atmosphere was friendly and open, and I am not afraid of asking any questions. He is also approachable after class and I do feel he cares about students. Many topics are helpful for my research. I recommend this course to all my colleagues (even if they are not at AgEcon).

Michael is one of my favorite professors at Purdue. He uses understandable language to interpret econometrics concepts, and he is always responsive to questions. He also involved questions that are helpful in job seeking. He has a few pop quizzes but most are straightforward. I admit the final project was challenging, but I did learn a lot.

For some reason, I feel a bit intimidated to take his classes. I am not able to tell why but feel that his classroom atmosphere is not friendly and conducive to learning with an open heart. His classes tend to be examine and judgement oriented, which make one feel uncomfortable. Econometrics classes could be more interesting.
a good researcher, an aweful teacher.
Generally not recommended if you are not required to take this course. The lecturer was not able to teach well.

To M.D., If you are not interested in dong research in agricultural economics, why you want to be a faculty in AGEC at Purdue? Just because of its less intense competition? You are just not fit to this program, tbh.
Avoid him at any cost!!! My only advice for both undergraduate and graduate students at Purdue.

Not recommended for taking this course, recommend taking from the department of economics instead. He really does not know what is the best way to teach at all. His projects is just not useful for research. HW is nothing useful either. But he emphasizes too much on quiz which further makes students feel like it is not for application.

This course cold have been more useful for graduate students doing applied research, but it was intentionally designed as an closed book exam-oriented and quiz-intensive course. The class environment is nit friendly and makes students feels extremely uncomfortable.

he seems to know a lot about research. Unfortunately, he won't learn much useful about research from his class. He said his class is not a workshop. It surprised me as he knows little about his economic research related to agriculture. He was not able to explain econometric knowledge in a clear way. He just doesn't like agricultural economics.

If I had the chance to take the econometric courses from econ department, I would definitely do so. This course is just too far away from what I need for my research. Not useless and not being taught well enough. The instructor is not easy to approach and satisfy.

Be aware of this professor. You will find him intentionally set vague criteria or guidance for some points, that's where he will examine and judge you by his own observation. Eg., the guidance for course project is very vague and you will most likely to schedule office hours and discuss with him, and each person will receive different treatments.

Overall class was helpful for me to understand the key concepts in econometrics and think about the application of those concepts. You have to know about the matrix formula and be prepared for the pop quizzes. His explanation was clear and he encouraged in-classroom discussion.
He is and will be the worst professor in my school life. He differentiate students by his own subjective assumptions. Avoid him at any cost.

Avoid this professor, he doesn't know how to teach at all. Course projects are assigned by his subjects, if ask for a change of topic, he will say no without any listening. I never had any experience of faculty displaying so strong personal dislike toward students. He is the only one. Terrible teaching overall, and need more teaching experience.

Professor Delgado is incredibly smart and he explains the concepts very well. The subject is very hard, though, so be prepared to work hard. Class is interesting and Professor Delgado is funny you just have to be paying attention.
Horrible. What a joke. You'll learn nothing and he'll test you on random facts from the appendix. Avoid if possible, especially at the graduate level.

Teaches straight out of the book. Homework is worth almost nothing and tests are open response, which make them excruciatingly hard. After the second midterm the class avg. was a 63. He curved the class 13pts, which is unheard of. Had to beg for students to go to office hours, even offered a bonus point (just 1), still no one went. Horrible teacher

Avoid this teacher! All grades are based on exams and homework. Homework does not count for much, so you have to do well on exams. Exams are also written. Each answer is a short response, so you really have to know your stuff. The curve only helps you so much but not enough to get the grade you want.
Never responds to emails and is poor teacher overall.  Avoid him at all costs
Worst professor I have had at Purdue. You have to do great on the exams, or else you won't pass. No personality at all. Good economist, AWFUL at teaching.

He doesn't really know how to teach. If you go to lecture, he will ask you to define and explain what he is talking about; he'll awkwardly stare at the class until someone says something. And yes, this goes on for the entire lecture. Tests are ridiculously hard.  To pass you need to do stellar on the two midterms (hw is only 5 pts each).
Very difficult to get an A, but mostly probably you can get a C
If you show up to class every day, you'll survive.
Unnecessarily difficult course, EAPS should NOT be this hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful class average gpa was a 2.5 DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never done so poorly in a course in my life up until now. The homework is weighted as if it were finals and being a day late on the homework is -25%. He gave a 60 mcq hw on the night of Thanksgiving and I was 2 days late to it, answered all questions correctly, and got a D-. Begged him for forgiveness because it dropped my grade by 2 letters

The lectures were crammed with way too much content in very little time. Felt like I was constantly behind on work. Homework was unnecessarily difficult, with 50-60 multiple-choice questions that seemed designed to confuse. The professor showed little empathy and didn't offer support. Freshmen should take EAPS 105 for a much easier experience.

He was very difficult to work with and incredibly rude with every interaction, the homework's were long and strenuous (50-60 questions per), the lectures had a lot of information to ingest with very short time periods to do so. Overall, would not recommend to anybody.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are no-tech/no slides, handwritten note yourself, with limited study material. Reviewing is very difficult. Exams are closed-note and test very detailed points from what he said on class you must memorize exactly. Videos are provided to learn coding html, but you will need to write out the exact code during exam. Do Not Recommend!

Dr. D is an effective lecturer, who, if paid attention to, provides clear conceptualizations through use of personal storytelling. I found that paying attention in class and taking concise notes helped me to succeed. He is old-school, and prohibits technology, but I felt that minimizing distractions helped me to stay focused.

Dr. D is an effective lecturer who explains concepts well. His work sessions prepare you well for HW assignments. Exam is a big portion of the grade, is fully closed‑book/notes, and is quite difficult, with some very specific details tested--I think he takes pride in its difficulty. But he does give partial credit. I did learn a lot in the class.

Mr. Dejoie deeply cares about MGMT 382 and has a lot of time under his belt, however, this class is painful to sit through sometimes. NO TECHNOLOGY in addition to no lecture slides makes you writing in your notebook every thought he spurts out since it's most likely going to be on the exam. If you miss a class you better get the notes from someone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN! You HAVE to take notes to do well. Practically no resources to learn if you miss class. All short-answer exam: questions require you to remember his specific ramblings/reasoning, not just "correct" answers (despite open-ended questions) - notes from previous sections can be different. No technology allowed - handwritten notes only. Very boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please put all the content in the PowerPoint presentation instead of relying on the professor to lecture, and don't even take notes. Not everyone is a native speaker. I have never seen an exam that is all short answer questions. The worst professor is the one you should choose. If you accidentally choose him, run away!

Absolutely HORRIBLE professor. He would ONLY reach out on Piazza and he would respond to issues with a lot of verbiage but little to no guidance. He loves to gloat about how hard his exam is but that is because it is all closed notes and difficult to prepare for. Mind you this is a Python course that can be for beginners. AVOID.

Group Projects are super easy but only worth a small part of your grade. His lectures are 10x more boring than any other teacher I've ever had. The tests (70% of grade) have questions that make you quote what he said in class which makes studying for them almost impossible. He loves to brag about how hard his class is and wants you to fail.

This professor made the course 10x more difficult than it should be. The material of this course is not bad, the way that it's structured is terrible. It doesn't feel like he wants everyone to succeed, even the peer evaluation is designed in a way where someone has to lose points even if everyone did equal work. Terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Switch to a different professor. There are a total of five assignments including the two exams worth 70% of your grade.  By the end of the semester I had grades for my first exam and first project.  Lectures are confusing as he goes on personal tangents often. The exams aren't too bad as they're purely based on lecture. Your notes are everything

By far one of the worst professors at Purdue. If you miss one of his lectures, you better hope the material covered that day isn't on the exam. His lectures are extremely boring and not engaging at all. If you need help, I suggest asking one of the TAs instead because he will grill you on how you don't understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very specific questions on exam. He also doesn't curve the class average to a 3.0.

Dr. D expects you to go to every single lecture, and if you miss class, he won't provide appropriate resources for you to learn the material. The lecture slides cover less than 10% of what you see on exams. His lectures are unbearable to listen to since he goes on tangents on his days at Texas A&M and on personal tales with no relation to class.

No slides or outside resources for topics, and you have to go to class everyday or else you won't make it. Exams are the hardest I've ever taken since it's off of what we talked about in class and it's all open answer with absolutely NO hints. He is very intellectual but lectures are so heavy it's hard to know everything we are expected to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are no slides at all, the exams are just based on his rambling for the entire class. The exams are worth 70% of your grade and the exam makes you refer straight from what he says in class. I wouldn't take this class if you can't learn from someone just sitting and talking.

All the content for the class is basically him rambling and you just have to try and keep up. Outdated lecture style. Often goes off on tangents and tests were hard. Project criteria makes no sense and you cannot equally grade groupmates. Avoid this professor, other lectures with different teachers have easier tests and a much easier overall class.

Some people don't like Dr D, but I enjoy being in his classes. He is very straight foreward and will tell you how it is and what he expects from you. If you follow along through the progression of the course and genuinely learn the code you will be fine. Don't work with a partner / copy others, just learn it.

Who would set a due date on Sunday at 12 am... Beware!!! The discussion board is due every week on Sunday "12 AM". Why can't he just tell students that it is Saturday 11:59 pm. I was too focused on "Sunday" and didn't realize it's actually due the day before. I don't know why but I feel like this is just tricking students into the wrong deadline.

The exams are challenging but in my section there was a significant curve that helped me out on one of the exams. Three group projects, but none of them take very long to complete. A few warnings: follow all directions on assignments carefully, and take detailed notes. Like, be way way way more detailed than you usually would.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took this class online and it was very disorganized. There was no clear schedule for him uploading lectures. His lectures were not necessarily related to the material, but him talking about unrelated topics. Exams are said to be based on lectures, but the exam format makes them difficult.

Dr. D is one of the worst professors I've ever had in Krannert. He provides few notes, basically zero slides, no study guides, and no practice exams. You just have to take notes on him rambling the whole class because the exams are based entirely on lecture. He is arrogant and scams you into buying his own textbook (which we never used). Avoid him

Worst professor I have had in Krannert. Doesn't know how to lecture concisely, loses track of lecture, doesn't have any notes, doesn't help students, doesn't care about students, extremely arrogant, extremely rude, not helpful with feedback. His approach to being a professor is as if he's doing us a favor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Personally I am not a fan of Roy Dejoie, he will not compromise with students and chews your ear off with his stories and nonsense. His method of teaching is outdated and scams students by writing his own textbook so he can pocket more money. I don't recommend him and hope I never have to take another one of his classes.

He is a great professor and answered my questions all of the time. This is a beginning coding class, and it was very challenging. I wish I could have done better but this was my first time ever coding. There are weekly quizzes from the reading and weekly labs. Labs are basically worked out in class though. Overall, a pretty good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy class as long as you show up to lectures and study your notes. Participation policy is really dumb but other than that great Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great lecture, need to attend class and participate, exams are based what is said in class! Need to take notes. Few assignment, so everything matter. Treat midterm like finals! Tough exam if do not pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dejoie is one of the best professors who teach programming at Purdue (and I have taken many coding classes with the CS department). He gives very clear instructions and uses a lot helpful examples in class that are similar to the homework(aka lab) assignments. If you skip lab days, you will definitely miss out on a LOT of valuable information.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most hard-grading professor at Krannert

I am a senior and I graduated with a 3.7 GPA using two and a half years. Let's be honest Purdue sucks and you don't have many options when it comes to selecting Upper division courses. But this guy is the only professor that I hope you guys could avoid at all cost. Boring lectures, exam you could never really prepare for,AVIOD AT ALL COSTS

Dr. D made class fun, engaging, and enjoyable and also has a lot of industry experience. Most of the class is lecture-based, so make sure to pay good attention and take good notes. There are three group projects that, combined, make up 30% of your grade, and then there is one midterm and a final. Participation is important in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class has relatively no application outside of MGMT382. If you aren't an amazing note taker good luck. He provides no practice exam or study guides for the exams. Lectures are nearly impossible to follow along and he has almost no slides for notes. You just have to take notes off what you hear.
Great teacher, must pay attention in the lectures and take good notes to do well. No need for a textbook, but everything he says is up for game on the tests.

Dr. D is one of my favorite professors since I've been in Krannert. Immensely helpful, funny, and knowledgeable. The class is difficult, and the tests are hard, but if you pay attention in class, you will be fine.

Professor Dejoie is among the best teachers I have had, ever. The course is not highly technical, but purposely made to give pragmatic knowledge for all majorsminors.  One of the best things about him, aside from always being there and excellent lectures is he has great industry experience. His course and teaching reflect this.
You do not need to buy the textbook, you have to participate during class to get credit, exams are all memorization of useless terms, cram a bunch before the exam and you will be fine

Dr. D keeps class fun and interesting. Didn't need to buy textbook. Be sure to take detailed notes because exams are based off lecture notes. Be sure to brush up on your memorization skills, you'll need them to do well on the exams!
u really have to pay attention in class and take all the notes or else you won't do well on the exam
Great Prof! Yes, goes on tangents (they are slightly related to the subject) if you can make the connections, you will MASTER the subject.
Dr. D rambles incessantly. Constantly going off on a tangent. Probably on 10% of class actually translates into knowledge transfer, the rest is absolute garbage.
No Comments

Dr. D is an awesome teacher.  He does grade a little hard but he make the class a TON of fun.  The tests aren't bad AS LONG AS YOU ATTEND THE REVIEW SESSIONS!  I think he's been my favorite professor at Krannert.

Had for MA 351. I wouldn't go as far as enthusiastic, but he shows a clear interest in the course. Lectures are relatively fast paced. Shows intent for students to succeed. Difficult to make office hours.

High level professor in Math at Purdue. Typically only teaches high level grad courses. Lots of homework and they take time. However, he gave review guides for exams and they are very helpful. Possible to get an A in the class if you work for it. Lectures are theory heavy where as exams tend to be more towards calculations besides T/F questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great professor. Doesn't seem to care about students and erases work quickly in lectures. Also pretty disorganized
Don't forget to call her Dr. Patel not Mrs. Patel

I took ENG 106 completely online. She rarely responded to emails. Never gave feedback on my essays. And gave very few instructions for some of the biggest projects in this course. Terrible teacher online. Maybe she is better in person?

Dr. Patel is an amazing professor. She gives a lot of work, but is fair and cares about her students. She also makes the work relevant and I enjoyed having an English class where I got to read things that werent just written by old white men. She challenged me without making things impossible and I learned a lot.

She gives grades based on her mood it seems like. She gives feedback when she gives perfect grade, saying great job, and when she deducts points, there is no comments, there is no way you can know why you got points off. Assignment I'm referring is to assignments that you have to just share your idea, so there are not certain rubric.

Super hard but fair. If you try to make excuses and don't own your faults then you will have an issue with her. She is VERY organized but if YOU don't read the syllabus and ask stupid questions, she won't respond. She always gave feedback ahead of due dates, when I asked, but I had to put the work in. Challenging. Not a class for slackers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you think you can skate by in her class, you are wrong. I took her online class and she had everything laid out nicely. After I got used to the format, everything was fine. She is direct and won't coddle you. If you can't take personal responsibility for your own actions or lack of it, then don't take her. Learned A LOT.

The assignments are very unclear and she is very disorganized. Since this is an online class, I tried to contact her with email many times throughout the semester. However, she only replied once with one sentence very rude and all the other times just ignored my emails. And she doesn't have office hours, this is a horrible class!!!

At the beginning I did not think I would like her, however as the year went on I really grew to like her. At times I would get extremely frustrated with her, however she pushed me to do my best in class and really try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: good teacher, however a bit unfair when it comes to assignments. On a personal level I really like her but as teacher she really grinds my gears.

Excellent professor that challenges you to grow. People that are complaining on here about her assigning too many journals are being a bit petty. This is college, except to have to write and study outside of class. What this professor gives you is an education, not just another silly and meaningless (cram-it-all) course.
Condescending and rude. Overly sarcastic. Online directions not consistent with syllabus.

Online - Whenever I asked about things I did not understand or inconsistencies between assignments and the course calendar, DP was incredibly rude in the responses - always told me to check it again and insisted that she had it right the first time.

Amazing teacher who has helped me to achieve a new level of writing. I can actually write a paper that I feel comfortable with. She uses many different techniques throughout the semester, but I like her style of repetition.
I think she is awesome. Had a great time in her class and learned how to write a paper I could be proud of.
interesting teacher

Too much writing... Journals.. what the hell? I know we have to write in college, but JOURNALS?... I don't think so..And also since we're talking about Popular Culture and all that, we have to watch a bit more movies since everything is relevant. In the book we have a lot of references to movies, and yet we watched only 1 movie.
Interesting class but she was not clear as to what she wanted in our assignments or papers. Has VERY different viewpoints.
No Comments

Even in his first sem teaching, he was a wonderful teacher. I actually enjoyed thermo conceptually because of him. He knew me by name a month later after i mentioned it to him on the first day, and others have attested to the same. He is accessible, helpful, and his lectures are clear and enriching. Hard to find someone who doesn't love him.
Really a wonderful person who takes the time to connect with his students, even in his first semester teaching. I enjoyed the upbeat tone he brought to thermo and learned a lot during his lectures

This was his first semester teaching, but he was outstanding. He was very approachable and cared about everyone's success. He is passionate about thermo, he brought things in to do live examples/show and tell for understanding. His lecturing is great, but when he runs low on time his accent is a bit hard to understand. Definitely a top 5 prof.

While this was Parveen's first semester teaching the course, I do hope he continues. He's very approachable and makes learning thermodynamics a bit less painful. Also hosted review sessions on weekends for the exams, which were very helpful. Overall, really cared about the students and their learning.

This class has a wild reputation, but it's honestly not that bad if you listen to the repeated advice everyone gives. Having a good group is huge. The TAs are pretty active online, so ask lots of questions because they can be really helpful. Biggest tip: don't procrastinate, it will absolutely catch up to you.

Deadman has a reputation as a difficult professor that is well-warranted. He is not a bad guy though, so talk to him and he will address your concerns. Pick a good lab partner who won't flake on you, and show up to lecture. Don't try to get people to sign the attendance sheet for you or put your name on in-class assignments, it won't work.
wasnt there for half the semester but still called me out for chatting during class

content was interesting but, the labs take hours, like 20+ hours. windows based so sometimes you get errors that aren't even your fault and you spent hours troubleshooting. GET A GOOD TA. go into the class knowing who your lab partners are bc that could make or break your grade. he gave us a test the day before thanksgiving break which was annoying

you need a good group for this class so go into it with people yk thats the most important thing otherwise ur cooked. labs take up a looooootttttttttt of time and what makes this class so hard is that there are random errors w windows that you cannot control so it takes hours to troubleshoot. also you need a good ta bc fade some of these tas .
This course is engineered to be harder than it should be in many way but for some reason this dude has a lot of d riders
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the type of guy to give an exam the last day before break 👎

The TAs are generally unhelpful and often don't respond to questions at all. Grading is extremely strict, which would be fine if real guidelines were provided. Expectations also vary between TAs, which is frustrating, especially when your own TA is unresponsive and others can't be contacted.

If you get groupmates that are clearly struggling on Lab 1, drop the class and replace it with another class. The full workload for this class is about 40+ hours a week for a 4 credit hour class. This is a recurring problem that I know Deadman is aware of, but he doesn't change the class structure.
Disorganized course. Hardly any effective guidance given.

Assigned an Exam during between the weekend and thanksgiving break. Prevented students from leaving early. Robert explains the material well and is kind towards students. Saved me from a fire once, love that guy.

The labs are VERY time consuming. If you dedicate time for the labs you learn a lot. A lot of time is spent in the lab outside of the actual lab section but Deadman's expectations seem to be reasonable given what you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Deadman is a great professor. Always willing to answer lab or lecture questions during office hours and very approachable. The class is difficult but very much doable. If you put effort into the class you'll see results. My advice to you is to get good lab partners are set a WEEKLY time to meet so you can make progress on the labs.

The course itself is hard but he does a great job of lecturing, way better than Salam. Attendance is taken by signing your name on a sheet and there are 5-6 pop quizzes throughout the semester. Overall great at teaching but will rarely show sympathy for his students. Pick a good lab partner; you cannot switch or drop them "under any circumstances".
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A small group of us were branch campus that were forced onto Purdue Main's classes online. Deadman sent a TA out to our campus that offered no help, and made the exam prep in person only (we sent one of ours to WL for this and was met with a rushed briefing that he couldn't take pictures of). He did try to help us, but not enough to keep any of us.

If you study and actually devote yourself in to the class, this is the class and the professor who will teach you A LOT! if you still can't pass after 200% of devotion to the class, at that point take the L Womp Womp...

I do not wanna take his class again but I learned so much. Great professor and very knowledgeable. His class demands that you work hard, but the topics are very relevant and helped me a lot for interviews.

Professor Deadman is the goat. He's passionate about teaching and genuinely cares for his students. Don't get me wrong—CNIT 24200 was very time-consuming and the hardest of the CNIT 200-level courses, but I left the class with a strong, fundamental understanding of systems administration.

This class is super difficult. The material is difficult, the grading is stringent, and it requires A LOT of effort just to get a B. That being said, Deadman is a good guy and very helpful, but the class will humble many students. Get a good lab group and you will be fine in the class. Also, make sure to memorize slides for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The type of teacher to drop a quiz during lecture knowing in advance that many people in the class would not be there watching a total solar eclipse. Very passionate for education though. You will suffer, but at least he is clear on what he expects. His TA's are hit or miss.
So far, the best professor I have had at this institution, and it's not really close. His classes require a lot of effort, but will teach you more than any others like them. Pick good lab partner(s).

He is tough but in a good way. Learned more in his two classes I've taken (242 & 344) then any other classes at Purdue. Don't procrastinate in lab, and choose your lab partner(s) wisely, but you'll learn a lot and probably gain a few grey hairs in the process. The TAs are actually knowledgeable and Deadman is also helpful if needed.
Pretty difficult but important class. Deadman is a good professor.

Deadman classes are in a league of their own for students who haven't really learned how to manage time well. Labs are what will get you. Labs take up a lot of time but the TAs, Deadman, other groups, and even Trent are alway willing to help. Show that you are putting in the effort and you will see good results. For exams just memorize the slides!

Positives: Material on exams is the EXACT material gone over in class, as well as the EXACT material listed on the study guide, study that and you will do well on exam. Nice guy.

Negatives: Lab grading standards are extremely harsh, instructions are non-existent, poor lectures, attendance taken on paper in 2022.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While Deadman is notorious for difficult classes, he is one of the most caring professors who actually gives a flying crap if the students learn the materials. His classes are one of the hardest ive ever taken and if you procrastinate labs they can take up to 30+ hours but you will learn what you are doing by the end of it.

Professor Deadman has very high positives and very low negatives.  Positives: funny, makes class enjoyable, willing to help, cares if you learn the material or not.  Negatives: overly strict on lab report criteria, which will make or break your grade.  Class in general is very demanding on your memory for the lecture portion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A true helicopter mom, cares far more about the class running in accordance with her arbitrary unnecessary rules than she does about any student's learning. I suggest only taking a class with prof Zulli if it's required.
really enjoyed this course, Dr. Zulli is so kind and made the material a lot of fun to learn

I enjoyed this class so much - actually decided to minor in Communication 100% because of Dr. Zulli. Her lectures are interactive and interesting, and the material is genuinely interesting to think about. Overall, this was a great course and I hope you have the chance to take it with her.
Tough grader.

I really enjoyed Dr. Zulli's lectures, she makes every class interesting despite what material she's covering. She is a fair grader and makes lectures fun. Definitely go to class, there are random participation activities and it's much easier to do in class than to do the homework.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had at Purdue. Zulli cares about her students, has clear and relevant lectures, and while it isn't a challenging class, I've walked away learning a lot! Can't recommend Dr. Zulli enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zulli was an excellent professor. This class was very useful and she made it very interesting. There are a few major papers that are worth a lot of points, but they aren't terribly hard. If you have questions go to her office hours and ask. The three exams are easy if you take good notes in class and do the assigned reading! She's great!

The teacher is great, however her TA was not. The class is easy, but contains a lot of assignments. There are lots of essays and other activities to do. She makes learning fun and the class is very interesting.
Exams online, participation activities in class for grade but she posts them online for homework for those who miss class but will make the activity way harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE her. She is an amazing professor and makes the class so fun. You need to show up to class and pay attention. Her exams aren't easy, but they are not overly difficult. A great professor who cares about her students and a great class.

I loved COM 253 with Dr. Zulli. The class always went by so fast, even though it was a power hour. If you go to class consistently, you will never have homework outside of the 2 papers because she does homework as in-class activities. Exams are online and open note. Great class, very informative.

Dr. Zulli is amazing. I was unsure if Public Relations was right for me before her course, and she gave me all of the tools I needed to make a confident decision about my major. She gave excellent feedback and was always very accessible. I wish I could have taken a full-length course with her rather than a Maymester!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The first class I had with her was a power hour, but she's the kind of professor that you don't mind listening to for that long. She can make boring info easy to listen to, doesn't ask for too many assignments, and grades tough but very fair. Also a fantastic human.

Excellent professor! I looked forward to class every week. Her lectures and slides were very dense and high-leveled but with her charisma and sense of humor made them fun and engaging. Loved how she would prompt class discussion, she graded hard but gave great feedback and rewards improvement, interesting assignments, all around awesome class.

Honestly, she is one of my favorite professors. Though, her discussion papers are no joke, and highly suggest starting them as soon as she assigns them. You'll thank me later. If you have a problem or circumstance in life or in class, talk to her if you need something. She is really caring about her students and wants the best for you always.
Dr. Zulli is one of the best professors I have had at Purdue. I would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: As a student in a technical major, Dr. Z really helped me to fulfill my com selective requirement. She was a great lecturer who made "going to class" enjoyable. I learned a lot from her lectures and even more from her feedback. She was very accessible and quick to respond with guidance. I would 10/10 recommend and would take another class of hers.
The class wasn't terribly difficult. Her exams were more in-depth than I expected, but after the first one it got easier. All of the assignments outside of the exams were fairly easy as well.
Did not like her one bit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is by far one of the best professors at Purdue! You can tell she really enjoys what she is talking about and makes every lecture interesting. As long as you go to class, pay attention, and study the lecture slides you should get an A!
Lectures were clear. Homework and exams reflected the material covered in class. The workload was reasonable if you stayed on top of the assignments.

I agree with most of these reviews so far. He clearly has a talent for lecturing, however it should be used in a more structured course. Much leeway needs to be given since it is a brand new class. He and TAs were very understanding of our concerns. However, be prepared to WRITE! Overall, great professor and great TA, but class is very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a great dude. CHM 224 was the lightest class ever if you put in effort when it mattered. This class is just graded by exams and lab reports for the most part, and are graded fairly. If you don't agree with your test score you can even have it regraded. Good prof couldn't recommend more.

Jeffrey is a fantastic professor - I really enjoyed the breadth of the lectures, many that were geared to helping us appreciate analytical chemistry and its impact across scientific disciplines. This was a truly exceptional introductory course that every student should take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing class and prof. Time management is a must. I wish this prof taught other courses. TAs were v helpful and always available.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Dick was a passionate lecturer and he kept the lectures entertaining. The labs were intense, but Prof. Dick was willing to listen to students and make changes to the class throughout the semester.

Dr. Dick was a good professor, but it was obvious he didn't particularly want to be there. This is evidenced by the amount of guest lecturers he had in class. Additionally, the lab reports were genuinely the worst thing I've ever done. There was one due every week, and it was to be written from scratch. There are worse classes to take though.

Jeffrey is a very caring professor and it is obvious that he wants his students to succeed. However, this class was a nightmare. I appreciate Jeffrey and his attempt, but it was not planned well enough. Labs didn't work, the write-ups were unnecessary, and the class was essentially intro to electrochemistry. Do not take if not required.

Some leeway has to be given for CHM 224 being a new course, but the labs are BLOATED and the write-ups take a very long time. Jeffrey is a very talented lecturer, but it feels like his talent is wasted on the current curriculum. Exams are take-home and very easy. None of the material is difficult; The hardest part of this class is time management.

reviews.comment: Dr. Dick is the most goated chemistry professor ever. His lectures are incredibly engaging and fun(which is really hard to do considering that the subject is analytical chemistry), and he is really understanding when it comes to anything. We can directly communicate our thoughts about anything, and he would adjust based upon what we said. TLDR;GOAT
Great CFD course. I learned a lot, and I would definitely recommend it.
Very unique experience for someone interested in learning about CFD. This course helped me advance my career in the direction I wanted.
I had to work hard, but it is a great course if your goal is learning
I learned a lot from this course. Highly recommend
I learned a lot in this class. I highly recommend it.
excellent prof
The professor is very thorough and explains things very well
Difficult course, but definitely worth taking if you really want to learn
The professor is a true expert on the topic. I learned a lot in this course.
The professor is able to explain very complicated concepts in a simple way.

This class was a mess. Despite the professor's knowledge, it was poorly organized. Before the first exam, there was no homework or practice test, and lecture notes lacked solved examples, leaving us clueless. Key topics like fast Poisson solver and FEM were skimmed. It lacked coding practice and challenging homework. I wouldn't recommend it.

Teacher provides NO background in class and jumps into coding. No example, skips steps assuming "you know"
Poor response on Weekends for Online Students.
Exams before first homework.
Quizzes programming heavy are timed just in case you are not stressed enough
Poor practice problems are provided without the solutions to verify one's work

RUN :)

The class is very confusing and poorly structure. Also, for an analytical class, there are not enough practice or resources that can get you prepared for the quizzes and exam. Very poor teaching abilities. The material provided is not very useful. Fluids - the main topic of the class, was not learned.

reviews.comment: Dr. Dillman seems like a great guy, but the purpose of this class makes no sense. This class is a massive waste of time, and nothing would change if it did not exist.

Probably the best professor for a CFI course. Easy course, but a lot of work assigned for outside of class that he admitted he really will not look at. He's very busy, often shows up late (most 30+ minutes), and will not respond to emails. Also it's dead week and he hasn't graded a single thing outside of daily attendance which is not helpful.

reviews.comment: The purpose of the course is kinda confusing. He basically lectures about a different part of aviation industry every class and all you have to do is write a brief summary. Lots of life and advice and a really chill and nice guy. Easy course to pass but pretty boring.

I overall still do not understand the purpose of this class. He talks the majority of the time about general life advice for being in aviation which is good but oftentimes he goes on tangents and it becomes confusing. Overall a nice guy though.

The class covers a wide variety of topics within the aviation industry but the assignments that go along with the lectures are very easy to complete as long as you somewhat pay attention to what the topic of the day is. Aside from the weekly assignment, there is very little other work that you need to do for this class.
Pretty funny guy with actual interesting and important lectures. I personally really enjoyed his class. He was also always accesible after class.

reviews.comment: Have not actually met him yet. Took AT1440 online, but he seems like a nice guy. AT1440dis was super easy, just watch the videos on 2x speed and fill out the sheets. And even then the videos are kinda interesting so not a total waste of time.
Brian Dillman is a great professor. He really cares about his students' success and has a lot of experience and knowledge in aviation.

Sometimes class got boring for me since I'm not a flight major. But he tries to keep us entertained. He's very interesting and knows a lot about aviation. He's a really cool guy and the class is not hard at all!
Overall, a pretty laid back and nice professor.
Prof. Dillman did a great job for students not even in flight. He made sure the class was fun for everyone. If you go to class every day you will get an A.

Dillman is a great guy and a great teacher. Being an aviation management major in a class thats mainly for flight students it was pretty boring, but Dillman did his best to keep the rest of us entertained.
Excellent professor!
Dillman is a great guy that really wants you to learn. Very relaxed teaching style but he still gets the material across in a clear way.  Hes the man. End of story!
funny and makes class interresting!
very nice, but boring class. overall very active teacher, and goes whats gonna be on the exam.
Dillman is the Dill-MAN.  Don't bother buying the materials other than the course packet.  He sometimes goes off on tangents but it is still interesting information!

Great professor,keeps class upbeat and tells jokes about airplanes.Always lets us call his cellphone prior to exams for extra help while studying.Inspiring pilot for future or current pilots to look up to
Dillman is awesome. Makes the boring stuff as easy as possible.
he is a cool guy and he can get his points accross pretty easily. he is also pretty funny.

safety meetings are totally boring, but the dillMAN keeps them interesting (as much as possible) and tends to let the upperclassmen not pay attention the whole time...with good reason...if u ACTUALLY have to PAY ATTENTION in these meetings, then i doubt your qualifications to hold a pilot's certificate
Yo yo yo!!! Dillman... rock on.

Dillman rocks, makes more clarity than Gross in the lecture I think.  Incorporates good examples in the lecture and prepares you for the exams.
Grandpa D rules!
