Safty meetings, may seem really boring but really helpful.  Anyone who takes AT seriously should note the importance to show up.
Good teacher, great guy.  Love having him in the aviation department.

The course I took was ancient western medicine and I had to WORK for my B. Very tough grader and values tons of detail. Tests were all made up of 10 short answer questions that had to be answered in 100 words minimum. This course took years off of my life.

If you are interested in Classical Epics, he taught an amazing class. Sync online class, with 10  500 word min papers a semester). He is the reason I'm now minoring in classical studies. I full intend to take pretty much any class he teaches. Highly recommend if you are interested in the topic. If you're not interested in the topic, don't take it.

When I took CLCS 235 I was excited. I had a deep love for Greek mythology and could not wait to learn more. Unfortunately, I was let down during this course. This professor lacked professionalism within his discussion posts and within his grading. Get ready for mindless reading and argumentative discussions as well. I do not recommend this class.

i took two classes with prof dickson (greek religion and roman religion). classes are pretty easy to pass and get a good grade in. the workload is very manageable. he used a textbook but the readings were optional. he's really fun and really nice and very knowledgeable about the classics 100% recommend taking a class with him
Course wasn't difficult, super interesting lectures. Inspired me to minor in Classics

This class was fine nothing special. The exams are kinda difficult if you did not watch the lectures. His essays are pretty self explanatory, kinda rough if you don't know much about greek mythology. Professor answers emails almost instantaneously and gives extensions for certain reasons. The class consists of 7 or 8 quizzes, 4 essays, and 3 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I surprisingly loved this class despite it being my third choice of a CLCS class. Professor Dickson is extremely knowledgeable about pretty much everything, and I always found his lectures to be extremely informative. The essays aren't graded super easily, so make sure to put in some effort and prove that you understand the subject matter.

Despite being online and during Maymester, the material isn't too overwhelming if you watch 3-4 mini-lectures a day. His lectures are also quite funny and not too boring. The grade is composed of quizzes, tests, and discussion posts. You probably need to take notes as his review slides aren't detailed enough for the quizzes/tests.
Not recommend

Taught the material in an engaging and interesting way despite being online. Had all of the lectures posted by the start of the semester with weekly lecture quizzes to keep you on track that were easy points if you've watched the videos. Prompts were clear and gave you more than enough to write about compared to the minimum counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the BEST prof I've ever had. He's engaging with material, responds timely to emails, and his classes are always accessible. Online lectures are pre-recorded, weekly quizzes but they're easy and he provides study sources, he has a decent sense of humor too. If you're a disabled student, you're going to love this professor.

So the mistake I made was underestimating this class because many people said that he was easy - DON'T. I did pretty bad on the tests (there were only 3, and were worth 60% of my grade), so I didn't get the A I wanted. However, the teacher and the class is really interesting and I don't regret taking this class. Really recommend it, do the work lol
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives really engaging lectures that are easy to pay attention to. He has a great storytelling style that makes the material easy to remember. Only grades are exams and quizzes, but theyre fairly easy if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you ask him for accessibility to the full lecture slides, he will probably give them to you. I didn't take too many notes during lecture because if you listen attentively, you will most likely absorb the important stuff. Be sure to review past quiz questions before the exam.

He has very engaging and interesting lectures and keeps the class interesting. He is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, and is accessible outside of class. As someone who only took this class for the culture requirement, I'm actually glad I took it and might take some of his other classes too.
Not a good proffesor when it comes to lectures. Tends to drone on, skips through slides too quickly, powerpoints are not helpful for notes

The dude's tests are exactly what he goes over during class and what are on his online practice tests.  No surprises, no stress.  Studied for all the tests the day of and aced them.  Brilliant teacher who can really hook you into his storytelling narratives during lecture.  Nothing negative about the man.

By far one of the best professors at Purdue. He wants you to learn, not simply absorb and then regurgitate the information. He is INCREDIBLY intelligent, and knows pretty much everything about anything.

I can't give you the perspective of an average student, since the subject matter is of interest to me. So if you dislike mythology, then stay away. I found this professor to be a good speaker. He even made a few jokes from time to time. All in all, I found his class enjoyable and would recommend it for anyone who has an interest in this subject.
Amazing Professor, funny, engaging, and a passionate scholar.
He is funny, engaging, and always willing to help. Both CLCS 233 and 235 were easy as long as you paid attention in lecture. I never even opened my book.

Lecture is mandatory, and pretty boring. You don't need to buy the books, you can find summaries of everything you need on his power points or through google. His tests are hard, but he gives you a study guide so that helps.
Great class! Great professor! Very helpful, lectures stick to exam material. Overall great experience. :)
He is a great professor! Everything u need to know for the exam is on the course website. So u don't have to buy the books. He's very helpful.
He was a great professor. Class is mandatory but interesting. Test are pretty difficult, however.
horrible.  rambles and gives no usable notes to study from.  hate this man.
Class was boring and not interesting at all. I think this is the most stupidest class I have ever taken!

He was a pretty good professor. He spoke clearly, made time for students, and was very interested in what he taught. I didn't really find the class itself horribly interesting, but I'd recommend him without a doubt if you like mythology.

Dickson is a class act. He explains the material well, better than any other professor I have had. If you go to class, listen, and take good notes you will definitely succeed in this class. Also take advantage of office hours, he was very helpful when I went to him with questions. Take this class!
Dickson is my favorite! I also took CLCS 330 with him and I am taking another class of his in the fall. AMAZING!
Very invested and interested. Helpful study guides. Super awesome!
Amazing!
Amazing professor.  Great course. Iloved mythology before and i'm thinking of minoring in classics...that's how much i love it!
Good.
I love this class ("The Epic").  A couple of these lectures have felt truly profound, but almost all are extremely entertaining. Knows his stuff.
Very interesting class. Sometimes he goes off on tangents and note-taking gets hard, but he gives very good study guides and sample questions for all tests.

One of my favorite professors. His mythology classes are AWESOME. Not easy, but awesome. I also had to work on an individual project with him once and he's a really nice guy who's passionate about mythology and it's significance today.
He was soooooo nice and helpful! Very passionate about his class! If you go 2 class and pay attention you will def. get at least a C-B in the class.
He is an awesome teacher and you will love going to class! He is also really helpful!

Dickson is a great teacher. His lectures were fun and clear, with charts and summaries he wrote himself to facilitate understanding of concepts. He knows his subject (mythology) and is a fluid, entertaining speaker. Highly recommended!
Excellent professor, possibly an all time favorite.  This is an extremely fun course, with storytime every day!!!
definitely good teacher! FUN class!

AWESOME teacher!!! He makes the class really fun to go to (outside of the attendence policy). Tests are great: over material covered in class, and he's willing to talk about the material with you. It's obvious he loves his subject! I totally recommend him
Awesome class! He is an great teacher and will help you with whatever you need!  It is also really fun to go to.
The lectures are incredibly long and very boring; they often don't relate to the topics the homework is on, and occur after we have quizzes on the concepts. Quizzes are returned incredibly late.
Very boring, lengthy lectures that often don't have to do with the current homework.

Very unclear expectations. Professor relies on very long slide decks and expects students to know every detail. Rules are vague or only buried in slides, not syllabus. Email instructions often contradict spoken comments—save them. Lectures are dry and especially tough at 7:30 a.m. because she basically reads off of them. Be prepped for blame-game.

Nice person. Teaches in a flipped classroom style, so that pre-lecture assignments teach you all the material. The class time is meant to be for the group work she assigns but she reteaches the material through a lecture for the whole class. Not engaging lectures.

His lectures are impossible to follow along with, and the only reason I was going was for attendance. I feel as though I didn't learn anything from the class. He doesn't answer questions very well either.
He will give you NO sympathy so don't ask for any. Absolutely no late homework. Also lab attendance is worth 3x more than lecture for some reason

MFET 361-In contention for the most boring and useless class of my life. Reads directly off slides with 0 external input. Strict attendance. Long hw and labs. 0 learning in the class, all assignments are semi-completed fill in the blank, 0 way to know if correct unless he mercifully puts a "Sanity Check" comment for what the output should be (rare)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A strange class to take. The entire course material reads like a work instruction from a shop floor with no intention to teach (go to this button - go to that button - click this to do this). Would recommend staying home and just do your excessively long hw from the lecture slides, which btw are on the level of "where is the insert button in word".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Um.... what was this class even? Professor Diao doesn't care about his students much. He doesn't really understand the tech, and the course material teaches us nothing. You're better off reading the lecture slides, and using them to complete the 50 question homeworks (not joking, 50 questions). It's all rote memory. Lectures are useless.

Dr. Dmitrieva was extremely kind and helpful. The class can be difficult if you don't attend and make sure to do the homework. It is very manageable. Dr. Dmitrieva helped me to catch up on quizzes when I could not attend, and I felt like she actually wanted her students to learn and cared about us as individuals. A very caring professor.

You can tell that Dr. Dmitrieva is very passionate about what she teaches. It is clear that she wants her students to gain a better understanding of the content covered in class, as she presents it in a fun and memorable way and allows us to pose questions and/or insights before every lecture. Definitely my favorite class I've ever taken!

Dmitrieva is a funny, sweet lady who is clearly knowledgeable about linguistics. Her lectures are almost entirely in her powerpoints (if you don't want to go to class, I guess you could just read them), but the way she delivers the material is quirky and memorable. She's a fair grader and will work with you if you can't make a deadline.

I thoroughly enjoyed him and his class so much I consider him my favorite professor (I'm only a sophomore though). He cares about students and talks to us as if we are equal. He is helpful and genuinely passionate about his job. He doesn't grade harshly and his lectures are amazingly done as well as interesting. Perfect mix of humor and knowledge

An extra credit assignment at the end of the semester is worth 5% of the exam category, which is great, and I highly recommend completing. Exams are based on textbook material, content covered in lecture, and supplemental reading assignments. As long as you do the work and pay attention during the lecture, the course is not difficult.

Great guy who is passionate about what he teaches. The lectures are him talking about a different topic each day that somewhat relates to the readings (you don't need to do them, but it's helpful). A large part of the class is discussion board posts, but they're easy enough, and so are the quizzes. I would recommend this class for an easy credit.

The previous reviews are quite misleading. Honestly, he was so approachable, and I really enjoyed the class. He took an interest in all of his students and was quite fair with grading. Super nice guy...never seen him pissed off or irritated. Definitely recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Other ratings seem unfair, easily the best class atmosphere compared to other classes this semester. Lectures can become a bit tedious at times for people that don't enjoy reading much, but Professor Dory is extremely knowledgeable and cares about what he does. The oral communication and presentations also boost your confidence a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The reviews previously received are a little misleading. His class can be somewhat monotonous at times though I could be biased because writing and reading is not a passion of mine. He is a very good guy who you can tell cares about the material. Gives plenty of bonus opportunities and Isn't a harsh grader. Doesn't respond too well to emails though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was scared going into this class because I'm not the best at english and all the reviews said he was awful. This honestly is untrue, the class is decently easy and he is a light grader for presentations. The readings are required but interesting for SCLAb. Not talking much in class wont harm your grade. Just know what is happening for the posts.

all the reviews couldnt be farther from the truth, hes the best professor ive had and pretty confident the best I ever will, his personality is just so positive and he was able to handle the most driest non responsive dumb class gracefully we actually felt bad for him
such an unprofessional and unpleasant professor. i have never met a professor that just flat out ghosted me when it came to issues of grading. lectures are long and b

To be honest? He was okay. His lectures are insanely boring and not engaging in the least. Very test heavy, only one midterm, one final, and 4 papers. The article reviews feel like busywork and are seemingly graded according to no real standards. The actual content of the class was interesting but he could have definitely done more with it.

reviews.comment: Had for SCLA 102. As long as you participated in class discussions and did HW (paragraphs on reading) it was fine. The content of the course itself was quite boring. He banned all tech from his classroom, citing privacy.

400 level poli sci professor turns 100 level oral communication class into a 400 level poli sci class

you will learn nothing about oral communication and everything about karl marx

apathetic towards any effort and interest
This guy just shouldn't be here
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Little HW, chill guy, lectures and slides are thorough and explanatory, I'm rockin with him.

Dr. Dory would be a relatively tolerable instructor if his comically inflated sense of self-importance did not make everybody who comes into contact with him feel like a 3rd grader. He's just rude and genuinely disinterested in your success. I'd be terrified to be his graduate assistant.

The bright space is unorganized and he wants you to get SIX books for one semester. He doesn't let you use technology in class so you cant even pirate these online. Do NOT take this class switch out at all costs. 3/3

I spent all of my time trying to understand the difficult readings rather than learning how to present well (the entire point of the class). Right off the the bat I could tell William had a superiority complex. He thinks he's better than all of his students, especially if you are not a business or engineering major. 2/3

Terrible, just terrible. His course assignments were so vague and impossible to know when stuff was due. He constantly treats his students as inferior and makes them feel unwelcomed. I was super excited to take poli sci as an elective and now I hate poli sci as a study, Just stay as far as way as possible from this course.

Don't take his class. Hw load isn't bad but he puts lots of reading on top of pop quizzes. His Brightspace is unorganized and doesn't disclose the exact dates of his exams. Attendance and participation is 10% of final grade but the class is nearly 100 people. And he doesn't want ppl to use phones or devices as if we're still in hs. Stubborn, cocky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Definitely take Dr. Pruim! His lectures were engaging, his assigned projects were fun, and overall I learned so much from his Storytelling with Data course. Incredible at providing feedback and, if you give yourself the time to truly learn the material, very worth it. Take Dr. Pruim if you get the chance!
Such a kind an amazing professor. Always has his students best interests at heart. All around amazing guy, very fortunate to have had him in class
Amazingly structured on brightspace
Was literally a few points away from a 4.0. He would not work with you on additional extra credit. Also takes quite long to reply to emails.

Doug was my absolute favorite part of this semester. He always had a positive attitude during lectures which made me excited to come to class. He made the material very interesting and engaging and tries to connect with all of his students even though it is a decent sized lecture hall. I'm so glad he is teaching this course now, he's the best.

Great professor who cares about his students. The class was extremely tailored to his students (and co-taught by Dr. Strimel who is also awesome). Few homework assignments, no exams, and one class-long project that is purposefully open-ended (they still explain it well) with a chance to win $3000 for it. Part of the Design and Innovation minor too!
The professor is really very helpful. Helps a lot for soft skill building.
Best professor so far in my MBA!! I wish I could take him for every class!

Doug is obviously a good guy, but his class was a little too subjective for my liking. In a class where individuality was promoted, his grading criteria varied day by day. I wish he would have been more honest about how he graded.

Doug is a great professor. He was really down-to-earth, funny, and cared about us as people. He knew everybody's names and was always willing to give feedback. Though the class felt like a waste of time, he taught really well and made it as fun as it could be. He's one of the few professors that genuinely seem like they love their job and it shows.
He really is an amazing educator. When it comes to papers, if he offers you to send it to him early for feedback, take it! You will regret if you don't.

Doug is fantastic.  If you get the chance to take any course with him, I highly recommend it.  He cares about his students and actually tries to connect with them.  He's great at reading people, and if you're not engaged he'll try everything you can to get you excited about whatever it is you're studying.

Awesome Professor, hilarious, and really tries to relate to his students. Today, he took all of us to get coffee before our class and even bought it for us! He is good at explaining things and if you dont understand it, all you have to do is ask and he is happy to help. I look forward to going to his class because its not just a boring lecture

The professor is nice but his class is formatted horribly and they are extremely nit picky about certain details. He requires his own textbook for the class, however in his textbook there are typos and grammatical errors.

Class is overall very easy. If you keep up with the RSS assignments, the project at the end of the semester requires little to no extra work. Lectures can be boring while still covering textbook. Exams are open note and unlimited time on lockdown browser. 

Overall makes class enjoyable and adds humor to make lectures less lame

Lectures in class have a lot of information but are dull. Amy and TA's are harsh graders. No opportunities for extra credit, no leniency in grading/late work. Every homework assignments matters and points are scarce. RSS Night is easy points but not worth as much as it should be. Absolutely have to go to class.

Scott talks too much but pretty good sales info, learned something from RSS. TA's, Scott, and Amy will not be your friends. They grade VERY hard, and you need to take hw/quizzes seriously. Worked my butt off and did not get an A. If this class is not needed, do not take it. You'll be frustrated, because material is simple, but grading is tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Does a great job keeping the class engaged. Class has a decent amount of work but it's actual things you will use in your life. Don't show up late to class, TA's will count you absent if you are late

This class, despite its relevance for sales careers through the RSS project, was my least favorite due to several factors. There's a $140 textbook authored by the professor.  Weekly quizzes are required for the first 8 weeks, with RSS assignments. Downey, lacks control over the class, with more responsibility falling on his assistant, Amy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course was bad. I have never worked so hard and not received an A. The amount of homework is absolutely ridiculous. The project is the equivalent of a full time job. I learned but my mental health was so poor during this class and he did not care at all. I was super sick and in the hospital and marked off for not being in class. Overall tough!

I had to buy his book for the class since not willing to provide a free ebook or discounted textbook. Got to say the textbook is the worst one I've ever seen. The notation and format are so messy. Not to mention, it is basically impossible to pinpoint keywords from the quiz question because there's no breakdown, pause, or subtitle in the textbook.

I absolutely loved this class because its the first thing I've learned that I Know I will use in my career. Homework is due twice and week and DON'T PROCRASTINATE It. The final project can be intimidating but utilized your TAs. Mine practiced with me 2 or 3 times and I end up doing super well. Class finishes 2 weeks before finals week:)

This is the first class I have EVER taken that I will undoubtedly use in my career. Dr. Downey is SO INTERESTING, the material is easy to understand, yet interesting and a good grade is not hard to come by. 10/10 would recommend business majors to take ACECON 331, he will not disappoint.
Dr. Downey is the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures drag on forever. I hated going to this class every day. He really makes an interesting subject seem boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Scott was very knowledgeable and his lectures were very useful and applicable to the sales career. I will definitely use what I learned during his class in my future. His projects may seem intimidating, but dig in and work hard at them because they are designed to get you out of your comfort zone and push yourself.

Eh. This class was mostly busy work, but it is an easy A if you do everything assigned. I learned a lot from the homework, but almost nothing from the class itself. They expect us to put time into the class, and yet they couldn't even check the quizzes for errors and spelling mistakes. Not impressed with him as a professor.

Great class even for those who aren't in agribusiness. It's mostly a sales class. If you work for it, you'll get an A. Downy may seem hard, but he knows what he is doing. He's informative, but he's a little strict.

The whole class is preparation for a night that you take a product you have been researching and you "sell it" to a professional salesman! It was intimidating at first, but if you take it one homework at a time, it is super easy! The sales night is intimidating too, but they find nice salesmen that give you advice and make it a comfortable setting.
There's a lot of homework, but it's not busy work - it's homework that prepares you for the final project.

This class is nothing but busy work.  I could barely keep my eyes open during his lecture.  He talks too much about himself which to me is a waste of my time.  This class is really easy but a pain in the ass.

My least favorite class I have ever taken.  So boring and all the information taught is useless.  The homework consumes too much time and is all busy work.  Literally just a class full of busy work. Easy to get a good grade but not worth the time that must be put in.

This class is an easy A. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are pop quizzes that are a quick way to bring up your grade. The tests are online and that was the only time I ever used the book. Overall just a boring class if you aren't interested in selling agricultural products. Dr. Downey is is very nice and reasonable.
Great professor, Interesting if you enjoy sales. Great guy outside of class as well. lots of homework but not too time consuming. plan your semester well and you can get an A pretty easily.

Good guy, boring teacher. HW is basically busy work (easy) but lots of assignments. The most helpful part of the class is the mock sale you perform at the end of the course. Easy A or B if you do all the assignments and go to class.

He is a great professor and if you make attmept to talk to him he will gEt to know you. He is really nice and cares about students. He also will provide you with great network oppurtuities if you make an effort in the class. The cLass is very helpful for the realworld.
Not a good teacher, decided to change my major from selling after this class.  It was easy, he was just not good.

Great guy, he really knows what he is talking about and he's actually a nice guy if you sit down and talk to him. Interesting for those in sales, probably boring for other majors. (I'm a major in sales of course...)
rss was super useful and hands on but its a bunch of busy work. and downy is a prick. his class is so boring and you learn nothing. at all.

THe project is annoying throughout the semester, but in the end it was worth while and you get a lot of useful experience. However, class time is extremely boring but you get a grade for attendance plus there are pop quizzes so it helps to go. The teacher came off arrogant to me, but overall the class is easy if you do the work

Class was decent, and project gave some useful experience.  He was completely useless, felt like he was trying to sell me things the whole time not actually teaching me anything. Had an inflated opinion of himself, to say the least.
DECENT TEACHER, I WAS MORE INTERESTED IN THE CLASS ITSELF.  LEARNED A LOT IN LECTURES, THE PROJECT.  HE GETS AN ATTITUDE EASILY, BUT OTHER THAN THAT HE DOES WELL.
Learned a lot from the RSS project.
This was an easy class, but the attendence policy sucked majorly. The lectures are boring but the RSS and SWAS projects were great 'hands on' experiences.
This class has so much real-world relevance, and he makes it fun.  The RSS projects are a pain, but they are great stepping stones for those interested in sales.
Grading system at Purdue is 90 and above is an a. He had it where a 92.5 and above was an A. Hmm. Shady!
No Comments
Great class and Dr. Downey makes it enjoyable. It seems overwhelming at first, but it is one of the best classes I have ever taken at Purdue.

He's a funny and kind guy. The test are hard but he does give you the question before hand. The questions are out of a bank of about 450 though. It's an extremely hard class. Free response are easy if you pay attention but you will never know what he'll throw on their do you gotta memorize it all.

Dr. Pappas is very kind and actually really funny when you go to class. However, there were not a ton of opportunities to earn points. His MCQs on exams are given ahead of time and he will pick a certain amount to show up on exams. Short answers are impossible though...Try to do well in lab if you struggle in lecture, that's about to save my grade.

Dr. Pappas is a great professor who clearly enjoys what he teaches. Provides practice multiple choice questions you can use to practice/memorize before exams as he will reuse those same questions, and free response questions are based off his learning objectives. This made the course significantly easier to study for.

Dr. Pappas is a great person and lecturer. He keeps the lectures entertaining and makes the topics exciting! Would absolutely take another class with him, however, the exams are very difficult. He gives you everything you need, but that means memorizing 400+ questions. The open-ended is quite difficult, too. Study at least 2 weeks in advanced.

TAKE IT ELSEWHERE!!! Do not waste your time, money, and effort with him!! He is such a lousy professor because he truly does not care. He gives you 400 MC questions to memorize for each exam which if you get them all right you get a C on the exam. The free response are so hard that you don't have time/ can't guess what he will he throw on there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He says on the first day that this class is a weed out class. He is a lazy and terrible professor who does not care about us learning anything. Take it anywhere else but here!! Do not put yourself thru misery! Your grade is based off the exams and if you don't do too hot on the exams- good luck. You memorize 400 MC questions to just get a 70%
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally loved Professor Gray, he's clearly young and learning the ropes, but he cares so much about the class. Great professor and decent classwork, be careful of the small things for sure!

Mid. Engr131 is a dogwork class anyways. He just kinda does his little lecture which is short. He answers questions okay. Sometimes he doesn't know what's on exam/what he's talking about but mostly he's in top of it. Why does this bs class need to be 2 hours? We'll never know
Professor Gray was my favorite professor this semester. He truly cared about me and my fellow students and our learning and I enjoyed his lectures.

Professor Yarger is honestly one of the best stat professors I've had at Purdue. He's really good at breaking stat theory down to plain english, and bringing in a conceptual layer where it would seem otherwise impossible. He's also pretty lively during lectures, promotes asking questions and really does not let it get boring in class.
Good prof, typically makes sense but idk much after the midterm and still got an A.

A large portion of the material I'd finally understand after looking up how to do it while attempting the homework, rather than understanding during lecture. He would often explain some of the simple concepts quite thoroughly while breezing past the difficult concepts, especially near the end of semester. Not a bad professor, but I'd prefer others.

Midterm worth 20% , final 20% and homework 45%. His midterm was like the practice midterm. He has a fun personality and is a chill guy. Topics can be confusing. Homework consists of 5-6 problems. Only 7 homeworks all semester, lowest one dropped. Not a tough grader. He is the only reason I actually went to class.

He is a great guy. very helpful in office hours. lectures are a little messy but you can self learn most of the topics. the grade breakdown was 60% homework and 40% exams. should be very easy to pass. exams are like the practice exam. hes such a chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Drown was great, although I only had him for the first few weeks of the semester. He makes sure to engage with his students during lecture and there are plenty of (mandatory) iClicker questions to ensure you understand the material. His tests were reflective of the material and were sometimes tough but fair.

This class was a difficult class and Dr. Drown would gloss over some of the topics, but overall the class went well. Drown teaches well and makes it easier to understand. I recommend going to the SI sessions and office hours. The book was not helpful.

Drown did a good job explaining the concepts and provided relevant examples to study. The course does cover a lot of content quickly, but Drown has no control over that. My key to succeeding was understanding the recitations and studying a few days before exams.

Organic chemistry is not easy but Dr. Drown did well explaining material. He was very accessible outside of class and encouraged questions. Of course the class moved fast, but Dr. Drown has no control of that.

Dr. Drown is easily accessible outside of class and will host extra office hours for students who are struggling. The class moves fast, but that's the nature of the beast that is organic chemistry. He is kind and approachable, which isn't something you can say about other faculty members in the department.

Lectures move very quickly, and leave very little room for questions. When asked questions little clarification is given- definitely plan on utilizing every office hours and SI sessions is you want a good grade.

Lectures provided plenty of examples and served as reference material in themselves; intentional in ensuring that notes remained as conducive to learning as possible. Receptive to feedback and exam averages; curved the third exam after averages dipped down. Excellent professor overall, and even better considering that this was his first year.
Attendance was mandatory every week. Assignments were graded unnecessarily hard, but the 30 pts extra credit makeup for any missed points. Just a bit more work than a 1-credit hour class warrants.

He took the 1 credit sophomore seminar class (280) wayyyy too seriously. Had mandatory class the Monday of Thanksgiving break, still expecting everyone to show up. He seems like a nice person, but needs to chill.

This was an experimental class, part of the professor's own research, and that was definitely felt. Clear emphasis on being student-led rather than professor-led, which isn't always a bad thing, but usually just felt disorganized. Class itself was pretty interesting and taught me a lot. I just wish it had been structured differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor takes notes in class but doesn't seem to really take in the feedback for the notes he writes down. He always has criticism. I find the course content to not reflect what I thought was the main purpose for the course. Says he's open to questions and able to help, but, when asked, sounds frustrated. Does not stand by what he says.

Professor Andrew Brightman asked my class to pretend to be "severely" disabled, video it, and upload it to YouTube as part of a HW. After class outcry he made the video optional, but not before retaliating against me and other students who raised the issue. Forgets details about his own writings. Homework often does not reflect course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took the summer online course on Regulatory Compliance. The professor changed halfway through the semester, it was super disorganized, there was no clear grading criteria for the essay. The prerecorded lectures from last year were used, which was ok, but none of the assignments/dates were the same. Assignments and quizzes announced the due date.
Worthless Class, Worthless assignments, Worthless, worthless, worthless.  Really don't bother with it.
Terrible professor. Worst I've had.
Worthless, the class and the professor.
Awful 1 credit hour seminar class.
disorganised class, assignments are tedious and the deadlines and requirements are never as initially given.  more work than a one credit seminar class should be.

Great EPICS professor who cares a lot about the students and the EPICS projects. He's always willing to help and looks out for students' well being, which lots of other professors don't do, and he often gives great feedback for presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet and caring professor.

Andrew is the best! I've had him as my EPICS professor for 3 semesters, going on 4 in the spring. He genuinely cares about his students, wants them to succeed, and will support them in anyway that he can. He is very serious about class participation though, and doesn't like when students aren't actively doing work during lab. Chill, funny, good guy
English king von

Prof. Davis' teachings never follow any straightforward path. He often spends tens of minutes on tangents. Attendance is not taken, participation is sometimes tracked (seemingly randomly).

He is a very nice person, and he genuinely cares about his students. He gives good feedback on your performance.

The class is graded by "attendance and participation" points, but he doesn't take attendance and only grades you based on how much you speak in class. On top of that, half of the class is typically used for speeches or him talking about random experiences in his past so there is not much time to get those participation points. Tough grader as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Huge part of our grade was participation but he inconsistently marks you down for it. Rambles about unrelated things and turns the class into a philosophy class. He also has a condescending tone and looks down on you if he doesn't agree with what you say. Constantly praises his structure of the class when there is no clear structure to begin with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He spends most classes talking, not allowing many students to participate even though it is a large part of the grade. He is very full of himself, and grades very hard for an intro level class. If you get him you should switch out, as other professors in this course are much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall a fine lecturer. He previously was an upper level Philo professor at UNC and as a result believes that he should throw the book at every undergrad attempting to pass his class. He does not provide rubrics for work or feedback other than scribbles that even he admits are "needing translation". I would strongly urge avoiding his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'll note it's his first year teaching at Purdue. We were graded on few assignments and only one rubric was posted. Grades were not posted until mid December. I feel as if my speech improvement was not recognized or reflected in my grades. Each class felt like a battle against to get my participation points because he calls on the same students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take his courses, or switch professors. He has no consistency in his grading, and used to be a high level philosophy professor at his old school so he's incredible difficult and a tough grader. He heavily encourages office hours, but he low-key deducts your grades if you don't go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely harsh grader.
I genuinely did not learn a single thing but I do know that I dropped a bag on the mandatory textbook AND an additional software. The class was just annoying

Laura Downey has been the first Purdue professor to make me question whether or not choosing higher education was something beneficial to me. I have done nothing to question my intelligence whilst completing work that I have not been prepared for in any way, shape, or form. Technologically incapable, and the lectures were blunt. Seems unprepared.

Horrible lecturer. Will not give direct answers to questions. Students are required to buy/use multiple software programs to complete homework assignments. Exams are proctored and are not directly taken from text, lectures, or homework.
She legitimately just read the slides and cannot teach. She gives no exam preparation whatsoever and just expects you to know how to do everything from the beginning. This course is so disorganized.

Avoid this class. She is so unorganized; half the time, you cannot find the assignments, due dates are mixed up all throughout Brightspace, and you never know what your overall grade is. She is also unhelpful when answering questions and quite condescending. The content itself is not difficult, but the class was terrible.

She seems uninterested in what she's teaching and is very hard to pay attention to. A lot of unnecessary busywork in and out of class. Assignment due dates were also extremely unclear and the instructions for each assignment were not enough for the students to craft responses that she would give higher grades to. Super strict on attendance too.
the class is set up so poorly and she is very technologically incompetent.
It's not a hard class at all, but it's very poorly structured. And when asking questions about the content, professor doesn't know how to answer, so most of the time questions go unanswered.

Instructions were unclear while working through simulations and when our group asked for help she gave unclear answers that didn't help. She grades harsh and when we asked for feedback, she responded with the smallest details as to why we got a low grade. Definitely go to office hours to get extra help because you'll need it!

I went through this semester pretty confident I would receive and A and low and behold right after course evaluations come out she then puts 500 points of assignments into the gradebook with harsh grading and very little feedback. When our group asked the professor about the assignment, the TA responded to our email and was rude.

I thought the lectures were clear, some of the assignments felt like busy-work, and she would mark points off but only give feedback that said "Well done!". However, material was not hard and I ended up with an A. Go to class, review somewhat for exams, follow the role play rubrics and you should be fine.

Similar to everyone else's reviews, I thought I was going to end up with an A and then she gave my group a 50% on our PharmaSim assignment and a 73% on our group project. After following up and asking many questions about why we received such a low grade, we got a rude email back from her TA. I would not recommend this class!

I would say many of the claims about a ridiculous amount of work for a very little amount of learning ring true. It's not a particularly hard course, the exams are annoying since there is no study material provided. Participation is scored subjectively, you could go to every class and participate in everything and not get the full score. Don't take

The professor grades harsh for a class that is easy and common sense. Says that 40% should obtain A's but then marks off on the most unnecessary marks I have ever seen to prevent this percentage. Does not give helpful feedback and randomly takes off points for being in her words "awful."

Overall, this class tricks you into thinking you are going to end with an easy A. I got great grades on the papers and individual stuff, but PharmaSim is truly the deciphering factor. Went from a 93% in the class up until the last week where she adjust the grades. Now it looks like a B. Very irritating, poor explanation for assignments, etc
Compared to every other MGMT 324 teacher her class is wildly more work. Take any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is mostly busy work. Almost nobody pays attention during lectures. On top of that, participation is 15% of your grade which is annoying because even if you show up to class and do the group case studies, she will still give a bad participation grade. Not to mention for, exams there are few helpful resources to help prepare that exist.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Downey is very kind and clearly cares about her students and the course material. Her marketing management class is way harder than any other because she assigns significantly more work than any other professor that teaches the course. She's very kind and I like her as a person, but I recommend taking the class with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you take this class be prepared to do a lot of group projects. It's not exactly hard just so annoying, especially for a summer class. It's not hard work just a lot of busy work, you use connect for all the assignments. No lectures just reading the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Since the class is new she asked us for insight about the class often. She knows what she's talking about when it comes to sales, homework was not bad at all. This class is very assignment heavy, stay on top of due dates. The only complaint I have is that grading is slow for this class. Professor Downey is amazing and tried to know us personally!
lots of work required and you probably won't learn much

The due dates are not clear at all. You will spend most of your time finding your assignments and their due date. Attendance is mandatory. Going to class is a waste of time since everything she taught is nothing more than your textbook. Please don't take this one if you have other options.

You will spend more time trying to find your homework than you will actually doing it. Insane amounts of busywork from three different sources (connect, marketshare, and Brightspace) and you will know when nothing is due. Received a rather confrontational email from Laura when I failed to complete one of the assignments on time.

Everything she says in class is already posted online. Tons of assignments every week with unclear due dates & messy scheduling. Material itself is not hard whatsoever, but the way she teaches makes it so painful. ~$110 for online textbook & HW access, no alternative option. If given the chance to take this class with a different prof, jump on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible. You will know when nothing is due or what you doing.

reviews.comment: Professor Downey assigns way too much busywork for a class like marketing. Attendance is required and group activities are typical, although they usually do not teach much. You teach yourself the class using Connect, and then attend lectures to hear that same information all over again in a less meaningful way.

This class was awful. It was the first in-person class I had after Covid and made me wish I had stayed online for the semester. So much work. The professor claims that she takes attendance for credit but theres no way to see that at the end of the semester. Lots of projects with the groups assigned based on seating chart.

This has been one of the worst classes I have taken. There is an overkill amount of work that most feels to no benefit of learning. My group ran into many issues with her either not responding to us or scoffing off our concerns. I have never had a professor here that made me feel they didn't care about us students but she has made me feel that way.

I was really nervous about this class due to these ratings, but it wasnt bad at all. As long as you keep track of due dates and stay on top of everything, the course very manageable. Professor Downey was great and wanted to help you succeed. She gave good guidance with the MarketShare simulation and was very responsive to emails.

As of fall 2020, this course is joke. This professor makes you pay in order to do homework, presentations and that simulation software that is absolutely useless and a money grabber. The hardest part about this course is navigating through the mess of tabs and assignments to figure what has to be done. You will learn nothing in this course.
She is extremely unorganized and does not have clear criteria. Would never take her class again.

Worst professor I have ever had. She is late to put in grades always so you never know what you have in the class. Blackboard is like a maze, extremely confusing which can cause you to miss deadlines for homework assignments. She only responds to emails if it's a simple question, if it's something complex forget about her emailing back. Terrible.

Class has way too much busy work. She uses resources A-Z in MGMT 323 to try and give students options to learn when it just makes everything more complicated. Unresponsive by email, reads straight off her lecture slides which are copy and pasted form the textbook. She has no original content.

Blackboard seems confusing basically all of the time. Lectures are boring. Feels like you haven't learned anything once you get on the exam. Marketshare is confusing. The only good part about this class is the group presentation/video if you get a good group. Good luck.

Seriously the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't teach one thing but expect you to apply things she won't teach you. Also you will not know your grade until she submits them so there is NO WAY to gage how you are doing in the class. I do not understand how someone can care this little about their job. All I have to say is good luck.

Good luck getting in contact with her if you need something. You can teach yourself this course if you just do the homework and practice quizzes. You will get random days off in class and due dates will be moved all over the place without warning.
Seems as though she actively tries to make the Blackboard page as confusing as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took this online and it was easy but annoying. MarketShare sucks, it was totally unnecessary. Coordinating with group members in different timezones just to do the marketing simulation was dumb. But the case presentation was easy, and the exams are pretty easy as long as you study the book well.

I have had continual issues trying to communicate with her outside of the classroom. She also stood us up during our online presentation. 18 people, 3 groups of 6, waited for her to join the online classroom presentation site we had to be on FOR AN HOUR. She never showed up, never sent an apology or email about her absence. She merely rescheduled.
too much homework

As long as you read the textbook every now and then, getting an A is easy peasy.  But if you ever have regrade requests or any other questions that you ask outside of class or by email, she likely won't bother to help or reply.

This class was sooooooooo easy. I did all of the online assignments the first week of class and then did not have to worry about them again. The lectures are super boring.  I could just feel the life being drained from my body. You'll get an A if you do the work, but good luck staying awake.
Very unhelpful professor. Will not make any accommodations for anything, even if there is no reason not too. Mediocre lecturer, not too hard of a class, but very unsympathetic and stubborn.

Prof. Downey requires online students to go to Purdue to take the midterms, or find an approved proctor on their own (approvedsatisfies many unreasonable criteria). She also scheduled a midterm for the weekend of July 4th, and refused to make accommodations for students that were leaving town that weekend. Her lectures are monotone and drawn out.

You cannot argue with her. She has her ways of grading you don't understand and she won't change. The exam is insanely difficult. You need to go through every little detail on textbook to ace on the exam and our average score is 60%. She won't cover everything on the lecture. You need to read the textbook to ace the exam.

I read all of these reviews before I took the class for my MGMT minor and was nervous this class was going to be my worst one yet. Total opposite, the class is pretty easy the homework is all online, and exams can be aced if you study vocab from the text. She cancelled class most days (TH @ 4:30) and let us out early pretty frequently. I recommend!

I felt I got a lot out of this class, as it made me think about marketing in a completely different way. I was very successful in this course, and I think that other people can too, with any effort. The instructor is very nice, just be sure to approach her in person instead of via email.

This professor is by far the absolute WORST professor I have EVER had at Purdue! I have emailed her 7 times over the course of the semester and HAVE NOT once received a reply from her. She is irresponsible and rude. I've emailed the TA twice this semester and he has NEVER emailed me back either. I just don't understand this lady.

She will over emphasize the textbook and say it is necessary to ready. Just study the power point slides on the homework website (they're a little hard to find) and know the key terms and some of the extra information. The class is curved as well. I got 90+ on all the exams using the slides and the average was around 75. Also, do the homework.

Laura is extremely cool. I just chose the self-study option, that way no class, no boredom. there are 8 mandatory classes or so the entire semester, and if u end up at the top of the marketing simulation game u get candyyy
Her lectures are extremly boring.  She has a mono-tone voice as she reads off the material.  Definate snooze fest and did not learn much at all.
Terrible teacher, clueless on how to use technology despite being a apple isheep.  Can't get enough of her iPad and doesn't even know how to turn it on.

She is very clueless in the subject she teaches. She never knows how to open her powerpoint so it usually takes upto 15mins of class.  SHe doesn't know how to use mymktlab. And overall,she sucks.  You don't even need to pay attention in class.  All you need to do is read the powerpoints and take the practice test on mymktlab.com

Dr. Downey doesn't seem very interested in marketing. She is not meant to be a lecturer, her nerves always seem to get the best of her. Her explanations aren't clear and she usually only repeats what students have already said about the cases we read. She should go back and review the course textbook because she doesn't seem to know very much.
Learned nothing.
This class is so hard. She doesn't teach at all! Two exams each cover one half of the book. Very predictable and she is so boring.
She is dumb.  The class is dumb.  Useless, boring overall.  I didn't learn anything.  It was somewhat difficult.

I found Laura to be a nice enough person. Lectures were boring though and involved mindless reviewing of PowerPoint slides. Reading the textbook is a must for exams. The Marketing Game activity at the end of the semester was the highlight of the semester; though overwhelming at first, I quickly became engrossed with it.
Horrible class. Very difficult.  Exams cover over 300 pages of in-depth reading each.  Hard grading.  Teach it yourself class.  Everyday is same routine, reading of power point slides.

Class time is dedicated to discussing a case study or taking quizzes/exams. Book chapters are long and quizzes/exams are very in-depth. This is not an easy class because the material just isn't covered during class time. This is basically a "teach yourself" course. She does take attendance every period, so going to class is necessary.

She is a mean, mean woman.  She kept everyone after class for like 20 mins one day and complained about it the whole time.  This class is stupid in my opinion and she is a very rude, self-centered woman who thinks that social guidelines don't apply to her.  Or at least she doesn't have to show respect to her students.  DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!

class was decent. TAs for labs and recitation are easy graders. make sure u know the material bc the tests are mostly just conceptual. challenge problems are sometimes interesting and sometimes just busywork depending on what u r interested in. don't take this course if u aren't all that interested in physics, especially with the challenge problems

Reverse classroom!! Tests are extremely concept heavy with little to no computation questions. Boilerexams help, but concepts should be studied as a supplement. The TAs were very easy graders, but the tests are from hell because of the low question count. Challenge problems are fun and labs are basically participation. Homework is difficult though.

reviews.comment: Teaches via iClicker. Told us first day of class that he would not be teaching during lectures, and he didn't... kinda. Challenge Problem assignments are fun, but mostly just busy work. If you can learn by yourself, this is an easy class. But if not...you're kinda screwed.
Be ready to fully rely on yourself and learn from all the reading assignments. Prof. Durbin is gonna ask you some questions, sometimes it can be deep and interesting, instead of "teaching" you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I actually could not get why his lectures exist if it covers 3% of what the textbook is going to show you. The weekly Homework problems are nothing to what the text book proffesors teach you. So, professor doesnt teach what's on the textbook, textbook doesnt prepare you for the homework, homework does not prepare you for test! DO NOT TAKE HIM PLEAS

Dr. Durbin and this class are about what you expect from a physics class. The lectures are dry but informative, and the assignments/exams feel like an accurate and fair reflection of the learning goals. This is a little disappointing for a class on a topic as interesting as quantum mechanics, but mechanics classes are typically quite boring.

He gets students to build their own study skills. Doesn't lecture, gets students to read textbook before class. good for independent learning styles

Few attempts on homework! Work with other students.
He's a very chill guy to talk to during office hours.
His challenge problems fascinating as a physics major; takes a lot of time.
He's a good teacher to be honest.

Durbin doesn't actually lecture in class, he just does problem solving in clicker questions. Whether you prefer that or not depends on you, but you learn all of the content from the mandatory textbook readings. He's nice in office hours and will sit down and help you but he feels very disorganized and is not always clear in his directions.

reviews.comment:
Yes, he "lectures" differently. I would've been more open to his type of teaching if he did it more effectively, but he didn't. We normally ran out of time before he could go through answers, or he wouldn't know the right answer himself.

The only good thing I will say is he is helpful during office hours and does encourage us to talk to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
On the flipped style of the class: He does not "teach" in lecture like normal. Instead you do reading assignments in-between lecture, then practice in lecture. I liked this style.

He is easy to access outside class. If you talk to him don't be surprised if he pushes back on an idea of yours. He isn't being rude, he is just thinking critically.
He does not teach.

Besides wiley plus homework, he has clicker questions in class. Also, there is a bi-weekly challenge problem, which is much harder than the homework, and often takes me up to 5 hours to complete a challenge problem. But it is my favorite class so far. The challenge problems gave me significant feedback on my logic and physics skills.

I actually loved Durbin's lecture style. You have to read the textbook before class and he will give you problems to solve in lecture so you can learn by doing, which I loved. This course is tough, and it could maybe be a 5-6 credit class for how much work it is (seriously), but I found it very rewarding and he gave a monster curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful start to my university life. Doesn't teach at all, just gives tons of iClicker questions, homework is awfully structured. do not recommend.

Attendance and reading the textbooks were both musts for this class. Durbin does not really lecture. Instead, he puts up a ton of iClicker and whiteboard questions that students work on with others in their assigned seats. When students ask questions he tends to go on tangents about other things and never answers the original question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives study guides and practice questions for essential topics but then refused to give us answers. He was only helpful during office hours giving one-on-one lessons. Read the textbook, don't rely on lectures. Work with other students, teach each other. Exam study: review textbook, concept focus, understand lecture & homework questions. WORK HARD!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was really helpful during office hours and really made an effort to help you understand something if you were struggling. The way he approached teaching the class was that he would assign a couple of chapters beforehand, and we would have to read them and answer reading essays - I found that quite helpful in learning how to study independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, he really enjoyed engaging with students and seeing how they worked through problems. His lectures were just review of textbook chapters, all learning was done through homework, which involved mainly just reading the textbook.
Absolutely amazing professor. Would not be able to pass the class if not for his ability to relate and teach at the level that he does.

This class is an absolute trainwreck. Durbin just kind of reads off of powerpoints that he found online. He doesn't even permit the TAs to give answers or how to even do any of the problems! If you really need to take this class, avoid taking it with Durbin. Hopefully he gets replaced by a professor that actually knows how to teach a class.
He does not teach the students at all, I would avoid if you havent taken a physics course before or take it the next semester.

reviews.comment: I have never worked so incredibly hard for such bad results. This class leaves students, particularly Pre-Meds completely lost in a subject they need to learn in order to succeed in future careers. Students are cheated out of a good education. reviews.comment: He doesnt teach in lecture. Instead, you do senseless whiteboard problems without being taught first how to do the type of problem. He barely explains anything. The HW and everything else is never taught in class. Youre basically on youre own.

reviews.comment: I didn't realize I was taking a physics class until halfway into the semester. Oh yea and I almost went blind tracking beads in lab but i guess it was worth it

He uses all of Maryland's material. I don't even think he looks at his slides before he comes to class. We are never given a straight answer, even when we do clicker questions. We spend the whole class going through one useless whiteboard problem that does not correlate to the exam material.

His lecture style is completely unorganized and large portions of the class time were wasted on white board problems that were not helpful and he didn't even answer them. Every guest lecturer we had taught better.
He's so horrible and non-specific in lecture, I'm not entirely sure he's ever given a straight answer.

In a subject so rarely taken before by life science majors, the best idea was to make not only a rigorous class in a never before seen subject, but add in a FLIPPED LECTURE. With only tedious reading assignments, confusing labs, and nothing but a an example and a quiz in lecture, this class will have you crying to your adviser.

reviews.comment: This class wasn't that hard, but it's a 100-level class. However, he is not a great teacher, and frankly, he's plain rude and sometime borderline abusive to students and staff. His attitude made me uncomfortable, and unapproachable. Would not take a course from him again.

One of the worst professors that I have ever had at Purdue. Questions and examples done in class are never given a clear answer. There is not enough time on exams. The recitation is extremely difficult. Questions on exams and equations needed are never even hinted at in class.
AFWUL TEACHER!

Gets all material from the University of Maryland, even notes. He doesn't teach. You are assigned readings online. There is no textbook. You go to lecture and he asks you questions that you work in a group with. He doesn't give a clear answer to the questions. There is not enough time for labs and they are very difficult. He is very rude/ unhelpful
Durbin assumes that you have read the chapter before class (not realistic due to the size of the reading assignments) and teaches like you already have mastered the material.
The class is really based off of recitation and reading, not lectures. Durbin's demonstrations were good. He left a lot of clicker questions unanswered unfortunately leaving the class puzzled.

This class is extremely easy, the most easiest A I ever got! Durbin is nice, class has iclicker questions. Exams are easy. Durbin always forget to point out the answer to the on-class question after explaining a lot about it! The explaining is not so clear sometimes:(, but overall is a pretty easy physics class after all, very light load.

Really nice guy and is helpful if you go to office hours, but one of the toughest classes I've ever taken. This course has changed a lot since when it first started. The department is trying to think of ways to lower the number students failing it. The more time you devote to this class, the better!
Pretty good, but I've had better.  Tests are fairly easy.  He posts the tests from last semester, they are very helpful.
Excellent demonstrations

Overall a pretty decent teacher, but I've had better. Uses a lot of visual aid, which is helpful. Right now PHYS172 is a new course, and theyre working out the kinks so its difficulty constantly changes.
Overall fairly straighforward

Durbin cannot teach worth a dime.  Don't get me wrong, I have nothing against him personally, and he is an extremely intelligent guy, but he couldn't teach a wheel to roll.  He demonstrates nothing of academic value in his lectures - thank God for the recitations...  On the bright side of things, his test are usually ridiculously easy.
Very Good Professor

Durbin was great.  He really made me enjoy physics.  What was hilarious, though, was when he taught collisions.  He banged two bowling balls together to display it.  After the demonstration, he told the class "Let me show you two more balls".  I haven't stopped laughing since. Great. Teacher.

He is an awesome guy.  I am very glad that he is teaching this class.  He keeps the subject interesting even though the class is difficult.  He definately enjoys his job and has a good sense of humor.  I recommend him.
I like all of the examples that he uses in his lectures.  He also seems to enjoy what he is doing as well.  I am glad that I am a semester behind!
This guy knows his Physics, explains it in a very clear fashion, and sounds like he actually enjoys what he's teaching. And he added one extra try in CHIP. Need I say more?

We didn't do much in class and most learning came from outside of class application to VIP. He was always kind of out of the loop with our projects and made some suggestions that personally wouldn't have have given. 

If you just do the class assignments you will be fine honestly.
He has lots of fluff work but it comes out helping a lot. Super nice guy and always made time to check in on each group. I would def take his class again.
Amazing and understanding
Lots of opportunities to get points. Group project throughout the whole semester. Easy if you do the work. Do not forget about the journal entries, those are the easiest to forget about.
Love Professor Dunlop! His class was easy and he was really nice. I'd take TLI213 again just to be with him- and I absolutely hate TLI classes!

He is super nice. The class itself is just a lot of busy work and he doesn't know how to use Brightspace so that can be confusing. But overall the class is easy and he's super lenient with assignments and grading.

Professor Dunlop is a little behind in technology, but he answers emails very fast.  Classes are boring, and the class has extremely easy exams.  The course project is about 100 pages of information when done, and it builds a business, which is relevant to entrepreneurship, but can also be dry.

reviews.comment: Professor Dunlop is one of the best professors I have had at Purdue. TLI 213 requires work in one group project over the semester, which allows you to know your team and the professor very well. If you're struggling, it is easy for him to notice through peer reviews, and he will often reach out to check in on you. Would take his class again anyday.
Great Lectures, Easy to comprehend, Fun to learn...

Professor Vincent Duffy is an outstanding instructor who explains complex human factors concepts with clarity and real-world relevance. His engaging teaching style and strong industry perspective make the course both intellectually rigorous and highly practical.
Great prof
Professor Duffy is a good professor. His courses are going to have a lot of homework every week so you need to take care of the deadlines. I would recommend students to his courses.

reviews.comment: Good for credit.
Awesome Professor, gives you plenty of chances to correct mistakes and gain extra points.

reviews.comment: I liked this course.

reviews.comment: Professor Duffy is very nice and cares about the success of his students. However, the course layout was confusing and somewhat disorganized.
The course is easy and the professor is great
I have already taken 2 subjects under prof. Duffy. I love his teaching style and the interesting assignments he gives us.
Class is interesting, but Brightspace and Packback are not very well organized

Professor Duffy aims to use relevant information as a part of this course; however, I felt some disconnection with the content of the course. I did not go away from this course feeling like a learned a lot about Applied Ergonomics. Also as an online student, the course felt incredibly disorganized.

His class certainly isn't hard, as most of the assignments are discussion posts or basically graded on completion. My biggest issue with the course and Professor Duffy was lack of clarity. The class doesn't have a progression of material that builds on itself like most other classes, but was a scattered collection of ideas that felt disorganized.
Lovely professor with amazing coursework highly practical in real world application

Professor Duffy is very articulate and his lectures are insightful and engaging. His classes aren't too tough, but they have engaging activities and you will learn what you expect to from him. He communicates well and makes expectations clear when giving assignments.
Easy going and knowledgeable. This is my third course with him

Professor Duffy's feedback is crucial for the group projects, so pay close attention to his notes. The class structure is clear, but participation matters a lot. Make sure to study consistently to handle the pop quizzes.

reviews.comment: The course content is strong and applicable to real engineering and management scenarios, but grading criteria and feedback could be clearer. Assignments require significant effort, and clearer examples or rubrics would improve the learning experience. Overall, a valuable class if you're prepared for a fast pace and detailed work.

The course content is strong and applicable to real engineering and management scenarios, but grading criteria and feedback could be clearer. Overall, great class - used an online software for ergonomics analysis which is very applicable when you are in the industry.  Many assignments and homeworks.

The online section of this class was sometimes hard to follow. For the midterm and final, we had a lot of projects and discussion posts due. Those weeks I had significantly more work, and it felt like it could've been spread across the semester a little more. Sometimes lectures were posted late, but he always gave enough time to complete it.
Good course for a basic overview of ergonomics
Course is a practitioners course, you will learn how to use RAMSIS for design, and ergonomic design.

Professor Duffy's lectures are well organized, and content is clearly structured. There is a lot of stuff to complete, but not too heavy. Good time management will help in completing everything well before deadline. One advice to students - clearly read the announcements if you are taking course in distance learning mode. Overall, a good course.

reviews.comment: Professor Duffy is a highly knowledgeable ergonomics professional with deep expertise in human factors, digital human modeling, and safety, which comes through clearly in his teaching. His teaching style blends conceptual explanations with practical applications, frequently tying class topics to real-world design and evaluation problems.

Professor Duffy is knowledgeable & the course content is good. However, the class uses many different tools & platforms, which can be confusing and easy to miss things. Instructions are often long, and exam-related updates were sometimes shared close to midterm and final exams, which added stress.Clearer & more consistent communication would help.

Professor Duffy is knowledgeable and the course content is good. However, the class uses many different tools and platforms, which can be confusing and easy to miss things. Prof. Duffy's lectures are informative and interesting; students learn about class subjects through real world examples and open discussions. Classes are group-project heavy, assignments are not too difficult, but are relevant to the covered topics.

Dr Duffy is a fantastic person and a supportive teacher. The course is about itself, though. There are quiz questions which ask you what the contents of your homework were. It is a v easy course if you are patient with it.
The professor is liberal with assignments, and quizzes are spoon-fed feed
fun professor

It's a good course, but students are supposed to read the entire ergonomics themselves based on their interests with little explanation in the class. Professor Duffy's passion about the subject comes through in every lecture. He also brings in super interesting guest lecturers to class.

Exams are quite easy if you know where to look in your notes.
Lots of assignments though it's a fun subject if you're interested in Human Factors Engineering

reviews.comment: Professor Duffy is clearly knowledgeable and passionate about ergonomics. The class was easy and straight forward, but definitely unorganized. He also didn't respond to any of the emails I sent throughout the semester, but typically pushed back or fixed due dates which were usually the concerns.

If you wanted to take a lower-maintenance course, I would suggest this one. There are weekly-ish discussion posts and some other misc. assignments to go with them. The exams are nothing to worry about if you come to class. Duffy is a pretty easy-going professor and often will give extensions. I had no problems reaching out to him outside of class.
Professor Duffy is incredibly kind and co-operative. His course is engaging and interactive.

The Lectures are easy to glide by and the professor will ask for class participation in the form of 2-4 min presentations which are easy to glide by. Attendance is taken by iclicker so being in the class is appreciated.
Content is easy. However, I didn't fully understand a single instruction since the beginning of this course.

This course is pretty easy both technically and in terms of workload. Dr Duffy organizes most of his courses in a similar way, so I was pretty used to the structure. However, I think overall course is very disorganized and hard to understand instructions... really hard..
I love Prof Duffy's class mainly because he is good at making students learn the concept .
Prof duffy is soo chill and he is very good in making students understand the concept.
Good setup for online class, long due dates for most items and professor answers emails same day.
Good Course

He was very engaging in this class and made sure to always relate what we were reading in the textbook to real world examples and stuff that was happening at the current time. He always emphasized group work and always looking to show that ergonomics are in all our day to day lives. I would take any of his classes if you are interested.

Professor Vincent Duffy is a highly knowledgeable instructor who explains human factors and ergonomics concepts clearly using real examples. The course is challenging but expectations are clear, making the learning experience rigorous and rewarding.

if you expect a normal frontal lecture don't take this class; the first part of the semester students are expected to choose a book chapter and present it, so all the book is explained this way with a 10 minute presentation each, with little to no depth where the student is expected to deepen the knowledge of the chapters to his own interest
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who wants to ensure his students are getting a good amount of knowledge regarding ergonomics and are able to understand basic principles. Touches on a wide variety of topics and encourages students to explore more about the ergonomics and human factors.
In general, it is fine.

Prof Duffy is a really good instructor for IE 578. He explains things clearly, uses practical examples, and keeps the class organized. The workload is reasonable and the assignments actually help you learn. Overall, a solid and supportive professor.
The professor was very knowledgeable and professional. He explained the class and expectations well. In his videos, he would remind students of due dates and assignments, which was very helpful!

Honestly the course is great for the most part. It's not a challenging course at all and Prof Duffy is one of the most caring profs out there. The assignments are a tad bit disorganized though but not enough to put one off of taking up this one under prof Duffy.

The professor was effective in teaching applied ergonomics and made the material easy to understand and relevant. The teaching style was clear and encouraged discussion. While there were many assignments and case studies, they reinforced learning and real-world application.

The professor was effective in teaching applied ergonomics and made the material easy to understand and relevant. While there were many assignments and case studies.
Really easy course thanks to the way Dr. Duffy takes the lecture.
